free.text: 1 GB disk; may power off idle, deleted after 180 days off

sql.math: 730 hours a month at $0.016 an hour. Whether the storage and connection limits fit your app is not guaranteed.
An idle database still bills for all 730 hours a month. Costs for files stored outside it are not included.

files.math: Aiven has no file storage plan of its own.

jobs.math: 5 apps × 730 hours a month × $0.03836 an hour. This is an example for the workers only, before queue and other outside costs.

facts.label: Free offer type
facts.value: Recurring Free tier for PostgreSQL, MySQL, Valkey, OpenSearch and Kafka; indefinite without a card, subject to inactivity/AUP/configuration rules. Separate 30-day trial credits cover paid services/features.

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: PostgreSQL Free: one service/type/organization; one node, 1 CPU, 1GB RAM, 1GB disk, max_connections 20, extensions, metrics/logs and backups. No pooling, VPC, static IPs, integrations, free forks, support or SLA.

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: MySQL Free: one service/type/organization; one node, 1 CPU, 1GB RAM, 1GB disk; max_connections 76. Backups/metrics/logs included, but no VPC/static IP/integrations/fork/support/SLA.

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: Valkey Free: one service/type/organization; one node, 1 CPU, 1GB RAM, maxmemory set to 50%; backups/metrics/logs. No VPC/static IP/integrations/forks/support/SLA.

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: OpenSearch Free: 4GB RAM, 20GB storage, two shards with maximum 20 shards/node, 50 concurrent connections, snapshots up to three days. One service/organization, fixed cloud/region and no security plugin/custom repositories/integrations.

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: Kafka Free: ingress and egress each up to 250KiB/s; up to five topics with two partitions each; retention up to three days; Schema Registry and REST proxy. One free service/organization.

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: Separate trial: 30 days from signup, up to 10 VMs, one VPC and 10 VPC peerings; one trial, credits assigned to one billing group. Current OpenSearch Developer landing advertises $50 credits.

facts.label: Inactivity, pause and deletion
facts.value: Free may power off in the first few hours with no initial use or after lack of continuing activity; ongoing-inactivity interval is not numeric. Notification precedes inactivity power-off; manual power-on available. Developer services are not auto-powered-off for inactivity.

facts.label: Inactivity, pause and deletion
facts.value: Powered-off PostgreSQL services are deleted after more than 180 days, including backups under Terms. Powered-off EOL services generally delete seven days after the later of EOL/power-off; OpenSearch/Valkey have exceptions.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: PostgreSQL/MySQL Developer advertised $5/month; exact public PostgreSQL developer-1 catalog rate in do-fra is USD $0.007/hour. Provider/region is assigned, not a selectable Frankfurt entitlement.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: PostgreSQL Hobbyist: do-fra catalog USD $0.016/hour, one node, 1 CPU, 1024MB RAM, 8192MB disk. Pricing displays starting $12/month and rounded $0.02/hour.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: PostgreSQL Startup-4: do-fra USD $0.103/hour, one node, 2 CPU, 4096MB RAM, 81920MB disk; AWS Frankfurt USD $0.158/hour for this plan.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: PostgreSQL Business-4: do-fra USD $0.247/hour for two nodes; Premium-4 USD $0.370/hour for three nodes. Each node in these catalog entries has 2 CPU/4096MB RAM.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: Other advertised entry prices: Valkey Developer $15/month, OpenSearch Developer $40/month, Kafka Developer $35/month, ClickHouse Developer $43/month. Custom plans start at USD $5,000/month.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Managed services accrue charges while powered on, rounded up to whole-hour units (minimum one hour), invoiced monthly in arrears. Underlying VM, normal networking, backup and maintenance/migration included for ordinary database plans.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Runtime current pricing: hourly plan charge until power-off/delete, no separate build/idle surcharge. AWS Frankfurt catalog startup-10-256 $0.00959/hour; startup-50-1024 $0.03836/hour, 1024MB RAM.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Kafka Professional page shows starting $180/month beside $3.84/hour, unlike the coherent small-plan hourly examples. Exact selected Professional quote cannot be inferred from that pair.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Idle powered-on service still bills its allocated hourly plan. Manual power-off stops new service charges, releases VMs and later restores from backups; no automatic workload-based PostgreSQL scale-to-zero/wake service documented.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Powering off Runtime leaves connected databases/services running and billing separately; powering on redeploys the previously deployed commit.

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: PostgreSQL normal managed plan pricing includes network traffic and cloud/region migration, with no separate Aiven per-GB egress line. App/provider endpoints can charge their side; PrivateLink is an extra feature.

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: Kafka/Valkey fair-use terms qualify the general included-network claim: monitor/consult above underlying network cost of 7.5% of service price; after consultation, fees can apply above 10%.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: Storage autoscaling is optional and upward-only: PostgreSQL threshold 85%, increases at least 10% subject to provider steps, with configured cap_gb and plan maximum. Extra disk costs accrue.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: A universal hard dollar spend cap, its cutoff guarantees and exact Free disk-full grace/resume rule were not established. Trial can restrict new service creation when credits would run out too fast.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: PostgreSQL direct max_connections: Free 20; dedicated limit guide Developer 15, Hobbyist 25; Startup/Business/Premium-4 100, -8 200, -16 400, -32 800, -64+ 1000.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: General pricing docs say PostgreSQL Developer max_connections 20, while the dedicated connection guide says 15. Three to six connections are reserved, and maintenance can also use ordinary slots.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Startup+ PgBouncer: transaction (default), session or statement mode; max client connections = min(max(RAM GB × 500, 5000), 50000). Backend DB connection limits still apply.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Plan disks include WAL, indexes and internal data; idle WAL can occupy space before steady-state cleanup. No uniform per-record/query-byte or guaranteed QPS ceiling found for all engines/plans.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: OpenSearch Developer CPU allocation is inconsistent: landing benefits/how-much sections say 1 CPU, while its detailed list and pricing matrix say 2 vCPU; both show 4GB RAM/30GB storage.

facts.label: Storage prices
facts.value: No standalone managed object-file storage plan is established in this database/Runtime catalog; database disk and backup object storage are not an app bucket tariff.

facts.label: File request and retrieval prices
facts.value: Native bucket PUT/GET/list/retrieval/image-processing price fields do not apply to the scoped managed database plans.

facts.label: Minimum storage and early deletion
facts.value: Object-class minimum billed object size/duration and archive early-deletion charges are outside the database-plan model.

facts.label: Vector/index limits
facts.value: PostgreSQL pgvector supports exact distance search and approximate indexes; official guide illustrates IVFFlat and a 1,536-dimensional HNSW use case.

facts.label: Vector/index limits
facts.value: Installed pgvector version, maximum indexed dimensions, index/record/namespace count and metadata ceiling for a particular Aiven plan were not established.

facts.label: Embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: pgvector tutorial requires embeddings generated separately, for example through an external API. Aiven AI editor/Managed Agents are additional services with their own terms, not a recurring free embedding/reranking quota.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Runtime plans are hourly allocated compute, not per-job invocations. startup-50-1024 is described as 0.5 vCPU/1024MB, priced $0.03836/hour in AWS Frankfurt catalog. Jobs/retries/waits consume the running app’s resources.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: A universal Runtime per-job timeout, forced CPU/RAM isolation per task, concurrent-job guarantee and automatic retry billing unit were not established.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Public free signup and 30-day trial need no credit card. Paid continuation requires a payment method; one trial per customer, credits tied to one billing group. Temporary dead-drop account email addresses are prohibited.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Free services are presented for learning/prototyping; paid Developer is aimed at development/side projects. Terms classify free services/features as Beta and exclude normal reliability promises. No complete country eligibility list established.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: AUP requires BAA before transmitting HIPAA PHI and message-level encryption for cardholder/sensitive authentication data; Runtime enhanced PCI/HIPAA environments need a separate supplemental agreement.

facts.label: Primary type and other roles
facts.value: SQL and managed databases (our classification), with cache/search/analytics, Kafka streaming and optional container application hosting through Aiven Runtime.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Managed databases include database credentials, monitoring, maintenance and service-specific backup/HA options. Runtime is separately billed managed container compute; PostgreSQL pg_cron schedules SQL inside the database.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Runtime can protect apps with Aiven Identity or one OIDC identity provider. This is app-access gating; customer remains responsible for application auth/access rules and independent content backups.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: PostgreSQL wire protocol and SQL clients/drivers such as psql; native protocols/clients for other engines. Console, REST management API, CLI, Terraform and Kubernetes operator manage services.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Runtime deploys container builds from GitHub repositories using Containerfile/Dockerfile or Compose manifests. Supported data-service image names create separately managed Aiven services.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: PostgreSQL uses DB users/roles and TLS connection credentials; service IP filters and eligible paid VPC/private networking restrict reachability. User/application must enforce table/row access; management RBAC is separate.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: TLS is default for most data services, but MySQL accepts unencrypted connections unless each user is required to use SSL; Valkey can have TLS disabled. Data and backups encrypted at rest.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Runtime apps public by default; can add Aiven Identity or OIDC gating, one auth method per app. Customer still owns app-level access controls and security.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: Detailed relational scope: native PostgreSQL SQL, relational tables, JSON/JSONB and extensions, not an emulated PostgreSQL API. Catalog default major 18, latest_available_version 18.6 at check time.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: Aiven follows upstream engine EOL; PostgreSQL 15–18 creation remains supported at this check. PG14 creation ended 2026-05-12 and EOL is 2026-11-12. Services can be automatically upgraded, powered off or deleted under EOL policy.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: PostgreSQL supports native atomic SQL transactions (commit/rollback/savepoints); Aiven’s outbox example commits related table writes and logical messages within one DB transaction.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: Read replicas use asynchronous replication; recently committed primary writes can lag on replicas. Exact configured default isolation/durability settings were not established without a running service.

facts.label: Test environments and branches
facts.value: Forks are independent service copies from latest backup or supported PITR, with their own paid plan/cloud resources. PostgreSQL Free/Developer cannot be used as fork destinations under their restrictions.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: PostgreSQL Startup/Hobbyist single-node recovery rebuilds from backups with downtime; Business has primary+one standby, Premium primary+two. Failed primary can automatically promote a standby; service hostname remains, IP can change.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Separate read-only replicas can be in other clouds/regions and are separately provisioned services. Remote replica promotion is manual; programmatic creation uses Startup plan for the replica.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: PostgreSQL logical replication and aiven_extras support publications/subscriptions/CDC; Kafka can transport change events with separately configured connectors.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Native end-user offline-write queue, reconnect conflict resolution and a complete mobile/web synchronization contract were not established for the database catalog.

facts.label: Extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: PostgreSQL extension catalog includes PostGIS, TimescaleDB, pg_trgm, RUM, pgvector, pg_cron and others. pgvectorscale listed for PG16/17 at 0.6.0. Untrusted/superuser-only extensions require explicit allowlisting.

facts.label: Upload and file limits
facts.value: No native user-upload bucket API/size limit applies to the scoped database offer. Runtime can run customer upload code, whose limits/storage provider must be specified separately.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: S3-compatible customer bucket API is not the function of the PostgreSQL/Runtime offer. S3/object storage used internally for backups is not a public S3 gateway.

facts.label: Delivery and private files
facts.value: Bucket public/private/signed-file URL/CDN plan fields do not describe managed database endpoints. Runtime HTTP access can be public or identity-gated.

facts.label: Filters and mixed search
facts.value: PostgreSQL SQL can combine relational filters/joins with vector operators; text-search extensions include pg_trgm/RUM. OpenSearch separately advertises semantic, hybrid and vector search.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: Managed Runtime runs customer container applications, including worker code; database pg_cron runs SQL inside PostgreSQL. Kafka brokers transport events but application consumers still need execution compute.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: pg_cron can run different jobs in parallel, but at most one instance of the same job; an overlapping scheduled run waits for the prior run to complete. Runtime worker retry/idempotency logic belongs to the application.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Durable background-job at-least/exactly-once delivery, replay after restart, deduplication windows, backoff and dead-letter policy were not found for Runtime/pg_cron as a combined product.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: pg_cron supports five-field cron and intervals of 1–59 seconds. Kafka Free/Developer retention is up to three days; those topic limits are separate from Runtime execution or SQL schedule persistence.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Maximum Runtime queued-job payload, durable delay window, scheduler timezone override and missed-run catch-up guarantee were not established.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Runtime build logs and application logs retained 24 hours; export via integrations for longer retention. pg_cron exposes cron.job_run_details with status/start/end/return message.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Default pg_cron run-history purge/retention and a managed job replay archive were not established.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Aiven-managed hosting has no customer server install. BYOC requires customer cloud account, sales enablement and IAM/network/infrastructure templates; Aiven still operates the services.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Paid service/region choices include AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, DigitalOcean, OVH and UpCloud depending on product/plan. Examples: do-fra, aws-eu-central-1 and google-europe-west3 are Frankfurt. Free and some Developer placement cannot be selected.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Backups normally use same-region object storage; providers without suitable object storage may use the nearest region of another provider. Moving a service does not migrate its existing backups. DPA sets conditions for EEA-hosted personal-data transfers.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Use standard PostgreSQL tools (pg_dump/pg_restore) to export/migrate; encrypted managed backups cannot be downloaded directly. Create your own logical dumps. Runtime source/container definitions remain in the customer repository.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Delete services/projects/organizations before deleting a personal account; managed organizational users have different rules. Trial-credit billing groups/organizations cannot be deleted normally before trial end without support.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Service Backups says backups delete 30 days after service deletion. Terms/DPA use agreement-termination deletion within 90 days or after technology’s maximum retention, unless instructed otherwise/legally retained; data return can incur costs.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: PostgreSQL automatic full backups daily, WAL copied every five minutes or new WAL file. Physical backups cover the PostgreSQL instance, not one selectively restored database/table; logical dumps provide finer export.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Free/Developer/Hobbyist pricing describes a single disaster-recovery backup rather than selectable PITR history. Hobbyist backup table says no retention, but HA guide says two-day Hobbyist history.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: PostgreSQL Startup retains two days, Business fourteen days, Premium thirty days of backup history/PITR per pricing and backup documentation.

facts.label: File recovery and protection
facts.value: Native file versioning/undelete/locks are outside this database-plan scope. Runtime terms assign independent application/content backup responsibility to the customer.

facts.label: Identity and old names
facts.value: Aiven, operated by Aiven Ltd; official site aiven.io. A catalog of managed data services, not one interchangeable database engine.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Aiven-managed cloud services governed by commercial service terms. Underlying engines are open source, but that does not grant a license to clone the Aiven management platform.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: BYOC runs Aiven-managed services in the customer cloud account; AWS, Google Cloud and Azure supported, with some other options by request. Aiven fees and cloud infrastructure bills are separate.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Aiven remains operating; service-specific hosted offers have ended: Aiven for M3DB and InfluxDB (2025-04-30), Caching migration to Valkey (2025-03-31), AlloyDB Omni (2025-12-05), Apache Cassandra (2026-01-07), and Dragonfly (2026-09-30). Aiven for MySQL Free sign-ups ended 2026-11-06; its remaining free services are scheduled for deletion on 2026-12-21 (free-offer change, not an Aiven-wide shutdown).

facts.label: Vendor home and main markets
facts.value: Aiven Ltd, Finland; privacy policy identifies Business ID 2795743-5. Services can be hosted in multiple countries independently of the vendor’s home.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Free has documentation-only/no support entitlement under product docs and Support Services. Paid plans include Basic best-effort same/next-business-day support. Essential/Advanced/Premium support are paid add-ons.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Formal managed-data SLA: 99.99% monthly SLO with service credits for Startup/Business/Premium under stated conditions; Free excluded. Runtime has separate 99.9% commercially reasonable-efforts wording.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: OpenSearch Developer marketing advertises 99.99% SLA, but formal service-credit section names Startup/Business/Premium. Exact Developer credit entitlement is unresolved.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Kafka Free pricing matrix labels support “Basic”, while the formal Support Services page excludes Free plans from all support tiers.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Public service-status site: status.aiven.io, with incident/update information. It is separate from the contractual SLA and paid support response commitments.

jobs.math: Does not offer a job queue or workflow service

facts.label: App connection options

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: New buckets and objects are private by default in the documented Cloud Manager workflow.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Access keys use an access key ID and secret key. The secret key is revealed once when created; users can revoke a key to cut off its future access.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Unlimited keys grant the key's full access across its selected regions. Limited keys can be restricted to selected buckets with no access, read-only, or read/write permissions.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: The published account quota is 100 Object Storage access keys. A limited access key can have up to 25 buckets by default.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Bucket policies support grants and denies, including IP address conditions. Policy files are limited to 20 KB. Bucket policies apply to a whole bucket rather than individual objects.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: ACL, CORS, custom-domain TLS, and default encryption differ by endpoint type. CORS and custom domains are available only on legacy E0/E1; object-level ACLs are also unavailable on E2/E3.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Public objects can be read by URL if the bucket permissions allow it. Public read/write is documented but Akamai warns that it is not recommended.

facts.value: A single non-multipart upload is limited to 5 GB. Larger objects require multipart upload.

facts.label: Upload and file limits
facts.value: Maximum object size is 5 TiB; a multipart upload may contain up to 10,000 parts.

facts.label: Upload and file limits
facts.value: Multipart part sizes are 5 MiB to 5 GiB, except the final part has no minimum size.

facts.label: Upload and file limits
facts.value: List-parts and list-multipart-uploads responses return at most 1,000 entries per request.

facts.label: Upload and file limits
facts.value: Object Storage operation request headers have an 8 KB total-size limit on the documented presigned URL API.

facts.value: The service supports S3-compatible object operations through its regional endpoint hosts and access-key credentials.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Multipart downloads are not supported. A GET request with the partNumber parameter returns the whole object instead of a part.

facts.value: AWS CLI v2.23.0+ and boto3 v1.36.0+ may fail PutObject or UploadPart requests because their newer S3 data-integrity protections are not supported. The docs suggest an older client or request-checksum setting as a workaround, which may not work for every command.

facts.value: Objects can be reached through HTTPS URLs on shared linodeobjects.com endpoints. Private is the default; ACLs or bucket policies can make content public.

facts.label: Delivery and private files
facts.value: The API can create signed object URLs for GET, PUT, or DELETE. Expiration is 360–3,600 seconds, default 3,600 seconds.

facts.label: Delivery and private files
facts.value: A custom domain with a TLS certificate is supported only for legacy E0/E1 endpoints, on a subdomain such as assets.example.com; apex domains are not supported.

facts.label: Delivery and private files

facts.label: Delivery and private files
facts.value: Akamai CDN can cache from an Object Storage bucket origin, but CDN delivery and its charges are separate from the storage product.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting

facts.label: Leaving and deleting

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Bucket versioning retains older versions, and lifecycle rules can expire old versions or abort incomplete multipart uploads. Every retained version and unfinished part still consumes billable storage.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Cancelling Object Storage deletes buckets, objects, and access keys. Akamai says to download important files before cancelling; the guide does not promise a restore period.

facts.label: File recovery and protection
facts.value: E2/E3 endpoints automatically encrypt uploaded objects at rest using AES256 SSE-S3 as the default rollout completes. The current rollout window is October 6 to November 16, 2026; this is not yet complete on the research date.

facts.label: File recovery and protection
facts.value: SSE-C lets customers supply their own object encryption key. Akamai says the object cannot be recovered without that key.

facts.label: File recovery and protection
facts.value: Object versioning retains old versions when content is replaced or deleted. Each retained version counts toward billable storage; first-party Cloud Manager, CLI, and API tools cannot manage versioning.

facts.label: File recovery and protection
facts.value: Object Lock supports governance and compliance retention modes on E0 through E3, and must be enabled when a bucket is created. Object Lock management uses S3 APIs, not Cloud Manager.

facts.label: File recovery and protection
facts.value: Lifecycle policies can expire objects, noncurrent versions, and unfinished multipart uploads. They run at midnight in the bucket's local time and large deletes may take more than one run.

facts.label: File recovery and protection
facts.value: Replication across multiple nodes within the storage system protects against underlying hardware errors, but a bucket endpoint itself is in one region. Cross-region continuity requires separate endpoints and a customer-designed copy/failover setup.

facts.value: A public Akamai service-status page is linked from the Object Storage docs and support page. I did not record a status incident as an uptime promise.

facts.value: Current serverless upper bounds: MySQL 256 ACUs; PostgreSQL 384 ACUs only with a capable engine and platform 4. PG384 range starts at PG14.23/15.18/16.14/17.10/18.4; older engine/platform combinations have lower limits.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Default regional quota is 40 DB clusters, adjustable; DB-instance quota is generally40 and Mumbai20, shared with other named RDS-related services. Aurora allows up to 15 readers per writer.

facts.value: Serverless max_connections derives from maximum configured ACUs, not instantaneous capacity; changing max ACUs needs reboot to refresh it. MySQL max1 ACU default 90, max4ACUs135; PG platform 4 max1ACU194, max4ACUs844. PG minimum 0/0.5 ACU caps max_connections at 2000.

facts.value: IAM controls RDS management; PostgreSQL roles, GRANT/REVOKE and the managed rds_superuser role control SQL access. Application credentials need their own least-privilege roles.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: PostgreSQL has native row-level security; pg_columnmask adds optional column masking on supported versions. Data API also requires IAM authorization and database credentials.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Full-configuration PostgreSQL can use VPC security groups/private networking and TLS. rds.force_ssl defaults on for PG17+, off for PG16 and older; check the chosen version and client verification.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: IAM database-authentication tokens last 15 minutes for establishing a connection; IAM does not replace SQL grants. Express gateway supports IAM authentication only.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: Aurora MySQL is MySQL-compatible SQL; current release history includes Aurora 3.14.0 compatible with MySQL 8.0.46 and Aurora MySQL 8.4.10. Aurora PostgreSQL release calendar includes majors 14–18 under standard support, with older majors on Extended Support where eligible.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: Engine support is versioned; moving beyond standard support can add Extended Support charges. Pick a supported engine/version/Region rather than treating compatibility as an indefinite free upgrade promise.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: PostgreSQL supports atomic SQL transactions, commit/rollback and savepoints; READ COMMITTED is default. REPEATABLE READ and SERIALIZABLE are available; READ UNCOMMITTED behaves as READ COMMITTED.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: MySQL writer supports READ UNCOMMITTED, READ COMMITTED, REPEATABLE READ and SERIALIZABLE. Readers normally use REPEATABLE READ; opt-in reader READ COMMITTED permits documented anomalies and is less strict than the writer's mode.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: Storage writes replicate synchronously across AZ storage nodes, while Aurora reader instances replicate asynchronously. Reads sent to a reader can lag the writer.

facts.label: Test environments and branches
facts.value: Copy-on-write clones create independent test clusters sharing unchanged pages; changed data adds storage. Up to 15 copy-on-write clones, then a subsequent clone is a full copy; clones stay in the source Region.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Up to 15 read-only Aurora replicas share the cluster volume; Aurora automatically detects failures and can promote a reader. Multi-AZ compute requires adding a reader in another AZ; each reader is separately billed.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Global Database adds asynchronous cross-Region replication and secondary clusters. Each Region's compute/storage and applicable replicated-write/transfer meters must be priced separately.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: PostgreSQL logical replication publishes selected table changes using WAL and subscriptions; native pgoutput and wal2json are documented. It requires configuration and does not itself provide browser offline conflict resolution.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: A native Aurora client-offline read/write queue and conflict-resolution contract was not found.

facts.label: Extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: PostgreSQL supports approved extensions, including pg_partman and pgvector; extension versions are tied to engine versions. pg_cron needs preload configuration and restart; arbitrary host-installed extensions are not implied.

facts.value: Not applicable to the Aurora database service; use a separate object-store record for app files.

facts.value: Not applicable to the Aurora database service; use a separate object-store record for app files.

facts.value: Not applicable to the Aurora database service; use a separate object-store record for app files.

facts.label: Filters and mixed search
facts.value: PostgreSQL vector similarity can share SQL tables with text and metadata; AWS's Bedrock setup shows HNSW cosine index, full-text GIN index and JSON metadata GIN index.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: PostgreSQL pg_cron runs scheduled SQL within the database. MySQL has a configurable Event Scheduler. These execute database-side work, not a general0.5 vCPU application container.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Auto-pause does not wake for pg_cron or MySQL scheduled events. Runs due while paused are skipped, not replayed on resume; auto-pause can cancel a currently running job.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Data API client timeouts/retries can duplicate a successful write if the client times out before the service. Application retries need transaction/idempotency handling.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: A blanket exactly-once guarantee, automatic failed-job retry policy, dead-letter queue and replay window for database schedules were not established.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: pg_cron uses recurring cron schedules and stored SQL commands; unschedule removes a schedule. Job definitions/history reside in SQL tables; executions during auto-pause do not form a retained queue.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: A hosted delayed-message payload ceiling, queue retention TTL and complete custom-time-zone contract were not established for these SQL schedulers.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: pg_cron records status, messages and start/end time in cron.job_run_details; cron.log_run can disable table history. Rows need customer purging; seven days is a suggested cleanup example, not enforced retention.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: PostgreSQL local logs default 4320 minutes/3 days; configurable1440–10080 minutes/1–7 days. Storage pressure can delete logs sooner. Publishing to CloudWatch supports longer retention under separate pricing.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Not applicable: no self-hosted Aurora edition was established; self-managed PostgreSQL/MySQL is a separate deployment/product.

facts.value: Express PostgreSQL is documented in all AWS Regions except GovCloud, UAE and Bahrain. It uses an IAM internet gateway instead of association with the customer's VPC.

facts.value: DPA §12.1 permits selecting processing Regions; transfers outside selected Regions are limited to customer-initiated services or legal/binding government orders.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: us-east-1 Standard storage: first eligible 25 GB-months USD 0, then USD 0.25/GB-month. Actual item attribute names/values, 100-byte per-item storage overhead and index storage count; some enabled features add overhead.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: us-east-1 Standard-IA provisioned: USD 0.00081/WCU-hour and USD 0.00016/RCU-hour.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: us-east-1 native vector index charges, in addition to the base table: Standard USD 0.52/GB vector writes and USD 0.002/GB searched; Standard-IA USD 0.65/GB writes and USD 0.0025/GB searched. Storage uses the applicable table-class GB-month rate.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: us-east-1 optional recovery/data movement: PITR USD 0.20/GB-month; on-demand backup USD 0.10/GB-month; restore USD 0.15/GB; full/incremental export USD 0.10/GB; import USD 0.15/GB.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: us-east-1 Streams GetRecords: first eligible 2.5 million requests/month USD 0, then USD 0.0000002/request (USD 0.02/100,000). Ordinary DynamoDB-triggered Lambda GetRecords and global-table reads have stated exemptions; Lambda Managed Instances are excluded from the Lambda exemption.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Query filters/projections do not reduce read units for the data evaluated. Failed conditional writes can still consume write capacity based on the existing item size, with a minimum of one unit.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Optional paid pre-warming and reserved-capacity/Database Savings Plan commitments exist. Reserved capacity has one-/three-year terms and is noncancellable/nontransferable under Service Terms; it is not required for on-demand use.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: us-east-1 global-table replicated-write catalog rates: Standard USD 0.625/million rWRUs or USD 0.00065/rWCU-hour; Standard-IA USD 0.78/million rWRUs or USD 0.00081/rWCU-hour.

facts.label: idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: On-demand throughput has no idle capacity charge; storage remains. Provisioned capacity is charged by allocated RCU/WCU-hours, including idle hours, and has a nonzero minimum.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: For DynamoDB, inbound transfer and transfer to AWS services in the same Region are USD 0/GB. Cross-Region transfer is charged as described by pricing; global replication is not assumed free.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: us-east-1 internet transfer, separate AWSDataTransfer meter: USD 0.09/GB for first 10,240 GB/month beyond the global free tier, then USD 0.085 for the next 40,960 GB, USD 0.07 for the next 102,400 GB and USD 0.05 thereafter.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: The DynamoDB pricing page disagrees with itself: its Free Tier summary says 1 GB internet transfer and 15 GB during the first 12 months; treat the first-year 15 GB line as legacy eligibility for accounts created before 2025-07-15. Data Transfer In/Out separately says 100 GB/month shared across AWS services/Regions, excluding China/GovCloud. AWS says accounts created on or after 2025-07-15 use the replacement credit/Free-plan offer; earlier accounts retain legacy terms.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: On-demand max read/write throughput can be set per table/GSI; excess is throttled. The docs explicitly call these best-effort targets that can be exceeded temporarily using burst capacity.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: The current signup FAQ describes optional monthly project spend limits starting at USD 20, alerts at 50%/75%/90% and project pausing at the limit unless increased. This is an AWS account/project control, not a DynamoDB-only pricing plan.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: DynamoDB-specific coverage/exclusions and retained-storage/backup behavior under the new project spend pause were not established.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: All DynamoDB size units are binary: 1 KB = 1,024 bytes and 1 GB = 1,073,741,824 bytes. Maximum item size is 400 KB including attribute names/values. Query/Scan pages are limited to 1 MB and use pagination.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: BatchGetItem: up to 100 items/16 MB. BatchWriteItem: up to 25 Put/Delete requests/16 MB. Partition-key value maximum 2,048 bytes; sort-key value maximum 1,024 bytes.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Default quotas per Region: 2,500 tables/account; 40,000 read and 40,000 write units/second per table in either capacity mode. Provisioned account defaults total 80,000 RCUs/80,000 WCUs; on-demand has no corresponding account throughput aggregate quota.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: On-demand scaling immediately accommodates up to twice the previous peak; abrupt growth above that can throttle unless prewarmed or ramped over the documented interval. Customer maximum-throughput settings are also best-effort burst-tolerant targets.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Default index quotas are 5 LSIs and 20 GSIs per table. With an LSI, all items and projected LSI views sharing a partition key have a 10 GB item-collection limit.

facts.label: storage prices
facts.value: Not applicable: DynamoDB is not a database-independent file/object storage service.

facts.label: file request and retrieval prices
facts.value: Not applicable: DynamoDB is not a database-independent file/object storage service.

facts.label: minimum storage and early deletion
facts.value: Not applicable: DynamoDB is not a database-independent file/object storage service.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: Native vector indexes require on-demand mode on the table and index; Standard/Standard-IA are supported. Maximum 4,096 dimensions, TopK 1 to 100, and 5 vector indexes/table by default, adjustable up to 20 while counting toward the GSI quota.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: Per index: at most 1 HASH partition key and 18 inline filter attributes. SearchVectors responses are limited to 16 MB with no pagination. Default per-vector-partition-key rates are 1 GBps searched and 10 MBps written, adjustable through support.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: Vectors are indexed as float32; higher-precision base-table numbers lose precision in the index. Vector/index storage is separate from base-table storage, and projected attributes add size.

facts.label: embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: SearchVectors requires the caller to supply the query vector; examples store embeddings generated elsewhere. No included embedding/reranking model allowance or model tariff was found for DynamoDB.

facts.label: run limits and pricing
facts.value: Streams reads are billed by GetRecords request, not active job seconds. Lambda worker invocation/duration/logs and Kinesis consumer costs are separate; no DynamoDB execution-memory/concurrency entitlement is published for a 0.5-vCPU/0.5-GB worker.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Public AWS signup is available to individuals/businesses legally able to contract. Current October-2026-era signup FAQ says most new customers need no payment method, though identity verification may require one.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Production use is permitted through the paid account plan; use must comply with the Agreement/AUP and applicable laws. Free account plans are for experimentation/proof-of-concepts and have service/feature restrictions.

facts.label: primary type and other roles
facts.value: Researcher classification: managed NoSQL key-value/document database, with transactional APIs, change-data streams, optional global tables and native vector indexes.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: Included database capabilities are table/index APIs, regional multi-AZ durability, optional Streams, optional PITR/backups, transactions and native vector indexing. Global tables add regional replicas with separate regional usage charges.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Apps call DynamoDB HTTPS APIs through AWS SDKs/CLI; supported operations include item Get/Put/Update/Delete, Query/Scan, batches and PartiQL's supported SQL-like statements. This is not a PostgreSQL/MySQL wire endpoint.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: IAM identity/resource policies control table/index/stream access. Fine-grained conditions can restrict ordinary item APIs by partition key/attributes; applications must use correctly scoped credentials and authorization.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: SearchVectors does not support DynamoDB fine-grained condition keys such as LeadingKeys/Attributes/Select. Access is granted at index ARN scope; a tenant query filter is not a substitute for authorization.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Tables, indexes, Streams and backups are encrypted at rest; the AWS-owned key option has no key fee. Customer/AWS-managed KMS keys have separate KMS use/quotas, and vector indexes inherit table encryption.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: Native DynamoDB key-value/document tables with typed attributes and primary-key access, Query/Scan and a supported PartiQL subset. No SQL joins/foreign-key relational engine is implied by PartiQL.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Ordinary reads are read-committed and eventually consistent by default. Strongly consistent GetItem/Query/Scan is supported on tables/LSIs, but not ordinary GSIs or Streams.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: TransactWriteItems/TransactGetItems provide all-or-nothing operations across up to 100 distinct items and 4 MB within one account/Region. Write client tokens give a 10-minute idempotency window. BatchWriteItem is not an atomic transaction.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: MREC global-table transactions are atomic only in the invoked Region; replication can expose partial transaction results elsewhere. MRSC global tables do not support transaction operations, although they support strongly consistent item reads across supported Regions.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Separate tables/accounts and DynamoDB Local support development. Backup/PITR restores create separate tables; no native copy-on-write branch/merge workflow was established.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Regional DynamoDB automatically replicates data across multiple AZs without customer-provisioned database nodes. Global Tables version 2019.11.21 supports multi-active regional replicas, with MREC or MRSC choices and regional usage charges.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: MREC is asynchronous with last-writer-wins conflict resolution; MRSC synchronously replicates to another Region before acknowledging writes. MRSC has supported geographic sets/topologies and no transaction operations or TTL configuration.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Optional DynamoDB Streams records item changes in near real time for 24 hours, with each record once in the stream and modifications ordered per item. Consumers/Lambda can react to changes.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: A built-in offline browser/mobile database with conflict resolution was not established in DynamoDB itself.

facts.label: extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Native indexing includes LSIs/GSIs and vector indexes using COSINE, EUCLIDEAN or DOT_PRODUCT similarity. DynamoDB does not expose a PostgreSQL-style installable-extension catalog.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: Not applicable: DynamoDB is not a database-independent file/object storage service.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Not applicable: DynamoDB is not a database-independent file/object storage service.

facts.label: delivery and private files
facts.value: Not applicable: DynamoDB is not a database-independent file/object storage service.

facts.label: filters and mixed search
facts.value: ANN search uses SearchVectors, not Query/Scan/PartiQL. SearchConditionExpression can filter top-level HASH/INLINE_FILTER attributes by equality only; comparison, range and IN operators are not yet available.

facts.label: filters and mixed search
facts.value: Vector results are eventually consistent, including when the underlying global table uses MRSC. The index synchronizes asynchronously; missing the vector-index HASH attribute silently excludes an otherwise valid base-table item from that index.

facts.label: filters and mixed search
facts.value: A native full-text/BM25-plus-vector hybrid-ranking API was not found in the inspected current vector docs.

facts.label: execution model and languages
facts.value: DynamoDB Streams is change-event coordination. You host consumer code yourself or use separately billed AWS Lambda; DynamoDB does not provide a general app-function runtime or per-job CPU/RAM shape.

facts.label: delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Lambda triggers retry a failed batch until success or expiry unless configured otherwise; smaller batches/retry limits/record-age limits can be configured. Stream records have per-item ordering, but consumer retries can repeat processing.

facts.label: schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Streams retains changes for up to 24 hours and supports up to 2 simultaneous shard readers for ordinary single-Region tables (1 recommended for global-table shards). Retention is not a delayed-job schedule.

facts.label: schedules and queue retention
facts.value: TTL deletes eligible items typically within a few days, not at a guaranteed execution time. MRSC global tables do not support TTL; a general cron/delay scheduler was not found as a native DynamoDB worker feature.

facts.label: logs and run history
facts.value: DynamoDB emits service throughput/throttling metrics to CloudWatch; Streams supplies a 24-hour change log. A DynamoDB-managed application execution-result history, worker-log retention or failed-job replay window beyond retained stream records was not found.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: DynamoDB Local is for development/testing, available as a free JRE download, Docker image or Maven dependency. Docs require JRE 17 or newer for Local 2.6.0 and above; the default local port is 8000.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Local ignores provisioned throughput, does not support PITR or vector indexes and does not model all cloud transaction conflicts. Its in-memory mode loses data on exit; file-backed data needs your own backup.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Tables are created in an AWS Region, with data automatically replicated across multiple AZs in that Region. The public DynamoDB endpoint catalog lists commercial, GovCloud and China-region endpoints; account/feature access can differ.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Global tables place replicas in selected Regions. MRSC uses supported geographic region sets and either 3 replicas or 2 replicas plus a witness; it is not an arbitrary all-region strong-consistency mesh.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: AWS Agreement allows customer-selected content regions, subject to legal-order exceptions; Privacy governs account information separately. Backups can be restored/copied across Regions through the documented workflows.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Export to S3 supports DynamoDB JSON/Amazon Ion and full/incremental exports, with PITR enabled. Import supports CSV, DynamoDB JSON or Amazon Ion into a new table; S3 costs remain separate.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: DeleteTable removes the table and indexes asynchronously; operations might still succeed during DELETING. A disabled stream is retained/deleted after 24 hours. PITR-enabled deletion creates a system backup retained up to 35 days under the pricing description.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Agreement section 5.3 gives a conditional 30-day content-retrieval period after qualifying termination, requiring amounts due to be paid; excluded termination cases differ. Free-plan account expiry has a separate 90-day rule. Exact final physical erasure timing for all DynamoDB backup copies was not established.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Opt-in PITR provides per-second restore points, default 35-day history configurable from 1 to 35 days. The newest restorable time is typically about 5 minutes behind current time; restoring creates a new table.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: On-demand snapshots are separately stored/encrypted and billed by backup size/duration. AWS Backup adds its own management/copy/cold-storage features; it is a separate service. Cold backups managed by AWS Backup have a 90-day minimum storage charge.

facts.label: file recovery and protection
facts.value: Not applicable: DynamoDB is not a database-independent file/object storage service.

facts.label: identity and old names
facts.value: Amazon DynamoDB, an AWS managed key-value and document database. DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is a separately charged caching service, which has its own pricing.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: Production DynamoDB is an AWS-operated hosted service under the AWS Customer Agreement and applicable Service Terms. There is no customer-operated production server edition established by these sources.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: DynamoDB Local is a free downloadable development/test implementation. An exact distribution-specific license was not established from its deployment/usage pages, DynamoDB Service Terms or generic Amazon Software License page.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Current active product with current pricing and documentation. No DynamoDB service shutdown, sunset or acquisition notice was found in AWS's maintenance, sunset and full-shutdown lists or the bounded official searches.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Note 2026-11-09: AWS reported a restored DynamoDB endpoint-DNS outage in US East (N. Virginia) on 2025-10-19/20; no shutdown or ownership change found.

facts.label: vendor home and main markets
facts.value: AWS Privacy Notice states Amazon Web Services, Inc. is in the United States; affiliates are worldwide. The contracting company depends on customer location under the Customer Agreement.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: Basic AWS Support includes customer service, docs/community and Health access. Technical support plans are separately purchased; no paid technical-response entitlement is inferred for the smallest DynamoDB bill.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: DynamoDB SLA: 99.99% Standard; 99.999% Global Tables only when all tables in the Region qualify throughout the cycle and reasonable failover attempts are made. Credits require a qualifying claim and must exceed USD 1.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: The public AWS Health status page returned no readable incident text in the direct reader. AWS's official DynamoDB us-east-1 RSS feed was readable and used as the regional alternative; no healthy/incident-free claim is made.

apps.name: Amazon ElastiCache
apps.line: Managed in-memory cache for Valkey, Redis OSS and Memcached.

free.text: $100 credits; Free Plan ends by 6 months, 90-day recovery window

cells.regions: Region-dependent; US East rates shown

sql.math: 730 hours × $0.0256 an hour for one t4g.small node. This assumes the data fits in 1 GB. Network and other charges are not included.
730 hours × $0.0256 an hour for a node that runs all month. Idle traffic doesn't stop this hourly charge.

files.math: This is a cache, not file storage.

jobs.math: Does not execute general background jobs

facts.label: free offer type
facts.value: No lasting ElastiCache Free plan quota is advertised for new accounts. Current offer is shared AWS promotional credit: USD 100 at signup and up to USD 100 earned through qualifying activities.

facts.label: free offer type
facts.value: Credit expiry disagrees: Free Tier Terms say 12 months; current FAQ General Q6/Advanced Features Q2 say 6 months, while its Paid Plan-upgrade and activity-credit answers still say 12 months.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: Historical pre-2025-07-15 cohort: 750 cache.t3.micro node-hours/month for 12 months; Serverless excluded. The 12-month window is historical by the 2026-11-05 research date, not a new-account ongoing allowance.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: Current Free Plan lasts at most six months or until shared credits are exhausted. Credit eligibility is limited to new customers, not additional accounts for a current/former customer. GovCloud/China credits have separate exclusions.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: Node clusters continue billing when available but idle; to stop cache-node charges, delete them. Manual snapshots survive deletion; automatic snapshots do not. No ordinary no-traffic auto-deletion rule is stated for paid caches.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: Free Plan expiration suspends account/resource access; upgrading within 90 days can recover access. Free Tier Terms permit reclaiming unused promotional resources after three months without use with 30 days' notice.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: US East (N. Virginia), us-east-1, USD: smallest listed t4g Valkey node cache.t4g.micro, 0.5 GiB RAM, $0.0128/node-hour. No on-demand long-term commitment, but each partial node-hour is billed as a full hour.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: us-east-1, USD: cache.t4g.micro Redis OSS or Memcached, 0.5 GiB RAM, $0.016/node-hour. Replicas and additional nodes are separately charged.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: Serverless has no account subscription/upfront commitment; minimum metered storage is 100 MB/cache for Valkey and 1 GB/cache for Redis OSS/Memcached. Raising usage minimums can create further idle charges.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Node-based Valkey, us-east-1, USD: t4g.small, 1.37 GiB RAM, $0.0256/node-hour; t4g.medium, 3.09 GiB, $0.052/node-hour. Pay for each provisioned node, including replicas.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Node-based Redis OSS/Memcached, us-east-1, USD: t4g.small $0.032/node-hour, t4g.medium $0.065/node-hour, with 1.37/3.09 GiB RAM respectively.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Serverless Valkey, us-east-1, USD: $0.084/GB-hour data storage and $0.0023/million ECPUs. Catalog unit rate is $0.0000000023/ECPU.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Serverless Redis OSS/Memcached, us-east-1, USD: $0.125/GB-hour and $0.0034/million ECPUs ($0.0000000034/ECPU). Minimum 1 GB metered data per cache.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Serverless ECPU combines processor work and transferred bytes. Simple GET/SET with ≤1 KB transferred uses 1 ECPU; 3.2 KB transfer can cost 3.2 ECPUs, and CPU-heavy commands can cost more.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Node-based Valkey 9+ durability: asynchronous writes add no durability fee; synchronous writes add 18% to standard node-hour pricing. Only supported families/topologies qualify; t4g does not.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Node-based Reserved Nodes commit for one or three years; Database Savings Plans commit to a USD/hour amount for one year. Reserved Nodes are not available for Serverless and are noncancellable/nonrefundable subject to the stated exceptions.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: us-east-1, USD, backup rate has a unit discrepancy: pricing says $0.085/GiB-month (all regions); the regional catalog labels backup storage $0.085/GB-month. Backup/create/restore transfer is free, but exact billing-size conversion is unresolved.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Redis OSS extended support: 80% of standard on-demand node rate in years 1/2 and 160% in year 3, in addition to the node charge. Region/date/engine eligibility applies; reservation discounts do not define the surcharge base.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Optional detailed CloudWatch metrics/alarms/querying and migration nodes may add charges. Serverless migration nodes have a separate 180-day account-level free period; cache storage/ECPU is billed throughout.

facts.label: idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Node-based capacity remains billed while idle; there is no documented cache stop/resume billing option equivalent to deleting the cluster.

facts.label: idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Serverless can reduce usage but does not scale its storage bill to zero: engine-specific minimum data still meters. User-set minimum ECPU/sec or storage is billed even when actual use is lower.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: Within us-east-1: Serverless with a VPC endpoint has no in-region data-transfer fee. Node-based same-AZ traffic has no transfer fee; cross-AZ application traffic is $0.01/GB on the application side, while the ElastiCache node side is uncharged.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: Serverless public endpoint same-region application traffic is $0.01/GB on the application side; cache side is uncharged. Cross-region routes differ by VPC/public endpoint and require standard route-specific AWS rates.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: Internet output has a shared 100 GB/month AWS allowance across participating services/regions, excluding China/GovCloud; standard AWS route rates apply beyond it. A cache does not get its own dedicated 100 GB allowance.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: Serverless maximum storage and ECPU/sec limits constrain cache use: storage pressure evicts TTL keys by LRU or returns OOM; exceeding ECPU/sec max throttles requests.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: Current signup FAQ offers Paid Plan project spend limits starting at $20/month as published, alerts at 50/75/90%, optional early controls and project pausing at the limit. The answer does not label the dollar currency or settle every ElastiCache deployment/ancillary charge.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Default regional account quotas: 40 Serverless caches; 300 non-reserved nodes; Memcached 60 nodes/cluster; cluster-mode Valkey/Redis 90 nodes/cluster. Some quotas can be increased; account Service Quotas is authoritative.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Serverless Valkey/Redis limits: 5,000 GiB/cache, 32 GiB/hash slot, 15,000,000 ECPU/sec/cache; per-slot 30K or 90K with replica reads. Max 65,000 concurrent clients/cache.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Serverless Valkey/Redis: 512 MiB maximum single element request, 1 GiB client query buffer, 39,999 arguments/request, 4 KiB key/channel name, 4 MiB Lua script and 5,000 ms Lua time limit before intervention.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Node RAM varies by type: listed t4g micro/small/medium have 0.5/1.37/3.09 GiB. Usable payload must allow reserved engine memory, key/index overhead and workload needs; nominal RAM is not a raw-data allowance.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: Node-based Valkey search: maximum 32,768 dimensions; 9.0+ up to 1,000 indexes and 1,000 fields/index, versus 8.2 up to 10 indexes and 50 fields/index. FT.SEARCH timeout clause max 60,000 ms.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: AWS's ElastiCache setup tutorial demonstrates HNSW/FLOAT32 embeddings. Raw vector arrays do not predict index RAM; search reserves and backfill behavior matter. Serverless is outside the documented search deployment.

facts.label: embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: ElastiCache stores/searches vectors; embedding and model inference are separate steps/services in AWS's agentic-memory/semantic-cache examples. No embedding-token or learned-reranking allowance is bundled into the cited node price.

facts.label: storage prices
facts.value: Not applicable: this is cache/key-value capacity, not native database-independent hot/archive file storage. S3 snapshot destinations are separate services.

facts.label: file request and retrieval prices
facts.value: Not applicable: no native file GET/PUT/retrieval/image-processing price applies. ECPU charges measure cache commands and transferred data.

facts.label: minimum storage and early deletion
facts.value: Not applicable for object minimum size, storage classes or early deletion. Cache minimum metered capacity is recorded under C12/C14.

facts.label: run limits and pricing
facts.value: Reference isolated 0.5 vCPU/0.5 GB workers, per-job wall time and invocation pricing do not apply to cache-node/ECPU pricing. Serverless Lua's 5-second intervention threshold is an engine limit.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Public account-based access via console/API/CLI. Current Free Tier FAQ says no payment method is needed for most new customers, although identity verification can require one. Paid account use can incur standard charges.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Free Plan accounts are for evaluation and should not process sensitive data; production users should distinguish them from a Paid Plan with promotional credits. Contractual capacity, export/trade restrictions and account-specific verification still apply.

facts.label: primary type and other roles
facts.value: Researcher classification: managed in-memory key-value store/cache. Secondary uses include sessions, leaderboards, pub/sub, stream data and node-based Valkey search; selected Valkey 9+ node clusters can additionally persist acknowledged writes.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: Native cache data structures/commands, TTL/eviction, Valkey/Redis pub-sub and streams, Lua scripts, replication/backups and monitoring. These do not include a managed app-login, uploaded-file/CDN or isolated application-functions bundle.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: Node-based Valkey supports vector search from 8.2; Valkey 9+ adds numeric/tag/full-text/hybrid search and aggregation. Optional Valkey 9+ durability is node-based only. Search is documented for node-based clusters; Serverless durability is explicitly unsupported.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Data-plane access uses Valkey/Redis or Memcached protocol clients; the AWS SDK/CLI manages caches rather than replacing engine data clients. Serverless Valkey/Redis requires a cluster-capable TLS client.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Serverless public endpoint is supported for Valkey 9.0+; all public connections require IAM authentication and TLS 1.3. GLIDE 2.2+ handles IAM token generation/refresh; examples cover Python, Java and Node.js.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Memcached auto-discovery clients identify/connect to cluster nodes; AWS documents PHP and .NET clients. Application clients must still match node/serverless TLS/protocol constraints.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Serverless encrypts at rest and in transit; node-based encryption is a configuration choice subject to engine/version support. IAM controls resource administration; Valkey/Redis RBAC access strings restrict key/command access.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Public Serverless Valkey 9+ requires IAM-only users and TLS 1.3; VPC-backed caches use network/security-group controls. Node-based clusters have no public endpoint option.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: IAM connection tokens last 15 minutes; connections disconnect after 12 hours unless reauthenticated with a fresh token. IAM AUTH/HELLO cannot be issued inside MULTI/EXEC/Lua, but regular data transactions on an authenticated connection are supported.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: Valkey, Redis OSS and Memcached are distinct supported engines. Serverless supports Valkey 7.2+, Redis OSS 7.1 and Memcached 1.6.22+; node-based versions span more older releases, subject to EOL/upgrade policies.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Valkey/Redis support MULTI/EXEC and Lua within the managed command subset. Upstream Valkey transactions serialize execution but do not roll back runtime command failures; other queued commands can still execute. This is not SQL-style rollback semantics.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Ordinary replicas are asynchronous and can lag or lose recent writes during failover. Serverless read port 6380 explicitly serves eventually consistent reads; primary port 6379 supports reads/writes.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Node-based Valkey 9+ optional durability: sync persists across at least two AZs before acknowledgment; async can lose up to ten seconds. Async rejects further writes if it cannot persist the accepted backlog within ten seconds.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Separate caches/clusters and snapshot restores can create development/test environments; restored caches are separate billable resources. No native copy-on-write branch allowance or branch tariff was found.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Valkey/Redis node groups support up to five read replicas per primary; Multi-AZ can fail over to a replica. Ordinary async replication can lose recent writes; durable sync mode changes this loss behavior.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Serverless stores redundant data across three AZs and manages failover without customers buying three separately billed node replicas. Global Datastore is a separate node-based cross-region replication option, not supported by Serverless.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Valkey/Redis pub/sub and streams are supported data primitives. Serverless pub/sub uses sharded pub/sub internally; keyspace-event notifications are not supported there.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Native full offline client synchronization/conflict resolution was not established.

facts.label: extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Node-based Valkey 8.2 search is vector-only; Valkey 9+ adds text, numeric, tag, aggregation and hybrid search at no separate search feature fee. Search is excluded from data-tiering nodes; t-family micro/small require at least 50%/30% memory reserve.

facts.label: filters and mixed search
facts.value: Valkey 9+ supports text/tag/numeric filters with vector retrieval and aggregation. Search permissions are checked at whole-index keyspace-prefix level, not row-by-row filtering of arbitrary keys.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: Not applicable as multipart/resumable file upload limits. Valkey/Redis protocol element/query/script limits are under D03.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Not applicable as an S3-compatible public storage API. Snapshot export copies a backup into the customer's S3 bucket, rather than exposing cache keys as S3 objects.

facts.label: delivery and private files
facts.value: Not applicable for file buckets, presigned file URLs or CDN delivery. Cache network/IAM/ACL access is described under C08/C18.

facts.label: execution model and languages
facts.value: Not a hosted worker/job-execution platform. Lua executes engine-side command logic; lists/streams can back an application-owned queue whose workers run elsewhere.

facts.label: delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: End-to-end job retry, duplicate handling, dead-letter and execution-order guarantees depend on the queue/worker implementation. Cache stream/list commands are not such a managed execution contract.

facts.label: schedules and queue retention
facts.value: No general durable cron/delayed-job service is included in the scoped cache offer. TTL controls cached-data expiry, not a promise to execute code at that time.

facts.label: logs and run history
facts.value: No native per-job execution-history/replay retention contract applies. Node/cache metrics and optional logs/monitoring concern the cache service.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Not applicable to self-hosting ElastiCache: AWS manages the service infrastructure. Upstream Valkey/Redis/Memcached self-hosting is a different product; ElastiCache on Outposts still uses AWS-managed hardware/services.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Caches are created in a selected AWS region; this research prices us-east-1 only. Serverless replicates across multiple AZs; node placement/replicas are configurable. Region/node-feature availability varies; use the linked matrix for another deployment.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Valkey/Redis snapshots can export .rdb files into an S3 bucket in the same region; move/copy afterwards for another region. Node-based Memcached has no snapshot export; Serverless Memcached export is supported. Data-tiering snapshots cannot export to S3.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Delete cache resources to stop ordinary usage charges; manual snapshots remain until separately deleted, automatic snapshots do not. AWS Privacy Notice covers account/personal information rather than customer cache content.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Exact physical purge time for deleted caches, replicas and retained backup copies was not established.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Valkey/Redis node-based and Serverless caches support snapshots; Memcached supports them only on Serverless. Restore creates a new cache, seeded from cache data/metadata, with snapshots stored in S3.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Automatic backups can run daily with retention up to 35 days; retention 0 disables them. Manual limit is 24/serverless cache per 24 hours, or 20 per node/24 hours for Valkey/Redis node clusters.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Backups/export restrictions: data-tiering snapshots cannot export to S3; Valkey/Redis snapshots can seed node or Serverless caches. Independent manual snapshots remain after cluster deletion; automatic ones are removed.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: An exact continuous point-in-time restore window and universal included/free snapshot-storage allowance were not established from current pricing and backup docs.

facts.label: file recovery and protection
facts.value: Not applicable for app-file versioning, object lock or undelete. Cache snapshot and eviction behavior are recorded separately under D05/C16.

facts.label: identity and old names
facts.value: Amazon ElastiCache, an AWS managed service with Valkey, Redis OSS and Memcached engines; official URL aws.amazon.com/elasticache/.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: Managed AWS service, not a downloadable self-hosted ElastiCache edition. AWS Customer Agreement and ElastiCache-specific Service Terms apply; §17.1 forbids accessing/tampering with software AWS installs on cache nodes.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Active node-based and Serverless offers; no whole-service shutdown, sunset or acquisition notice found in the official pricing, FAQ, current deployment and lifecycle pages searched.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Note 2026-11-09: Redis OSS 4/5 standard support ended in January 2026 and paid Extended Support is available; this is an engine-version support change, not an ElastiCache retirement.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Current docs list Valkey through 9.1. Serverless automatic minor/patch updates and customer-controlled major upgrades differ from node-based maintenance/version management. Search and durability availability must be checked per engine/deployment.

facts.label: vendor home and main markets
facts.value: AWS operates internationally through contracting entities determined by account location. The contracting-party table lists Amazon Web Services, Inc., Seattle, United States, and AWS EMEA SARL in Luxembourg, among others.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: Basic AWS support includes customer service, documentation and re:Post; technical-support plans are separately purchased. AWS Health (https://health.aws.amazon.com/health/status) is the status/incident path; no paid technical-response target is included in the smallest cache price.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: Serverless and qualifying node-based Multi-AZ have a 99.99% monthly SLA; node Single-AZ is 99.5%. Memcached Cross-AZ/previous-generation Multi-AZ have separate 99.9% terms. Credits, exclusions, configuration definitions and claim deadlines apply.
