facts.label: Free offer type
facts.value: Current offer is credit-funded: USD $100 at signup plus up to $100 earned, shared across eligible AWS services. Free plan ends after six months or credit exhaustion; Paid use continues at regular rates.

facts.label: Free offer type
facts.value: Credit expiry is inconsistent: RDS pricing says up to 12 months; current Free Tier FAQ General Q6/Advanced Features Q2 says six months, while Free Plan Q8 and earned-credit Q5 says 12 months.

facts.label: Free offer type
facts.value: Legacy eligibility cutoff differs: RDS pricing/Free page says before July 15, 2025; the User Guide overview says before July 17, 2025. Both describe a 12-month legacy window.

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: Restricted Free: Single-AZ t3.micro for MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL or SQL Server Express; t4g.micro for the first three engines. RDS Custom, Reserved Instances and other deployment types are excluded.

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: Historical legacy offer: 750 eligible instance-hours/month aggregated by the published engine/class rules, 20 GB gp2 storage/month and 20 GB automated-backup storage/month for one year.

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: A complete current restricted-Free storage/project/connection ceiling beyond the published classes/deployment restrictions was not found.

facts.label: Inactivity, pause and deletion
facts.value: Free-plan expiry closes/suspends access; upgrade to Paid within 90 days to recover data/resources. Without upgrading AWS says account/content are permanently deleted after that window.

facts.label: Inactivity, pause and deletion
facts.value: Stopped RDS instances restart automatically after seven consecutive days. Data/configuration persist; start explicitly to use the database before then.

facts.label: Inactivity, pause and deletion
facts.value: No universal ordinary paid-RDS idle-deletion timer was established.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: On-Demand has no upfront fee or fixed monthly/seat commitment. N. Virginia PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB t4g.micro Single-AZ cost USD $0.016/instance-hour, plus allocated storage and other applicable meters.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: SQL Server Express t3.micro Single-AZ public catalog rate is USD $0.022/hour, license included; storage/CPU/network remain separate. SQL Server Agent is documented for Enterprise/Standard/Web, not this Express example.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: Prices are before applicable indirect taxes unless law requires otherwise. Example rates use the catalog's USD currency, without conversion or negotiated discounts.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: N. Virginia Single-AZ PostgreSQL/MySQL/SQL Server gp3 allocated storage: USD $0.115/GB-month; extra gp3 IOPS USD $0.02/IOPS-month where provisioned above the included baseline. Actual read/write request counts are not separately billed on gp3.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Small gp3 PostgreSQL/MySQL/MariaDB/Db2 allocation: 20–399 GiB includes baseline 3, 000 IOPS and 125 MiB/s; higher allocation/engine thresholds can change included performance and billable extras.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: RDS usage bills per second with a ten-minute minimum. Provisioned storage/IOPS also meter by time; additional IOPS cost even when unused. Engine-specific On-Demand rules and optional reservations still apply.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: PostgreSQL/MySQL/MariaDB T3/T4g excess CPU credits: $0.075/vCPU-hour. SQL Server T3: $0.144/vCPU-hour. Unlimited mode compares average CPU against baseline over rolling 24 hours; RI discounts do not cover credits.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Reserved Instances commit for one or three years; Database Savings Plans use a one-year dollar/hour commitment. Capacity reservations and associated-service meters can add charges independently of whether queries run.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Db2 Marketplace licensing is billed separately from the RDS infrastructure tariff; Oracle BYOL and SQL Server BYOM also require customer entitlements/media and may have separate vendor/support costs.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Public IPv4 addresses add $0.005/address-hour, including the RDS example in VPC pricing. Publicly accessible stopped RDS instances continue the IPv4 charge.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Pricing/catalog use GB-month, while the RDS billing guide says GiB/month for storage/backups. Minimum gp3 allocation is documented in GiB.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: N. Virginia PostgreSQL Multi-AZ DB instance: t4g.micro USD $0.032/hour for the paired deployment; gp3 storage USD $0.23/GB-month. Additional provisioned gp3 IOPS USD $0.04/IOPS-month.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Ordinary RDS DB-instance compute bills while running, including zero-query hours. Manual stop removes instance-hour charges; provisioned storage/IOPS, backup and applicable public IPv4 charges continue.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Cannot stop an instance that is or has a read replica. SQL Server Multi-AZ instances cannot be stopped. Stop/start can take substantial time and automatically ends after seven days.

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: Shared internet-out allowance:100 GB/month aggregated across AWS services/Regions except China/GovCloud. N. Virginia ordinary outbound tariff beyond it: first10 TB $0.09/GB, next40 TB $0.085, next100 TB $0.07, above150 TB $0.05.

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: RDS↔EC2 same AZ and Multi-AZ replication transfer are free. Cross-AZ application traffic charges the EC2 side $0.01/GB in/out, with no additional RDS-side charge per the pricing text.

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: Public transfer catalog: N. Virginia→Ohio USD $0.01/GB; N. Virginia→Oregon USD $0.02/GB. Cross-Region snapshot/backup copies additionally incur destination backup storage.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: Service Quotas block additional resource creation when limits are reached. Storage autoscaling can grow allocation to the configured maximum, never shrink it; it is not a monthly dollar cap.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: Ordinary AWS Budgets alerts/actions can lag usage billing; costs may exceed the notification threshold before action. A budget email alone is not a guaranteed cap.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: New AWS experience Paid projects can set a spend limit: minimum greater of $20 or conservative projected spend; pre-tax, credits excluded. Notifications at 50/75/90%; limit attainment pauses project resources.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: Raise the spend limit to reactivate; some resources need manual restart. No action within90 days of a project pause causes permanent project-data deletion; up to ten projects may have spend limits.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Small gp3 allocations start at 20 GiB; primary gp3 volumes reach65, 536 GiB under the engine-specific table. SQL Server can use supported additional volumes for up to 256 TiB total; class/edition/volume conditions apply.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Regional DB-instance quota generally40, Mumbai20; quotas can be raised. The quota counts RDS/Aurora/Neptune/DocumentDB instances together. Read-replica quota is generally15/primary, with engine-specific limits and support.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: PostgreSQL default max_connections = LEAST(DBInstanceClassMemory/9531392, 5000); MySQL = DBInstanceClassMemory/12582880; MariaDB 10.5+ = LEAST(DBInstanceClassMemory/25165760, 12000). Memory variable excludes reserved overhead.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Db2 connection limit64, 000 is not configurable. SQL Server's user-connections setting allows0–32767, with 0 labelled unlimited; actual safe concurrency still depends on resources/engine settings.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Universal native query/request and row-size ceilings across all six engines were not established.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Oracle processes defaults to LEAST(DBInstanceClassMemory/9868951, 20000), allowed80–20000; sessions allowed100–65535 with no single published default in the table.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: MySQL's external-export guide lists maximum max_allowed_packet and slave_max_allowed_packet values of 1 GB and recommends them for that replication/export setup.

facts.label: Storage prices
facts.value: Not applicable to standard RDS as an independent app-file store.

facts.label: File request and retrieval prices
facts.value: Not applicable to standard RDS as an independent app-file store.

facts.label: Minimum storage and early deletion
facts.value: Not applicable to standard RDS as an independent app-file store.

facts.label: Vector/index limits
facts.value: RDS PostgreSQL pgvector supports HNSW and vector data. AWS's RDS-specific pgvector0.7 announcement gives indexed maxima4, 000 dimensions for halfvec and 64, 000 for binary vectors; sparsevec holds up to 1, 000 nonzero dimensions.

facts.label: Vector/index limits
facts.value: The AWS HNSW example explicitly uses1, 536-dimension vectors on RDS PostgreSQL. It demonstrates syntax/capability, not micro-instance sizing or a directory workload benchmark.

facts.label: Vector/index limits
facts.value: A separate hosted vector-record/index/metadata quota and complete current limits for every vector type and RDS engine were not established.

facts.label: Embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: Embedding generation is separate from stored vectors. The AWS RDS article names Titan embeddings as an external source; RDS for Oracle also documents a separate Bedrock integration.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: pg_cron default concurrent jobs5, requiring max_worker_processes greater than cron.max_running_jobs. SQL Server Multi-AZ Agent has10, 000-job limit, raiseable via Support. Jobs consume ordinary instance/storage resources.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Universal scheduled-job timeouts, dedicated per-job CPU/RAM and exact incremental retry/wait charges were not established.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Self-service console/CLI/API creation; Paid plan explicitly supports production applications. Current Free signup usually needs no payment method, although AWS can request one for identity verification.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: New Free plan/credits require a genuinely new AWS customer. Existing or previously held accounts are ineligible. SQL Server Developer is non-production only; Web Edition has public web-hosting usage restrictions.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Complete country eligibility and an express commercial-production permission for the restricted Free plan were not established.

facts.label: Primary type and other roles
facts.value: Researcher classification: managed relational SQL databases; optional PostgreSQL vector search and database-side scheduled work. RDS Custom is a separate managed mode with greater host access.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Native SQL databases, managed storage/backups, monitoring, replicas and administrative APIs. App-user login, independent file buckets and general application functions use separate services rather than RDS allowances.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Use standard engine protocols/drivers and clients, such as psql/pgAdmin, Oracle SQL*Plus and Db2 CLP. AWS SDK/CLI/RDS API manages infrastructure; this is not a generic HTTP SQL Data API for these six engines.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: RDS Proxy is optional managed pooling, not part of a free universal connection allowance. Multi-AZ DB clusters expose writer/reader/instance endpoints with different routing roles.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: IAM controls AWS management; engine roles/grants control SQL data. Standard RDS master users have managed privileges, not unrestricted host/root access; app connections need appropriate least-privilege database roles.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: VPC networking/security groups and SSL/TLS are supported. RDS PostgreSQL rds.force_ssl defaults on for 15+, off for 14 and older; configure certificate verification for the client.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: IAM database authentication is documented for MariaDB/MySQL/PostgreSQL, with 15-minute authentication tokens; token expiry does not terminate an established session. Database grants still apply.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: Native managed relational engines: Db2, MariaDB, Microsoft SQL Server, MySQL, Oracle and PostgreSQL, using each engine's SQL dialect. Ordinary RDS restricts system procedures/host access.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: Current PostgreSQL release notes list18.6 as available and 19 RC1/betas in the Preview environment. MySQL version guide lists8.4/8.0 and separate26.7/9.x previews. Select a currently available engine/version in the chosen Region.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: MariaDB version guide includes 11.8/11.4 and older supported branches, with 12.3.1 Preview separate. Oracle chapter lists26ai, 21c, 19c; Db2 lists11.5.9/12.1.4 for Standard/Advanced and 12.1.4 Community. SQL Server's chapter lists2016, 2017, 2019, 2022 and 2025 with edition/version conditions.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: Engine major/minor support dates and Extended Support can change the bill; upgrades/patches are managed through RDS maintenance/version controls. SQL Server Developer/Web and Oracle/Db2 licensing conditions still apply to the selected version.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: PostgreSQL transactions group SQL statements into committed/rolled-back units; default isolation is READ COMMITTED. Native transaction settings are configurable; no atomicity across unrelated RDS instances or AWS services is claimed.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: Multi-AZ DB instance uses synchronous standby replication; Multi-AZ DB cluster uses semisynchronous replication to two readers, requiring acknowledgement from at least one before commit, not execution/commit on every reader.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: Ordinary read replicas use asynchronous replication and can lag. A single cross-engine consistency/isolation guarantee beyond each engine's documented transaction behavior was not established.

facts.label: Test environments and branches
facts.value: Snapshot/PITR restores create separate instances/environments and add charges. Blue/Green Deployments provide synchronized staging for MariaDB/MySQL/PostgreSQL, then controlled switchover.

facts.label: Test environments and branches
facts.value: A standard-RDS six-engine shared-storage copy-on-write branch allowance/count/lifetime was not found.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Multi-AZ DB instance: one synchronous standby in another AZ, automatic failover; standby does not serve reads. Multi-AZ DB cluster: writer plus two readable failover targets across three AZs.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Read replicas are separately billed instances/storage; support and promotion rules vary by engine. Cross-Region replicas incur transfer; a read replica is not automatically the synchronous Multi-AZ standby.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: RDS PostgreSQL logical replication publishes table changes via WAL/replication slots; the guide documents pgoutput and wal2json. Setup and retained logs consume resources.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Native offline client caching, queued offline writes and conflict-resolution guarantees were not found for the standard RDS service.

facts.label: Extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: RDS PostgreSQL supports approved PostGIS, pg_partman, pg_cron, pg_tle and other extensions. Trusted extension installation for PG13+ can use database CREATE rights; rds.allowed_extensions can restrict installation.

facts.label: Upload and file limits
facts.value: Not applicable to standard RDS as an independent app-file store.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Not applicable to standard RDS as an independent app-file store.

facts.label: Delivery and private files
facts.value: Not applicable to standard RDS as an independent app-file store.

facts.label: Filters and mixed search
facts.value: PostgreSQL vector distance operations can be combined with ordinary SQL data/filters. HNSW is documented; search/index choices and recall depend on schema, extension version and query.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: PostgreSQL pg_cron runs scheduled SQL inside the DB instance. SQL Server Agent runs T-SQL administrative jobs on documented Enterprise/Standard/Web editions. Oracle has DBMS_SCHEDULER administrative procedures.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: SQL Server maintenance/backup processes can interrupt or cancel Agent jobs. Multi-AZ Agent job replication is opt-in and restricted to documented T-SQL job categories/steps.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: One RDS-wide exactly-once, automatic failed-job retry, deduplication or dead-letter/replay guarantee was not established.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: pg_cron stores recurring cron schedules and SQL commands; unschedule removes a definition. SQL Server Agent supports scheduled/event/on-demand jobs; Oracle documents changing scheduler time zone and repeat interval.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Universal delayed-message payload/queue TTL and guaranteed catch-up behavior after a stopped database resumes were not established.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: pg_cron records status/message/start/end in cron.job_run_details; customers must purge it. Its seven-day cleanup is an example, not fixed service retention. SQL Server Agent history can be viewed in SSMS.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: RDS PostgreSQL local logs default 3 days/4320 minutes; configurable1–7 days/1440–10080 minutes. CloudWatch publishing provides a separate retention/billing path.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: RDS Custom grants host control but adds customer responsibilities: Oracle OS patching/customer media and shared database upkeep; SQL Server CEV versus RDS-provided engine versions split patch/install responsibility. Unsupported customization can breach the support perimeter.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: RDS endpoint table lists 36 Region IDs: us-east-2, us-east-1, us-west-1, us-west-2, af-south-1, ap-east-1, ap-south-2, ap-southeast-3, ap-southeast-5, ap-southeast-4, ap-south-1, ap-southeast-6, ap-northeast-3, ap-northeast-2, ap-southeast-1, ap-southeast-2, ap-east-2, ap-southeast-7, ap-northeast-1, ca-central-1, ca-west-1, eu-central-1, eu-west-1, eu-west-2, eu-south-1, eu-west-3, eu-south-2, eu-north-1, eu-central-2, il-central-1, mx-central-1, me-south-1, me-central-1, sa-east-1, us-gov-east-1, us-gov-west-1. Engine/version/class availability varies.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Resources/data are not copied across Regions unless configured. Multi-AZ uses separate AZs within one Region; cross-Region backups/replicas are separate configuration and cost choices.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: DPA §12.1 allows choosing processing Regions and limits transfers outside them to customer-initiated services or legal/binding government orders.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: PostgreSQL logical dump/restore uses pg_dump and pg_restore/psql; SQL Server supports native .bak backup/restore through S3 with edition/size restrictions. Other engines have their own migration tools and grants.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Snapshot export writes Parquet to S3 for analysis; the guide explicitly says the exported files cannot directly restore a new RDS instance or import into an existing one.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: PostgreSQL snapshot-export example says $0.013/GB of source snapshot; the N. Virginia catalog says USD $0.010/GB. Selecting only part of a snapshot does not reduce the example's source-size billing basis.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Deleting an instance can retain a final/manual snapshot and selected automated backups; those remain separate billable resources. Final snapshot preserves restore data; deleting the instance does not delete every manual copy.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Customer Agreement §5.3 provides a qualified30-day post-termination retrieval period. DPA §14 gives service-control return/deletion terms through90 days, subject to the agreement.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Exact physical-erasure deadlines for every database volume, retained snapshot/backup and account record were not established.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: MySQL can export to an external same-or-newer MySQL server using mysqldump plus temporary replication, then stop replication after cutover.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Oracle Data Pump supports moving RDS Oracle data to another Oracle database using dump files or a database link. Db2 documents transferring files between the DB instance and a same-Region S3 bucket through stored procedures/IAM.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: DB-instance automated-backup retention0–35 days, where0 disables it. Defaults: API/CLI1 day if unspecified; console7 days. Multi-AZ DB clusters require1–35 days. Changing instance retention between0 and nonzero causes an outage.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Automatic snapshots cover the entire instance/all supported storage volumes; first is full and later snapshots incremental. Backups are stored in S3; PITR creates a new instance within the selected recovery window.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Free backup allowance equals100% of regional account provisioned database storage. Excess MySQL/PostgreSQL backup storage in N.Virginia is USD$0.095/GB-month; retained orphan snapshots remain billable.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: No new automated backups while stopped; RDS excludes stopped time when computing retention, so backups can persist longer than the nominal retention period. Manual/final snapshots survive instance deletion until removed.

facts.label: File recovery and protection
facts.value: Not applicable to standard RDS as an independent app-file store.

facts.label: Identity and old names
facts.value: Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS), from Amazon Web Services (AWS). This record covers Db2, MariaDB, Microsoft SQL Server, MySQL, Oracle and PostgreSQL; Aurora has a separate research record.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Ordinary RDS is an AWS-hosted commercial service; AWS manages infrastructure and engine operations, with restricted administrative privileges and no host shell access.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Oracle: License Included only for Standard Edition 2; BYOL for Enterprise Edition and Standard Edition 2, with appropriate Oracle licenses/support and separately licensed features.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: SQL Server: License Included for Enterprise, Standard, Web and Express. BYOM uses existing licenses with active Software Assurance/License Mobility; Enterprise, Standard and Developer are documented. Developer is non-production only.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Db2: BYOL or hourly IBM licenses through AWS Marketplace for Standard/Advanced. Community Edition has no IBM license fee but still requires IBM Customer/Site IDs and paid RDS infrastructure.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: RDS Custom supports Oracle and SQL Server, granting database/OS administration under a shared-responsibility model. Oracle Custom uses customer media/licenses; SQL Server Custom supports LI/BYOM.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage

facts.value: Primary type: hosted vector storage and approximate similarity search. Secondary role: a vector-storage layer for Bedrock Knowledge Bases and OpenSearch integrations. These are our directory labels.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: Native service stores keyed float32 vectors with optional metadata, maintains vector indexes and performs ANN similarity queries. IAM policies, encryption and vector APIs are part of the service.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: Bedrock Knowledge Bases can fetch/chunk source content, generate embeddings and write vectors; OpenSearch adds search/analytics capabilities. Those are integrations with separate service resources and charges.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Uses a dedicated HTTPS API, AWS Signature Version 4 credentials, AWS CLI s3vectors commands and AWS SDK clients; regional endpoints support IPv4/IPv6.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Native operations include PutVectors, GetVectors, ListVectors, QueryVectors, DeleteVectors and bucket/index management. Query responses normally return keys, optionally distances/metadata; GetVectors can retrieve actual vectors.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Every request needs AWS credentials and authorization. IAM/resource policies can scope access to vector buckets, indexes and operations using the s3vectors namespace; all Block Public Access settings remain enabled and cannot be disabled.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Querying with metadata filters or requesting metadata needs GetVectors as well as QueryVectors permission; keys/distances alone have a narrower permission requirement.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Data is encrypted at rest with SSE-S3 by default; customer-managed KMS is optional. An index can have a different encryption configuration from its bucket; bucket encryption choice is fixed at bucket creation.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: PrivateLink interface endpoints provide private access, endpoint policies and regional/zonal DNS. Regional endpoints support HTTPS/SigV4 and IPv4/IPv6.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: Managed dense float32 vector index with keyed retrieval and approximate nearest-neighbor search, using cosine or Euclidean distance. It does not expose a general SQL/document query engine through these native operations.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Writes are strongly consistent, so newly written/updated/deleted vectors are immediately reflected in supported access/query behavior. ListVectors is explicitly described as strongly consistent in the native FAQ.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: A native multi-vector/multi-index ACID transaction, compare-and-swap revision condition or rollback guarantee was not found in the inspected write/delete/query APIs and legal materials.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Separate vector indexes/buckets can isolate test data, but each retained copy incurs its own applicable storage and operations. Core index dimensions, metric and non-filterable keys cannot be edited after creation.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Native copy-on-write development branching, preview-environment quotas and automatic branch expiry were not found.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: AWS manages durable storage; native security docs describe 11-nines durability. No customer-provisioned vector read-replica count or selectable failover topology is documented in this offer.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: S3 Vectors-specific cross-region replication setup, replica pricing and customer-visible recovery-time guarantees were not established.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: A native client changefeed, S3-object event notification mapping, durable offline-write SDK and automatic offline conflict-resolution behavior were not found for vector buckets.

facts.label: extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: The specialized native index is managed vector ANN with metadata filtering. Advanced full-text/hybrid queries and aggregations are documented through OpenSearch integration rather than as native vector-bucket query operators.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: Multipart/resumable user-file uploads are outside the native vector interface. Its vector-batch/body/metadata limits are recorded under D03/V01.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Vector buckets use s3vectors APIs and ARNs instead of S3 object APIs. General-purpose S3-compatible upload clients do not automatically support PutVectors/QueryVectors.

facts.label: delivery and private files
facts.value: Public file hosting, website buckets, CDN delivery and signed file-download products are outside this private vector-store interface.

facts.label: filters and mixed search
facts.value: Native metadata supports strings, numbers, booleans and lists with equality, range, membership and logical conditions. ENHANCED mode additionally supports $startsWith and evaluates filters before vector search.

facts.label: filters and mixed search
facts.value: Buckets created on/after 2026-09-30 default to ENHANCED and cannot use CLASSIC. Earlier buckets default to CLASSIC even for later new indexes until their default is changed; existing indexes can update mode in place.

facts.label: filters and mixed search
facts.value: ENHANCED allows up to 100 filter constraints/query, counted by evaluated values. CLASSIC can return fewer than topK for selective filters; ANN results remain approximate in either mode.

facts.label: filters and mixed search
facts.value: Native full-text keyword scoring/fusion and document reranking are not established by QueryVectors. OpenSearch integration supplies richer search, while a one-time export creates a separate OpenSearch collection that remains active.

facts.label: execution model and languages
facts.value: General-purpose application worker execution and queue delivery are outside this native vector-store product; optional model/ingestion pipelines run in other services.

facts.label: delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Queue delivery, task acknowledgment and exactly-once worker execution do not describe the native vector data API. API retry/throttling behavior is recorded under C16.

facts.label: schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Managed cron, delayed jobs and retained queue-message days are outside the vector-store scope.

facts.label: logs and run history
facts.value: Per-job execution history/replay retention is outside scope. CloudTrail API audit events are separate from application worker logs.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps

facts.value: Default max_document_size is 8,000,000 bytes measured from the serialized Erlang document-body representation, excluding attachments; oversized creates/updates return 413.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Default max_http_request_size is 4,294,967,296 bytes (4 GiB, with 1 GiB = 1,073,741,824 bytes). It applies to the whole request body, including bulk/multipart operations. Default max_dbs_open is 100 simultaneously open databases.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Usable capacity and client concurrency depend on the operator's hardware, Erlang/HTTP settings, open-file limits, data size and indexes. The performance guide covers OS file-descriptor tuning; no universal plan-style connection or stored-GB quota applies.

facts.label: storage prices
facts.value: Not applicable: no vendor-hosted per-GB, per-operation, minimum-retention or early-deletion storage tariff for self-hosted CouchDB attachments.

facts.label: file request and retrieval prices
facts.value: Not applicable: no vendor-hosted per-GB, per-operation, minimum-retention or early-deletion storage tariff for self-hosted CouchDB attachments.

facts.label: minimum storage and early deletion
facts.value: Not applicable: no vendor-hosted per-GB, per-operation, minimum-retention or early-deletion storage tariff for self-hosted CouchDB attachments.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: Not applicable to a native vector module: the inspected 3.5.3 query/search catalog covers Mango, MapReduce and optional Lucene text search, with no documented vector-index/model service.

facts.label: embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: Not applicable to a native vector module: the inspected 3.5.3 query/search catalog covers Mango, MapReduce and optional Lucene text search, with no documented vector-index/model service.

facts.label: run limits and pricing
facts.value: Not applicable to a managed app-job/worker service. CouchDB design functions execute database queries/validation/updates; _changes can notify an external application, but worker runtime and workflow policies belong to that application.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Hosted-account signup/card/country eligibility is not applicable. The software license grants worldwide, royalty-free use, including use in commercial software subject to its conditions; deployment requires the operator to create a server administrator.

facts.label: primary type and other roles
facts.value: Researcher classification: self-hosted JSON document database with clustering, HTTP replication, offline-client integration and document attachments.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: Core services include JSON documents, binary attachments, HTTP CRUD/query APIs, database users/roles, Mango selectors, JavaScript MapReduce/design functions and replication. Fauxton provides web administration.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: HTTP/JSON REST APIs support arbitrary HTTP-capable languages/clients. Binary attachments have GET/HEAD/PUT/DELETE endpoints. PouchDB is an ecosystem client for browser/mobile local storage and replication.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: CouchDB 3.x requires a server administrator to start. Newly created databases default to admin_only security; database members can read all documents and write ordinary documents in that database.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Database read authorization is scoped by _security names/roles. A permitted member's access includes all documents; filtered replication or a changes filter is not per-document read authorization.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Basic and cookie authentication are documented; proxy/JWT handlers are configurable. The shipped configuration includes SSL settings for operator-supplied TLS certificates.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: JSON documents with _id/_rev metadata; Mango JSON selectors and indexes, plus JavaScript MapReduce views. Binary attachments belong to documents.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Single-document updates are atomic and use optimistic revision checks/MVCC. Concurrent edits can return 409 conflict; reads use a consistent snapshot for that read operation.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: _bulk_docs operations are explicitly non-atomic: some documents can succeed and others fail. Replication is eventually consistent; conflicting branches have a deterministic winning revision, while applications may need to merge the other leaves.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Create independent development databases/instances through replication or restore; these copies consume your storage/compute. No copy-on-write database branching or automatic test-to-production data merge was established.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Default cluster configuration q=2 and n=3 means 2 shards with 3 replicas each: 6 shard-replica files. The setup wizard uses n=1 for standalone, n=2 for two nodes and n=3 for larger clusters.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: At least 3 nodes is strongly recommended for a cluster. Read/write acknowledgement quorums are configurable; the theory guide distinguishes 201 writes meeting the required acknowledgements from 202 when fewer nodes respond.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: _changes supports normal polling, longpoll, continuous and EventSource feeds. Only the latest change for a given document is guaranteed; intermediate document states may be absent.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Replication is one-way push or pull and can run once or continuously; two-way sync uses replication in both directions. CouchDB's project site identifies PouchDB as a browser/mobile companion for offline-first applications.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Replicated conflicts preserve competing revisions and select one deterministic visible winner; retrieving/merging conflicting leaves remains an application responsibility.

facts.label: extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Mango JSON indexes and MapReduce views are native. Nouveau adds Lucene full-text search through a separately running server, is experimental, and can change endpoints/invalidate indexes in future releases.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: Release default.ini lists max_attachment_size=1,073,741,824 bytes (1 GiB). The document-body limit excludes attachments; the separate whole-HTTP-request default is 4,294,967,296 bytes.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: Attachments upload via PUT /{db}/{docid}/{attname} and download as raw content with its stored Content-Type. Updating an existing document requires the revision token or If-Match.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Native attachment access is CouchDB HTTP/REST (GET/HEAD/PUT/DELETE) under document URLs, with ETags and revision arguments.

facts.label: delivery and private files
facts.value: Attachment retrieval requires the database's read permission and returns the attachment's media type. Database membership/security protects the containing documents and attachments.

facts.label: filters and mixed search
facts.value: Not applicable to a native vector module: the inspected 3.5.3 query/search catalog covers Mango, MapReduce and optional Lucene text search, with no documented vector-index/model service.

facts.label: execution model and languages
facts.value: Not applicable to a managed app-job/worker service. CouchDB design functions execute database queries/validation/updates; _changes can notify an external application, but worker runtime and workflow policies belong to that application.

facts.label: delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Not applicable to a managed app-job/worker service. CouchDB design functions execute database queries/validation/updates; _changes can notify an external application, but worker runtime and workflow policies belong to that application.

facts.label: schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Not applicable to a managed app-job/worker service. CouchDB design functions execute database queries/validation/updates; _changes can notify an external application, but worker runtime and workflow policies belong to that application.

facts.label: logs and run history
facts.value: Not applicable to a managed app-job/worker service. CouchDB design functions execute database queries/validation/updates; _changes can notify an external application, but worker runtime and workflow policies belong to that application.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Operate one node or your own cluster: install supported packages/source, configure administrator credentials, storage, network/TLS and replication, then maintain upgrades, backups, compaction and monitoring.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Runtime docs disagree: 3.5.3 release notes require Erlang/OTP 27 minimum, but the tagged Unix build-dependency list still includes OTP 26, 27 and 28.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Optional Nouveau Java requirements also disagree: its dedicated installation guide requires Java 21 or newer, while the generic Unix dependency list says minimum 11 and recommends 19/20.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: No universal minimum production CPU/RAM/disk size was found in the inspected installation, performance, clustering and license pages.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: The operator chooses node, replica, backup and client locations. Replication can copy databases between installations over HTTP; no Apache-operated region catalog applies.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Data can be copied through CouchDB replication and retrieved through HTTP document/attachment APIs. Official backup guidance also supports copying .couch database/index files plus configuration and logs as appropriate.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Document deletion, purge and compaction have different effects. Compaction removes obsolete content while retaining revision metadata; enable_database_recovery=false is the documented default, while enabling it renames deleted database files for manual recovery/removal.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: The operator arranges backup/retention. Official methods include replication to another installation, copying .couch database/index files and storage snapshots; configuration and relevant logs need separate coverage.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Old document revisions are not a durable historical backup: compaction removes obsolete bodies and retains small revision metadata. Compaction recreates files and can require roughly twice the relevant disk space while running.

facts.label: file recovery and protection
facts.value: Attachments follow document revisions and can be replicated/backed up with database data. A rev query can retrieve an available revision's attachment, but revision history is not an indefinite archive and compaction can remove obsolete content.

facts.label: identity and old names
facts.value: Apache CouchDB, an Apache Software Foundation project. The researched release is 3.5.3.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: Self-hosted open-source software under Apache License 2.0. The 3.5.3 distribution LICENSE also lists bundled third-party components and their notices/licenses.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Active release: the official site lists 3.5.3 dated 2026-10-12, and current 3.5.3 release notes are available. No project shutdown, sunset or acquisition notice was found in the bounded official search.

facts.label: vendor home and main markets
facts.value: The Apache Software Foundation is a US 501(c)(3) charitable organization; its Privacy Policy gives a Wilmington, Delaware, US contact address.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: Community support includes user mailing lists, GitHub issues, IRC and Slack. Apache License 2.0 supplies the software as-is without a hosted uptime commitment; a chosen commercial support/hosting contract is separate.

apps.name: Appwrite
apps.line: Backend platform with databases, login, file storage and functions.

cells.metered: $25/month Pro; usage and native SQL can add charges
cells.regions: 6 available Cloud regions

The $25 base plan still applies to an idle project, because hosting is not billed down to zero.
