status.label: Security incident
status.text: 2026-11-01 runtime incident; one customer's code and logs accessed; wider secret access unconfirmed

facts.label: Recurring Free offer
facts.value: Hosted Free is recurring, with one Free organization per account and two projects. Free allocations are shared across the two projects.

facts.label: Special programs
facts.value: OSS program offers eligible projects Pro benefits subject to review, with annual reassessment. Education has two projects and prohibits commercial use.

facts.label: Free included resources
facts.value: Free: 5GB bandwidth, 2GB storage, 750K executions and 75K MAU.

facts.label: Free object-count conflict
facts.value: Pricing capture: one database, one bucket and two functions per project. Free downgrade documentation: one database, three buckets and five functions.

facts.label: Pro included resources
facts.value: Pro: 2TB bandwidth, 150GB storage, 3.5M executions and 200K MAU per project.

facts.label: Start included resources
facts.value: Start announcement: per project 80GB bandwidth, 40GB storage, 1.5M executions, 100K MAU; ten databases, ten buckets, ten functions and 25-minute builds.

facts.label: Database read/write allowance — Free
facts.value: 500,000 reads and 250,000 writes per month; excess is throttled rather than purchased automatically.

facts.label: Database read/write allowance — Pro/Scale
facts.value: 1.75M reads and 750K writes per month; excess $0.060 per 100K reads and $0.10 per 100K writes.

facts.label: Free inactivity pause
facts.value: Seven consecutive days without development activity in the Console causes a pause. API access and scheduled/background work stop; Console resume is documented.

facts.label: Free deletion and paid inactivity
facts.value: Paused Free projects are deleted after 90 days, with email warning; resume or upgrade before deletion. Pro and Enterprise do not pause/delete for inactivity.

facts.label: Pro minimum commitment
facts.value: Pro from $25/month including one project; additional projects $15/month.

facts.label: Start minimum commitment
facts.value: Start from $10/month in eligible markets; announcement says checkout may use local currency.

facts.label: Billing period and tax
facts.value: Billing docs define a 30-day period beginning when the plan changes; recurring projects/add-ons billed in advance and usage afterward. Tax ID is supported; tax-inclusive/exclusive treatment not stated.

facts.label: Refund conditions
facts.value: Non-refundable by default. First-time Cloud dissatisfaction requests within 14 days are discretionary and require no significant usage; general requests later than 30 days excluded.

facts.label: Serverless versus dedicated database billing
facts.value: Serverless TablesDB has $0 fixed compute plus project storage and read/write meters. Dedicated database reads/writes are included in the tier; compute starts at $10/month.

facts.label: Native PostgreSQL Starter
facts.value: Starter: one core, 1GB RAM, 10GB storage, 50GB bandwidth, 100 connections, $10/month; compute prorated by hour. Storage excess $0.125/GB/month; bandwidth excess $0.08/GB/month.

facts.label: Dedicated replicas, PITR and credits
facts.value: Each HA replica costs 100% of its compute tier; PITR adds 20% of the base. Pricing advertises $10 monthly database compute credits. Credit eligibility, allocation across projects and applicable add-ons remain unclear.

facts.label: Platform excess rates
facts.value: Effective pricing notice: bandwidth $15/100GB and storage $2.8/100GB.

facts.label: Function compute rate conflict
facts.value: Compute billing docs say excess $0.09/GB-hour; effective pricing notice and indexed comparison say $0.06/GB-hour.

facts.label: Function compute counting conflict
facts.value: Docs describe memory GB × active hours, but the specification table lists 0.25 hourly usage for 512MB/0.5CPU and 4 for 2GB/2CPU. Build and execution use the same compute pool.

facts.label: Compute allowances and rounding
facts.value: Free includes 100GB-hours; Pro 1,000GB-hours. Minimum billed execution time and partial-second rounding were not found.

facts.label: Execution and Sites meters
facts.value: Pricing capture lists $2 per million extra executions. Sites shares platform storage, bandwidth, compute and execution meters.

facts.label: Native PostgreSQL scale to zero
facts.value: Whole-database idle timeout defaults to 15 minutes and is configurable from 5 to 60 minutes without connections. Manual pause retains storage/configuration and stops compute.

facts.label: Idle charges and wake uncertainty
facts.value: Scale-to-zero does not remove the Cloud subscription or retained storage. Exact native-database paused billing, automatic wake trigger/latency and function cold-start billing were not fully established.

facts.label: Platform transfer scope
facts.value: Free/Pro bandwidth allowances and platform excess price are published. S3 inbound and outbound traffic both count toward project network usage.

facts.label: Unresolved transfer routes
facts.value: Separate free ingress, same-region/internal traffic exemption, cache-hit discount, and backup/export transfer pricing were not found as a complete matrix.

facts.label: Spend-cap scope
facts.value: Organization budget cap is set in USD and covers automatic add-ons, excluding the recurring plan cost. Default alert at 75%, with up to three alert checkpoints.

facts.label: Limit enforcement
facts.value: Pro buys resources until cap. At cap: API bandwidth denied, new users/invites blocked, function execution and Realtime subscriptions disabled; file uploads stop until storage falls below limit. Free cannot buy overages.

facts.label: Embeddings cap exception conflict
facts.value: Embedding docs say tokens count toward the budget cap but paid embedding creation is never hard-blocked. General cap docs describe stopping automatic scaling at the cap.

facts.label: Fair-use controls
facts.value: Cloud fair-use policy allows throttling or suspension for misuse/excessive resource use. Numeric allowances do not override abuse rules.

facts.label: TablesDB operation limits
facts.value: Transaction operations: Free 100, Pro 1,000, Scale 2,500. Bulk create/update/upsert/delete: Free 100 rows and Pro 1,000 rows per request.

facts.label: TablesDB type/query capacity
facts.value: List queries default to 25 results. Text-type maximum lengths differ: varchar/text 16,383 characters; mediumtext 4,194,303; longtext 1,073,741,823. Aggregate row/request byte ceiling not established.

facts.label: Native PostgreSQL pool and limits
facts.value: Pooler port 6432; transaction mode default, session mode unavailable with HA. Pool size 1–1,000 per user; pooler maxConnections does not cap all incoming clients.

facts.label: PostgreSQL idle transaction limit
facts.value: Idle inside an open transaction: 900 seconds default, configurable 60–86,400 seconds. Idle between ordinary queries is not affected by this setting.

facts.label: File storage price and allocation
facts.value: Platform storage excess $2.8/100GB; stored files share the plan storage allowance rather than a separate hot/archive price table.

facts.label: File request/retrieval rates
facts.value: Upload, list, download and multipart operations are documented; a distinct per-request or retrieval price was not found.

facts.label: Image transformation meter
facts.value: Billed by unique origin images, not each transformed variant; unlimited variants per counted origin. Pricing capture: Pro 100 origins/month, excess $5/1,000 origins.

facts.label: Minimum object billing/early delete
facts.value: Minimum billable object size, minimum storage duration and early-delete penalty not found in inspected official storage and billing pages.

facts.label: VectorsDB dimensions and record model
facts.value: Collection dimension 1–16,000, fixed after creation; required embedding array and optional JSON metadata. HNSW index supports cosine, dot-product and Euclidean distance.

facts.label: Vector capacity unknowns
facts.value: Total indexed vector count, per-record metadata bytes, billed HNSW overhead and performance-based capacity for the directory workload were not found.

facts.label: Built-in embeddings
facts.value: nomic-embed-text: 768 dimensions, $0.10/million tokens; all-minilm: 384 dimensions, $0.05/million. Free 1M tokens/model/month, Pro 10M, Scale 100M; paid excess rounded up per started million.

facts.label: External embedding path
facts.value: Precomputed vectors can be submitted to VectorsDB; the caller must supply a compatible dimension. External model charges and model-specific data processing are outside the published built-in rates.

facts.label: Function specifications/timeouts
facts.value: Default Free specification 512MB/0.5CPU; Pro can choose larger build/runtime specifications separately. Global execution maximum 900 seconds; synchronous calls hard-timeout at 30 seconds.

facts.label: Build limits and concurrency gap
facts.value: Build timeout Free 15 minutes, Pro/Scale 45 minutes, Enterprise custom. Cloud simultaneous execution ceiling, queued waiting charge and retry billing were not established.

facts.label: Free signup card requirement
facts.value: Whether a payment card is required to create a normal Free account was not established from current production pages.

facts.label: Paid payment and eligibility
facts.value: Native databases require a paid plan and attached payment method. Start eligibility depends on selected markets and a card issued in an eligible country; the full country list is not published in the inspected announcement.

facts.label: Commercial use and age restrictions
facts.value: No explicit ordinary Free commercial-use ban found. Education explicitly excludes commercial use; Privacy says users under 18 need parent/guardian involvement. No complete general country-eligibility list found.

facts.label: Payment-method conflict
facts.value: Current Pricing/Manage billing say credit/debit cards; Terms explicitly include PayPal as a valid subscription payment method.

facts.label: Primary type and overlaps
facts.value: Researcher classification: backend platform. Secondary roles: relational/document/vector databases, authentication, files, managed functions, Realtime, Messaging and frontend hosting.

facts.label: Native services
facts.value: Auth, Databases, Storage, Functions, Realtime, Messaging, Sites and Avatars have official platform documentation.

facts.label: APIs and official SDKs
facts.value: REST, GraphQL and WebSocket interfaces. Client SDKs include Web, Flutter, Apple, Android, React Native and Unity beta; server SDKs include Node.js, Python, Dart, PHP, Ruby, .NET, Go, Swift, Kotlin and Rust.

facts.label: Native SQL and object protocols
facts.value: Managed PostgreSQL uses port 5432; MySQL uses 3306 and standard engine drivers. Storage exposes a separate path-style S3-compatible interface.

facts.label: TablesDB access defaults
facts.value: No end-user access by default. Either a table grant or a row grant suffices; row permissions apply only when Row Security is enabled.

facts.label: Storage access defaults
facts.value: Buckets grant no access by default. Bucket or file grants can authorize access; per-file rules require File Security enabled.

facts.label: Native PostgreSQL network controls
facts.value: Public stable hostname; TLS terminates at Appwrite edge. Empty IP allowlist permits any address with credentials; up to 100 IPv4/IPv6/CIDR entries apply to direct, pooler and SQL API access.

facts.label: Encryption scope
facts.value: Optional AES-128-GCM storage encryption applies to files smaller than 20MB. Pro+ text-column encryption is available; encrypted columns cannot be queried.

facts.label: Function authorization and secrets
facts.value: Functions have execute roles and per-execution scoped API keys. Domain HTTP calls are guest requests; docs require application JWT handling when authentication is needed.

facts.label: TablesDB query model
facts.value: Typed relational tables exposed through Appwrite JSON APIs and Query operators; SQL under the hood is not a public arbitrary-SQL promise.

facts.label: DocumentsDB model
facts.value: Schemaless JSON-style documents organized in databases and collections, with filtering, sorting and pagination.

facts.label: Native PostgreSQL versions
facts.value: PostgreSQL 18 by default; PostgreSQL 17 selectable at creation; engine-native SQL, ORM and migrations.

facts.label: Native MySQL versions
facts.value: MySQL 8.4 default; 8.0 selectable at creation, with native SQL drivers and a dedicated database hostname.

facts.label: Shared database eligibility conflict
facts.value: Database overview describes TablesDB, DocumentsDB and VectorsDB on shared or dedicated infrastructure; direct Pricing lists only TablesDB under serverless and the other types under dedicated.

facts.label: TablesDB transactions
facts.value: Staged operations commit in order inside a database transaction, see earlier staged writes, and conflict if an affected row changed outside the transaction. Cross-table/database scope; schema changes excluded.

facts.label: DocumentsDB transactions
facts.value: Stage document/bulk/atomic-number operations and commit atomically across databases/collections; changes outside the transaction can cause a conflict. Index/schema changes excluded.

facts.label: Native PostgreSQL isolation
facts.value: Native BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK and savepoints; default Read Committed; Repeatable Read and Serializable available. Serialization errors require application retry.

facts.label: Native MySQL isolation
facts.value: InnoDB default Repeatable Read; Read Committed, Serializable and Read Uncommitted available. A failed statement need not abort the transaction; DDL can commit implicitly.

facts.label: Cloud project environments
facts.value: SDKs document selecting an environment within the same project ID, with separate resources, users and API keys. Current per-plan environment count and charge not established.

facts.label: PostgreSQL branches
facts.value: Snapshot copy with separate endpoint; parent credentials reused, no merge-back or pooler. TTL default 24h, range 300–604,800 seconds. Fixed lightweight compute; full parent provisioned storage billed for branch lifetime.

facts.label: PostgreSQL HA/failover
facts.value: Up to five same-region full replicas; automatic promotion and stable-host repointing. Default async can lose recent writes. Sync/quorum wait for flush, not necessarily read replay; unavailable replicas can reduce required acknowledgements.

facts.label: MySQL HA/failover
facts.value: Up to five replicas, same region/specification as primary, separately billed. Async default; sync/quorum options; automatic least-lag promotion with client reconnect to unchanged hostname.

facts.label: Realtime versus offline
facts.value: Appwrite Realtime delivers platform events. TablesDB offline guide requires local storage/RxDB, push/pull synchronization and a chosen conflict strategy.

facts.label: TablesDB indexes
facts.value: Key, unique and fulltext indexes; fulltext required for the search query method. Query performance depends on appropriate single/composite indexes.

facts.label: PostgreSQL extensions
facts.value: Managed catalog includes PostGIS, pgvector and pg_trgm; no extra extension fee. Platform cap 50 installed extensions; arbitrary package installation is not promised.

facts.label: Cloud maximum file sizes
facts.value: Pricing capture lists Free 50MB and Pro 5GB maximum files. Bucket settings can impose a smaller size or an extension allowlist of at most 100 entries.

facts.label: Upload chunks and rate limits
facts.value: Create-file API uses chunks up to 5MB with Content-Range and x-appwrite-id on subsequent requests; SDK handles chunking. Client endpoint rate limit 60 requests/minute/IP; server API-key calls exempt from this endpoint limit.

facts.label: Self-host file size
facts.value: Self-host storage maximum defaults to 30MB and is configurable. Adapters include local, AWS S3, DigitalOcean Spaces, Backblaze, Akamai and Wasabi.

facts.label: Supported S3 surface
facts.value: SigV4, path-style addressing; bucket/list/object read-write-copy-delete and multipart operations, including ranges and metadata. Multipart parts must be contiguous from 1; abandoned uploads cleaned after 24 hours.

facts.label: S3 incompatibilities
facts.value: No gateway support for object versioning, Object Lock, lifecycle, tags, bucket policies/CORS configuration, notifications or restores; unsupported operations return 501. ACL private is accepted but ignored; SSE headers ignored.

facts.label: Private links and presigning
facts.value: Native file tokens authorize holders without normal user permissions and may have expiry or no expiry. S3 presigned URLs expire within seven days.

facts.label: CDN and custom endpoint
facts.value: Cloud CDN is available to all projects. Custom domains can front the Appwrite API, including file endpoints, with DNS verification and TLS certificate generation.

facts.label: Vector filtering and search
facts.value: Metadata comparison/string/logical queries can combine with vector nearest-neighbor search. One vector query per request; large inputs can use POST createQuery. Dropped vector index falls back to scanning.

facts.label: Hybrid keyword/vector fusion
facts.value: A native keyword-plus-vector fusion method and ranking contract were not established in the inspected guides.

facts.label: Cloud function runtime selection
facts.value: Cloud list includes Node.js 22/25, Bun 1.3, Deno 2.6, Go 1.26, Python 3.14, Dart 3.11, PHP 8.4, Ruby 4.0 and Rust 1.83, among older supported versions.

facts.label: Async queue and retry contract
facts.value: Asynchronous function executions are queued. Retry defaults/backoff, delivery duplicates/order, dead-letter queue, idempotency and failed-job replay guarantees were not found.

facts.label: Schedules and delayed execution
facts.value: UTC cron, interval and one-off delayed async executions. Intervals minimum one minute, except Free/Education 60 minutes. Free/Education cron can run up to five minutes late.

facts.label: Queue retention and payload ceiling
facts.value: Maximum queued lifetime, maximum delayed horizon, queue TTL and a general execution-payload byte ceiling were not established.

facts.label: Execution log data
facts.value: Execution records have IDs/states and configurable logs. Request/response bodies are not automatically logged; response bodies/headers only return synchronously.

facts.label: Log retention conflict
facts.value: Function execution docs: Free 24 hours and Pro seven days. Indexed pricing says Free logs one hour; scope or freshness difference unresolved.

facts.label: History export/replay
facts.value: Execution listing/inspection exists, but a complete log-export or failed-run replay feature/retention contract was not found.

facts.label: Self-host minimum and operations
facts.value: Installation minimum two CPU cores, 4GB RAM, 2GB swap, Docker and Compose v2. Operator owns capacity, TLS, delivery integrations, backups and updates.

facts.label: Self-host database selection
facts.value: Installer 2.7.0 offers PostgreSQL default, MariaDB and MongoDB; selection cannot be changed after installation and Appwrite API stays the same.

facts.label: Self-host backup and upgrade work
facts.value: Back up database, storage volumes, configuration and encryption secrets; perform upgrades/migrations according to supported version paths. Managed Cloud backup automation is not supplied merely by installing Docker.

facts.label: Self-host versus Cloud limits
facts.value: Self-host function idle-container cleanup and worker settings are configurable; default build/execution timeout 900 seconds. Cloud CDN, managed native SQL operations and billing quotas cannot be assumed to apply.

facts.label: Core regions
facts.value: Available: Frankfurt fra, New York nyc, Sydney syd, San Francisco sfo, Singapore sgp, Toronto tor. Bangalore, Amsterdam and London are coming-soon entries.

facts.label: Native SQL placement and residency gaps
facts.value: Native PostgreSQL resides in its project region and says data does not leave that region. Core backup docs say remote/off-instance storage, without a complete backup/worker residency matrix or cross-region migration rule.

facts.label: TablesDB export
facts.value: CSV export supports selected columns/filters. Relationships export IDs rather than nested records; permission export depends on Row Security. Large exports use emailed expiring download links.

facts.label: File and native SQL exit paths
facts.value: Storage has download and S3 GET access. Native SQL exposes engine drivers and standard tooling; engine-native exports require caller tooling and transfer capacity.

facts.label: Account deletion and purge timing
facts.value: Privacy permits account deletion through Console settings or contact. Legal/tax/dispute retention exceptions and remaining public activity are described; no universal exact physical purge deadline found.

facts.label: TablesDB managed backup and restore
facts.value: Cloud Pro/Enterprise hot, encrypted, remotely stored backups; Pro daily, Enterprise configurable. Restore creates a new database name/ID rather than overwriting the source.

facts.label: PostgreSQL backup policies
facts.value: Automatic policy from creation. Pro one daily policy with seven-day retention; Scale unlimited policies with cron and 1–36,500-day retention. Manual backups are not pruned on the scheduled-policy cycle.

facts.label: PostgreSQL PITR and restore
facts.value: Optional WAL-based PITR has 1–35-day window. Backup/PITR restore is in-place, interrupts availability and discards changes after the recovery target. Initial PITR window is unavailable until first archive segment.

facts.label: MySQL backup and PITR differences
facts.value: Pro one daily seven-day policy. PITR archives binary logs and is enabled by default with seven-day retention when created through API; configurable 1–35 days, separately billed. Restore overwrites current data.

facts.label: Backup file coverage and extra meters
facts.value: Database backup pages do not establish restoration of Storage file bodies, users, deployments or secrets. Separate backup storage/download charges and TablesDB PITR are not fully published in inspected pages.

facts.label: Start backup inclusion
facts.value: Start announcement includes daily backups retained seven days and email support.

facts.label: File backup/version recovery
facts.value: S3 versioning/Object Lock/restore APIs are unsupported. Native file undelete/version-history guarantees and managed file-body backup retention were not established.

facts.label: Identity and vendor
facts.value: Appwrite; current privacy policy names Appwrite Code Ltd. Official product URL https://appwrite.io/. No former product name established.

facts.label: Hosting editions
facts.value: Managed Appwrite Cloud and self-hosted software. Cloud operates the infrastructure; the self-host operator supplies and maintains it.

facts.label: Software license
facts.value: Repository LICENSE has the three BSD redistribution conditions: preserve notices, reproduce binary notices, and no endorsement without permission. Classification: BSD-3-Clause.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access
facts.value: Operating public Cloud and self-host offers. Company timeline records Cloud general availability in September 2025 and native PostgreSQL/MySQL in September 2026.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access
facts.value: Note 2026-11-09: Appwrite’s November 4 report confirms that an attacker read one customer’s Function code/logs and changed its code for 31 seconds. A separate Frankfurt runtime credential could have read secret environment variables in 1,022 notified Sites/Functions projects; Appwrite found no evidence of those reads but cannot rule them out because its infrastructure provider’s audit log is incomplete. The incident was on Appwrite Cloud. The status page separately records a resolved 13-minute all-region Sites HTTP 500 on November 2. No product shutdown, sale or rebrand found.

facts.label: Vendor home
facts.value: Remote-first team; legal entity known. Physical headquarters and a complete served-market list were not found.

facts.label: Support paths
facts.value: Pricing capture: Free community support and Pro email. Enterprise offers custom support/hosting.

facts.label: Public status
facts.value: Public status at https://appwrite.online/. Fetched page warns it has not updated since 2026-11-03 14:24 UTC.

facts.label: Uptime promise conflict
facts.value: Formal uptime page: Free none, Pro 99.5%, Scale 99.9%, Enterprise 99.95% monthly. Indexed pricing comparison displays no Pro SLA.

facts.label: SLA credit conditions
facts.value: Uptime credits: 10%, 25% or 50% according to outage band; claim within 30 days. Usage charges excluded; scheduled maintenance, external events/network and customer errors excluded.

facts.label: Response SLA scope
facts.value: Support SLA publishes Silver/Gold/Platinum tiers, but their mapping to small Cloud plans is not established. Gold critical response one hour and Platinum 15 minutes, 24/7; Silver critical unsupported.

apps.name: AWS Amplify
apps.line: Builds app backends from AWS database, login, storage and function services.

free.text: $100 credits; free plan closes at 6 months, data deleted after 90 days

cells.regions: AWS Region-dependent
cells.selfhost: No, cloud resources run on AWS

sql.math: $0.48 for AppSync, plus $0.0125 for reads and $0.0125 for writes. This assumes the free storage and transfer allowances still left apply. The total is $0.505.
Stored table data and selected API resources still count while idle. No full idle total is given.

files.math: 100 GB of storage at $0.023 a GB, plus 100,000 requests at $0.005 per 1,000, plus 1,000,000 requests at $0.0004 per 1,000. The total is $3.20. Data transfer is not included.

jobs.math: 10,000 runs, each one second at 512 MB, use 5,000 GB-seconds (memory multiplied by time). That fits within 400,000 free GB-seconds a month, if that allowance is still available.

facts.label: New-customer credit offer
facts.value: For AWS accounts created on or after 2025-07-15, the legacy 12-month Free Tier was replaced by USD $100 at signup and up to USD $100 earned credits. These are account-level credits, not $200 automatically or a permanent free backend; accounts created before the cutoff retain legacy eligibility and terms.

facts.label: Free plan versus recurring allowances
facts.value: For accounts created on or after 2025-07-15, the new Free account plan lasts up to six months or until credits are exhausted; paid accounts continue with usage billing. Accounts created before the cutoff stay in the legacy program. Always-free allowances remain distinct from time-limited account access and service trials.

facts.label: Credit expiry inconsistency
facts.value: Amplify pricing says use credits within 12 months of account creation. Billing FAQ says 12 months after issuance in one answer and after account creation in another.

facts.label: DynamoDB recurring Free Tier
facts.value: Per Region/per payer: Standard storage 25GB, provisioned 25 read and 25 write capacity units, and 2.5M stream reads monthly are listed.

facts.label: Lambda recurring Free Tier
facts.value: Lambda Event Functions list one million requests and 400,000 GB-seconds per month. Provisioned Concurrency does not receive this free tier.

facts.label: Cognito Lite and Essentials allowances
facts.value: Direct/social login: 10,000 MAU/month per account or AWS organization for Lite/Essentials; no Plus free tier. SAML/OIDC federation has a separate 50-MAU allowance.

facts.label: Legacy AppSync offer
facts.value: AppSync pricing still lists 250,000 query/mutations, 250,000 realtime updates and 600,000 connection-minutes, expiring after 12 months. AWS says 12-month Free Tier offers remain for accounts created before 2025-07-15; newer accounts use the credit/Free-plan offer. AppSync pricing does not reconcile whether its old allowance applies to new-plan accounts.

facts.label: Legacy hosting/storage offers
facts.value: Amplify pricing has a 12-month hosting allowance table alongside its newer six-month Free-plan notice; S3 FAQ also retains old signup allowances. AWS’s 2025-07-15 change makes those 12-month offers legacy for eligible accounts created before the cutoff; newer accounts use credits/Free plan. Existing legacy account terms are unchanged.

facts.label: Free account expiry and retained data
facts.value: Free plan closes at six months/credit exhaustion. Content is retained 90 days; upgrading within that period can reopen access, otherwise the account/content is permanently erased per plan docs.

facts.label: Ordinary idle backend lifecycle
facts.value: No Amplify-wide paid-backend pause/deletion timer was found. Stopping the sandbox watcher does not delete its deployed CloudFormation resources; explicit sandbox deletion is separate.

facts.label: Amplify backend commitment
facts.value: Backend has no monthly minimum; collaboration has no per-seat charge. Pay for the selected underlying resources; frontend hosting and support are separate choices.

facts.label: Currency, invoices and tax
facts.value: Agreement fees exclude indirect taxes except where local law requires otherwise. AWS India can display USD but invoices INR at its invoice-date conversion rate.

facts.label: AppSync API/realtime meters
facts.value: GraphQL query/mutation $4/million; realtime updates $2/million; connections $0.08/million minutes. Data transfer separately billed at EC2 rates; optional cache.small $0.044/hour.

facts.label: DynamoDB request/storage rate example
facts.value: US East (N. Virginia), Standard on-demand examples use $0.625/million write units, $0.125/million read units and $0.25/GB-month storage.

facts.label: Provisioned database capacity
facts.value: Provisioned mode charges hourly allocated capacity even when unused. The pricing example uses $0.00065/WCU-hour and $0.00013/RCU-hour in us-east-1.

facts.label: Cognito paid examples
facts.value: Essentials examples charge $0.015/MAU above its applicable allowance; Lite first paid band $0.0055/MAU. Plus and advanced security are different paid variants.

facts.label: Frontend-hosting charges, optional
facts.value: Amplify Standard build $0.01/minute; CDN storage $0.023/GB-month; served transfer $0.15/GB; SSR $0.30/million requests plus $0.20/GB-hour. WAF association $15/app-month plus AWS WAF fees.

facts.label: Idle charges by architecture
facts.value: On-demand data/API/function paths avoid an allocated-instance fee, but stored files/tables/backups persist. Provisioned DB capacity, AppSync cache and Lambda provisioned concurrency remain chargeable while allocated.

facts.label: Cold starts and initialization
facts.value: Lambda reuses environments or creates new ones. Billing includes initialization outside the handler; extensions and selected warm-capacity options can add billed work. No universal cold-start latency promise found.

facts.label: Internet transfer allowance conflict
facts.value: AWS network FAQ says 100GB/month free internet outbound, shared across services/Regions except China/GovCloud. DynamoDB Free Tier list still says 1GB, or 15GB first year.

facts.label: S3 transfer routing
facts.value: S3 FAQ: same-region AWS-service/S3 traffic and same-region COPY avoid transfer fees; cross-region flows have source-region charges. Other network services in a path can add processing fees.

facts.label: Transfer cost exclusions
facts.value: Amplify Hosting has its own served-GB rate; AppSync uses EC2 rates. Complete backend endpoint-to-endpoint/cache/backup/export routing cannot be priced from total GB alone.

facts.label: Budget alerts are not a hard cap
facts.value: AWS Budgets updates up to three times daily, typically 8–12 hours apart. Charges can exceed thresholds before alerts arrive. Taxes/support/refunds can be included or excluded.

facts.label: Budget actions and Free-plan exception
facts.value: Budget actions can apply IAM/SCP restrictions or target EC2/RDS resources; these do not describe shutting down every existing backend meter. Free account plan instead stops at expiry/credits, unless upgraded.

facts.label: Automatic paid conversion/credits
facts.value: Creating/joining Organizations or setting up Control Tower automatically upgrades the Free account plan and immediately expires its credits. Other listed business programs can also trigger upgrade.

facts.label: DynamoDB item/query limits
facts.value: Maximum item 400KB including attribute names/values; nested attributes 32 levels. Binary units: 1KB = 1,024 bytes. Expression string limit 4KB.

facts.label: Read/write unit conversion
facts.value: Ordinary write unit covers up to 1KB; strong read up to 4KB, eventual read half the strong-read units. Transactional reads/writes double ordinary unit work.

facts.label: Capacity and tables
facts.value: Initial DynamoDB table quota 2,500/Region; default per-table request throughput 40,000 read/write units per second, adjustable. No practical table item/byte size limit stated.

facts.label: API response and subscription limits
facts.value: AppSync maximum request execution 30 seconds; evaluated response 5MB; subscription payload 240KB; 200 subscriptions per client connection, adjustable.

facts.label: SQL connection pools
facts.value: Existing SQL adapter can use separately billed RDS Proxy to avoid excess direct connections. No universal ten-connection capacity or pooled database tier comes with Amplify.

facts.label: Query page and consumed work
facts.value: DynamoDB Query pages are limited to 1MB; filters apply after items are read. Billed read work follows items/sizes examined, not only returned attributes/results.

facts.label: Storage class and price basis
facts.value: Amplify Storage uses S3; default object class is Standard. S3 storage billing uses binary GB: 2^30 bytes. Region/class/volume affect rate.

facts.label: US East Standard reference rate
facts.value: Official AWS solution cost guide quotes $0.023/GB-month for the first 50TB. Main S3 pricing reader did not expose selected-region Standard storage table.

facts.label: Standard file request rates
facts.value: US East official reference: PUT/COPY/POST/LIST $0.005 per 1,000; GET $0.0004 per 1,000. Main S3 pricing independently confirms the GET rate in its US East example.

facts.label: Retrieval/image fees
facts.value: Storage class controls retrieval/restore charges. Amplify file-download FAQ says image compression/CDN caching is not provided by its Storage client; custom processing or delivery is separate.

facts.label: Standard minimum billing
facts.value: S3 Standard comparison explicitly lists no minimum storage duration and no minimum billable object size.

facts.label: Other class floors
facts.value: Standard-IA/One Zone-IA: 128KB minimum, 30 days. Glacier Instant/Flexible: 90 days; Deep Archive: 180 days. Early delete/overwrite/transition can incur remaining-duration charges.

facts.label: DynamoDB vector limits
facts.value: Vector indexes: 4,096 dimensions maximum, five indexes/table initially (adjustable up to 20), TopK at most 100, 18 inline filters.

facts.label: Vector edition/storage requirements
facts.value: Vector index and base table must use on-demand mode; f32 index precision, 16MB response maximum, no result pagination or PartiQL vector access. Index storage is separate from base table/projections.

facts.label: Vector meters
facts.value: Vector writes bill indexed GB; searches bill processed/returned GB; index storage bills GB-month in addition to base table. Writes/searches have a 1KB minimum charge.

facts.label: US East vector rate example
facts.value: Standard vector example uses $0.52/GB indexed writes, $0.002/GB search work and $0.25/GB-month index storage, in addition to base-table charges.

facts.label: Embeddings and reranking
facts.value: DynamoDB stores caller-provided embeddings; model generation/reranking is a separate workload. Amplify AI Kit bills Bedrock tokens per model without markup; no universal included vector-model allowance found.

facts.label: Amplify function defaults
facts.value: defineFunction default timeout three seconds; configurable to 900 seconds. Memory default 512MB, configurable 128–10,240MB; ephemeral storage default 512MB, configurable to 10,240MB.

facts.label: CPU and concurrency
facts.value: Lambda CPU scales with memory; one vCPU equivalent at 1,769MB. Regional default concurrent executions 1,000, but new accounts have reduced quotas.

facts.label: Lambda price and duration scope
facts.value: US East x86 examples: $0.20/million requests and $0.0000166667/GB-second. Billed work includes initialization/extensions; allocated Provisioned Concurrency and extra temporary storage price separately.

facts.label: AWS account/payment requirement
facts.value: Cloud deployment requires AWS credentials/account. Free plan signup requires a payment method for identity verification; it is not a no-card offer.

facts.label: Eligibility and production scope
facts.value: Free plan/credits are for new customers who have not previously had an AWS account. Paid plan is the documented production/scaling path; cloud sandboxes are explicitly development-only.

facts.label: Country and use restrictions
facts.value: Complete Amplify signup-country/payment-country eligibility was not found in the inspected account/pricing/terms pages. Domain use requires necessary rights.

facts.label: Primary type and overlaps
facts.value: Researcher classification: backend platform/toolkit that provisions and connects AWS services. Secondary roles: auth, database APIs, files, functions, realtime and frontend deployment.

facts.label: Backend components and bill owners
facts.value: Amplify Auth uses Cognito; Data uses AppSync and DynamoDB; Storage provisions S3; Functions provisions Lambda. Each underlying service has its own bill and limits.

facts.label: Auth delivery extras
facts.value: Cognito SMS for verification/MFA/recovery and email verification incur separate SNS/SES delivery pricing. MAU allowance does not include unlimited messages.

facts.label: AI and model extras
facts.value: Amplify AI Kit uses Bedrock on-demand inference, charged to the customer account with no Amplify markup. Model/region/token prices vary.

facts.label: Client languages and APIs
facts.value: Official guides cover React/Next.js/Angular/Vue/JavaScript, React Native, Flutter, Android and Swift. Amplify Data exposes generated GraphQL client/query/mutation/subscription APIs.

facts.label: SQL and direct service access
facts.value: Existing MySQL/PostgreSQL can connect through an AppSync SQL Lambda adapter with stored connection secrets. Database hosting, proxy and adapter execution cost separately. S3 remains actual AWS S3.

facts.label: Data authorization defaults
facts.value: Data rules deny by default and support public API key, guest IAM identity, authenticated users, owner, groups, OIDC and custom Lambda rules. Multiple rules can grant access.

facts.label: Public sample and privileged credentials
facts.value: Quickstart uses a 30-day public AppSync API key. It is a public-access mechanism, not a secret administrator credential. Cloud deployment uses IAM/SSO credentials with infrastructure privileges.

facts.label: File rules and identities
facts.value: Storage starts with no file access. Rules grant path access to guests, authenticated users, groups or individual Cognito identity IDs; multiple buckets can be configured.

facts.label: Server secret handling
facts.value: Amplify supports secret() references separately from ordinary function environment values. Ordinary values can appear in plaintext build artifacts and CloudFormation events.

facts.label: Stored-file encryption
facts.value: New S3 objects use SSE-S3 by default, AES-256-GCM, without an additional SSE-S3 fee. Customer-managed KMS is a separate configuration/cost choice.

facts.label: SQL networking scope
facts.value: SQL adapter connects with TLS and can use RDS VPC settings/proxy; local schema generation needs database reachability. Proxy adds cost and can add waiting latency.

facts.label: Default generated data model
facts.value: Each Gen 2 a.model creates a DynamoDB table and generated CRUD/realtime APIs through AppSync. DynamoDB is a key-value/document engine, not SQL emulation.

facts.label: Existing SQL and Blocks variants
facts.value: Gen 2 can combine existing MySQL/PostgreSQL models with DynamoDB models. Blocks Preview adds separate database capabilities through a nested CDK stack; existing Amplify resources remain.

facts.label: DynamoDB read consistency
facts.value: Table/LSI reads default eventually consistent, with optional strong reads; GSI/stream reads are eventually consistent. Successful writes persist; read-committed isolation does not stop later concurrent changes.

facts.label: Resolver consistency control
facts.value: AppSync GetItem resolver consistentRead is optional and defaults false. Exact generated resolver settings for every Amplify model/version were not established.

facts.label: Atomic transaction scope
facts.value: DynamoDB TransactWriteItems is all-or-nothing for up to 100 items/4MB across tables in one account/Region. Client idempotency token lasts ten minutes; batch writes can partially succeed.

facts.label: Generated transaction integration gap
facts.value: A first-class Gen 2 generated-client transaction method/default was not found in inspected setup, custom-data navigation, parity and override guides. Underlying transactions require a chosen custom integration.

facts.label: Cloud sandbox behavior
facts.value: Each developer can deploy isolated real AWS resources for development. Some sandbox GSI edits drop/recreate the table; unsupported Cognito changes can recreate the user pool.

facts.label: Git branch environments
facts.value: Fullstack branches deploy isolated infrastructure/code; branch auto-disconnection can remove the associated branch when Git branch is deleted. Data snapshot/merge-back semantics are not documented there.

facts.label: Replication and failover scope
facts.value: DynamoDB global tables are multi-active across Regions; replicas serve reads/writes. Eventual consistency default, optional multi-region strong consistency; application traffic must shift to a healthy Region.

facts.label: Realtime versus offline — generations
facts.value: Generated Gen 2 subscriptions provide live create/update/delete events. Feature matrix explicitly lists DataStore and its conflict detection as Gen 1 supported, Gen 2 unsupported.

facts.label: Secondary indexes
facts.value: Gen 2 secondaryIndexes supports custom partition/sort keys, query names and projection choices. DynamoDB defaults: 20 GSIs and five LSIs per table.

facts.label: Text/vector extension scope
facts.value: DynamoDB has separately configured vector indexes; Gen 1 searchable is not directly present in Gen 2, whose matrix points to OpenSearch integration.

facts.label: Current S3 multipart limits
facts.value: S3 multipart maximum object 48.8TiB; 10,000 parts; each 5MiB–5GiB, except final part has no minimum.

facts.label: Amplify upload mechanics
facts.value: uploadData supports pause/resume/cancel; automatically multipart above 5MB. Upload tasks initiated over one hour ago are automatically cancelled, but incomplete S3 parts can remain and need lifecycle cleanup.

facts.label: Client maximum gap
facts.value: No separate numeric end-to-end Amplify browser SDK maximum file size was found in current Upload/Storage setup docs. S3 service maximum alone does not prove client fit.

facts.label: S3 interface and SDK surface
facts.value: Storage provisions real S3 buckets; full AWS service APIs can be used with proper IAM. Amplify client offers a narrower helper interface; downloadData always gets latest object version.

facts.label: Signed private downloads/uploads
facts.value: getUrl produces signed GET/PUT links. Default expiry 900 seconds; session credentials cap it at one hour. Optional existence validation performs a check.

facts.label: CDN/custom-domain scope
facts.value: Amplify Storage client FAQ does not provide CloudFront caching for its S3 buckets. Managed Amplify Hosting serves frontend assets separately; a custom file CDN/domain needs its own architecture and costs.

facts.label: Vector filters and similarity
facts.value: DynamoDB vector indexes offer cosine, dot product and Euclidean scoring. SearchConditionExpression currently supports equality on index partition/inline fields; comparison/range/IN not available.

facts.label: Tenant authorization warning
facts.value: SearchVectors has no fine-grained IAM partition-key isolation. Scoping to a tenant key is not a security boundary; distinct tables/indexes with grants are documented for strict data-layer isolation.

facts.label: Hybrid and Amplify integration scope
facts.value: AWS vector decision guide lists no DynamoDB hybrid search. No generated Amplify vector-search operation/automatic permissions mapping was established in inspected Gen 2 Data docs.

facts.label: Managed runtime path
facts.value: Gen 2 defineFunction runs TypeScript/Node on Lambda Event Functions. Custom CDK functions can use other Lambda runtimes/languages; new MicroVM/Web/Managed Instances modes are separate configurations.

facts.label: Runtime version documentation gap
facts.value: Amplify configuration guide still says default Node 18; current Lambda runtime guide marks Node 18 deprecated since September 1, 2025 and lists supported Node 22/24. Current package-version default not verified.

facts.label: Lambda async failure policy
facts.value: Function errors default to two retries, after one and two minutes. Throttle/system failures retry with backoff for up to six hours. Duplicate deliveries can occur and expired/unprocessed events can be discarded.

facts.label: Discarded events and redelivery
facts.value: Lambda supports dead-letter queues and on-failure destinations; configured retries 0–2 and maximum async event age 60–21,600 seconds. Replay needs retained events and a deliberate reinvocation path.

facts.label: EventBridge delivery retry layer
facts.value: EventBridge target delivery defaults up to 24 hours/185 attempts with backoff/jitter; failures drop unless DLQ configured. Lambda may separately retry after accepting an asynchronous event.

facts.label: Amplify recurring schedules
facts.value: defineFunction schedule uses EventBridge rules, supports interval/cron/multiple schedules; custom function schedule property unsupported. Legacy scheduled rules use UTC+0, minute precision.

facts.label: One-off delayed alternative
facts.value: EventBridge Scheduler supports one-time/rate/cron with selected time zone and 60-second precision. It is an optional separately configured service, not a documented defineFunction schedule mode.

facts.label: Invocation payload and retention
facts.value: Ordinary Lambda invocation payload: synchronous 6MB request/response; async 1MB. Async maximum event age configurable 60 seconds–six hours.

facts.label: Function logs and export
facts.value: Amplify streams function logs to terminal/file in sandbox mode. CloudWatch log groups can export to S3; export availability can lag 12 hours and tasks time out at 24 hours.

facts.label: Log retention defaults and costs
facts.value: Generic CloudWatch Logs retains indefinitely unless retention configured. Exact Amplify-created function-log retention was not found in function config/streaming docs. Logs add ingestion/storage/query/export costs.

facts.label: Data API logging is separate
facts.value: Amplify Data logging:true defaults to one-week retention, no field logs and excluding verbose content; configuration can change this. Logging full request parameters can retain sensitive payloads.

facts.label: Local tools and cloud operations
facts.value: Data guide prerequisites Node >=18.16.0, npm >=6.14.4, Git >=2.14.1. Cloud sandbox needs AWS profile/CDK bootstrap; developer maintains code, IAM, backups and resource cleanup.

facts.label: Self-managed hosting/local Blocks scope
facts.value: Self-managed hosting is Preview and deploys to AWS; Blocks Preview can run local in-memory/filesystem implementations. No independent full Cognito/AppSync/DynamoDB production self-host bundle or server RAM floor established.

facts.label: Amplify deployment regions
facts.value: Amplify endpoint list: us-east-1/2, us-west-1/2, ap-east-1, ap-south-1, ap-northeast-1/2/3, ap-southeast-1/2, ca-central-1, eu-central-1, eu-west-1/2/3, eu-south-1, eu-north-1, me-south-1, sa-east-1.

facts.label: Content location and additional copies
facts.value: Customer chooses AWS content Regions; AWS states it will not move/replicate outside them without agreement, with service-initiated/legal exceptions. Replication/export and AI inference profiles can intentionally cross Regions.

facts.label: Region migration/availability gap
facts.value: A complete Amplify-plus-every-component region matrix and one-step region migration contract were not found. AppSync endpoint availability differs from the Amplify list.

facts.label: DynamoDB export
facts.value: PITR-enabled tables export full/incremental DynamoDB JSON or Amazon Ion to S3 without consuming read capacity. Export storage/PUT and cross-region transfer can add charges.

facts.label: File and user export paths
facts.value: S3 files can be downloaded; Cognito ListUsers returns paginated user attributes/basic details with IAM permission. A complete password/identity/session-preserving migration export was not established.

facts.label: Deleting a deployed environment
facts.value: Amplify supports deletion protection and retention policies on supported resources; protection can make sandbox deletion fail. Sandbox delete explicitly ignores resource removal policies and deletes resources.

facts.label: AWS account closure
facts.value: Account closure has a 90-day reopening period; content/resources are deleted after permanent closure with stated CloudTrail exceptions. Outstanding invoices/commitments remain; reopening can restart charges.

facts.label: Privacy retention scope
facts.value: AWS Privacy Notice excludes customer application content and separately allows retaining account/contact/invoice/security records for legal/business purposes after closure. No one universal physical purge deadline found.

facts.label: Enable backups on generated tables
facts.value: Amplify documents CDK configuration for DynamoDB PITR/deletion protection and scheduled AWS Backup. Backup automation is a configuration choice, not established as enabled by default for every model.

facts.label: PITR retention and restore
facts.value: DynamoDB PITR default window 35 days, configurable 1–35; shortening does not lower its size-based price. Restores create a new independent table and can target another Region.

facts.label: Backup prices and coverage
facts.value: US East disaster-recovery guide: PITR $0.20/GB-month, restore $0.15/GB. On-demand snapshots and AWS Backup have separate storage/retention pricing. DynamoDB backup does not constitute a complete Amplify project backup.

facts.label: Version history and delete recovery
facts.value: S3 Versioning is disabled by default. Once enabled, ordinary delete creates a marker and old versions can be restored; each full retained version is charged, not only changed bytes.

facts.label: Object retention and replication
facts.value: S3 Object Lock requires versioning and supports retention/legal holds. S3 same/cross-region replication is asynchronous; existing objects need Batch Replication.

facts.label: Identity and generations
facts.value: AWS Amplify, provided by Amazon Web Services. Amplify Gen 1 and Gen 2 are generations; Amplify Hosting is the managed frontend hosting service, not another database vendor.

facts.label: Managed and local modes
facts.value: Cloud backends use AWS-managed resources in the customer account; Amplify libraries and deployment tooling run locally. Self-managed hosting still deploys S3/CloudFront/Lambda infrastructure on AWS.

facts.label: JavaScript and backend licenses
facts.value: Amplify JavaScript and Amplify backend repository LICENSE files both specify Apache License 2.0.

facts.label: Current access stage
facts.value: Gen 2 is the current documented code-first backend. Gen 1 entered maintenance on 2026-05-01, receives only critical bug fixes and security patches, and reaches end of life on 2027-05-01. AWS Blocks and self-managed hosting remain separately labelled Preview.

facts.label: Regional service incident
facts.value: Note 2026-11-09: AWS Health listed Amplify among services disrupted during the March 2026 Middle East incident; the public notice gives no Amplify-specific impact details.

facts.label: Preview service conditions
facts.value: AWS Service Terms exclude beta/preview services from service-level agreements and describe evaluation use, possible changes/termination and possible data inaccessibility.

facts.label: Vendor jurisdiction and contracting party
facts.value: AWS Customer Agreement lists Amazon Web Services, Inc., Seattle, USA as the default contracting party; a country-based table assigns other entities, including AWS India and AWS EMEA.

facts.label: Included support
facts.value: Basic Support is included: customer service, documentation, re:Post community, core Trusted Advisor checks and AWS Health. It is not a published included engineering response SLA for every application issue.

facts.label: Optional paid support
facts.value: Business Support+ minimum $29/account/month or percentage of charges, whichever higher; initial spend band 9% up to $10K. Minimum support commitment 30 days. Production-down response listed under one hour.

facts.label: Status availability
facts.value: Official public AWS Health dashboard is https://health.aws.amazon.com/health/status. Its fetched page had no readable status body, so live operational state was not verified.

facts.label: Amplify Console SLA
facts.value: Formal Amplify Console SLA states 99.95% monthly per Region; credit bands 10%, 25%, 100%, with claim by end of second billing cycle after incident and minimum credit greater than $1 USD.

facts.label: Underlying backend SLAs
facts.value: AppSync SLA 99.95%; DynamoDB Standard 99.99%, eligible Global Tables 99.999%, monthly with their own definitions/exclusions.

apps.name: AWS Step Functions
apps.line: Coordinates cloud workflows with states, retries, waits and branches.

free.text: 4,000 Standard state transitions each month

cells.regions: Many AWS Regions; integration support varies

sql.math: Workflow service, not a database
Workflow service, not a database

files.math: Does not store app files

jobs.math: Each of 10,000 workflows has 5 transitions (steps). The first 4,000 transitions are free, and the rest cost $0.025 per 1,000. Connected services are not included. The total is $1.15.

apps.news: News check 2026-11-09: no sale, shutdown, rebrand, or incident found for AWS Step Functions.

facts.label: Free offer type

facts.label: Leaving and deleting

facts.label: File recovery and protection

facts.value: Azure Storage account restore is available for up to 14 days under supported conditions and is described as best effort.

facts.label: free offer type
facts.value: Lasting Cosmos DB free tier: opt in at creation, one eligible account per Azure subscription. Separate Azure new-account trial: USD 200 credit for 30 days and selected 12-month allowances.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: Cosmos DB free tier: first 1,000 RU/s and 25 GB per account, including eligible manual/autoscale and single/multiple write regions; usage above it is billed. Serverless is excluded.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: Eligible new Azure free account plus Cosmos free tier: combined 1,400 RU/s and 50 GB for the first 12 months, then 1,000 RU/s and 25 GB for the Cosmos account lifetime.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: A legacy pricing FAQ still describes 400 RU/s and 5 GB; the dedicated free-tier docs and pricing introduction describe 1,000 RU/s and 25 GB.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: Cosmos DB reserves the right to delete empty accounts, defined as accounts without databases/collections. The limit page does not give an inactivity interval for that right.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: No precise automatic pause/deletion timetable for a nonempty, idle paid/free-tier account was established.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: East US, USD PAYG serverless: no minimum operations, RU reservation, upfront capacity payment or minimum service charge; retained storage and actual operations still bill.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: East US, USD PAYG manual: new small resource minimum 400 RU/s. Base rate USD 0.008 per 100 RU/s-hour; USD 0.032/hour before storage, transfers, backup extras and taxes (our calculation).

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: East US, USD PAYG transactional data/index storage: USD 0.25 per GB/month per region.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: East US, USD PAYG serverless: USD 0.25 per 1 million consumed RUs; availability-zone requests use a 1.25 multiplier.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: East US, USD PAYG General Purpose autoscale: USD 0.012 per 100 scaled RU/s-hour (1.5 × the manual base rate); billed using hourly scaling, including its minimum.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: East US, USD PAYG Business Critical multi-write base: USD 0.016 per 100 RU/s-hour in each region. Standard General Purpose zone-enabled regions multiply RU/s by 1.25; autoscale availability zones have no extra zone charge.

facts.label: idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Manual throughput continues to bill idle provisioned capacity. Autoscale moves within 10%–100% of configured Tmax; entry Tmax 1,000 means an idle floor of 100 RU/s, not zero.

facts.label: idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Serverless has no reserved-throughput idle bill. Zero operations means zero operation RUs, while retained storage, paid backups and any other selected services remain.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: Cosmos-specific table, USD, East US/North America origin: ingress and same-region/intra-zone transfer free; first 5 GB/month outbound free, then USD 0.05/GB to another region or the internet.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: Cosmos table's 5-GB/USD 0.05 North America outbound schedule differs from the general Azure Bandwidth page's 100-GB free allowance and USD 0.087/GB next 10 TB for North America/Europe internet egress over Microsoft Premium Global Network.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: Free-tier excess usage bills regular prices; provisioned throughput exhaustion can return HTTP 429. An account total-throughput ceiling blocks new resources, increases or extra regions that would exceed it; autoscale counts configured Tmax.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: Azure budgets send alerts; they do not stop resources or consumption. Cost data typically arrives in 8–24 hours and budgets evaluate every 24 hours.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: 500 combined databases plus containers per account; 25 containers per shared-throughput database. The 500 count is combined, not 500 of each.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Regular item/request maximum 2 MB; item size is UTF-8 JSON length. Query page response up to 4 MB and operation/page execution up to 5 seconds. Transactional batch maximum 100 operations, 2 MB total and 5 seconds.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: MongoDB RU supports up to 16-MB documents through its large-document feature, rather than a generic increase to the NoSQL 2-MB limit.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Regular full logical partition key: 20 GB and up to 10,000 RU/s. Hierarchical keys support up to three levels to spread larger first-level groups; overall container storage is listed as unlimited.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Serverless container starts with 5,000 RU/s; each physical partition can handle up to 5,000 RU/s as the container grows. Shared database throughput and provisioned RU settings are unavailable.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Manual minimum starts at 400 RU/s; autoscale starts with Tmax 1,000 RU/s. Storage volume, historical highest throughput and shared-container count can raise the permitted minimum.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Gremlin-specific: 30-second traversal timeout, repeat limit 32, idle WebSocket lifetime 1 hour.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: No universal plan-level SQL-style concurrent-connection quota was established across all SDK/API modes.

facts.label: storage prices
facts.value: Not applicable as a current general file-storage plan. East US USD 0.25/GB/month is database data/index storage, not a Blob/S3 bucket tariff.

facts.label: file request and retrieval prices
facts.value: No general file upload/read/image-processing tariff is included; database operations use RUs and external file services bill separately.

facts.label: minimum storage and early deletion
facts.value: Object archival minimum size/retention and early-deletion fees are outside the current database file scope.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: NoSQL policy types: float32, float16, int8, uint8, one policy per unique path. flat indexes allow up to 505 dimensions; quantizedFlat and DiskANN up to 4,096.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: quantizedFlat/DiskANN require at least 1,000 vectors for quantization; below this they scan. Shared-throughput accounts are unsupported, and vector indexing/search cannot be disabled once enabled on a container.

facts.label: embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: Embedding generation uses an external model/provider in the vector workflow; its tokens/compute are additional to Cosmos storage/RUs. Index writes and searches themselves consume database resources.

facts.label: embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: Native Semantic Reranker preview: East US USD 1 per 1,000 calls; up to 50 documents/call and 2,048 tokens per context-document pair. Separate feature enablement and roles are required.

facts.label: run limits and pricing
facts.value: Database operations: 5 seconds, 2-MB request, 100-operation batch. Per-container defaults: 100 stored procedures and 50 UDFs, increaseable by support. Database work consumes RUs; worker CPU/memory charges belong to the external host.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Public self-service Azure account. Phone, Microsoft or GitHub account, and non-prepaid credit/debit card required; Hong Kong and Brazil accept credit cards only. Billing address must match an available country/region.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Commercial customer solutions and production use are allowed subject to Azure terms. The Azure free account does not itself prohibit production; usage beyond allowances needs paid billing.

facts.label: primary type and other roles
facts.value: Primary directory type: document and graph databases (our classification). Other roles: key-value/wide-column/table APIs, native vector and text search, database change feeds.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: Native database APIs, indexing, replication, backup, JavaScript database procedures/triggers, and change feeds. App user login, general file hosting and arbitrary function workers are additional services or application code.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: NoSQL REST/SDK access; current overview lists .NET, Java, JavaScript, Python, Go and Rust SDKs. MongoDB RU, Cassandra, Gremlin and Table have their own protocol/driver compatibility surfaces.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: NoSQL supports Entra managed identities and native data-plane role-based access to items, separate from control-plane management roles; keys also exist. Grant only required permissions and avoid placing account keys in public clients.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Private endpoints and disabling public network access are documented; encryption at rest and optional customer-managed/client-side encryption are supported.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: NoSQL: distributed JSON documents with SQL-like queries, partition keys and native indexing. MongoDB RU, Cassandra CQL, Gremlin graph and Table endpoints are separate API choices.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: NoSQL ACID transactions with snapshot isolation operate within one logical partition of one container. Transactional batch and JavaScript procedures support this scope; ETags allow conditional optimistic writes.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Five consistency levels: strong, bounded staleness, session, consistent prefix and eventual. Strong/bounded-staleness reads cost twice the RUs of weaker reads; availability and possible regional-outage data loss depend on the configuration.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: MongoDB RU API 4.2 multi-document transactions require one nonsharded collection; cross-collection/cross-shard transactions are unsupported. Cassandra lightweight transactions are unsupported with multi-region writes.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Local emulator supports development/testing. Separate cloud accounts/databases/containers isolate environments with their own metered use; point-in-time restore can create a separate account copy.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: No built-in copy-on-write branch plan, branch count or lifetime was established.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Managed replicas protect against node failures. Provisioned accounts support extra read regions, service-managed/manual regional failover and Business Critical multiple writable regions; extra regions add throughput/storage cost.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Zone redundancy depends on region support. Serverless can enable zones when a new account is created; an existing non-zone serverless account cannot convert in place and still cannot add a second region.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Latest-version feed captures creates/updates, can combine intermediate versions, and omits deletes. All-versions-and-deletes mode captures every change within continuous-backup retention, is NoSQL-only, and uses preview enablement.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: A complete offline client read/write/conflict-resolution SDK contract was not established.

facts.label: extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: NoSQL supports configurable JSON indexes, unique keys, native vector search and BM25 full-text/hybrid ranking. Multi-language full-text support is early preview with regional caveats.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: Legacy attachment feature is being deprecated; the limits page lists 2 GB maximum attachment size per account. REST attachments can reference externally stored media; generic NoSQL items remain limited to 2 MB.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: S3 bucket operations are not an applicable Cosmos database API comparison; the migration tool's AWS S3 extension is a source/sink adapter, not a Cosmos S3 endpoint.

facts.label: delivery and private files
facts.value: Public/private buckets, signed file-delivery links, CDN and custom-domain file delivery require a separate storage/delivery scope.

facts.label: filters and mixed search
facts.value: VectorDistance searches can combine with NoSQL WHERE filters; full-text BM25 and vector results combine through reciprocal rank fusion (RRF).

facts.label: execution model and languages
facts.value: JavaScript procedures/triggers/UDFs run within NoSQL database contexts. General background workers run elsewhere. The change feed processor library supports .NET/Java; Python/Node.js use the pull model.

facts.label: delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Change feed processor is at-least-once, tracks checkpoints/leases in a container and can replay failed batches. Feed reads and lease maintenance both consume RUs.

facts.label: schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Feed replay depends on mode: retained latest item versions versus all changes/deletes within continuous-backup retention. Initial checkpoints/start time affect what can be replayed.

facts.label: schedules and queue retention
facts.value: General delayed/recurring job schedules and queue-retention tariffs are outside this product's execution scope.

facts.label: logs and run history
facts.value: Cosmos integrates with Azure Monitor metrics/diagnostic logs, and processor lifecycle/error callbacks instrument consumers. It does not supply a complete external-worker run-history product.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Local emulator is for development/testing, not recommended for production. It lacks service geo-replication/scale-out and serverless throughput; Windows and Linux emulator generations differ and can lag cloud features.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Provisioned accounts can select multiple Azure regions; serverless is permanently single-region. Account data is geo-replicated to selected regions, with availability-zone options where supported.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Periodic backups use separate storage and configured redundancy; continuous backups are taken in account regions and are not automatically geo-disaster resistant unless another account region is explicitly added.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Microsoft DPA governs customer data processing, transfers and retention. Its geography commitments refer to the applicable Product Terms; selecting a region alone is not a blanket legal-compliance finding.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Official open-source Data Migration Tool imports/exports via source/sink extensions, including Cosmos NoSQL, JSON, CSV, Parquet and other targets. Export reads consume Cosmos RUs and can incur outbound transfer.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Platform backup files cannot be directly listed, deleted or downloaded by customers. Recovery is performed through Cosmos restore workflows within retention.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: DPA: except free trials/LinkedIn, data remaining after subscription end is retained in a limited-function account for 90 days for extraction, then deleted within an additional 90 days unless retention exceptions apply. This is not a resource-delete completion deadline.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Periodic backup: full backup every 4 hours, latest two copies kept by default; configurable interval/retention, minimum interval 1 hour. Deleted provisioned-container/shared-database snapshots are retained for 30 days under documented conditions; restore requires support.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Periodic storage: first two copies included. East US USD additional backup-data rates: LRS 0.10, ZRS 0.125, RA-GRS 0.20 per GB/month.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Continuous backup retention tiers: 7, 30 or 35 days. Restore eligible points into a new or supported existing account. Supported APIs: NoSQL, MongoDB RU, Gremlin and Table; Cassandra is excluded.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: East US USD: continuous 7-day backup storage is free; 30/35-day storage is USD 0.20 per GB/month per region; each restore costs USD 0.15 per GB restored on every tier.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Continuous backups are local/zone redundant within account regions, not automatically cross-region disaster protection. Continuous mode cannot revert to periodic. Analytical-store data is excluded from backup/restore.

facts.label: file recovery and protection
facts.value: Object versioning/locks/file undelete are outside this database scope; database recovery does not establish recovery of externally stored files.

facts.label: identity and old names
facts.value: Azure Cosmos DB, a Microsoft Azure managed database service. Its vCore-based MongoDB offer was renamed Azure DocumentDB on 2025-11-18; Azure Cosmos DB for PostgreSQL is separately on a retirement path.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: Managed hosted service under Azure subscription/product terms. The production Cosmos DB engine is not offered here as self-hosted open-source software.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Operating and publicly available. Current pricing distinguishes General Purpose and Business Critical (formerly multi-write-region accounts); manual, autoscale and serverless are capacity/billing choices.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: vCore-based Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB was renamed Azure DocumentDB on 2025-11-18. Azure Cosmos DB for PostgreSQL is on a retirement path, is not recommended for new projects, and has no final retirement date published as of 2026-11-09.

facts.label: vendor home and main markets
facts.value: Microsoft is based in Redmond, Washington, United States. Azure access depends on account/billing-country availability; this business location does not locate customer databases.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: Azure Basic includes billing/subscription help, docs/community help and health notifications; technical support is a separate paid support plan. Public Azure Status lists regional/service incidents; subscription-specific incidents are available through Service Health.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: Provisioned Cosmos SLA: single region 99.99%; single region with availability zones 99.995%; multi-region reads 99.999%; multiple writable locations 99.999%. Service-credit terms and configuration conditions apply.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: Serverless docs say zone-enabled serverless SLAs align with single-region writes with availability zones, while the downloaded consolidated availability credit tables are labelled for provisioned resources; exact serverless credit applicability needs contract clarification.
