facts.value: pg_cron runs scheduled SQL inside PostgreSQL. Allowlist it, load via shared_preload_libraries/restart, then create it. It is not a separate 0.5-vCPU application-code worker.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Multiple jobs can run in parallel, but a given job does not overlap itself; a due rerun queues until that job’s prior instance finishes.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: A managed retry/backoff policy, cross-failure deduplication window, dead-letter queue and automatic replay guarantee were not found.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Cron schedules recurring SQL; catalog cron.timezone defaults to GMT where exposed and is static. cron.database_name defaults to postgres; schedule_in_database supports another database.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: A queue-style maximum delayed-message age or payload-retention SLA was not established for pg_cron.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: cron.log_run defaults on and records runs in cron.job_run_details. Upstream pg_cron says rows are not automatically cleaned; users can delete their own history and schedule cleanup.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Server-log capture for download is off by default; when enabled, default retention three days, configurable 1–7 days. Diagnostic export can use Log Analytics with separate ingestion/retention charges.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: A native failed-job replay interface and Azure-specific fixed retention promise for cron results were not established.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Not applicable: this offer is Microsoft-operated PostgreSQL. Running upstream PostgreSQL yourself is a different deployment with your own maintenance, backup and HA responsibilities.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Choose an Azure region. The PostgreSQL matrix lists East US, West Europe, UK South, Central India, Southeast Asia, Japan East, Australia East and Brazil South, with different compute/HA/geo-backup availability.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Native backups are local/zone redundant depending on region; optional geo backup replicates to an Azure paired region. PITR normally creates a server in the source region; geo-restore has separate eligibility.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: DPA permits international transfers subject to safeguards and defines Core Services data-at-rest/EU boundary obligations through Product Terms. External AI integration introduces its configured endpoint.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Export with pg_dump; restore using pg_restore/psql. pg_dumpall can include roles/permissions. Native managed physical-backup files cannot be exported to another provider.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Deleted-server restore can be attempted within five days from the original Azure subscription, if backups remain. The guide explicitly says success is not guaranteed.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: DPA generally retains remaining online-service data in a limited account for 90 days after subscription termination, then deletes within a further 90 days, subject to exceptions including free trials/authorized retention.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Exact physical purge timing for one deleted PostgreSQL server was not established.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Subscription owners can cancel in the portal after exporting needed data. Subscription deletion normally becomes available after three days for customer-led subscriptions or seven days for partner/field channels; resources must be removed first.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Azure does not automatically delete the Azure account. The cancellation guide describes 30–90 days before permanent data deletion, while DPA subscription-retention rules have their own scope/exceptions.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Automatic snapshot backups daily; first is full, later differential. If unchanged, snapshots can pause until a new modification. WAL archiving is workload-driven; generally the recovery-point delay is up to five minutes.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Default native retention seven days, adjustable 7–35 days; AES-256 at rest. On-demand snapshots are supported under the retention window. Stopped-server backups are retained.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: PITR creates a new same-region server; geo restore requires configured geo backup and can lose data not yet replicated. Native backup files are not portable downloads; use logical dumps to leave.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Separate vaulted LTR v1 uses logical pg_dump backups and retains up to ten years. The main database backup/SSD v2 articles do not describe the newer physical v2 Preview consistently with their old LTR restrictions.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Vaulted backup v2 is Preview: physical incremental disk snapshots for Flexible Server/Elastic Clusters, including Premium SSD v2, with retention 7 days to ten years. PostgreSQL 15+ on General Purpose/Memory Optimized and region/restore restrictions apply.

facts.label: File recovery and protection
facts.value: Not applicable to this managed database record: object versioning/locks/recovery.

facts.label: Hosting and license

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: PostgreSQL Single Server retired March 28, 2025. Its vaulted scheduled backups stopped on that date; retained recovery points still have storage charges, and Restore as Files remains available. Flexible Server remains the current offer.

facts.value: Zone-HA credits: 10% below 99.99% to 99%; 25% below 99% to 95%; 100% below 95%. Azure claims must reach Microsoft within 60 days with incident evidence.

facts.value: Lasting hosted SQL free tier for the lifetime of the Azure subscription, with monthly reset. Separate Azure-account USD $200 credit expires after 30 days; it is not this recurring SQL allowance.

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: Each free database/month: 100,000 vCore seconds, 32 GB data and 32 GB backups; up to ten databases/subscription. Unused vCore seconds do not roll over.

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: AutoPause-at-limit free configuration: maximum four vCores/32 GB, PITR seven days with local backup redundancy; no LTR, Data Sync, Elastic Jobs, DNS aliases, elastic pool or failover-group membership.

facts.label: Inactivity, pause and deletion
facts.value: Free databases auto-pause after 15 inactive minutes; the delay is fixed. An open session can prevent pause. AutoPause at monthly exhaustion makes the database inaccessible until the next calendar month.

facts.label: Inactivity, pause and deletion
facts.value: Paid-overage selection cannot be switched back to monthly-limit AutoPause. Leaving the free tier for another service tier is permanent for that database.

facts.label: Inactivity, pause and deletion
facts.value: No ordinary free/paid database deletion timer based only on low query activity was found. Service/offer suspension and explicit deletion remain separate policies.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: Verified low paid DTU configuration: Basic, 5 DTUs/2 GB included storage. East US retail meter B is USD $0.161 per day; database billing is hourly. No paid seat minimum is stated for this single database.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: PAYG pricing has no upfront long-term commitment; optional reservations/savings/Azure Hybrid Benefit have separate terms. Serverless does not support AHB or Azure Reservations discounts.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: USD retail calculations exclude taxes. MOSA says prices are tax-exclusive unless the invoice specifies otherwise; agreement/currency and negotiated prices can differ.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: A universal cheapest monthly paid bill was not established across DTU and pausable vCore models. Basic is a verified fixed-resource reference; a paused serverless database can have a lower retained-storage-only bill.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: East US GP Gen5 serverless: USD $0.521758 per billed vCore-hour; billed per second. Compute is max(min vCores, used vCores, min memory GB/3, used memory GB/3).

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: A documented max-four/min-0.5-vCore configuration has 2.1 GB minimum memory, giving a 0.7-vCore billing floor while online. Zero compute applies only while actually paused.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: GP storage East US USD $0.115/GB-month. GP/BC bill configured maximum data size plus 30% extra billable log storage; tempdb is included in compute.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Minimum storage descriptions differ: pricing says GP can configure 5 GB–4 TB, while the vCore/scaling docs allow 1 GB minimum in 1-GB increments.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: DTU compute/storage/I/O are bundled. DTU PITR backup storage has no extra charge; LTR is separate. Basic storage cannot exceed its 2 GB limit.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: East US PITR backup meters: LRS/ZRS USD $0.10/GB-month; RA-GRS/RA-GZRS $0.20/GB-month. GP/BC include backup capacity equal to configured maximum data size; excess bills separately.

facts.label: Billing meters

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: East US DTU Standard S0/S1: USD $0.4839/$0.9677 per day. Provisioned database compute bills each hour at the highest applicable tier/size, even if active for only part of the hour.

facts.value: Hyperscale uses allocated data storage (minimum 10 GB, up to 128 TB), no separate log-storage charge, and separately billed replica compute. API has distinct Gen5 serverless products at $0.378 and $0.585/vCore-hour; exact current product mapping was not settled.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: The API also exposes $0.20/million IO-operation meters for some GP/BC/Hyperscale products. Their current applicable charging scope was not established from the inspected pricing/cost docs.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Serverless GP auto-pause delay: 15–10,080 minutes, default 60; Hyperscale pause is Preview with minimum/default 60. Database login/activity resumes paused compute.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Pause needs zero sessions and zero user-workload CPU throughout the delay. Geo replication/failover groups, LTR, DNS aliases and use as an Elastic Jobs metadata database can prevent it.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: While paused, serverless compute cost is zero but storage remains. Provisioned/DTU databases continue charging while idle. Resuming can initially return error 40613; applications must retry.

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: Standard Azure egress applies: inbound and same-region service transfer free; North America/Europe Premium Global Network internet egress first 100 GB/month free, next 10 TB at USD $0.087/GB.

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: Outbound between North American regions or between European regions: USD $0.02/GB; from those continents to another continent: $0.05/GB. Egress during a qualifying Azure exit can use the documented support-credit process.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: SQL free AutoPause enforces the monthly free limit by making the database inaccessible until reset. BillOverUsage continues charging and is irreversible back to AutoPause.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: Cost Management budgets alert without stopping resources. Typical cost arrival is 8–24 hours and evaluation every 24 hours. Ordinary PAYG/commitment subscriptions have no credit spending-limit switch.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: DTU/resource exhaustion can throttle throughput or reject work. Database maximum size is configurable within tier limits; increasing it changes vCore storage billing. Hyperscale allocation grows with use.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Basic: 5 DTUs, 2 GB maximum/included data, 30 concurrent workers, 30 concurrent logins, 300 concurrent sessions. It provides less than one vCore and HDD-backed data storage.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Standard DTU maximum data size 1 TB; Premium 4 TB. GP/BC capacity depends on hardware/vCores; Hyperscale scales allocated storage from 10 GB up to 128 TB.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Logical server: up to 5,000 databases; default/maximum 250 logical servers per subscription/region in the published table. Subscription vCore quotas differ by offer and include serverless configured maxima.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Serverless compute/memory/IO limits depend on configured vCore range; an active database has a minimum bill even with zero user workload. Resource exhaustion throttles or rejects work.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: One universal app-facing SQL request/query-byte cap and included application connection-pool quota were not established.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: For ordinary rowstore data, the on-page row plus overhead is limited to 8,060 bytes. Large-object data and supported variable-width overflow can live off-page, so this is not a universal maximum logical record payload.

facts.label: Storage prices
facts.value: Not applicable to this managed SQL database record: independent file storage price.

facts.value: Not applicable to this managed SQL database record: file request/retrieval price.

facts.label: Minimum storage and early deletion
facts.value: Not applicable to this managed SQL database record: object minimum-size/retention fees.

facts.label: Vector/index limits
facts.value: Native VECTOR uses float32 by default: 1–1,998 dimensions. Float16 supports up to 3,996 dimensions and is GA in Azure SQL Database.

facts.label: Vector/index limits
facts.value: Latest DiskANN vector indexes require at least 100 non-NULL vectors; no partitioned vector indexes. Earlier-format index limitations differ and require drop/recreate to migrate.

facts.label: Vector/index limits
facts.value: A separate universal vector-count, namespace or metadata-byte quota was not found beyond normal database/type/storage constraints.

facts.label: Embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS uses an external model definition/endpoint. Database vector storage/search is separate from model execution, access credentials and provider/token charges.

facts.label: Embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: An included general embedding/reranking allowance, fixed model price and universal remote-model data-residency guarantee were not established.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: JA100/200/400/800 support 100/200/400/800 concurrent target connections. Excess targets queue. Agents, metadata DB and target DB resources are billed separately; S1+ metadata is recommended.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Job-step timeout defaults to 43,200 seconds (12 hours) and is configurable. T-SQL text uses nvarchar(max); CPU/RAM come from target databases, not a separately chosen 0.5-vCPU job instance.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: The SQL free tier requires an Azure account/subscription and works with most subscription types; Azure for Students Starter is excluded. Up to ten free databases per subscription.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: If using the introductory Azure free-account path, terms require phone, Microsoft/GitHub account and non-prepaid credit/debit card; Hong Kong/Brazil accept credit cards only.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Free SQL is recommended primarily for development/proof of concept and has no SLA. Explicit general commercial-production entitlement under that free tier, and one universal card rule across subscription programs, were not established.

facts.label: Primary type and other roles
facts.value: Researcher classification: managed relational SQL database, with vector search and optional scheduled SQL jobs. Single databases and elastic pools have different resource/billing scopes.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Native managed SQL, backups, automatic maintenance and SQL security. Native vector types/search are available; Elastic Jobs is a separately billed SQL-job service.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Included app-customer login MAU, independent uploaded-file storage and general JavaScript/Python function-hosting quotas were not established.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Native SQL/TDS connections through Microsoft SQL clients/drivers. The free-tier guide names .NET Microsoft.Data.SqlClient, Python mssql-python, sqlcmd, SSMS, VS Code and the portal query editor.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: SQL and Microsoft Entra authentication; database users/roles restrict privileges. Row-level security supports record filters/block predicates; authorization policies must be designed for the app.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Firewall/VNet/private-endpoint controls restrict network reachability. TLS encrypted TDS is enforced; current minimum TLS is 1.2. Validate the server certificate rather than trusting it unconditionally.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Transparent Data Encryption protects at rest; customer-managed keys and Always Encrypted offer separate key/data-use controls. Intel SGX enclave support has the dated migration notice in C04.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: Managed Microsoft SQL Database Engine with T-SQL. Microsoft updates the engine/service; database compatibility level and feature support differ from choosing a self-managed SQL Server release.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: DTU single databases: Basic, Standard, Premium. vCore: General Purpose, Business Critical, Hyperscale; serverless is Gen5 GP/Hyperscale only. Elastic pools share an allocation across databases.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: SQL transactions support multiple statements. READ COMMITTED is the default; Azure SQL Database defaults READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT to ON, giving statement-start row-versioned reads.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: Readable secondary replicas can lag the primary; read scale-out uses snapshot isolation and does not provide identical immediate read-after-write observations across endpoints.

facts.label: Test environments and branches
facts.value: Database copy creates a transactionally consistent, independent database on the same/different logical server. Hyperscale same-region snapshot copies can be fast; cross-region/redundancy changes can require a data copy.

facts.label: Test environments and branches
facts.value: No included copy-on-write branch count/lifetime or branch-specific tariff found.

facts.label: Test environments and branches
facts.value: Free databases cannot be copied until converted to a paid tier. Existing databases cannot be converted or restored into the free tier.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Built-in local HA is part of the database service; eligible tiers can enable zone redundancy. Basic/Standard lack the zone-redundant deployment option in the availability matrix.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Read scale-out is included for Premium/Business Critical HA replicas; Hyperscale can use separately configured readable replicas. GP/Basic/Standard are not assigned an included read-scale endpoint.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Active geo-replication supports up to four readable secondaries, asynchronously replicated and separately billed. Failover groups add coordinated failover/listener management under their conditions.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Existing SQL Data Sync can synchronize selected tables bidirectionally with Hub wins/Member wins policy and a configured interval. It is retiring and closed to subscriptions without prior use.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: A native disconnected-client read/write sync guarantee, durable app-client event quota and universal conflict-resolution mechanism beyond the named Data Sync feature were not established.

facts.label: Extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Native SQL indexing/search features include vector type/DiskANN approximate indexes, full-text search, SQL filtering and spatial data functions, subject to tier/feature restrictions. No arbitrary PostgreSQL/MySQL extension binary catalog applies.

facts.label: Upload and file limits
facts.value: Not applicable to this managed SQL database record: object upload limits.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Not applicable to this managed SQL database record: S3 object API compatibility.

facts.label: Delivery and private files
facts.value: Not applicable to this managed SQL database record: file delivery/private links/CDN.

facts.label: Filters and mixed search
facts.value: Exact vector distance and latest approximate VECTOR_SEARCH support SQL predicates; current indexes add iterative filtering and full DML. New queries use SELECT TOP (N) WITH APPROXIMATE; legacy TOP_N is deprecated.

facts.label: Filters and mixed search
facts.value: Microsoft documents SQL hybrid search combining full-text/vector queries and Reciprocal Rank Fusion. It is a SQL implementation pattern, not an independently priced search service or guaranteed relevance score.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: Elastic Jobs is a managed agent that runs T-SQL scripts in target SQL databases on demand/schedule. It needs a separate job metadata database; SQL Server Agent is a different service.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Default retries: ten after the initial attempt; initial delay one second, maximum delay 120 seconds, backoff multiplier 2.0. Final failures/timeouts are recorded in jobs.job_executions.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Docs require the author to make scripts idempotent: safe to run again with the same result. A guaranteed cross-failure exactly-once side effect, universal deduplication window or managed dead-letter queue was not established.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Jobs support recurring and one-time schedules; scheduling start/end times use UTC. Step order and per-pool max_parallelism can be configured.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: A queue-style maximum pending-message age/payload-retention promise was not found. The published command type is nvarchar(max), not a fixed product-wide message-byte limit.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Execution history is stored in jobs.job_executions and purged automatically after 45 days; sp_purge_jobhistory can remove newer history. Results can be written to a specified SQL output table.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Portal monitoring and Azure Alerts are available. An automatically idempotent failed-job replay contract or included unlimited diagnostic-log retention was not established.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Not applicable: Azure SQL Database is Microsoft-managed. SQL Server on a VM/on premises is a separate deployment requiring its own license, patching, backups and operations.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Choose a logical-server region; region/zone/compute features vary. Gen5 and regional matrices cover locations including East US, West Europe, UK South, Central India, Southeast Asia, Japan East and Australia East.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Free-tier Advanced configuration pins all free databases in a subscription to the first selected region. Geo-secondary databases and backup redundancy have separate location choices.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: DPA defines geographic at-rest/EU-boundary commitments and safeguards for international transfers. External AI models use their configured endpoint, which can add another processing location.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Export schema/data as BACPAC using SqlPackage or supported service tools. For consistency, stop writes or export a transactionally consistent copy; blob-export BACPAC limit is 200 GB.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Deleted databases can be restored within retained PITR history on the source server. Logical-server recovery is a separate Preview: soft-delete retention 1–7 days when enabled.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Without logical-server soft-delete protection, deleting the server removes its databases/PITR recovery path; retained LTR can restore elsewhere. Restoring a protected server still requires database restore and reconfiguration of dropped connections/security resources.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Subscription owners can cancel/delete Azure subscriptions subject to required waits/resource cleanup. Azure does not automatically delete the Azure account. DPA generally provides 90-day post-termination extraction plus up to another 90 days to delete, with exceptions.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Exact physical purge time for a particular deleted SQL database/server was not established. Recovery windows, immutable recent backups and contract retention do not define one uniform erasure clock.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Outside Hyperscale: full backups weekly, differential every 12/24 hours, log backups about every ten minutes depending on activity. Default PITR retention seven days; configurable 1–35, except Basic 1–7.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: PITR creates a new database rather than overwriting the original. Geo restore needs suitable geo-redundant backups; LRS/ZRS do not provide the same regional recovery option.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Automatic backup immutability protects up to the most recent seven days of PITR by default at no extra cost; not currently available for Hyperscale.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Optional LTR retains full backups up to ten years, with separate storage charges. Native free AutoPause mode has seven-day local PITR and no LTR.

facts.value: Current public service with a documented free tier and paid purchasing models. No acquisition or complete Azure SQL Database shutdown notice found in the inspected product, pricing and lifecycle pages.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: Same connection sees its own writes; reads on that replica move forward. Different connections/app instances may see older data because replication is asynchronous.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: Cross-instance read-after-write can pass replication_index from the write to the read; the replica waits locally until that position is applied. SDK support varies, with direct SQL API as a fallback.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: Writes execute on one active primary and commit to its WAL before storage upload. Upload happens every ten seconds or 4,096 changed-page frames, whichever is first; unuploaded writes can be lost in failover.

facts.label: Test environments and branches

facts.label: Test environments and branches

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Primary failure automatically promotes another primary and syncs from storage; failed-replica requests forward elsewhere. If storage and primary fail together, availability waits for storage recovery. Writes during a primary change have a documented 60-second timeout.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Read replicas are provisioned dynamically in configured regions and proxy writes to the primary. Their published storage charge applies only while serving traffic, by the hour.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Replication is server-to-server asynchronous SQL replication. A database-native app-change subscription API, disconnected-client writes and universal offline conflict resolution were not established.

facts.label: Extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Managed connection differences include WAL and fixed 4,096-byte pages, foreign-key enforcement on by default, and unsupported ATTACH DATABASE, CREATE TEMP TABLE, manual VACUUM/ANALYZE/checkpoint controls.

facts.label: Data access controls

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: PostgreSQL engine supports GRANT and row-level security. Policies need explicit configuration; owners normally bypass RLS unless forced. These are upstream PostgreSQL semantics, not a preconfigured app tenant policy.

facts.label: Data access controls

facts.label: Transactions and consistency

facts.label: Replicas and failover

facts.label: Data transfer costs

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: If transfer exceeds the fair-use amount, CloudAMQP gives 30 days to resolve the overage; afterward, additional traffic charges may appear on later invoices.

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: The exact fee for traffic above the fair-use allowance was not published on the current pricing page, FAQ, or Terms checked.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: Shared plans send warning emails at 70% and 100% of allowed usage. At the max connection limit, new connections are blocked; existing connections are not disconnected.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: Terms say usage above free limits requires purchase of additional resources or services; accounts may be suspended for overage use. The exact fee and any hard cutoff behavior beyond the shared-plan connection rule are not published.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Shared RabbitMQ and LavinMQ message quotas are counted per month; the quota resets on the first of each month.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: A counted shared-plan message event is either a message published to the broker or a message consumed from it. One publish-then-consume cycle therefore uses two quota units.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Shared plans have a maximum of 200 channels per connection and 200 consumers per channel.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Dedicated RabbitMQ plan throughput and connection figures are benchmarks, not guaranteed ceilings; actual results depend on broker, nodes, message size, routing, TLS, and publishers/consumers.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Dedicated LavinMQ plans list per-tier storage, connection, and queue limits rather than a monthly message quota. A single LavinMQ server can process hundreds of thousands of messages per second according to its broker FAQ.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: CloudAMQP does not charge for application execution time because it does not run the customer's workers; separate worker compute prices and concurrency limits are not applicable to the broker service.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Self-service setup is available through email, Google, or GitHub signup; an account is needed to create an instance.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Free shared instances require no billing information. Paid plans require a credit card to activate, with invoice or wire-transfer arrangements available by contacting billing.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: The free RabbitMQ plan is labelled for development and the free LavinMQ plan for development, prototypes, and small hobby projects. The pages checked do not clearly say whether free plans may be used for commercial production.

facts.label: Primary type and other roles
facts.value: Primary type: managed message queue and broker. It also supports stream queues and pub/sub messaging.

facts.label: Primary type and other roles
facts.value: CloudAMQP hosts the broker; application workers and business logic run in the customer's application environment.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: RabbitMQ and LavinMQ both provide message queues and broker functions; LavinMQ also supports streaming.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Both broker options include a management interface, alarms, and email support on shared and dedicated plans.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Monitoring, broker metrics, logs, and configurable alarms are provided for supported plans; some integrations and alarm types are dedicated-only.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Webhooks and external integrations can send alarms or metrics to services such as Slack, PagerDuty, Teams, and OpenTelemetry-compatible tools.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: The CloudAMQP pages checked describe broker, management, monitoring, and alarm features; they do not list app authentication, file storage, a relational database, or worker execution as included services.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: LavinMQ plans support AMQP 0-9-1, HTTP, MQTT, and WebSockets. LavinMQ does not implement AMQP 1.0 or STOMP.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Applications can use AMQP libraries; official code samples cover Ruby, Python, Celery, JavaScript, TypeScript, PHP, Java, Clojure, Go, Rust, .NET, and Crystal.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: CloudAMQP exposes a management HTTP API and remote RabbitMQ administration over TLS; SSH access to managed nodes is not available.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: TLS is available for broker connections. Customer-side TLS must be enabled to encrypt traffic between the application and broker.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Each instance uses broker credentials. Shared-plan vhosts separate queue namespaces on a multi-tenant broker; this is not the same as dedicated hardware.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Dedicated instances support IP firewall rules in AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud; dedicated VPC is a paid add-on.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: TLS protects traffic only when enabled by the customer application. Disk encryption at rest is enabled by default for service data on cloud platforms that support it; multi-node clusters can replicate message data across availability zones.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: CloudAMQP says it has SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliance material in its Trust Center; HIPAA customers may request a Business Associate Agreement.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: CloudAMQP manages the RabbitMQ or LavinMQ broker; it does not execute customer jobs. Customers connect their own workers using AMQP clients or supported protocols.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: Official examples cover Ruby, Python, Celery, JavaScript, TypeScript, PHP, Java, Clojure, Go, Rust, .NET, and Crystal; broker clients are also available from the wider AMQP ecosystems.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: RabbitMQ delivery can be at-most-once or at-least-once depending on queue durability, message persistence, publisher confirms, and consumer acknowledgements. It does not provide native exactly-once delivery.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: When a RabbitMQ consumer disconnects before acknowledging a message, unacknowledged messages can be requeued and delivered again.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: RabbitMQ supports retry and failure routing through acknowledgements, dead-letter exchanges, and message TTL. LavinMQ also supports dead-lettering, TTL, delayed exchanges, and message deduplication features.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: CloudAMQP added RabbitMQ Message Deduplication Plugin support for RabbitMQ 4.2 and 4.3 on October 14, 2026.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: RabbitMQ Little Lemur and Tough Tiger list a maximum idle queue time of 28 days. The current LavinMQ shared plan cards do not state a corresponding idle-queue-time limit.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Free-plan maximum messages held in queues are 10,000 for RabbitMQ Little Lemur and 20,000 for LavinMQ Loyal Lemming. Paid shared caps are 100,000 for RabbitMQ Tough Tiger and 200,000 for LavinMQ Elegant Ermine.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: RabbitMQ and LavinMQ accept messages up to 128 MiB on CloudAMQP; the limit is configurable.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Delayed work can be built with RabbitMQ message TTL plus dead-lettering, or a supported RabbitMQ delayed-message plugin; LavinMQ supports delayed exchanges. This is message delay, not a recurring calendar scheduler.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: The pages checked do not publish one maximum message-retention duration for dedicated queues. RabbitMQ TTL and queue policies can be configured; LavinMQ supports long queues, but no single hosted retention cap was stated.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: CloudAMQP broker logs are size-based, with at least six weeks of history stated in the FAQ.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Dedicated instances can download broker logs; log integrations can send logs to external systems.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Dedicated RabbitMQ automatically backs up broker definitions, but not message contents. Messages must be protected through broker durability, persistence, replication, and the customer's recovery design.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: CloudAMQP does not publish an execution-run history or job replay interface because it hosts a message broker rather than a workflow runner. Replay depends on broker type and queue/stream configuration.

apps.news: News check 2026-11-09: no sale, shutdown, rebrand, or data-exposure incident found for Durable Objects.

facts.label: free offer type
facts.value: Recurring Workers Free allowances for SQLite Durable Objects; daily compute/operation quotas and retained account storage. This is not only a time-limited trial or self-hosted software.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: Workers Free: 100,000 Durable Object requests/day; 13,000 GB-s duration/day, account allocations. Daily quotas reset at 00:00 UTC.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: Workers Free SQLite: 5 million rows read/day, 100,000 rows written/day, 5 GB stored/account. Maximum 100 Durable Object classes/account; individual objects are not subject to a fixed count cap.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: Free per-object storage disagrees within the limits page: main table says 10 GB, subject to Free's 5 GB account cap; storage-full FAQ says Free 1 GB/object.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: Idle objects can hibernate or be evicted and restart on a later event; RAM state is lost, persisted storage remains. Hibernatable idle objects typically hibernate after about 10 seconds.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: No fixed Free inactivity-to-data-deletion deadline was found. Developer terms allow, but do not promise, content access for up to 30 days after trial/subscription termination and disclaim an obligation to retain it.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: Workers Paid minimum USD 5/account/month; includes monthly allocations for Durable Objects and other named Workers services. It is not USD 5 per Durable Object.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: Published Self-Serve prices exclude applicable taxes unless stated otherwise; taxes may be added. No annual prepayment or seat minimum is stated for the USD 5 Workers Paid path.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Paid Durable Object compute: 1 million requests/month included, then USD 0.15/million; 400,000 GB-s/month included, then USD 12.50/million GB-s.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Compute overage is rounded up to the next billing unit after the included allocation. The page explicitly rounds 500,000 excess GB-s up to 1 million GB-s.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Duration uses wall-clock active/non-hibernatable time and a billed allocation of 128 MB per object, regardless of actual memory use. Simultaneous requests on one object share its elapsed active time.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: HTTP requests, RPC sessions and alarm invocations count as DO requests. Opening a WebSocket counts once; incoming WebSocket messages receive a 20:1 billing ratio; outgoing messages and protocol pings are uncharged.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Paid SQLite storage: 25 billion rows read/month included, then USD 0.001/million; 50 million rows written/month included, then USD 1/million; 5 GB-month included, then USD 0.20/GB-month.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Rows scanned can exceed rows returned; index maintenance adds written rows. setAlarm() adds a row write. Retained SQLite metadata remains billable until deleteAll(), even after deleting user records.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Legacy key-value Paid: 1 million read units/month included then USD 0.20/million; 1 million writes then USD 1/million; 1 million delete requests then USD 1/million; 1 GB storage included then USD 0.20/GB-month.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Legacy reads/writes round each key's data into 4 KB units. Deletes are counted per key/delete regardless of size; the worked delete example is charged, despite the ambiguous phrase 'Delete requests are unmetered.'

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: A calling Worker has its own request/CPU charges: Paid includes 10 million requests and 30 million CPU-ms/month, then USD 0.30/million requests and USD 0.02/million CPU-ms. Worker wall time is not the DO duration meter.

facts.label: idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: No DO duration charge when idle and eligible for hibernation, including the period before actual hibernation. Standard WebSocket accept() keeps duration running for the connection; Hibernation API avoids that idle duration.

facts.label: idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Pending I/O, timers and unfinished requests can prevent hibernation. A pending I/O operation can keep the object alive and billed for up to 15 minutes; later operations can extend activity.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: Workers Paid pricing expressly states no additional data-transfer egress or bandwidth-throughput charges. DO's own page lists compute/storage and no separate region-transfer tariff.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: On Free, exceeding a meter makes further operations of that type fail; daily limits reset at 00:00 UTC. Paid excess usage is billed at the published rates.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: CPU limits can bound an invocation, but a guaranteed account-wide dollar cap covering DO requests, duration and retained storage was not found.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Paid SQLite: 10 GB/object, unlimited storage per account/class subject to object caps; 500 classes/account. Free has 5 GB/account and 100 classes; per-object Free size is conflicting under C10.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: SQLite key plus value combined: 2 MB. SQL row/string/BLOB: 2 MB; 100 columns/table; SQL statement 100 KB; 100 bound parameters; 32 function arguments; LIKE/GLOB patterns 50 bytes.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: One object is inherently single-threaded with a soft 1,000 requests/second limit; overload can queue and then return an error. No traditional SQL connection pool is exposed by its storage API.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: SQLite request CPU: 30 seconds default, configurable to 5 minutes; 6 simultaneous outgoing connections/request. Received WebSocket messages max 32 MiB; outbound fetch request body 100 MiB by default.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Legacy key-value: default 50 GB/account, increase by request; no per-object/class storage cap stated. Keys max 2 KiB, values 128 KiB. Paid access restrictions still apply.

facts.label: storage prices
facts.value: Not applicable to the scoped Durable Objects service.

facts.label: file request and retrieval prices
facts.value: Not applicable to the scoped Durable Objects service.

facts.label: minimum storage and early deletion
facts.value: Not applicable to the scoped Durable Objects service.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: Not applicable as a dedicated vector-store plan. No native vector-index dimensions/capacity are assigned to Durable Objects in the inspected storage API.

facts.label: embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: No bundled embedding/reranking service in the scoped Durable Objects tariff; external model or Vectorize usage would need separate sourcing and billing.

facts.label: run limits and pricing
facts.value: Alarm handlers max 15 minutes wall time; object CPU defaults to 30 seconds and can be raised to 5 minutes. Fixed 128 MB billed allocation/object; one alarm handler at a time per object.

facts.label: run limits and pricing
facts.value: Each alarm invocation, including a retry, is a DO request and consumes active wall-clock duration; each setAlarm() is a SQLite row write or legacy KV write unit.

facts.label: run limits and pricing
facts.value: Waiting for a future alarm while hibernated does not incur active duration. In-handler network waiting/pending I/O can remain billed, even though it does not consume CPU seconds.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: SQLite-backed Durable Objects do not require a paid Workers plan. Legacy key-value storage requires Workers Paid and an eligible existing legacy namespace.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Self-Serve terms prohibit processing or collecting personal/business credit-card information on web properties receiving Free Services. Protected health information requires written consent.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Whether Free signup requires a card, a complete country restriction list, and an explicit Durable Objects Free commercial-production permission were not established.

facts.label: primary type and other roles
facts.value: Our classification: managed stateful compute with private SQLite/key-value databases; real-time coordination and native scheduled jobs are secondary roles.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: Native persistent object storage, executing application code, RPC/HTTP handlers, WebSockets and alarms. App login, general file buckets, vector indexes and durable multi-step workflows are not bundled by this Durable Objects offer.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Workers bindings address a namespace/object; HTTP fetch, RPC methods and WebSockets provide app-facing access. Storage API is private inside the object; this is not a Postgres/MySQL TCP endpoint.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: JavaScript/TypeScript examples are documented in Getting started. Cloudflare also officially supports defining Durable Objects in Python.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Storage is private to one object. Application code and Worker bindings control access; row/user authorization must be implemented by the app rather than assumed from an SQL role or public storage URL.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Durable Object management permissions follow the implementing Worker's roles. Metadata Read-Only exposes metrics/logs/traces; Data Studio requires at least Editor access and can modify SQL data.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Object data and metadata are automatically encrypted at rest with Cloudflare-managed keys; internal object/Worker transfers and API/Wrangler access use TLS.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: New SQLite-backed objects offer SQL plus synchronous/asynchronous key-value APIs over private embedded SQLite. Legacy key-value-backed objects offer asynchronous KV and alarms, without SQL or PITR.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: Exact deployed SQLite engine version and a customer-selectable engine upgrade/version policy were not established.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Storage is strongly consistent and transactional within one object. Individual storage methods are implicitly atomic/isolated; explicit transaction and transactionSync APIs group operations.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Single-threaded execution does not make arbitrary application awaits a global transaction. Consume SQL cursors synchronously before awaiting; an open cursor can otherwise observe later writes that eventually roll back.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Wrangler supports local development; named deployment environments have distinct Durable Object namespaces and data. Remote staging storage consumes the same account's applicable allocations.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Native copy-on-write database branching or automatic production-data cloning was not established.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Cloudflare manages object restarts/failover; committed storage survives process eviction. Storage API notes alarms may be delayed up to a minute during maintenance/failover.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: A customer-configurable read-replica topology, exact replica count/locations and contractual DO-specific RPO/RTO were not established.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: WebSockets support live bidirectional client coordination. The Hibernation API preserves connected clients while the object sleeps; RAM is reconstructed on wake and attachments can preserve connection metadata.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: A native durable offline client write queue, automatic conflict merging and complete offline sync protocol were not established.

facts.label: extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: SQLite supports FTS5 full-text search including fts5vocab, JSON functions/operators and math functions, within its documented SQLite subset.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: Not applicable to the scoped Durable Objects service.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Not applicable to the scoped Durable Objects service.

facts.label: delivery and private files
facts.value: Not applicable to the scoped Durable Objects service.

facts.label: filters and mixed search
facts.value: SQL filters and FTS5 keyword search are covered under D08. A native dense/sparse/hybrid vector-search product is outside this scoped offer.

facts.label: execution model and languages
facts.value: Native managed alarm handlers execute the Durable Object's application code; the alarm guide uses JavaScript/TypeScript. Python Durable Objects are also officially offered, but full Python alarm API parity was not independently established here.

facts.label: delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Alarms guarantee at-least-once execution; uncaught exceptions trigger exponential backoff starting at 2 seconds, up to 6 retries. Only one alarm() runs at once per object.

facts.label: delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Retries apply to the latest setAlarm(); after exhaustion the alarm stops unless application logic reschedules. Calling deleteAlarm() during a handler can prevent retries only on a best-effort basis.

facts.label: schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Each object has one pending alarm timestamp, in Unix epoch milliseconds; setAlarm() replaces it. Multiple or recurring events require storing a schedule and rescheduling the next alarm in application code.

facts.label: schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Maximum future scheduling horizon and a distinct pending-alarm/job-payload retention duration were not found. Job payload normally lives in the object's storage and inherits D03 record/size limits.

facts.label: logs and run history
facts.value: DO logs use opt-in Workers Logs through the implementing Worker; metrics include request/storage/duration analytics. Shared logs are not automatically a persistent per-job result store.

facts.label: logs and run history
facts.value: Current Workers Logs: Free 200,000 events/day retained 3 days; Paid 20 million/month included then USD 0.60/million, retained 7 days. The docs announce a pricing change on December 1, 2026.

facts.label: logs and run history
facts.value: A built-in alarm run-history retention period, result-artifact store, dead-letter inbox and one-click failed-job replay were not established.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Not applicable to operating the Cloudflare-hosted service. Local Wrangler development is available, but is not a self-hosted production Durable Objects edition with a published minimum server shape.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Jurisdiction constraints eu, us and fedramp restrict object execution and persistence to the chosen jurisdiction. Calling Workers can still run elsewhere; object IDs can be logged outside that jurisdiction for billing/debugging.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Default placement is near the first request; location hints are best effort and only affect initial placement. Objects currently do not relocate automatically after creation.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Object code can read SQL results or iterate key-value data and implement an export path. A supported downloadable complete SQLite database/export command was not found.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: deleteAll() removes the private SQLite database contents atomically. From compatibility date 2026-02-24 it also deletes the active alarm; earlier dates need deleteAlarm() or the compatibility flag.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Class deletion removes the namespace's data through the documented class lifecycle configuration. SQLite and legacy-KV storage cannot simply be switched in place; an automatic legacy-KV-to-SQLite migration is still described as future work.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: DPA requires deletion or return of processed personal data at customer choice on termination/expiry/completion. No DO-specific physical purge deadline for backups or complete account deletion timetable was found.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: SQLite objects have point-in-time recovery to any point in the previous 30 days, covering SQL and hidden KV data. API uses bookmarks/timestamps and schedules restoration for the next object session.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Legacy key-value objects do not have the SQLite PITR API. The published DO tariff lists no separately priced PITR SKU.

facts.label: file recovery and protection
facts.value: Not applicable to the scoped Durable Objects service.

facts.label: identity and old names
facts.value: Cloudflare Durable Objects, a Cloudflare Developer Platform service; official product documentation is the directory URL.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: Cloudflare-hosted managed service under its Self-Serve Subscription Agreement and Developer Platform terms. No production self-hosted Durable Objects service edition identified.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Active public offer; SQLite storage and SQL API are generally available, on Workers Free and Paid. No whole-product shutdown, sunset or acquisition notice found in the inspected current product docs and changelog notice.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Since July 9, 2026, accounts without an existing key-value-backed namespace cannot create one. Existing legacy users retain access; new users should use SQLite.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Published SQLite billing notice targets January 7, 2026, no earlier; current API pages still describe January 2026 in future tense. Actual first billing date was not independently established.

facts.label: vendor home and main markets
facts.value: Operator Cloudflare, Inc.; privacy policy lists a San Francisco, California, United States contact address. Complete customer-country eligibility is not established by that address.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: Community and developer Discord are the Free technical-help routes; Free support cases are limited to account, billing and registrar issues. General support docs offer support cases on paid plans, with response terms depending on the actual plan.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: Public operational notices: Cloudflare System Status. No DO-specific numeric uptime SLA or guaranteed technical-response time attached to the Free/USD 5 path was found.

facts.value: Workers Paid: first 1,000,000 standard operations per account billing month included, then $0.40 per additional million operations. Queue pricing page uses $; Workers plan page labels USD.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: A Queue above the first 10,000 on Workers Paid costs $0.10 per additional queue per month; default account limit is 10,000 and can be increased.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: One operation is charged for each 64 KB (64,000 bytes) written, read, or deleted; 65 KB and 127 KB each count as two chunks per action.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Message sizes include about 100 bytes of internal metadata, and metadata counts toward the 128 KB message cap.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: A message under 64 KB normally incurs one write, one read, and one delete when successfully delivered and acknowledged: three Queue operations total.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Operations are counted per message, not per batch; a processed batch of 10 small messages has 10 writes, 10 reads, and 10 deletes.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Each retry adds a read per 64 KB message chunk; retrying a batch of 10 small messages adds 10 read operations for that retry.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: A failed message routed to a DLQ incurs an additional write per 64 KB chunk; Cloudflare's example of three retries plus a fourth failed attempt counts five reads.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: A message that expires before being read incurs a write and delete per 64 KB chunk; it has no read operation.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Pull requests to an empty queue incur a read operation; push consumers on an empty queue are not invoked and incur no empty-batch read.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Purging a queue is one billable Queue operation regardless of how many stored messages are deleted.

facts.label: Billing meters

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Retrying a message adds a billable read; Worker retries also invoke and bill the Worker under Workers usage.

facts.label: Primary type and other roles
facts.value: Supports Cloudflare event subscriptions and R2 event notifications as message sources; neither changes the product into object storage.

facts.value: Producers can publish individual messages or batches; workers can send from request handlers or Durable Objects.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Supports retry and delayed delivery, including a configurable retry delay and one-time message delay.

facts.value: Event subscriptions can publish selected Cloudflare service events to Queues; the Free-plan announcement says event subscriptions are included.

facts.value: Queues is a message buffer, not a database, identity service, file store, or general-purpose code runner. Workers or an external HTTP consumer perform the application work.

facts.value: Maximum producer sendBatch is 100 messages or 256 KB total, whichever limit is reached first.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Push-consumer batch timeout defaults to 5 seconds and can be set from 0 to 60 seconds; whichever batch-size or timeout threshold is reached first triggers delivery.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Per-queue throughput is capped at 5,000 messages per second; sends above the limit return Too Many Requests until rate drops. Multiple queues can scale total throughput.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Per-queue unconsumed backlog cap is 25 GB; sending at the cap returns Storage Limit Exceeded.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Recurring schedules are not published as a Queues feature in the queue overview, configuration, and delay pages checked; delay is one time.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Queue metrics include backlog bytes/count, oldest-message time, average consumer concurrency, billable operations, bytes, lag, and retry count.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Metrics are available in the Cloudflare dashboard and programmatically through GraphQL/HTTP; recent backlog fields are also available through Queue REST and JavaScript APIs.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Queue audit logs record configuration changes such as create/delete queue and attach/remove consumer; they are always enabled.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: DLQ messages can be inspected and processed by configuring a consumer on the DLQ; this is manual recovery, not a one-click replay promise.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: No Queue-specific message-level execution-history or metrics-retention period was found in Queue Metrics, Audit Logs, and API docs checked.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Worker consumer logs are Workers Logs, a separate Workers feature and pricing/retention meter; they are not a Queues operation allowance.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Default queues store and process messages across Cloudflare's global network; there is no individual region selector in this default mode.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Optional jurisdiction eu restricts storage and processing to the European Union.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Optional jurisdiction us restricts storage and processing to the United States.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Optional jurisdiction fedramp restricts storage and processing to FedRAMP-Moderate data centers.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: A jurisdiction must be set when a queue is created and cannot be added, changed, or removed later; a DLQ must use the same jurisdiction.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Workers can produce to or consume from a jurisdiction-restricted queue from any location; the jurisdiction limits where Queues stores and processes messages.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Messages can be pulled through the HTTP API and acknowledged by the client; this is the documented route for reading messages into an external system.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Purge permanently removes queued messages and is irreversible; in-flight messages may still be processed and messages arriving during purge may remain.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Without a DLQ, messages at the retry limit are permanently deleted; unconsumed messages on a DLQ with no active consumer expire after four days.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Cloudflare's Developer Platform terms say Customer Content may be accessible for up to 30 days after trial/subscription end, but Cloudflare has no obligation to retain it after termination.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: No Queue-specific backup snapshot, bulk export format, or recovery point schedule was found in Queue docs and Developer Platform terms checked.

facts.label: Identity and old names
facts.value: Cloudflare Queues; managed message queue in Cloudflare's Developer Platform.

facts.label: Identity and old names
facts.value: No former product name or successor is identified in the Queue docs, product changelog, or Cloudflare Queues blog tag checked.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Cloudflare operates the hosted Queue service; deployment is managed in a Cloudflare account.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: No self-hosted Queues edition or software license is offered in the Queue docs; software license field is not applicable to this hosted service.

facts.value: Active and generally available (GA), not a beta service.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Latest product-level lifecycle change reviewed: queues can be restricted to EU, US, or FedRAMP-Moderate jurisdictions; announced October 12, 2026.

facts.value: Queues became available on Workers Free on February 4, 2026, with 10,000 daily operations and 24-hour Free retention.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: No closure, sunset, or acquisition notice for Queues was identified in the product changelogs, Queues blog tag, Cloudflare acquisitions blog tag, or press-release newsroom checked.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Status page listed Queues as Operational at check time; the page showed incidents on 2 of the last 30 days and 4 of the last 90 days.

facts.label: Vendor home and main markets
facts.value: Privacy Policy names Cloudflare, Inc. and gives its address in San Francisco, California, USA.

facts.label: Vendor home and main markets
facts.value: Complete country-by-country market availability for Queues is not published on the product overview, pricing, or data-location pages checked.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Free plan users are directed to Cloudflare Community and Discord for technical help; Free users can open cases only for billing, account, and registrar issues.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Paid plans can submit support cases; Business and Enterprise also have live chat, and Enterprise has emergency phone support.

facts.value: Support docs state Free, Pro, and Business have no contractual SLA; Queue-specific uptime SLA was not found in Queue docs or Developer Platform terms checked.
