facts.value: Public status page has a Queues component and is the vendor's current service-status source.

apps.name: Cloudflare R2
apps.line: S3-compatible object storage with no egress fees.

free.text: Free each month: 10 GB-month, 1M writes, 10M reads

cells.regions: Auto, 6 hints

sql.math: Does not provide a database.
Does not provide a database.

files.math: (100 GB − 10 GB free) × $0.015 a GB a month. 100,000 writes and 1 million reads fit within the free allowances. Outbound data (egress) costs $0.

jobs.math: Does not run jobs.

facts.label: Free offer type
facts.value: Recurring monthly no-cost usage for R2 Standard storage and operations; it is not presented as a time-limited R2 trial.

facts.label: General free-service terms
facts.value: Cloudflare's agreement says free or trial services may end at the end of a trial, when paid service starts, or when Cloudflare terminates the free service. R2's pricing page separately describes monthly included usage.

facts.label: Free offer production scope
facts.value: Pricing applies to R2 usage generally, but no explicit sentence was found saying whether every free-tier workload is permitted for commercial production. Production custom-domain delivery is documented separately.

facts.label: Standard free storage
facts.value: 10 GB-month per month in Standard storage. Storage usage is measured as average daily storage over a 30-day billing period.

facts.label: Standard free Class A
facts.value: 1 million Class A requests per month.

facts.label: Standard free Class B
facts.value: 10 million Class B requests per month.

facts.label: Free egress
facts.value: Internet egress is free for R2 Standard and Infrequent Access; included free egress has no numeric monthly cap in the R2 pricing table.

facts.label: Infrequent Access free use
facts.value: No free storage, Class A, Class B, or retrieval allowance is listed for Infrequent Access. The Standard allowance does not apply to IA.

facts.label: Account bucket allowance
facts.value: First 100,000 buckets per account are included across storage classes; each additional bucket is $0.10 per month.

facts.label: Idle storage behavior
facts.value: R2 has no compute instance to sleep or wake. Object storage remains until deleted or affected by a configured lifecycle rule or a service/account action.

facts.label: Inactivity pause or expiry
facts.value: No automatic inactivity-based bucket sleep, pause, or data-expiry interval was found in R2 pricing, limits, lifecycle, or terms pages checked.

facts.label: Failed payment
facts.value: Cloudflare may suspend R2 access after payment failure; requests can error while data remains secure. If payment details are not updated within 30 days, data associated with usage-based services may be deleted.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: No fixed R2 plan fee is shown. R2 is usage-based with recurring included Standard usage; charges begin when the applicable allowance is exceeded.

facts.label: Price change and cancellation terms
facts.value: The agreement permits price changes with at least 30 days' notice. It says fees are nonrefundable; ongoing usage-based access may end on cancellation rather than continue to a prepaid term end.

facts.label: Plan and tax conditions
facts.value: R2 rates are shown in USD. The price page does not state a regional price split or tax-inclusive total; tax depends on billing profile and jurisdiction.

facts.label: Standard storage meter
facts.value: $0.015 per GB-month after the included Standard allowance. A GB-month is based on average daily storage over a 30-day billing period.

facts.label: Infrequent Access storage meter
facts.value: $0.01 per GB-month, plus the separate IA operation and retrieval charges below.

facts.label: Standard Class A meter
facts.value: $4.50 per million requests after the Standard free quota. Includes writes, lists, copies, multipart operations, bucket configuration writes, and Standard-to-IA transitions.

facts.label: IA Class A meter
facts.value: $9.00 per million requests.

facts.label: Standard Class B meter
facts.value: $0.36 per million requests after the Standard free quota. Includes reads and selected bucket/configuration reads.

facts.label: IA Class B meter
facts.value: $0.90 per million requests.

facts.label: IA retrieval meter
facts.value: $0.01 per GB retrieved from Infrequent Access, including object reads and copies.

facts.label: Free operations
facts.value: DeleteObject, DeleteBucket, and AbortMultipartUpload are listed as free operations.

facts.label: Billing unit rounding
facts.value: Cloudflare rounds each billable quantity up to the next billing unit: million requests, GB-month, or GB retrieved.

facts.label: Failed and denied requests
facts.value: Authentication or authorization failures are not charged. Authenticated requests that fail later can count; documented examples include conditional PUT returning 412 and bad digest returning 400.

facts.label: Additional bucket fee
facts.value: $0.10 per bucket per month above the first 100,000 account buckets.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Not applicable: R2 is object storage and does not provide an R2 compute instance to pause or scale to zero. Workers that use R2 are a separate service.

facts.label: Egress to the public internet
facts.value: $0 R2 egress for both storage classes. Direct egress through the S3 API, Workers API, or r2.dev is free.

facts.label: Connected product charges
facts.value: Other metered services connected to an R2 bucket may charge their own fees. Workers request/CPU charges are separate from R2 storage and operation charges.

facts.label: Inbound transfer fee
facts.value: The R2 pricing page lists storage, operations, retrieval, and egress but no separate R2 upload-ingress rate.

facts.label: Cross-region transfer rate
facts.value: No separate R2 cross-region transfer rate was found in R2 pricing or data-location documentation.

facts.label: Quota and overage behavior
facts.value: The Standard free allowance is included monthly; paid usage above it is billed using R2's usage meters. The listed bucket-count limit defaults to 100,000 and additional buckets have a published fee.

facts.label: Spend alert
facts.value: Pay-as-you-go accounts can set an account-wide USD budget alert for combined usage-based products. The alert sends one email per period after threshold crossing.

facts.label: Spend cap and automatic cutoff
facts.value: Budget alerts are informational and do not pause or cap usage. No R2-specific hard spending cap or automatic cutoff at a chosen spend value was found.

facts.label: Default budget-alert rollout
facts.value: Cloudflare said it was rolling out a default $10 account-level alert to eligible pay-as-you-go accounts, in cohorts; the rollout notice says the default alert is informational.

facts.label: Standard storage price
facts.value: USD $0.015 per GB-month. Standard is the default class for a newly created bucket unless another default is chosen.

facts.label: Infrequent Access storage price
facts.value: USD $0.01 per GB-month.

facts.label: Regional price split
facts.value: The public R2 storage table does not list different rates for automatic placement, location hints, or EU/US jurisdictions.

facts.label: Standard request prices
facts.value: Standard Class A: USD $4.50/million; Class B: USD $0.36/million. Monthly allowances are 1M A and 10M B.

facts.label: Infrequent Access request prices
facts.value: IA Class A: USD $9.00/million; Class B: USD $0.90/million.

facts.label: Class A examples
facts.value: PutObject, CopyObject, ListObjects, multipart operations, bucket configuration writes, and lifecycle Standard-to-IA transition are Class A examples.

facts.label: Class B and free-operation examples
facts.value: GetObject, HeadObject, and selected bucket reads are Class B; DeleteObject, DeleteBucket, and AbortMultipartUpload are free operations.

facts.label: IA retrieval fee
facts.value: USD $0.01 per GB retrieved, including reads or copies of IA objects.

facts.label: Minimum size and billing unit
facts.value: R2 storage is metered in GB-months using average daily storage over a 30-day billing period. The pricing and storage-class pages do not state a minimum billable object size.

facts.label: Standard minimum duration
facts.value: No minimum storage duration is listed for Standard.

facts.label: IA minimum duration
facts.value: Infrequent Access has a 30-day minimum; deleting, moving, or replacing earlier does not avoid the remaining minimum charge.

facts.label: Signup and starting access
facts.value: Requires a Cloudflare account and an R2 subscription enabled through the dashboard checkout flow. R2's published monthly free allowance is available without a stated trial end date. No signup was submitted.

facts.label: Payment method
facts.value: Cloudflare terms say a credit card is required for paid services, while newer billing setup docs require a primary payment method and list cards, PayPal, wallets, and US instant bank payments. The newer setup page indicates card is not the only current method.

facts.label: Acceptable use
facts.value: The general agreement prohibits unlawful content, intellectual-property infringement, malicious code, phishing, spam, and other technical abuse. It requires users to comply with applicable laws and sanctions restrictions.

facts.label: Trial length and credits
facts.value: No R2-specific time-limited trial or expiring credit was listed on the R2 pricing or start pages checked. The offer is described as free monthly usage.

facts.label: Country eligibility
facts.value: A complete country-by-country R2 signup eligibility list was not found. Cloudflare's billing page lists payment methods, but that is not a full R2 country availability list.

facts.label: Commercial use
facts.value: Public R2 pages do not describe the recurring free allowance as development-only. Production public delivery is supported using custom domains; the r2.dev URL is explicitly for non-production.

facts.label: Primary type
facts.value: Hosted object storage for unstructured data, stored as objects in buckets.

facts.label: Other roles and scope
facts.value: S3-compatible storage API, public file origin, and storage for apps. R2 is a storage product; Workers is an optional compute/runtime product that can call it.

facts.label: Included file capabilities
facts.value: R2 includes object buckets, S3-compatible access, lifecycle rules, bucket locks, CORS configuration, and optional per-request access logs.

facts.label: Workers relationship
facts.value: R2 can be accessed from a Worker binding, but it can also be used through S3-compatible API, Cloudflare REST API, CLI, or dashboard. A Workers plan is not required just to store or access objects through those other routes.

facts.label: R2 Data Catalog
facts.value: R2 Data Catalog is an additional Iceberg catalog feature with its own operation and compaction meters, billed in addition to normal R2 storage and operations.

facts.label: Storage API options
facts.value: Three published API surfaces: Workers API, S3-compatible HTTP API, and Cloudflare REST API. Dashboard and Wrangler CLI are also documented management paths.

facts.label: S3 endpoint and region setting
facts.value: Standard endpoint is https://<ACCOUNT_ID>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com; the S3 region setting is auto. Empty region and us-east-1 alias to auto for tools that require a region.

facts.label: SDK and tool options
facts.value: S3-compatible SDKs and tools can be used by changing the endpoint. Official docs provide JavaScript and Python examples and point to Go, Java, PHP, Ruby, and Rust examples; Wrangler and rclone are documented.

facts.label: Browser uploads and downloads
facts.value: Presigned URLs allow a backend to grant temporary object-level access without giving the client API credentials. Browser use still needs an appropriate CORS policy.

facts.label: Presigned URL limits
facts.value: Presigned URL expiry is from 1 second to 7 days. Supported methods are GET, HEAD, PUT, and DELETE; HTML-form POST is not currently supported.

facts.label: Default access
facts.value: Buckets are private by default. Public access requires an explicit change, using a custom domain or the Cloudflare-managed r2.dev URL.

facts.label: API credentials
facts.value: R2 API tokens support Admin Read/Write, Admin Read Only, Object Read/Write, and Object Read Only. Object tokens can be scoped to buckets; temporary credentials can narrow access to objects or prefixes.

facts.label: Temporary credential lifetime
facts.value: Temporary credentials can last up to 604,800 seconds, or seven days, and inherit no more permission than their parent token.

facts.label: Encryption at rest
facts.value: All objects and metadata are encrypted at rest automatically. Cloudflare manages the default keys; R2 uses AES-256 with GCM as its preferred mode.

facts.label: Encryption in transit
facts.value: R2 client transfers use TLS/SSL. For a custom domain, plaintext HTTP can be disabled by enabling Always Use HTTPS.

facts.label: Customer-provided encryption key
facts.value: R2 documents Server-Side Encryption with Customer-Provided Keys (SSE-C). Cloudflare cannot recover object bodies if the customer loses the key.

facts.label: AWS-managed encryption headers
facts.value: The R2 S3 compatibility matrix marks AWS SSE/SSE-KMS headers as unsupported for relevant upload operations; use R2 default encryption or documented SSE-C.

facts.label: Public domain security
facts.value: A custom domain can use Cloudflare Cache and separate access controls. The r2.dev URL is rate-limited and lacks custom-domain WAF rules, access controls, caching controls, and bot management features.

facts.label: Browser-origin controls
facts.value: CORS configuration supports public buckets and presigned URL workflows. CORS does not itself grant permission to a private object.

facts.label: Maximum object size
facts.value: Limit table states up to 5 TiB/object and its footnote clarifies maximum is 5 GiB below 5 TiB, or 4.995 TiB.

facts.label: Single-part upload size
facts.value: Limit table states 5 GiB for a single-part upload; its footnote clarifies the effective maximum is 5 MiB less, or 4.995 GiB.

facts.label: Multipart uploads
facts.value: Multipart upload supports up to 10,000 parts and 5 TiB nominal object size, with resumable and parallel part uploads.

facts.label: Multipart part size
facts.value: Parts are 5 MiB to 5 GiB; the final part may be smaller than 5 MiB. All non-final parts must use the same size.

facts.label: Multipart expiry
facts.value: Incomplete multipart uploads are automatically aborted after seven days by default; a custom lifecycle policy can change this behavior.

facts.label: Key and metadata limits
facts.value: Object key length: 1,024 bytes. Object metadata: 8,192 bytes.

facts.label: S3 compatibility
facts.value: R2 implements an S3-compatible API at the account endpoint. Its current operation matrix marks support per API and feature; compatibility is not full AWS S3 parity.

facts.label: API compatibility gaps
facts.value: Current matrix marks S3 bucket versioning operations and AWS Object Lock configuration unsupported. R2's own bucket-lock feature is separate and supported.

facts.label: S3 operation behavior
facts.value: Common object operations include Get, Head, Put, Copy, Delete, List, and multipart endpoints, but conditional headers, checksum variants, owner headers, and encryption features vary by operation.

facts.label: S3 region parameter
facts.value: S3 clients should use region auto; empty region and us-east-1 are compatibility aliases.

facts.label: Public/private default
facts.value: Buckets are private by default. Public read access must be explicitly enabled through a custom domain or a r2.dev development URL.

facts.label: Private temporary links
facts.value: Presigned GET, HEAD, PUT, and DELETE URLs support temporary access for 1 second to 7 days and do not expose the API secret to the recipient.

facts.label: Custom domain and cache
facts.value: Custom domains expose objects through a domain controlled by the customer and can use Cloudflare Cache. Up to 100 custom domains are allowed per bucket.

facts.label: r2.dev limitations
facts.value: The managed r2.dev URL is rate-limited and intended for non-production use. It does not offer the custom-domain WAF, access-control, cache-control, and bot-management features.

facts.label: CORS and browser use
facts.value: CORS is configurable per bucket. Browser access using presigned URLs still needs the bucket CORS policy to permit the page origin and request.

facts.label: Egress and delivery fees
facts.value: R2 direct internet egress is free. Custom-domain requests may also use separate Cloudflare products such as Workers, WAF, or cache features, which have their own billing conditions.

facts.label: Default region choice
facts.value: Automatic is the default. At bucket creation, it chooses the closest available region based on the caller's location.

facts.label: Location hints
facts.value: Optional best-effort hints: WNAM, ENAM, WEUR, EEUR, APAC, and OC. Hints are not guarantees and are only honored the first time a bucket name is created.

facts.label: Jurisdictional location
facts.value: Published jurisdiction options are EU, US, and FedRAMP. The jurisdiction guarantees objects are stored and processed within the chosen jurisdiction; it cannot be changed after bucket creation.

facts.label: Jurisdiction endpoint and scope
facts.value: Jurisdiction buckets require jurisdiction-specific S3 endpoints. EU, US, and FedRAMP endpoints are documented; a jurisdiction endpoint cannot access buckets outside that jurisdiction.

facts.label: Published price by location
facts.value: R2's current public rate table shows one USD rate per storage class and no separate price for the location hints or listed jurisdictions.

facts.label: Download and migration path
facts.value: Objects can be downloaded via dashboard, Workers API, S3 API, or CLI. Cloudflare documents S3-compatible SDKs and rclone; Super Slurper and Sippy are inbound migration options.

facts.label: Bucket empty/delete behavior
facts.value: Emptying a bucket permanently deletes its objects and cannot be undone. A bucket must be empty, and lock rules removed, before deleting it.

facts.label: Object deletion recovery
facts.value: The R2 S3 API matrix does not list versioning as implemented. Deleted objects cannot be recovered through the documented empty-bucket action; durability is not deletion recovery.

facts.label: Object export format
facts.value: R2 presents objects through its S3-compatible API and standard object download methods. No R2-specific bulk export archive format was identified.

facts.label: Deletion after account closure
facts.value: Exact R2 object-removal timing after account closure or service termination was not found in public R2 docs, Cloudflare terms, or privacy policy.

facts.label: Object durability
facts.value: Cloudflare states 99.999999999% annual durability (eleven nines) and describes replication and/or erasure coding across data centers within a geographic region.

facts.label: Availability and recovery
facts.value: Enterprise R2 SLA is 99.9% monthly uptime; bucket locks can prevent overwrite/deletion for a configured retention period, but R2 durability alone does not restore deleted objects.

facts.label: Bucket lock scope
facts.value: R2 native bucket-lock rules can retain selected prefixes for a duration, until a date, or indefinitely. They block deletion, overwrites, and lifecycle removal while applicable; up to 1,000 rules per bucket.

facts.label: Backup, version history, and restore
facts.value: No general R2 point-in-time restore, object version history, or backup restore workflow was found in the R2 docs or terms reviewed. R2-native bucket locks are available, but are not a restore system.

facts.label: Identity and old names
facts.value: Current product: Cloudflare R2 Storage, usually called R2. Vendor: Cloudflare, Inc. Official docs: https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/.

facts.label: Former names
facts.value: No former product name was identified in the R2 overview, product docs, or R2-tagged blog material checked.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Cloudflare-operated hosted service. No self-hosted R2 server or downloadable R2 software edition is offered in the R2 product docs.

facts.label: Service terms
facts.value: R2 use is covered by Cloudflare's Self-Serve Subscription Agreement and applicable product terms; there is no separate R2 software license listed for a self-host edition.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Active hosted service with current pricing, limits, API, and product documentation.

facts.label: Recent product activity
facts.value: R2 changelog entry dated November 3, 2026 adds request metrics by region and HTTP error code.

facts.label: Parent-company change
facts.value: Cloudflare's acquisitions-tagged blog says the Deno team is joining Cloudflare, dated October 9, 2026. This notice does not name R2 or change its availability.

facts.label: General service termination terms
facts.value: The Self-Serve Subscription Agreement reserves Cloudflare's right to suspend or terminate access, and to modify or discontinue a service, at its discretion and without notice. No R2-specific suspension notice was found.

facts.label: Vendor home and main markets
facts.value: Cloudflare lists its headquarters in San Francisco, California, United States and offices in multiple countries. This is company location, not R2 data location.

facts.label: Support and status
facts.value: Cloudflare publishes a public service status page and R2 troubleshooting/error docs. A paid support agreement can apply to Enterprise customers.

facts.label: R2 service commitment
facts.value: The R2 Enterprise SLA sets a 99.9% monthly uptime percentage and service credits of 10%, 25%, or 50% at published thresholds. It is an Enterprise subscription SLA.

facts.label: Non-Enterprise SLA
facts.value: The public R2 SLA page is titled Enterprise Subscription SLA. No matching uptime-credit promise for self-serve R2 was found in that page or the R2 docs checked.

apps.name: Cloudflare Vectorize

free.text: 30M queried and 5M stored vector dimensions monthly

cells.regions: Account-level rates; no region-specific price listed

$0.0718 for stored vectors, plus the $5 Workers Paid account minimum. Worker compute is extra.

files.math: Vector records are not a general file store.

facts.label: Free offer type

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: Workers Free: 30 million queried vector dimensions per account per month, 5 million stored vector dimensions per account, and 100 indexes per account.

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: Workers Free: up to 1,000 namespaces per index.

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: Free-plan behavior after an allowance is exceeded is not stated on the Vectorize pricing FAQ, limits page, or self-serve terms.

facts.label: Inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: With no queries, Vectorize does not bill queried vector dimensions. Stored-vector charges can continue while vectors remain above the included allowance.

facts.label: Inactivity, pause, and deletion

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: A Workers Free account can create and use Vectorize within its published allowances; a paid plan is not required just to start.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: Workers Paid has a minimum account charge of $5 USD per month. This is the Workers plan floor, not a Vectorize usage rate.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Vectorize charges by queried vector dimensions: (vectors in the index + query count) × dimensions per vector, aggregated at account level.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Workers Paid includes 50 million queried vector dimensions monthly; additional queried dimensions cost $0.01 per million.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Vectorize says it does not bill CPU, memory, or active-index hours.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Vectorize itself has no CPU, memory, or active-index-hour charge. Query-dimension use is zero when no queries are sent; retained stored dimensions may still be billable.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: Vectorize pricing states there are no data transfer or egress fees for the product.

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: The product pricing page publishes no separate region-to-region Vectorize transfer rate.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: On Workers Paid, usage above the included queried/stored dimensions and index allowance is billed at the Vectorize rates above.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: Workers Free overage action is not published in the Vectorize docs or self-serve terms searched.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: No Vectorize-specific spend cap or guaranteed automatic cutoff was found in product pricing, limits, or the Cloudflare self-serve terms.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Current V2 maximum: 20,000,000 vectors per index; 1 to 1,536 dimensions per vector, stored at 32-bit precision.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits

apps.name: Cloudinary

free.text: 25 shared credits/month; 1 GB storage per credit

facts.label: Free offer type
facts.value: Ongoing Free plan for Image & Video APIs, shown as free forever with 25 credits per month; it is not just a temporary trial.

facts.label: Credit reset and usage period
facts.value: Free transformation and bandwidth usage are measured over a rolling 30-day window; stored size is a current snapshot.

facts.label: Free monthly credit pool
facts.value: Free includes 25 credits shared across transformations, storage, and bandwidth. This is one shared pool, not 25 credits for each resource.

facts.label: Free credit conversion: transformations
facts.value: One credit covers 1,000 image transformations; chained image manipulations count as one when Cloudinary generates a new derivative.

facts.label: Free credit conversion: storage
facts.value: One credit covers 1 GB of stored assets. Free backups stored by Cloudinary also count against storage credits.

facts.label: Free credit conversion: image bandwidth
facts.value: One credit covers 1 GB of image bandwidth delivered. Certain CDN-in-front/origin-metering arrangements can instead use 1 credit per 0.5 GB.

facts.label: Free credit conversion: video bandwidth
facts.value: On Free, one credit covers 1 GB of delivered video bandwidth. Paid self-service plans receive 2 GB of video bandwidth per credit.

facts.label: Transformation timing
facts.value: A transformation credit is used when a new derivative is first generated. Upload-time incoming transformations and eager cache-warming transformations count; repeat delivery of an already cached derivative does not count again.

facts.label: Video transformation example
facts.value: For common progressive H.264 output, the detailed transformation guide uses 2 transformation counts per processed second at SD and 4 per second at HD. That is 500 SD seconds or 250 HD seconds per 1,000-count credit for these output types.

facts.label: Free account seats and accounts
facts.value: Free includes 3 users and 1 account.

facts.label: Free maximum upload sizes and image dimensions
facts.value: Free plan caps listed on Compare Plans: image 10 MB, video 100 MB, raw file 10 MB, image 25 MP, and multi-frame image 50 MP.

facts.label: Free Admin API rate limit
facts.value: The Free plan comparison lists 500 Admin API requests per hour.

facts.label: Free add-on access
facts.value: Pricing includes access to free add-ons; each add-on has its own allowance and limit. Reaching an add-on quota can stop that add-on until renewal or a tier change.

facts.label: Free PDF and archive delivery
facts.value: Free accounts block delivery of PDFs and archive formats such as ZIP by default. The account owner can enable this in product-environment Security settings; paid plans remove these default delivery restrictions.

facts.label: Inactivity pause
facts.value: No inactivity timer that sleeps, pauses, or expires a Free media environment was found in the pricing, billing, usage, or terms pages checked.

facts.label: Over-quota account status
facts.value: Fixed plans use soft limits: warnings appear around 90%; after repeated notices, an over-quota fixed-plan account may be disabled. Pro PAYG overage is billed on the regular billing date rather than immediately blocked.

facts.label: Cancellation and recovery window
facts.value: After cancellation, the account is disabled and stored media is inaccessible. Admins have 30 days to restore it; after 30 days, product environments, assets, metadata, and settings are permanently removed.

facts.label: Free price
facts.value: Free plan: $0, shown as free forever. No card is required for signup.

facts.label: Plus price
facts.value: Plus: $99 per month, or $89 per month on an annual subscription; 225 monthly credits, 3 users, and 2 accounts.

facts.label: Advanced price
facts.value: Advanced: $249 per month, or $224 per month on an annual subscription; 600 monthly credits, 5 users, and 3 accounts.

facts.label: Advanced Extra price
facts.value: Advanced Extra: $549 per month, or $494 per month on an annual subscription; 1,350 monthly credits, 5 users, and 5 product environments.

facts.label: Pro PAYG price
facts.value: Pro: $1,099 per month, or $989 per month on an annual subscription; 2,750 monthly credits, 5 users, and 5 product environments. Billing docs call this plan Pro PAYG.

facts.label: Enterprise price
facts.value: Enterprise price and unit volume are custom; Cloudinary directs customers to contact sales.

facts.label: Currency code and taxes
facts.value: Public cards use a dollar sign but do not label it with a currency code. Terms say applicable taxes are added and are the customer's responsibility.

facts.label: Published plan-list mismatch
facts.value: The pricing page shows Free, Plus, Advanced, and Enterprise cards; the current billing guide names Plus, Advanced, Advanced Extra, and Pro PAYG as self-service paid plan types. The compare FAQ says there are five additional plans but lists only Advanced Extra and Pro with prices.

facts.label: Payment and cancellation terms
facts.value: Paid self-service plans accept listed credit cards and, where available, Google Pay or Apple Pay. Enterprise can use bank transfer. Terms say fees are not refundable and applicable taxes are additional.

facts.label: Shared base credit meter
facts.value: Free and self-service paid plans draw transformations, storage, image bandwidth, and video bandwidth from one credit pool; advanced add-ons and extra seats/environments can be separately billed.

facts.label: Transformation charge meter
facts.value: Image derivatives count when generated; a complex image chain is one count. Video transformations are counted per processed second at a rate affected by resolution and output type.

facts.label: Video rate variations
facts.value: The transformation guide gives separate processing rates by resolution and codec; for example H.264 SD is 2 counts per second and HD is 4, while some codec and HDR outputs count more.

facts.label: Storage usage meter
facts.value: Storage usage includes originals, cached transformed derivatives, and revisions retained in Cloudinary backup storage.

facts.label: Image bandwidth usage meter
facts.value: Successful image deliveries are counted by delivered file size; normally one credit per GB of image bandwidth. Some CDN-in-front/origin arrangements use one credit per 0.5 GB.

facts.label: Video bandwidth usage meter
facts.value: Delivered video bandwidth costs 1 GB per credit on Free and 2 GB per credit on paid self-service plans.

facts.label: Usage windows by plan
facts.value: Free, Plus, Advanced, and Advanced Extra use rolling 30-day transformation and bandwidth usage; Pro PAYG and Enterprise use a billing usage month. Storage is current stored size.

facts.label: Add-ons and extra capacity
facts.value: Paid add-ons, extra users, and extra product environments are billed separately from base credits. Add-on quotas have their own renewal and limits.

facts.label: Pro PAYG overage rate
facts.value: Pro PAYG over-quota usage is billed as overage on the regular billing date, but an exact public per-credit overage rate was not found.

facts.label: Failed delivery or request price
facts.value: No separate per-request price schedule for Upload API, Admin API, or CDN delivery was found; plans include IO/request costs while credit consumption follows their published resource meters.

facts.label: Add-on price schedule
facts.value: Add-on pricing is separate and varies by add-on; no single general add-on rate applies to every image/video account.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Not applicable: Cloudinary exposes managed upload and transformation APIs, not user-provisioned compute instances that an app owner can pause or scale to zero.

facts.label: Image and video delivery transfer
facts.value: Delivery bandwidth is part of the shared credit system: 1 GB image bandwidth per credit, and 1 GB video bandwidth per Free credit or 2 GB per paid self-service credit.

facts.label: Origin/CDN arrangement
facts.value: With certain CDN-in-front arrangements, image-origin metering can use 0.5 GB per credit instead of the usual 1 GB per credit.

facts.label: Inbound upload and storage transfer
facts.value: The plan FAQ says pricing covers managed storage, IO, and delivery requests; no independent upload-ingress rate is listed in the pricing or upload docs checked.

facts.label: Other CDN or origin costs
facts.value: The Cloudinary credit examples do not cover charges from a separate origin-storage provider or a CDN the customer places in front.

facts.label: Warnings and overage control
facts.value: Usage warnings appear at about 90%. Fixed plans prompt upgrade or reduction and may be disabled after repeated warnings; Pro PAYG bills overage on the regular bill date.

facts.label: Spend alert
facts.value: Console usage and delivery reports are available; a billing overview says Enterprise users may opt into notifications at a specified usage percentage. No Free-specific user-set spend alert was confirmed.

facts.label: Hard spending cap
facts.value: No customer-set dollar spend cap or guaranteed stop-at-budget feature was found in the current pricing, billing, usage, or terms pages checked.

facts.label: Add-on hard limit
facts.value: Add-ons with usage quotas stop when that quota is exhausted until the quota renews or the customer changes tiers.

facts.label: Account disablement and restoration
facts.value: Repeated warnings for a fixed-plan account may lead to disablement; switching to a plan that supports usage can re-enable it. After more than 30 days disabled or canceled, assets and environments may already have been removed.

facts.label: Included managed storage
facts.value: Storage is bundled into the shared credit pool at 1 GB per credit, with originals, cached derivatives, and retained revisions counted. There is no separate published per-GB-month price for the base credit plan.

facts.label: Storage-class split
facts.value: No hot, infrequent-access, archive, or retrieval storage class is listed for Image & Video APIs.

facts.label: Enterprise storage
facts.value: Enterprise uses custom units and custom volume pricing rather than the published self-service credit conversion.

facts.label: File request and IO pricing
facts.value: The plan FAQ says Cloudinary pricing covers managed-storage IO costs and CDN viewing requests. No separate public price per upload, list, or read request was found.

facts.label: Transformation and delivery charges
facts.value: New transformations consume transformation credits; successful delivery consumes bandwidth credits based on delivered bytes. Cached repeats do not generate a new transformation count.

facts.label: Admin API limit versus price
facts.value: Free has a listed 500 Admin API requests/hour limit; this is an hourly limit, not a published per-request fee. Upload API is documented as rate-unlimited.

facts.label: Minimum storage and early deletion
facts.value: No minimum retained time, minimum billable object size, or early-deletion charge was found in Cloudinary's pricing, billing, or delete-asset docs.

facts.label: Public signup
facts.value: The Free plan is available for self-service signup and the pricing page says no credit card is required. No form was submitted.

facts.label: Country and account eligibility limits
facts.value: No complete country eligibility list or country-specific self-serve restriction was found in the pricing, billing, or Terms of Use pages checked.

facts.label: Free-plan commercial production wording
facts.value: The Free plan includes the public Upload API, CDN delivery, and ongoing use, but the checked pricing and terms pages do not state a clear blanket permission or prohibition for commercial production on Free.

facts.label: Trial length
facts.value: The Image & Video API Free plan is described as free forever, not a time-limited trial.

facts.label: Primary type
facts.value: Hosted media file management: upload, store, transform, optimize, and deliver images and video through a CDN.

facts.label: Other roles and scope
facts.value: Media asset management, API-based uploads, image and video processing, and CDN delivery. It is not a general-purpose database or an S3-compatible object bucket product.

facts.label: Included media services
facts.value: Free includes upload widget and API, search, remote fetch, automatic-backup capability and revision tracking, image/video transformations, video transcoding and adaptive streaming, CDN delivery, and free add-on access.

facts.label: Paid plan additions
facts.value: Plus adds backup to a customer's S3 bucket, auto-tagging based search, paid add-ons, expedited support, allowlist/blocklist access, and role-based multi-user administration. Advanced adds custom CNAME, optional HTTPS SSL, and authentication options.

facts.label: Other backend capabilities
facts.value: The checked plan and API pages describe media management and processing, not a relational database, user-auth service, general serverless function host, or scheduled job runner.

facts.label: Media transformations
facts.value: Image and video tools include resizing/cropping, format conversion, effects, overlays, and video edits. Adaptive streaming can deliver HLS or MPEG-DASH renditions from one video.

facts.label: API and protocol
facts.value: Cloudinary exposes HTTPS REST APIs for upload, asset management, search, and transformation/delivery URLs. The Upload API is documented as rate-unlimited; other APIs can have account-specific rate limits.

facts.label: Backend SDKs
facts.value: Official backend SDKs are listed for Node.js, Python, PHP, Java, Ruby/Rails, .NET, Go, and Dart.

facts.label: Web and mobile integrations
facts.value: Official front-end SDKs include JavaScript, React, Vue, Angular, and Next.js; mobile SDKs include iOS, Android, Flutter, React Native, and Kotlin.

facts.label: Client-side upload
facts.value: Browser and mobile uploads are supported through the Upload API, upload widget, upload presets, and SDKs. Unsigned uploads can be restricted with a preset; signed uploads require a server-generated signature.

facts.label: Public and restricted delivery types
facts.value: Cloudinary supports upload, private, and authenticated delivery types. The default upload delivery type is publicly accessible unless access controls are configured.

facts.label: Private originals and derived files
facts.value: Private delivery restricts the original, but derived transformation URLs may be public unless strict transformation controls are enabled. Authenticated delivery protects originals and derivatives behind signed access.

facts.label: Signed uploads and credentials
facts.value: Signed uploads use the account API secret to create a server-side signature. Cloudinary says to keep that secret off the browser or mobile client; unsigned upload presets can limit client-side parameters.

facts.label: Signed/private file links
facts.value: Signed URLs and access tokens can be used to control delivery; an authenticated asset requires signed access, and token/cookie delivery features are plan-dependent.

facts.label: Custom domain delivery
facts.value: Advanced includes custom CNAME support and optional HTTPS SSL; the compare plan page says an SSL certificate may cost extra.

facts.label: Account and user permissions
facts.value: Plus includes role-based multi-user administration and allowlist/blocklist asset access; Free includes up to 3 users but does not list these Plus features.

facts.label: Encryption and security detail
facts.value: Cloudinary's Trust center publishes security and privacy resources, but the reviewed public product pages did not provide enough detail to assert every encryption setting or plan-level control here.

facts.label: Account security controls
facts.value: Cloudinary documents allowed-IP restrictions for Admin API calls and Console logins, signed uploads, and controls that can block delivery of potentially risky PDF and archive types.

facts.label: Current privacy and DPA notice
facts.value: Cloudinary's legal updates page lists a Privacy Policy update effective September 15, 2026 and a DPA update dated June 1, 2026.

facts.label: Image, video, and raw upload maxima
facts.value: Pricing lists Free/Plus/Advanced maximum file sizes: images 10/20/40 MB, video 100 MB/2 GB/4 GB, and raw files 10/20/40 MB. Enterprise is custom.

facts.label: Image pixel limits
facts.value: Maximum image size is 25 MP on Free and Plus, 50 MP on Advanced, and custom on Enterprise; multi-frame maxima are 50, 100, and 200 MP respectively.

facts.label: Chunked uploads
facts.value: Files larger than 100 MB must be uploaded in chunks through the API. The Upload Widget and Media Library handle chunking automatically.

facts.label: Very large upload handling
facts.value: Files larger than 20 GB require the asynchronous upload option; total size caps remain plan/account dependent.

facts.label: Supported asset types
facts.value: Cloudinary's upload API supports image, video/audio, and raw file resource types.

facts.label: Image formats and conversions
facts.value: Cloudinary accepts common image and multi-frame formats and can convert uploaded images to supported delivery formats such as JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, or JPEG XL, depending on account and browser support.

facts.label: Upload file restrictions
facts.value: Maximum upload size is determined by plan and account configuration; files above 100 MB use chunked uploads. The plan table gives the public image/video/raw limits above.

facts.label: S3 and object API compatibility
facts.value: No S3-compatible client endpoint or general object-storage protocol was found in Cloudinary's REST, upload, asset-management, or SDK docs. Cloudinary provides its own HTTPS APIs and SDKs.

facts.label: S3 backup integration
facts.value: Paid plans can send backups to a customer-owned S3 bucket; this is a backup destination, not client-side S3-compatible access to Cloudinary assets.

facts.label: CDN delivery
facts.value: Image and video assets are delivered through Cloudinary's CDN from delivery URLs. Pricing includes viewing bandwidth and delivery requests within plan pricing and credit usage.

facts.label: CDN network and optimization
facts.value: Cloudinary documents delivery through multiple CDNs, including Akamai, Fastly, and Cloudflare, and uses caching with transformation URLs. Optimizations can reduce delivered file size, which also changes bandwidth usage.

facts.label: Public and private files
facts.value: Public upload delivery is the default; private and authenticated delivery types are available for restricted media.

facts.label: Signed links and private access
facts.value: Signed URLs are supported for private/authenticated delivery. Authenticated originals and derivatives require authorized signed delivery; private derivatives may otherwise be public unless strict transformations are enabled.

facts.label: Browser upload restrictions
facts.value: Unsigned uploads from browsers or mobile clients can use restricted upload presets; signed upload uses a server-side signature and secret.

facts.label: Custom domain and TLS
facts.value: Custom CNAME delivery is listed on Advanced and Enterprise; optional HTTPS SSL is an additional-cost feature on the compare page.

facts.label: Private CDN and custom hostname
facts.value: Private CDN distributions and custom delivery hostnames require Advanced or higher and Cloudinary setup. The delivery documentation says custom hostnames have an additional cost.

facts.label: Delivery authentication tiers
facts.value: Pricing lists authentication options starting with Advanced; token-based and cookie-based authentication are shown as plan comparison features.

facts.label: External delivery costs
facts.value: Customer use of a separate CDN or origin storage can carry charges from that provider, and Cloudinary's billing guide notes a different origin metering rate for some fronted-CDN arrangements.

facts.label: Default storage location
facts.value: Cloudinary says media is stored in US data centers by default.

facts.label: Enterprise data-location request
facts.value: Enterprise accounts can request storage in other locations, including EU or AP data centers. The public page does not list a full selectable region matrix.

facts.label: API/datacenter coverage
facts.value: The status page separately lists operational US, EU, and AP datacenter APIs; it does not establish that an account's stored originals or backups are placed in each location.

facts.label: Export path
facts.value: Assets can be retrieved through the Media Library, delivery URLs, and Admin/Get Resources API; documentation describes scripting a copy of existing assets to another storage provider.

facts.label: Customer-owned backup
facts.value: Paid plans can back up to the customer's own storage bucket; Plus explicitly lists backup to an S3 bucket.

facts.label: Backup recovery
facts.value: If automatic backup is enabled, original assets and earlier versions can be restored. Derived and fetched copies may be regenerated; without a backup, deleted originals may not be recoverable.

facts.label: Backup retention period
facts.value: No fixed public number of days for retaining backed-up asset versions was found in the backup, pricing, or billing pages checked.

facts.label: Deleting an asset
facts.value: An asset is removed from Cloudinary cloud storage immediately and permanently; delivered copies may remain in Cloudinary CDN caches for up to 30 days without invalidation. Media Library deletion requests invalidation automatically; API deletion needs the invalidation parameter.

facts.label: Account cancellation and removal
facts.value: Cancellation disables access; the 30-day restore period ends with permanent removal of environments, assets, metadata, and settings.

facts.label: Privacy-policy content retention
facts.value: The current Privacy Policy says uploaded content is deleted following termination or deactivation, but does not define the precise deletion moment. Billing docs separately describe a 30-day account restore window.

facts.label: Automatic backup and revisions
facts.value: Automatic backup is off by default. When enabled, Cloudinary stores a copy of each new original upload in a secondary write-protected location and tracks asset revisions; Free backup is held by Cloudinary and counts against storage credits.

facts.label: Backup destinations
facts.value: Backup can use Cloudinary's default storage or, on paid plans, a customer-owned Amazon S3 bucket, Google Cloud Storage bucket, or Azure Blob Storage container.

facts.label: Restoring and downloading versions
facts.value: When backup is enabled, versions can be listed, downloaded, restored, or deleted through the Admin API or Media Library. A download URL returned for a backed-up version is valid for one hour.

facts.label: Own-bucket backup
facts.value: A paid plan can back up to a customer's own storage bucket; Enterprise can also choose to store Cloudinary originals in external cloud storage.

facts.label: Recovery from deletion
facts.value: Deleted Cloudinary assets are immediately removed from cloud storage; restore is possible from backup only when automatic backup was enabled. CDN cache copies may persist until invalidated.

facts.label: Replication and durability claims
facts.value: Cloudinary describes managed storage and redundant backup but no public customer-selected replication count or object-lock control was identified in the plan pages checked.

facts.label: Backup retention
facts.value: The public backup docs reviewed explain backup and restore but do not state a fixed number of days for backup-version retention.

facts.label: Identity and old names
facts.value: Cloudinary Image & Video APIs, described in billing docs as Programmable Media. Vendor: Cloudinary. Official product URL: https://cloudinary.com/.

facts.label: Former names
facts.value: No earlier name for this API product was identified in the product overview, billing docs, or newsroom checked.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Cloudinary operates the image and video service as a hosted cloud platform. Its SDKs call Cloudinary APIs; no self-hosted core server edition is offered in the product or deployment docs checked.

facts.label: Service terms
facts.value: Use is governed by Cloudinary's Terms of Use for self-serve accounts; Enterprise customers are directed to a separate subscription agreement. No open-source license applies to the hosted service.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Active hosted product with current pricing, billing documentation, upload APIs, SDKs, and image/video product pages.

facts.label: Product service status
facts.value: Cloudinary's status page reported all systems operational, including US, EU, and AP datacenters, Upload API, Admin API, Media Transformation API, and Media Delivery.

facts.label: Recent company and product activity
facts.value: The Cloudinary blog archive listed posts through November 4, 2026; the newsroom listed press releases through October 28, 2026.

facts.label: Acquisition history and shutdown search
facts.value: The official newsroom lists Cloudinary's Indivio acquisition on January 12, 2022. No later acquisition or shutdown notice was identified in the newsroom, blog archive, product docs, or status page searched.

facts.label: Free support
facts.value: Free lists forums, tickets, and email support.

facts.label: Paid and Enterprise support
facts.value: Plus lists expedited support. Enterprise lists Enterprise support, an SLA, and a designated customer success manager.

facts.label: Service status
facts.value: Public real-time status page was available and reported all systems operational at the time checked.

facts.label: Uptime statement
facts.value: Cloudinary's Trust page states a 99.9% uptime commitment; the public Trust page does not set out the service-credit terms or self-service plan eligibility.

facts.label: Free offer type
facts.value: Current new-user hosted offer is trial credit, not an established recurring free database allowance. Trial ends at 30 days or credit exhaustion.

facts.label: Free offer type
facts.value: Legacy Basic: recurring $15/month credit for eligible pay-as-you-go organizations; annual/multi-year contracts excluded. Payment method required for this allowance.

facts.label: Free offer type
facts.value: Self-hosted Enterprise Free is free licensed software for eligible businesses; Enterprise Trial is a separate 30-day license. Hosting costs remain the operator's.

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: Current trial cap: $400 organization credit and 30 days, whichever ends first. No independent monthly free storage/read/write/seat allocation was established for new Continuum users.

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: Legacy Basic allowance is shared across the organization: $15 equals 50 million RU plus 10 GiB-month at published rates; those are a combined example, not two independent free pools.

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: Enterprise Free renews annually and requires telemetry; absent telemetry for 7 days can throttle to five concurrent open transactions. Free expired licenses throttle after a 30-day grace period.

facts.label: Inactivity, pause and deletion
facts.value: Continuum trial end pauses clusters; 30-day grace to add payment and resume paid use, then deletion if no payment method is added.

facts.label: Inactivity, pause and deletion
facts.value: A universal inactivity deletion interval for ordinary paid Continuum clusters was not located.

facts.label: Inactivity, pause and deletion
facts.value: Billing failures can lead to deletion after multiple reminders; marketplace cancellation needs replacement payment within 6 hours to avoid cluster deletion.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: Continuum pay-as-you-go: no upfront commitment; ongoing provisioned resources are billable. A universal minimum cluster configuration or mandatory seat fee was not established.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: Legacy pricing page lists Standard from $146/month and Advanced from $476/month; these are existing-customer entry figures, not new Continuum quotes.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: Self-hosted paid Enterprise license price is quote-based; eligible Enterprise Free has no software license charge.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Continuum: provisioned compute, storage, backups, transfer and add-ons; USD, minute metering, monthly billing, $1/credit; no per-query charge.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: AWS us-east-1: compute Standard $0.092/vCPU-hour, Mission Critical $0.162/vCPU-hour; storage Standard $0.32/logical GiB-month (3 replicas), Mission Critical $0.155/provisioned GiB-month.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: AWS us-east-1 backup storage $0.023/GiB-month. Standard CDC add-on $0.006/vCPU-hour; Mission Critical CDC, PCR and virtualization each $0.023/vCPU-hour while active.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Mission Critical Plenum physical storage is free during preview; final production storage rates are not yet set in the table.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Legacy Basic: $0.20/million request units and $0.50/GiB-month; RUs include SQL, background work and applicable network activity.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Continuum provisioned compute is charged while idle. Virtual clusters have no separate charge but share a paid host and its virtualization add-on.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Legacy Basic can consume zero query compute at zero activity, but stored data and background work can still incur charges. Self-hosted idle infrastructure remains operator-funded.

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: Ingress free. AWS same-region $0.01/GiB; US/Canada/Europe cross-region $0.025/GiB, N. Virginia–Ohio $0.0125/GiB.

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: AWS US/Canada/Europe internet: $0.09216/GiB for first 10 TiB/month. Other tiers/origins differ; Azure uses GB.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: A guaranteed organization-wide dollar spend cap covering all Continuum meters was not located.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: Legacy Basic supports RU/storage limits. RU exhaustion disables service until raised or reset; storage exhaustion restricts writes, with cleanup exceptions.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Current Continuum universal maximum database size, maximum SQL request size, and hard per-cluster connection ceiling were not established.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Documented engine defaults: per-gateway connection limit -1 (unlimited setting); row-size error guardrail 80 MiB and logging guardrail 16 MiB per row/column family; statement timeout default 0s (disabled).

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Connection-pool guidance: Cloud maximum connection lifetime 30 minutes; recommend recycling within 5–30 minutes with jitter. Pool size depends on workload and CPU.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: STRING and BYTES support variable-sized values; docs warn that large values harm performance. BYTES guidance is below 1 MB, not a hard unlimited-upload promise.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Legacy Basic documentation: up to 30,000 RU/s. Legacy Standard: 2-vCPU minimum, 200-vCPU maximum.

facts.label: Storage prices
facts.value: Not applicable to this database product's standalone file storage rates.

facts.label: File request and retrieval prices
facts.value: Not applicable to this database product's file operation/retrieval billing.

facts.label: Minimum storage and early deletion
facts.value: Not applicable to this database product's object minimums and early deletion.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Not applicable: this offer was not established as a per-job CPU/memory/invocation pricing and timeout limits.

facts.label: Vector/index limits
facts.value: VECTOR stores fixed-length floating-point arrays; vector indexes support approximate nearest-neighbor search with L2, cosine and negative-inner-product operators.

facts.label: Vector/index limits
facts.value: A numeric maximum dimension, per-index record count, index-count limit, namespace quota and metadata-size quota were not located for current hosted plans.

facts.label: Vector/index limits
facts.value: Creating a vector index on a nonempty table requires disabling SQL safe updates and blocks writes during backfill. IMPORT INTO cannot target a table with a vector index; import before indexing.

facts.label: Embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: Included embedding generation, reranking models, token prices and model-provider allowances were not established.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: New Cloud organizations: 30-day/$400 trial; Standard needs no card, Mission Critical requires a card.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Cloud use requires authority to accept terms and compliance with export/sanctions laws; AUP restricts resale, abuse and unapproved security testing. A complete country allow/deny list was not located.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Enterprise Free self-hosted: combined parent/affiliate annual revenue below $10 million; government entities excluded; deploy on own hardware or own cloud account. Offering third parties a database service requires a paid license.

facts.label: Primary type and other roles
facts.value: Researcher classification: distributed SQL database; managed database, self-hosted database and vector/search capabilities.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Core bundle: SQL database, managed backups/restore, SQL access controls and vector/text/geospatial search. External-sink CDC is an add-on on both current cloud editions.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: PostgreSQL wire protocol 3.0 and PostgreSQL-style connection URLs; compatible drivers/ORMs can connect. Default SQL port 26257; connection options include TLS parameters.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Cloud access uses SQL clients/drivers; Cloud API manages infrastructure. Standard network access must be authorized; AWS PrivateLink and Google Private Service Connect (Preview in the connection guide) are documented options.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Cloud roles for users/groups/service accounts can be scoped to organization, folder or cluster; SQL users and record-access policies remain a separate database authorization layer.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Both current editions include row-level security, column encryption and ingress private connectivity. Mission Critical adds CMEK and egress perimeter controls; some private endpoints require provisioned storage.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Cloud advertises encryption at rest and in transit, TLS 1.3, and IP allowlists. These need configuration appropriate to the app; sensitive data obligations also appear in service terms.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: Native CockroachDB distributed SQL engine, not PostgreSQL binaries. PostgreSQL wire compatibility and a substantial SQL subset; current v26.4 documentation reports PostgreSQL 18 compatibility metadata.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: ACID transactions can atomically cover multiple rows/tables; default SERIALIZABLE isolation. READ COMMITTED is also supported with weaker isolation.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: Applications must handle transaction-retry errors (40001) and ambiguous results (40003); automatic retry is conditional, including result-buffer limits.

facts.label: Test environments and branches
facts.value: Separate clusters and backup/restore provide environment isolation; virtual clusters share a paid host. Current copy-on-write database-branch quotas and pricing were not established.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Self-hosted production guidance: at least three independent nodes for the default three-replica topology; three availability zones for zone resilience, or three regions for region resilience.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Mission Critical PCR is a separately charged, limited-access add-on with provisioned storage. It continuously replicates asynchronously to an independent standby and provides a failover workflow.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: CDC emits row changes at least once; first emission per key is ordered by timestamp. External sinks include Kafka, cloud storage, webhooks and Pub/Sub; sinkless streams end with the SQL connection.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: A built-in client offline read/write cache, reconnection merge policy and offline conflict-resolution contract were not found.

facts.label: Extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Built-in vector indexes, full-text TSVECTOR/TSQUERY indexes and geospatial GEOMETRY/GEOGRAPHY indexes. This is native SQL functionality, not permission to install arbitrary PostgreSQL extensions.

facts.label: Upload and file limits
facts.value: Not applicable to this database product's file/multipart upload limits.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Not applicable to this database product's an S3-compatible object endpoint.

facts.label: Delivery and private files
facts.value: Not applicable to this database product's bucket/CDN/signed-file delivery.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Self-hosting requires operating nodes/storage/networking, TLS and credentials, clocks, monitoring, backups and upgrades. Production guidance recommends at least 3 nodes, typically 8+ vCPU/node and 4 GiB RAM/vCPU; avoid burstable/shared-core machines.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Continuum management platform is cloud-only. Self-hosted license entitlement does not supply managed hosting, backup operations or cloud support; track release support windows and renew any Free license.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: Not applicable: this offer was not established as a general application-worker runtime or language allocation.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Not applicable: this offer was not established as a general queue delivery/retry/dead-letter contract.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Not applicable: this offer was not established as a application queue payload and message-retention limits.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Not applicable: this offer was not established as a application job run-history retention and replay.

facts.label: Filters and mixed search
facts.value: SQL can combine vectors with ordinary data filters. Vector-index prefix columns need constrained values; IN lists are supported, while inequality predicates are not accelerated as prefix filters.

facts.label: Filters and mixed search
facts.value: Native keyword search uses TSVECTOR/TSQUERY and ranking; trigram search is another option. Combining keyword/vector result ranking requires an application/query design.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Continuum Standard: AWS and GCP; Mission Critical: AWS, GCP and Azure. Single- and multi-region deployment options differ by storage model.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Standard AWS: us-east-1, us-east-2, us-west-2, eu-west-1, eu-west-2, eu-central-1, ap-south-1, ap-southeast-1, ap-southeast-3. Standard GCP: us-central1, us-east1, us-west2, europe-west1/2/3, asia-south1, asia-southeast1.

facts.value: Mission Critical Plenum preview: single-region, v26.3+, selected AWS us-east-1/us-west-2/eu-central-1/eu-west-1; provisioned storage required for multi-region and host clusters.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: SQL EXPORT writes query results as CSV or Parquet to external storage. This is data export, not automatic conversion of every schema object or application service.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: v26.4 compatibility docs support schema-only plain PostgreSQL 18 pg_dump output; data-bearing dumps, non-plain archives, pg_restore and pg_dumpall are not supported import paths.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: DPA requires deletion of covered Personal Data as soon as reasonably practicable and within 30 days after agreement termination, unless legally required to retain it; download before deletion.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Privacy Policy directs account-information deletion requests to support@cockroachlabs.com; cached/archived copies may persist. Billing docs retain a card after organization deletion to settle charges, removable through Support afterward.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: EU Data Act Addendum applies only to covered EU deployments/customers. It describes up to two months' switching notice, a normally 30-day transition, then a 30-day retrieval window; legal retention exceptions remain.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Current Standard and Mission Critical both include managed backups, encrypted backups, revision history and point-in-time recovery capability. Online restore is Mission Critical only.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Managed backups: hourly default; configurable 5 minutes–24 hours. Default retention 30 days, choices from 2 to 365 days; price follows stored backup data.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Deleted-cluster backups persist and bill through retention; agreement termination caps retention at 30 days. Cross-cluster restore is same organization; deleted-cluster restore needs Support.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Self-hosted BACKUP supports full/incremental cluster, database or table backups; operator provides storage and schedules. Tested targets include S3, GCS and Azure Blob; other S3-compatible stores are untested.

facts.label: File recovery and protection
facts.value: Not applicable to this database product's object versioning and delete recovery.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Hosted: Continuum Standard uses shared infrastructure; Mission Critical uses dedicated infrastructure. Continuum itself is not self-hostable.

facts.label: Hosting and license

facts.label: Hosting and license
