facts.label: Free offer type
facts.value: Recurring hosted Free plan with monthly metered allowances and hard resource caps. Starter retains included amounts and permits paid overages.

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: Per team: 0.5 GB database, 1 GB files/backups, 0.5 GB search storage; monthly 1M calls, 20 GB-hours actions, 1 GB database I/O, 3,000 query-GB searches and 1 GB egress.

facts.label: Free team and deployments
facts.value: Free/Starter: 1–6 developers, 40 deployments per team, S16 class. No separate native-auth MAU allowance was found.

facts.label: Pause and resume
facts.value: Manual pause keeps data; new function calls fail. Scheduled functions queue until resume; cron occurrences are skipped. Resume in dashboard.

facts.label: Ordinary idle deletion
facts.value: No universal automatic inactivity pause, expiration or purge interval for ordinary Free production deployments was found.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: Starter: $0/month base plus usage beyond included resources. No mandatory paid developer fee shown for its 1–6 developer range.

facts.label: Professional commitment
facts.value: Professional: $25 per developer/month, supporting 1–20 developers. A one-developer team has a $25 monthly seat base.

facts.label: Business and Enterprise commitment
facts.value: Business: $2,500 monthly minimum, 1–50 developers without a per-developer fee. Enterprise: custom contract and unlimited developers.

facts.label: Currency and taxes
facts.value: Published rates use $. Terms make fees tax-exclusive and use the currency in the Order Form. A universal ISO currency statement for self-service rates was not found.

facts.label: Starter billing meters
facts.value: US East: calls $2.20/1M; actions $0.33/GB-hour; database $0.22/GB-month; database I/O $0.22/GB; search storage $0.55/GB-month; searches $0.11/1,000 query-GB, after allowances.

facts.label: Professional billing meters
facts.value: US East: 25M calls then $2/1M; 250 action GB-hours then $0.30/GB-hour; 50 GB database then $0.20/GB-month; 50 GB database I/O then $0.20/GB; 1 GB search then $0.50/GB-month; 50,000 query-GB then $0.10/1,000.

facts.label: Billable activity and data
facts.value: Calls include client invocations, scheduled executions, subscription updates and file accesses. Database storage includes rows and indexes; database I/O counts document/index transfer between functions and database.

facts.label: Billing rounding and minimum increment
facts.value: Invoice rounding, minimum action duration, and partial-million/partial-1,000 search billing increments were not established.

facts.label: Business/Enterprise deployment fees
facts.value: Published Monthly Pricing: S16 $0.04; S256 $0.08; D1024 $2,800; D2048 $5,600 per active deployment, prorated daily. Dedicated extra action concurrency: $350 per 1,024.

facts.label: Business/Enterprise database meters
facts.value: Serverless: calls $2/1M, database $0.20/GB-month, I/O $0.20/GB, query/mutation compute $0. Dedicated: calls $0.20/1M, database $0.45/GB-month, I/O $0.15/GB and compute $0.45/GB-hour.

facts.label: Business/Enterprise action meters
facts.value: Convex runtime action compute $0.16/GB-hour of CPU time; Node runtime $0.32/GB-hour. Search storage $0.50/GB-month and searches $0.10/1,000 query-GB.

facts.label: Idle serverless compute
facts.value: Free/Starter/Professional serverless query/mutation compute has no time-based charge. Actions bill measured execution; retained database, search and file/backup storage remain billable.

facts.label: Business/Enterprise idle deployment fee
facts.value: Per-deployment fees are waived for paused deployments or after 30 days without function calls. The plan minimum and retained-storage meters are separate.

facts.label: Starter data transfer
facts.value: 1 GB/month included; $0.132 per additional GB at US East pricing.

facts.label: Professional and enterprise transfer
facts.value: Professional: 50 GB/month then $0.12/GB. Business/Enterprise standard table: $0.12/GB.

facts.label: Transfer routes and remaining gaps
facts.value: Usage-limit docs count file downloads, outgoing fetch and log-stream egress. Limits also include internal file access and backup generation/restoration. A complete ingress/inter-region exemption matrix and mapping of all database client traffic were not found.

facts.label: Free overages
facts.value: Free has hard resource caps; operations that insert/update data may fail after resource limits. Starter and higher can exceed included resources with usage charges, within deployment-class limits.

facts.label: Team spend controls
facts.value: Warning threshold emails the team. Disable threshold disables all team projects; seat fees are excluded. Raising/removing it can re-enable projects.

facts.label: Deployment usage controls
facts.value: Per-deployment daily/monthly UTC windows; warnings and disabling thresholds for supported usage meters. Disabled deployment resumes at reset or after raising/removing the threshold.

facts.label: Cap financial guarantee
facts.value: Terms say overage charges accrue despite optional caps/alerts; docs do not promise instantaneous enforcement or zero overshoot.

facts.label: Capacity and sessions
facts.value: S16/S256: 1 TB dataset limit, 1,000/10,000 sessions. D1024/D2048: 4/8 TB and 100,000/200,000 sessions. Free storage cap still applies below class capacity.

facts.label: Record and transaction limits
facts.value: Document 1 MiB. Transaction read/write ceilings 16 MiB each; scans 32,000 documents, writes 16,000; function arguments/results 16 MiB, with Node action arguments limited to 5 MiB.

facts.label: Starter file storage
facts.value: 1 GB included, then $0.033/GB-month, US East. User files and retained logical backup archives share the file-storage meter.

facts.label: Other paid file storage
facts.value: Professional: 100 GB included, then $0.03/GB-month. Business/Enterprise standard rate: $0.03/GB-month.

facts.label: File request and retrieval billing
facts.value: File accesses count as function calls; egress and action compute can also apply. The documented upload flow uses an upload-URL mutation, file POST and storage-ID mutation.

facts.label: Minimum storage and early deletion
facts.value: Minimum billed object size/capacity, minimum retention duration and early-deletion charge were not found.

facts.label: Vector and index limits
facts.value: Vectors use array(float64); dimensions 2–4,096; up to 4 vector indexes/table within 32 total indexes, 16 filter fields/index, 64 filter expressions/search and 256 results/search.

facts.label: Embedding and model extras
facts.value: Vector-search example calls an external embedding API before searching. Convex action/call/search charges apply separately; provider/model token charges depend on the chosen embedding service.

facts.label: Runtime resource and duration limits
facts.value: Convex runtime: 64 MiB RAM, action limit 30 minutes; Node: 512 MiB, action limit 10 minutes. Query/mutation user code limit 1 second, excluding database operations.

facts.label: Concurrent executions
facts.value: S16: 16 queries, 16 mutations, 64 actions per runtime, 8 scheduled jobs. S256: 256 queries/mutations, 512 Convex actions, 256 Node actions and 256 scheduled jobs.

facts.label: Wait/retry billing precision
facts.value: Small-plan actions are priced in GB-hours; Business/Enterprise distinguishes Convex CPU-time billing from Node GB-hours. Exact idle-wait treatment, failed-attempt charging and duration rounding were not fully established.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Public self-service access. Terms permit app builders to embed the service in customer-facing products on designated serverless types; dedicated types have a stated restriction.

facts.label: Card and geographic eligibility
facts.value: Free signup card requirement and a complete eligible-country list were not found. Export-control compliance is required.

facts.label: Primary type and other roles
facts.value: Researcher classification: hosted backend platform; relational document database, functions, realtime, auth, files, search and jobs.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Native database, query/mutation/action functions, realtime subscriptions, files, full-text/vector search and scheduled/cron functions. Optional Workpool and Workflow components add orchestration.

facts.label: Included login
facts.value: Convex Auth runs in the backend and supports client-side React and React Native. OIDC/JWT integrations can use external identity providers. Convex Auth is beta; Next.js support is experimental.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: JavaScript/TypeScript reactive client over WebSockets; HTTP client in runtimes with fetch, including browsers and Node.js. React integration supplied.

facts.label: Other clients and HTTP API
facts.value: Official Python and Rust clients; HTTP endpoints call public queries, mutations and actions from other languages. HTTP JSON format does not preserve all Convex input/output type distinctions.

facts.label: Server runtimes
facts.value: Backend functions use JavaScript/TypeScript. Default Convex runtime supports browser-style APIs and WebAssembly; Node.js is action-only, default 24 with 22/24 selectable.

facts.label: Record and function access
facts.value: Deployment endpoints are public internet endpoints. Verify OIDC/JWT identity and write authorization checks in public functions; identity validation alone does not restrict which records a user can access.

facts.label: Team roles and secrets
facts.value: Team Admin/Developer and per-project Admin roles; Developers can read production data but cannot write without project-admin access. Environment variables are deployment-scoped; project defaults are supported.

facts.label: Network access
facts.value: Documented outbound IPs are shared by deployments in each region; source-IP allowlisting alone is not authentication. Main site says Convex in your VPC is coming soon; Enterprise pricing offers BYOC.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: Custom Convex database engine; JSON-like documents with relational modeling and optional schema. Query/mutation JavaScript APIs replace writing SQL.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: Mutations are atomic transactions across their database changes. Optimistic concurrency control supplies serializability and retries conflicting deterministic transactions.

facts.label: Actions and search consistency
facts.value: Actions are outside a single database transaction. Vector indexes are up to date immediately after writes, but subsequent action queries can observe documents changed/deleted since search.

facts.label: Development and preview environments
facts.value: Each project has production and personal dev deployments. Preview deployments are isolated temporary environments: expire after 5 days on Free/Starter, 14 days on Professional/Business/Enterprise.

facts.label: Database branch semantics
facts.value: Automatic copy-on-write database branching was not established. Preview docs describe new environments and explicit seeding; backups can import data across deployments.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Database state is replicated across physical availability zones. Customer-controlled read replicas, failover controls and numerical recovery-time/recovery-point objectives were not established.

facts.label: Live updates and client retries
facts.value: Queries automatically subscribe to dependency changes; client results share a consistent snapshot. React reconnects automatically and retries mutations with backend once-only execution protection.

facts.label: Offline persistence scope
facts.value: Durable offline read cache, offline mutation survival across browser restarts, and a default offline conflict-resolution policy were not established.

facts.label: Specialized indexes
facts.value: Ordinary schema-defined database indexes, full-text indexes and vector indexes. Text search uses BM25-based relevance and prefix matching; it has no typo tolerance.

facts.label: Upload limits
facts.value: Generated upload URL expires after 1 hour; direct POST has no stated file-size ceiling but a 2-minute timeout. App functions decide who receives an upload URL.

facts.label: Multipart and resumable uploads
facts.value: Native S3 multipart/resumable upload behavior and an operation-by-operation compatibility matrix were not found.

facts.label: Storage API compatibility
facts.value: Native app-facing APIs use storage IDs, generateUploadUrl, getUrl/get, store and delete. S3 client compatibility was not established. Self-host S3 persistence is a different interface.

facts.label: File access and link expiry
facts.value: getUrl creates bearer-accessible links: anyone with a link can reuse it. Revocation requires deleting/reuploading the file. Per-request auth requires an HTTP action; response ceiling 100 MiB.

facts.label: Custom domains and delivery
facts.value: Professional supports custom domains. Overriding CONVEX_CLOUD_URL changes file/upload URLs; deployments are served through Cloudflare with baseline network DDoS protection.

facts.label: Vector filters and similarity
facts.value: Dense approximate nearest-neighbor search using cosine similarity; indexed equality and OR filters. Search runs in actions.

facts.label: Mixed keyword/vector search
facts.value: Separate full-text and vector APIs are documented. A native combined ranking/fusion API was not found in the checked pages.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: Managed server-side JavaScript/TypeScript functions; scheduler invokes mutations/actions. External services can be called from actions; no separate worker host is needed for supported runtime code.

facts.label: Base scheduler delivery
facts.value: Scheduled mutations execute exactly once, retry internal errors and fail on developer errors. Scheduled actions execute at most once and are not automatically retried; app code must check outcomes and reschedule.

facts.label: Optional work queues/workflows
facts.value: Workpool supports configurable action retries with exponential backoff/jitter and parallelism. Actions must be made idempotent. Workflow adds persisted multi-step execution and configurable retry/restart.

facts.label: Ordering and dead-letter handling
facts.value: A base-scheduler FIFO contract, deduplication-key window and automatic dead-letter queue/replay policy were not found. Failed status and manual rescheduling are documented instead.

facts.label: Scheduling and retention
facts.value: runAfter uses millisecond delays; runAt uses an epoch timestamp. Pending jobs persist in the database across restarts and can be months ahead. Cron uses UTC; overlapping occurrences can be skipped.

facts.label: Scheduled payload conflict
facts.value: Scheduler guide: 1,000 functions with 8MB total arguments. Limits: 1,000 per mutation, 4 MiB per scheduled call, 16 MiB total arguments and 1M outstanding jobs.

facts.label: Job result history
facts.value: Base scheduled-function results remain available for 7 days after completion. Workflow completion storage is not automatically cleaned; cleanup is explicit.

facts.label: Logs and export
facts.value: Dashboard exposes a short recent history; Professional adds log streams to Axiom, Datadog, PostHog or a webhook. Streams are best effort and can lose or duplicate events.

facts.label: Dashboard log retention
facts.value: An exact built-in dashboard log retention duration or storage quota was not found.

facts.label: Self-host operations and gaps
facts.value: Run backend, dashboard and frontend; Docker setup defaults to persistent SQLite/local storage. Optional Postgres/MySQL persistence and S3 backend storage are documented. Operator owns routing, persistence, backups and upgrades.

facts.label: Production hardware minimum
facts.value: A general production CPU/RAM minimum was not found in the self-host and own-infrastructure guides. No hosting-cost floor is estimated.

facts.label: Regions and migration
facts.value: Deployment choices: aws-us-east-1, aws-eu-west-1, aws-ap-southeast-2 and aws-ca-central-1. All deployment infrastructure is assigned to that region; existing deployment region cannot change.

facts.label: Regional pricing and policy scope
facts.value: N. Virginia is 1.0x; Ireland, Sydney and Canada Central usage is 1.3x. AWS/PlanetScale processing follows deployment selection; support, analytics and other subprocessors have separate locations.

facts.label: Data export and migration
facts.value: Download ZIP snapshots with table documents.jsonl files and optional _storage metadata/file bytes; CLI export and paginated Data Sync export are documented.

facts.label: Project and account deletion
facts.value: Project deletion is permanent and unrecoverable, including deployments/data. Account deletion requires handling sole-admin teams and deleting projects in single-member teams.

facts.label: Termination and retained copies
facts.value: Terms require return/destruction of confidential information within 30 days. DPA requires personal-data deletion on expiry/termination but excludes backup/archive copies until the retention schedule or legal requirements permit deletion.

facts.label: Physical backup purge deadline
facts.value: A fixed purge deadline for all deleted project data, backup/archive copies and personal account information was not found.

facts.label: Manual and daily backups
facts.value: Logical snapshots contain tables and optional files. Manual backups: 7 days; Free/Starter store up to 2 per deployment. Professional supports scheduled daily/weekly backups; daily retention 7 days.

facts.label: Weekly retention conflict

facts.value: Operational cluster services: Data, Query, Index, Search, Eventing and Analytics, subject to selected node shape/services. App Services adds user authentication and mobile/edge synchronization as linked infrastructure.

facts.value: Official Couchbase SDKs and couchbases:// TLS connections, cbsh, cbq, import/export/backup tools and a separately enabled Data API. Cluster credentials, allowed IPs and IPv4 connectivity are required for SDK access.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Data API offers HTTP access, but SQL++ multi-statement transactions are not supported through its Query passthrough; use supported SDKs/cbq for transactions. Data API load-balancer/time/data fees can apply even when the cluster is off.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Capella organization/project roles and cluster-access credentials have separate scopes; credentials can be restricted to buckets/scopes/collections. Allowed-IP lists and TLS 1.2+ secure connections; at-rest encryption is enabled.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: VPC peering and provider private endpoints are supported on eligible paid configurations. App Services adds user authentication, channel/role access and a JavaScript access-control/data-validation function; it is separate from Capella UI SSO.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: Couchbase Server JSON/key-value engine, SQL++ query language, buckets/scopes/collections. Current Capella docs support Server 8.0; patches are managed by Capella and compatible older versions can be selected for paid clusters.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Distributed ACID transactions can span documents, nodes, collections, scopes and buckets within one datacenter. Read Committed isolation with Monotonic Atomic View and optimistic CAS checks; default transaction durability is majority.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Queries use asynchronously maintained indexes; transactional DML uses request_plus visibility semantics. Durability is tunable. Single-node Capella bucket minimum durability is fixed at None, without multi-node redundancy.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Separate projects/clusters and backup/restore migrations support isolated development environments. Free-to-paid data transfer uses an explicit backup/restore path.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Native copy-on-write branch count, lifetime or branch pricing was not established.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Multi-node buckets can replicate across cluster nodes; multi-AZ placement is available with Developer Pro/Enterprise, whereas Basic is single AZ. Configure enough replicas to match the node/zone topology; one node has no redundancy/SLA.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: XDCR replicates bucket data between clusters, including one-way/two-way and remote self-managed destinations. It does not replicate indexes; Capella-to-Capella replication across different cloud providers is unsupported.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: App Services plus Couchbase Lite supports local/offline mobile/IoT apps that sync when network access returns. User/channel access and app authentication are configured per App Endpoint; Basic, Anonymous and OIDC options are documented.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Active-active XDCR with linked App Services requires Server 7.6.6+ and App Services 4.0+ on both clusters with cross-cluster versioning. Earlier combinations can corrupt data; current docs describe automatic conflict handling for supported combinations.

facts.label: extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Primary/secondary SQL++ indexes, Search full-text/geospatial indexes, Search Vector indexes, Composite Vector indexes and Hyperscale Vector indexes are distinct choices. Search/Index/Eventing services need suitable allocated nodes/resources.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: App Services Public REST attachment maximum is 20 MB. PUT creates/replaces an attachment for a document revision; Content-Type defaults to application/octet-stream, and If-Match/rev controls updates.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Document attachment GET/PUT/HEAD/DELETE and BLIP replication are the applicable APIs. This is not an S3-compatible bucket endpoint; bucket here means Couchbase's database container.

facts.label: delivery and private files
facts.value: Attachments can be fetched through the App Services document API; user/channel policies govern synced document access. Unsafe response content types can force download via Content-Disposition.

facts.label: filters and mixed search
facts.value: Composite vector indexes apply scalar filters before similarity work; Hyperscale uses optimized vector indexes with filtering options; Search Vector indexes combine text, scalar, geospatial and vector search.

facts.label: execution model and languages
facts.value: Eventing runs managed JavaScript handlers on document mutations or timers, using Eventing nodes/resources in the cluster. OnUpdate/OnDelete/OnDeploy differ from arbitrary request-response workers.

facts.label: delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Rapid document changes can be deduplicated into one OnUpdate event; ordering is per document. Timers have a documented one-execution guarantee across node failures/rebalances but can be delayed by backlogs.

facts.label: delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: A complete general-job retry/backoff, failed-message queue and arbitrary replay contract was not established.

facts.label: schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Timers schedule callbacks against wall-clock time with persistent Eventing metadata; callbacks may execute on a different node and inherit the parent timeout. Scan granularity/backlog can delay firing.

facts.label: schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Function deployment feed boundary can be Everything or From Now; pause checkpoints mutation processing. These controls do not provide a standalone cron/queue-history storage plan.

facts.label: logs and run history
facts.value: Eventing has function log() files, lifecycle system logs, success/failure/timeout/backlog metrics and a UI Log view. Capella organization/project/cluster Activity Log events retain 2 years, a different scope from function logs.

facts.label: logs and run history
facts.value: Exact hosted function-log retention/rotation, per-run result retention and a failed-job replay UI contract were not established.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Not applicable to Capella as a self-hostable cloud platform. Related self-managed Couchbase Server needs its own administration/license review; it is not the same deployment mode or price.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Choose AWS, GCP or Azure and a supported region at creation. App Services region support has its own matrix; free clusters have a limited regional subset. Cloud/region/CIDR are not among the normal in-place modification settings.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Cloud Snapshots are initially in the cluster cloud/region. AWS/Azure clusters on Server 7.6.6+ can copy snapshots to two extra regions; GCP snapshot cross-region replication is unsupported, and Azure CMEK snapshots cannot use cross-region copies.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Export/migrate with JSON cbexport, cbbackupmgr, bucket backup downloads or supported XDCR. cbexport does not preserve scope/collection hierarchy; indexes/functions/configuration have method-specific export gaps.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Free-to-paid upgrade is not in-place migration: signup docs say the existing free cluster is deleted during upgrade. Back up first with cbbackupmgr and restore to the paid resource; a paid organization may create another free cluster separately.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: On termination there is no guaranteed hosted retention window; the MSA/fee addendum permit destruction of content/backups. DPA authorizes deletion subject to legal retention exceptions.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: An exact deadline for physical erasure of all customer data/backups after resource/account closure was not established.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Free tier lacks managed backup/restore, but cbbackupmgr can make client-run backups and restore free data to a paid cluster. Paid bucket backups are optional, scheduled or on demand; Basic offers 24-hour intervals, higher plans up to hourly.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Bucket backup series starts full, then incremental. Scheduled retention is 30 days to 5 years; on-demand backups retain 30 days. Cost-optimized retention keeps recent cycles for four weeks and only monthly restore points longer.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Bucket backups are per-item consistent, not a guaranteed cluster-wide point-in-time snapshot, and exclude cluster settings. Cloud Snapshots back up the cluster but exclude Memory Only bucket data.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: AWS N. Virginia pricing lists bucket backup USD 0.07/GB/month and Cloud Snapshots 0.14 credits/GB/month. Billing docs meter backup storage in GiB and apply regional/plan rates.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Bucket backup downloads: archive must be at most 5 TB; retrieve URL within 12 hours of readiness and start download within 1 hour after copying. Download-file storage and outbound traffic add charges. Cluster snapshots cannot be downloaded.

facts.label: file recovery and protection
facts.value: Attachment updates/revision parameters are documented, but a guaranteed long-term file-version/undelete/object-lock retention policy was not established.

facts.label: identity and old names
facts.value: Couchbase Capella, operated by Couchbase, Inc., now privately held after Haveli Investments completed its acquisition on September 24, 2025. Capella Operational is the transactional database scope used below.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: Managed hosted Couchbase Server under the Capella Master Service Agreement. Self-managed Couchbase Server is a separate product; a Capella subscription is not a license to self-host the full cloud control plane.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Operating, public signup. Haveli Investments completed its acquisition of Couchbase on 2025-09-24 and took it private. No Capella shutdown or customer-data breach was found in the checked product, release and status pages.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Current pricing calls Capella Analytics 'Operational Insights Capella' and says pricing is unchanged. Legacy Management API v3.0 was removed in January 2025. The old daily bucket-backup scheduling option was deprecated for new clusters in January 2023.

facts.label: vendor home and main markets
facts.value: Couchbase, Inc., San Jose, California, United States. Hosts deployments on AWS, Google Cloud and Azure; this vendor location is not customer data residency.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: Free/Basic: forums. Developer Pro: P1 response goal 8 hours, Enterprise: 30 minutes; both P1/P2 are 24×7, lower severities use business hours and longer goals. Support tickets via control plane; public Couchbase status page available.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: Formal paid SLA: Basic 99.50%, Developer Pro/Enterprise 99.99%, subject to credits/claims/exclusions. Paid single-node Basic/Developer Pro have no SLA; free tier is excluded. Maintenance and customer-scheduled downtime are excluded.

facts.label: free offer type
facts.value: Hosted Free is a recurring plan with monthly allocations, distinct from trial references in the legal terms. MIT local/server software has no vendor subscription fee; hosting/operations remain the user's cost.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: Hosted Free KV: 1 GiB storage, 1,000,000 read units/month with 4 KiB unit label, 500,000 write units/month with 1 KiB label.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: Hosted Free application allocations: 1 million HTTP requests/month, 20 GiB egress, 10 active CPU hours, 150 GiB-hours memory time, 10 GiB revision storage, 10 apps, 3 members and 5 custom domains.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: Free supports at most 10 Cron jobs per revision; paid removes that documented Cron count limit. Local software is not subject to hosted plan allocations.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: Unassigning a hosted KV instance removes app access but preserves the database/data for reassignment. Persistent local SQLite paths survive process runs; :memory: storage is discarded when the process exits.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: expireIn is in milliseconds and specifies the earliest permissible deletion time; a key can remain visible longer. Matching expirations set in one atomic operation expire atomically.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: No fixed hosted inactivity-to-KV-deletion period or post-shutdown KV recovery window was found.

facts.label: least paid commitment

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: Explicit ISO currency for the tariff, tax inclusion and a separate KV-only paid subscription were not established.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Pro KV includes 5 GiB, 5 million 4-KiB-labelled read units/month and 2.5 million 1-KiB-labelled write units/month; extra reads $1/million, writes $2.50/million, storage displayed $0.75/GiB.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Builder KV includes 10 GiB, 25 million reads/month and 12.5 million writes/month; same posted overage rates. Enterprise quotas/rates are custom.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Exact KV storage time-proration/rounding, read/write block rounding per key versus command, check/delete/watch/retry charging and metadata/index storage accounting were not fully established for new Deploy.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Pro/Builder app overages: HTTP requests $2/million; egress $0.20/GiB; active CPU $0.10/hour; memory $0.025/GiB-hour; revision storage $0.08/GiB-month.

facts.label: billing meters

facts.label: idle compute and scale to zero

facts.label: idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Idle cutoff is described as approximately 20–30 seconds in Pricing, but 5 seconds to 10 minutes in Runtime. An exact billable idle tail cannot be predicted from request counts alone.

facts.label: idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Self-hosted denokv can stop/start with its persistent volume when the chosen host supports it; the official Fly example uses scale-to-zero. This is infrastructure-dependent and no host bill is quoted here.

facts.label: data transfer costs

facts.value: Current scope, enforcement latency, reset behavior and KV/storage coverage of Paid spend limits were not established. Usage guide retains a past-dated future promise of controls before October 1, 2025.

facts.value: Exact action when new-Deploy Free KV read/write/storage limits are exceeded was not found.

facts.value: Serialized keys max 2 KiB/2,048 bytes; serialized values max 64 KiB. Values include supported structured-clone objects, arrays, typed bytes, maps, dates and other documented types.

facts.value: Transaction guide: getMany max 10 keys, 100 checks/atomic operation, 1,000 mutations, 800 KiB total operation including overhead, 90 KiB total keys; watch max 10 keys.

facts.value: List batch size conflicts: Operations says default 500 and Transactions allows max 1,000; current runtime API says default limit or 100, maximum 500 with larger values clamped.

facts.value: Acceptable-use examples include company websites, e-commerce and DB-backed APIs; prohibited examples include mining, highly CPU-intensive ML, media hosting for external sites, scrapers, forward proxies and VPNs.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Free pricing says personal use/smaller projects. An explicit unrestricted Free commercial-production grant, exhaustive eligible-country list and new-signup acceptance during the sunset were not established.

facts.label: primary type and other roles
facts.value: Our classification: transactional key-value database; hosted managed storage, embedded local SQLite and standalone self-hosted server. Change watching and local durable queue APIs are secondary roles.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: Native KV supports structured values, ordered keys/ranges, atomic transactions, key expiration and watching changes. Current hosted assignment gives isolated per-timeline databases.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: New Deploy supports managed application execution and Cron alongside KV, but explicitly does not support KV enqueue/listenQueue. Standalone KV Connect also lacks queue transport; embedded local SQLite/in-memory backends support queues.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Hosted app code uses Deno.openKv() with automatic per-timeline assignment. Local Deno can use explicit SQLite paths or :memory:; self-hosted clients use KV Connect URLs and tokens.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Current hosted reference publishes an external v2 connector URL and personal/org token support; the Node guide says external access to new Deploy is not exposed. Public instructions conflict.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Official @deno/kv client targets Node 18+, supports remote KV Connect, local SQLite native modules and in-memory backends. V8 serialization compatibility matters; Bun is rejected by default in the documented client path.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Hosted KV assignment isolates timeline databases; app code connects without an explicit access token. External access instructions require a personal or organization token. End-user key/record authorization remains app code.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Organization docs say all members currently have owner permissions. Self-hosted denokv uses an access token, and the operator must add a TLS-terminating proxy; the server itself speaks plain HTTP.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Hosted KV reference states encryption in transit and at rest. Local/server SQLite file encryption, filesystem permissions, secrets, reverse proxy and backups are the operator's responsibility.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: Hosted Deno KV uses FoundationDB according to the product Quick Start; embedded local KV and standalone denokv use SQLite. KV exposes structured key/value access, not SQL queries into either engine.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: Exact hosted FoundationDB version and a customer-selectable managed engine upgrade policy were not found. Self-host software release is separately recorded in C04.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Reads default to strong consistency, with eventual reads optional; writes are strong. getMany reads a consistent snapshot across its requested keys.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Atomic operations group checks and mutations with optimistic concurrency control: matching versionstamps permit commit; failed checks cause no mutations and return ok:false. Application code must retry conflicts when appropriate.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: A list operation reads snapshots in batches. Entries within a batch are consistent; a long iteration across batches is not one global snapshot. Batch default/ceiling wording conflicts under D03.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Hosted Deploy creates isolated logical KV databases for production, branch and preview timelines, assigned automatically. Local :memory: tests are ephemeral; explicit SQLite paths provide separate persistent datasets.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Automatic production-data copy, KV branch count/lifetime, branch-storage attribution and cleanup rules were not established.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Current hosted KV reference describes quorum durability across at least three primary-region data centers and read replicas in Europe/Asia. Exact current failover RPO/RTO and customer-controlled replica management were not established.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Self-hosted denokv is one stateful SQLite-backed server; the README warns against independent multi-instance auto-scaling. Its S3 synchronization mode can expose a read replica of an existing compatible backup stream.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: kv.watch(keys) returns a ReadableStream of current watched entries when versionstamps change; it may coalesce rapid changes and skip intermediate states. Official server/local feature tables support watch.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Native offline client write persistence, reconnect reconciliation and automatic client-side conflict merging were not established.

facts.label: extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Secondary indexes are application-maintained extra KV keys. Recommended pointer indexes reduce duplication but require index-to-primary double reads and atomic maintenance to avoid inconsistent keys.

facts.label: extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Unsigned 64-bit KV values support atomic sum/min/max. Native installable SQLite extensions, full-text/geospatial engines or managed vector indexes were not found in the public KV API.

facts.label: delivery and private files
facts.value: Not applicable to a separate file-storage module: none is in this Deno KV scope.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: Conditional binary storage: a serialized KV value must fit 64 KiB. Larger files need an application-defined chunking/external-storage design; a native complete-file upload/multipart/resumable limit was not established.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Live database access uses KV API/KV Connect (HTTP metadata plus Protobuf data path), not a native S3 file API. Documented S3-compatible buckets are backup targets/artifacts, not interchangeable live KV buckets.

facts.label: filters and mixed search
facts.value: No scoped dense/sparse/hybrid vector-query interface; ordered key/range selectors and manual secondary indexes are the documented query model.

facts.label: execution model and languages
facts.value: Hosted new Deploy: Deno.Kv.enqueue/listenQueue are unsupported. Deno.cron runs managed JavaScript/TypeScript handler code as a separate platform capability usable with KV.

facts.label: execution model and languages
facts.value: Embedded Deno SQLite and official npm local/in-memory backends support enqueue/listenQueue in an application process. Remote KV Connect, including standalone denokv, does not include queue operations.

facts.label: delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Local/runtime queue handlers are at least once, may receive duplicates and have no strict delivery-order guarantee. Failed handlers retry; backoffSchedule customizes delays, and keysIfUndelivered can preserve undelivered payloads.

facts.label: delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Default retry counts are backend-specific: official npm lightweight in-memory backend documents maxQueueAttempts default 10. A universal current Deno-local/SQLite retry count and exactly-once external side-effect guarantee were not established.

facts.label: delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Hosted Cron has no retries by default; optional backoffSchedule supports at most 5 retries, each delay at most 1 hour. Schedule continues independently; colliding runs/retries follow the skip-overlap policy.

facts.label: schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Local enqueue delay is in milliseconds; default zero. Enqueue may participate in an atomic KV transaction, allowing state changes and enqueuing to commit together.

facts.label: schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Maximum local queue delay, total undelivered-message retention, queue payload ceiling and portable per-backend capacity were not established.

facts.label: schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Hosted Cron accepts 5-field Unix schedules or structured schedules in UTC; register at module top level. Jobs run separately on production and git-branch timelines; Free max 10/revision.

facts.label: logs and run history
facts.value: Hosted Cron dashboard records execution status/history and links OpenTelemetry traces. Logs/traces retention: Free 1 day, Pro/Builder 1 week; app metrics history Free 1 month, Pro/Builder 3 months.

facts.label: logs and run history
facts.value: Exact hosted Cron history/result retention independent of telemetry, one-click replay and local queue dead-letter/history UI were not established. Self-hosted logs/results require operator-managed persistence.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Embedded: install Deno, enable unstable KV, choose a persistent SQLite path and grant file read/write access; or use :memory: only when data may disappear at process exit.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Standalone: deploy denokv binary/container with persistent volume and access token; use one stateful SQLite instance, add an HTTPS proxy, and maintain updates, backups and monitoring yourself.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Self-hosted feature gaps: SQLite instead of managed FoundationDB distribution/control plane; no KV Connect queues; no hosted per-timeline provisioning, plan support or vendor-managed recovery guarantee.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Universal minimum RAM/vCPU, production storage sizing and a complete safe monthly self-host bill were not established in the official deployment docs.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Current hosted KV reference fixes primary storage at Northern Virginia us-east4, replicated across at least three data centers with quorum durability; it describes read replicas in Europe and Asia.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Application execution regions us/eu/global are different from the KV primary region. Self-hosted SQLite/denokv data location and backup targets are selected by the operator.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Classic-to-new KV data is not automatically migrated; support assistance is required by the guide. October sunset announcement offers paying-customer migration support to Workers, without a published direct KV-to-Workers data map.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: KV list/get can read out entries for a custom export; values use structured/V8 serialization, and multi-batch listings are not one consistent snapshot. Self-hosted SQLite and existing S3 backup artifacts provide separate portability paths.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Hosted KV Delete removes all KV databases/data belonging to that instance; unassignment alone retains data. Generic database-link deletion wording does not override the KV-specific destructive rule.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Organization deletion instructions differ: January org reference requires support; March 12 changelog says dashboard deletion is available.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Exact physical purge timing for deleted KV, replicas/backups and user accounts was not established. Terms refer to a DPA, but an accessible official copy was not located in this search.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Current hosted backup entitlement is unresolved: generic KV Backups describes continuous customer-owned S3/GCS backups, but uses Classic project UI; new-platform launch notes say manual backups unavailable and current KV page provides no new backup workflow.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: A current hosted backup retention window, restore API/UI, separate backup fee, user-configured backup location and exact data recovery point were not established.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Self-hosted: operator maintains SQLite backups. denokv can sync existing compatible S3 backup artifacts, list recoverable points and check out a point via pitr sync/list/checkout.

facts.label: file recovery and protection
facts.value: Not applicable to a separate file-storage module: none is in this Deno KV scope.

facts.label: identity and old names
facts.value: Deno KV is Deno's key-value database API. Its hosted Deno Deploy service is scheduled to shut down after Deno's October 9, 2026 announcement; the open-source self-hosted implementation is separate. The Deno team is joining Cloudflare.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: Hosted: managed Deno Deploy service under Deno's Terms and Conditions. Local Deno CLI embeds SQLite; standalone denokv exposes SQLite-backed storage over KV Connect.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: Deno runtime and standalone denokv are MIT-licensed open-source software. Commercial use, modification and redistribution are permitted subject to the license notice/conditions; infrastructure is separate.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: On October 9, 2026, Deno announced that its team is joining Cloudflare and that Deno Deploy will shut down after six months of continued operation. The exact calendar shutdown date is not published. Hosted Deno KV on Deploy is affected; open-source self-hosted Deno KV is not included in the shutdown notice.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: The same announcement commits to one year of monthly runtime bug/security maintenance before ending Deno-led runtime development. Open-source code remains available; no separate denokv maintenance end date is specified.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Deploy Classic and subhosting v1 had a July 20, 2026 shutdown deadline. New Deploy KV data is not automatically populated from Classic; the migration guide directs customers to support for assistance.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: The new Deno Deploy platform was announced generally available February 3, 2026. Deno KV runtime APIs remain explicitly unstable and require --unstable-kv in the CLI.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Official denokv latest-release metadata: 0.14.0, published June 6, 2026 at 08:36:53 UTC.

facts.label: vendor home and main markets
facts.value: Current published legal entity: Deno Land Inc.; Privacy Policy gives a San Diego, California, USA mailing address. The October announcement separately describes the team joining Cloudflare.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: Pricing includes community Discord on all plans; email support on Pro/Builder/Enterprise. Support docs give email/ticket tracking; migration help is explicitly offered in the sunset notice for paying customers.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: Free/Pro/Builder have no reliability or email-response SLA in the plan table. Enterprise advertises 99.95% reliability and an email SLA, but complete covered-service/credit conditions were not established.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: Deno Status is public; self-hosted availability, monitoring and incident response belong to the operator rather than Deno Deploy's status page.

apps.name: DigitalOcean Managed Databases
apps.line: Managed PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Valkey, OpenSearch, and Kafka clusters.

free.text: $5 signup credit, expires after 90 days

cells.metered: PG/MySQL Standard $15.15/mo table; docs say from $15
cells.regions: 12 shared locations; some regions have limited plans

sql.math: The cost is capped at $15.15 a month, because 730 hours × $0.02254 an hour would be more. Engine docs also say from $15.
The provisioned node still costs $15.15 a month with zero traffic. Engine docs also say from $15.

files.math: Managed databases do not provide file storage.

jobs.math: Three Kafka brokers cost $148.80 a month. Separate worker costs are not priced, so the full job total is unknown.

facts.label: Free offer type
facts.value: First-team signup credit: $5, expires 90 days, nontransferable; applies to all products except SaaS Add-Ons. No recurring free managed-database allocation established.

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: Free use constrained by $5 shared credit and expiry, not a separately published database size/read/write/seat allowance.

facts.label: Inactivity, pause and deletion
facts.value: A regular inactivity sleep/delete interval for managed clusters was not located.

facts.label: Inactivity, pause and deletion
facts.value: Unpaid accounts move through hold, suspension and possible permanent resource deletion; fixed stage timings are explicitly unpublished. Deleted resources cannot be recovered.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: Main table Standard PG/MySQL smallest row: 1 GiB RAM, 1 vCPU, 10–30 GiB disk, $0.02254/hour and $15.15/month. Engine pricing docs still say from $15/month.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: Advanced PG/MySQL docs: from $130/month for 8 GiB/2-vCPU node; extra storage $0.115/GiB-month. Matching standby nodes bill separately.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: Other displayed entry rows: MongoDB $15.23/month; Valkey $15/month; OpenSearch $19.60/month; Kafka three-broker configuration $148.80/month.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Sized cluster/node time plus allocated storage; main table shows hourly rates and monthly caps. Standard SQL extra storage $0.215/GiB-month; increments in main table 10 GiB.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Monthly billing for prior resource use, with possible mid-month automatic charges by account tier. Taxes can apply.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: A customer-controlled managed-database pause/automatic scale-to-zero/wake contract was not established.

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: Traffic to/from managed databases does not consume the bandwidth billing transfer allowance, per engine pricing docs.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: Spend alerts email at selected budget percentages; database alerts do not establish a service-stopping hard dollar cap. Optional pausing described in the alert docs is for Serverless Inference keys.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: MongoDB blocks writes at 97% disk use. Valkey has configurable memory eviction policy. These protect storage/memory, not the invoice.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Default 10 database clusters per account/team, increase on request. PG/MySQL/Mongo cluster limit 3 nodes; Kafka 15 nodes.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: PG backend connections: 1 GiB=22, 2=47, 4=97; up to 21 PgBouncer pools and 1,000 client connections depending on plan. Pooling defaults to transaction mode.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: MySQL table: 1 GiB=75, 2=150, 4=400 available backend connections; documented memory-overhead formula does not align transparently with those small-node rows.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Valkey connections the greater of 10,000 or 4×memory MB; up to 200 new connections/sec per CPU; usable data RAM below nominal RAM. Storage not independently selectable.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Main table smallest SQL disk range 10–30 GiB in 10 GiB steps; Mongo smallest 15–25 GiB; OpenSearch smallest 40–200 GiB. Record/request maxima across every engine not located.

facts.label: Storage prices
facts.value: Not applicable to the managed database service's file-storage prices.

facts.label: File request and retrieval prices
facts.value: Not applicable to the managed database service's file operations/retrieval.

facts.label: Minimum storage and early deletion
facts.value: Not applicable to the managed database service's object early-delete minimums.

facts.label: Vector/index limits
facts.value: PG vector(1536) example supported; enable vector per database. Standard vectorscale supplies disk-resident StreamingDiskANN/SBQ; HNSW is memory-bound.

facts.label: Vector/index limits
facts.value: OpenSearch k-NN graph indexes supported; no disk-resident ANN option on Managed OpenSearch. Changing vector engine/dimension/space type requires new index/reindex.

facts.label: Vector/index limits
facts.value: Managed numeric maximum dimensions, index count, namespaces and metadata limits not established.

facts.label: Embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: Embeddings may be generated externally or via OpenSearch ML Commons remote connector; provider API key and allowed external endpoint needed.

facts.label: Embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: Included embedding/reranking price or free model quota not located in database pricing/terms.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Kafka displayed entry $148.80/month for three brokers; no dedicated per-job 0.5-vCPU/0.5-GB worker allocation, execution timeout or invocation price established.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Public signup and valid payment method required before creating resources; credit is not a no-payment-method signup offer. Payment options include cards and alternatives.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Terms require trade/sanctions compliance and restrict sanctioned regions/parties. A complete current signup country allow/deny list not located.

facts.label: Primary type and other roles
facts.value: Our classification: managed databases; SQL (PostgreSQL/MySQL), document (MongoDB), key/value (Valkey), search/vector (OpenSearch/Postgres) and event streaming (Kafka).

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Engine-specific managed updates, network access, logs and metrics; backup/PITR and forking differ. This fee does not bundle Spaces uploads, app login or general function hosting.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: PostgreSQL native SQL clients/URIs; Control Panel, doctl and REST API for management, with official Godo (Go) and PyDo (Python) examples.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Other engine clients/protocols depend on selected engine: MySQL, MongoDB, Redis-compatible Valkey, Kafka brokers and OpenSearch APIs; do not use one PostgreSQL client for all.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: PostgreSQL encryption: LUKS at rest, TLS in transit. Trusted sources restrict incoming app servers/resources/IPs; private hostname is for the same VPC.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: PG Standard verify-full uses downloaded CA; Advanced uses system trust, libpq 16+ and sslrootcert=system. Default require encrypts without server identity verification.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: PostgreSQL has no full superuser; SQL access policy configured by roles/clients. MongoDB new users default to doadmin permissions; API supports read-write/read-only roles. OpenSearch exposes only doadmin, no managed user administration.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Trusted sources: 2,000 IP-address default limit; PostgreSQL security guide also limits to 100 firewall rules, no IPv6 trusted-source rules.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: PostgreSQL Standard new versions 15–18, Advanced 16–18, default 18. MySQL new Standard/Advanced version 8.4. MongoDB new 7/8; Valkey 8/9; OpenSearch 2.19/3.3/3.6; Kafka 3.9/4.2/4.3.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: PG/MySQL Standard and Advanced are distinct managed architectures. Advanced PG has consensus leader election and pooler; MySQL has consensus replication and proxy.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: PostgreSQL engine default Read Committed uses statement snapshots; Repeatable Read/Serializable available and can need retry. MySQL InnoDB default Repeatable Read; four standard isolation levels supported.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: Managed MongoDB default read/write concern and exact transaction/topology behavior not established from inspected DO pages.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: Valkey advertises atomic operations and Lua scripting; this is not a blanket SQL rollback or cross-service transaction promise.

facts.label: Test environments and branches
facts.value: Forking offered for PG/MySQL/Mongo/Valkey/OpenSearch, not Kafka. Valkey forks require default persistence:rdb; persistence:off prevents them.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Single-node automatic replacement has a single point of failure; standby replicas provide redundancy. Backups/WAL recovery can lose recent writes; overview says WAL backup interval five minutes.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Advanced PG 1/2/3-node topology; Advanced MySQL 1 or 3 nodes, HA requires 3. Proxy/pooler stabilizes endpoint but existing connections can break.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Limits say Advanced lacks Shared CPU, but Oct 15 plan notice explicitly adds it. New availability must be verified for selected account/region.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: PostgreSQL session pooling supports LISTEN/NOTIFY; streaming/caching engines can feed app events. A complete client offline-sync/conflict-merging SDK was not found.

facts.label: Extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Standard PG18 catalog includes PostGIS, pg_trgm, vector, vectorscale and pg_cron. Advanced has restricted catalog: vector pre-installed; pg_trgm available; PostGIS/vectorscale/pg_cron not listed.

facts.label: Upload and file limits
facts.value: Not applicable to the managed database service's multipart file uploads.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Not applicable to the managed database service's S3 object endpoint.

facts.label: Delivery and private files
facts.value: Not applicable to the managed database service's CDN/private-file delivery.

facts.label: Filters and mixed search
facts.value: PG hybrid guide combines tsvector/GIN keyword search and vector ranking with reciprocal-rank fusion and SQL filters; OpenSearch bundles hybrid-search plugins.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: Kafka is managed event-stream storage/brokers; application consumers/workers run elsewhere. Standard PG offers pg_cron SQL scheduling; Advanced catalog does not list pg_cron.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Topic replication and acknowledgements configurable; a general exactly-once business-job/retry/dead-letter contract was not located.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Kafka topic retention_ms/retention_bytes, cleanup policy and max_message_bytes configurable; Terraform partition default/minimum 3, maximum 2,048, replica minimum/default 2.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: UI topic guide says both time/size conditions must apply; Terraform describes separate time/size limits without resolving combined-condition semantics. Default retention and exact managed maximum payload not verified.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Logs/metrics exist, but fixed broker-log retention and application job run-history/replay retention were not established.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Not applicable: this is vendor-managed infrastructure. Running native engines on a Droplet is a separate self-managed deployment, not a free edition of this service.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Six engines listed in nyc1/2/3, ams3, sfo2/3, sgp1, lon1, fra1, tor1, blr1, syd1. atl1/ric1/mkc1/mem1 have partial plan availability.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Standbys remain in the primary's region; read-only nodes can be geographic replicas where edition permits. MongoDB cannot relocate/cross-region fork; export/import needed.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Full backup-location matrix and a guarantee that all account/support metadata stays in chosen database region were not established.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Destroying a PG cluster irreversibly removes contents and automated backups; export before deletion. Control Panel, CLI and API deletion available.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: PG exit options include pg_dump/pg_restore and aiven-db-migrate. Vendor's third-party migration guide only states PG12–17 support, not current default PG18.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: DPA §7.6: delete covered Personal Data within 30 days of deactivation, with no interruption by relogin; legal/archived backup exceptions. Privacy separately says account data within 90 days of purging.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Terms permit immediate forfeiture/destruction on termination and provide no obligation to return content after closure; export first.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: PG daily backups/PITR retain 7 days; restore creates new primary and requires re-adding standbys/read-only nodes. Backup time cannot be changed.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: MySQL, MongoDB and OpenSearch have 7-day PITR paths in engine limits/feature matrix; Valkey and Kafka do not support backup/restore/PITR equivalently.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Kafka limits contain generic seven-day PITR known-issue text despite explicit no-PITR/no-backups engine section.

facts.label: File recovery and protection
facts.value: Not applicable to the managed database service's object version recovery.

facts.label: Identity and old names
facts.value: DigitalOcean Managed Databases, operated by DigitalOcean, LLC. Redis-based Managed Caching is no longer available for new clusters as of 2025-04-30; Valkey is the current cache engine.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Vendor-hosted, managed nodes on DigitalOcean infrastructure; no self-hosted edition of this control-plane service established.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Operating. Standard SQL restrictions apply to new clusters from Oct 15, 2026 for accounts with no previous PG/MySQL cluster, and Nov 30 for all accounts. New Standard limited to 1/2/4 GiB and no standby/read-only nodes.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Existing SQL clusters are exempt from that plan restriction, including resizing, forks/restores and adding replicas. Advanced receives 8–64 GiB Basic Shared CPU options per the notice.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: DigitalOcean MySQL 8.0 reached end of life on October 30, 2026; forced upgrades to 8.4 begin during maintenance windows, with disconnections even for HA clusters.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: New Redis-based Managed Caching cluster creation stopped on April 30, 2025; Valkey is the replacement cache engine. The notice confirms the new-cluster cutoff but does not say existing Redis clusters were shut down.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: PostgreSQL Standard v14 is scheduled to reach end of life on November 12, 2026; it became unavailable to new clusters on May 12, 2026. New PostgreSQL defaults to v18; Kafka defaults to 4.3 and Valkey to 9.

facts.label: Vendor home and main markets
facts.value: Legal provider DigitalOcean, LLC; a complete eligible-country/customer-market list was not established.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Starter: free ticket support, advertised <24h response. Developer $24/month <8h; Standard $99 <2h; Premium $999 <30min. Higher plans add channels.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Database SLA targets 99.95% with standby nodes; 99.5% without. Per cluster, external-connectivity outage >5 minutes, exclusions apply.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Future credit remedy, claim by end of second following billing cycle with logs/evidence; >$1 credit threshold. Maintenance, app problems and overload excluded.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Public status page provides service components and incident history.

apps.name: DigitalOcean Spaces
apps.line: Store objects with an S3-compatible API and optional CDN delivery.

free.text: $5 signup credit, expires after 90 days

cells.regions: 13 Standard regions; Cold Storage excludes BLR1

sql.math: Spaces is object storage, not a database
Spaces is object storage, not a database

files.math: The $5 subscription includes 250 GiB stored and 1,024 GiB outbound. 100 GB stored and 100 GB out fit within those amounts.

jobs.math: Spaces stores files; it does not run background jobs

facts.label: Free offer type
facts.value: No recurring free Spaces tier is published. New DigitalOcean teams may use the general one-time USD $5 signup credit for up to 90 days.

facts.label: Historical trial
facts.value: Spaces release notes say the Spaces free trial was deprecated on 27 September 2018. The current signup credit is a separate account offer.

facts.label: Promotional allowance limits
facts.value: The published signup allowance is USD $5 credit per first team, expiring after 90 days. It is not a storage quota or recurring monthly free amount.

facts.label: Inactivity pause or data expiry
facts.value: No idle-bucket sleep, pause, or inactivity-expiry interval was published in Spaces pricing, limits, creation docs, or service terms checked.

facts.label: Unpaid account handling
facts.value: For unresolved past-due accounts, DigitalOcean may suspend the account, power down resources, and later permanently delete resources. It publishes no fixed time from past-due status to deletion.

facts.label: Least ongoing Standard commitment
facts.value: USD $5.00 per month for the Spaces Standard Storage subscription. It starts with the first bucket and ends when all buckets are destroyed; cancellation is hourly prorated.

facts.label: Cold-only base subscription
facts.value: The exact minimum total for an account using only Cold Storage is unclear: the pricing page defines the USD $5.00 base as a Standard Storage subscription, while separately listing Cold storage and shared bandwidth meters.

facts.label: Billing currency and taxes
facts.value: DigitalOcean invoices and accepts payment in USD only. Prices exclude taxes unless stated otherwise; applicable taxes depend on account location and law.

facts.label: Standard storage allowance and overage
facts.value: Standard subscription includes 250 GiB of storage shared across buckets; storage above that allowance is USD $0.02 per GiB per month.

facts.label: Standard outbound allowance and overage
facts.value: Subscription includes 1,024 GiB of outbound data transfer across buckets; additional transfer to the internet is USD $0.01 per GiB.

facts.label: Inbound transfer
facts.value: Upload/inbound bandwidth to Spaces does not count against the Spaces outbound transfer allowance.

facts.label: Regional Droplet transfer exceptions
facts.value: Publicly listed free outbound transfers apply from NYC3 to NYC1/2/3; SGP1 to SGP1; SFO2 or SFO3 to SFO1/2/3; AMS3 to AMS2/3; FRA1, SYD1, BLR1, ATL1, LON1, or TOR1 to a Droplet in the same named region.

facts.label: Private VPC Spaces transfer
facts.value: Droplets using the VPC-local DNS resolver can reach Spaces through DigitalOcean's internal network without using the Spaces outbound allowance. Cross-region internal routing is listed for AMS, NYC, and SFO region groups; other cross-group traffic uses the public endpoint and standard rate.

facts.label: CDN price and transfer meter
facts.value: CDN has no additional subscription price. CDN delivery and transfer from bucket origin to edge use the same shared Spaces outbound allowance and overage rate.

facts.label: Cold storage rate
facts.value: Cold Storage is billed at USD $0.007 per GiB stored per month.

facts.label: Cold retrieval rate
facts.value: Cold Storage retrieval costs USD $0.01 per GiB retrieved, subject to the published average-daily-usage retrieval waiver.

facts.label: Cold retrieval waiver
facts.value: Retrieval charges are waived for the amount of Cold data retrieved up to that account's average daily Cold Storage usage for the month.

facts.label: Cold minimum and early delete
facts.value: Cold objects have a 30-day minimum storage charge. Early deletions beyond the first 250 GiB each month are charged proportionally for remaining days; overwriting is billed as deleting then creating.

facts.label: Standard request charges
facts.value: The Standard pricing table lists the subscription, storage overage, and bandwidth overage; it does not list an additional per-request charge.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Not applicable. Spaces stores objects and does not run customer application compute.

facts.label: Internet transfer direction
facts.value: Outbound bucket-to-internet transfer is pooled at 1,024 GiB per subscription then charged USD $0.01/GiB; inbound transfer is not counted against this allowance.

facts.label: Cross-region object move costs
facts.value: A bucket cannot move directly across regions; the documented method creates a destination bucket and copies objects with a compatible client such as rclone. Cross-region transfers use download/upload rather than cross-region CopyObject.

facts.label: Cross-provider transfer rate
facts.value: No standalone Spaces price for transferring a bucket to another provider was published in the Spaces pricing and migration pages checked.

facts.label: What happens at included quota
facts.value: Storage and outbound transfer above the included amounts are billed at published overage rates; the docs do not describe an automatic hard stop at 250 GiB or 1,024 GiB.

facts.label: Spend alerts
facts.value: Team or organization spend alerts email when actual spending crosses user-set monthly budget percentages. Alerts can track specific products; the docs do not describe them as a Spaces usage cutoff.

facts.label: Billing suspension
facts.value: Unresolved past-due balances may lead to suspension and permanent resource deletion. DigitalOcean says the timing between stages varies by account and gives no fixed schedule.

facts.label: Prepaid or usage commitment
facts.value: The normal Spaces monthly price is usage-billed and cancellable by destroying all buckets; no Spaces-specific committed-use minimum was found in its pricing page.

facts.label: Standard storage rate
facts.value: USD $5.00/month subscription includes 250 GiB across buckets; extra Standard storage is USD $0.02/GiB/month.

facts.label: Cold Storage rate
facts.value: USD $0.007/GiB/month, charged by stored amount; separate from Standard bucket storage.

facts.label: Billing unit and tax
facts.value: Prices are in USD and use GiB units in the Spaces price table; prices exclude applicable tax.

facts.label: Region price split
facts.value: The pricing page gives one rate per class and meter rather than separate rates for each available bucket region.

facts.label: Standard request pricing
facts.value: The current Spaces pricing page does not publish a separate per-GET, PUT, LIST, or other Standard request charge.

facts.label: Cold retrieval price
facts.value: USD $0.01 per GiB retrieved; waiver applies up to the average daily Cold usage for the month.

facts.label: Cold minimum retrieval billing
facts.value: Each Cold object read has a minimum retrieval billing amount of 128 KiB, including partial or smaller reads.

facts.label: Cold per-bucket operation rates
facts.value: Cold buckets support up to 450 write, 250 read, and 25 list requests per second per bucket.

facts.label: Standard minimum object size
facts.value: Standard objects have a minimum billable size of 4 KiB, rounded up; stored size includes data and metadata.

facts.label: Cold minimum object size
facts.value: Cold objects smaller than 128 KiB are billed as 128 KiB.

facts.label: Cold retention minimum
facts.value: Each Cold object has a 30-day minimum storage charge.

facts.label: Early-deletion allowance
facts.value: The first 250 GiB per month of early-deleted Cold data is exempt from early-delete charges; additional early deletions are charged proportionally for remaining days.

facts.label: Signup path
facts.value: A user can start through the DigitalOcean control panel by creating a bucket; the first bucket starts the Spaces subscription. No signup was submitted.

facts.label: Payment methods
facts.value: DigitalOcean documents cards, PayPal, Google Pay, Apple Pay, Alipay, Link, limited-availability crypto, and US ACH bank debit.

facts.label: Signup credit
facts.value: DigitalOcean automatically applies a USD $5 credit to the first team; it expires 90 days after signup and applies to products except SaaS add-ons. A valid payment method is required before creating resources.

facts.label: Signup country eligibility
facts.value: A complete country-by-country eligibility list for opening a Spaces account was not found in the product setup, payment-method, billing, or service-term pages checked.

facts.label: Service use restrictions
facts.value: The acceptable-use rules prohibit unlawful, abusive, infringing, or harmful use of DigitalOcean services.

facts.label: Commercial use
facts.value: The product and pricing pages describe paid object storage for apps and business use; they do not limit the Standard subscription to development or non-commercial use.

facts.label: Primary type
facts.value: Hosted object and file storage. Data is stored in buckets as objects.

facts.label: Other roles and scope
facts.value: S3-compatible origin storage, optional public file delivery, static website endpoint, and built-in CDN for Standard Storage. It is not a transactional database.

facts.label: Main included service
facts.value: Spaces provides hosted buckets and objects with an S3-compatible API; inbound uploads are accepted and Standard storage can be delivered from its origin endpoint.

facts.label: CDN inclusion
facts.value: Standard Storage can enable the built-in CDN without a separate CDN subscription fee. The CDN's origin and edge transfer still count toward the Spaces transfer allowance.

facts.label: Other backend services
facts.value: Spaces is storage and delivery; its product docs do not describe built-in database, user authentication, application compute, or job-runner services.

facts.label: API and endpoint
facts.value: Spaces exposes an S3-compatible API at a region endpoint in the form <region>.digitaloceanspaces.com; each bucket also has its own origin URL.

facts.label: Client libraries
facts.value: Official docs give setup examples for AWS SDKs for JavaScript, Go, PHP, Python/Boto3, Ruby, and .NET.

facts.label: CLI and migration tools
facts.value: DigitalOcean documents S3-compatible tools including s3cmd, AWS CLI, and rclone for object operations and transfers.

facts.label: Authentication signing
facts.value: Spaces supports AWS Signature Version 4 (recommended) and Signature Version 2 for older clients.

facts.label: Temporary file access
facts.value: S3 presigned URLs can grant time-limited access to private objects without handing the recipient the Spaces key pair.

facts.label: Default file access
facts.value: Uploaded files are Private by default. An owner can set a file or bucket to public-read; anyone with a public URL can then read it.

facts.label: Access keys and permissions
facts.value: Access keys can be scoped to specific buckets with Read or Read/Write/Delete permissions, or granted full access to supported APIs. The secret is shown only at creation or regeneration.

facts.label: Key and account separation
facts.value: Spaces keys grant S3 API access, not control-panel access. DigitalOcean Teams manage resources in the control panel; one can share account/team access but not individual buckets through the Teams mechanism.

facts.label: Bucket policy support
facts.value: Standard Storage supports S3-compatible bucket policies through the API. Limited per-bucket keys cannot be combined with PutBucketPolicy on the same bucket.

facts.label: Cold Storage access
facts.value: Cold buckets require signed S3 requests with valid access keys; they do not support bucket policies, CORS, or public website/CDN options.

facts.label: Transport security
facts.value: Product docs say Spaces data transfers use HTTPS.

facts.label: Standard single PUT size
facts.value: Standard PUT requests can be up to 5 GB.

facts.label: Multipart part limits
facts.value: Multipart parts may be up to 5 GB and must be at least 5 MiB except the final part.

facts.label: Multipart object maximum
facts.value: Multipart upload supports up to 10,000 parts and 5 TB total object size.

facts.label: CDN presigned upload payload
facts.value: Presigned multipart uploads and PUT requests sent to the CDN are capped at 8,100 KiB (7.91 MiB).

facts.label: Incomplete multipart cleanup
facts.value: Incomplete multipart uploads older than 30 days are deleted automatically.

facts.label: Standard operation rate
facts.value: New Spaces buckets support up to 800 total operations per second; LIST operations may be further rate-limited at high load.

facts.label: Bucket and key counts
facts.value: Standard account limit is 100 buckets and 200 access keys; support can be contacted to request an increase.

facts.label: Object count
facts.value: Buckets created in or after July 2021 support up to 100 million unversioned or 50 million versioned objects.

facts.label: Bucket name rules
