facts.value: Bucket name must be globally unique, 3–63 characters, lowercase letters/numbers/dashes, and start with a letter or number. It cannot be changed after creation.

facts.label: S3 compatibility scope
facts.value: Spaces provides an S3-compatible API with partial support for Amazon S3 features; unsupported calls return NotImplemented.

facts.label: Supported common operations
facts.value: Compatibility table includes object copy, multipart upload, presigned URLs, object listing, and API-managed policies/versioning with restrictions.

facts.label: Cross-region copy restriction
facts.value: CopyObject and multipart UploadPartCopy do not support cross-region or cross-cluster copies.

facts.label: Bucket versioning
facts.value: S3 versioning is supported, but can only be enabled or disabled through the Spaces API, not the control panel.

facts.label: Lifecycle and logging limits
facts.value: Lifecycle supports time-based object expiration and cleanup of incomplete multipart uploads, not tag-based rules. Access logging is API-only and source and target buckets must differ.

facts.label: Encryption and website API gaps
facts.value: S3 compatibility supports customer-provided SSE-C keys, not bucket-level encryption configuration. Standard buckets support static website hosting, but CDN is not available for website endpoints.

facts.label: Public and private files
facts.value: Objects are private by default. Standard Storage supports public-read ACLs and private objects; presigned URLs can grant time-limited access to a private object.

facts.label: Built-in CDN charge
facts.value: Standard buckets can enable a built-in CDN for no separate CDN fee. CDN delivery and origin-to-edge transfer use the same Spaces outbound allowance and overage.

facts.label: CDN region and endpoint
facts.value: CDN is available in every Spaces region and serves from a global network of points of presence. Default endpoint format is <bucket>.<region>.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com.

facts.label: Custom domain and certificate
facts.value: A custom secure subdomain can be attached to the CDN endpoint with a DigitalOcean Let's Encrypt certificate or uploaded certificate.

facts.label: Default cache time and purge
facts.value: Default CDN edge cache TTL is 1 hour; it can be changed and individual cached objects or folders can be purged.

facts.label: Presigned URL CDN behavior
facts.value: Presigned URLs are forwarded to the origin and are not cached, so they do not gain CDN cache-hit benefits and can cause extra bandwidth charges.

facts.label: Cold delivery gap
facts.value: Cold Storage does not support CDN/custom CDN endpoints, static website hosting, public access, CORS, or bucket policies; only signed S3 requests are supported.

facts.label: Browser CORS
facts.value: Standard buckets support configurable CORS rules for browser requests from other origins. CORS does not grant object permission by itself; ACLs or bucket policy still apply.

facts.label: Standard regions
facts.value: Standard Storage is listed in NYC3, AMS3, SFO2, SFO3, SGP1, LON1, FRA1, TOR1, BLR1, SYD1, ATL1, RIC1, and MKC1.

facts.label: Cold regions
facts.value: Cold Storage is listed in the same regions except BLR1.

facts.label: Bucket region control
facts.value: The user chooses the bucket's datacenter at creation; the region is part of its endpoint and cannot later be changed. Moving data requires a new bucket and manual copy.

facts.label: Data-location legal promise
facts.value: The Terms say the customer selects a geographic region and jurisdiction, but also allow DigitalOcean to store or transfer content in other regions or jurisdictions unless agreed otherwise in writing.

facts.label: FAQ versus contract wording
facts.value: The GDPR FAQ says proprietary customer data uploaded to Spaces remains in the chosen region unless DigitalOcean informs the customer otherwise; the newer Terms allow storage or transfer elsewhere unless agreed otherwise in writing.

facts.label: Regional price differences
facts.value: No separate regional price table or region-specific rate was published in the current Spaces pricing guide; the guide gives one USD rate per storage and transfer meter.

facts.label: Export and local backup
facts.value: Objects can be downloaded with S3-compatible tools such as s3cmd; DigitalOcean states there are no built-in Spaces backups and recommends a second bucket, local copy, or third-party backup tool.

facts.label: Region or team migration
facts.value: A bucket cannot be moved directly to another region or team/account. Create a new bucket and copy its objects with rclone or another compatible tool.

facts.label: Bucket deletion and billing
facts.value: Destroying a bucket permanently deletes its contents after asynchronous processing. A pending-destruction bucket is not billed; destroying the last bucket ends the subscription.

facts.label: Bucket deletion timing
facts.value: Official pages conflict: the limits page says the bucket name is unavailable for a one-week pending-destruction period; the deletion guide, verified earlier, says destruction takes at least two weeks and may take longer with data size.

facts.label: Account-closure data timing
facts.value: The Terms say service content may be forfeited or destroyed at termination and DigitalOcean has no obligation to keep it available. The Privacy Policy says account data is deleted within 90 days of account purge, but that statement concerns account data/personal information and is not an object-retention schedule.

facts.label: Built-in backup
facts.value: Spaces has no built-in bucket backup. DigitalOcean recommends copying data to another bucket or local storage, or using a third-party backup tool.

facts.label: Version history and restore
facts.value: Standard buckets support optional S3 object versioning through the API; previous versions can be listed and restored by removing a delete marker.

facts.label: Durability design
facts.value: DigitalOcean says Spaces uses Ceph redundancy and fault tolerance to protect against hardware failures.

facts.label: Cold durability and recovery
facts.value: Cold Storage is described as having the same durability as Standard, but lower retrieval throughput and higher latency; the docs still recommend maintaining an independent backup.

facts.label: Recovery after account deletion
facts.value: The Terms and Spaces deletion docs do not publish a recoverable snapshot or restoration path after permanent bucket/account deletion.

facts.label: Current identity
facts.value: DigitalOcean Spaces Object Storage, commonly called Spaces. Vendor: DigitalOcean, LLC. Official product page: https://www.digitalocean.com/products/spaces.

facts.label: Former names
facts.value: No former name was identified in the product overview, docs, release notes, or product-tagged company material checked.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: DigitalOcean-operated hosted service. There is no self-hosted Spaces software edition or Spaces source-code license in the official product docs.

facts.label: Service agreement
facts.value: Spaces use is governed by DigitalOcean's Terms of Service, universal service terms, and product documentation.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Active hosted service. Current pricing, supported regions, API instructions, limits, and status components are published.

facts.label: Latest product release note checked
facts.value: The Spaces release-notes page lists an 8 April 2026 update: Droplets using the VPC-local DNS resolver can route Spaces traffic internally without consuming Spaces outbound transfer.

facts.label: Cold Storage release stage
facts.value: Cold Storage is generally available, not preview or beta, according to the product update dated 2 December 2025.

facts.label: Shutdown or sunset notices
facts.value: No Spaces-specific shutdown, sunset, or closure notice was found in the product release notes, DigitalOcean Blog, newsroom, or product overview checked.

facts.label: Parent-company acquisition
facts.value: DigitalOcean announced its acquisition of Paperspace in July 2023 to expand AI/ML offerings. The announcement does not mention a change to Spaces.

facts.label: General service-change clause
facts.value: The Terms of Service reserve DigitalOcean's right to change or discontinue services. It says the company will endeavor to give practical advance notice, with listed emergency, legal, and intellectual-property exceptions.

facts.label: Vendor home and main markets
facts.value: DigitalOcean says it is headquartered in the United States and has data centers and customers in the EU and other countries. This is company context, not a Spaces data-residency promise.

facts.label: Included support
facts.value: All customers get free ticket-based support 24 hours a day, 7 days a week; Starter plan target response is under 24 hours.

facts.label: Current service status
facts.value: The status page listed Spaces and Spaces CDN as operational when checked on 2026-11-06.

facts.label: Standard Storage SLA
facts.value: Spaces Standard Storage SLA commits to 99.9% monthly uptime per bucket, subject to its exclusions and claim process.

facts.label: Cold Storage SLA
facts.value: Cold Storage has a separate 99.5% monthly uptime commitment per bucket and its own exclusions and service-credit process.

apps.name: Dragonfly
apps.line: Redis-compatible key-value storage with managed Cloud and self-hosted options.

free.text: Self-host: 100 production vCPUs; Cloud bills active; no idle pause/deletion

cells.regions: AWS, GCP, or Azure; choose a region per datastore
cells.selfhost: Yes, DSAL free up to 100 aggregate production vCPUs

sql.math: 3 GB development instances cost about USD $36 a month. Whether the data fits, transfer and the exact total are unknown.
The 12.5 GB example costs USD $137.50 a month while active. Whether the minimum size fits and network charges are unknown.

files.math: Dragonfly has no file storage product.

jobs.math: Workers run separately. A 12.5 GB broker adds USD $137.50 a month, if it is big enough. Worker cost and the full total are unknown.

facts.label: free offer type
facts.value: Cloud: no lasting free datastore tier; the vendor advertises a free trial. Free Bronze support is a support entitlement, not free database hosting.

facts.label: free offer type
facts.value: Self-hosted current edition: recurring zero software-license charge within the DSAL free production allowance, with unlimited non-production use under its conditions. Hosting, operations and optional support are separate.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: Self-hosted DSAL free production ceiling: 100 aggregate provisioned vCPUs; replicas and affiliates count. The license does not express the allowance as a fixed free GB/read/write/project budget.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: Cloud free-trial storage, operations, seats/projects, credit ceiling and expiry were not quantified in the inspected public pages.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: Active Cloud stores continue accruing provisioned-memory charges without requests; deleting a datastore stops its charges. Cloud Terms reserve deletion of datastores and cessation of service for unpaid fees.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: No public automatic inactivity-pause interval, idle-deletion interval or guaranteed recovery window after a stopped/deleted Cloud datastore was found.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: Cloud Flex advertised starting at USD 36/month; documentation describes 3 GB development instances at around USD 36/month in popular regions, with provider/region-dependent prices. This is not a region-fixed guaranteed production plan price.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: Cloud Business advertised starting at USD 2,000/month; BYOC pricing requires a quote. Self-hosted Enterprise above its free production allowance also requires a commercial quote.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Standard Cloud charges per GB of provisioned memory per month, prorated hourly; provider, region and Standard/Enhanced/Extreme compute tier affect the rate. AWS us-east-1 Enhanced example: USD 11.0/GB-month.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Cloud bills all allocated primary and replica memory. Its example uses a 730-hour normalized month and rounds a partial active hour upward: 2 days + 1 hour + 10 minutes becomes 50 billable hours.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Network transfer and optional paid support are additional meters. The standard Cloud price description does not list a per-read/write/command or per-job invocation tariff.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Separate snapshot-storage/backup-request rates, all SSD-tiering component rates and a complete machine/region tariff were not established from the inspected price documentation.

facts.label: idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: An active, idle Cloud datastore still pays for provisioned memory. MCP documents explicit stop/start tools; no automatic request-driven scale-to-zero feature is documented in the inspected pages.

facts.label: idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: What data survives a manual stop, the exact restart path/cold-start behavior and any continuing stopped-store or retained-backup fees are unresolved.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: Cloud passes through public cloud-vendor transfer rates for internet, cross-cloud, cross-region and potentially cross-availability-zone traffic. HA replication can add cross-zone transfer; private networking is recommended to reduce cost.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: Exact tenant-level 5 GB internet-egress cost and applicable account allowances for the reference workload cannot be established without the selected network route/provider billing conditions.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: Cloud provisioned memory/tier can be resized. At capacity, NoEviction returns out-of-memory errors; Cache mode evicts items. These are data-capacity behaviors, not financial spend caps.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: Usage/cost information updates every few hours; transfer may lag up to 24 hours. Public guaranteed account-wide hard spend caps, budget-alert thresholds and their enforcement/exclusions were not found.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Known Limitations states up to two billion keys per CPU thread; lists/sets/hashes up to two billion values; string values up to 256 MB; command arguments up to 256 MB; TTL up to roughly 136 years (larger TTL rounded down).

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Self-host defaults: maxclients=64,000 concurrent clients; max_multi_bulk_len=65,536 command arguments (configurable); dbnum=16 logical databases. These defaults are not promised limits for each Cloud shape.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: The argument-size guidance needs care: Known Limitations says 256 MB per argument/string, while the flags page defaults the RESP parser's max_bulk_len to 2,147,483,648 bytes. The effective accepted/storable large-value boundary by build is unresolved.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Cloud single-shard documentation describes vertical capacity up to 600 GB; managed Swarm up to 15 TB, with larger needs directed to support. Up to two replicas can be added per primary/shard.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Cloud CPU:memory tiers are Standard, Enhanced and Extreme; Enhanced has twice Standard's CPU for the same RAM, Extreme four times. Published bandwidth tables list distinct provisioned shapes rather than arbitrary 1 GB increments.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: A fixed connection ceiling and guaranteed QPS/compute capacity for the cheapest development instance were not found.

facts.label: storage prices
facts.value: Not applicable to database-independent file storage prices: Dragonfly sells datastore capacity, not upload buckets.

facts.label: file request and retrieval prices
facts.value: Not applicable to upload/list/file retrieval and image-processing tariffs for a file product.

facts.label: minimum storage and early deletion
facts.value: Not applicable to file-object minimum sizes or early-deletion storage-class rules.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: Native vector indexes support FLAT and HNSW with configurable DIM; supported types include FLOAT32, FLOAT64, FLOAT16, BFLOAT16, INT8 and UINT8; distance metrics include L2, inner product and cosine.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: A maximum vector dimension, fixed maximum vector/index count, metadata-size allowance and per-tenant namespace quota were not established.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: Vectors and indexes consume provisioned datastore resources; the published standard Cloud tariff is allocated GB-month plus transfer, with no separate per-vector/search tariff in that price summary.

facts.label: embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: A bundled text-embedding or reranking model, its token/request allowance and an official model-provider price were not found. External embedding/reranking costs remain additional unknown inputs.

facts.label: run limits and pricing
facts.value: Cloud queue brokerage follows allocated-memory and network billing. Application job duration, CPU/RAM, concurrency, timeout, waits and retries also depend on the external worker host and framework.

facts.label: run limits and pricing
facts.value: Dragonfly-specific all-in per-job prices, maximum worker run duration and a universal managed-worker concurrency quota were not published in the inspected material.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Cloud: public account creation and organization setup; getting-started docs require adding a payment credit card before creating the first datastore. Homepage says account/get-started access needs no card.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Cloud Terms require age 18+, legal capacity and lawful use; Dragonfly may decline subscription requests. Payment documentation also permits AWS, GCP and Azure Marketplace billing.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Trial duration, credit amount, conversion rules and a complete signup-country restriction list were not found.

facts.label: primary type and other roles
facts.value: Researcher classification: key-value database/cache; secondary roles: Redis/Memcached replacement, queue broker, document/full-text/vector search.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: Native database services include Redis-style data structures, JSON/search/vector commands, Pub/Sub, Streams, server-side Lua, persistence and replication. BullMQ/Sidekiq are broker integrations that require application workers.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: The documented Cloud product manages datastores, networking, backups and monitoring. A bundled end-user login service, file-upload buckets or general application-function runtime was not found.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Redis RESP2/RESP3 over database connections; single-shard emulated mode accepts standalone or cluster clients, while Swarm requires Redis Cluster-aware clients. Memcached support is a separate specialization.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Officially tested Redis client libraries include Go go-redis; Java Jedis; JS/TS node-redis and ioredis; Python redis-py; PHP phpredis/Predis; Ruby redis-rb; Rust redis-rs.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Redis compatibility is a command matrix, not blanket parity: CLIENT TRACKING has limitations and some administrative/cluster commands are unsupported.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Cloud public endpoints enable TLS and passkey authentication by default; public passkeys cannot be disabled. Private endpoints default to TLS/passkey disabled and can enable them; private network connections/peering are supported.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Database ACLs restrict users, commands and key patterns; default-user permissions must be tightened where needed. Application users should be mediated by a trusted server, not given the datastore's unrestricted credential.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Self-host defaults include empty requirepass, TLS disabled and bind on all interfaces when no bind address is set. Operators must explicitly configure authentication, network binding, ACLs and TLS.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: DSAL includes usage reporting that may not be intentionally disabled; routine firewall blocking/air-gapped environments are explicitly permitted. The announcement describes environment metadata and says stored customer data is not sent in it.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: Dragonfly is its own multithreaded in-memory engine with Redis-compatible commands, not a hosted Redis distribution. It supports strings, hashes, lists, sets, sorted sets, JSON, Streams, Pub/Sub and specialized search commands.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: The latest self-hosted release checked is v2.1; the exact binary/version currently deployed to an individual Dragonfly Cloud datastore was not established from public documentation.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: MULTI queues commands and EXEC executes the transaction atomically; WATCH permits optimistic checks and EXEC can return null if watched keys changed.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Server-side Lua is supported in a restricted sandbox. Declared-key access is the normal path; permitting undeclared keys changes locking behavior and can lock the whole datastore.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: A complete published consistency/isolation and acknowledged-write-loss guarantee spanning Cloud Swarm shards, replica reads and failover was not found.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Cloud offers separately billed 3 GB development datastores. Separate stores can isolate testing, while choosing the cluster mode is a creation-time decision.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Native copy-on-write database branches, automatic pull-request preview stores and their isolated pricing/restore behavior were not documented.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Cloud supports primary plus up to two replicas, managed failure detection/promotion, and configurable availability zones. Swarm read replicas are enabled by default and require appropriate Redis client routing.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Self-host supports primary/replica replication; REPLICAOF can replace existing local data. Kubernetes Operator can manage failover with multiple replicas; bare-server deployments require operator-managed orchestration.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Native Redis Pub/Sub and Streams commands are listed as supported, including consumer-group read/acknowledgment operations in the compatibility matrix.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: A managed offline-client write queue, automatic reconnect reconciliation and conflict-resolution contract were not found.

facts.label: extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Native FT indexes support HASH or JSON records and TEXT, TAG, NUMERIC, VECTOR and GEO fields. These are Dragonfly command implementations, not a statement that arbitrary Redis modules can be loaded.

facts.label: extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Cloud SSD tiering is documented for AWS/GCP, requires Enhanced compute or a supported BYOC family, and can extend capacity eightfold by offloading large string values; keys and small values remain in RAM.

facts.label: delivery and private files
facts.value: Not applicable to native app-file buckets, CDN/custom-domain file delivery or bucket signed-download links.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: Conditional binary-in-database use: string values are documented up to 256 MB; there is no native file-upload multipart/resumable interface established by these database APIs.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: The app-facing protocol is Redis/Memcached, not a published S3 object API. Self-host snapshotting can write to an external S3/S3-compatible destination; that makes Dragonfly an S3 client for backups.

facts.label: filters and mixed search
facts.value: FT.SEARCH combines vector KNN with record filters; searchable schema includes text, numeric, tag and geo fields. FT.HYBRID combines keyword and vector retrieval with reciprocal-rank fusion or weighted linear fusion.

facts.label: filters and mixed search
facts.value: FT.HYBRID has specific constraints: KNN and RANGE are alternatives, and its FILTER option cannot be combined with RANGE. Query strings have a default 10,240-byte flag limit.

facts.label: execution model and languages
facts.value: Dragonfly coordinates queues as a Redis-compatible broker; BullMQ uses external Node.js workers and Sidekiq external Ruby workers. Cloud manages the broker datastore rather than hosting those application job processes.

facts.label: execution model and languages
facts.value: BullMQ configuration uses emulated cluster mode and hashtag locking; related queues need compatible hash tags. An undeclared-Lua-keys fallback locks the whole datastore and has a performance tradeoff.

facts.label: delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: A complete broker-plus-worker contract for retries/backoff, exactly-once execution, deduplication windows, failed-job retention and replay was not established.

facts.label: schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Delayed/recurring queue behavior, maximum retained job age and serialized job-payload limits require the selected framework/configuration; no universal hosted queue-retention period was found.

facts.label: logs and run history
facts.value: Cloud provides datastore dashboards and a Prometheus-compatible metrics endpoint. Self-host slow-log defaults include a 10,000-microsecond threshold and 20 retained entries.

facts.label: logs and run history
facts.value: A fixed Cloud job-log/result-history retention, included log storage/export allowance and hosted replay price were not found.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Self-host installation paths include Docker/Compose, Kubernetes Operator/Helm, binaries and Linux packages. Supported architectures are x86_64 (minimum Sandy Bridge) and arm64; Linux 4.14+ is supported, with 5.10+ recommended.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Operators run and update the engine, configure maximum memory, credentials/TLS/network policy, durable snapshot storage/schedules and restore tests, monitoring and HA orchestration. S3/host/backup/transfer bills remain external.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Current DSAL production vCPU counting includes replicas and affiliates; unconstrained test/staging use does not make live business workloads non-production. More than 100 concurrent production vCPUs needs a commercial agreement.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: A universal production minimum RAM/CPU or a sourced cheapest safe server for these workloads was not established.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Cloud offers AWS, GCP and Azure. A provider and region are chosen when creating the store; provider/region and cluster mode cannot subsequently be changed on that store.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Cloud allows one primary zone and up to two replica zones. Complete current region identifiers and a precise backup-storage residency matrix were not found in public material.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Self-host snapshot export can use Redis-compatible RDB with df_snapshot_format=false; default Dragonfly snapshots use multiple DFS files. Cloud can import RDB from an accessible/signed URL and restore stored backups.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Cloud backup download/export instructions and the completeness of a direct Cloud-to-self-host export path were not established.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Cloud Terms: within 90 days after termination/expiry or written request, return or permanently destroy customer data; contact details may be retained for internal records. DPA §11: delete or pseudonymize customer personal data within 90 days after processing ceases, with authorized/legal exceptions.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Cloud provides manual backups and scheduled hourly/daily/weekly backups, with configured retention in days and expiry. MCP manual-backup tool specifically documents seven-day default retention and up to 30 days.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Cloud restore clears the target datastore's existing data. Swarm backup contains all shards; restoring to Swarm requires the same shard count and replaces slot distribution. Single-shard to Swarm import is supported; Swarm to single-shard restore is not.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Cloud imports Redis RDB using an accessible URL, including a signed URL; the source must meet documented cloud compatibility. Exact point-in-time recovery to an arbitrary second and published backup RPO/RTO were not found.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Self-host supports SAVE/BGSAVE and snapshot_cron scheduling. Default df_snapshot_format=true uses Dragonfly DFS files; false writes Redis-compatible RDB. A configured shutdown snapshot can be loaded on restart.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Self-host snapshots can target local storage or S3/S3-compatible storage such as MinIO; the backup guide labels S3 snapshot support a preview feature. Operators supply storage credentials, retention and recovery procedures.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Append-only-file (AOF) persistence is currently documented as unsupported; the November 4 Enterprise announcement lists AOF among planned future features.

facts.label: file recovery and protection
facts.value: Not applicable to a database-independent file versioning/lock/undelete service.

facts.label: identity and old names
facts.value: Dragonfly, maintained by DragonflyDB; official URL https://www.dragonflydb.io/. The current self-hosted continuation is named Dragonfly Enterprise from v2.1; Dragonfly Cloud is the managed service.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: Self-hosted v2.1 onward: Dragonfly Source-Available License (DSAL), not an OSI open-source license. Production use without a paid commercial license is limited to 100 aggregate provisioned vCPUs across the licensee and affiliates, including replicas, standbys and failover instances.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: Self-hosted v2.1 onward: non-production development, testing, staging and CI use is unrestricted by the production vCPU limit; above the production allowance requires a separate commercial license. Standalone database/cache service or product distribution is restricted.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: Earlier self-hosted releases retain their own BSL 1.1 terms. The v2.0.0 file identifies Business Source License 1.1, restricts competing datastore offerings, and names Apache License 2.0 as its Change License; conversion is the earlier of its stated 2030-11-01 Change Date or the fourth anniversary of the version's first public distribution.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: Hosted Dragonfly Cloud: proprietary subscription service under the Cloud Terms and applicable Order; BYOC is a managed deployment option with separate pricing. The November 4 license announcement says Cloud is unchanged.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Operating with public Cloud getting-started documentation and self-hosted releases. Latest official release checked: v2.1, published 2026-11-04 at 16:10:57 UTC. New features and fixes continue in Dragonfly Enterprise.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Lifecycle news search: no Dragonfly acquisition or whole-product shutdown notice found in the inspected company blog, About/product material and /news section. The material change found is the 2026-11-04 Enterprise/license announcement.

facts.label: vendor home and main markets
facts.value: Licensor/service operator: DragonflyDB Ltd., a company incorporated in Israel. A complete country-by-country commercial availability list was not established.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: Cloud Bronze support: included free, business-hours console widget/email, best effort. Silver: greater of USD 199/month or 4.9% of monthly bill, business-hours support and 8-hour Slack response.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: Cloud Gold: greater of USD 1,500/month or 9.9% of monthly bill; 24/7 coverage, P0 response under 1 hour and Slack response 8 hours.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: SLA: 99.95% monthly availability target for multi-AZ HA; 99.5% for standalone. Development stores and console access are excluded; credits and exclusions apply, with claims within five business days.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: A public vendor-operated incident/status page URL was not established.

apps.name: FalkorDB
apps.line: Query property graphs with Cypher, vector search, and full-text search.

free.text: 100 MB RAM and a maximum 100 MB graph dataset

cells.metered: Startup $0.100/GB-hour; $73 per 730 hours at 1 GB RAM
cells.regions: AWS and GCP; Cloud Enterprise also supports Azure

sql.math: A 2 GB Startup plan is a $146 subtotal for 730 hours, if 1.5 GB of graph capacity fits. Transfer and extras are unknown.
The same 2 GB allocation, running for 730 hours, costs $146. Costs for a stopped month and any extra storage or backup charges are unknown.

files.math: FalkorDB has no general file storage.

jobs.math: FalkorDB does not provide hosted background-job workers

apps.news: News check 2026-11-09: no sale, shutdown, rebrand, customer-data breach, or license change found for FalkorDB.

facts.label: free offer type
facts.value: Cloud has an ongoing Free tier, not just a credit trial; no card required. It is presented for evaluation, prototyping and MVPs, with inactivity rules.

facts.label: free offer type
facts.value: Self-hosted software has no recurring hosted-plan fee under its SSPL license; you supply and pay for infrastructure and operations.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: Cloud Free: 100 MB RAM and maximum graph dataset 100 MB; multiple graphs and graph access controls within that instance; standalone deployment.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: Cloud Free: numeric monthly read/write quotas, connection limit, graph-count limit, project count and team-seat allowance not found.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: Cloud Free is stopped after 1 day without use and deleted after 7 days; deleted instance data cannot be recovered. It has no persistence or backups.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: Paid stopped instances are removed after 14 days; a final snapshot is taken before removal and remains restorable for the next 14 days. All snapshots expire after 14 days.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: Cloud Startup: $0.100 per Memory GB/hour; 1 GB RAM entry size, advertised $73/month on a 730-hour assumption. Maximum graph dataset at that size is 0.75 GB.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: Cloud Pro entry conflicts: the plans page and Pro FAQ start at $350 per 8 GB/month, but the same Pro guide lists a 2-core, 4 GB standalone configuration at $0.440/hour and $321.20/730 hours.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: Cloud Enterprise/BYOA: custom hourly configuration and contract; no public minimum commitment confirmed.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Cloud Startup meter: allocated Memory GB/hour at $0.100. Pro base meter: $0.200 per core/hour plus $0.01 per Memory GB/hour.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Cloud Pro replicated HA example: one primary plus one replica, each 2 cores and 4 GB, costs $1.300/hour; the guide also charges an extra 2 cores and 2 GB for Sentinel.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Cloud billing shows memory, storage, CPU, replicas and other usage; paid tiers are charged by hourly usage. Enterprise rates depend on custom resources.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Cloud ISO currency, rate-specific regions, exact sub-hour rounding/minimum charge, storage/backup extras and tax treatment not found in the public tariff docs.

facts.label: idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Cloud running paid instances use allocated-resource hourly prices; no automatic request-driven scale-to-zero rule was found. Zero queries do not reduce the published allocation formula.

facts.label: idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Cloud exact charges while manually stopped, wake timing and continuing storage/snapshot fees were not found.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: Cloud internet egress, inter-region traffic, replica traffic, backup download and import/export transfer rates/allowances not found.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: Cloud Cost Explorer and usage breakdown provide visibility. A documented hard spend cap, budget-alert threshold, overage grace period or universal automatic bill cutoff was not found.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Cloud Startup maximum graph dataset is about 75% of RAM: 0.75 GB at 1 GB RAM; 1.5 GB at 2 GB RAM. Pro table: 2 GB dataset at 4 GB RAM, 6 GB at 8 GB RAM.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Core configuration: RESULTSET_SIZE defaults to 10,000 rows; QUERY_MEM_CAPACITY has no cap at its default; MAX_QUEUED_QUERIES defaults to effectively unlimited UINT64_MAX. These are tunable server settings.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Cloud numeric connection cap, per-node/property size ceiling and plan-specific query/request quotas were not found.

facts.label: storage prices
facts.value: Not applicable: app file-object storage pricing.

facts.label: file request and retrieval prices
facts.value: Not applicable: app upload/list/read/retrieval and image-processing request pricing.

facts.label: minimum storage and early deletion
facts.value: Not applicable: object minimum capacity and early-deletion fees.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: HNSW vector index supports 1–4096 dimensions and cosine or Euclidean distance; vector values use vecf32 float32 data. Indexes can target node or relationship properties.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: HNSW defaults: M=16, efConstruction=200, efRuntime=10.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: Numeric vector/index counts, namespace caps and Cloud per-plan vector quotas were not found.

facts.label: embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: GraphRAG-SDK integrates external language/embedding models; its quickstart supplies OPENAI_API_KEY and model/embedder configuration. Cloud graph prices do not provide a sourced all-in model bill.

facts.label: run limits and pricing
facts.value: Core JS_HEAP_SIZE defaults to 268,435,456 bytes; JS_STACK_SIZE defaults to 1,048,576 bytes. TIMEOUT_MAX and TIMEOUT_DEFAULT govern read/write queries, with 0 disabling the configured limit.

facts.label: run limits and pricing
facts.value: Not applicable: an all-in 0.5-vCPU/0.5-GB background-job tariff or invocation allowance.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Cloud self-service Free, Startup and Pro subscriptions are auto-approved. Enterprise and Enterprise BYOA require approval. Signup asks for work email, name and company name; company URL is optional; Google/GitHub sign-in is offered.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Cloud Free does not require a payment method. Paid instances require one unless billing is arranged by contract; Stripe processes payments.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Cloud terms of use and Cloud privacy-policy text could not be verified; country exclusions, exact production-use restrictions, refunds and tax treatment remain unverified.

facts.label: primary type and other roles
facts.value: Primary: property-graph database. Secondary: vector similarity, full-text search and GraphRAG integrations. These directory labels are our classification.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: Both editions provide graph queries, graph-level access controls, range/full-text/vector indexes and a graph Browser. JavaScript UDFs extend queries. Consumer login, app file storage and general background workers are outside the documented database bundle.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: Cloud Free: no TLS, persistence, backups, HA or private VPC. Startup adds TLS and 12-hour backups. Pro adds continuous persistence and optional replicated/multi-zone deployments. Enterprise adds private customer networks and advanced monitoring.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Native Redis/RESP connection, normally port 6379; GRAPH.QUERY and GRAPH.RO_QUERY execute Cypher. Official client list includes Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Java, Go, Rust, PHP and C#.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Bolt support is experimental, disabled by default with BOLT_PORT=-1; enabling it uses the configured port, commonly 7687.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Both editions: ACLs restrict graph-name patterns and allowed commands; current docs also describe separate read/write graph permissions. Self-hosted ACL changes need a configured ACL file and ACL SAVE to survive restart.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Cloud database users: Read, Write, Admin and Custom ACL roles. New-user role starts at Admin; default instance user cannot be deleted or renamed, but its password and role can change.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Cloud TLS is available from Startup and must be enabled at creation; it cannot be changed later. Free has no TLS. Enterprise customer networks support peering and private IPs with no public endpoint.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: Self-hosted core: in-memory property-graph engine implemented in Rust from v6.0, loaded as Redis module graph; sparse-matrix/GraphBLAS architecture. Cypher/openCypher subset plus FalkorDB extensions, not full SQL or guaranteed full Neo4j compatibility.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: Cloud exposes FalkorDB graph/Cypher commands, but a plan-wide guaranteed deployed engine version or upgrade schedule was not found.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Core docs: each single write query is atomic, including compound clauses and schema changes. Writes serialize per graph; concurrent readers see a consistent pre-write snapshot.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Multi-query all-or-none guidance conflicts: FalkorDB recommends Redis MULTI/EXEC, but official Redis transactions documentation states runtime command errors do not roll back other commands.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Self-hosted: run separate instances locally or use GRAPH.COPY to make a consistent graph copy including indexes and constraints. Cloud can clone from another instance through RDB import.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Cloud branch counts, branch lifetime, copy-on-write billing and free development-instance allowance were not found.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Self-hosted: asynchronous single-primary replication; replicas serve GRAPH.RO_QUERY and may lag. Automatic promotion requires configured Sentinel or cluster failover; an ordinary replica alone does not automatically promote.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Self-hosted cluster partitions graph keys across Redis Cluster's 16,384 hash slots. A graph is one key and resides entirely on one shard.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Cloud Free/Startup are standalone. Pro supports standalone or primary/replica deployments in one or multiple zones; replicated HA has automatic failover and a higher published tariff.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Cloud Pro sharded-cluster availability conflicts: main pricing marks cluster deployment included; current Cloud overview and create-instance table reserve it for Enterprise/BYOA.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Native app-client live subscriptions, offline read/write synchronization and conflict-resolution guarantees were not found.

facts.label: extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Both editions expose range/geospatial, full-text and vector indexes through graph queries. Range indexes support nodes and relationships; full-text is based on RediSearch capabilities.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: Not applicable: general user-file upload limits.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Not applicable: exposing an S3-compatible object-store API.

facts.label: delivery and private files
facts.value: Not applicable: public/private app buckets, CDN and file domains.

facts.label: filters and mixed search
facts.value: Vector query procedures return nodes/relationships with scores and compose with Cypher graph traversals and filters. Full-text keyword search and range filters are also available.

facts.label: execution model and languages
facts.value: In-database JavaScript UDFs extend Cypher, loaded through GRAPH.UDF commands; a UDF can calculate values but cannot add, change or delete graph entities itself.

facts.label: delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Not applicable: general queue delivery, duplicate protection, dead-letter queue and replay guarantees.

facts.label: schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Cloud Pro/Enterprise support scheduled RDB export/import operations: up to 2 schedules per instance; periods at least 60 minutes in multiples of 15; start minutes 0/15/30/45. Disabled after 3 consecutive failures.

facts.label: schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Not applicable: general delayed-job payload size, message retention and consumer timeout.

facts.label: logs and run history
facts.value: Core GRAPH.SLOWLOG retains up to 10 slowest queries per graph, qualifying at 10 ms or more; RESET clears it. Cloud paid hosted tiers offer Grafana metrics, slow-query display and server-log streaming.

facts.label: logs and run history
facts.value: Cloud exact server-log and import/export task-history retention, byte allowance and paid export/replay policy were not found.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Self-hosting requires Redis plus the FalkorDB module or a packaged Docker image, enough RAM for graphs/indexes, persistent disk/volumes when required, credentials, monitoring, backups and upgrades managed by the operator.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: v6.0 Rust and v4.x C releases have incompatible replication protocols. Upgrade an entire replication group; current latest/6.0 images are Rust, while latest-alpine remains C v4.20.7 and there is no v6.0 Alpine image.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Cloud Free/Startup/Pro run on AWS or GCP; hosted Enterprise adds Azure; Enterprise BYOA uses the customer's AWS account. Provider and region are chosen when creating an instance.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Cloud complete region identifiers and binding residency/backup-location commitments were not established. Backup lists display region; snapshot copy allows a destination region.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Cloud exports RDB to a temporary download link, GCS or S3. Download links last 1 hour. Import supports a file up to 2 GB, a URL, cloud storage or another instance; data must fit destination capacity.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Cloud import erases the destination after taking a safety copy; moving tier or deployment type requires a new instance, import and client cutover, followed by deletion of the old instance.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Cloud unsubscription requires deleting its instances first. Exact customer-database erasure timing after ordinary deletion, account closure and backup expiration exceptions remain unverified.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Self-hosted: retain RDB/AOF files and migrate/restore with compatible versions; the operator controls volumes, copies and deletion.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Cloud Free has no persistence, automatic backups or snapshots; export an RDB while it is running if you need a copy.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Cloud Startup and Pro: automatic backups every 12 hours, retained 7 days. Manual snapshots last 14 days. Restore creates a new instance and keeps the source running.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Cloud Enterprise: automatic backups every 2 hours, retained 2 days; snapshots retained 14 days. Main pricing describes Enterprise backup configuration as custom.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Pro/Enterprise continuous persistence uses AOF plus snapshots; default appendfsync everysec can lose roughly 1 second of writes in a crash.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Self-hosted: configurable RDB snapshots and AOF persistence; appendfsync policy trades write durability against performance. You operate disk volumes, retention and restore testing.

facts.label: file recovery and protection
facts.value: Not applicable: user-file versions, object locks and file recovery.

facts.label: identity and old names
facts.value: FalkorDB; operated by FalkorDB Inc.; official site https://www.falkordb.com/.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: Self-hosted core v6.0.3: Server Side Public License v1, SSPL-1.0, dated October 16, 2018. Source-available software with service-source obligations.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: Self-hosted commercial use is possible under SSPL obligations; vendor offers a separate commercial license. Internal use has a different scope from providing FalkorDB as a service to others.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: Hosted Cloud: Free and Startup use multi-tenant hosting; Pro and Enterprise use dedicated hosting. Enterprise BYOA runs in the customer's own AWS account.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Operating public product and signup path; latest public stable release v6.0.3, published 2026-10-22. v6.0.0 introduced the Rust engine on 2026-09-29.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Cloud management API is beta; endpoint and request/response shapes may change.

facts.label: vendor home and main markets
facts.value: FalkorDB Inc.; stated address in Dover, Delaware, United States. A complete list of countries served was not established.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: Cloud Free and Startup: community support; support docs also list ticket email and Discord. Enterprise has dedicated support/account management. Public status page is available.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: Cloud Pro support hours conflict: main pricing says business hours; Cloud tier comparison and Pro Support/FAQ say 24/7.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: Cloud public numeric uptime SLA, exclusions, service-credit rules and small-plan response-time commitments were not verified.

Filebase provides object storage, not a database

jobs.math: Filebase stores and delivers files; it does not run background jobs

facts.label: Free offer type
facts.value: The Free plan is presented as an ongoing free tier, not a time-limited trial.

facts.label: Free tier expiry
facts.value: No expiration date is listed for the current Free tier; its public page says it remains usable within the plan limits.

facts.label: Shared account storage by plan
facts.value: Free includes 5 GB and Pro includes 500 GB, pooled across Object Storage and IPFS. Pro storage above the allowance is $0.015/GB.

facts.label: IPFS pinned-file count
facts.value: Free includes up to 500 pinned files; Pro lists unlimited pinned files.

facts.label: Bucket count
facts.value: Free allows 1 bucket; Pro allows 100 buckets. The plan table does not split this allowance by S3 and IPFS bucket type.

facts.label: IPFS egress by plan
facts.value: Current pricing lists 10 GB for Free and 250 GB for Pro per month; Pro overage is $0.015/GB.

facts.label: IPNS quota
facts.value: The current plan table includes 1 IPNS name on Free and 100 on Pro.

facts.label: Sites and gateways quota
facts.value: Free includes 1 Site + CDN and 1 Gateway + CDN; Pro includes 10 Sites + CDN and 5 Gateways + CDN.

facts.label: Bucket CID support
facts.value: The plan page says bucket CID support is not included on Free and is included on Pro.

facts.label: Object API included operations
facts.value: Current pricing includes 100,000 Class A and 1 million Class B operations on Free, and 1 million Class A and 10 million Class B on Pro.

facts.label: Free API request limit
facts.value: The pricing table labels Free API requests as limited but gives no numerical monthly request allowance.

facts.label: Pro API request limit
facts.value: Pro API requests are described as unlimited for normal use, subject to internal safeguards against extreme volumes; no numeric threshold is given.

facts.label: Inactivity pause or deletion
facts.value: No idle-account interval, automatic sleep, or inactivity-based deletion rule was found in pricing, FAQ, account, terms, privacy, or service-limit pages checked.

facts.label: Lowest paid plan
facts.value: Pro costs USD $7.50 per month, billed monthly and cancelable at any time.

facts.label: Enterprise price
facts.value: Enterprise is custom or volume-based pricing; an exact public starting price was not found.

facts.label: Taxes and cancellation
facts.value: Terms say listed fees exclude applicable taxes; cancellation takes effect immediately and accrued usage fees can still be charged.

facts.label: Storage usage meter
facts.value: Storage costs $0.015 per GB-month, based on average peak daily use during the billing period. The detailed billing docs define 1 GB as 2^30 bytes.

facts.label: Storage meter rounding
facts.value: Storage is billed fractionally by GB-month; the detailed guide says it is not rounded up to a whole GB or whole month.

facts.label: Class A request rate
facts.value: On Pro, Class A operations above the included allowance cost USD $4.50 per million requests. Operations are rounded up to the next whole million.

facts.label: Class B request rate
facts.value: On Pro, Class B operations above the included allowance cost USD $0.36 per million requests, rounded up to whole millions.

facts.label: Free request allowance discrepancy
facts.value: The current pricing page says Free has 100K Class A and 1M Class B included; detailed pricing docs say Free has 1M Class A and 10M Class B. I use the newer pricing page for current tiers.

facts.label: Free S3 API operation groups
facts.value: DeleteObject, DeleteObjects, DeleteBucket, and AbortMultipartUpload are listed as free S3 operations. Platform API requests are also described as free in the detailed billing guide.

facts.label: Billing currency and cycle
facts.value: Filebase states charges are in USD and billed monthly, on the signup calendar day, with a 30-day prorated cycle for partial months.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Not applicable: Filebase is a storage and delivery service; no user compute instance is part of these products.

facts.label: Paid S3 object egress
facts.value: S3-compatible Object Storage egress is free on paid plans with no monthly cap, according to the pricing docs.

facts.label: Free S3 object egress
facts.value: Current plan and free pages label Object Egress as free but do not state a numeric Free-plan cap; signup and detailed docs state 5 GB/month for Free, after which downloads are blocked.

facts.label: IPFS Free bandwidth discrepancy
facts.value: Current pricing and free pages list 10 GB of IPFS egress/bandwidth per month; signup docs list 5 GB/month. I use 10 GB from the current plan pages, while flagging the older signup-doc value.

facts.label: Pro IPFS egress price
facts.value: Pro includes 250 GB of IPFS egress per month; additional IPFS bandwidth is USD $0.015/GB.

facts.label: Inbound transfer
facts.value: Uploads to Filebase are described as free and do not count as bandwidth usage, including IPFS uploads.

facts.label: Separate region-to-region transfer rate
facts.value: No region-to-region transfer rate was found in pricing or endpoint documentation; S3 Object Storage has one global endpoint without per-region buckets.

facts.label: Free quota enforcement
facts.value: Detailed docs say Free accounts do not incur overages; exceeding storage or bandwidth makes the account read-only or causes downloads to return 403 until the limit resets or the plan is upgraded.

facts.label: Paid overages
facts.value: Pro storage, Class A/B operations, and IPFS bandwidth have published overage rates; the public docs do not describe an automatic spend cap at those limits.

facts.label: Spend alert and hard spend cap
facts.value: No user-set monthly budget alert or spend-cap control was found in pricing, account billing, FAQ, or terms pages checked.

facts.label: API high-volume safeguards
facts.value: Pro API requests are unlimited for normal product use, but the pricing page says Filebase may ask unusually high-volume customers to use a plan designed for that scale.

facts.label: Late payment suspension
facts.value: Terms allow immediate suspension without notice for late payment; storage not paid before funding depletion may be removed within 30 days.

facts.label: S3 storage rate
facts.value: S3 Object Storage has one storage tier at USD $0.015 per GB-month; no separate Standard or archive class is listed.

facts.label: Free and Pro S3 storage allowance
facts.value: The shared 5 GB Free and 500 GB Pro allowances apply to Object Storage and IPFS together, not separately to each service.

facts.label: IPFS storage allowance and overage
facts.value: IPFS uses the same pooled storage allowance; Pro storage above the account allowance is $0.015/GB.

facts.label: Region price split
facts.value: The price pages publish one storage rate and do not split it by data center or customer region.

facts.label: S3 Class A pricing
facts.value: Pro includes 1M Class A operations; additional operations cost $4.50 per million, billed in whole-million blocks.

facts.label: S3 Class B pricing
facts.value: Pro includes 10M Class B operations; additional operations cost $0.36 per million, billed in whole-million blocks.

facts.label: Free S3 operation allowance
facts.value: Current pricing lists 100K Class A and 1M Class B for Free, while detailed docs list 1M and 10M.

facts.label: Free operation types and errors
facts.value: DeleteObject, DeleteObjects, DeleteBucket, and AbortMultipartUpload are listed as free; unauthorized and failed requests are not billed in the detailed guide.

facts.label: IPFS pin API request price
facts.value: No per-request price for Pinning Service API calls was found in the current pricing table, IPFS API docs, or detailed billing guide.

facts.label: IPFS pin API request rate
facts.value: The Pinning Service API documentation gives a rate limit of 100 requests per second.

facts.label: Minimum object size and duration
facts.value: The billing guide says there is no minimum object size or minimum storage duration for S3 Object Storage.

facts.label: Early deletion charge
facts.value: No early-delete fee is listed; Filebase describes one storage class and no minimum object duration.

facts.label: IPFS unpin behavior
facts.value: Removing an IPFS pin or deleting its object stops Filebase from guaranteeing persistence; the CID may remain available if another IPFS peer has pinned it.

facts.label: Self-service signup
facts.value: The docs describe email-and-password signup with email confirmation; no account was created for this research.

facts.label: Free signup and payment card
facts.value: A Filebase account and free tier are available without a credit card or commitment.

facts.label: Signup email restriction and age
facts.value: Temporary email addresses are not accepted. The incorporated Terms of Use say users must be at least 18.

facts.label: Country eligibility
facts.value: A country-by-country signup or service eligibility list was not found in the signup docs, terms, pricing, or About pages checked.

facts.label: Commercial-use restriction on Free
facts.value: The current free-plan page describes small launches and real workloads, while the 2019 Acceptable Use Policy prohibits using free trial accounts to offer commercial paid services. The current free tier is expressly called a free tier, not a trial, so its commercial-use rule is unclear.

facts.label: Primary type
facts.value: Hosted object storage and IPFS pinning. The S3 product stores bucket objects; IPFS storage pins content-addressed files and exposes CIDs.

facts.label: Other roles and scope
facts.value: S3-compatible file storage includes a built-in CDN. The IPFS side adds IPNS names, dedicated gateways, Sites, and an IPFS RPC endpoint.

facts.label: S3 object storage service
facts.value: The object-storage tier provides buckets and objects through an S3-compatible API at s3.filebase.io.

facts.label: IPFS pinning service
facts.value: IPFS bucket uploads are automatically pinned; existing CIDs can be added through the IPFS Pinning Service API.

facts.label: Adjacent IPFS services
facts.value: IPNS, dedicated gateways, Filebase Sites, and RPC are available on the IPFS product side, with plan quotas shown separately on pricing.

facts.label: S3 connection protocol and endpoint
facts.value: The S3 API uses HTTPS endpoint https://s3.filebase.io, region auto, and Signature Version 4.

facts.label: IPFS S3 endpoint
facts.value: The IPFS-backed S3 endpoint is https://s3.filebase.com, with region us-east-1 for client configuration.

facts.label: SDK and client options
facts.value: The docs provide AWS SDK examples for JavaScript, Python, and Go, and list official SDK guides for Java, .NET, PHP, Ruby, and Rust; AWS CLI and other S3 tools are covered.

facts.label: IPFS client options
facts.value: Filebase documents the IPFS Pinning Service API for compatible clients such as IPFS CLI and IPFS Desktop, plus its S3 endpoint and Kubo-compatible RPC API.

facts.label: S3 bucket access default
facts.value: Object Storage buckets are private by default; public buckets allow unsigned HTTPS reads, and private buckets require authenticated requests.

facts.label: S3 access granularity
facts.value: Filebase issues one account-wide S3 key pair with full read/write access to all buckets; it does not support per-key scoping or IAM-style policies.

facts.label: Temporary S3 access
facts.value: Presigned URLs can grant one operation on one object until the URL expires, without sharing the account secret key.

facts.label: S3 encryption at rest and in transit
facts.value: S3 object encryption at rest and TLS in transit are on by default; the vendor manages encryption keys and includes no separate encryption fee.

facts.label: Customer-controlled encryption keys
facts.value: SSE-C is unsupported and the accepted aws:kms header is treated as AES-256 without a separate KMS integration.

facts.label: Terms versus current encryption docs
facts.value: The current S3 encryption docs say Filebase-managed at-rest encryption; the Storage Terms say users must configure appropriate security and refer to local encryption. Their coverage of the new S3 product is not clearly reconciled.

facts.label: IPFS gateway access controls
facts.value: Dedicated gateways can be public, limited to CIDs pinned to the account, or limited to an allowlist; optional HTTP Basic authentication is documented.

facts.label: Sensitive data restriction
facts.value: The Terms prohibit processing protected health information, cardholder data, and specified sensitive personal data requiring heightened protections.

facts.label: S3 upload method and single-request limit
facts.value: A single PUT is limited to 5 GB; files over 5 GB require multipart upload.

facts.label: Multipart limits
facts.value: Multipart parts can be up to 5 GB; an object can have up to 10,000 parts and total 5 TB.

facts.label: Bucket name and object key limits
facts.value: Bucket names are 3–63 characters; object keys allow up to 1,024 UTF-8 characters.

facts.label: S3 API rate and response
facts.value: The S3 API limit is 500 requests per second per account; excess traffic returns 503 Slow Down and standard retry-with-backoff is recommended.

facts.label: IPFS upload interfaces
facts.value: IPFS content can be uploaded through the console, the IPFS S3 endpoint, or by re-pinning an existing CID through the Pinning Service API; folders can be uploaded as CAR files.

facts.label: IPFS-specific file size limit
facts.value: A separate maximum CID size or maximum IPFS pin count per individual object was not located in the IPFS pinning, upload, plan, and service-limits docs checked.

facts.label: S3 operations fully supported
facts.value: The compatibility matrix lists core object reads, writes, deletes, up-to-1,000-key DeleteObjects, Filebase-to-Filebase CopyObject, and multipart operations as supported.

facts.label: S3 partial compatibility
facts.value: The matrix marks some features partial, including GetObjectAcl behavior, PutObjectAcl handling, and read-only versioning or lifecycle operations.

facts.label: S3 unsupported features
facts.value: The matrix says bucket policies, object tags, replication, inventory, object versioning writes, lifecycle writes, logging configuration, and archive RestoreObject are not supported.

facts.label: Marketing compatibility claim
facts.value: The About page says 100% S3 compatible, but the current operation matrix lists partial and unsupported AWS S3 features.

facts.label: S3 public and private behavior
facts.value: Buckets are private by default; public buckets allow unsigned HTTPS GETs. Public/private status is bucket-wide, and a bucket cannot mix public and private objects.

facts.label: Free-plan public bucket access
facts.value: The current public/private access guide says Free accounts cannot create public buckets; use private access or a paid plan for public object delivery.

facts.label: S3 built-in CDN
facts.value: Public S3 objects are served through Filebase's global CDN; the pricing and billing docs say there is no separate CDN fee.

facts.label: S3 CDN and private reads
facts.value: Authenticated private-bucket reads are not served from the public cache; presigned requests are forwarded to the origin and are not cached.

facts.label: IPFS gateway choices
facts.value: Current pricing lists 1 Gateway + CDN for Free and 5 for Pro. The docs describe dedicated gateways separately but do not make clear whether the plan counts mean dedicated gateways or a combined gateway allowance.

facts.label: IPFS Sites and custom domains
facts.value: Sites + CDN quotas are 1 for Free and 10 for Pro; custom domains are not included on Free and are included on Pro.

facts.label: IPFS bandwidth and delivery
facts.value: IPFS delivery is metered across IPFS S3 reads, dedicated and public gateways, Bitswap, trustless gateway responses, RPC, and Sites.

facts.label: S3 endpoint location setting
facts.value: S3 Object Storage uses endpoint s3.filebase.io and region auto; docs say there are no per-region buckets.

facts.label: IPFS endpoint region setting
facts.value: IPFS-backed buckets use s3.filebase.com and region us-east-1 for client configuration.

facts.label: Physical data placement
facts.value: About describes global infrastructure, but current docs do not give a selectable S3 region or clear data-location control. Older Terms and IPFS materials describe distributed nodes or geo-redundancy, so current placement guarantees are unclear.

facts.label: Region-specific pricing
facts.value: No different S3 or IPFS prices by region are listed; current public pricing gives one set of USD rates.

facts.label: S3 object export
facts.value: Objects can be downloaded with the AWS CLI, an SDK, or the console; Filebase does not provide a separate export bundle.

facts.label: IPFS pin migration
facts.value: Existing CIDs can be imported or re-pinned through the Pinning Service API; Filebase also documents migration tools and an importer.

facts.label: Account closure
facts.value: To close an account, usage must first be reduced to 5 GB or less, then a closure request must be emailed from the registered address. The guide says all buckets and contents are permanently deleted and keys revoked.

facts.label: Data recovery after suspension or termination
facts.value: Terms say suspended or terminated storage may not be recoverable; the service guide tells users to export before account closure.

facts.label: Deletion timing for billing data
facts.value: The account-closure guide says billing information is retained as required by tax/accounting law, typically 7 years; it does not state an exact object purge interval after account closure.

facts.label: Object backup and recovery
facts.value: Terms put responsibility for backups on the customer and disclaim responsibility for loss; the object API matrix does not support versioning writes or replication.

facts.label: S3 delete recovery
facts.value: No undelete or recovery window for deleted S3 objects was found in the object docs, compatibility matrix, and account closure guide checked.

facts.label: IPFS pin persistence
facts.value: Filebase says uploaded IPFS objects remain pinned while stored in the account; deleting/unpinning stops Filebase's persistence guarantee, though other peers may retain the CID.

facts.label: IPFS redundancy statement
facts.value: A 2022 Filebase post described IPFS content as replicated across three servers in different data centers and countries; no current service page confirms that this remains the current topology.

facts.label: Current identity
facts.value: Filebase, Inc. offers Filebase Object Storage, the S3-compatible object storage product, and Filebase IPFS Storage, which includes pinning and related IPFS services.

facts.label: Former product names
facts.value: No former name for the current Filebase Object Storage or IPFS pinning service was identified in the product page, docs, About page, or company blog checked.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Both offerings are Filebase-operated hosted services. The public docs do not offer a downloadable Filebase storage server or a self-hosted Filebase edition.

facts.label: Current S3 infrastructure
facts.value: The May 2026 launch post says the new S3 Object Storage service runs on bare-metal infrastructure operated by Filebase.

facts.label: Terms architecture scope
facts.value: The current Terms of Service, last updated 2025-11-20, describe third-party storage nodes, local encryption, and user-configured redundancy. The 2026 S3 launch describes Filebase-operated bare metal, so it is unclear how the older distributed-storage terms apply to each current service.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Active hosted services: current plan pages, setup docs, API docs, and an operational status page are available.

facts.label: S3 launch stage
facts.value: Filebase announced its S3-compatible Object Storage launch on 2026-05-20 and described it as available then.

facts.label: Current service retirement and acquisition search
facts.value: No current Filebase acquisition, shutdown, or sunset notice was found in the company blog, About/News page, current product docs, or current pricing page.

facts.label: Historical integration retirements
facts.value: Filebase said Skynet and Storj integrations would be removed on 2022-10-15, with affected data deleted after that date; it announced the Sia integration sunset on 2023-08-16. These were integrations, not the current S3 or IPFS services.

facts.label: Legal contact location
facts.value: The Terms list a Filebase contact address in Boston, Massachusetts. About describes the team as distributed and says it serves customers worldwide.

facts.label: Headquarters and primary market
facts.value: No official headquarters statement or primary-market list was found in the Terms or About pages checked.

facts.label: Support by plan
facts.value: The Free plan points to self-serve docs; Pro lists priority email support; Enterprise lists dedicated support, email, and Slack Connect.

facts.label: Service status
facts.value: The public status page showed API, dashboard, dedicated gateways, and public gateway online when checked; it did not list object storage as a separate component.

facts.label: Uptime promise
facts.value: Pro has no published uptime SLA; Enterprise pricing says an SLA is included but does not publish its percentage or full terms.

facts.label: Formal support response times
facts.value: No public first-response or resolution-time commitment was found in pricing, FAQ, docs, status, or terms checked.

facts.label: Policy currency
facts.value: The Privacy Policy and Acceptable Use Policy are dated 2019, while the Storage Terms are dated 2025-11-20.

Filestack is a file API, not a database

files.math: The Scale plan includes 350 GB of storage, 125,000 uploads and 400 GB of bandwidth. 100 GB stored, 100,000 uploads and 100 GB out fit within those amounts.

jobs.math: Scale workflow executions (runs) cost $0.015 each. A generic job does not clearly match one workflow run, so the cost is unknown.

facts.label: Free offer type
facts.value: Free is an ongoing hosted plan, advertised as $0 forever and staying active. It is separate from the time-limited paid-plan trial prompt.

facts.label: Free-plan limit behavior
facts.value: The linked Service Terms say Free accounts are not charged overages and Filestack may block service until the next billing cycle after a limit is exceeded.

facts.label: Free monthly file-service quotas
facts.value: Free: 500 uploads, 1,000 transformations, 1 GB bandwidth per month; 1 GB Filestack storage is a standing amount, not a monthly reset.

facts.label: Start plan limits
facts.value: Start: 20,000 uploads, 50,000 transformations and 75 GB bandwidth per month; 50 GB Filestack storage.

facts.label: Grow plan limits

facts.label: Scale plan limits
facts.value: Scale: 125,000 uploads, 300,000 transformations and 400 GB bandwidth per month; 350 GB Filestack storage.

facts.label: Enterprise limits
facts.value: Enterprise quotas for bandwidth, uploads, transformations, storage, workflows and maximum file size are custom.

facts.label: Maximum file size
facts.value: Maximum size is Free 20 MB, Start 1 GB, Grow 2 GB, Scale 5 GB, Enterprise custom.
