facts.label: Free offer type
facts.value: Pub/Sub has a recurring free usage allowance that does not expire, subject to Google Cloud Free Tier eligibility and changes to the offer.

facts.label: Free offer type
facts.value: New Google Cloud customers are offered USD $300 in general Google Cloud credits; this is not a Pub/Sub-only allowance.

facts.label: Free offer type
facts.value: The Free Tier page says the monthly product allowance does not expire, but is available only to eligible customers and may change.

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: The exact Pub/Sub service-pricing allowance is the first 10 GiB each calendar month of Message Delivery Basic SKU throughput per billing account.

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: The general monthly Pub/Sub Free Tier is shown as 10 GB of messages per month on the Free Tier and product pages.

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: The 10 GiB allowance is attached to the billing account's Basic SKU, not separately allocated per topic or subscription.

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: BigQuery and Cloud Storage export throughput and import-topic throughput do not receive the first 10 GiB free allowance.

facts.label: Inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: Pub/Sub documentation does not describe an idle-project sleep or pause policy; individual subscriptions have a separate inactivity expiration rule.

facts.label: Inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: A subscription expires after 31 days of inactivity by default; activity or a resource update resets the clock. The policy can be changed or disabled.

facts.label: Inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: A topic's published messages are not retained for replay unless topic retention is configured; topic retention can be set up to 31 days.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: The lowest ongoing Pub/Sub commitment shown is usage-based: the first eligible 10 GiB/month is free, then Basic throughput is billed by TiB. No fixed Pub/Sub monthly minimum is listed.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: Pub/Sub charges are separate from paid Google Cloud Customer Care plans; every Google Cloud customer, including Free Trial users, receives Basic Support.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Standard Message Delivery Basic throughput after the allowance is USD $40 per TiB in all Google Cloud regions.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Throughput counts bytes published to a topic and bytes read from a subscription; each publish and each delivered subscription read contributes usage.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Billable message volume includes encoded body bytes, each attribute key and value, 20 bytes for the timestamp, the generated message ID, and applicable optional fields.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Pub/Sub assesses a minimum of 1 KB for each request, regardless of the sizes of messages in it; batching small messages can reduce this minimum-size effect.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: BigQuery export subscription reads cost USD $50 per TiB in all regions; Pub/Sub adds no BigQuery data-ingestion fee, but BigQuery storage and extraction can still cost extra.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Cloud Storage export subscription reads cost USD $50 per TiB in all regions; Cloud Storage storage, retrieval, and replication fees can also apply.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Import topics from Kinesis Data Streams cost USD $50 per TiB in all regions; the source can add its own egress charges.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Import topics from Cloud Storage, Azure Event Hubs, AWS MSK, or Confluent Cloud cost USD $80 per TiB in all regions; source charges may also apply.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Direct Bigtable export is in Preview, but the Pub/Sub pricing table checked does not state a Bigtable-subscription rate.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Message storage is USD $0.27 per GiB-month; the Pub/Sub pricing page shows one rate and no regional price split.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Storage can be billed for topic-retained messages, acknowledged messages retained on a subscription, snapshots, and old unacknowledged backlog.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Creating a snapshot with an existing unacknowledged backlog adds a one-time fee equal to storing that backlog for seven days.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: User-defined single-message transform processing costs USD $40 per TiB in all regions, based on the larger of input or output message size.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: AI Inference single-message transform processing costs USD $60 per TiB in all regions, based on input plus the enriched message size; Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform charges also apply.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Pub/Sub pricing does not publish a fixed fee per topic, subscription, or message count; the listed meters are throughput, storage, transforms, and data transfer.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Scale-to-zero and idle worker compute are not applicable to Pub/Sub itself: it is a managed messaging service and does not run customer job code.

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: Pub/Sub charges no fee for data transferred into Pub/Sub; a source provider can still charge its own egress.

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: Pub/Sub has no zone data-transfer fee, but traffic crossing Google Cloud region boundaries follows VPC network rates.

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: Representative VPC inter-region rates are USD $0.02/GiB North America-to-North America, $0.05/GiB North America-to-Europe, and $0.08/GiB North America-to-Asia.

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: A message crossing a region boundary can incur transfer fees on each crossing, including separate delivery to multiple subscribers in other regions.

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: Egress from Pub/Sub to another Google Cloud product is not automatically exempt from network charges.

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: Filtered messages still incur throughput fees but have no transfer fee; the 1,000-byte minimum does not apply to automatically acknowledged filtered messages.

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: A topic project pays for a publish-to-storage region crossing; a subscription project pays for a storage-to-subscriber crossing.

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: Pub/Sub has no single public USD rate for every region pair; the applicable VPC table depends on source and destination regions.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: Google Cloud billing budgets can alert on spend by account, project, service, or label, but alerts alone do not stop usage or billing.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: Pub/Sub quotas limit request and throughput rates; adjustable quotas can be requested, while documented resource-count and payload-size limits cannot be increased.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: The Pub/Sub pricing and quota pages do not state whether Pub/Sub-specific spend-cap budgets are supported.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: There is no per-run duration, execution-second, or worker-memory price for Pub/Sub itself; message throughput, retention, transforms, and transfer are its main usage meters.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Publish request maximum is 10 MB total and 1,000 messages; one message's data field can be up to 10 MB.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: The StreamingPull stream limit is 10 MB/s per open stream; unary Pull responses are limited to 1,000 messages and 10 MB.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Pub/Sub throughput quota units use decimal 1 kB = 1,000 bytes. Large regions are europe-west1, europe-west4, us-central1, us-east1, us-east4, us-west1, and us-west2; medium regions include asia-east1, asia-northeast1, asia-southeast1, europe-west2, and europe-west3; other regions are in the small bucket.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Default regional publisher quotas are 240,000,000 kB/min (4 GB/s) in large regions, 48,000,000 kB/min (800 MB/s) in medium regions, and 12,000,000 kB/min (200 MB/s) in small regions.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Default regional Pull, StreamingPull, and acknowledgment throughput quotas are 240,000,000 kB/min in large regions, 48,000,000 kB/min in medium regions, and 24,000,000 kB/min in small regions.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Default regional Push quotas are 26,400,000 kB/min in large regions, 8,400,000 kB/min in medium regions, and 2,400,000 kB/min in small regions. BigQuery and Cloud Storage export quotas are 240,000,000, 48,000,000, and 12,000,000 kB/min for those same buckets.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Maximum open StreamingPull connections per region are 72,000 in large regions, 48,000 in medium regions, and 24,000 in small regions.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Per project, limits include 10,000 topics, 10,000 attached or detached subscriptions, 5,000 snapshots, and 10,000 schemas; a topic can have 10,000 attached subscriptions.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Pub/Sub is available through Google Cloud's self-service console, API, CLI, and client libraries; a Google Cloud account and project are required.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: The Google Cloud Free Tier describes Pub/Sub's free monthly usage as available to eligible customers; the pages checked do not give a complete country or account eligibility list.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: The pricing, Free Tier, and terms pages checked do not say whether a payment card is required before Pub/Sub can be used.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Google Cloud's terms permit use and integration of its services into a customer application that has material value independent of the services.

facts.label: Primary type and other roles
facts.value: Primary role: managed publish-and-subscribe messaging for application events and service-to-service communication.

facts.label: Primary type and other roles
facts.value: Pub/Sub also supports event streaming and direct ingestion or export to Google Cloud analytics and storage services.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Pub/Sub provides topics, subscriptions, message publishing and delivery, and durable message retention.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Subscription controls include message filters, retry policies, dead-letter topics, ordering, and exactly-once delivery options.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Topics can use schemas to validate messages and single-message transforms to modify or enrich them.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Native export subscriptions can write messages directly to BigQuery or Cloud Storage; Bigtable subscriptions are in Preview.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Pub/Sub import topics can ingest from Cloud Storage, Kinesis Data Streams, Azure Event Hubs, AWS MSK, and Confluent Cloud.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Pub/Sub is a broker, not a hosted application runtime: subscribers run in the customer's environment or use a supported export destination.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Applications can call Pub/Sub through REST or gRPC APIs, the Google Cloud CLI, or official client libraries.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Official client-library setup pages list C++, C#, Go, Java, Node.js, PHP, Python, Ruby, and Rust.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Pull clients can use unary Pull or bidirectional StreamingPull; Google recommends StreamingPull with a high-level library for high throughput and low latency.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Push subscriptions deliver HTTPS requests to an endpoint; the customer supplies and operates that endpoint.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Pub/Sub API calls use Google Cloud authentication and IAM; API keys are not a supported authentication method.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Publisher and subscriber roles can be granted at project or individual-resource level; separate roles control publishing, consuming, and administration.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Authenticated push can include a Google-signed JWT in the request authorization header; the receiver must validate it.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Pub/Sub advertises always-on encryption; customer-managed encryption keys are supported for Pub/Sub messages.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Google Cloud's service privacy notice applies to service data and distinguishes it from customer data; customer-data processing is covered by the Cloud Data Processing Addendum.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: Pub/Sub manages message storage, routing, and delivery; application code runs in the customer's subscriber or export destination.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: Official client libraries are listed for C++, C#, Go, Java, Node.js, PHP, Python, Ruby, and Rust; REST and gRPC are also available.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: Push delivery requires a reachable HTTPS endpoint; pull workers maintain their own connections and processing capacity.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: The initial acknowledgment deadline defaults to 10 seconds; a custom deadline can be set from 10 seconds through 600 seconds, and clients can extend it.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Default delivery is at least once and has no ordering guarantee; applications must handle possible duplicate delivery.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Exactly-once delivery is optional and supported only for pull subscriptions, not push; its guarantee is scoped within a Google Cloud region.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Ordered delivery requires an ordering key, ordering enabled when the subscription is created, and publishing related messages in the same region.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: An ordering key can be up to 1 KB; the maximum publisher throughput for each key is 1 MB/s.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: When an ordered message is redelivered, later messages with the same key can also be redelivered; ordering might not be preserved after best-effort dead-letter forwarding.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Retry is immediate by default; exponential backoff can be configured with a maximum delay of 600 seconds.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: A dead-letter topic can be configured per subscription, with an approximate maximum-attempt setting from 5 to 100; the default is 5.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Push delivery is an HTTPS POST; status 102, 200, 201, 202, or 204 acknowledges the request, while other responses cause redelivery.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Push delivery sends one message per request and has service-managed flow control; pull supports batched delivery and client-side flow control.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: A subscription filter can inspect message attributes, not the message body; nonmatching messages are automatically acknowledged.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Subscription filters still incur message-throughput fees for filtered messages but no data-transfer fees; the 1,000-byte minimum does not apply to them.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Pub/Sub has no published native recurring job scheduler or delayed-run schedule; its docs describe topics and subscription delivery, not scheduled execution.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Unacknowledged messages are retained for 7 days by default; subscription retention can be set from 10 minutes to 31 days.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Topic retention is optional and can preserve published messages for up to 31 days for replay across attached subscriptions.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Message data is limited to 10 MB; a publish request is limited to 10 MB total and 1,000 messages.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Pub/Sub does not impose a numeric message-count cap on retained subscription backlog; available retention time and storage billing still apply.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Pub/Sub provides Cloud Monitoring metrics and dashboards for topic throughput, backlog, delivery latency, and dead-letter counts.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Pub/Sub audit logs cover resource administration and access events, but do not log message-level Publish, Subscribe, or Acknowledge operations.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: The Pub/Sub monitoring and audit pages checked do not state a Pub/Sub-specific retention period for metrics or audit logs.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Subscription backlog is the message replay/recovery mechanism; snapshots can preserve a subscription's state for seek operations, with storage charges.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Pub/Sub uses a global namespace; by default, a global-endpoint publish is stored in the nearest Google Cloud region.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: A topic message-storage policy can restrict message contents to named Google Cloud regions; it does not support zone or multi-region location names.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: With enforceInTransit enabled, publish and subscriber requests through a disallowed region are rejected; push delivery is constrained to allowed regions too.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Pub/Sub throughput rates are published as the same USD rate in all Google Cloud regions; cross-region network charges still vary by region pair.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Google's service terms say regional storage commitments apply to services listed in its data-residency directory; Pub/Sub's configurable message-storage policy is the product-specific location control checked here.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Messages can be consumed through Pull/StreamingPull or exported by a BigQuery or Cloud Storage subscription; Bigtable export remains Preview.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Pub/Sub Lite migration options named by Google are Pub/Sub and Managed Service for Apache Kafka.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: A customer can delete topics and subscriptions through the console, CLI, or APIs; a subscription that expires loses its backlog.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: The Cloud Data Processing Addendum says customer-directed data deletion is completed as soon as reasonably practicable and within a maximum of 180 days; after contract end there can be a recovery period up to 30 days followed by a maximum 180-day deletion period.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: The current public Pub/Sub pages checked do not describe a one-click bulk export of all topic and subscription configuration plus message backlog as a single portable archive.

facts.label: Identity and old names
facts.value: Google Cloud Pub/Sub is the messaging service listed in apps.md; the listed URL resolves to Google's official Pub/Sub product page.

facts.label: Identity and old names
facts.value: The product pages checked use “Pub/Sub” and “Cloud Pub/Sub”; no former product name was stated.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Pub/Sub is a Google-managed cloud service; the customer uses APIs and client libraries and does not operate Pub/Sub servers.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: A self-hosted Pub/Sub server or a separate Pub/Sub software license is not offered as part of this product.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Pub/Sub is generally available and maintained; current release notes continue to list service features and regional changes.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Pub/Sub Lite is deprecated, unavailable to new customers since September 24, 2024, and scheduled to shut down January 31, 2027.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Google's Pub/Sub pricing page still lists March 18, 2026 as the Pub/Sub Lite shutdown date; this conflicts with the newer January 31, 2027 date in the migration guide.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: The release notes list an October 1, 2026 Gemini Enterprise code-generation feature for UDF transforms, April 2026 Bigtable export Preview and AI Inference transform GA, and a January 2026 Bangkok region launch.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: The Ruby v2 and Go v1 Pub/Sub client libraries are deprecated; they stopped receiving security and bug fixes on July 31, 2026. The service itself remains active.

facts.label: Vendor home and main markets
facts.value: The provider is Google LLC or the applicable Google entity named under Google Cloud's terms; Pub/Sub is offered across Google Cloud regions.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Basic Support is included for every Google Cloud customer, including Free Trial accounts; it provides documentation, community forums, billing assistance, and Active Assist.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: The public Google Cloud Service Health dashboard is the status page for Google Cloud services and regions.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Pub/Sub's service-level objective is at least 99.95% monthly uptime.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: The Pub/Sub SLA provides service credits of 10% at 99%–<99.95% monthly uptime, 25% at 95%–<99%, and 50% below 95%.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: MySQL/PostgreSQL extended support adds $0.07/vCPU-hour in years 1–2 and $0.14 in year 3 in Iowa; HA $0.14/$0.28. Shared-core instances have separate per-instance rates.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: One- and three-year committed-use discounts are optional. Shared-core instance charges, serverless exports and extended-support charges are excluded from those discounts; SQL Server license fees are also excluded.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Detailed partial-second section rounds milliseconds to the nearest second, below 500 ms down; an earlier shared-instance paragraph instead says each second counts toward a full billable minute.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: No request-driven sleep/wake used in the documented activation model: ALWAYS keeps the instance running; NEVER stops it until manual start. Compute charges suspend when stopped; provisioned storage and IP charges remain.

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: Ingress free in Cloud SQL's table. Same-region Compute Engine and same-region replica traffic free; cross-region traffic $0.12/GiB; other Google products free intra-continent, $0.12/GiB inter-continent.

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: Public-internet egress $0.19/GiB; internet through Cloud Interconnect $0.05/GiB. Idle IPv4 $0.01/hour. No recurring general internet-egress allowance published in these Cloud SQL tables.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: Alerts-only budgets monitor costs and send notifications; Cloud SQL is absent from the current spend-cap eligible-service list (Gemini API, Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, Cloud Run and Cloud Run functions).

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: Storage auto-increase is enabled by default; default limit 0 means grow up to the instance tier maximum. A custom storage limit restricts growth, not total dollar spending; a full instance can stop or reject work.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: PostgreSQL dedicated storage up to 64 TB; initial disk minimum documented as 10 GB. Dedicated general-purpose Enterprise up to 96 vCPU/624 GB, with regional restrictions.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Shared-core capacity differs across sources: instance settings list up to 3054 GB; the shared-instance pricing table lists 3062 GiB. An authoritative reconciliation was not established.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: PostgreSQL connections depend on instance memory and max_connections; replica setting must be at least the primary's. max_connections + autovacuum_max_workers + max_worker_processes cannot exceed 262142; a single table limit is 32 TB.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: PostgreSQL Data API: 10 concurrent queries per instance, 100 queries/minute/project/region, 512 KiB request and 10 MiB response. Management API quotas are separate from native SQL capacity.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: PostgreSQL Enterprise Plus managed pooling defaults to 5,000 client connections per pooler, roughly one pooler per four vCPU with at least one. Enabling pooling on an existing instance restarts it; transaction pooling does not support LISTEN and several session features.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Project instance quota depends on SQL network architecture: up to 1000 with new architecture, 100 with old, 100–1000 mixed; read replicas count. Quota increases can be requested.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Storage can now be manually shrunk on supported dedicated primary/read-replica instances, with restart/downtime and a computed safe minimum. Shared-core instances, cascading replicas and Terraform shrink are excluded.

facts.label: File storage prices
facts.value: Not applicable to Cloud SQL's managed relational-database scope.

facts.label: File request and retrieval prices
facts.value: Not applicable to Cloud SQL's managed relational-database scope.

facts.label: Minimum storage and early deletion
facts.value: Not applicable to Cloud SQL's managed relational-database scope.

facts.label: Vector/index limits
facts.value: For PostgreSQL with supported pgvector, upstream vector storage supports 16,000 dimensions; HNSW/IVFFlat float32 vector indexes support 2,000. The proposed 1536-dimensional workload fits that type limit, but memory/index overhead still needs sizing.

facts.label: Vector/index limits
facts.value: MySQL 8.0/8.4 vectors: up to 16,000 dimensions; 9.7: 16,383, default 2048. One vector index per table; vector-indexed tables cannot use table partitioning.

facts.label: Embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: PostgreSQL can store externally generated embeddings or call Vertex AI through google_ml_integration; model endpoints also support Anthropic, Hugging Face, OpenAI and custom providers. Non-Vertex providers require public IP in this integration.

facts.label: Embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: External model price table lists non-Gemini text embeddings at $0.000025 per 1,000 count online and $0.00002 batch, with no output charge. The displayed count unit is not defined clearly enough here to convert the approved workload to a model bill; no universal included model/reranking allowance established.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Not applicable as an all-in worker/invocation price. Scheduled SQL consumes the provisioned database's resources; the approved 0.5-vCPU application-worker scenario is not a Cloud SQL runtime configuration.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Self-service through a Google Cloud account/project with billing enabled. General trial requires a valid credit card or other supported payment method and identity/payment verification; some countries also require bank verification.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Cloud terms permit GCP integration into applications with independent material value. Country-specific payment availability varies; a complete Cloud SQL-specific eligible-country list was not established.

facts.label: Primary type and other roles
facts.value: Researcher classification: managed relational SQL databases. Secondary roles: vector search, geographic/text search and database replication.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Managed database instances, maintenance, backups, monitoring and optional HA/read replicas. App hosting, end-user login, object storage and general application functions use separate services rather than a bundled Cloud SQL backend plan.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Native engine wire protocols and ordinary database drivers; public or private IP. Official Java, Python, Go and Node.js language connectors plus Cloud SQL Auth Proxy; proxy does not create private-network reachability.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: PostgreSQL Data API runs DDL/DML/query statements through the Admin API or gcloud when explicitly enabled. Suited to short administrative SQL; default access is disallowed.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Public direct connections require authorized networks; private options include Private Service Connect or private services access. Proxy uses IAM and TLS 1.3, with database authentication still required.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: PostgreSQL default sslMode permits unencrypted and encrypted connections; choose ENCRYPTED_ONLY or trusted client certificate enforcement to require transport protection. At-rest data/backups are encrypted; customer-managed KMS keys are optional.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: IAM controls management access; PostgreSQL IAM database authentication can use users/service accounts/groups and one-hour OAuth tokens, automatically refreshed by connectors. Grant database privileges separately.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: PostgreSQL supports column grants, restricted views and row-level security policies for tenant-specific reads/writes. Table owners and BYPASSRLS roles can bypass policies; FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY can subject an owner to them.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Customer Data is governed by the DPA; the Cloud Privacy Notice separately covers Service Data such as account, billing and usage information. Billing transaction Service Data is typically retained at least five years for tax/accounting duties.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: Native PostgreSQL 9.6–18; version policy lists PostgreSQL 18 as default. Cloud SQL Enterprise Plus supports PostgreSQL 12–18; older majors are Enterprise-only and can incur extended-support fees.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: Native MySQL 5.6, 5.7, 8.0, 8.4 and 9.7; current policy default 8.4. Plus supports 8.0/8.4/9.7; Enterprise also supports the older majors.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: SQL Server 2017, 2019, 2022 and 2025 with engine-edition restrictions. Cloud SQL Enterprise Plus requires SQL Server engine Enterprise 2019/2022/2025; Cloud SQL Enterprise supports the broader engine-edition matrix.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: Default PostgreSQL version conflicts: version policy/FAQ and the instance-settings table say 18; later instance-settings guidance says accept default PostgreSQL 16.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: Creation defaults depend on interface/version: console defaults to Cloud SQL Enterprise Plus; CLI/API PostgreSQL 16+ and MySQL 8.4/9.7 default Plus, older versions default Enterprise. SQL Server CLI/API defaults Enterprise.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: PostgreSQL supports transactions with default Read Committed isolation; a query sees committed data at its start, so successive queries in one transaction can see different committed changes. Stronger isolation is configurable.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: MySQL defaults to REPEATABLE READ; session isolation can be changed. SQL Server documents UNCOMMITTED, READ COMMITTED, REPEATABLE READ, SNAPSHOT and SERIALIZABLE modes.

facts.label: Test environments and branches
facts.value: Separate independent instance clones. Standard clone uses a full backup; eligible same-zone MySQL/PostgreSQL fast clone uses an instant snapshot when disk properties match. PITR clones use the standard workflow.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Regional HA uses a primary and standby in separate zones with synchronous writes to both disks before commit; failover redirects to the standby. Existing connections close and applications must reconnect using the same connection identity.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: PostgreSQL read replicas are asynchronous and read-only, in-region or cross-region; promotion makes an independent primary. Replica lag can produce stale reads or lost recent changes on disaster promotion; each replica is separately billed.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: PostgreSQL native logical replication/decoding and pglogical are documented. Enable cloudsql.logical_decoding; pglogical also needs its own enable flag and restarts. This is a database change stream, not a complete client sync service.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: A native mobile/browser offline cache, offline write replay and end-user conflict-resolution guarantee were not found.

facts.label: Extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: PostgreSQL supported extension catalog includes PostGIS, pgvector, pg_cron and pglogical; only allow-listed extensions can be installed, on a primary. PostgreSQL 18 has PostGIS 3.6.0; PostgreSQL 13+ supports pgvector 0.8.5.

facts.label: Extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: MySQL vector search supports SQL vector columns and ScaNN approximate indexes, with version-specific behavior. It is a database feature alongside ordinary relational data, not a separately provisioned vector namespace service.

facts.label: Upload and file limits
facts.value: Not applicable to Cloud SQL's managed relational-database scope.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Not applicable to Cloud SQL's managed relational-database scope.

facts.label: Delivery and private files
facts.value: Not applicable to Cloud SQL's managed relational-database scope.

facts.label: Filters and mixed search
facts.value: PostgreSQL vector queries can use SQL WHERE filters and combine ranking with text search. Approximate-index filters can leave fewer results; pgvector 0.8+ iterative scans can search further. Enforce tenant authorization separately.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: PostgreSQL pg_cron 1.6.4 on supported PostgreSQL 10+ schedules SQL commands inside the database. Application workers in arbitrary languages remain outside this managed database scope.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Not applicable to the primary service: no app queue delivery contract evaluated.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Recurring database SQL is supported through pg_cron. App-message payload size and queue-retention guarantees are outside this database scheduler scope.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Not applicable as app-job run history/replay. Database metrics and query insights are available, with edition-specific retention, but are not application-job execution records.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Not applicable: Cloud SQL itself is a managed Google Cloud service. Running upstream PostgreSQL/MySQL/SQL Server yourself is a different offering with different maintenance, licensing and backup duties.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Instance region is selected at creation; existing instance location cannot be changed in place. Current regional support matrix varies by edition and machine series.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Published examples: us-central1 Iowa, us-east1 South Carolina, europe-west1 Belgium, europe-west2 London, asia-south1 Mumbai, asia-south2 Delhi, asia-southeast1 Singapore and australia-southeast1 Sydney. Full current matrix linked.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Instance data is in its selected region. Standard backups default to the geographically closest multi-region (Iowa → us) unless configured otherwise; Enhanced backups use their vault location. Cross-region replicas have their own chosen region.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: PostgreSQL portable export through pg_dump/pg_dumpall and restore through pg_restore; MySQL SQL dump or CSV export; SQL Server BAK and SqlPackage BACPAC options.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Serverless export has an additional $0.01/GiB Iowa charge, plus destination storage/transfer. Ordinary exports can affect database performance; standard Cloud SQL backups are managed recovery artifacts, so portable dumps are the exit path.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Delete replicas first and disable deletion protection before deleting a primary. Underlying instance resources can take up to four days to delete. Final/retained backups and separately created PSC endpoints or DNS resources need separate attention.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: DPA: unrecoverable customer deletion instructions completed as soon as practical, maximum 180 days, subject to legal retention. At contract end, recovery period up to 30 days precedes the maximum-180-day deletion process; continuing agreements can defer the instruction.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Standard backups: daily automated backups, retention configurable 1–365 days; on-demand backups retained until explicitly removed. Restore protects database contents, not files independently stored in Cloud Storage or app code.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Enhanced backups use Backup and DR backup vaults, enforced retention, hourly/daily/weekly/monthly/yearly schedules and up to 10 years (3653 days). Vaults can live in a separate project, surviving source-project deletion.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: PostgreSQL PITR logs: Enterprise 1–7 days, default 7; Plus 1–35 days, default 14. Enterprise console creation enables PITR by default; CLI/API/Terraform require explicit enablement. Plus enables PITR by default regardless of creation method.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: PITR always creates a new instance rather than restoring into an existing instance. Enabling PITR later can restart the instance. Backups created through non-console methods also need explicit configuration per the PITR guide.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Final standard backup default retention 30 days, configurable 1–365; Enhanced can retain up to 10 years. Deleted-instance recovery can be requested from Customer Care within four days; retained/final backup settings must be checked explicitly.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Standard backup used-storage rate in Iowa is $0.000109589/GiB-hour. Enhanced vault storage is $0.000061644/GiB-hour plus active Cloud SQL protection management $0.000068493/GiB-hour of stored backup data; transfer can add charges.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: PostgreSQL unlogged table contents are not preserved by backup restore, HA failover or read replicas; use logged tables for durable recovery.

facts.label: File recovery and protection
facts.value: Not applicable to Cloud SQL's managed relational-database scope.

facts.label: Identity and old names
facts.value: Google Cloud SQL, a Google Cloud product. Current official product name and URL established; no separate former product name established.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Google-hosted managed service under Google Cloud terms; Enterprise and Enterprise Plus. No downloadable Cloud SQL service edition identified.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Active public service with current pricing, creation documentation and maintained engine versions. No whole-product shutdown, sunset or acquisition notice found in this bounded review.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: MySQL 5.6/5.7 retire February 1, 2028; MySQL 8.0 enters paid extended support January 1, 2027 and retires July 1, 2029. PostgreSQL 9.6–12 retire February 1, 2028; PostgreSQL 13 is already in extended support; PostgreSQL 14 enters it February 1, 2027.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: SQL Server 2017: no new instances after April 12, 2027; Cloud SQL support ends October 13, 2027. SQL Server does not use Cloud SQL's MySQL/PostgreSQL extended-support program.

facts.label: Vendor home and main markets
facts.value: Google LLC is the contracting entity for US billing addresses and locations not otherwise listed. Other billing countries use listed regional entities; Google LLC's stated address is Mountain View, California, United States.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Basic Support included: docs, community forums, billing assistance and Active Assist. Standard technical support costs the higher of $29/month or 3% of eligible monthly list-price charges.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: SLA: Enterprise qualifying HA instances 99.95%; Enterprise Plus qualifying HA or read pools with at least two nodes 99.99%. Shared-core, single-zone and one-node read pools excluded.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Public service status and incident history available through Google Cloud Service Health.

Cloud Storage stores objects, not SQL databases

files.math: 100 GB is 93.1323 GiB (one GiB is 2³⁰ bytes). Storage: 93.1323 × 730 × $0.000027397. Requests: 100 × $0.005, plus 1,000 × $0.0004. Outbound data: 93.1323 × $0.12. These add up to about $13.94. There is no free tier.

jobs.math: Cloud Storage stores files and does not run background jobs

facts.label: free offer type
facts.value: Cloud Storage has an ongoing monthly Free Tier for eligible billing accounts; it is distinct from the 90-day new-user trial.

facts.label: free offer type
facts.value: New eligible users can receive a $300 Welcome credit for 90 days; a valid payment method is required, but Google says Free Trial usage does not incur a bill.

facts.label: free offer type
facts.value: The $300 Free Trial credit is temporary; to keep trial resources running after the trial ends, the user must upgrade to a Paid billing account.

facts.label: free limits

facts.label: free limits

facts.label: free limits

facts.value: Always Free includes 100 GB of outbound data transfer per month from North America to region destinations, excluding China and Australia.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: The product homepage summarizes the offer as 5 GiB and 55,000 operations; the detailed Free Tier table gives 5 GB-months and separate 5,000 Class A plus 50,000 Class B limits. The detailed table is used for the limits above.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: No automatic sleep or idle-project deletion interval for a paid Cloud Storage bucket was found in the pricing page, storage FAQs, lifecycle docs, or Google Cloud Terms.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: A Free Trial billing account closes when its 90 days expire or its $300 credit is exhausted unless upgraded; resources stop, then enter a 30-day recovery window before permanent deletion.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: Deleting objects with the default soft-delete policy does not immediately remove them; the default hold is 7 days and can be configured from 7 to 90 days or disabled.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: Pricing is usage-based by storage, operations, retrieval, and transfer. The reviewed product pricing page does not list a separate Cloud Storage subscription tier or fixed instance fee.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: A minimum monthly Cloud Storage spend or a universal post-trial monthly commitment was not stated on the reviewed pricing, Free Tier, or terms pages.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Storage is billed by each object's storage class and exact time in storage, prorated to the sub-second; live, noncurrent, and soft-deleted objects count.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Requests are grouped into Class A, Class B, and free operations; the operation class depends on the request and the object or bucket storage class.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Reads, copies, moves, or rewrites from Nearline, Coldline, or Archive can incur retrieval fees in addition to request and network charges.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Writes to dual-region and multi-region buckets can incur inter-region replication charges; premium turbo replication can have its own charge.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Autoclass adds an object management fee and may charge for some transitions; Storage Intelligence is a separate product with its own fees.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Cloud Storage buckets can be tagged for $0.005 per tag per month; tag operations are not eligible for Always Free operations.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Billing-account currency can differ from the USD display; Google says localized Cloud SKU rates apply when the account pays in another currency.

facts.label: idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Compute, wake-up, and scale-to-zero billing do not apply to Cloud Storage itself; it is a storage service, not a compute runtime.

facts.label: data transfer costs

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: Data read from a Cloud Storage regional bucket in Iowa (us-central1) to a Google Cloud destination in Northern America is $0.02/GB; pricing is based on bucket and destination locations.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: Data transfer within the same Cloud Storage location is free; for a regional bucket, access from Google Cloud services in the same region is listed as the same location.

facts.label: data transfer costs

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: Internet egress to Asia destinations excluding China, but including Hong Kong, costs $0.12/GiB for 0–10 TiB per month per account, then $0.11/GiB from 10–150 TiB and $0.08/GiB above 150 TiB.

facts.label: data transfer costs

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: Internet egress to Australia costs $0.19/GiB for the first 0–10 TiB per month per account, then $0.18/GiB from 10–150 TiB and $0.15/GiB above 150 TiB.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: These general egress rates are separate from Cloud CDN, load-balancer, Rapid Cache, or Rapid Bucket network fees.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: Use above the monthly Free Tier limits is charged at standard prices on a paid billing account; a Free Trial credit can cover eligible overage during the trial.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: Cloud Billing budgets can send alerts and can trigger programmatic actions, but an alerts-only budget does not itself cap service use or spending.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: Google documents spend-cap budgets for eligible projects; they block usage and cost accrual when the configured cap is reached, but this is an account-level billing control, not a Cloud Storage quota.

facts.label: overages and bill controls

facts.label: data access controls

facts.value: Valkey, Iowa us-central1, USD per node-hour on-demand: custom-micro 2.5 GB 0.0616; custom-mini 3.75 GB 0.0924; standard-small 6.5 GB 0.1425; highmem-medium 13 GB 0.1923.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Valkey, Iowa us-central1, USD per node-hour on-demand: highcpu-medium 13 GB 0.4986; standard-large 26 GB 0.5698; highmem-xlarge 58 GB 0.8581; highmem-2xlarge 110 GB 1.6274.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Valkey bills one-second increments for every allocated primary and replica. Iowa us-central1 AOF persistence adds USD 0.00054795 per provisioned GB-hour; backups add USD 0.00011111 per stored backup GB-hour, minimum 24 hours per backup.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Redis Basic, Iowa us-central1, USD/GiB-hour: M2 5–10 GiB 0.027; M3 11–35 GiB 0.023; M4 36–100 GiB 0.019; M5 above 100 GiB 0.016.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Redis Standard without enabled read replicas, Iowa us-central1, USD/GiB-hour: M2 0.054; M3 0.046; M4 0.035; M5 0.030. With read replicas enabled, separate per-node rates are M2 0.027, M3 0.023, M4 0.019 and M5 0.016, multiplied by primary plus replica count.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Redis Basic/Standard capacity charges are rounded upward to the nearest second; the tariff is provisioned GiB, not GB payload or per-command usage. RDB persistence has no extra instance charge; exported Cloud Storage files are separate.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Redis Cluster, Iowa us-central1, USD/node-hour: redis-highmem-medium 13 GB 0.1923, redis-highcpu-medium 13 GB 0.4986, redis-standard-large 26 GB 0.5698, redis-highmem-xlarge 58 GB 0.8581 and redis-highmem-2xlarge 110 GB 1.6274.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Redis Cluster, Iowa us-central1: per-second provisioned node billing, including replicas; AOF adds USD 0.00054795/provisioned GB-hour; backup storage USD 0.00011111/GB-hour with 24-hour minimum per backup.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Memcached, Iowa us-central1: USD 0.05/vCPU-hour plus USD 0.0044/GiB-hour when a node is at most 4 GiB, or USD 0.0089/GiB-hour for a node above 4 GiB; multiply both by node count.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: CUDs: 20% off eligible one-year usage or 40% off eligible three-year usage, shared across eligible Memorystore spending on the billing account. Fixed hourly commitments cannot be canceled and remain payable when unused; Redis M1 and Valkey custom nodes are excluded.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Discount evidence conflicts for extras: regional pricing tables display one-/three-year discounted backup/AOF columns, but the CUD guide expressly excludes backups, persistence and outbound transfer from eligible spending.

facts.label: idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: No request-driven scale to zero: retained allocated capacity incurs charges even without commands. Deleting compute does not erase retained backups or cancel a CUD financial commitment.

facts.label: idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: A documented pause/resume mode retaining all data without allocated-memory charges was not found, including for Memcached.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: Valkey and Redis Cluster: Memorystore PSC endpoints have no hourly endpoint charge; same-zone client traffic has no consumer data-processing charge. Different-zone client traffic is charged USD 0.01/GiB; inter-region and cross-region replication traffic adds route-based charges.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: Redis Basic/Standard: no Memorystore-side charge for client ingress/egress within the same region; the client resource can still charge cross-zone traffic. Between two North American Google regions the published Memorystore outbound rate is USD 0.02/GiB.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: Memcached: only same-region clients are supported, and Memorystore charges no ingress/egress fee for that service traffic; other Google Cloud client/network resources can still charge for their traffic.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: The reference workload's 5 GB internet transfer cannot be priced as direct public Memorystore egress; an application, network path and its own internet tariff are required.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: Valkey/Redis memory exhaustion follows configured eviction policies or noeviction errors; Memcached normally evicts, while disable-evictions=true instead rejects writes until memory is available. Capacity resizing changes allocated cost.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: Management request quotas apply to provisioning APIs, not billed data commands. Redis, Valkey and Memcached docs do not impose a total query-count quota equivalent to a free read/write budget.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: Alerts-only Cloud Billing budgets send notifications and do not cap spending. Google's spend-cap feature currently lists Gemini API, Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, Cloud Run and Cloud Run functions as eligible; Memorystore is not listed, and ongoing persistent resource charges are not paused by caps.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Valkey custom-pico: 1.25 GB total/1.08 GB default writable, two vCPUs, 16,000 default and 32,000 maximum clients per node. Shared-core-nano: 1.4 GB total/1.12 GB writable hard limit, 0.5 vCPU, 5,000 clients maximum.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Valkey standard-small: 6.5 GB total/5.2 GB writable, two vCPUs, 16,000 default/32,000 maximum clients; highmem-medium: 13 GB total/10.4 GB writable, two vCPUs, 32,000 default/64,000 maximum clients.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Valkey usage-unit limit is 250 per instance, counting shard_count × (1 + replica_count). Cluster Mode Disabled databases default to 16 and can be configured to 100 at creation; Cluster Mode Enabled version 9.0+ defaults to one and can configure up to 100.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Valkey fixes proto-bulk-max-len at 256 MB and does not let customers modify it. Management quota is 10 create/delete requests per project/minute and 60 instance API requests per project/minute.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Redis Basic/Standard primary size up to 300 GB as expressed in tier docs; tariff/allocation pages measure provisioned GiB. Connected clients: 65,000 per node, with lower TLS limits possible for Redis 6.x and earlier.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Redis default per-project regional capacity quota is 1 TB. Logical database configuration defaults to 16 and can be set to 1–100 at creation; the quotas page lists 16 databases as its generic instance limit.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Redis Cluster node capacities range from 1.4 GB total/1.12 GB default writable on redis-shared-core-nano to 110 GB total/88 GB writable on redis-highmem-2xlarge. Its 6.5 GB redis-standard-small defaults to 16,000 clients, maximum 32,000.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Redis Cluster specification illustrates a 250-node aggregate envelope: 250 primaries with no replicas, 125 primaries with one replica each, or fewer primaries with more replicas. Replication reduces writable primary capacity for the same node count.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Memcached: one to 20 nodes/instance, identical configurations; one or even-numbered 2–32 vCPUs/node, with regional availability restrictions; node RAM 1 to 256 GB subject to CPU:RAM constraints. 65,000 clients/node.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Memcached item limit defaults to 1,048,576 bytes; configurable 524,288 to 134,217,728 bytes, divisible by the 524,288-byte slab size and no more than half allocated cache memory. Reserved memory defaults to 10% for newer instances.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Maximum Redis/Redis Cluster value size and all node-specific CPU/throughput ceilings were not established from the inspected limits/configuration pages.

facts.label: storage prices
facts.value: Not applicable to a native, database-independent file/object-storage product.

facts.label: file request and retrieval prices
facts.value: Not applicable to a native, database-independent file/object-storage product.

facts.label: minimum storage and early deletion
facts.value: Not applicable to a native, database-independent file/object-storage product.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: Valkey vector indexes: FLAT or HNSW; FLOAT32; L2, inner-product or cosine distance; 1 to 32,768 dimensions and at most 10 indexed fields. HNSW EF_CONSTRUCTION/EF_RUNTIME maximum 4,096; FT.CREATE documents M maximum 512.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: Valkey vector availability: all supported versions/tiers/regions, only for instances created after 2024-09-13. Vectors are stored both in the keyspace and the index, so raw embedding size understates RAM usage.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: Redis Basic/Standard vector search requires version 7.2 and is available across tiers/supported regions; dimensions up to 32,768, at most 10 index attributes, and EF construction/runtime up to 4,096. Vectors are duplicated in keyspace/index memory.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: Redis Cluster vector limits independently document maximum 32,768 dimensions, 10 attributes and 4,096 EF parameters; vectors are stored in keyspace plus the index and searches fan out over shard-local indexes. Availability is across supported versions/tiers/regions, for clusters created after 2024-09-13.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: Valkey JSON indexing documentation conflicts: FT.CREATE says only HASH is supported, but FT.SEARCH says JSON documents can be indexed with FT.CREATE. Native JSON module availability does not settle the vector-index format by version.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: A fixed maximum vector count, index count or metadata-byte entitlement by Memorystore node type was not established.

facts.label: embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: Embedding generation and reranking model allowances/rates are not listed in the engine tariffs. Native vector storage/search requires external or application-generated embeddings; no model-specific all-in bill was established.

facts.label: run limits and pricing
facts.value: Broker cost is the selected engine's allocated-capacity/node tariff and networking. External worker CPU, RAM, duration, concurrency, timeout, waiting/retry charges require a chosen compute host and queue framework.

facts.label: run limits and pricing
facts.value: No all-in hosted worker execution shape, per-job fee or universal application run-duration/concurrency limit was found for Memorystore itself.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Requires a Google Cloud account/project, enabled product APIs, billing and suitable private-network configuration. Free Trial signup requires a credit card or another valid payment method and may require bank verification depending on country.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Shared Google Cloud Free Trial eligibility: never previously a paying Google Cloud/Maps Platform/Firebase user and no previous Free Trial. Upgrading enables paid usage; Cloud Terms also impose lawful use/export restrictions.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Engine-specific country signup exclusions and a separate Memorystore commercial-use eligibility matrix were not found.

facts.label: primary type and other roles
facts.value: Researcher classification: managed key-value databases/caches; secondary uses include sessions, counters/leaderboards, messaging/Streams and vector retrieval on supported Redis/Valkey deployments.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: Valkey/Redis provide managed data structures, supported scripting, Pub/Sub/Streams, database networking and monitoring. Backups/persistence, replica behavior and search vary by engine. Memcached is a distributed key/value cache without replicated keys.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: A Memorystore allowance for end-user login/MAU, file buckets, hosted application functions or external worker execution was not found.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Valkey: native Valkey/Redis-compatible clients; Cluster Mode Enabled uses a discovery endpoint and cluster-aware clients; Cluster Mode Disabled has primary and reader endpoints. Redis Cluster also requires cluster-aware topology handling.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Redis Basic/Standard: standard Redis protocol/client libraries through a private network; supported app environments include Compute Engine, GKE, Cloud Run and functions, with appropriate VPC access. Memcached: binary/ASCII protocols and ordinary Memcached client libraries.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: REST/gcloud APIs manage instances and backups; data commands use the selected engine protocol. Supported/blocked command lists constrain managed Valkey and Redis functionality.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Valkey/Redis Cluster are private through PSC; IAM controls resource management. Valkey additionally supports IAM database authentication, token auth and managed ACL policies, with availability recorded in its release notes.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Valkey IAM tokens normally expire after one hour; authenticated existing connections can continue, while new connections need a valid token. TLS should be enabled because AUTH itself does not encrypt a token.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Redis Basic/Standard supports optional Redis AUTH and optional TLS 1.2+; its versions table says Redis 7.0 ACL improvements/modules are not supported. A trusted backend must mediate untrusted app users.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Memcached is limited to the authorized private VPC/region; the supported-version matrix explicitly marks TLS unsupported, including for its supported 1.6.15 release.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: Valkey supports versions 7.2, 8.0, 9.0 and 9.1; default 9.1. Upgrade to a newer supported version is possible; downgrade after upgrading is not supported.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: Redis Basic/Standard supports 3.2, 4.0, 5.0, 6.x, 7.0 and 7.2; default 7.2. Google maintains one listed patch level per major version and applies critical security updates.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: Redis Cluster is a managed sharded Redis-compatible service with a restricted command library. A current public supported-engine-version matrix was not established from its overview/specification/command docs.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: Memcached supports 1.5.16 and 1.6.15, default 1.5.16. Its 1.6.15 feature matrix supports meta protocol, but not warm-cache restart, extstore or TLS.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Valkey and Redis/Redis Cluster list MULTI, EXEC, WATCH and Lua-related commands in their supported command libraries. The migration guide describes atomic execution of Lua application logic.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Exact multi-key transaction/hash-slot scope, replica-read consistency and acknowledged-write loss guarantees for every engine/topology were not established from the inspected managed-service docs.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Memcached provides CAS (check-and-set) unless disable-cas=true; it detects whether an item's value changed since retrieval. No multi-record database transaction facility was established in the inspected managed Memcached docs.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Vector search on Valkey, Redis and Redis Cluster does not adhere to transaction semantics because search thread-pool work is asynchronous.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Separate projects/instances can isolate development and production; shared-core-nano on Valkey/Redis Cluster is explicitly recommended only for development/testing. Those instances still have provisioned-capacity charges.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: No native copy-on-write database branches, automatic preview environments or free staging-clone entitlement was found.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Valkey: one primary and zero to five replicas per shard; automatic placement across zones and replicas provide HA/read throughput. Each replica adds a billable node; HA protection is separate from backup protection.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Redis Basic: no replication/automatic failover. Standard: cross-zone replication and automatic failover; enabling read replicas permits up to five replicas on M2+ capacity tiers and changes billing to primary-plus-replica nodes.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Redis Cluster: managed primary/replica sharding and automatic HA failover, with additional nodes billed; exact topology limits are in its own cluster specification. Cross-region replication adds separately priced instances/network transfer.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Memcached distributes different keys across nodes without replicating them. Multiple zones/nodes reduce common failure exposure but do not create a failover copy of every cached item.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Redis/Valkey supported commands include Pub/Sub and Streams consumer groups; Valkey configuration can enable keyspace notifications, with no events enabled by default.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: A managed offline browser/mobile write cache, reconnect conflict-resolution policy and cross-device sync contract were not found.

facts.label: extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Valkey 1.0 JSON and Bloom modules were declared GA in April 2026 release notes; supported versions document geo features. Redis Basic/Standard's version matrix says arbitrary Redis modules are unsupported, while native vector search is separately supported.

facts.label: extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Memcached's 1.6.15 meta protocol is supported; no native vector index/secondary document-search module is established for that engine.

facts.label: delivery and private files
facts.value: Not applicable to a native, database-independent file/object-storage product.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: Conditional binary-value use: Memcached max item size defaults to 1 MiB and is configurable up to 128 MiB subject to documented slab/cache constraints; Valkey's unmodifiable bulk parser maximum is 256 MB.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Datastore clients use Valkey/Redis or Memcached protocols. Redis RDB import/export uses external Google Cloud Storage; it does not expose an S3-compatible object API from Memorystore.

facts.label: filters and mixed search
facts.value: Valkey supports vector nearest-neighbor queries filtered by NUMERIC and TAG attributes; FT.SEARCH examples combine city tags and price ranges with KNN. FT.CREATE says tag/numeric fields are used with vectors, not standalone filter-only queries.

facts.label: filters and mixed search
facts.value: A full-text BM25/keyword-plus-vector fusion contract across Memorystore Redis/Valkey variants was not established from the inspected native vector command docs.

facts.label: execution model and languages
facts.value: Valkey/Redis support Lists, Streams and server-side scripting commands usable for messaging/broker patterns. Application worker code runs on a separate host; a Memorystore node is not a general managed application-job runtime.

facts.label: delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Streams support XACK, XREADGROUP, XPENDING and claim commands in the managed command lists; end-to-end job retries, deduplication and exactly-once processing depend on application/framework behavior.

facts.label: delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: A Memorystore end-to-end queue retry/backoff policy, duplicate-protection window, dead-letter retention and replay contract was not published in the inspected sources.

facts.label: schedules and queue retention
facts.value: No product-level delayed-job schedule, guaranteed queued-job lifetime or framework-independent serialized job-payload quota was found.

facts.label: logs and run history
facts.value: Cloud metrics/command diagnostic configuration are available, but no included worker stdout/result-history retention, replay UI or per-job log/export allowance was found.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Not applicable to a self-hosted Memorystore edition: this entry is the Google-managed service. Self-managed upstream Valkey, Redis and Memcached require separate product/license/operational research.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Memcached does not provide instance-level authentication. Only trusted clients on its authorized VPC should have access; control-plane operations are managed using IAM.

facts.label: logs and run history
facts.value: Redis Basic/Standard's configuration table lists slowlog-log-slower-than=10,000 microseconds and slowlog-max-len=128 entries. These are database command diagnostics, not worker stdout or job-result retention.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: Redis Cluster's own overview identifies its engine as open-source Redis 7.x, with a managed subset of the Redis command library.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Valkey: selectable regional deployment and zonal replicas; the published locations matrix includes us-central1 Iowa, us-east1 South Carolina, europe-west1 Belgium, europe-west2 London, asia-south1 Mumbai and asia-southeast1 Singapore, among others.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Redis Basic/Standard: region chosen on creation, with geographic/zone restrictions in its own regions documentation. Iowa us-central1, London europe-west2, Mumbai asia-south1 and Singapore asia-southeast1 are listed.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Redis Cluster: its own locations matrix includes us-central1, us-east1, europe-west1, europe-west2, asia-south1 and asia-southeast1; multi-zone topology is a distinct HA setting.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Memcached: nodes remain in the selected region, with automatic or selected zone distribution; the authorized VPC is selected at creation and cannot later be changed. Cross-region client access is unsupported.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Public tariff region selectors and supported-region docs are not fully synchronized, so extra selector entries must not alone be treated as deployable product locations. Exact backup-location guarantees and every SKU-by-zone availability combination were not established.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Redis Basic/Standard exports and imports native RDB via customer Cloud Storage buckets. Imports overwrite existing data and have availability/compatibility constraints; vector-search RDB files have extra compatibility restrictions.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Valkey/Redis Cluster backups can seed a new instance; they cannot import into an existing instance. Backup collections are independent of instance deletion and can be exported/analyzed using backup operations.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Memcached-to-Valkey migration requires changing client libraries, connection setup and commands, then validating/repopulating the new store. It is not a protocol-transparent engine-name switch.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Cloud Data Processing Addendum §6.1: a deletion instruction during the term is completed as soon as practicable, within 180 days, with legal exceptions. §6.2: end-of-term deletion follows a recovery period up to 30 days, then the stated maximum 180-day completion period, subject to exceptions/deferred instructions.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Valkey supports either RDB or AOF persistence, not both at once. RDB trades snapshot staleness for lower overhead; AOF can persist every second or every write, with performance/durability tradeoffs.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Valkey automated daily backups: configurable UTC start, default retention 35 days, maximum 365 days. On-demand backup CLI TTL: minimum one day, default 100 years when omitted; these differ from scheduled-backup defaults.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Valkey backups are point-in-time snapshots in independent backup collections; deletion of an instance leaves its collection. Restore seeds a newly created instance rather than overwriting an existing one. Backup storage has a 24-hour minimum charge.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Redis Basic/Standard RDB persistence supports snapshot intervals of one, six, 12 or 24 hours and retains the latest successful recovery snapshot only. It adds no extra instance charge; snapshots are not available for manual point selection/restoration. Current overview documentation says RDB snapshots are enabled by default when new instances are created through the console.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Redis RDB persistence is available from Redis 5.0 and is recovery protection; Basic can cold restart/full-flush without applicable recovery. Standard normally recovers from a replica, with a snapshot fallback when needed. AOF is not supported in Redis Basic/Standard.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Redis Cluster supports independent on-demand/automated backup collections and restore into a new cluster. Collections survive cluster deletion and storage is charged separately with a 24-hour minimum per backup.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Redis Cluster supports either AOF or RDB persistence, not both at once. Its own backup guide sets daily automated retention default 35 days, maximum 365; on-demand CLI TTL minimum one day, omitted default 100 years.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Memcached is a non-replicated cache; the official migration guide identifies AOF/RDB persistence as Valkey features unavailable in Memcached, and its supported-version table marks warm-cache restart unsupported.

facts.label: file recovery and protection
facts.value: Not applicable to a native, database-independent file/object-storage product.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: A contractual arbitrary-second PITR guarantee or fixed restore RPO/RTO for Valkey/Redis Cluster was not established; a snapshot's creation time and a configured persistence cadence are not guaranteed loss/recovery bounds.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Valkey backup export writes RDB files to a customer regional Cloud Storage bucket in the same region as the backup; the service needs permission to create objects. Restoring managed backups seeds a new instance in the same region.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Valkey RDB persistence adds no extra billing charge, retains only the most recent automated recovery snapshot and supports one/six/12/24-hour intervals. These internal recovery snapshots are distinct from separately billed retained backup collections.

facts.label: identity and old names
facts.value: Google Memorystore, Google Cloud's managed in-memory datastore family: Memorystore for Valkey, Memorystore for Redis, Memorystore for Redis Cluster and Memorystore for Memcached.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: Hosted Google Cloud service governed by Google Cloud Terms and service-specific documentation; no self-hosted Memorystore control plane or downloadable Memorystore server edition is offered in the inspected product documentation.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Memorystore for Memcached is deprecated: no longer recommended from 2026-01-20; after 2027-02-01, new-project creation is restricted unless Memcached instances already exist in the project; service use and Cloud Customer Care end on 2029-01-31. Google recommends migrating to Valkey.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Valkey, Redis and Redis Cluster remain publicly offered. Valkey 9.1 became generally available in September 2026; current docs make 9.1 the default.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Company-news check: searched Google Cloud blog and press/newsroom for Memorystore acquisition, shutdown, sunset and deprecation news. Found the Memcached retirement and active Valkey releases; no acquisition or retirement of the entire Memorystore family was found.

facts.label: vendor home and main markets
facts.value: Vendor: Google Cloud. Contracting entity depends on customer billing address; for example United States customers contract with Google LLC and Indian GCP customers with Google Cloud India Private Limited.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: Support paths include public documentation, community Stack Overflow/Google Groups/Slack and paid Cloud Customer Care packages. Community Google-engineer replies are unofficial; technical-response commitments depend on the support package.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: Public incident/status source: Google Cloud Service Health dashboard, https://status.cloud.google.com/.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: SLA outside Stockholm: multi-zone HA Valkey/Redis Cluster target 99.99%; single-zone HA 99.9%; Redis Standard 99.9%. Stockholm multi-zone HA target is 99.95%. Basic Redis, zero-replica instances and shared-core-nano are not equivalent covered HA configurations.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: Memcached SLA applicability needs clarification: the SLA table still lists 99.9%, but the same SLA excludes deprecated services and the product is officially deprecated. Do not present its historical table entry as an unconditional current promise.

Hatchet needs a database to keep its state, but it is not a managed database product.

files.math: Hatchet does not provide file storage.

jobs.math: 10,000 task runs fit within the 1 million runs included each month. Hatchet does not price the outside worker compute.

facts.label: Free offer type

facts.label: Free limits

facts.label: Free limits

facts.label: Free limits

facts.label: Free limits

facts.label: Free limits

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: Configurable webhook endpoints: 10 no-card or 100 card-on-file.

facts.label: Free limits

facts.label: Free limits
