facts.value: Default owner is below superuser. Heroku credential management supports at most 120 credentials on applicable plans, and credentials/connection strings can rotate; external consumers must track updates.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Salesforce privacy notice covers personal data processed as controller and excludes customer processor data; DPA governs customer personal data processing. Privacy retention depends on purpose/legal duties rather than one universal account-data deadline.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: Managed PostgreSQL with SQL and ordinary PostgreSQL clients. Current version policy lists 18 as default, 16/17 available and 15 deprecating; major versions are supported for about three years, not upstream's five.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: Extensions are allow-listed and default owner has no true superuser. Essential and Advanced use AWS RDS-related connection/extension settings; do not assume unrestricted self-managed PostgreSQL feature parity.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: Transactions can group statements with BEGIN/COMMIT; uncommitted row changes are not visible to other transactions. Heroku documents READ COMMITTED as default and configurable SERIALIZABLE with application handling of serialization failures.

facts.label: Test environments and branches
facts.value: Writable snapshot forks are supported Advanced and classic Standard or higher, not Essential. A fork is independent and stops tracking its parent. Classic fast forks may be up to 30 hours old.

facts.label: Test environments and branches
facts.value: Advanced forks copy leader-pool data but do not include a standby/HA by default. Separate test/review-app resources accrue usage; local PostgreSQL is recommended for environment parity.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Classic Premium/Private/Shield primaries include a hidden standby in another availability zone and automatic failover. Standby replication is asynchronous, so recent committed changes can be lost; external clients may need updated connection strings.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Classic read followers are separately billed, read-only and subject to lag; they cannot be chained. Plan-dependent follower limits exist, with a recommendation not to exceed ten. Followers do not automatically get a hidden standby even on Premium/Private/Shield.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Advanced HA leader pool has a leader plus standby; a follower pool needs at least two instances for its own HA. Default leader provisioning enables HA. Documentation says failover has no expected data loss, unlike classic; no-follower/no-standby recovery must create a replacement.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Advanced supports managed logical replication to/from external PostgreSQL or another Advanced cluster, using CLI 11.11.0+. Schema/DDL and sequence state do not automatically replicate; replica identity is needed for applicable updates/deletes.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: A native end-user offline cache, queued offline writes and conflict-resolution contract were not found.

facts.label: Extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Allow-listed extensions include PostGIS, pgvector, pg_trgm, trigger notifications via tcn and built-in full-text search support. Essential excludes foreign data wrappers, pg_partman and pg_prewarm; only listed extensions are available.

facts.label: Extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: pgvector supports exact search, HNSW and IVFFlat indexes; Heroku Connect and Streaming Data Connectors do not synchronize vector data types.

facts.label: Filters and mixed search
facts.value: SQL filters can combine vector search with metadata; PostgreSQL full-text search can be combined for hybrid ranking. Approximate-index filters may return too few results; iterative scans require a supporting extension version.

facts.label: Upload and file limits
facts.value: Not applicable to the managed PostgreSQL database scope.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Not applicable to the managed PostgreSQL database scope.

facts.label: Delivery and private files
facts.value: Not applicable to the managed PostgreSQL database scope.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: Not applicable as an application-worker execution service. Heroku app code and scheduler jobs run on separately billed dynos; the Postgres add-on supplies database access.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Not applicable to the database add-on as a queue-delivery contract; application retries, ordering, deduplication and failed-job replay require the chosen worker/queue system.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Not applicable as durable application-message scheduling/retention. PGBackups schedules create database dumps; they are not user-job queues.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Not applicable as app-job history/replay. Essential has no Postgres logs; other tiers publish database logs/metrics, with platform log retention separate from job results.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Not applicable: Heroku Postgres is provider-operated. Local PostgreSQL is a development-parity option, not a self-hosted Heroku service edition with managed recovery, networking and billing parity.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Common Runtime uses us (United States) and eu (Europe); Essential only in AWS us-east-1/us or eu-west-1/eu. Private Space regions include Dublin, Frankfurt, London, Montreal, Mumbai, Oregon, Singapore, Sydney, Tokyo and Virginia.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Primary database data and continuous-protection base backups/WAL stay in the database region. PGBackups snapshots and Dataclips are stored in the US. Use your own pg_dump for another logical-backup location.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Existing apps do not move region in place; redeploy/migrate. Private Space apps inherit their Space region; add-on regional availability must be checked separately.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Portable exports use pg_dump custom-format files and pg_restore; PGBackups capture/download works on supported plans, while direct logical dumps cover larger databases and tiers without PGBackups.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: PGBackups export URLs are public bearer URLs expiring after 60 minutes. Restoring a PGBackup deletes existing target data first; no partial restore into an existing database through that command.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Heroku security policy keeps a deprovisioned app/database storage volume for one week, then destroys it. The May 2026 product architecture document says database Customer Data is deleted within 30 days of final termination, subject to law.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: PGBackups for deprovisioned add-ons are deleted after a short, unspecified grace period; download before removal. Personal-account closure is irreversible and can be blocked by accrued/unpaid billing; invoices/logs become inaccessible after closure.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Physical continuous protection uses filesystem snapshots/base backups plus WAL. Average/low-change capture aims for at least daily snapshots; physical backups contain structural state and indexes, unlike logical dumps.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Rollback availability: Essential none; Standard up to four days; Premium/Private/Shield and Advanced up to seven days. Rollback creates a new billable database rather than rewinding the original in place; seconds in requested timestamps are ignored.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Essential PGBackups: up to five retained manual backups; scheduled retention seven daily days and one weekly backup, no monthly backups.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Standard PGBackups: 25 manual; scheduled seven daily days/four weekly weeks, no monthly snapshots. Premium: 50 manual; seven daily days/eight weekly weeks/12 monthly backups.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: PGBackups is not supported on Advanced or Shield. Direct pg_dump is the documented logical-export alternative. PGBackups is intended for moderately loaded databases up to 20 GB; bigger/heavy databases need another logical-backup approach.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Scheduled logical backup failures send no notification; verify success. Attachment swaps or plan migrations can lose the effective schedule. Standard PGBackups storage is in the US regardless of database region.

facts.label: File recovery and protection
facts.value: Not applicable to the managed PostgreSQL database scope.

facts.label: Identity and old names
facts.value: Heroku Postgres, the Heroku-managed PostgreSQL service. Heroku is part of Salesforce; credit-card transactions contract with Heroku, Inc., a Delaware corporation.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Hosted managed service: Essential, Advanced and classic Standard/Premium/Private/Shield tiers. No self-hosted Heroku Postgres service edition identified; the service follows Salesforce/Heroku agreements.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Heroku moved to sustaining engineering on February 6, 2026, emphasizing stability, security, reliability and support over new feature development. Credit-card customers can continue using the platform; new Enterprise Account contracts are no longer offered.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Heroku Postgres Advanced became generally available October 6, 2026. This supersedes the May 18 limited-GA notice requiring an access-request support ticket.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Free hobby-dev Postgres ended November 28, 2022. PostgreSQL 15 is deprecating, with EOL February 28, 2027; 16/17/18 have published EOL targets Q3 2027/2028/2029.

facts.label: Vendor home and main markets
facts.value: Credit-card legal entity is Heroku, Inc., Delaware, United States. Salesforce's stated corporate address is San Francisco, California; a complete served-country list was not established.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Paid add-on customers get limited technical support through official tickets; billing/account help available to all. Published base support hours: 9am to 9pm US Eastern, Monday to Friday excluding US holidays. Optional premium support offers 24×7.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Plan guidance: Essential expected uptime 99.5%; Standard tolerates up to one hour downtime/month; Premium/Private/Shield up to 15 minutes, on a 30-day basis. These are published expectations, not a validated self-service service-credit SLA.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Current contractual service-credit SLA for ordinary self-service Postgres plans was not established. Official Heroku pages link a public status dashboard; its fetched route returned no readable incident text.

apps.name: Hetzner Object Storage
apps.line: S3-compatible object storage with shared storage and egress allowances.

free.text: No free tier; €7.72/month while any bucket is active, even if empty

cells.metered: €7.72/month account base includes 1 TB storage and egress
cells.regions: Falkenstein, Nuremberg, or Helsinki; one site per bucket

sql.math: Hetzner Object Storage is not a database
Hetzner Object Storage is not a database

files.math: 100 GB is 0.1 TB, which is 72 TB-hours of storage and 0.1 TB of outbound data (egress). Both fit within the included amounts for 30 days, and upload and download requests (PUT and GET) are free.

jobs.math: Hetzner Object Storage stores files; it does not run background jobs

facts.label: free offer type
facts.value: No separate lasting free plan, free trial, or introductory credit is published for Object Storage in the current pricing and product materials.

facts.label: free offer type
facts.value: A bucket incurs the account base charge for every hour at least one bucket is active, including an empty bucket; this is incompatible with treating the service as free while a bucket exists.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: Free-plan quotas for storage, requests, projects, or users are not applicable because Hetzner does not publish a free plan for Object Storage.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: Buckets do not automatically sleep when unused. Hetzner bills each hour with at least one active bucket, even if it is empty.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: The reviewed product docs do not publish an idle grace period that pauses or deletes a bucket automatically.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: Deleting a bucket requires it to be empty and its Console protection to be inactive. If an account has no active bucket, the account-wide hourly base charge no longer accrues.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: Current German product pricing shows a base price of €7.72 per month including Germany's 19% VAT. It applies per Object Storage account across buckets and locations, not per Hetzner Cloud server.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: Hetzner's VAT policy says net prices are the same for customers; tax is based on the customer's residence. German customers pay 19% VAT; eligible EU business customers with a valid VAT ID use reverse charge.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: The English product FAQ shows €0.0104 per active hour excluding VAT; the German FAQ shows €0.0124 per hour including 19% VAT. The monthly price is capped and the German page gives the €7.72 gross monthly base.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: The product is billed monthly; the general cancellation guide says Object Storage is prorated for the period held and not billed above its monthly price.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Base billing starts in each hour when an account has at least one active bucket. The base price is hourly, with a monthly cap.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: The base includes 1 TB of storage quota and 1 TB of egress quota at full-month use; the storage allowance is measured in TB-hours and the egress allowance in TB.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: The maximum included storage quota is 744 TB-hours and 1.1160 TB traffic in a 31-day month; 720 TB-hours and 1.0800 TB in a 30-day month.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: In 29-day and 28-day months, maximum included quotas are 696 TB-hours and 1.0440 TB, and 672 TB-hours and 1.0080 TB, respectively.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Storage is metered as TB-hours: stored TB multiplied by hours held. Example formula in the docs: 1 TB for 1 hour equals 1 TB-hour.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: The base quota is aggregated across buckets, projects, and locations on the account; unused monthly allowance expires and does not roll over.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Current German pricing gives the monthly base as €7.72 including 19% VAT and the hourly figure as €0.0124 including 19% VAT. Current English pricing shows €0.0104 per hour excluding VAT.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: The current German product FAQ displays egress overage as €1.1900 per TB including 19% VAT. Its surrounding overage text says prices exclude VAT, so the current page's tax labels conflict.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: The current product page says excess storage is billed per TB-hour, but the numeric amount is blank in the English and German live FAQ text.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: The current page says storage and traffic overages are billed in increments of 100 MB, with usage precision of four decimal places in TB.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Incoming traffic, internal traffic in network zone eu-central, and S3 API operations such as PUT, GET, and DELETE are listed as free. GET response egress can still be billable.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: The 2024 launch announcement listed €0.0067 per TB-hour for extra storage and €1.00 per TB egress before VAT. Those figures are historical and not treated as current following the April 2026 price change.

facts.label: idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Compute billing and scale-to-zero behavior are not applicable to this storage-only service.

facts.label: idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: There is no compute that wakes on request; buckets are addressed through S3 endpoints.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: Ingress is free. Egress to the public internet is pooled against the included 1 TB monthly quota, then metered per TB.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: Internal traffic within Hetzner's eu-central network zone is listed as free.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: The current German product FAQ displays €1.1900 per TB of egress including 19% VAT; the English FAQ's current price text omits the number.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: S3 requests are free, but egress generated by a GET is billed against the egress allowance or overage rate.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: If monthly storage or egress exceeds its accumulated allowance, Hetzner bills the excess pay-as-you-go.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: Hetzner says the base is capped at a monthly price; excess storage and traffic remain separate meters and are not included in that base cap.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: The reviewed Object Storage pricing FAQ, billing docs, and terms do not publish a product-specific hard usage cutoff or a guaranteed total-spend cap for overages.

facts.label: storage prices
facts.value: Hetzner lists one Standard storage class; the general FAQ shows no hot, cold, or archive class menu.

facts.label: storage prices
facts.value: The account base includes up to 1 TB of storage allowance, measured as TB-hours: up to 720 TB-hours in a 30-day month.

facts.label: storage prices
facts.value: The numeric current extra-storage rate per TB-hour is not visible in the live English or German product FAQ or the linked overview docs.

facts.label: file request and retrieval prices
facts.value: PUT, GET, and DELETE API operations are listed as free; incoming traffic is also free.

facts.label: file request and retrieval prices
facts.value: Egress above the pooled allowance is billed per TB; the current German FAQ displays €1.1900/TB including 19% VAT, while its generic overage note says prices exclude VAT.

facts.label: file request and retrieval prices
facts.value: The service has no archive retrieval fee schedule because the docs identify one Standard class; Restore is among the unsupported S3 actions.

facts.label: minimum storage and early deletion
facts.value: The minimum billable object size is 64 kB. An object smaller than that is billed as 64 kB.

facts.label: minimum storage and early deletion
facts.value: The reviewed pricing and bucket docs do not state a minimum storage duration or an early-deletion fee for the Standard class.

facts.label: minimum storage and early deletion
facts.value: The account base charge can still apply while an empty bucket exists; an empty bucket is not a zero-cost object-storage account.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: A customer can create a bucket in a Hetzner project through the Hetzner Console; bucket setup asks for a location, unique name, and public or private visibility.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: A Hetzner account and project are needed to create buckets and S3 credentials in the Console.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: The public pricing, setup, terms, and FAQ pages reviewed do not state whether a payment card is required before ordering Object Storage.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: The product pages list storage locations, not a complete list of countries whose residents may open accounts. The terms require lawful use and include additional terms for customers located in the United States.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: The general terms prohibit illegal or infringing content, spam, and cryptocurrency-mining applications. They allow suspension or termination for listed violations.

facts.label: primary type and other roles
facts.value: Primary type: managed object storage for unstructured files in buckets. This directory classification follows Hetzner's description of objects, buckets, and S3 access.

facts.label: primary type and other roles
facts.value: Objects are read or replaced as whole objects; this is not a block volume or a database. Hetzner warns that the service is not suited to every S3 workload.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: The included product is bucket-based file/object storage with an S3 API.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: A managed database, user authentication service, application runtime, serverless functions, or job queue is not listed as part of Object Storage.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: The service exposes a basic-compatible Amazon S3 API at a location-specific endpoint. The documented endpoints are fsn1.your-objectstorage.com, nbg1.your-objectstorage.com, and hel1.your-objectstorage.com.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Hetzner documents the AWS CLI, AWS SDKs, curl, S3cmd, MinIO AIStor Client, and other compatible tools for connecting to buckets.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: AWS SDK examples are documented for Python, Go, and .NET; S3-compatible libraries can also be configured with the endpoint and credentials.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Authentication uses an access key and secret key with AWS Signature Version 4. Keys are created in the Hetzner Console.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: The Console handles basic tasks such as creating buckets and credentials; bucket and object management otherwise uses the S3 API.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Hetzner says a dedicated API for Hetzner-specific features such as generating credentials or checking usage is not currently available.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Buckets can be public or private. Private buckets require S3 credentials; a public bucket permits unauthenticated reads by object URL, while writes still need credentials.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Public bucket visibility permits reading objects but does not permit listing the bucket contents.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: By default, each S3 key pair in a project can read and write every existing and future bucket in that project.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Bucket policies can restrict access by key, but the policy element NotAction is not supported. Restricting keys can also make objects unavailable in the Hetzner Console file list.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: A private object's presigned URL can grant time-limited browser or command-line download access without giving the recipient S3 keys.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Object data is not encrypted at rest by default. Hetzner supports SSE-C on upload, with a customer-provided key that Hetzner does not keep.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: The product page says backup objects are protected from unauthorized reading by server-side encryption, while the technical FAQ says there is no default data-at-rest encryption and lists customer-provided SSE-C.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: TLS 1.3 and TLS 1.2 are documented for the API; Hetzner labels TLS 1.2 deprecated and says support will end in the near future.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: A Data Processing Agreement is available, but the general terms say it is not concluded automatically; customers who process third-party personal data must arrange it through their customer account.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Hetzner's privacy policy covers personal data processed through its websites and online services; it does not give a product-specific Object Storage data-retention schedule.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: Up to 100 buckets may be created; each bucket may hold up to 100 TB and 50,000,000 objects.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: A single PUT can upload an object up to 5 GB; larger uploads require multipart, with an upper limit of 5 GB per part.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: A multipart upload can contain up to 10,000 parts, and an object can be up to 5 TB.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: Custom metadata is limited to 8 kB per object.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: The documented limit is 256 active parallel TCP sessions per source IP.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: The documented request limit is 750 requests per second per source IP.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: The documented request limit is 750 requests per second per bucket.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: The documented throughput limit is 10 Gbit/s per bucket for reading or writing.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: The FAQ does not publish allowed file-type restrictions; the storage API accepts objects, and application-level file validation remains the customer's responsibility.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: The docs explain multipart uploads, but do not promise a separate provider-managed resumable-upload feature.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: The API offers basic compatibility with standard Amazon S3 actions and data types, not full S3 parity.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Supported access uses the Amazon S3 REST API, Hetzner endpoints, and S3-compatible tools such as AWS CLI, S3cmd, rclone, and MinIO AIStor Client.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Bucket creation supports only the documented Object Lock and ACL headers, with private or public-read ACL values; the creation configuration accepts LocationConstraint.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: SSE-C is the only listed S3 server-side encryption mode; copying SSE-C encrypted objects is unsupported.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: The supported-actions page marks Request-Payment, Notifications, Accelerate, Website, Analytics, Intelligent Tiering, Inventory, Logging, Metrics, Ownership Controls, Replication, Tagging, Restore, Select, Torrent, GetObjectAttributes, and CreateSession as unsupported.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: CopyObject is supported only when source and destination are the same bucket.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: For noncurrent-version lifecycle expiration, only the NoncurrentDays option is supported.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Custom bucket domains and the bucket website feature are not native supported actions.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Bucket policy NotAction is unsupported; Hetzner's policy FAQ says it has no effect even if accepted.

facts.label: delivery and private files
facts.value: Buckets may be private or public. Public buckets serve objects by URL; private buckets require S3 credentials unless a signed URL is issued.

facts.label: delivery and private files
facts.value: Presigned URLs grant time-limited access to a private object without sharing the S3 secret key with the recipient.

facts.label: delivery and private files
facts.value: Assigning a custom domain directly to a bucket is not supported. A CNAME by itself may fail because the request host and TLS SNI must match the bucket endpoint.

facts.label: delivery and private files
facts.value: Hetzner documents user-run NGINX and S3 Proxy approaches for a custom domain; these need a server and are not included Object Storage delivery features.

facts.label: delivery and private files
facts.value: No built-in CDN is included. Hetzner recommends a third-party CDN for public objects served to large audiences.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Buckets can be placed in Falkenstein, Germany (FSN1), Nuremberg, Germany (NBG1), or Helsinki, Finland (HEL1).

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Each bucket's data is stored exclusively in the single data center selected when creating that bucket. The data is not automatically stored in all three locations.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: The endpoints are fsn1.your-objectstorage.com, nbg1.your-objectstorage.com, and hel1.your-objectstorage.com, respectively.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: The base charge and included usage are account-wide across projects and locations; the current published EUR price is not a location-specific rate.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: The FAQ describes built-in redundancy within the selected cluster. Cross-location replication is not supported by the S3 API action list.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Hetzner markets the service as GDPR-compliant, but the bucket location alone does not establish legal suitability for a customer's data or use case.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Data can be copied through S3-compatible tools, including MinIO AIStor Client, rclone, S3cmd, and AWS CLI. Hetzner publishes a migration guide from another S3 provider.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: The migration guide warns that rclone, S3cmd, and AWS CLI do not copy custom metadata in its listed workflows; it suggests MinIO AIStor Client when metadata must be preserved.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Hetzner's general cancellation guide lists Hetzner Console as the cancellation interface for Object Storage and says data may be deleted immediately after cancellation, with no recovery.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Object Lock does not extend the customer contract. Hetzner says it permanently deletes stored data after contract termination even when an object retention period remains.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Hetzner's DPA describes returning or deleting customer personal data on request after the main contract ends, subject to legal obligations and the DPA terms.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: No separate export fee is stated in the migration guide; download traffic is subject to Object Storage's egress meter and allowance.

facts.label: file recovery and protection
facts.value: Versioning can retain prior object versions after replacement or deletion; each stored version consumes storage.

facts.label: file recovery and protection
facts.value: Object Lock can use legal hold or retention, including Governance and Compliance modes; enabling Object Lock is required when the bucket is created.

facts.label: file recovery and protection
facts.value: Lifecycle rules can expire current objects, remove noncurrent versions, clear expired delete markers, and abort incomplete multipart uploads.

facts.label: file recovery and protection
facts.value: Hetzner does not promise an automatic customer backup copy for Object Storage; its technical measures list puts the backup and recovery plan on the customer and recommend external backups.

facts.label: file recovery and protection
facts.value: Each object is distributed across multiple servers in its selected cluster; Hetzner says erasure coding can preserve data integrity despite failure of up to three storage servers.

facts.label: file recovery and protection
facts.value: Replication to another location is not supported by the S3 API action list, and each bucket is stored at one selected data center.

facts.label: file recovery and protection
facts.value: After contract termination, Hetzner says it permanently deletes stored data even when versioning or Object Lock retention was enabled.

facts.label: identity and old names
facts.value: The current product name is Hetzner Object Storage. The official product page and docs describe it as S3-compatible storage; the docs sometimes use “Hetzner Cloud Object Storage” as a descriptive phrase.

facts.label: identity and old names
facts.value: No former product name was published on the product page, Object Storage docs index, overview, or launch announcement.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: Hetzner operates the hosted service. Customers manage buckets and objects through the Hetzner Console and S3-compatible API.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: A self-hosted Hetzner Object Storage software license is not applicable to this hosted product.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: The product page, pricing information, docs, and public bucket-creation guide are live. The app row is active, and the service is presented as orderable.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Current incident: Object Storage in FSN1 was partially degraded from 2026-11-06 08:55 UTC. Hetzner said specific customer buckets were affected and some requests could fail or time out; status was Investigating.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: A previous HEL1 incident affecting some buckets, with elevated response times and stalled requests, was closed on 2026-10-22.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: A previous high-traffic incident affecting Object Storage was marked resolved on 2026-09-29. The status history described occasional request timeouts while Hetzner expanded capacity.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: IBM Cloud's account-type page says Pay-As-You-Go accounts require payment information; a separate free-trial signup page advertises trial access without requiring a credit card.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions

facts.label: signup and use restrictions

facts.label: primary type and other roles
facts.value: Primary type: hosted object storage for unstructured files and data. This directory classification follows IBM's service overview.

facts.label: primary type and other roles
facts.value: Secondary roles include backup targets, archive, media, application assets, and analytics data. COS is not an application database or compute runtime.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: The service includes buckets and object storage operations, plus native lifecycle, versioning, replication, retention/Object Lock, quotas, and IAM integration where supported by region and instance type.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: COS does not bundle an application database, end-user authentication, serverless functions, or job workers. IBM IAM controls cloud resource access; it is not an app-user identity system.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: Continuous Backup is an optional COS feature with its own backup-storage and restore charges; it is not included as an unlimited free backup.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: COS exposes a REST API with a subset of the Amazon S3 API; IBM lists supported operations and differences.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Applications can authenticate with IBM IAM tokens or HMAC service credentials; the S3-compatible API is available over HTTPS.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: IBM publishes COS SDKs for Java, Python, Go, Node.js, and other languages, as well as CLI access.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: The S3-compatible API paginates object listings; a list request returns up to 1,000 keys, and an instance supports up to 1,000 buckets.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: IBM's compatibility guide advises users to configure a COS endpoint and HMAC credentials explicitly when adapting AWS SDKs.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: New buckets are private unless the customer configures public access; public access requires enabling the account-level setting and applying bucket policy or object ACL rules.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: IBM IAM policies can scope service credentials to an instance, bucket, or object; service credentials are associated with a service ID.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: IBM encrypts stored data at rest by default. Optional customer-managed encryption can use Key Protect or Hyper Protect Crypto Services, which are separate IBM services.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: COS supports customer-provided encryption keys (SSE-C) for object requests in addition to IBM-managed encryption.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: COS API endpoints support TLS; IBM's endpoint documentation lists HTTPS access and location-specific service endpoints.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Customers can restrict network access with bucket IP firewalls and related context-based restrictions where supported.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: IBM documents CORS settings for browser-based cross-origin requests; CORS does not replace IAM or bucket authorization.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: COS data is strongly consistent for object operations; bucket configuration updates can take longer to propagate.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: Maximum individual object size is 10 TB when using multipart upload; a single-threaded PUT is limited to 5 GB.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: Multipart upload supports up to 10,000 parts, each up to 5 GB; IBM requires parts to be at least 5 MB except for the final part.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: Multipart upload can be paused/retried by managing parts; incomplete uploads must be completed or aborted and otherwise continue to consume storage.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: IBM documents object keys up to 1,024 characters; bucket names and names follow S3-compatible naming constraints.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: IBM documents a subset of S3-compatible REST operations for buckets, objects, multipart transfers, ACLs, and related configuration; consult the compatibility matrix before migrating tools.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: The published instance maximum is 1,000 buckets; object listings return at most 1,000 keys per request and require pagination for larger results.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: IBM warns that rate limits can produce HTTP 429 or 503 responses; applications should back off and retry rather than assume unlimited request rate.

facts.label: delivery and private files
facts.value: Buckets are private by default. Customers can grant public access through account settings and bucket policies, or issue authenticated application requests.

facts.label: delivery and private files
facts.value: COS does not automatically provide a static-website hosting product; IBM says a web server or another service is needed to serve site behavior such as index pages.

facts.label: delivery and private files
facts.value: COS has public, private, and direct endpoint options; public outbound transfer can incur COS bandwidth charges, while private/direct endpoint traffic is listed as free.

facts.label: delivery and private files
facts.value: No bundled CDN or custom-domain delivery feature is listed as part of the COS storage plan; IBM Cloud CDN or another delivery layer is a separate service choice.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: COS offers Regional, Cross Region, and Single Data Center resiliency choices; regional and cross-region options span multiple zones/locations, while Single Data Center is confined to one data center.

facts.label: regions and data location

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: A selected storage location is a product configuration; it does not by itself prove legal suitability or regulatory compliance for a customer's data.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Objects can be downloaded or copied through the S3-compatible API, SDKs, CLI, or console; IBM also documents replication and migration workflows.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Bucket location or storage class cannot simply be edited to migrate existing objects; create a destination bucket and copy or replicate data.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Deleting a COS instance allows restoration during a seven-day reclamation period; after the reclamation completes, the instance and remaining data are irreversibly deleted.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Versioning retains prior object versions after overwrite or deletion and can help recover them; versioning must be configured for the bucket.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Object Lock provides retention and legal-hold controls for supported buckets; locked objects cannot be deleted before the applicable retention allows it.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: IBM's privacy statement explains IBM's general handling of personal information; the Cloud Terms point to service and account-specific agreements and data-processing terms.

facts.value: Versioning retains prior object versions after overwrite or delete, but must be enabled and increases stored bytes that can be billed.

facts.label: file recovery and protection
facts.value: Replication copies objects asynchronously to a configured destination bucket; it supports regional or cross-region designs where available but can replicate accidental changes/deletions depending on configuration.

facts.label: file recovery and protection
facts.value: Object Lock supports retention and legal holds for eligible buckets; IBM added replication of Object Lock settings in June 2026.

facts.label: file recovery and protection
facts.value: Continuous Backup offers point-in-time backup and restore to a backup vault; it must be configured and incurs separate storage and restore fees.

facts.label: file recovery and protection
facts.value: COS does not create a user-configured continuous backup of every bucket by default; IBM's backup feature is optional and must be set up.

facts.label: file recovery and protection
facts.value: IBM's service resiliency SLO states 99.999999999999% durability, but that is not an object-version recovery guarantee or contractual data-loss warranty.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: At Lite storage over 1 GB, new/create/update writes receive HTTP 402; reads/deletes remain available. Upgrade restores writes immediately; deleting below the cap restores them within 24 hours.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: Exceeding provisioned throughput rejects requests with HTTP 429 by request class over a sliding one-second window; other classes can continue. Requests are admitted again within seconds after usage falls.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: IBM Cloud spending notifications trigger at 80%, 90% and 100% of configured thresholds; they do not stop charges. Storage over Standard's included allowance is billable.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Classic and Gen 2 limits: JSON document 1 MB, single attachment 10 MB, total request body 64 MB, partition 10 GB; consult support before a database exceeds 5 TB. Default request timeout 60 s, partition-scoped timeout 5 s.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Classic and Gen 2 Limits list 64 MB request bodies; the Classic CouchDB comparison and replication example still use 11 MB.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Gen 2: default 200 databases/instance; Standard supports 1–100 capacity blocks; Isolated supports 40/60/80/100 and up to 16 TB physical storage. Capacity is shared by all databases in an instance.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Exact per-instance HTTP connection/stream cap and recommended SDK pool ceiling were not found.

facts.value: Document attachments share database storage and its included allowance; a separate hot/archive bucket-class tariff was not established. Classic published above-20-GB rate is $0.0014/GB/hour; Gen 2 numeric rate remains unverified.

facts.value: Attachment create/update/read/delete goes through document/attachment APIs and reserved database capacity; a separate per-file-request or retrieval tariff was not found.

facts.value: Not applicable: independent object-store classes, per-object minimum storage duration or archive early-deletion pricing.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: Native vector indexes, supported dimensions and vector-count quotas were not found in the inspected Cloudant docs.

facts.label: embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: Not applicable to an established native Cloudant embedding/reranking module; no such module or included token allowance was established.

facts.label: run limits and pricing
facts.value: Database request limits are 60 seconds by default and 5 seconds for partition requests; no separate included vCPU/GB-second/invocation worker bundle is established.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: New IBM Cloud accounts are Pay-As-You-Go and require card information for identity verification, including when using a Lite service. Grandfathered Lite accounts created before 2021-10-25 remain distinct.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Classic Lite is positioned for evaluation/testing; Standard supports development and production. Exact country exclusions, full usage restrictions and Cloudant-specific contract conditions could not be verified.

facts.label: primary type and other roles
facts.value: Primary: managed JSON document database. Secondary: full-text search, MapReduce/Mango queries, replication and offline app integrations. These directory labels are our classification.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: Native JSON databases, queries/indexes, document attachments, changes feeds and CouchDB-compatible replication. Official full-app examples add separate Code Engine/Object Storage services; Cloudant IAM secures database access rather than providing app-user MAU authentication.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: HTTPS REST/JSON API and officially supported Java, Node.js, Python and Go SDKs. API/replication compatibility with CouchDB has documented differences.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Classic supports IAM or IAM plus legacy credentials. Gen 2 supports IAM only; migrating changes the service URL and credentials, and the original URL cannot be retained.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Classic supports database/instance-scoped IAM roles and legacy database keys; use IAM-only when relying on restricted IAM roles, because broader legacy credentials can defeat intended restrictions. Broader IAM policies override narrower grants.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Cloudant access uses HTTPS and TLS 1.2+; at-rest encryption is provided. Classic Dedicated Hardware supports customer Key Protect keys selected at provisioning; Gen 2 security docs describe provider-managed keys.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Classic shared Lite/Standard have public endpoints; IP allowlisting is reserved for dedicated environments. Gen 2 has public and VPE endpoints and context-based restrictions for IP/VPC zones; its public endpoint cannot be disabled.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: Managed CouchDB-based JSON document store, partitioned/sharded; REST document access, Mango/Cloudant Query selectors, MapReduce views and full-text search. No relational SQL/multi-document join engine is implied.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Eventually consistent, multi-primary distributed model; concurrent updates use MVCC and _rev checks, with HTTP 409 for stale revisions. Replication conflicts require application resolution.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Bulk document writes are not an all-or-none multi-document transaction. Even HTTP 201 can contain per-document failures; inspect each result. Related business data must be modeled for these semantics.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Independent test databases/instances can be provisioned; replication or JSON backup/restore can clone data. Database counts and provisioned instance resources still apply.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Built-in in-region redundancy writes three copies; documented multizone deployments remain readable/writable through zone outages without customer failover. Single-zone Classic locations have a different failure boundary.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Cross-region active-active/active-passive replication is customer configured per database. The application detects regional failure and reroutes; no replication-latency SLA is documented. Source reads and target writes consume each instance's capacity.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: _changes supports normal, long-poll and continuous feeds. Clients reconnect when feeds close. PouchDB integration enables local browser data and bidirectional synchronization when connectivity returns.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Tombstone cleanup is planned/rolling out in late 2026: deleted metadata remains at least 90 days, then is removed, typically 1–7 days later. Consumers/replicas offline beyond 90 days can miss deletes.

facts.label: extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: JSON/Mango indexes, partial indexes, MapReduce views and Lucene full-text search. Limits list unlimited global indexes and 10 partition indexes. Gen 2 launch notes identify Lucene 10.

facts.label: extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Geospatial availability conflicts: current product marketing advertises geospatial indexing, but the dedicated notice says Geo support ended in 2023 and _geo endpoints return 404.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: Attachments are BLOBs in _attachments, with MIME type/name; upload using attachment PUT or inline base64. Single attachment limit 10 MB, single JSON document 1 MB, overall request limit disputed as D03.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Not applicable: an S3-compatible object-store API. Cloudant uses CouchDB-style document/attachment HTTPS endpoints.

facts.label: delivery and private files
facts.value: Attachment GET returns raw content through the database's authenticated HTTPS API. A native per-file expiring signed URL, CDN or custom-domain delivery feature was not found.

facts.label: filters and mixed search
facts.value: Keyword/full-text search and JSON selector filters are documented; a native dense/sparse vector-plus-keyword ranking mode was not established.

facts.label: execution model and languages
facts.value: Cloudant runs database design-document JavaScript for indexing/filtering; Classic is migrating from SpiderMonkey to QuickJS with ES2023 support. This is not a general serverless worker platform.

facts.label: delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Not applicable: general message-queue delivery, deduplication, dead-letter and replay guarantees.

facts.label: schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Not applicable: general delayed-job payload/queue retention or included cron worker. Backup guide suggests customer-operated cron/scripts around CouchBackup.

facts.label: logs and run history
facts.value: Classic database logs can route to a separately provisioned IBM Cloud Logs instance; active-task and replication-task monitoring are available.

facts.label: logs and run history
facts.value: Cloudant-specific included log-retention days/bytes, historical task-retention guarantee and log export fee were not found.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Not applicable: IBM Cloudant is hosted/managed; there is no self-hosted Cloudant edition established by these sources. Apache CouchDB is the separate self-managed alternative.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Gen 2 region lists conflict: Plans lists us-south, eu-de, eu-gb, eu-es, au-syd, us-east; the September 30 release adds ca-tor, jp-tok, jp-osa, in-mum and br-sao. Generation overview omits in-mum from its broader list.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Classic plan guide lists Chennai and Seoul as single-zone, plus Dallas, Frankfurt, London, Osaka, Sydney, Tokyo and Washington DC. Frankfurt is EU-managed and has account/API-key access conditions.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Cloudant governance docs say URL-bearing logs can leave the deployment region for centralized logging. The specific data-sheet exhibit describing processing locations could not be read.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Export using CouchDB-compatible replication or CouchBackup JSON-lines files; index design documents can move, but indexes must rebuild. CouchBackup does not support Cloudant databases containing attachments and excludes _security settings.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Instance deletion has a 7-day grace period before instance data and authentication information are deleted. Support-ticket information is excluded. Ordinary database deletion cannot be undone through the service.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Database deletion retains internal trash for up to 48 hours before filesystem removal; document deletion leaves tombstone metadata. Compaction timing for old document bodies is not guaranteed.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Gen 1 to Gen 2 migration uses continuous replication into a new instance and a client cutover; source can keep running. Standard-Gen2 to Isolated-Gen2 cannot be changed in place and also requires a new instance/replication.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Automatic three-copy redundancy is included, but Cloudant does not automatically back up customer databases. You must run and retain your backups; no included nightly retention/PITR window is promised by the backup guide.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Supported CouchBackup exports JSON in batches; it is not a precise point-in-time snapshot. _security and attachments are unsupported/excluded; design-document index definitions restore, then indexes rebuild.

facts.label: file recovery and protection
facts.value: Attachments do not have independent revisions; document revisions are transient and compacted, not durable file versioning. CouchBackup does not support Cloudant attachment databases; plan a different file-protection path.

facts.label: identity and old names
facts.value: IBM Cloudant, operated by IBM; official URL https://www.ibm.com/products/cloudant. Older materials use Cloudant and Cloudant NoSQL DB.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: Hosted database service under IBM cloud agreements. Classic Lite/Standard share infrastructure; Dedicated Hardware hosts Standard instances on a private cluster. Gen 2 offers shared Standard and single-tenant Isolated.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: Built on Apache CouchDB, with largely compatible APIs and replication protocol. CouchDB is a separate self-managed project; its open-source license must not be assigned to the entire Cloudant hosted service.

facts.value: Billable execution unit: one durable function run or one step execution. A run with five steps consumes six executions.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing

facts.label: Run limits and pricing

facts.label: Run limits and pricing

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Concurrency counts actively executing steps, not all existing runs; sleeping and waiting runs release their execution slot.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Retries can increase execution usage; the pricing FAQ says multi-step jobs with retries use more executions but does not itemize whether each failed attempt is billed as a separate execution in every case.

facts.label: Primary type and other roles
facts.value: Primary directory type: jobs, queues, and events. Inngest coordinates durable, event-triggered function workflows with persistent steps, retries, waits, and flow control.

facts.label: Primary type and other roles
facts.value: Inngest also provides event ingestion, event queues, scheduling, realtime messaging, observability, and AI evaluation features; it is not a general database or user-authentication backend.

facts.value: Cloud includes durable function orchestration, event intake and queues, flow control, event/cron triggers, retries, and run/step observability; individual quotas differ by plan.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Inngest does not host the customer's normal application database or application endpoint; its executor calls an HTTP endpoint or connected worker supplied by the customer.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Sandboxes are isolated microVMs for commands run inside a function. They are public beta for Pro and higher accounts using the TypeScript SDK, and have separate compute pricing.

facts.value: Officially linked SDKs include TypeScript, Python, Go, and Kotlin; use the matching SDK and its current compatibility guide for the app runtime.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Functions can be served as HTTP endpoints on a supported host or run through Inngest Connect workers that maintain a connection to Cloud.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: The platform exposes event and function APIs; events can be sent from an SDK or through the HTTP API.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Event and cron triggers can start functions; step.waitForEvent() and sleep primitives pause a durable run.

facts.value: Inngest signs requests to customer apps with environment-scoped signing keys and TLS; SDKs validate signatures and timestamps help prevent replay of requests.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Cloud API keys are scoped to environments; production and test environments have separate apps, functions, event history, and credentials.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Inngest says database data is encrypted at rest and application traffic uses TLS/SSL encryption in transit.

facts.label: Data access controls

facts.label: Data access controls

facts.label: Execution model and languages

facts.label: Execution model and languages

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Each step.run() has its own retry count; default is four retries after the initial attempt. Completed prior steps are reused when a later step retries.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: TypeScript SDK v4 allows configuring 0–20 retries; setting zero disables automatic retries. Other SDK versions may differ.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Retry policy uses exponential backoff and jitter; retryable work can run again, so side effects should be safe to repeat.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Events and runs can be replayed or resumed using the documented run-management tools; replay can repeat application side effects.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: The inspected event, retry, and concurrency docs do not promise globally ordered processing or exactly-once delivery across all functions and keys.

facts.value: Inngest supports cron and event-triggered schedule patterns. A user-configured wait can last up to one year, subject to maximum run duration by plan.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention

facts.label: Primary type and other roles
facts.value: Researcher classification: backend platform; relational SQL database, authentication, files, functions, realtime, vector search and container hosting.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Native database, auth, object files, realtime and edge functions; optional Custom Compute and Model Gateway. Storage and functions have plan quotas.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Cloud-managed email or custom SMTP; SMS and push are roadmap items. Self-hosting needs its own SMTP provider, including for auth email.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Direct Postgres connection string for Cloud, supporting psql and native tools; privileged postgres role, TLS sslmode=require. REST database API through PostgREST.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Official TypeScript/JavaScript SDK for browsers, Node and edge runtimes; Swift for Apple platforms; Kotlin for Android and Multiplatform.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: HTTP REST callable from other languages; SigV4 S3 clients through a partial gateway; realtime clients use Socket.IO.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: New managed tables enable row-level security by default; no policy means default-deny. Anonymous key uses anon role; full-access project API key bypasses row rules.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Organization Administrator manages projects/members; Developer cannot manage members. Membership grants access to every project in that organization.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Function secrets encrypted at rest, hidden in lists, optionally expiring/protected; environment variables are plain configuration. Realtime and file policies use Postgres row rules.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Cloud private endpoints/IP allowlists not found; self-hosted production Compose binds database and PostgREST ports to loopback.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: Full PostgreSQL SQL database; docs architecture identifies PostgreSQL 15 and PostgREST 12.2. Self-hosted production image tag is postgres:v15.13.4.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: Cloud minor/major version maintenance policy and selectable database versions not found.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: Documented direct SQL import supports --single-transaction: a failed statement rolls the whole import back.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: SDK multi-call transaction contract, default hosted isolation/replica consistency and cross-request atomicity not established.

facts.label: Test environments and branches
facts.value: Branches on OSS 2.1.0+: isolated child project/EC2; full schema+data or schema-only; three-way configuration/schema merge, user rows not auto-merged. Containers/sites excluded.

facts.label: Test environments and branches
facts.value: Branch quotas: 3 parent projects per org, 2 active branches per parent, no nesting. Merge does not delete branch; exact branch-specific tariff/plan eligibility not found.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Region announcement describes cross-region replication/automatic failover as future exploration. Current read-replica topology, managed failover and prices not established.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Socket.IO realtime: database-trigger broadcasts, channel publish/subscribe, presence and webhook fan-out; message history retained according to configurable days or indefinitely when null.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Persistent offline reads/writes, missed-event completeness and conflict resolution guarantees not found.

facts.label: Extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: pgvector with HNSW and IVFFlat indexes; self-host config preloads pg_cron, http, pgcrypto and insforge_pg_utils. Full managed extension/version catalog not found.

facts.label: Upload and file limits
facts.value: S3 gateway: PutObject up to 5 GB; multipart up to 5 TB. Project max 50 S3 keys; clock-skew tolerance 15 minutes.

facts.label: Upload and file limits
facts.value: Self-host REST/SDK upload default 50 MB, configurable; storage-config API accepts maxFileSizeMb 1–200. Larger S3-gateway objects use its separate limits.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Partial AWS SigV4 S3 gateway, path-style only. No session tokens, virtual-host addressing or gateway presigned URLs; versioning, SSE-C/KMS, ACL, object lock, tagging, lifecycle and CORS return 501.

facts.label: Delivery and private files
facts.value: Public buckets serve directly; private require auth/signed strategy. Bucket-create REST API defaults isPublic to true unless specified.

facts.label: Delivery and private files
facts.value: Overview claims native presigned URLs and backend never proxies bytes; detailed gateway says presigned URLs unsupported, while self-host proxy mode explicitly streams through backend.

facts.label: Delivery and private files
facts.value: CloudFront integration mentioned for AWS-backed storage only; a current Cloud files custom-domain/CDN inclusion and price matrix not found.

facts.label: Filters and mixed search
facts.value: Vector similarity and score threshold SQL/RPC documented; ordinary SDK supports equality/range/pattern filters; per-user data access uses RLS.

facts.label: Filters and mixed search
facts.value: Packaged sparse-vector/keyword+dense hybrid ranking and reranker behavior not established.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: Managed HTTP edge functions execute JavaScript/TypeScript in Deno; HTTP, database triggers and schedules. Optional Docker-image Custom Compute runs long-lived workers/other container languages.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: REST reference still says Cloud Deno Subhosting; June 18 migration notice says new Cloud functions run Deno Deploy v2.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Functions overview promises schedule retry on failure; dedicated Schedules Limits says failed runs logged but not retried; function must be idempotent.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Job ordering, deduplication window, dead-letter queue, durable replay and exactly-once delivery not found.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Schedule overview says five-field cron, no seconds and minimum 1 minute; create-schedule API accepts five-field cron OR 1–59-second interval form.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Schedule API accepts JSON body and headers; queue/delay TTL, maximum payload and Cloud schedule timezone not found.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Functions capture structured invocation logs; containers provide logs by service/time; schedules record status/duration with paginated history and configurable retentionDays (integer ≥1 or null).

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Plan-specific function/container history retention and replay guarantees not found; log search warns CloudWatch ignores offset and can repeat first-page results.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Production self-host minimum: 2 vCPU, 2 GB RAM, 20 GB SSD, Ubuntu 22.04+; recommended 4 vCPU/4 GB+/40 GB+. Docker Compose runs Postgres, PostgREST, Node backend/dashboard and local Deno.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Operator handles TLS/firewall, credentials, updates, backups and restore. Guide includes pre-update backup, rollback and off-site copy; local storage default, optional external S3/MinIO/RustFS.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Cloud sender unavailable in ordinary self-hosted instances: bring SMTP. Custom Compute can use opt-in local Docker socket or your Fly account; local Docker has no scale-to-zero and no compute persistent volumes.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Selectable project identifiers: us-east, us-west, eu-central, ap-southeast. Region article states database/backend infrastructure created there with equal pricing.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: US location names conflict: dedicated region article says Ohio/Oregon; Launch v2 says Virginia/California. Frankfurt and Singapore agree.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Backups, object bodies, edge functions, container machines and model processing lack one verified component-specific placement/migration matrix.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Cloud Postgres supports pg_dump/pg_restore/psql via direct connection; storage export via S3 tooling or object downloads. Backend deletion also removes branches but not an externally deployed Site.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Termination: on request, limited-period Customer Data export then ordinary-course deletion, except law. No exact Customer Data export window or backend purge deadline given.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Personal-data deletion by email: acknowledge within 5 business days; complete within 30 days of verification, up to 90 for complex requests. Account contacts kept 60 days; User Content active copies 30 days, backups up to 90; legal exceptions.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Cloud paid active projects: full daily database backups, 7-day retention. Free 1 manual backup slot, paid 5; manual snapshots kept until deletion.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Restore replaces current database, makes project temporarily offline and loses later writes; file objects excluded. Self-host manual and configurable scheduled backups available.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Point-in-time recovery, Cloud backup-specific fees/storage accounting and a formal restore-time guarantee not found.

facts.label: File recovery and protection
facts.value: Gateway versioning and object lock unsupported; uploading the same key replaces current object. Database backups exclude uploaded files.

facts.label: File recovery and protection
facts.value: Cloud file undelete window, native file-backup schedule and storage replication/recovery guarantee not found.

facts.label: Identity and old names
facts.value: InsForge; official site insforge.dev; vendor InsForge, Inc. No former product name established.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: InsForge Cloud managed hosting plus a production self-hosting path on your own Linux/Docker infrastructure.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Public InsForge repository: Apache-2.0. Hosted service access is governed separately by InsForge's Terms.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Active public Free/Pro/Enterprise offers; self-service start links. Account provisioning was not tested.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: New Cloud projects from June 18, 2026 use Deno Deploy v2; older projects needed v2.2.2 and a function redeploy before July 20, 2026.

facts.label: Vendor home and main markets
facts.value: InsForge, Inc., a Delaware corporation; privacy policy says headquartered in the United States. Complete served-country list not established.

facts.value: Free help via Discord/docs; Pro announcement promises priority email and Discord; Enterprise card lists dedicated technical support.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Public status page exists. At check it listed operational Cloud regions and degraded Deno Edge Network/OpenRouter; website footer still said all systems operational.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Numerical uptime SLA, service-credit schedule and small-plan support-response guarantee not found.

facts.label: Primary type and other roles
facts.value: Our classification: hosted managed SQL database, with optional vector, geographic and time-series extensions. Separate overlap with Koyeb hosting and deployment.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Database Service includes a persistent PostgreSQL cluster, multiple logical databases, SQL roles and supported extensions; it is independent of application deployment lifecycle.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Koyeb also offers web/API services and Workers, billed as separate compute. App login, file/object storage and a durable job workflow are not established as bundled database entitlements.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Native PostgreSQL connection URL and compatible clients, including psql; standard PostgreSQL port 5432. Connection details are available through the Koyeb control panel.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Logical databases and roles can be managed through the control panel, CLI, API or SQL; app examples cover common PostgreSQL clients and ORMs.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Default database role owns the initial database; default names are koyeb-adm and koyebdb unless changed. New roles receive generated passwords but no existing object privileges by default; grant needed permissions explicitly.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: SQL role password reset affects new sessions; existing sessions continue. SQL-direct password changes cannot be synchronized back to the control panel/CLI/API; reset through Koyeb to restore consistent credentials.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: TLS/SSL is required for all Koyeb database connections in the official Wiki.js deployment guide.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Native PostgreSQL row-level security is available as an engine control: configure policies explicitly. Tables have no row policies by default; owners and BYPASSRLS roles normally bypass them.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Database private endpoints, database IP allowlists and the applicability of Koyeb's app service mesh were not established.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: Native PostgreSQL SQL service, described as 100% PostgreSQL-compatible; initial database is koyebdb, configurable role owner.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: Version list conflicts within the database page: creation and extension matrix include PostgreSQL 14, 15, 16 and 17; Limitations says only 14, 15 and 16.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: PostgreSQL 16 transactions group changes so the whole transaction commits or none does. Read Committed's default snapshot is per statement; Repeatable Read and Serializable are available and can require retries.

facts.label: Test environments and branches
facts.value: Separate logical databases and role owners can be created within a service. Koyeb describes CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE for local test copies and pg_dump/pg_restore for portable copies.

facts.label: Test environments and branches
facts.value: Managed copy-on-write branching, preview-environment database automation, branch quotas and branch-specific prices were not found.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Read replica provisioning, replica count/location, automatic failover mechanism, RPO/RTO and extra replica charges were not established.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Managed client live-query service, offline reads/writes and conflict handling were not found. Documented bidirectional synchronization concerns logical-database/role management metadata, not app records.

facts.value: PostGIS: 3.3.3 for PG14–16, 3.5.0 for PG17. TimescaleDB: 2.10.1 for PG14–15, 2.13.0 for PG16, 2.17.1 for PG17; only Apache-2 licensed features, no compression.

facts.value: Not applicable: S3 object compatibility.
