facts.value: Full signup-country restrictions and an exhaustive payment-method eligibility list were not found.

facts.label: Primary type and other roles
facts.value: Our classification: managed multi-engine database platform. Secondary roles: vectors/search, document/key-value/analytics/time-series/graph databases, local database tooling, and an included HTTP queue on Valkey.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Managed databases, query consoles, native/HTTP access, branches and backups according to engine/plan. Auth tooling scaffolds/manages schema and user rows; the application runs Better Auth or another login library itself.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Valkey includes VQueue webhook delivery without a separate queue subscription. PostgreSQL can run opt-in scheduled SQL; this is not general-purpose app function hosting.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: DuckDB 2 can use managed DuckLake on Pro/Dedicated; local tables, a PostgreSQL catalog and Parquet objects are distinct data components. No general app file-upload/bucket service established.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Standard engine clients connect with generated TLS connection strings. PostgreSQL/MySQL families offer pooled/direct paths; Redis/Valkey have Upstash-compatible REST, MySQL/MariaDB PlanetScale-compatible HTTP, and PostgreSQL a Neon-compatible HTTP driver.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Postgres HTTP supports non-interactive sql.transaction batches; interactive WebSocket Pool transactions are unsupported. mTLS enforcement refuses the Neon HTTP path; use a certificate-capable connection.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Weaviate's stable managed path is REST/GraphQL HTTPS. Its connection guide says v4 SDK gRPC defaults are not exposed, while product/tutorial pages describe gRPC rollout or show it.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: TLS 1.3 only on all plans. Databases run in isolated customer containers/private networks behind the TLS front door. No VPC peering or private link; public ingress credentials remain necessary.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: IP allowlisting is opt-in per database on all plans: empty list admits any source with valid credentials; adding entries restricts to IPv4/IPv6/CIDR entries. Data HTTP endpoints, including VQueue, also enforce it.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: PostgreSQL mTLS on Pro/Dedicated requires both client certificate and password. Per-database CA rotation invalidates issued certs; restoring a pre-rotation backup can restore old CA material, requiring another rotation.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Account/database-scoped API keys are hashed and revealed once. Database-key rotation permits old key for 24 hours, account rotation revokes immediately; revocation is immediate. Expiry can be 10 minutes to 30 days by API, otherwise never.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: PostgreSQL owner has superuser on its instance; create restricted SQL login roles for app access and sync them into the pooler after creation/password changes. Dashboard team members can connect to all team databases; owner controls destructive platform actions.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Staff read access requires a time-limited user grant, with justified break-glass access recorded/surfaced. Live volumes have no added application-level encryption or customer-managed keys; R2 backups are encrypted at rest.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: Nineteen hosted engines span SQL, documents, key/value, search, vectors, graph and time-series/analytics. Standard PostgreSQL uses its own SQL/wire protocol; DuckDB/SQLite can use a PostgreSQL wire facade without becoming PostgreSQL engines.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: New PostgreSQL databases track latest stable major with version pinning from the chooser. Docs explicitly discuss PostgreSQL 18.6 and opt-in PostgreSQL 19 beta 3 for scheduled jobs; this is not a complete current engine/version matrix.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: MongoDB-compatible choices are DocumentDB and FerretDB, not upstream MongoDB server. MongoDB, CockroachDB and SurrealDB are local/CLI-only, including on Dedicated.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: PostgreSQL 18 engine: transaction changes commit together or have no effect; Read Committed default uses a statement-start snapshot. Repeatable Read/Serializable are available and can require retries.

facts.label: Test environments and branches
facts.value: Branches are independent writable copies, with separate credentials and no ongoing replication. Standard storage makes full copies; enabling Branching uses copy-on-write. Seventeen engines branch; CouchDB and TigerBeetle are excluded.

facts.label: Test environments and branches
facts.value: Branch counting conflicts: Branching guide says branches count as databases; engine pages and Multi-tenancy say they do not consume plan database slots. PostgreSQL page advertises per-parent branch allowances Free 1, Solo 3, Pro 10.

facts.label: Test environments and branches
facts.value: Preview/Development-labelled branches hibernate after 20 idle minutes and cannot be pinned on shared infrastructure. GitHub integration currently maintains one staging branch; automatic per-feature-branch mode is not enabled yet.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: No standby/HA at any plan: Layerbase describes its databases as single-node with backups. Multi-region replication/failover is not offered; no numerical restore/failover objective is promised.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: CouchDB on Pro supports its native replication/offline workflows with a client such as PouchDB. Conflicting revisions are retained and the application must decide how to merge them; this is not a platform-wide managed offline-sync layer.

facts.label: Extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: PostgreSQL contrib includes pg_trgm, pgcrypto, uuid-ossp, hstore, citext, ltree, tablefunc, unaccent and postgres_fdw. pg_cron 1.6 is opt-in on supported builds; pgvector, pg_stat_statements and pg_net are not available.

facts.label: Extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Core PostGIS: PostgreSQL 18 has 3.6.4; PG19 beta has PostGIS 3.7.0rc2 preview. All plans can opt in. Raster/GDAL, topology, tiger geocoder, address_standardizer, SFCGAL and network-downloaded datum grids are excluded.

facts.label: Upload and file limits
facts.value: Not applicable: general app file multipart/resumable upload limits.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Not applicable: Layerbase does not establish its own S3-compatible app bucket API.

facts.label: Delivery and private files
facts.value: Not applicable: public/private file buckets, signed file delivery and CDN pricing.

facts.label: Filters and mixed search
facts.value: Qdrant offers vectors with payload filtering, hybrid search and recommendation APIs; Weaviate offers schema-driven vector/keyword hybrid search with REST/GraphQL. These are separate hosted engines; PostgreSQL pgvector is unavailable.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: VQueue is durable HTTP webhook coordination included with Valkey on every plan, using a subset of @upstash/qstash. It stores before acknowledging; receiver executes elsewhere. PostgreSQL pg_cron is separate in-database SQL scheduling.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: VQueue is at-least-once: 2xx succeeds, non-2xx including redirects fails, redirects not followed; backoff 4/16/64 seconds, capped 64 thereafter. Deduplication IDs last 24 hours; same ID changed content returns 409. Receiver still needs durable idempotency.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: VQueue state is server SQLite, separate from Valkey and its backups. Hibernation does not pause delivery; stopped DB/restricted account defers it. Password rotation changes publisher token and derived signing key without managed overlap.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: VQueue: delay/notBefore up to seven days, payload 64 KiB, headers 8 KiB, URL 8,192 chars; batches at most 100 messages and 8 MiB. Pending/dead-letter payloads do not expire; archives have no automatic deletion.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Queue capacity: 1,000 local payloads/account/server, 10,000/host; history 10,000 records/account, 100,000/host. Admission stops at caps/disk pressure. Delivered payloads can archive after 24 hours only after verified R2 readback.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: VQueue dashboard/API supports status/error inspection, explicit DLQ replay and export with base64 bodies; no cancel/pause control. pg_cron completed history retains at most seven days or 10,000 runs; displayed output truncates at 16,384 characters.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Local CLI requires Node.js 20+ and native engine binaries on macOS/Linux/Windows; no Docker or cloud account needed for local commands. User owns hardware, access controls, updates and off-machine backups.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: SpinDB commercial license price and a supported production resource minimum were not established. Commercial runtime use requires a paid license despite local Desktop's personal-use offer and ISC wrapper.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Current location guide: shared Free/Solo/Pro can choose us-east (Ashburn, Virginia) or eu-west (France) at creation, no extra region fee. Existing databases stay there; creating another database is needed to change region.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Security FAQ still says shared databases have no region choice and no EU hosting, contradicting Pricing, Lifecycle, Support and Data Residency's EU West choice.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Dedicated choices: US East Virginia, US West Oregon and São Paulo Brazil, dependent on size. US/Dedicated backups use global R2; EU West database backups use EU-jurisdiction R2. Managed DuckLake R2 is not region-pinned.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Every plan can export a fresh engine dump or download retained backups. Locked/archived/sleep-policy-paused databases remain exportable; offline export is limited to five per database per 24 hours. Finished exports last seven days, only the newest kept.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Normal database Destroy requires a final recoverable backup or is refused. Explicit transient TTL expiry skips that safeguard. Dedicated month-to-month cancel backs up then destroys the server immediately, without prorated refund.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Account deletion semantics conflict: dedicated deletion/security docs say default soft purge retains backups for support recovery, with optional explicit erasure. Terms/Privacy/residency still describe account deletion purging associated backups.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Deletion guide's explicit backup-erasure option removes all copies immediately; full verified erasure also removes related identifying records. Privacy retains operational logs about 30 days, billing records where required, a 90-day erasure record, and marketing suppression until opt-in.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Per-database backup cadence conflicts: Pricing/engine pages call it daily, while Backups and Security say every 12 hours on paid shared plans plus a final dump on sleep. No-change runs may be skipped.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Solo: three manual slots per database and seven-day scheduled retention. Pro: ten manual slots and 30-day scheduled retention. Dedicated: hourly default, configurable hourly/6h/12h/daily, 30-day rolling retention.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Backups in off-host R2 have checksums verified on restore. Ordinary dump restore overwrites the running database; take a fresh backup first. Volume snapshots are checked every six hours, snapshotting changes and at least weekly.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: PITR is opt-in and off by default on Pro and above for always-on PostgreSQL/FerretDB. It replays WAL into a new database and leaves source unchanged; restored database counts toward plan quota.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Exact numeric PITR lookback, archive-storage quota and a contractual end-to-end recovery objective were not found; PITR guide says a rolling window measured in days and shows it in the dashboard.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Backup scope matters: SQL dumps cover the platform-provisioned database, excluding user-created extra logical databases; Redis/Valkey snapshots cover all 16 logical DBs. DuckLake Parquet data is never copied by Layerbase backups.

facts.label: File recovery and protection
facts.value: Not applicable: general app file versioning/lock/recovery contract.

facts.label: Identity and old names
facts.value: Layerbase; managed product Layerbase Cloud, operated by Layerbase, LLC. Layerbase CLI was previously called SpinDB; that runtime history is not a former name for the entire cloud service.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Hosted shared Free/Solo/Pro and managed single-tenant Dedicated servers. The cloud platform is not open source. Local Desktop and CLI run engine processes on the user's hardware.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: CLI repository license: ISC. Underlying SpinDB runtime: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0, with any commercial use requiring a separate paid license, including internal for-profit business use.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Active public signup/pricing and documentation. Database-plan beta terms run June 2026 to July 2027; paid plan changes receive at least 60 days' notice, while Free features may change with an existing-database grace window.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: No shutdown, sunset or acquisition notice found in the inspected official pages. About states independent ownership, no outside investors, and founder-operated business.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: TigerBeetle cloud is Alpha; PostgreSQL 19 builds and PostGIS 3.7 release candidate are opt-in previews. Agent Servers are a separate beta product.

facts.label: Vendor home and main markets
facts.value: Layerbase, LLC, based in Austin, Texas, United States; company states it was formed July 15, 2025.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Signed-in support request page plus public bob@layerbase.com pre-sales contact; support@layerbase.com is also published. Terms give Free no support/availability obligation.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: No published uptime SLA document; Terms disclaim uptime, recovery time and durability guarantees unless separately agreed. Public dashboard status is available.

facts.value: Push API allowance scope conflict: price tables say the 30,000/day pool is shared with push; storage FAQ says push is free and does not consume the free pool.

facts.label: Inactivity, pause and deletion

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: Developer may incur metered extras without upgrading. Standard LeanEngine minimum listed size 1 CPU/512 MB: China RMB 2/day; international USD 1.6/day; its billing is independent of Developer/Business.

facts.label: Least paid commitment

facts.value: International Business: object API $0.04/1,000 requests, database $0.05/GB/day; China Business: RMB 1/10,000 requests, database RMB 0.10/GB/day. Developer 1 GB database free then same storage rate.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Failed object API requests still count except 429 throttling; saveAll/fetchAll count underlying objects, while a query returning multiple objects counts once.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Standard engine billed each day by chosen size and maximum instance count that day, deducted next day. LeanDB partial days count as full days, even unused.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: File billing can lag 3 days; most services charge after usage. Exact storage averaging, minimum billable bytes and request-block rounding not found.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: International LiveQuery: $1/1,000 subscriptions/day and $0.04/1,000 messages/day; China RMB4/1,000 subscriptions/day and RMB2/10,000 messages/day. Full-text: international $0.04/1,000 requests + $0.10/GB/day index; China RMB2.5/10,000 + RMB0.8/GB/day index.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: LeanCache 128 MB minimum: international USD0.4/day, China RMB1/day. China MySQL minimum 512 MB RAM RMB2.5/day; 20 GB disk included. No current international MySQL tariff established.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Trial engine sleeps after 30 minutes with no external request; request wakes it, documented 5–30 seconds; after 18 hours in 24, forced sleep returns 503. Standard instances stay running.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Allocated standard engine and LeanDB continue charging idle. To stop engine charges, remove/downgrade standard allocations; daily-peak final charge follows next day.

facts.label: Data transfer costs

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: Database/API-response transfer price, inter-region/backup transfer and complete CDN-origin exemptions not established.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: Developer API/day and 3-thread exhaustion returns 429; IM beyond 500 DAU blocks new logins. Files/SMS can keep accruing charges. Balance alerts by SMS/email; negative balance stops service.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: Engine autoscale min/max instance count configurable; no guaranteed overall dollar cap covering delayed files, minimums and all products found.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Business processing threads default 60, price table says up to 200; support can adjust. Query cap 1,000 records; multi-record response ≤6 MB, single-result response ≤16 MB; indexed-field length ≤1 KB.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Class-count conflict: console guide says 300 Classes/app; REST guide says 500 Classes/app and 300 fields/Class.

facts.value: File upload/read/list/retrieval billing and separate thumbnail-processing tariff not established.

facts.label: File request and retrieval prices
facts.value: China image moderation: RMB 0.26 per 100 checks, 100 checks free; outside Business minimum. JS guide limits thumbnail source images to 20 MB and says international thumbnails unsupported.

facts.label: Minimum storage and early deletion
facts.value: Minimum billed object size/capacity, minimum retained days, early-deletion fees and storage time-integration rules not found.

facts.label: Vector/index limits
facts.value: Not applicable to the documented LeanStorage/LeanDB offer: no native vector service/index specification established.

facts.label: Embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: No native embedding/reranking billing component established; any external model/provider would need separate research.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Cloud function response timeout 15 seconds; queue timeout default/max 15,000 ms. Generic engine ingress up to 100 MB/60 seconds; China shared-edge ingress may be 60 MB/10 seconds.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Before-hook timeout conflict: main function guide 10 seconds; Engine FAQ says 15 seconds. Both give after-hooks 3 seconds.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Queue executes 1 job at a time/app; 100 enqueue QPS, 10,000 enqueue/day, max 1,000 queued. Engine default app max 12 instances; paid size starts 1 CPU/512 MB; free is 0.5 CPU/256 MB.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Closed to new users and new apps. Historical Developer/Business/Enterprise marketing cannot establish current self-service eligibility.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Existing domestic data/engine apps require a custom domain; relevant domestic domains need filing/registration. Historical card requirement and complete country eligibility not established.

facts.label: Primary type and other roles
facts.value: Researcher classification: backend platform; JSON object database, accounts, files, container functions, live queries, messaging, queues and optional managed SQL/cache.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: LeanStorage object data/files, built-in user accounts, LiveQuery, LeanEngine functions/hooks, schedules/Cloud Queue, push, IM and game services. LeanDB MySQL/Redis are separately provisioned.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: User management is listed among free services, but calls/storage still have underlying meters; SMS and file services can bill even on Developer.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Object API uses HTTP JSON/REST v1.1 and SDKs, without JDBC/ODBC access to LeanStorage. Official docs cover Java/Android, Objective-C, Swift, JS, Python, PHP, .NET, Flutter and Go.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: LeanEngine supports Node.js, Python, Java, PHP, .NET, Go and C++ backends. LeanDB uses native MySQL/Redis clients inside engine; CLI proxy is for development/testing, not production.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Class, field and object ACL controls; session-based user/role rules. Public AppKey is constrained by permissions; MasterKey bypasses them and must stay server-side.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Collaborators can receive all or custom permissions. Engine Secret environment variables are hidden after save; changes require redeploy.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Web safe domains restrict browser origins with exceptions; cloud functions are outside that restriction. Domestic independent IP is an ingress isolation/availability feature, not proof of private networking.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: LeanStorage stores schema-free JSON-compatible objects in Classes, queried with LCQuery/REST constraints; no cross-Class SQL joins. MongoDB is referenced in implementation/backup docs, not exposed as a general Mongo wire endpoint.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: Optional LeanDB MySQL docs specify MySQL 5.6; LeanCache specifies Redis 6, using native clients from LeanEngine.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: LeanStorage has no complete transaction feature; one save on one object updates its fields atomically. Atomic increment, unique indexes and conditional updates available.

facts.label: Test environments and branches

facts.label: Replicas and failover

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: LeanStorage read-replica placement, reader endpoint, failover procedure and cross-region replication price not found.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: LiveQuery uses WebSockets to notify matching object changes after subscription; nested subqueries and selected-return-field projections unsupported in LiveQuery.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Durable offline writes, conflict reconciliation and complete missed-event replay not established.

facts.label: Upload and file limits
facts.value: SDK/CLI upload route documented; object REST API says it cannot upload bytes and creates a file entry from an existing URL. That URL remains externally hosted, not copied into LeanCloud.

facts.label: Execution model and languages

free.text: Free GPLv2 server; no provider quota or hosted idle rule; you run it

cells.metered: Community software $0; Enterprise pricing by quote
cells.regions: Choose the region for your own server

The software license stays $0. Kept host, data, backups and operations depend on your provider.

files.math: MariaDB Server does not provide file storage.

jobs.math: SQL events have no fee per run, but they use database resources that are not priced. No general worker is included.

facts.label: Free offer type
facts.value: Free offer is downloadable GPLv2 software without a time-limited hosted allowance. Enterprise subscriptions and any offered evaluations have separate terms; no cloud free-tier quota is assigned here.

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: Not applicable: no provider-granted monthly compute/read/write/storage/project/seat allowance for standalone Community Server.

facts.label: Inactivity, pause and deletion
facts.value: Self-hosted service lifecycle is operator-controlled. Starting/stopping is through OS/daemon tooling; database storage lives in the configured datadir. No hosted-account idle archival/deletion schedule applies to this software record.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: No Community software purchase is required. Smallest Enterprise subscription price, minimum purchased quantity and a public solo-developer checkout commitment were not established; current self-managed pricing says request a quote.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: Commercial default order term is one year unless specified otherwise, automatically renewing yearly with at least 60 days' non-renewal notice. Fees are non-cancelable/non-refundable; invoice currency applies and taxes are additional.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Community Server has no vendor per-query, per-vector, connection-hour or GB-storage software meter under its GPL. Infrastructure, backup destinations, electricity and administration are operator costs.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Commercial quantities can be Servers/Instances, Cores, vCPUs or Compute Units as ordered. An Instance is a daemon in a physical/virtual/container host; Compute Unit is at most four Cores/vCPUs and 16 GB RAM unless ordered otherwise. Excess subscribed usage is billable.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Not applicable as a vendor compute meter: stopping idle Community Server changes the operator's runtime, while hosting/storage charges follow its separately chosen infrastructure.

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: Not applicable as a Server tariff: internet egress, replica links and backup shipping use operator infrastructure; no vendor per-GB hosted transfer price belongs to this self-managed entry.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: Not applicable: provider budget alerts, automatic paid overages and a hosted dollar spend cap. Paid subscription excess quantities follow the commercial contract; host budget controls require a chosen provider.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: Operator can restrict accounts by queries/updates/connections per hour, simultaneous connections and statement time. New accounts start without privileges; granting access and choosing limits is explicit configuration.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: max_connections default 151, configurable 10 to 100,000; one additional reserved administrative connection. Real capacity also depends on file descriptors, thread/OS limits and memory.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: max_allowed_packet server default 16,777,216 bytes, documented as 16M; client default 1,073,741,824 bytes, documented as 1GB. Range 1,024 to 1,073,741,824 bytes. max_statement_time defaults to zero, meaning no configured limit for its covered statements.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: InnoDB: at most 1,017 columns and 64 secondary indexes/table; logical combined row-size limit 65,535 bytes with off-page BLOB/TEXT counted specially. Default 16KB pages permit a documented maximum 64TB tablespace; filesystem/storage still constrain deployment.

facts.label: File storage prices
facts.value: Not applicable: Server does not provide a general app object-storage price table.

facts.label: File request and retrieval prices
facts.value: Not applicable: object upload/read/list/retrieval request pricing.

facts.label: Minimum storage and early deletion
facts.value: Not applicable: object-class minimum size, retained days or early-delete billing.

facts.label: Vector/index limits
facts.value: VECTOR(N) supports at most 16,383 dimensions from 11.7.1; indexed vector must be NOT NULL and match dimensionality. Only one vector index per table, using cosine or Euclidean distance.

facts.label: Vector/index limits
facts.value: MHNSW index M range 3 to 200, default 6. Per-index cache ceiling defaults to 16,777,216 bytes, labelled 16 MB by docs, and is configurable with mhnsw_max_cache_size.

facts.label: Embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: Vector columns store precomputed float32 values generated by a model. Additional MCP/RAG/framework products can connect model generation/search, but the standalone Server license does not specify an included model/token/rerank allowance.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: No separate Community invocation/execution-second software fee. Each event execution uses a database connection and server resources; no per-job 0.5-vCPU/0.5-GB machine allotment or managed concurrency SKU applies.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Community package installation has no MariaDB account/card step or hosted trial requirement. GPLv2 permits running for commercial as well as personal work; distribution conditions still apply.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Commercial subscriptions are order-based and have export/sanctions restrictions. Current agreement lists Belarus, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Russia, Syria, Venezuela and listed Russian-occupied Ukrainian territories among restricted countries/areas.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Current Enterprise Server download is gated by an Enterprise subscription and login; Community package access is a different path.

facts.label: Primary type and other roles
facts.value: Our classification: self-hosted relational SQL database; optional native vectors, JSON/geographic features, SQL events and replication/clustering. Enterprise Platform bundles additional products.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Server includes SQL storage/querying, database users/roles, stored routines/triggers/events, native vector features on supported versions and replication capabilities. Application login/session handling, file delivery and general app compute are separate.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Enterprise Platform adds components such as MaxScale, enterprise backup/monitoring and tier-dependent clustering/RAG tools. The Cloud managed service is outside this Server record's hosting/cost scope.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Native MariaDB/MySQL-compatible client protocol; TCP port 3306 and local socket/pipe options. Official connector families include C, C++, Java/J, R2DBC, .NET, Node.js, ODBC and Python.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: MariaDB and MySQL diverge in SQL/features/replication behavior; existing MySQL clients often work, but current-version migration must follow compatibility notes rather than assume a universal drop-in replacement.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Users are name@host accounts with grants/roles. Newly created users have no privileges; use restricted application users. Many Linux packages bind to 127.0.0.1, but upstream defaults and packages differ; configure interface/firewall deliberately.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: MariaDB 10.4+ mariadb-install-db normally creates root@localhost with Unix-socket authentication and an initially invalid password alternative. OS-root access over the socket differs from an open passwordless remote root account.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Zero-configuration TLS is available from 11.4 and enabled/verified by default with compatible MariaDB server/client 11.4+ and supported authentication plugins. Other plugin/client paths need their own TLS/certificate setup.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Optional feedback uploads configuration/hardware/version/plugin usage, not database contents, according to Foundation policy. Commercial support uploads and usage metadata have separate contractual/privacy handling.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: Relational SQL engine with pluggable storage engines; InnoDB is the documented default. JSON, GIS and supported-version native vectors extend SQL rather than replace it with a document-only API.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: Vector edition/version split: Community introduction in 11.7, generally available from 11.8; Enterprise backport from 11.4.5-3, also in Enterprise 11.8.3-1 and later.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: InnoDB supports START TRANSACTION/COMMIT/ROLLBACK and consistent snapshots. Autocommit is on by default; many DDL/administrative statements implicitly commit. Nontransactional storage engines do not inherit InnoDB's rollback behavior.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: Default InnoDB isolation is REPEATABLE READ; READ UNCOMMITTED, READ COMMITTED and SERIALIZABLE can be selected. A replica or differently configured storage engine is not automatically the same read-consistency boundary.

facts.label: Test environments and branches
facts.value: Dev/test copies can use independent server processes with isolated data directories/ports/sockets, or restore a dump/backup into a separate test environment. No automatic hosted preview entitlement is included.

facts.label: Test environments and branches
facts.value: A native managed copy-on-write branch API, branch quotas, preview cleanup or branch-specific tariff was not established in the inspected Server/install/backup and self-managed pricing/legal pages.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Standard primary/replica replication is asynchronous; semisynchronous mode can wait for receipt acknowledgment from a replica. Operator configures/provisions replicas, monitoring and promotion.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Galera uses virtually synchronous write-set replication/certification across a primary component, with wsrep provider and cluster membership controls. Routing/load balancing and availability operations require separate configuration/resources.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: A bundled reactive app-client API, managed offline writes and app conflict-resolution SDK were not established. Server binary-log replication and SQL Event Scheduler are different features.

facts.label: Extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Specialized search includes native VECTOR INDEX on supported versions and SQL full-text search; official hybrid-search guide combines them with Reciprocal Rank Fusion. GIS features are also documented at Server level.

facts.label: Upload and file limits
facts.value: Not applicable: app multipart/resumable file-upload limits.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Not applicable: an S3-compatible app object API for MariaDB Server.

facts.label: Delivery and private files
facts.value: Not applicable: app public/private buckets, signed file delivery or CDN pricing.

facts.label: Filters and mixed search
facts.value: SQL filters can combine structured data with vectors; full-text plus vector results can be fused using SQL RRF. Indexed nearest-neighbor search needs matching distance and literal ascending distance ORDER BY plus LIMIT; wrapping it or threshold-only search can force scans.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: Event Scheduler executes SQL once or repeatedly inside MariaDB; stored procedures/events use SQL, not an arbitrary managed language worker. Scheduler defaults OFF and needs enabling; EVENT privilege is required to create events.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: A queue-style automatic retry/backoff policy, deduplication window, dead-letter store or exactly-once delivery contract was not found for Event Scheduler.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: CREATE EVENT supports AT timestamps or recurring EVERY intervals with STARTS/ENDS; no microsecond interval units. EVENTS metadata records the time zone, default SYSTEM. Docs state dates beyond 2038-01-19 are unsupported.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Expired events are dropped by default unless ON COMPLETION PRESERVE is chosen. Event definition lifetime is not retention of every result or a guarantee that missed schedules replay after downtime.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: INFORMATION_SCHEMA.EVENTS/SHOW EVENTS expose definitions, status, scheduling time zone and LAST_EXECUTED. A complete per-run audit/history, retained days and managed replay UI were not established.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Install native OS packages/binaries, manage configuration/datadir and OS service, apply supported updates, set users/TLS/firewall, and arrange monitoring, backup scheduling/offsite copies and restore tests.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Current Foundation policy: new Community LTS binaries for three years plus two further years of critical/security source releases; releases up to 11.4 have the older five-year binary period. Enterprise/extended maintenance follows its own subscription policy.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: A workload-independent safe production CPU/RAM/disk minimum for the six approved workloads was not established. Hardware guide says settings/workload matter and recommends representative benchmarking.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Not applicable: a MariaDB Server plan region catalog. Operator chooses server placement, datadir, replicas and backup destinations; no vendor residency guarantee is created by local installation.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Foundation website and commercial website/support data follow different privacy policies. Commercial policy permits international processing; Foundation feedback plugin is optional and inactive by default.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: mariadb-dump exports logical SQL; backup overview also describes CSV/XML output. Restoring elsewhere depends on SQL/engine/version compatibility. Logical dumps exclude configuration/log files, and routines/events need explicit options.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: DROP DATABASE removes its database/tables after privilege checks. Operator remains responsible for retained dumps, replicas, log files and storage erasure; no vendor self-hosted-data removal deadline applies.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Website/support personal-data deletion is handled through the relevant Foundation/company privacy process; company retains data as necessary for purpose/legal obligations without one universal day count.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Operator schedules and retains logical mariadb-dump backups or physical mariadb-backup backups. No bundled managed daily schedule, retained-day entitlement or offsite destination is supplied with Community Server.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Physical full backups must be prepared before restore; restoration requires a stopped server and empty destination datadir, with appropriate filesystem ownership. Incrementals depend on an appropriate full/base chain.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Binary-log PITR restores a full/incremental backup, finds its recorded log position and replays retained binary logs to the target time. Binary logging must be enabled and logs preserved.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: MariaDB 13.0 InnoDB log-archive PITR is a different path: no shipped backup tool currently generates/restores that archive format; mariadb-backup fails with innodb_log_archive=ON. Recovery has consistency/DDL limitations.

facts.label: File recovery and protection
facts.value: Not applicable: a hosted file-versioning, object-lock or file-delete recovery contract.

facts.label: Identity and old names
facts.value: MariaDB Server; Community Server is the open-source distribution. Enterprise Server and MariaDB Cloud are separate named offerings. Core daemon mariadbd was formerly named mysqld.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Community Server is GPLv2 open-source software, installed on the operator's machine. Running the program is not restricted by the GPL; redistribution/modification retain the license's conditions.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Enterprise Server itself is also GPLv2 under the current subscription agreement. Other Enterprise Platform components have their own licenses; the separate Software License Terms expressly preserve FOSS/BSL terms.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Active maintained project. Current release catalog lists 13.0.2 Stable, 13.1.1 RC and 13.2.0 Preview; supported LTS lines include 12.3, 11.8, 11.4 and 10.11.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Community Server 10.6 ended normal maintenance July 6, 2026. Published Community maintenance table gives 12.3 to June 12, 2029; 11.8 to June 4, 2028; 11.4 to May 29, 2029; 10.11 to February 16, 2028.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: K1 announced completion of its acquisition of MariaDB plc on September 10, 2024. The Foundation separately commits to Server continuity and GPLv2 independence from commercial entities; no whole-Server shutdown notice found.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: MariaDB plc announced a corporate brand change on November 4, 2026 alongside Enterprise Platform 2027; the MariaDB Server project remains active and separately maintained by the MariaDB Foundation.

facts.label: Vendor home and main markets
facts.value: MariaDB Foundation is a nonprofit incorporated in Delaware, USA. Commercial privacy policy identifies MariaDB plc, Ireland, and subsidiaries; the commercial website contact address is Redwood City, California, USA. MariaDB plc introduced a new brand identity on November 4, 2026; the Foundation and Server project remain separately identified.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Community help: official docs, Zulip and maria-discuss. Foundation does not provide commercial support. Current corporate paid support comparison excludes Community Server and directs users toward Enterprise coverage.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Enterprise support policy's S1 initial-response goals: Standard 30 minutes, Premium 15 minutes, 24×7 for critical production outages. S2 to S4 are 24×5; these are initial responses, not restoration deadlines or software uptime percentages.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: GPL Server is supplied without warranty; running one's own server does not come with a hosted availability SLA. Operator must monitor its own instance rather than use a vendor cloud status page as proof of its uptime.

cells.metered: Cloud from $20/mo; usage or provisioned resources
cells.regions: 9 clusters; Paris and Frankfurt EU, London UK

Meilisearch is a search engine, not a SQL database

files.math: Meilisearch does not provide general file storage.

jobs.math: Meilisearch indexes records; it does not run customer jobs

facts.label: Free offer type
facts.value: Cloud: time-limited 14-day trial, no credit card required; no permanent free Cloud tier was advertised on the current pricing page.

facts.label: Free offer type
facts.value: Self-hosted Community Edition: free software under MIT; hosting, storage, network and operator time are the user’s responsibility.

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: Cloud trial length is published as 14 days, but a trial document, search, storage or bandwidth allowance was not stated. The pricing estimator’s 100K document / 50K search example is a calculator example, not a stated free-trial quota.

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: Resource-based Cloud billing has no published documents/search count cap; capacity and performance are bounded by the provisioned CPU, RAM and storage.

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: The vendor says self-hosted Meilisearch can be deployed with no product usage limits. The engine still has documented technical limits and depends on the operator’s hardware/OS.

facts.label: Inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: Cloud’s 14-day trial expiry is stated, but an inactivity timeout, auto-pause, auto-delete interval, restore window or behavior after trial end was not stated on the pricing, first-project, terms, privacy or changelog pages checked.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: Cloud is advertised as starting at $20/month. Terms say prices are in dollars and exclude applicable taxes; the pricing page does not identify a region or ISO currency code for the starting figure.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: Enterprise: custom quote. Self-hosted Community software has no vendor subscription price; infrastructure cost is outside this product price.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Usage-based billing uses document and search consumption. Resource-based billing uses selected dedicated CPU/RAM plus auto-scaling storage. Cloud bills at team level and can mix the two models on one invoice.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Current pricing estimator shows a usage-based example of $30/month for 100K documents and 50K searches. It also shows an XS resource example: 0.5 vCPU, 1 GB RAM, $18/month instance plus a displayed $5/month disk line for 32 GiB billed (2.9 GiB calculated).

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: The October 2026 Cloud IP allowlist add-on costs $10/month per project and supports up to 100 IPv4/CIDR entries. Disabling the add-on leaves filtering in force until the billing cycle ends unless entries are removed.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Current per-unit prices for extra documents/searches, storage rates by region, model-provider charges and invoice rounding are not specified on the current pricing page. An older official comparison described Build-plan overages, but the current pricing page presents usage/resource billing rather than that named tier; I did not carry those older rates forward.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Resource-based Cloud allocates dedicated CPU/RAM and bills for provisioned resources; no scale-to-zero behavior is described. A quiet instance should not be assumed to stop its provisioned-resource charge.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Whether usage-based Cloud stops billing completely when idle, and whether a minimum monthly fee continues, was not found in pricing, Cloud docs, terms or changelog.

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: A current Meilisearch Cloud egress, bandwidth or cross-region transfer rate/free allowance was not found. The resource-pricing article explicitly described bandwidth billing as a planned future improvement; that does not establish a zero rate.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: Public documentation did not state a guaranteed spend cap, hard quota cutoff, overage action, budget alert threshold or bill-stop behavior. A 2025 resource-pricing post said alerts were planned; the current pricing page and current roadmap do not make that a bill-control promise.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Engine hard limit: one index can contain at most 4,294,967,296 documents. Cloud usage-based documents/searches are billed separately; this engine maximum is not a plan allowance.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Cloud dashboard file upload is limited to 20 MB. For larger datasets, docs direct users to the add-documents API or official importer. Engine HTTP payload default is 100,000,000 bytes (about 100 MB); self-host operators can change it. No separate Cloud API request ceiling was stated on this page.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Search defaults to a 20-hit limit and can return at most 1,000 results by default; index setting maxTotalHits can change the cap. Search query terms after the tenth are ignored.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Default concurrent search queue is 1,000 requests; new requests over the queue can be rejected with 503. The self-host configuration option can change the queue size.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: A primary-key value is limited to 511 bytes; each filterable attribute value is limited to 468 bytes; one index allows up to 65,536 attributes.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: A fixed Cloud project connection cap, maximum indexed bytes/documents for usage-based plans, and Cloud-specific API payload cap beyond the UI limit were not stated in pricing or docs.

facts.label: Storage prices
facts.value: Not applicable: Meilisearch indexes searchable records; it does not sell general-purpose file/object storage.

facts.label: File request and retrieval prices
facts.value: Not applicable: no file-object request/retrieval product is offered in the reviewed product/docs pages.

facts.label: Minimum storage and early deletion
facts.value: Not applicable: no hot/archive file storage classes or object retention fees are offered.

facts.label: Vector/index limits
facts.value: Meilisearch can store vectors in documents and supports multiple named embedders. Each embedder/model has a configured dimension count. General per-index document limit is 4,294,967,296.

facts.label: Vector/index limits
facts.value: A maximum vector dimension count, maximum vector count separate from document count, and vector-specific Cloud storage quota were not published in the vector/docs, pricing, terms or changelog pages checked.

facts.label: Embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: Embeddings can be produced by configured providers such as OpenAI, Hugging Face, Ollama or a compatible REST endpoint, or supplied by the customer. Meilisearch can send document templates to the provider and caches embeddings for unchanged documents.

facts.label: Embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: Exact per-model token/request rates and any current Meilisearch AI add-on rate were not found on the pricing page or in the provider/search docs. A model provider may bill separately; no zero-cost model claim is made.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Not applicable to user-code execution pricing: Cloud bills search/index usage or provisioned search resources, not customer function runtime, memory or invocations.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: A developer can create a Cloud account and project through public self-service signup. Cloud advertises a 14-day trial with no credit card required. No signup was submitted.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Country eligibility and a country-by-country availability list were not found in the public pricing, first-project docs or terms checked.

facts.label: Primary type and other roles
facts.value: Primary type: hosted and self-hosted search engine/search index. Secondary roles: full-text, faceted, geospatial, vector, semantic and hybrid search. It indexes JSON-like documents; it is not a general-purpose SQL database.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Cloud includes managed search/indexing, API keys, Cloud project management, automatic backups, engine upgrades, analytics/monitoring features and email support. Hybrid search is available in both Community Edition and Cloud; chat/conversational tools and other managed platform features vary by plan.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Meilisearch is a search service, not a full backend bundle. The reviewed feature list does not offer built-in app-user authentication, general file/object storage, or customer code/functions. Keep an application’s source database and authentication provider separate.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: HTTP REST API; official SDKs: JavaScript, Python, PHP, Ruby, Go, Rust, Java, .NET, Swift and Dart.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Official frontend connectors include InstantSearch.js and Autocomplete.js, with React and Vue guides. SDKs and REST use a project host URL and API key.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Official integration docs include MCP, Vercel AI SDK, LangChain and Firebase syncing; these are integrations, not extra bundled backend services.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Self-hosted production requires a master key of at least 16 bytes. API keys can be scoped by actions, index and expiry. In development mode without a master key, routes can be unprotected; production mode requires the key.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Cloud automatically creates a master key and default API keys for each project. Cloud project IP allowlisting is a paid $10/month add-on, limited to 100 IPv4/CIDR entries.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Tenant tokens can embed search filters and restrict search results for each app user. They do not restrict admin/indexing operations, and they do not replace the app’s own authentication system.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Cloud advertises SOC 2 Type II and a DPA; Paris/Frankfurt projects are described as storing documents, indexes and backups in the selected region. Meilisearch’s EU page says AES-256 at rest and TLS in transit.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: SSO SAML is listed for Enterprise. The current roadmap lists granular RBAC as under consideration; do not assume Cloud self-serve has dashboard RBAC.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: Search index of JSON documents, grouped into indexes with a primary key. Meilisearch uses the LMDB key-value store internally. It is not SQL-compatible and is not a replacement for the authoritative application database.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: REST document and search endpoints; search requests support full-text, filter, sort, facets and semantic/hybrid parameters.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: Document writes and many index/settings operations are asynchronous tasks. A request returns a task identifier/status; applications can poll or use task webhooks. This is not a documented multi-statement SQL transaction API.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: A completed task indicates the index update has finished. Applications should wait for success before relying on newly indexed content in search. No multi-index atomic commit or SQL isolation mode is documented.

facts.label: Test environments and branches
facts.value: A Cloud project is a container for indexes, tasks and billing. A developer can create separate projects for development and production; no copy-on-write branch feature was found in the project docs checked.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Sharding is the one current Enterprise Edition-exclusive engine feature, available by commercial license for production self-hosting and as a Cloud Enterprise capability. Do not count it as Community Edition or Cloud self-serve.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Cloud self-serve offers managed auto-scaling; the comparison lists multi-region deployment for Cloud, while Enterprise adds sharding and replication. Exact failover RTO/RPO and topology are not promised by the reviewed pages.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Meilisearch can send a webhook to a configured URL when asynchronous tasks finish. This signals indexing-task completion; it is not a database changefeed with record-level live subscriptions.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Persistent offline writes, bidirectional data sync, conflict-resolution rules and a Cloud changefeed were not described in the product docs checked.

facts.label: Extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Native full-text search, typo tolerance, facets/filters, geo search, vector storage and hybrid search are supported.

facts.label: Upload and file limits
facts.value: Not applicable: no customer file storage/upload service. The Cloud dashboard’s dataset-upload size is an indexing input limit recorded under D03.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Not applicable: no object-storage API is offered.

facts.label: Delivery and private files
facts.value: Not applicable: no bucket, CDN, signed file URL or file-delivery product is offered. Search access controls are recorded under C18.

facts.label: Filters and mixed search
facts.value: Hybrid retrieval combines full-text keyword matching and semantic vector search. The semanticRatio setting ranges from 0 (full-text) to 1 (semantic), with values between them blending both. Search filters can also be used.

facts.label: Filters and mixed search
facts.value: Tenant tokens embed filters to restrict each user’s search results within a shared index. Tokens apply to search only, not indexing/admin endpoints.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: Not applicable as a customer job runner: Meilisearch indexes and searches records; it does not host the application’s arbitrary user code or workers.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Internal indexing operations are queued tasks with enqueued, processing, succeeded, failed or canceled states; failures can include an error object. A task-completion webhook is available for self-hosted instances.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: A customer-facing retry policy, exactly-once/deduplication guarantee, ordering guarantee or replay window for external jobs is not documented because the product does not provide a general job queue.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Not applicable: no user-controlled recurring/delayed job scheduler or message-retention service is offered. Internal indexing tasks are not a general-purpose customer queue.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Internal task database has a documented 20 GiB maximum. After it grows above roughly 1 million entries, Meilisearch tries to remove finished task records; 20 GiB is described as roughly 10–30 million tasks depending on setup. This is task history, not application log retention.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Cloud log-retention duration and export/replay retention for customer application logs were not found in pricing, docs, terms or changelog.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: For self-hosted Community Edition, the operator supplies a machine/container, persistent data volume, network access, production master key, HTTPS/reverse proxy, restart policy, backups and version upgrades. Official docs provide Docker and production deployment paths.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: A universal supported minimum CPU/RAM/disk size for production was not published in the deployment and performance docs checked. Requirements depend on index shape and workload; no cheap-server estimate is invented.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Compared with Cloud, Community self-hosting leaves upgrades, backups, scaling and monitoring to the operator and does not include Cloud UI/analytics or Enterprise-only sharding.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Cloud projects are created in a selected region. The official Cloud status page currently lists NYC, LON, SFO, FRA, SGP, JPN, SAO, PAR and SYD clusters. The roadmap marks Paris, São Paulo and Sydney as launched in Q2 2026.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: For projects in Paris (PAR) or Frankfurt (FRA), Meilisearch says documents, indexes and backups stay in the selected EU region. London (LON) is offered for UK data residency. This is a vendor statement, not a legal-compliance conclusion.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Backup placement guarantees for non-EU clusters were not found. Region selection and backup placement were checked in the EU residency page, roadmap, status page, pricing, terms, privacy and changelog.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Cloud project snapshots can be exported and restored on a self-hosted instance. The vendor says the same REST API/SDK integration can move between Cloud and self-hosted.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Cloud automatic backups are included for self-serve and Enterprise. Backup frequency and retention were not stated on the feature comparison page. Point-in-time restoration is under consideration and described as available on-demand for Enterprise.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Self-hosted operators can create snapshots for recovery and dumps for migration/version changes. They must store and retain these backups themselves.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Cloud content remains the customer’s property. The terms allow Meilisearch to continue hosting/processing it after termination when needed for reversibility, legal obligations or liability defense.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: The exact time to purge indexed content, backups and account data after project cancellation/deletion was not stated in the terms or product docs checked. The privacy policy’s personal-data retention periods are not a Cloud index/backups deletion schedule.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Cloud feature comparison says automatic backups are included in Cloud self-serve and Enterprise. Public pages checked did not specify schedule, retention duration, restore SLA or backup storage charge.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Self-hosted snapshot backups support periodic recovery; dumps are used for migration/version changes. The operator chooses schedule and storage location.

facts.label: File recovery and protection
facts.value: Not applicable: no object versioning, file retention or object-lock product. Search-engine snapshots are covered under D05.

facts.label: Identity and former names
facts.value: Meilisearch; developed by Meili SAS, a French company. Official URL is https://www.meilisearch.com/. No former product name was stated on the current product, docs, or legal pages checked.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Meilisearch Cloud is managed SaaS; self-hosted Meilisearch is available. Cloud runs the same engine family and handles infrastructure, upgrades and automatic backups.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Self-hosted Community Edition is free and MIT licensed. It includes core full-text and AI-powered search; the operator runs infrastructure, upgrades, backups and monitoring.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Self-hosted Enterprise Edition code is under BUSL-1.1. The license allows testing, development and evaluation; production use of those files requires a commercial license. The Change License is MIT after four years for each licensed version. The current docs identify sharding as the only EE-exclusive engine feature.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Cloud is not a free self-hosted MIT deployment: it is supplied under Meilisearch Cloud’s SaaS terms. Its platform features include managed backups and Cloud UI; Enterprise adds custom support/governance features.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Active; GitHub’s latest release page resolves to Meilisearch v1.56.1. The official docs changelog lists v1.56 on October 26, 2026.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: The October 2026 Company news / Release post says v1.55 and v1.56 are live on Cloud and describes a newly shipped Cloud IP allowlist add-on.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: No acquisition, shutdown, sunset or product-retirement notice was found in the official blog listing, Company news posts, roadmap or current product/legal pages checked.

facts.label: Vendor home and main markets
facts.value: The legal entity is Meili SAS, incorporated under French law and registered in Paris, France. Cloud markets itself internationally; the selectable regions are recorded under C17.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Cloud pricing lists email support. Self-host Community users are directed to GitHub/Discord. Enterprise advertises dedicated Slack support; its SLA lists 1-hour response for urgent issues, 24 hours for normal issues and 1 business day for low-priority requests.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: SLA availability is conflicting across official sources: the marketing comparison lists Cloud self-serve at 99.9% and Enterprise up to 99.999%; the formal SLA says it applies to Enterprise customers and guarantees 99.9%, while pricing says “up to 99.999%” for Enterprise.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Public Cloud status and incident page are available. The status page showed all listed services operational when checked.

apps.name: MemCachier
apps.line: Managed Memcached-compatible cache for sessions, counters, and query results.

free.text: 25MB; 10 connections; disabled after 30 idle days; data retention unclear

cells.metered: Basic from about $14/mo; Heroku 1 GB cap is $70/mo
cells.regions: AWS and DigitalOcean clusters; availability unclear
