The $70 cap for a full billing cycle continues while the cache is provisioned, even with zero traffic. Whether 1 GB of data fits is not verified.

files.math: MemCachier is a cache, not durable file storage.

jobs.math: MemCachier does not run background jobs

facts.label: free offer type
facts.value: Lasting free Developer offer: $0, 25 MB and basic analytics, marketed as free forever. It is a development cache, subject to inactivity disabling rather than a published time-limited credit trial.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: Developer includes 25 MB cache capacity, one proxy server and 10 connections. Paid Basic lists unlimited connections; the free limit is not ten app users or ten projects.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: A free read/write/request allowance, fixed QPS entitlement, cache/account count ceiling and explicit per-item metadata overhead were not published in inspected free-plan material.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: Development caches are disabled after 30 days of inactivity. Authentication then fails; the cache can be re-enabled from dashboard Settings, and an enable-cache API operation is documented.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: Whether disabled caches retain every stored value, a maximum disabled retention period, and a numeric automatic deletion deadline were not found.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: Moving from the development plan to a production plan loses the cache because the clusters are strongly separated. Other upgrades/downgrades are documented as not resetting the cache; plan changes require no client-code changes.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: Direct-site entry: Basic starts at approximately $14/month for the 100 MB/250 MB/500 MB family. The headline does not identify the exact provider/region, ISO dollar currency or each size's exact price.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: Direct Advanced starts at approximately $58/month for the 1/2.5/5/7.5 GB family; Business starts approximately $440/month for 10/25/50/75/100 GB. Enterprise is a custom quote.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: Official Heroku sales-channel listing: 100 MB maximum $15/month, 250 MB $25/month, 500 MB $40/month and 1 GB $70/month; Developer is free. Listed hourly equivalents are approximate.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Direct plans are charged by the hour; Terms describe monthly credit-card collection and taxes excluded. Exact hourly fractions, partial-hour rounding, direct-site dollar ISO code and a full capacity/provider/region tariff were not established.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Heroku add-ons accrue charges while provisioned, regardless of traffic, and platform billing prorates add-ons to the second based on creation/destruction time.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: The published plan model is allocated cache capacity/features rather than separate listed per-get/per-set meters. A complete fee schedule for request/connection/bandwidth extras, custom support and refunds was not found.

facts.label: idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Heroku paid MemCachier add-ons continue accruing while provisioned with zero traffic. Free development disabling after 30 days is an access rule, not a published paid-plan compute scale-to-zero feature.

facts.label: idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: A paid automatic scale-to-zero or durable pause/resume mode with stopped capacity charges was not found.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: No explicit network ingress/egress, cross-region or internet transfer price/allowance was found for native MemCachier plans.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: Cache/app colocation is recommended; optional TLS can access a cache from outside its datacenter. Exact outside-datacenter network reachability, pricing and required configuration were not fully established.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: Plan changes are explicit upgrades/downgrades. Memory hit rate/usage alerts are available from Basic 100 MB+, delivered by email or Slack; they monitor cache performance/capacity, not invoice totals.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: Automatic plan upgrades, bill-budget thresholds, a guaranteed hard financial cap and the full behavior at memory/connection limits were not specified in inspected billing/limits pages.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Maximum key-plus-value object size is 1 MB, including the key. A set, append or prepend that grows the pair must stay within this combined limit.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Direct plan capacities: Developer 25 MB; Basic 100/250/500 MB; Advanced 1/2.5/5/7.5 GB; Business 10/25/50/75/100 GB; Enterprise larger by quote.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Developer: 10 connections and one proxy. Basic: unlimited advertised connections and one proxy; Advanced: two to three proxies; Business: four to six. No fixed CPU, QPS or per-client request-rate guarantee was found.

facts.label: storage prices
facts.value: Not applicable to a native database-independent file/object-storage service.

facts.label: file request and retrieval prices
facts.value: Not applicable to a native database-independent file/object-storage service.

facts.label: minimum storage and early deletion
facts.value: Not applicable to a native database-independent file/object-storage service.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: Not applicable to the documented native cache service; external vector search/inference would need its own provider.

facts.label: embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: Not applicable to the documented native cache service; external vector search/inference would need its own provider.

facts.label: run limits and pricing
facts.value: No native managed-worker machine, invocation price, job timeout/concurrency or billed waiting/retry model applies to this cache service. Any external worker costs are outside its capacity plan.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Direct public account form asks for email and password and advertises a free account; no form was submitted. Paid resources are charged to a credit card under the Terms, while add-on channels have their own platform billing.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: A guaranteed no-card condition for completing a free-cache setup, a full signup-country list and explicit production/commercial eligibility for Developer were not found.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Terms require users to be over 13 and not barred by applicable US/resident-country laws; AUP restricts abuse and unauthorized resale. Splitting multiple apps to act as one and avoid fees is prohibited.

facts.label: primary type and other roles
facts.value: Researcher classification: hosted key-value cache, compatible with Memcached protocols. Secondary uses include database/query/result caching, sessions and counters; it is not an authoritative durable database.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: Native scope: managed in-memory cache, proxy endpoints, authentication/credential controls, cache analytics and optional alerts/introspection by plan. It manages no application worker processes in the documented cache interface.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: Bundled app-user authentication/MAU, file buckets, general functions and managed workflow execution were not found.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Supports Memcache binary and ASCII protocols; all service connections require authentication. Binary SASL is the documented preferred path; ASCII uses MemCachier's extension that sends a set command containing username/password before normal commands.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Documented tested clients include Node.js memjs, Python pylibmc/python-binary-memcached, Ruby Dalli, PHP php-memcached and Java Xmemcached/spymemcached. The integration guide identifies Go mc as maintained by MemCachier.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Client-support docs disagree for Rust: the native matrix marks memcached-rs unsupported, while the vendor's Heroku guide recommends it with SASL support from version 0.4.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Analytics API V2 exposes cache metadata, credentials, stats, alerts and introspection through authenticated HTTP requests. Only credentials with API capability can use it; cache data operations normally use Memcache.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Every cache requires its own username/password; clients must authenticate. Multiple credentials support rotation, with primary credentials integrated into platform configuration.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Basic adds credential management; Advanced adds access controls. Credentials can be restricted to read-only or denied flush/API capabilities. The API specifically says development caches cannot manage credentials.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Optional TLS/SSL connections are documented, including a Heroku stunnel buildpack with CA verification. Native documentation generally assumes same-datacenter plain connections; TLS is not described as mandatory.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Enterprise advertises SAML sign-on, a dedicated cluster in a separate VPC and multi-AZ setups. These are not included in the free Developer plan.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Cache data is kept in memory, not written to disk. Customers can encrypt values in their application. The provider's account/configuration metadata is a separate retained data category.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: MemCachier implements an in-memory key/value Memcache service, protocol-compliant with Memcached but built on its own engine. It is not Redis, SQL or a managed version of the upstream Memcached binary.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: A current engine build/version, supported protocol-opcode/version matrix and a fixed maintenance/release support window were not found.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Vendor-contributed Advanced Memcache guide documents thread-safe increments/decrements, append/prepend and compare-and-swap using version-checked writes. CAS protects a single item's conditional update.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: A multi-key ACID transaction contract, consistency model across failover/proxies, and zero acknowledged-write-loss guarantee were not established.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Local development uses an independently run Memcached process; default examples install it without SASL, so arbitrary credentials can be ignored locally. Hosted development and production clusters are separate.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Native copy-on-write cache branches, isolated preview deployments and snapshot-clone retention/prices were not found.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Production plans advertise high-availability clusters/proxies. Vendor explanations say contents are spread over servers and a server failure can lose part of the cache; client/app code must tolerate misses.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: The official Heroku listing says all production caches are replicated and describes automatic switching after node failure. Exact replication factor, zone placement on non-Enterprise plans and resulting data-loss bounds remain unclear.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Application cache freshness is managed using key expiration, deletion/invalidation and flush operations. An expiration of zero disables TTL expiry, but it does not prevent eviction, failure loss or deprovisioning.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: A native Pub/Sub/changefeed service, managed browser offline writes/reconciliation and conflict-resolution policy were not found.

facts.label: extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Native secondary indexes, geo/full-text indexes or a customer-loadable extension/module catalogue were not found.

facts.label: delivery and private files
facts.value: Not applicable to a native database-independent file/object-storage service.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: Conditional bytes-as-values use: the combined key and value must fit the 1 MB object limit. MemCachier recommends a disk cache/database instead for larger values; this is not a multipart/resumable upload service.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: The exposed application protocol is Memcache binary/ASCII with authentication, not an S3 object API. No backup object API is offered by the cache-only/no-backup design.

facts.label: filters and mixed search
facts.value: Not applicable to the documented native cache service; external vector search/inference would need its own provider.

facts.label: execution model and languages
facts.value: The managed service stores cached values and serves Memcache commands; it does not execute general application workers. Native client languages include the supported Memcache library environments, not hosted job-runtime languages.

facts.label: delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Native job-delivery retries, deduplication, dead-letter storage and replay contracts are not applicable to the documented cache-only interface.

facts.label: schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Native delayed/recurring job scheduling and queue-retention limits are not applicable. Key TTL controls cached-item expiry; it does not schedule work or guarantee a queued job survives.

facts.label: logs and run history
facts.value: Relevant cache diagnostics: Advanced 1 GB+ introspection includes recently hot/missed/mutated keys and the last 100 requests per server; all plans include cache metrics, with historical analytics on paid plans.

facts.label: logs and run history
facts.value: Exact historical-metric retention days, full cache-log export retention and worker-history/replay integration details were not found in accessible native docs; linked CacheSight documentation failed to open.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Not applicable to a self-hosted MemCachier server edition. Local testing uses the separate upstream Memcached project; the hosted implementation and control plane are not supplied as a self-host package here.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Security policy names AWS and DigitalOcean as cache infrastructure providers and says customers choose the cache datacenter. Heroku-provisioned caches are hosted on AWS.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Live status components include AWS ap-northeast-1, ap-southeast-1, eu-central-1, eu-west-1, us-east-1 and us-west-2; DigitalOcean ams3, blr1, fra1, lon1, nyc1, nyc3, sfo2, sgp1 and tor1.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Official Heroku listing shows Common Runtime United States/Europe and installability in several Private Spaces, including Dublin, Frankfurt, London, Mumbai, Oregon, Singapore, Tokyo and Virginia.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Provider lists differ: Subprocessors still names Azure and Rackspace, while the newer Security policy names AWS/DigitalOcean and the live status page shows those latter providers. Current new-cache availability for Azure/Rackspace and a complete region matrix remain unresolved.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: After deprovisioning, MemCachier blocks access and removes cached data from memory over the next several days, after which it is unrecoverable.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Published DPA §9 allows a written return/delete request within 30 days of term end, with completion within 90 days after receipt and legal-retention exceptions. Privacy separately retains account information as reasonably needed, including legal/accounting purposes.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: No native complete cache-export/snapshot download procedure or migration-preserved format was established. Terms put voluntary export on the customer and promise only reasonable efforts for access after termination with cause.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: MemCachier explicitly does not back up customer caches: contents stay in memory and must be treated as disposable. No cache RDB/AOF/PITR recovery service is promised.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Provider configuration and cache metadata are backed up every minute to redundant infrastructure; these backups are not the application cache contents.

facts.label: file recovery and protection
facts.value: Not applicable to a native database-independent file/object-storage service.

facts.label: identity and old names
facts.value: MemCachier, operated by MemCachier, Inc.; official URL https://www.memcachier.com/. It is sold directly and through hosted-platform add-ons, including its linked official Heroku listing.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: Managed proprietary service under MemCachier Terms; its engine is a custom implementation, explicitly not based on the Memcached server. No self-hosted MemCachier server edition/license was found.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Public pricing and signup remain available; its status page displayed live clusters and no status messages in the previous week when checked. This establishes public service signals, not an authenticated service test.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Blog and company press/about check found no acquisition or whole-service shutdown/sunset notice. The blog index's newest visible post is dated 2023-09-08; the official Heroku integration guide is marked updated 2025-08-06.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Historical feature retirement: the vendor says its New Relic plugin is no longer available because New Relic retired the plugin offering. The current marketplace description/status still contains old New Relic references.

facts.label: vendor home and main markets
facts.value: Operator is a US company, MemCachier, Inc. Terms/About identify San Francisco; Privacy gives a New York contact address. A single current headquarters address was not established.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: Basic includes best-effort support; Business advertises 24/7 support and Enterprise a dedicated account manager. Developer includes 24/7 monitoring, which is not the same as 24/7 human support.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: Public status URL is https://status.memcachier.com/. Native docs point users to the support portal and Contact page; a vendor blog also supplies support@memcachier.com.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: The official support portal could not be read: HTTPS fetch reset the connection and the web fetch also reported it inaccessible. Contact and public docs remain readable alternatives.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: The linked CacheSight detailed analytics documentation timed out and was inaccessible through web fetch, including its docs index. Native analytics/API docs and vendor blog provided partial official copies.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: A numeric uptime SLA, service-credit formula, response-time guarantee and complete paid support surcharge were not found.

apps.name: Milvus
apps.line: Open-source vector database for similarity search and metadata filtering.

free.text: Apache-2.0; no hosted quota or idle rule; host compute and storage yourself

cells.metered: Community software $0; hosting and storage are separate
cells.regions: Choose your own hosting region

sql.math: The Community license is $0. Host size, object storage, backups, transfer and embedding rates depend on the provider you choose.
The license is $0. Kept host, storage, backups and provider minimums decide the idle cost.

files.math: Milvus does not provide file storage for users.

jobs.math: Milvus does not run customer code or background jobs

facts.label: Free offer type
facts.value: Milvus is free, open-source software under Apache 2.0, rather than a hosted trial or credit offer.

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: Not applicable to a hosted free-plan allowance: this record covers self-hosted software with no free-plan account or hosted quota. Engine and Lite technical limits are recorded under D03 and V01.

facts.label: Inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: Not applicable to vendor-managed inactivity or deletion: the operator runs Milvus and controls when the process and underlying storage are stopped or removed.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: Self-hosted Milvus has no vendor software subscription commitment; the Apache-licensed code is free to use. Hosting, object storage, backups, monitoring, and model inference are separately selected by the operator.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Not applicable to Milvus software billing: self-hosted code does not meter documents, searches, stored data, or runtime for a vendor invoice. The operator’s infrastructure and model-provider bills are separate.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Not applicable to product-level hosted compute billing. A self-hosted server consumes the machine and dependent services while the operator leaves them running; Milvus does not manage the host’s scale-to-zero billing.

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: Not applicable to a Milvus vendor egress tariff for the self-hosted edition. Network transfer is charged, if at all, by the operator’s compute, network, and object-storage providers.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: Not applicable to product-level spend caps or overages because the self-hosted software does not issue a metered service bill. Infrastructure alerts or budget stops are configured with the operator’s providers.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Current 3.0.x limits page: up to 65,536 collections per instance; 1,024 partitions, 16 shards, and 64 fields per collection; entity count is listed as unlimited.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Current 3.0.x limits page: maximum vector dimension 32,768; VARCHAR 65,535 bytes; resource names 255 characters; insert, search, and query payload 64 MB per RPC.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Current 3.0.x limits page: topK and number of query vectors per search (nq) are each capped at 16,384. Loaded data must use less than 90% of total QueryNode memory to leave engine headroom.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: A version-current hard maximum for active client connections and a per-entity byte ceiling were not found in current 3.0.x limits, connection, system-configuration, or release pages checked.

facts.label: Storage prices
facts.value: Not applicable: Milvus does not sell general-purpose user file/object storage. Its internal object-store dependency holds database persistence and index files.

facts.label: File request and retrieval prices
facts.value: Not applicable: there is no user file-upload or object retrieval API priced by Milvus.

facts.label: Minimum storage and early deletion
facts.value: Not applicable: Milvus has no user-facing hot/archive file tiers or file-retention charge.

facts.label: Vector/index limits
facts.value: The current engine supports dense FLOAT32, FLOAT16, BFLOAT16, INT8 and binary vector fields, plus SPARSE_FLOAT_VECTOR. Sparse vectors do not declare a fixed dimension in the schema.

facts.label: Vector/index limits
facts.value: The 3.0.x limits page sets a maximum dense-vector dimension of 32,768 and lists no maximum entity count. Per-instance capacity still depends on memory, object storage, index choice, and replicas.

facts.label: Vector/index limits
facts.value: Milvus Lite 3.2.2 is a local subset: it supports dense and sparse vectors and listed CPU indexes, but no distributed scaling or server production controls. Authentication, RBAC, and TLS are not supported.

facts.label: Embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: Milvus can call configured embedding providers from a collection Function, including OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Bedrock, Vertex AI, Voyage AI, Cohere, and Hugging Face options. The operator supplies credentials and model settings.

facts.label: Embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: The embedding provider bills its own model use. Milvus documentation does not specify the providers’ current token prices or a single Milvus-owned embedding/reranking rate.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Not applicable to function execution rates: Milvus does not meter customer invocation, CPU-second, memory, or worker runtime.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Download and local use are public through the repository and package instructions; the self-hosted software does not require a vendor account or signup form.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: The Apache 2.0 license permits commercial use subject to its notice and license conditions. Country or account eligibility rules for the self-hosted code are not a product signup gate.

facts.label: Primary type and other roles
facts.value: Primary type: self-hosted vector database and similarity-search engine. It stores embeddings with structured fields and returns matching entities; it is not a general SQL database.

facts.label: Primary type and other roles
facts.value: Other roles include dense and sparse vector search, metadata filtering, keyword/full-text search, hybrid retrieval, and external-table retrieval in the 3.0 line.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Milvus provides vector persistence, indexing, filtering, similarity search, insert/upsert/delete, and text/hybrid retrieval. It does not provide a complete application backend around those features.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Milvus authentication and role controls protect database access, but Milvus does not replace an app’s end-user identity provider or session system.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Persistent server deployments require metadata, write-ahead-log, and object-storage components; the Docker Compose setup supplies local containers for these dependencies. Milvus Lite uses local storage instead.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Milvus Functions can generate embeddings or BM25 sparse vectors as part of indexing/search workflows, but they do not host arbitrary application code. Text-embedding Functions call configured inference providers.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Milvus exposes gRPC and REST APIs. The default local server address in the connection guide is localhost:19530.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Current overview lists official Python, Go, Java, Node.js, and C++ clients; C# is community-contributed, and Rust is under development.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Milvus Lite is a Python-local path. The server client path can be used from supported SDKs where the application can reach the configured endpoint; no browser-native database protocol is claimed.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: A comprehensive guarantee that each client SDK works in every browser, edge runtime, or serverless runtime was not found in the SDK and connection documentation checked.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Authentication is off by default in self-hosted Milvus. When enabled, the initial root user is root with password Milvus; the docs say to change credentials and create limited users.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: RBAC grants privileges at instance, database, and collection scope through users and roles.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Milvus supports one-way TLS and mutual TLS for client connections, and optional internal TLS between components. The operator configures certificates and network boundaries.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Milvus Lite does not support authentication, users, RBAC, or TLS; its guide warns against exposing it to an untrusted network.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: For shared collections, a trusted application must apply tenant filters; the product docs do not describe row-level RBAC on individual entities.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: Milvus is a vector database organized into databases, collections, entities, and typed fields. A collection resembles a table, but its API and query model focus on vector and scalar search rather than SQL.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: A schema includes one primary field, one or more vector/scalar fields, and optional dynamic JSON fields; primary keys may be INT64 or VARCHAR.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: Search/query supports Strong, Bounded Staleness, Session, and Eventually consistency; Bounded Staleness is the documented default.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: The consistency docs describe read visibility, not multi-statement ACID transactions. I did not find a public multi-operation transaction/rollback contract in the consistency, collection, upsert, REST API overview, or product FAQ pages checked.

facts.label: Test environments and branches
facts.value: Milvus supports named databases within an instance, which can separate collections and access grants.

facts.label: Test environments and branches
facts.value: Separate local Lite files or separate server deployments can be used for development and production. A hosted-style branch that clones a deployment with copy-on-write semantics was not found in the local development, snapshot, or deployment docs checked.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Distributed deployments can scale components separately; in-memory replicas can improve search availability and query performance.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Milvus CDC can replicate changes between self-hosted clusters for a primary/standby arrangement. It requires separate deployment and operator-controlled traffic switchover/failover.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: A universal RTO/RPO, cross-region recovery guarantee, or managed automatic failover promise was not found in the self-host deployment, replica, CDC, or release documentation checked.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Milvus CDC can stream supported database mutations between Milvus instances in sequence, including inserts, deletes, and upserts.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Durable offline client writes, bidirectional sync, conflict resolution, and a client subscription API were not found in the client, CDC, or change-data documentation checked.

facts.label: Extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Milvus supports HNSW, IVF, DiskANN, SCANN, FLAT, sparse inverted indexes, binary indexes, and GPU indexes, with supported search behavior depending on the chosen index.

facts.label: Extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Additional search modes include BM25 full-text, geometry fields, scalar filtering, range/grouping, and hybrid dense/sparse or multi-vector retrieval.

facts.label: Upload and file limits
facts.value: Not applicable: no end-user file upload service. BulkWriter/import handles database rows and data files as ingestion, not hosted file objects.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Not applicable as an object-store API product: Milvus does not expose an S3-compatible user bucket. It can use configured object storage internally.

facts.label: Delivery and private files
facts.value: Not applicable: there are no user file buckets, signed file URLs, CDN, or custom file domains.

facts.label: Filters and mixed search
facts.value: Milvus supports filtered vector search, dense/sparse hybrid search, and rank fusion; filtering can use scalar and JSON fields.

facts.label: Filters and mixed search
facts.value: Multi-tenancy options include database, collection, partition, and partition-key patterns. RBAC is scoped to instance/database/collection, so shared-collection tenant filtering must be enforced by trusted application code.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: Not applicable as a user-code job runner: Milvus stores and retrieves vectors and does not host application workers or arbitrary user functions.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Not applicable as a customer queue: Milvus has internal indexing and import operations, but no general-purpose app job or message delivery service.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Not applicable: Milvus has no user-controlled task scheduler or delayed-job retention service.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Not applicable to hosted customer job history or log retention. Self-hosted operators can collect metrics/logs in their own monitoring stack; no vendor retention term applies.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Current deployment requirements recommend at least 4 CPU cores and 16 GB RAM for Standalone; Cluster recommends 8 or more cores and 128 GB RAM. RAM “requirement” entries are 8 GB Standalone and 32 GB Cluster; vector/index size affects actual need.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Hardware needs at least one documented SIMD set (SSE4.2, AVX, AVX2, or AVX-512); the guide recommends SSD storage and Linux/Kubernetes for cluster deployment.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Standalone and Distributed server deployments use a metadata store, object storage, and WAL/message-queue layer. The current Docker Compose install starts Milvus with etcd and MinIO and uses embedded Woodpecker.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Milvus Lite runs within the application’s local Python environment and storage directory; the current guide requires Python 3.10+ and compatible dependency wheels. Concurrent writes to one Lite database directory are not supported safely, and only one process may own that directory.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Self-hosting means the operator handles upgrades, backups, TLS, authentication defaults, monitoring, scaling, storage-provider credentials, and recovery testing.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Self-hosted deployment has no vendor region selector; the operator chooses the compute location and the location of the configured metadata, WAL, and object-storage services.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Milvus supports object-storage backends including MinIO, S3-compatible stores, Azure Blob Storage, Google Cloud Storage, Aliyun OSS, and Tencent COS; compatibility can differ by WAL mode and provider semantics.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Milvus BulkWriter supports local JSON and Parquet preparation; Bulk Insert imports prepared files from configured object storage. CLI commands support export and import operations.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Milvus Lite has a dump command that exports a collection into BulkWriter JSON files. The Lite 3.x exporter cannot directly open an original Lite 2.x database directory; export using its old version first.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Milvus 3.0 collection snapshots can be restored only into a new collection in the same cluster. A snapshot references existing data and is not a complete independent disaster-recovery backup.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Current Milvus Backup documentation in the repository supports restoring 3.0 backups to 3.0 and 2.2–2.6 backups to 3.0; it says the latest tool supports backups from 2.2 onward and restore targets 2.5 onward. The older Milvus docs compatibility table stops at 2.6.x.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Data deletion is operator controlled. Milvus TTL hides expired entities from results and physically reclaims them after compaction; current docs say this is typically within 24 hours, not immediate erasure at the TTL instant.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Milvus 3.0 snapshots provide point-in-time collection views. They are immutable, may share underlying segment data, and restore as a new collection on the same cluster; retained snapshots can prevent storage reclamation.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: The Milvus Backup utility offers CLI/API backup and restore. Its current repository guide documents backups from Milvus 2.2 onward and restores to 2.5 onward, including 3.0; Milvus 3.0.1+ uses snapshots by default.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: No automatic backup frequency, retention schedule, or recovery-time objective is provided with the self-hosted software; the operator must schedule and verify backups.

facts.label: File recovery and protection
facts.value: Not applicable: there is no user-file versioning or object-lock product. Collection snapshots and backups cover database data instead.

facts.label: Identity and former names
facts.value: Milvus is the open-source vector database at milvus.io, maintained as a project under the LF AI & Data Foundation.

facts.label: Identity and former names
facts.value: I did not find a former product name on the current project overview, release notes, or repository checked.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Self-hosted software is available as Milvus Lite (local Python library), Standalone (one service instance), and Distributed (clustered components). These share the Milvus client API, but Lite lacks some server capabilities.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: The Milvus repository and project documentation identify Apache License 2.0. Commercial use, modification, and redistribution are allowed under that license’s conditions.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Related service note: Zilliz Cloud is a separately billed managed Milvus offering; this record covers the self-hosted software.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Active. GitHub’s latest release URL resolves to Milvus v3.0.5, dated October 30, 2026; the official release notes also list v3.0.5.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: The repository also has a maintained 2.6.x line; the release page showed v2.6.26, dated October 26, 2026. Milvus 3.0 reached general availability with v3.0.1 after the v3.0.0 release.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Milvus Lite is separately versioned in the current local guide: its example uses Lite 3.2.2 with PyMilvus 3.0.2. The package number is not treated as the Milvus server’s latest release.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: No acquisition, shutdown, sunset, or project-retirement notice was found in the official project blog, maintainer company blog, GitHub releases, roadmap, or current project pages checked.

facts.label: Vendor home and main markets
facts.value: Milvus is an LF AI & Data Foundation open-source project. The current project material checked did not name a vendor legal entity or its home country for the self-hosted software.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Public support paths include the project GitHub, Slack, Discord, and Milvus Office Hours.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: A contractual uptime SLA or vendor-operated incident status page for self-hosted Milvus was not found in the project documentation, project repository, or community pages checked.

facts.label: free offer type
facts.value: Core Free is an ongoing no-cost database allowance, not a credit trial. Flex is hourly paid usage; Dedicated paid capacity is separate. Free backup preview and trigger daily free usage are separate allowances.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: Core Free: one cluster/project by default; 0.5 GB total uncompressed BSON plus normal indexes in docs (pricing labels it 512 MB); shared RAM/vCPU; three-node replica set.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: Core Free: 100 operations/sec, 500 connections, 100 databases and 500 collections total; 32 MB in-memory sort and 50-stage aggregation limit.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: Core Free: 10 GB in and 10 GB out per rolling 7-day period; overage throttles rather than charging outgoing transfer. No private endpoint/peering, customer-managed encryption key or database-log download.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: Triggers share a project-level daily free tier: 50,000 requests, 25 compute hours and 0.5 GB external data transfer; thresholds are measured independently and reset daily.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: Free automatically pauses after 30 days with zero connections; email warning 7 days before pause. Manual resume is required and may fail if the paused engine is too old to restore to a current version.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: Flex cannot be paused and does not automatically pause when idle. Eligible non-NVMe M10+ clusters can pause for up to 30 days, then automatically resume; after resuming they must run at least 60 minutes before another pause.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: A universal hard deletion/retention deadline for indefinitely inactive Free clusters was not found.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: Core Flex base: USD $0.0110/hour, nominal $8/month, with a cluster charge cap of USD $30/month. Tariff is presented for supported AWS/Azure/GCP Flex regions without separate regional rates.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: Core Dedicated headline starts at USD $0.08/hour and $56.94/month; Infinite preview headline starts at USD $0.09/hour. Cloud/provider region for these headline rates is not specified on the price card.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: Exact current Core/Infinite M10 compute quote for AWS us-east-1 could not be obtained from the read-only calculator view.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Flex hourly tiers in USD: 0–100 ops/sec $0.0110; 100–200 $0.0205; 200–300 $0.0288; 300–400 $0.0356; 400–500 $0.0411. Includes 5 GB storage and unlimited uncharged cluster data transfer.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Dedicated Core meters cluster configuration, storage, backups, data transfer and selected add-ons. Increasing disk can bill the full configured storage size, not just bytes above the original default; extra regions/nodes change price.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Infinite preview separately meters provisioned compute per two-node HA shard plus extra nodes, uncompressed logical GB-hours, extended backup GB-hours and network transfer. Idle provisioned compute remains billable; default 24-hour continuous backup is included.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Direct Atlas examples use USD; taxes are additional under Cloud Terms. Exact sub-hour compute rounding and a named AWS us-east-1 storage/compute tariff for the full Dedicated example were not established.

facts.label: idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Flex keeps its base hourly charge while idle. Dedicated/Infinite running allocations remain billable; eligible paused clusters are charged for storage and automatically resume after 30 days.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: Core Free and Flex have no outgoing cluster data-transfer charge in supported regions; inbound transfers are uncharged. Free retains 10 GB in/out rolling-week throttles; Flex has an unlimited transfer inclusion.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: Dedicated AWS regional ranges, USD/GB: same region $0.00–$0.01, different region $0.02–$0.15, internet $0.09–$0.16. The table does not assign a unique internet unit price to us-east-1.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: Dedicated AWS us-east-1 PrivateLink Atlas fee: USD $0.0450 per endpoint-hour plus $0.0120 per Atlas Private Endpoint Capacity Unit; AWS bills its own interface-endpoint costs separately.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: Cloud snapshot export flat service fee: USD $0.125/GB exported to S3, Azure Blob or GCS, plus cloud transfer. The export fee is not region differentiated on the page; provider network charges remain route-specific.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: Free/Flex enforce hard storage and operational limits, with cooldown/queuing above operation thresholds; Flex maximum is 500 ops/sec and 5 GB. Flex cluster pricing cap does not cap trigger, model, support or other service bills.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: Billing alerts notify on project/organization daily or current spend thresholds. Dedicated autoscaling can increase resource charges; alert documentation does not establish a hard total-bill cutoff.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: All database documents have the 16 MiB BSON size limit. Core Free/Flex restrict BSON nesting to 50 levels, aggregation to 50 stages, prohibit disk spill and limit sort memory to 32 MB.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Core Flex: 5 GB uncompressed data/normal indexes, 500 connections, 100 databases/500 collections total and max 500 read/write operations/sec; no storage autoscaling or sharding.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Core M10 service-limit example: 1,500 connections per node, with 10 reserved by Atlas; Core normally has three replica-set nodes. Limits vary by tier/class/provider and connection route.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Infinite preview supports up to 128 TB logical storage and 5,000 active collections/indexes per replica set; general M10–M60 and selected M40–M60 Low-CPU tiers. Max storage can be capped, blocking writes but continuing reads.

facts.label: storage prices
facts.value: GridFS uses database collections/storage, not a separately priced object-storage bucket. Flex 5 GB and Free storage caps include stored file chunks and associated normal indexes; Dedicated depends on configured storage.

facts.label: file request and retrieval prices
facts.value: No independent per-upload/download/list/retrieval GridFS tariff was found; chunks generate database work and network traffic under the chosen cluster model.

facts.label: minimum storage and early deletion
facts.value: Not applicable: standalone object-storage classes, per-object minimum retained days and archive early-deletion rules.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: Core Vector Search supports up to 8,192 dimensions, ANN/HNSW and exact nearest-neighbor search; supports cosine, Euclidean and dot product, float32/BinData and documented quantization options.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: Free: max 3 combined Search/Vector Search indexes; Flex: max 10. Dedicated capacity depends on tier/workload. Search indexes update asynchronously; normal BSON/cluster quotas remain separate.

facts.label: embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: Optional Automated Embedding/Voyage AI is token-priced separately from database/search resources. Billing example: voyage-4 USD $0.06 per million tokens; default unscoped inference may use any cloud/geography, not the cluster region.

facts.label: embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: Automated Embedding provides a one-time 200 million-token allocation per model at organization level, shared across projects; tokens do not refresh. US/Europe-scoped inference costs 1.1× the model price.

facts.label: run limits and pricing
facts.value: Functions: 300-second runtime cap, 350 MB memory cap, 1,000 async operations, 25 net sockets and 18 MB incoming arguments. Trigger default concurrency is 10,000; higher unordered M10+ limits require configuration/support.

facts.label: run limits and pricing
facts.value: Triggers USD overage rates: requests $2/1M for first 25M daily, $1/1M for next tier to 250M, $0.75/1M beyond; external transfer $0.12/GB. Source rates are global service rates without separate cloud/region rows.

facts.label: run limits and pricing
facts.value: Compute rate presentation is inconsistent: Trigger Billing quotes $10/500 runtime hours and approximately $0.000000005/ms, but those values are not exactly equal. Memory multiplier increases per 32 MB.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Public Free signup path, no card required for the free database. Paid backup preview requires a payment method. Cloud Terms allow service use under the agreement and place responsibility for credentials/data protection on the customer.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: An exhaustive list of eligible customer countries and a Free-specific commercial-production entitlement were not found.

facts.label: primary type and other roles
facts.value: Primary: managed BSON document database. Secondary: aggregation, full-text/vector search, change streams, GridFS files and surviving database/scheduled triggers. These directory labels are our classification.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: Atlas Core includes database access, indexes, change streams and GridFS through MongoDB drivers; database/scheduled triggers run Functions. Optional Search Nodes, Stream Processing, inference, federation and support can add separate charges.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: Flex trigger support conflicts: Flex billing advertises 'triggers'; current Database Triggers and Triggers Limitations explicitly say database triggers cannot be defined on Flex.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Native MongoDB wire protocol and mongodb+srv connection strings through official language drivers, mongosh and Compass. Database credentials and IP/network access must be configured; retired Data API/GraphQL URLs are not current connection options.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Official driver catalog includes C/C++, C#/.NET, Go, Java, JavaScript/Node.js, Kotlin, PHP, Python, Ruby, Rust and Scala; runtime/version compatibility is driver-specific.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Database users differ from Atlas console users. Configure database roles, collection/database scope and optional custom roles; restrict client IPs through project network access lists.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Free/Flex lack private endpoints, network peering, customer-managed encryption keys and database auditing. Dedicated supports private network access; private connectivity and advanced security may add fees.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: Core runs native MongoDB BSON/document queries and aggregation. Free currently runs MongoDB 8.0; Flex at least 8.0, with upgrades controlled by Atlas. Dedicated has selectable supported release policies; Infinite preview runs latest 9.x.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: MongoDB single-document updates are atomic; multi-document ACID transactions span collections/databases on replica sets and sharded clusters, with guarantees determined by read/write concerns.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Search/vector indexes are eventually consistent with underlying collection changes. A committed database write may not be immediately searchable.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Independent Atlas projects/clusters and copy/restore support isolated testing. No native copy-on-write database-branch plan allowance was established.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Core replica sets provide automated primary failover and secondaries; Free replication factor is fixed at three. Dedicated adds optional multiregion/multicloud, read-only and analytics nodes at extra configured cost.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Infinite uses a two-node HA compute pair with storage-managed failover rather than the Core three-node replication architecture; optional extra read-only nodes are separately metered.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Native MongoDB change streams support live change notifications and resume tokens; successful resume depends on the required history remaining in the oplog. Device Sync/offline app-user synchronization was retired.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Flex change-stream support is inconsistent across docs: Flex limits describe change-stream filters and trigger limits list 10 streams, while Database Triggers says Flex does not support change streams.

facts.label: extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Core provides normal document indexes, aggregation and MongoDB Search/Vector Search. Colocated search is available on Free/Flex within index caps; dedicated Search Nodes require M10+. Infinite preview excludes Search/Vector Search.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: GridFS stores files exceeding 16 MiB by splitting into default 255 KiB chunks and a metadata document. It supports retrieving ranges without loading the whole file at once.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Not applicable: a native S3-compatible GridFS API. Files are accessed with MongoDB driver GridFS APIs; backup export to S3/Blob/GCS is a separate feature.

facts.label: delivery and private files
facts.value: GridFS follows database authentication and role permissions. Retired Static Hosting/HTTPS endpoints must not be presented as a current native signed-file URL, custom-domain/CDN service.

facts.label: filters and mixed search
facts.value: Core supports typed vector pre-filters and native keyword/vector hybrid search. $rankFusion combines ranks; $scoreFusion combines scores, with version requirements and serial sub-pipelines documented.

facts.label: execution model and languages
facts.value: Surviving Atlas database/scheduled triggers execute JavaScript Functions on a separate serverless compute layer, or forward events to AWS EventBridge. Functions in triggers use system context; general SDK-callable App Services functions are retired.

facts.label: delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Trigger event processing is at least once; duplicates can occur after failures. Ordered triggers serialize, unordered triggers run in parallel. Lost oplog history can suspend a trigger; auto-resume skips missed events.

facts.label: delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: A universal retry schedule, maximum retry duration, dead-letter queue and arbitrary failed-job replay contract were not found.

facts.label: schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Scheduled triggers use five-field cron evaluated in UTC, with minute granularity and optional skip-on-re-enable behavior. They pass no arguments to their linked function.

facts.label: logs and run history
facts.value: Trigger/Function logs retain 10 days; query pages return up to 100 entries. Console lines truncate to 512 bytes and only 25 lines per entry are saved. Forwarding/download can preserve logs externally.

facts.label: logs and run history
facts.value: Free/Flex cannot download database logs; trigger logs are a separate facility. Infinite preview also excludes database-log download/sync. External log storage or forwarding can add resource and egress charges.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Not applicable to self-hosting the Atlas cloud platform. Atlas Core/Infinite are managed editions; local MongoDB development and self-managed Enterprise/Community software are separate deployment/license choices.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Core supports AWS, Azure and Google Cloud, with tier-specific region matrices. AWS us-east-1 is Northern Virginia / US_EAST_1 and supports Free, Flex, M10+ and Infinite preview in the matrix.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Core Dedicated can distribute electable/read-only/analytics/search nodes across regions/providers. Infinite preview is AWS-only and single-region, with a different two-node HA-shard architecture.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Free/Flex snapshot locations can differ from deployment locations: Hong Kong backs up to Australia; many other nonlisted locations back up to Ireland; USA deployments back up in USA.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Default automated embedding inference can run in any cloud/geography; optional US or Europe scope costs 1.1× model rate. External log export routes through the Atlas control plane in AWS us-east-1; DPA governs processing and subprocessors.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Export/migrate using mongodump/mongorestore with BSON dumps; tier-specific unsupported options apply. Core Free/Flex exclude user/role dumps, oplog replay and UUID-preserving restore options described in their limits.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Termination can delete cluster data, search indexes and snapshots, subject to configured retained-backup/compliance options. Cloud Terms provide no obligation to retain a terminated cluster/snapshots; export first.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: DPA promises deletion of customer personal data upon termination/request unless law requires retention; an exact universal database/account physical-erasure deadline was not found.

facts.label: backups and restore

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Core Flex automatically takes one daily snapshot from a secondary beginning 24 hours after creation; retains last 8. No custom policy, on-demand snapshots, PITR or sharded restore; snapshots can download/restore.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Core Dedicated Cloud Backup uses provider snapshots and configurable retention/schedules; Continuous Cloud Backup adds point-in-time recovery. Backups, restore networking and export can be separate charges.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: AWS us-east-1 backup example: public calculator metadata lists snapshot backup price USD $0.14/GB-month, consistent with the AWS range in configuration docs. Dedicated backup charges appear as GB-days.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Infinite preview includes 24 hours of continuous backup; longer retained history is charged independently in backup GB-hours. Retention can extend up to 3 years within preview constraints.

facts.label: file recovery and protection
facts.value: GridFS does not provide atomic whole-file replacement or multi-document transaction support; applications can keep file versions and atomically update a metadata pointer. Database backup/retention applies to stored collections.

facts.label: free limits

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: Hosted inactivity pause, project expiry and provider deletion windows are not applicable. The operator controls process startup/shutdown and retains its own database/backup files.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: Hosted paid minimum, seat commitment, trial conversion and regional subscription taxes are not applicable to Community Edition software.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Vendor hourly capacity, request, failed-operation and overage billing meters are not applicable to the self-managed server distribution.

facts.label: idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Managed scale-to-zero billing, automatic wake and idle price rules are not applicable. Stopping your server does not establish whether a separately rented disk or machine stops charging.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: MongoDB Community software has no hosted ingress/egress/inter-region tariff to apply. The operator's network and storage providers determine any transfer cost.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: Hosted overage handling, monetary spend caps and account billing alerts are not applicable. Resource/query limits protect a server; they do not cap an external provider's bill.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: General server limits include 16 MiB maximum BSON document size, at most 100 nesting levels, 64 normal indexes per collection and 32 fields per compound index.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Connections are controlled by net.maxIncomingConnections and OS limits. Current Linux default is (RLIMIT_NOFILE / 2) × 0.8; Windows lists 1,000,000. This is a connection ceiling, not a supported user count or query-throughput guarantee.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: MongoDB 9.0 defaults to 10,000 concurrently open multi-document transactions for external clients. Per-operation memory defaults to the larger of 1 GB or 20% of process-available memory; exceeding it can fail the operation.

facts.label: storage prices
facts.value: Hosted per-GB-month hot/archive storage tariffs are not applicable. GridFS stores file chunks and metadata inside operator-provided database storage.

facts.label: file request and retrieval prices
facts.value: Vendor upload/read/list/retrieval request prices and request-block rounding are not applicable to self-hosted GridFS. A file operation may involve several database chunk operations.

facts.label: minimum storage and early deletion
facts.value: Hosted storage-class minimum retained days, early-delete fees and minimum billed object size are not applicable.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: Self-managed mongot uses the MongoDB Search/Vector Search engine and index semantics, including HNSW/flat options, cosine/dot-product/Euclidean similarity and quantization. The vector field limit is 8,192 dimensions.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: Self-managed search storage and memory are operator-sized; index size need not match BSON collection size. Sizing guide recommends room for rebuilding, generally double index disk space, and reports read-only mode at 90% disk use.

facts.label: embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: Self-managed Automated Embedding is preview, requires mongot 1.70.1+ and Server 8.3+, and sends text to Voyage AI using configured API keys. Direct Voyage or MongoDB-proxy billing paths exist; paid inference is separate from free database software.

facts.label: embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: For production, embedding docs call for separate index-time/query-time keys and outbound endpoint access. Changing model/dimensions/path can force re-embedding and incur model charges; embeddings are stored in a separate internal database.

facts.label: run limits and pricing
facts.value: Hosted per-invocation/runtime prices, worker memory/CPU plans and retry/wait billing are not applicable. Any application worker needs separately provisioned compute and its own limits.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Public installation packages and source are available without creating a hosted database subscription. No hosted signup/card/trial requirement applies to running the software itself.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Vendor FAQ says ordinary applications, including SaaS using MongoDB as their database, do not trigger section 13 merely by doing so. Offering MongoDB functionality itself as a public service invokes section 13's service-source obligations; internal-only use is distinguished.

facts.label: primary type and other roles
facts.value: Primary: self-hosted BSON document database. Secondary: aggregation, replication/sharding, change streams, GridFS files and optional self-managed full-text/vector search. These directory roles are our classification.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: Includes document CRUD/aggregation, indexes, database users/roles, native replica sets/sharding, change streams and driver-based GridFS. Optional mongot adds Search/Vector Search.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: Community lacks Enterprise's auditing, Kerberos and in-memory storage engine. Native encrypted storage engine is Enterprise-only; managed automation/backups and a paid support contract are separate products.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: MongoDB wire-protocol clients use mongodb:// or DNS-seeded mongodb+srv:// connection strings. Official tools include mongosh and Compass; configure authentication, network binding and TLS for remote access.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Official library catalog lists C, C++, C#, Go, Java, Kotlin, Node.js, PHP, Python, Ruby, Rust, Scala and TypeScript. Compatibility varies by driver/server/runtime version; community libraries are separately labelled.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Access control is disabled by default in the server; enable authorization explicitly. RBAC grants resource/action privileges and built-in/custom roles; permissions are additive across a user's roles.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Community supports SCRAM and X.509 authentication. Bind defaults to localhost; production guidance calls for trusted-network/firewall controls and TLS on client and inter-node links.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Native WiredTiger encryption-at-rest engine and auditing are Enterprise features. Community operators can use filesystem/block-device encryption and must protect data/key/config files themselves.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: Native MongoDB BSON document engine with MongoDB Query Language and aggregation. WiredTiger provides persistent storage; this record uses current 9.0 documentation and the 9.0.4 download.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: You choose when to install self-managed releases and patches. Binary upgrade and feature compatibility version (FCV) are separate steps. From 9.0, self-managed receives major releases and annual x.5 Feature Updates, rather than every intervening minor.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Single-document operations are atomic. Multi-document ACID transactions cover collections/databases and sharded deployments, with configured read/write concern; standalone deployments do not support multi-document transactions.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Majority read concern normally returns durable majority-acknowledged data; transactional majority guarantees require commit with majority write concern. A node's latest value is not necessarily the system's latest value.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: mongot maintains a separate search index through change streams. Search indexes are eventually consistent with collection writes, rather than part of the atomic database transaction commit.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Separate local/remote instances and dump/restore support isolated development and test data. The atlas-local evaluation image can bundle mongod/mongot, but is single-node and not a production deployment target.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: A native copy-on-write database-branch allowance or automatic branch-merge feature was not established.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Native replica sets elect a new primary after failure when a voting majority is available. Writes pause during election; configured secondary reads may continue. The operator provides all machines, placement and monitoring.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Production guidance uses three-member replica sets and separate machines with redundant power/network paths. Replicas each consume storage/resources; placing processes on one machine does not provide the documented failure isolation.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Native change streams watch a collection, database or deployment on replica sets/sharded clusters, with WiredTiger. Resume depends on available change/oplog history; clients must handle disconnects and resume failures.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: A bundled mobile offline-write queue and application conflict-resolution contract were not found for Community Server.

facts.label: extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Normal MongoDB includes text indexes/$text and 2d/2dsphere geospatial indexes. Rich Search/Vector Search uses separately deployed mongot and its own storage, resources, credentials and upgrade cycle.

facts.label: extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Current mongot Community production paths are Linux tarball/container or Kubernetes Operator. Linux instructions require Community 8.3+ and an initiated replica set with keyfile access control; Kubernetes minimums include Server 8.3.4+, mongot 1.70.1+ and Operator 1.9.1+.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: GridFS bypasses the 16 MiB single-document limit with default 255 KiB chunks and a separate metadata collection. It supports range access without loading an entire file into memory.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: A native S3 object-service compatibility matrix is not applicable. GridFS is accessed through MongoDB driver APIs or mongofiles, rather than a native S3 bucket endpoint.

facts.label: delivery and private files
facts.value: Database access controls protect GridFS collections; an application supplies browser-facing download/upload authorization and HTTP delivery. Native CDN domains and signed object URLs are not established by the GridFS API.

facts.label: filters and mixed search
facts.value: Community supports full-text/vector hybrid search through mongot. Index filters and search pipeline composition are available; current hybrid guide documents rankFusion on 8.0+ and scoreFusion on 8.3+, subject to deployed server/search compatibility.

facts.label: execution model and languages
facts.value: A managed function/job-worker service and selectable execution languages are not applicable to Community Server. Database query expressions and change streams are not a general hosted job runtime.

facts.label: delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Managed job retry, exactly-once delivery, dead-letter handling and failed-job replay contracts are not applicable to this database distribution.

facts.label: schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Hosted cron/delayed-job scheduling and queue payload/retention allowances are not applicable.

facts.label: logs and run history
facts.value: Managed job run-history/replay retention is not applicable. Database logs can be written/rotated by the operator; mongot logs and metrics also need operator forwarding and retention.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Install and secure mongod, maintain persistent storage, patch versions/OS, configure replica topology and backups, monitor capacity and test recovery. mongot adds a separate process/storage/configuration and its own restart/patch responsibilities.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: 64-bit supported platforms are required. Current production notes require AVX on supported x86_64 CPUs and ARMv8.2-A or later on ARM64. Server supports selected Linux, Windows and macOS versions; mongot production binaries target Linux x86_64/aarch64.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: WiredTiger's default internal cache is max(50% × (RAM − 1 GB), 0.256 GB), with additional memory needed outside the cache and for filesystem caching. Container memory constraints and search index resources must be sized separately.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: You control database/log/backup placement and recovery. Search tarball installation does not install a systemd service; arrange process supervision. For mongot, configure TLS/authentication, monitoring and storage encryption at the host layer.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Vendor region catalogue and managed residency guarantee are not applicable. You place database servers, replica members, backups and optional search storage on your own infrastructure.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: mongodump exports BSON data plus metadata/options and index definitions; mongorestore imports dumps. Tools document same major-version or feature-compatibility-version restore scope. mongoexport produces JSON/CSV, not a full backup.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: db.dropDatabase removes the current database and associated data files, but does not delete its database users. Backups, copied exports and separate search files remain operator responsibilities.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Hosted account-erasure deadlines and vendor-managed backup purge periods are not applicable. Website privacy terms govern personal-data handling in vendor interactions, not an operator's database-retention schedule.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Operators can use mongodump/mongorestore for small deployments or filesystem snapshots/data-file copies. A live filesystem snapshot requires journaling with journal and data on the same logical volume; plain file copies require stopping writes.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: mongodump includes collection metadata/options and index definitions; --oplog can include writes during the dump under its documented conditions. A full continuous PITR service and automatic retention schedule are not included with these tools.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Backup frequency, retained copies, off-site storage and restore tests are operator choices. mongot indexes can rebuild from restored mongod data; keep index configuration and operational configuration needed to reconstruct the deployment.

facts.label: file recovery and protection
facts.value: GridFS does not support multi-document transactions or atomic replacement of an entire file. Apps can retain file versions and atomically switch a metadata pointer; backup the relevant collections yourself.

facts.label: identity and old names
facts.value: MongoDB Community Edition, also labelled MongoDB Community Server in the download center; maintained by MongoDB, Inc.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: Community Server uses Server Side Public License version 1, dated 2018-10-16 (SSPL-1.0). It is source available; MongoDB states SSPL is not OSI-approved open source.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: The separate mongot search engine is also available under SSPL; you run and maintain it alongside mongod. Enterprise Advanced is a different commercial offering.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Current download selector also offers 8.3.13, 8.0.34 and 7.0.45. Community platform docs cover 9.x, 8.x and 7.x. Availability of older archived binaries does not mean ongoing maintenance.

facts.value: Published MongoDB Server EOL schedule: 9.0 on 2031-10-31; 8.3 and 8.0 on 2029-10-31; 7.0 on 2027-08-31. 8.2 ended 2026-07-31 and 6.0 ended 2025-07-31.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: The product FAQ still says Search starts at Community 8.2, while current installation/compatibility docs require 8.3 or later, with 8.3.4+ for Kubernetes-managed deployments; 8.2 is now EOL.

facts.label: vendor home and main markets
facts.value: MongoDB, Inc.; US headquarters in New York City and international headquarters in Dublin, Ireland, with offices across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
