facts.value: FAQ states data volumes and backups are encrypted. The contract separately says OVHcloud does not specifically encrypt customer Content and assigns content confidentiality measures to the customer.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: Current documented versions: PostgreSQL 15/16/17/18; MySQL 8.4; MongoDB 7.0/8.0; Valkey 8.1/9.1. Engines use their own SQL, document or key-value interfaces.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: PostgreSQL supports multi-statement BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK transactions as standard engine behavior; managed PgBouncer statement mode cannot run multi-statement transactions.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Actual SQL default isolation/synchronous-replication configuration, Valkey consistency settings and a universal cross-engine durability guarantee were not established.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Managed MongoDB defaults to primary read preference and majority write concern. Clients may change these in connection strings or per operation; w=1 acknowledges only the primary and trades durability for lower latency.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Database forking is supported across the four current engines and clones a new service from backups for testing/upgrades. It creates separately billable resources, not a free instant copy-on-write branch entitlement.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: SQL HA tiers use primary plus replica(s): Business/Production 2 nodes; Enterprise/Advanced 3. Automatic failover can take seconds to about 1 minute, and writes are discarded/unavailable during promotion.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: MongoDB Production has 3 nodes; Advanced permits 3–7 including an optional analytics node. Current Valkey Production has 2 nodes (primary/replica); Discovery is single-node.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: A managed application-client offline-write queue, conflict resolution and durable replay service were not established.

facts.label: extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: PostgreSQL approved extensions include PostGIS, pg_trgm, pgvector, pgvectorscale and pg_cron. Unsupported extensions cannot be installed; availability depends on PG version and dependencies.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: Multipart/resumable file-upload limits are outside this service's client interface.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Customer S3 object-operation compatibility is outside this managed-database interface.

facts.label: delivery and private files
facts.value: Bucket permissions, signed file URLs, CDN delivery and custom asset domains require a separate file-serving product.

facts.label: filters and mixed search
facts.value: Upstream pgvector supports exact/ANN distance search and SQL filters; ANN filters can reduce returned neighbors. Iterative scanning is a version-dependent remedy from 0.8.0; managed PostGIS/trigram/text extensions allow separate SQL search features.

facts.label: execution model and languages
facts.value: PostgreSQL supports pg_cron for scheduled SQL inside the database; it does not allocate a general JavaScript/Python worker machine. Other hosted app/worker resources need their own service.

facts.label: delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Upstream pg_cron runs different jobs in parallel but only one execution of a particular job at a time; another scheduled occurrence queues behind it. This is not a general exactly-once distributed task contract.

facts.label: delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: A managed retry/backoff, dead-letter, deduplication window and failed-job replay policy was not found for this database offer.

facts.label: schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Upstream pg_cron accepts cron schedules and stores definitions in cron.job; timezone configuration and sub-minute syntax depend on the actual installed version/settings.

facts.label: schedules and queue retention
facts.value: A vendor-guaranteed queued-run lifetime, payload cap and retention window for scheduled SQL were not established.

facts.label: logs and run history
facts.value: Upstream cron.job_run_details can record runs and is not automatically cleaned; users can delete their own records. Managed PostgreSQL logs retain 1,000 lines and metrics 1 calendar month; these are different histories.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Self-host deployment requirements are not applicable to the managed service. OVHcloud runs hardware/OS/engine maintenance; customer retains access, schema, performance, export and disaster-recovery responsibilities.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Customers choose service region; cluster nodes must stay in the same region. Engine docs say availability across Public Cloud 1-AZ/3-AZ regions; exact SKU/plan availability must be checked at creation.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Documented database backup-region identifiers include BHS, DE, GRA, SBG, UK, WAW, RBX, SGP, SYD, EU-WEST-PAR, EU-SOUTH-MIL and AP-SOUTH-MUM. Baseline here is GRA/Gravelines, France.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: GRA backups default to SBG; UK, DE, WAW, RBX, Paris and Milan default to GRA. BHS defaults to SBG; Singapore, Sydney and Mumbai default to BHS. Backup locality can therefore cross countries/continents.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Backup regions can be configured: MongoDB accepts one location; other engines accept one matching service region or two locations including the service region. DPA also permits necessary remote processing/sub-processors.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Standard import/export tools are supported: PostgreSQL pg_dump/pg_restore and MySQL mysqldump/mysqlimport. Platform-made backups cannot be downloaded directly; restore to another service, then dump.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: At DBaaS termination, data becomes immediately inaccessible through encryption-key deletion. Encrypted remnants can persist 2 days to 1 month depending on removal cycle; this is not a recovery guarantee.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: The controller privacy policy has different retention schedules for account, payment and legal records; deleting a database does not erase all invoice/account records. Rights requests are available under the UK policy.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: PostgreSQL/MySQL Essential/Discovery: daily backups retained 2 days.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: PostgreSQL/MySQL Business/Production: daily backups retained 14 days.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: PostgreSQL/MySQL Enterprise/Advanced: daily backups retained 30 days.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: MongoDB Production: daily backups, 7-day retention; Advanced: daily backups, 30-day retention and PITR for the last 24 hours.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Valkey Discovery: backups every 12 hours, retained 1 day; Production: every 12 hours, retained 3 days. RDB persistence off disables backups/forks and loses data on restart/power-off; AOF is unavailable.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: UK contract says an automatic weekly backup, while current engine docs promise daily SQL/MongoDB and twice-daily Valkey schedules. Current operational schedule and contractual language therefore differ.

facts.label: file recovery and protection
facts.value: Object versioning, bucket locks and object undelete do not describe database backups.

facts.label: identity and old names
facts.value: OVHcloud Public Cloud Databases, marketed as Cloud Databases; this record covers the managed Public Cloud catalogue, not Web Cloud Databases or self-managed databases on a VPS.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: Managed service: OVHcloud/partners operate dedicated cluster nodes; customers manage data schemas, app access, tuning and business continuity. This is not a self-host distribution of OVHcloud's control plane.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: PostgreSQL uses the PostgreSQL License; MySQL uses MySQL Community GPL, with license cost included and no bring-your-own-license option.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: Valkey uses BSD 3-Clause; both current MongoDB plans are labelled MongoDB Community License, included in the service with no BYOL.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Current catalogue and paid engine provisioning guides are active. No whole-catalogue shutdown, acquisition or rename was found in the official product, lifecycle and contract pages checked.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: MongoDB Discovery (db2-free) reached end of sale on 31 August 2026, suspension on 31 October 2026, and scheduled deletion with all data on 30 November 2026. The global guide confirms the notice, not just the US FAQ.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Gen 2 DB1 tiers retain Essential/Business/Enterprise names; Gen 3 B3 tiers use Discovery/Production/Advanced. Pricing says both generations remain available.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: DBMS lifecycle policy follows upstream end of life. Running affected versions are automatically upgraded upon EOL; sleeping/powered-off affected services become inaccessible and their backups are deleted.

facts.label: vendor home and main markets
facts.value: For the UK scope used here the contractual provider is OVH Limited; customer-data processing terms and controller privacy policy distinguish the contracting company from affiliates/sub-processors.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: Standard support/resources are available; higher Premium/Business/Enterprise support is account-wide and separately chosen. Business/Enterprise offer 24/7 phone/ticket support; Standard/Premium business-hours channels differ.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: Database SLA: Essential/Discovery/Free none; single-AZ Business/Production 99.90%, Enterprise/Advanced 99.95%; multi-AZ Production 99.95%, Advanced 99.99%.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: SLA downtime requires loss of access to all instances for over 3 consecutive minutes, measured from incident-ticket opening. Credits depend on the missed threshold and are capped at 30% of the impacted service's monthly cost; exclusions apply.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: Public Cloud status page publishes component incidents and planned maintenance; it is broader than this database record.

free.text: 1 app, up to 10,000 objects; 90 idle days may delete data

cells.regions: AWS US, EU, or Japan; exact region unclear

sql.math: €25 is the known plan subtotal if app data fits 10 GB. Object count, request and transfer costs are unknown.
€25 a month continues when idle, if billable data stays within 10 GB. Actual indexed storage and other costs are unclear.

files.math: Para Cloud has no published hosted file storage plan.

jobs.math: €25 is the known app part. Webhook workers need separate hosting, and they have no published price for running time.

apps.news: News check 2026-11-09: no sale, shutdown, rebrand, or incident found for Para.

facts.label: Free offer type
facts.value: Cloud has an ongoing Free plan, not a timed credit trial: one app/up to 10,000 objects. FAQ says Free may be kept indefinitely, subject to Terms' deletion after over 90 inactive days. Self-host software is separately free.

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: Cloud Free: one app, shared database, maximum 10,000 stored objects; advertised encryption at rest and high availability/failover. No GB, read/write, MAU, seat or compute allowance is quantified on its card.

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: Exact Free byte capacity, API rate/count, concurrent clients, user/seat limits and which auxiliary objects count toward 10,000 not found.

facts.label: Inactivity, pause and deletion
facts.value: Free accounts inactive for over 90 days are deleted along with all app data.

facts.label: Inactivity, pause and deletion
facts.value: Definition of activity, warning schedule, recovery after idle deletion and paid idle-retention/pause rules not specified in the searched pages.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: Paid Cloud €25 per app/month with dedicated database and 10 GB storage. Annual option pays ten months for twelve; EU VAT excluded, with site stating VAT not applicable outside EU.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Additional Cloud storage €1.5 per GB/month above included 10 GB. App credits buy additional dedicated app/database/index allocations; no separate public CPU/GB-second invocation tariff found.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Exact GB definition, measured average/peak capacity, part-month storage integration, billing rounding, quotas on requests/transfer and paid app-credit checkout/proration formula not found.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Terms say monthly/annual billing in arrears; FAQ says card charged immediately after checkout and prorated extra charges immediately on downgrade.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Paid subscription auto-renews until cancelled; no published per-request compute rate offsets the plan price when requests fall to zero.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Automatic request-idle scale-to-zero, free wake delay, paid manual pause and which retained-data fees survive a pause not found.

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: Cloud internet ingress/egress, cross-region replication, export transfer allowances and per-GB charges not found.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: Storage limit is soft per recovered FAQ. Free overage prompts an email requesting upgrade/payment details; after seven days without those details the account is deactivated until payment is provided.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: Whole-bill hard spend cap, configurable budget alerts, grace-usage billing details and paid overage enforcement thresholds not found.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Software defaults: 1,048,576-byte incoming JSON entity limit; 256 data types/app; page result default 30, max page number 1000, max limit parameter 256; configurable.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Cloud maximum object bytes, capacity above 10 GB, API throughput/connections and plan-specific batch limits not established.

facts.label: Storage prices
facts.value: No separately specified Para Cloud file-storage allowance or file GB-month rate found. The €1.5/GB/month price is app storage; FileStore is a software integration with local disk or a separately configured S3 bucket.

facts.label: Storage prices
facts.value: Storage prose says S3 writes use Reduced Redundancy, while current AWSFileStore source sets no explicit storage class. No current Cloud hot/archive class mapping established.

facts.label: File request and retrieval prices
facts.value: Para file upload/list/read/retrieval/image-processing tariffs and billing blocks not found; local/S3 integration docs do not price the chosen infrastructure/provider.

facts.label: Minimum storage and early deletion
facts.value: Para-specific minimum file capacity, billed object size, retained duration and early-deletion fee not found; external provider/bucket policy would need its own terms.

facts.label: Vector/index limits
facts.value: No dedicated vector-index product or documented vector dimension/index/namespace limits. Para's documented search layer is Lucene/Elasticsearch text/field/geo search, with pluggable backends.

facts.label: Embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: Embedding generation/reranking model service and token tariff do not apply to the documented Para offering. External AI code may use REST data but would be an added service.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Self-host configurable executor thread count defaults to 2; webhooks disabled by default. River polling defaults: interval 10 seconds, empty-queue sleep 60 seconds; SQS long-poll setting must be 0 to 20 seconds.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Hosted webhook queue quota, delivery throughput/concurrency, CPU/RAM allocation, full HTTP response timeout and execution/wait/retry prices not found.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Cloud Free requires no credit card; public start/sign-in path. Terms restrict customers to age 18 or above; AUP permits legitimate business/organizational use subject to agreements.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Complete country eligibility and a separate explicit Free production-use guarantee not established. Free is positioned for prototypes/small apps; Paid is positioned for production.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Current DPA Article 3 describes personal-data categories as personal identifiers and data subjects as employees/associates; it excludes processor liability for sensitive-data incidents. Broader app-data contractual coverage is not clarified.

facts.label: Primary type and other roles
facts.value: Researcher classification: backend platform/API and object-persistence framework; schemaless JSON, search, cache, auth, webhooks and optional Java storage/queue integrations.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Cloud provides object persistence on DynamoDB, Elasticsearch search, object cache, user/JWT authentication and permission APIs. Paid includes backup/restore and advertised PITR; server code has optional webhooks and integrations.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Files and WebSockets are marked planned/not supported in the current official client feature matrix. FileStore exists as a server integration; custom Java resource handlers exist as plugins. Hosted functions/runtime and file quota not established.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: REST/HTTP JSON; official Java, JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, PHP, C#/.NET, Swift/iOS and Android clients. Java may embed Para directly. App signing uses AWS Signature v4; users use JWT.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Java/JS/Android clients have asynchronous methods; other listed clients synchronous. Quickstart warns single-thread restricted serverless environments to avoid async calls or disable executor service.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: New app users default-deny except their own object/children; grant per-user/resource HTTP methods, OWN-owner access or explicit anonymous/public permission. Signed app requests and app super-JWTs have full API access.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: App secrets can be rotated with POST /v1/_newkeys; self-host mTLS and TLS/reverse-proxy guidance are documented. Cloud advertises encryption at rest; customer-configurable private network/IP allowlist not established.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: Cloud docs identify DynamoDB persistence plus Elasticsearch indexing/cache. Self-host defaults H2 plus Lucene; optional SQL, DynamoDB, MongoDB and Cassandra adapters. App-facing data model is Para JSON objects/REST.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: Exact Cloud database/search versions and a supported SQL-dialect/version matrix for every plugin not found.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: Optimistic locking is per object: opt in with positive version; matching conditional update succeeds, mismatch reports version=-1. DynamoDB DAO supports it. Database, index and cache updates can become inconsistent; client may need retry/reconciliation.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: Para API multi-object ACID transaction/isolation guarantees, cross-region read consistency and atomic batch semantics not published in the searched pages.

facts.label: Test environments and branches
facts.value: Separate Para apps provide namespaces, credentials, types and permissions; table/index sharing depends on adapter/configuration. Local H2/Lucene development and production profiles available; paid Cloud charges per app.

facts.label: Test environments and branches
facts.value: Apps page says single-table app sharing is not implemented; DynamoDB adapter docs describe implemented shared-table mode using prefixed keys and isSharingTable. The generic page's scope/version is not reconciled.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Cloud advertises high availability/failover on both plans and cross-region replication. Number/location of copies, RPO/RTO, routing and automatic recovery procedure are not specified.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Self-host Elasticsearch exposes replica/auto-expand settings; DynamoDB adapter can use configured replica regions. Operator owns the external cluster and its replica costs.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Official clients mark WebSockets planned; server webhooks send asynchronous HTTP object/custom events. Native offline client storage, queued writes and conflict reconciliation not established.

facts.label: Extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Search layer provides full-text Lucene syntax, exact field/term filters, wildcard, prefix, geo-nearby and more-like-this queries; Elasticsearch plugin supports normal/nested custom-field indexing.

facts.label: Upload and file limits
facts.value: Software local/S3 upload-size settings default to 10, described as MB. S3 implementation enforces config ×1024×1024 bytes, so default is 10,485,760 bytes; buffers input then makes one putObject request.

facts.label: Upload and file limits
facts.value: Hosted file upload entitlement/global file-size ceiling, allowed-type restrictions and resumable/multipart API support not established; client matrix marks Files planned.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: FileStore Java interface exposes load/store/delete; official AWSFileStore uses S3 getObject/putObject/deleteObject. Para's hosted REST is JSON object API; no Para public S3 gateway/operation-compatibility matrix established.

facts.label: Delivery and private files
facts.value: Current S3 plugin explicitly requests PUBLIC_READ ACL on writes and returns a direct bucket URL. Bucket policy/ACL support still determines acceptance/access. It is not an automatically private file path protected by Para object permissions.

facts.label: Delivery and private files
facts.value: Para-managed file presigning, private CDN access, image transformations and custom-domain pricing/configuration not found.

facts.label: Filters and mixed search
facts.value: Confirmed keyword/field/geo/more-like-this search is covered under D08; native dense/sparse vector plus keyword ranking is not a documented Para offering.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: Para webhooks coordinate asynchronous HTTP POST deliveries to your endpoint; queue/river runs in Para. Local in-memory queue or optional SQS plugin; not a published managed arbitrary-code function machine.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Docs describe non-2xx delivery as failure and disable a webhook after 10 failures by default. Current Webhook source defaults repeatedDeliveryAttempts to 1; River caps repeated deliveries at 100 and sends copies in parallel, not failure-only backoff.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Docs say SQS messages are deleted after processing; current AWSQueueUtils queues deleteMessageBatch immediately after receive, before the River processes returned bodies. Docs accept all 2xx; River's failure test is abs(code−200)>10, which differs.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Native exactly-once side effects, ordering, deduplication window, durable failed-event storage/DLQ and replay policy not established. LocalQueue is explicitly nonpersistent and removes messages when pulled.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: No hosted cron/delay scheduling API, maximum scheduling horizon, pending-message TTL/retention or payload ceiling documented for Para webhooks. Local queue disappears on process loss; SQS needs provider-side configuration.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Self-host SLF4J/Logback logs include main/metrics/access logging guidance. Current server logback.xml rotates main archives monthly, history 6 periods, 100MB chunks/500MB total; metric history 7 daily periods/1GB cap.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Cloud log/run-history retained days/bytes, access/export facilities, failed-delivery replay and extra retention prices not found.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Self-host needs a supported Java runtime/JAR or Docker, writable data/index/config storage, plugins/drivers for external backends, secrets/TLS, database/object backups and your own scaling/monitoring. H2/Lucene/Caffeine can run locally without external database/search services.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Current quickstart and compiler configuration require Java 21+, while repository README still says JDK 8+. Cloud-install example suggests 512MB instance or larger, 1GB recommended; no complete production resource minimum established.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Operator handles upgrades and H2/plugin schema migrations, backups and external file/queue recovery; paid Cloud has managed updates/scaling/backups. Official plugins require server restart after install/remove.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Cloud page lists AWS US, EU or JP and automatic failover; it also describes cross-region replication. Exact AWS region IDs, selection/migration controls and component/backup locations are not given.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Cloud advertises US/EU/JP hosting while current DPA Article 10 says processing under that agreement will not take place outside the EEA. Applicability of US/JP choices under the DPA is unresolved.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Hosted GET /v1/_export returns a ZIP containing JSON Para objects; PUT /v1/_import accepts an exported ZIP and overwrites existing objects. Cloud UI backup/restore/download is a paid feature.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Each app can delete itself through DELETE /v1/app/myapp; Terms permit account cancellation without refund. On termination, email a retrieval request within 14 days of notice; content is not deleted earlier than the stated 14-day termination/notice rule.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Privacy permits email access/correction/deletion requests. Signed DPA Article 16 offers deletion or return after service, subject to legal retention, and permits compliance records; exact live/backups purge deadline not stated.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Paid Cloud advertises backup/restore and PITR; app-object export is ZIP/JSON, with import overwriting existing objects. Free card omits backup/restore entitlement.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Cloud backup frequency, retained days, PITR window/precision, restore targets, encryption/key controls, file exclusions and extra recovery charges not found.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Self-host H2 docs give Script/RunScript backup/restore for the whole database including child apps. H2 upgrades may require export with old engine and import with new engine, with Para stopped.

facts.label: File recovery and protection
facts.value: FileStore supports deletion, but no Para managed version-history/undelete/retention-lock/replicated file-backup offer is specified. App ZIP/JSON export does not establish inclusion of external file bytes.

facts.label: Identity and old names
facts.value: Para, developed by Erudika; paraio.org is the software/docs site and paraio.com is the hosted service. No former product name established.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Self-hosted executable Java JAR/Docker, embeddable JVM framework and separately managed Para Cloud. Paid Cloud includes managed updates/backups/scaling; self-host operators manage these.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Core Para source is Apache-2.0; official S3/SQS plugins also identify Apache-2.0. Dependency/provider service terms remain separate.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Active public Cloud offer; latest GitHub release API identifies stable 1.57.0, published 2026-10-09. It fixes a critical multitenancy PATCH vulnerability. Cloud runtime version not established.

facts.label: Vendor home and main markets
facts.value: Erudika EOOD, Sofia, Bulgaria; current Terms use Erudika LTD. Impressum gives 4 Lelinska chuka Str., Sofia 1618 and VAT BG-200368755.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Paid email support; support page gives support@paraio.com and forum. Self-host community support. Free card says community only, but the same Cloud FAQ and older hosted card also list email support.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Official site links status.erudika.com. Reader could not access it; direct fetch returned an empty parsed page, and a later fetch failed. Live operational status could not be checked.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Contractual uptime percentage, service-credit schedule and support-response target not found; Terms expressly disclaim continuous/uninterrupted availability.

apps.name: Parse Server
apps.line: Self-hosted backend framework with auth, files, Cloud Code, and jobs.

free.text: Apache-2.0; no hosted quota or idle rule; you run the server and database

cells.metered: Software $0; infrastructure is yours to run
cells.regions: Choose your host region

sql.math: $0 software fee. App server, database, storage, traffic and backups depend on the provider you pick.
The software stays $0. Kept server, database, file and backup costs depend on the host.

files.math: Parse has a file API. File capacity, requests, delivery and provider rates are separate and not priced.

jobs.math: Jobs have no software fee. Server capacity and worker size are not priced until a host is chosen.

apps.news: News check 2026-11-09: no sale, shutdown, rebrand, or incident found for Parse Server.

facts.label: Free offer type
facts.value: Free open-source software, not a recurring managed free tier or trial credits. Server/database/file/backup capacity is supplied separately.

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: Hosted free-plan GB, API calls, MAU, projects, seats and function credits do not apply. Software has configurable limits and finite infrastructure, recorded under D03/F04/J02.

facts.label: Inactivity, pause and deletion
facts.value: Provider-managed inactive project sleep/deletion/resume rules do not apply to the self-hosted project. Owner/selected host controls process and retained data.

facts.label: Inactivity, pause and deletion
facts.value: 9.11.0 expireInactiveSessions defaults true and sessionLength is 31,536,000 seconds; extendSessionOnUse defaults false. These affect login sessions, not expiry of the app's database.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: No mandatory paid Parse Server subscription, project fee or seat minimum; no vendor-managed least-paid plan to quote. Third-party hosts listed by Wiki are separate products.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: No Parse Server invoice meter for CPU, GB, requests, failed work or waiting. Operator's hosting, database, object storage, network and optional adapters/providers supply the actual bill.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Central scale-to-zero billing/wake policy does not apply. Running/stopping Node, LiveQuery and database/file services depends on chosen infrastructure; persistent data must survive process/container replacement.

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: No uniform Parse Community ingress/egress/inter-region/export transfer tariff; routes/costs depend on server, database and file provider, including proxy versus direct file delivery.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: Vendor overage/grace-period/budget/spend-cap policy does not apply to this software. Host/provider bill controls must be researched for the selected deployment.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: Operator can configure API rate limits and request-complexity limits. Current option help cautions that per-instance rate counts do not automatically form one shared counter across a load-balanced cluster.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: 9.11.0 default query limit 100; maxLimit unset/unlimited by default. Request-complexity batch/depth/include/subquery caps default -1 (disabled) and can be configured; master/maintenance requests exempt from those complexity caps.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: MongoDB driver maxPoolSize/minPoolSize/readConcern/readPreference options exposed; PostgreSQL URL supports pool/timeouts. No one portable Parse-wide DB-size, connection or effective object-payload ceiling is published.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: For MongoDB-backed objects, engine BSON document ceiling is 16 mebibytes; Parse metadata/encoding and HTTP/proxy limits can reduce usable application payload. This is not a file limit because GridFS splits files.

facts.label: Storage prices
facts.value: No Parse GB-month storage tariff or paid storage class. Choose MongoDB GridFS, filesystem, S3 or GCS adapter; capacity/replicas/archive pricing depend on that deployment.

facts.label: Storage prices
facts.value: Current README defaults to GridFSBucketAdapter; older file-adapter guide calls GridStoreAdapter the default. In 9.11.0 GridStoreAdapter throws an unsupported error and directs users to GridFSBucketAdapter.

facts.label: File request and retrieval prices
facts.value: No Parse file-operation/retrieval/image-request billing blocks; selected filesystem/database/object/CDN infrastructure determines costs. Cloud Code may implement transformations but does not include a managed image tariff.

facts.label: Minimum storage and early deletion
facts.value: Parse software imposes no vendor storage billing floor or early-deletion invoice. Provider/object-class minimum size/duration and retained backup bills require the chosen provider's terms.

facts.label: Vector/index limits
facts.value: No dedicated Parse vector-index offering or documented dimensions/index/namespace limits in the searched object/query/database guides.

facts.label: Embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: No bundled embedding/reranking/model tariff; any external AI calls in Cloud Code are an additional integration and provider bill.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: No per-job CPU/RAM SKU, execution-second charge or vendor concurrency allotment. Runtime/worker sizing, process limits and network timeout policy depend on owner/host configuration.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Universal maximum job/function wall time, isolated per-run memory, durable waiting/suspension behavior and restart recovery limits not published in the searched Parse sources.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: No Parse-hosting signup, payment card or trial required to download/run the software. Apache-2.0 permits commercial use subject to its conditions. Hosting/database/email/push-provider accounts, if chosen, have separate rules.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Community Terms/Privacy govern the forum, not apps deployed with Parse Server. Forum minimum age and retention language are not copied into backend customer eligibility.

facts.label: Primary type and other roles
facts.value: Researcher classification: backend platform/framework with object data API, authentication, files, Cloud Code, jobs, push and realtime LiveQuery.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Object data/auth/roles/sessions; REST and optional generated GraphQL; Node.js Cloud Functions/triggers/jobs; files via adapters; LiveQuery; push integrations with credentials supplied by operator.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: REST JSON, generated GraphQL (mountGraphQL defaults false), LiveQuery WebSockets. Official connection examples cover Swift/Objective-C Apple platforms, Android, JavaScript, .NET and PHP.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: 9.11.0 package engine ranges: Node >=20.19.0 <21, >=22.13.0 <23, >=24.11.0 <25 or >=26.13.0 <27. Cloud Code shares the server's Node runtime.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: README Node compatibility table says 22.12.0 minimum; 9.11.0 package requires 22.13.0. Use installed-release engine constraints when resolving that difference.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Class-level permissions and per-object ACLs/roles restrict operations; a request must pass both. App IDs/client keys are public identifiers; master/maintenance keys bypass normal client checks and belong only on trusted servers.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: 9.11.0 defaults allowClientClassCreation=false, enforcePrivateUsers=true and masterKeyIps=['127.0.0.1','::1']. Optional route allowlist restricts external REST routes; file/pages/GraphQL routes are excluded from that option.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Security guide's general introductory defaults say clients can create classes; 9.11.0 default explicitly disables client class creation.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: Native backing databases MongoDB or PostgreSQL; Parse exposes classes/objects, pointers/relations and JSON queries. Release README lists MongoDB 7/8 and PostgreSQL 16/17/18; version table gives exact minima and PostGIS combinations.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: PostgreSQL adapter loads from postgres URI, supports TLS/pool options; relations/pointers resolve joins in memory, schema mutation uses ALTER TABLE, and files need an external adapter.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: 9.11.0 POST /batch with transaction=true creates a transactional session; any sub-request error aborts, otherwise commits. Both Mongo and Postgres adapters implement transaction sessions; ordinary batch calls do not imply atomicity.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: MongoDB transactions require a capable database topology/settings. MongoDB documents single-document atomicity and multi-document transactions with guarantees affected by configured read/write concerns.

facts.label: Test environments and branches
facts.value: Can develop locally and deploy separate server/database environments. README explicitly says no multi-tenancy and only one Parse Server instance per Express app; Cloud Code has access to its Node process environment.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: MongoDB readPreference supports PRIMARY (default), PRIMARY_PREFERRED, SECONDARY, SECONDARY_PREFERRED and NEAREST, including include/subquery preferences. Database replica topology, elections and resource costs are operator/provider responsibilities.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Older Mongo read-preference guide says the setting is Cloud Code only; current JavaScript query guide documents client query.readPreference including include/subquery parameters.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: LiveQuery sends create/enter/update/leave/delete events over WebSocket for configured classes; JS client reconnects with exponential backoff and resubscribes. Separate LiveQuery instances can scale through Redis pub/sub.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: JS local datastore supports pinned objects and offline local queries; pinned objects update on fetch/save or subscribed LiveQuery events. Aggregate/distinct local queries not supported.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Missed-event durable replay, JS offline-write conflict rules and end-to-end automatic reconciliation guarantees not established in searched guides.

facts.label: Extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Text/full-text, relational and geo queries; schema/index management depends on database. PostGIS for geographic Postgres features; operator maintains indexes. Mongo aggregation is available with master access.

facts.label: Upload and file limits
facts.value: 9.11.0 maxUploadSize default '20mb', configurable; reverse proxy/body limits must also permit upload. Default upload allowed for authenticated users, disabled for anonymous/public users.

facts.label: Upload and file limits
facts.value: REST file guide says maximum 10 megabytes; 9.11.0 option default is '20mb'.

facts.label: Upload and file limits
facts.value: 9.11.0 permits configurable extension patterns, with default blocks for active browser formats such as HTML/SVG/XML for non-master uploaders. Current GridFS/S3 adapters support streaming; native client resumable-upload session/part limits not established.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Client protocol is Parse Files REST/SDK. S3 adapter consumes backend S3 GET/PUT/DELETE, HEAD/create-bucket and SDK multipart streaming; custom endpoint recipes support selected S3-compatible providers.

facts.label: Delivery and private files
facts.value: 9.11.0 file downloads default enabled for public, anonymous and authenticated users. FileDownload options can restrict groups; beforeFind file trigger can apply custom checks. A referring object's ACL alone is not a file-URL authorization rule.

facts.label: Delivery and private files
facts.value: S3 adapter supports proxied/direct access, custom baseUrl/cache headers and optional presigned URLs. Presigning defaults false; expiry is configurable and omitted value is delegated to AWS SDK. Direct mode requests public-read unless fileAcl overrides it.

facts.label: Delivery and private files
facts.value: No bundled CDN service/custom-domain subscription; configure provider CDN/DNS/reverse proxy as needed. GridFS and FS support optional AES-256-GCM file encryption with a separately retained key.

facts.label: Filters and mixed search
facts.value: Keyword/full-text and metadata filters confirmed under D08; managed dense/sparse vector plus keyword ranking is not a documented Parse service.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: JavaScript Cloud Code functions/triggers/jobs execute inside Parse Server's Node process; same runtime as server. Not isolated managed FaaS machines. HTTP webhooks may run external handlers.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: Cloud Jobs invoked through master-protected REST return X-Parse-Job-Status-Id. 9.11.0 writes running status, schedules handler via process.nextTick, then records succeeded/failed.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Experimental request idempotency uses X-Parse-Request-Id, configured paths and default 300-second retention; paths default empty. Must be enabled on server and supported client; not a production exactly-once workflow guarantee.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Automatic failed-job retry/backoff, ordered delivery, durable pending-work queue, deduplication beyond configured request records, DLQ and crash-resume guarantees not established.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Cloud Code guide recommends external scheduling and says scheduling is not currently supported there. 9.11.0 has CRUD routes for _JobSchedule records, but that does not establish a running scheduler/cron execution guarantee.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Maximum delay/horizon, timezone guarantees, durable queue TTL and job payload ceiling not specified as a portable Parse job contract.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: _JobStatus records running/succeeded/failed, created/finished time and message; query with master key or view in Dashboard. Server logs default to console and daily rotating JSON files in ./logs; configurable transports.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: maxLogFiles unset means no configured automatic log removal; can be file count or days suffix. Logger query defaults to last 7 days/10 results, which is a query window, not seven-day retention.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Fixed job-history retained days/bytes, built-in failed-run replay/checkpoint restore and export-retention service level not found.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Run compatible Node.js/Express plus MongoDB or PostgreSQL; configure server URL, secrets, Cloud Code, TLS/firewall and backups. Postgres files require a non-GridFS adapter; optional email/push providers and Redis add dependencies.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: For multiple FS-backed server instances, all must share the same persistent file storage. Separate LiveQuery can scale through Redis pub/sub. No safe production CPU/RAM minimum or full workload capacity guarantee found.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Operator owns upgrades, adapters/engine compatibility, migrations, backup tests and monitoring; release/alpha/LTS differ. Cloud Code is not a tenant sandbox; separate apps/environments need process/resource isolation.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: No vendor selectable-region matrix: operator chooses server/database/file/backup locations. Separate file stores/Redis/LiveQuery components can be deployed separately.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Native exports: MongoDB mongodump emits BSON plus metadata/index definitions and restores with mongorestore; PostgreSQL pg_dump emits SQL or archive formats for psql/pg_restore.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: REST/SDK can delete objects/users and master-authorized files. Deleting an object referencing a file does not delete the file itself; external file storage needs separate migration/deletion.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Central account closure or physical-data/backup purge deadline does not apply to self-host software. Operator and selected provider control live, replica, file and backup erasure; forum privacy is unrelated.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Operator can export MongoDB data with mongodump and restore compatible BSON/metadata with mongorestore; PostgreSQL uses SQL/archive exports and psql/pg_restore. These are native engine tools, not automatic Parse backups.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Backup scope depends on chosen adapter: GridFS stores bytes in MongoDB; S3/FS/GCS bytes live outside a PostgreSQL or separate metadata database. Full-app recovery also needs Cloud Code/configuration and encryption keys.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: No Parse Community automatic backup/PITR schedule, retention days, restore-time promise or backup price applies. Operator selects/configures engine/host recovery and tests it.

facts.label: File recovery and protection
facts.value: Deleting Parse object/file reference does not delete file bytes. Explicit master-authorized file delete removes via adapter; default random filename prefixes avoid name collisions, not a version-history interface.

facts.label: File recovery and protection
facts.value: Parse-level version-history/undelete/retention-lock APIs and fixed file-recovery window not found. Any provider versioning, replicas or backup retention needs separate configuration.

facts.label: Identity and old names
facts.value: Parse Server, maintained by Parse Community; official repository parse-community/parse-server. This record covers the Node.js server software, separately from the old Parse hosted backend and independent hosting providers.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Self-hosted Node.js/Express server, standalone/Docker or mounted in an Express application. Third-party Parse hosting exists separately.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Parse Server license Apache-2.0. No-charge copyright/patent grants allow use, modification and distribution subject to license conditions; dependencies/adapters have their own license files.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Active; latest stable release 9.11.0 published 2026-11-03. Main branches release/alpha; previous major receives LTS attention, with limited maintenance/security commitments described in README.

facts.label: Vendor home and main markets
facts.value: No single hosting vendor home/market applies to this community software record; a business domicile for the project itself was not established.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Community help via issue tracker, forum/chat linked in README. Security reports have a dedicated disclosure policy/contact; no paid support entitlement included with the software.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: A central hosted uptime/status or service-credit promise is not applicable. Each deployment can expose /parse/health; operator monitors it. Apache license disclaims warranties.

facts.value: Neki public egress includes 100 GB/month per production branch or 10 GB per development branch; us-east-1 excess is $0.060/GB. Replication within a shard and backup transfer are not network-billed.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: A current Vitess app-egress tariff/allowance was not established from its pricing and plan guide; do not silently apply the Postgres allowance or treat the omission as zero.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: Organization spend alerts email administrators at 75% and 100% of the selected monthly budget. Coupons can overrun and continue charging the saved payment method.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: Postgres disk autoscaling is enabled by default and can be bounded by a configured storage limit; a maximum 65,536 GB network disk is documented. Database Traffic Control can warn/block matched query workloads.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: An enforced global USD spend cap with cutoff behavior across every billing meter was not established.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Postgres network-attached disk can grow to 65,536 GB (labelled 64 TB). Compute/storage and IOPS ceilings depend on chosen SKU/architecture; Metal disk follows selected storage SKU.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Managed PgBouncer defaults: 100 client connections per process, default_pool_size 20 per user/database pair, query_wait_timeout 120 seconds. Settings are configurable; several pool instances can multiply aggregate client capacity.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: The exact PS-5 direct max_connections setting and a managed Postgres universal query timeout/row-size limit were not established. Docs direct customers to the cluster Parameters tab for actual max_connections.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Vitess: 2,048 tables including views; 1,017 columns/table; query limits 100,000 returned/updated/deleted rows, 64 MiB result set, 900-second autocommit timeout and 20-second transaction timeout. Connections older than 24 hours may be terminated.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Vitess disk maxima conflict: system-limits guide states network disk 4 TB and Metal 110 GB–7.4 TB, while the current price catalogue lists larger Metal options, including M-5120 with 14,992 GiB.

facts.label: storage prices
facts.value: Standalone file-storage GB-month/class pricing is not part of this managed database offer.

facts.label: file request and retrieval prices
facts.value: File upload/list/read/retrieval/image-processing request prices do not apply to the database plans.

facts.label: minimum storage and early deletion
facts.value: Object minimum-retention and early-deletion billing rules are outside this service's scope.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: Managed Postgres lists pgvector 0.8.5 and pgvectorscale 0.9.0. Versioned upstream pgvector allows vector values up to 16,000 dimensions; HNSW/IVFFlat vector indexes support up to 2,000 and halfvec indexes up to 4,000.

facts.label: embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: An included app embedding/reranking model allowance and provider/model tariff were not established.

facts.label: run limits and pricing
facts.value: Managed pg_cron defaults cron.max_running_jobs to 1, configurable at least 1 and no higher than cluster max_worker_processes. cron.log_run and cron.log_statement default true; cron.database_name defaults postgres.

facts.label: run limits and pricing
facts.value: A separate per-invocation/execution-second cron tariff, per-job CPU/RAM reservation and universal managed job-duration limit were not established.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Base is self-service. Direct organizations require a valid debit/credit card; prepaid cards are not accepted. Terms also allow ACH unless otherwise agreed. A card preauthorization may be temporary.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: New accounts have large-size restrictions until an invoice of at least $100 has been successfully paid: general plans page caps choices at PS-160/M-320; larger sizes can be unlocked through support.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Use is subject to US/export restrictions and the AUP. Terms restrict resale, unapproved cryptocurrency mining, telecom use and certain sensitive/payment data; HIPAA use requires an executed BAA.

facts.label: primary type and other roles
facts.value: Researcher classification: managed relational databases. Postgres is a single-primary PostgreSQL service; Vitess provides MySQL sharding; Neki provides Postgres sharding.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: Database hosting includes branching, query insights, backups and connection infrastructure; PostgreSQL additionally supports SQL scheduling via pg_cron and logical CDC integrations. Application-user login, object delivery and general app workers require separate application/services.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Postgres connects using the standard PostgreSQL protocol: direct port 5432 or transaction-pooled PgBouncer port 6432. Standard drivers/ORMs work; HTTP/WebSocket access via the supported Neon serverless driver is documented for runtimes lacking TCP.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Vitess accepts native MySQL clients and branch credentials; MySQL-native and caching-SHA2 authentication are supported. CLI/API manage resources. Neki uses the Postgres protocol through routers, not PgBouncer username-routing conventions.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: All database connections require TLS; public connectivity is the default. Postgres offers app-specific roles/SQL grants; the default postgres role is near-superuser, NOSUPERUSER but BYPASSRLS, and should not be an app credential.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Postgres IP rules can target role/schema and only affect new connections. Adding private connectivity does not disable public access; configure explicit IP restrictions for private-only access.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Vitess passwords are branch-scoped with selectable roles/connection targets and optional per-password IP allowlists. No IP restriction means all source addresses are allowed with valid credentials; deleted passwords disconnect clients within five minutes.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Security docs describe encryption at rest/in transit and public/private database access. SSO is an optional Base add-on at $199/month; Enterprise options include dedicated/customer-owned cloud infrastructure.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: Regular PlanetScale Postgres uses PostgreSQL; the current extension catalogue has version tables for Postgres 18.6 and 17.11. It offers native SQL and curated extensions, with managed-role restrictions.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: Vitess databases run MySQL 8/InnoDB through Vitess. Only InnoDB is supported; stored procedures/functions/triggers/events, native CREATE USER, logical CREATE DATABASE and JSON_TABLE have limitations or are unsupported.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: Neki runs real PostgreSQL on shards behind its own SQL-parsing routers. A topology controls where data lives; it can start unsharded. It is not a port of Vitess or a guarantee of identical cross-shard behavior.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Regular Postgres supports multi-statement transactions, including via transaction-mode PgBouncer. HA commits are confirmed after durable storage on at least one replica; replica reads can lag and should not be assumed to give immediate read-your-writes.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Neki single-shard transactions retain PostgreSQL atomic commit/snapshot behavior; transactions spanning shards do not share an atomic commit or common snapshot.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Vitess's actual managed cross-shard atomicity/isolation configuration was not established from the checked compatibility, sharding and system-limit guides.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Postgres branches are isolated, separately billed clusters. Ordinary creation starts empty, without even a schema copy; restore from backup supplies schema/data. No automated schema merge/deploy-request workflow is provided for regular Postgres.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Default Postgres/Vitess development branch limit is 100 per database, configurable from 1 to 5,000; higher limits require support. Paid-plan development-hour allowances differ between engines.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Vitess provides branching, Data Branching and safe online-schema deploy requests. Neki branches isolate routers/shards/configuration and billing; ordinary creation is empty and backup restoration creates another charged branch.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Regular Postgres HA uses one primary plus two replicas in three AZs with automated promotion/rerouting. Single-node has no standing HA replica; switching to HA adds them. Extra/dedicated replicas incur additional charges.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Vitess production cluster includes primary plus two replicas; read-only regions and extra replicas add costs. Neki shard production SKUs also include primary plus two replicas and separately priced router capacity.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Neki development topology conflicts: pricing says development shards are HA with at least two replicas and no single-node configuration; backup restore guide says development profiles use one node per shard and zero replicas in its example.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Regular Postgres supports logical CDC to external consumers after WAL/slot/role configuration. Failover-safe slots and replication settings matter; client-side LISTEN/NOTIFY/session features require direct connections rather than transaction pooling.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Durable end-user offline reads/writes, conflict resolution and replay guarantees were not established for the managed products.

facts.label: extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Postgres supports a curated extension catalogue including pgvector 0.8.5, pgvectorscale 0.9.0, PostGIS 3.6.4, pg_cron 1.6.7, pg_trgm and TimescaleDB Apache 2 edition. Some installations need dashboard activation and a restart.

facts.label: extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: TIN provides a Postgres full-text inverted index, BM25 ranking, query language and highlighting; it can form the lexical side of hybrid search with pgvector.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: Multipart/resumable file uploads and maximum upload-object size are outside the database connection service.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Customer S3 object API compatibility is not applicable to the hosted database interface.

facts.label: delivery and private files
facts.value: Public/private file buckets, signed asset URLs, CDN and file domains require a separate application/storage product.

facts.label: filters and mixed search
facts.value: pgvector supports exact/ANN distance search with SQL predicates; ANN filtering can reduce returned rows, with iterative scanning available in 0.8.5. PlanetScale's TIN guide shows lexical and vector queries whose ranked results are combined in the application.

facts.label: execution model and languages
facts.value: pg_cron executes scheduled SQL inside Postgres, under the scheduling user's privileges. This is shared database compute rather than managed JavaScript/Python application workers.

facts.label: delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: pg_cron v1.6.7 permits parallel different jobs but only one active run of the same job; a later occurrence waits for that run to finish. Runs on a hot standby do not execute until promotion.

facts.label: delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Managed automatic retries/backoff, dead-letter handling, deduplication windows and failed-run replay policy were not established.

facts.label: schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Versioned pg_cron supports cron expressions, last-day-of-month syntax and intervals of 1–59 seconds; job definitions are in cron.job. Upstream default timezone is GMT, configurable; PlanetScale's exact configured timezone is not stated on its parameter page.

facts.label: schedules and queue retention
facts.value: A managed queued-run expiry, payload-size contract and guaranteed retention for waiting scheduler occurrences were not established.

facts.label: logs and run history
facts.value: Managed Postgres logs default to 7-day retention. pg_cron run logging is on by default; upstream cron.job_run_details rows are not automatically cleaned and users can remove their own history.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Customer-operated self-host deployment requirements do not apply to this hosted Product record. PlanetScale Managed operates within customer cloud infrastructure under an Enterprise service; it is not a free self-host edition.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Available region list: 12 AWS, 7 GCP and 3 Azure regions. Azure currently supports Postgres/Neki, not Vitess. AWS default for new databases is us-east-2; the comparison explicitly selects us-east-1.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: AWS identifiers: ap-northeast-1, ap-south-1, ap-southeast-1/2, ca-central-1, eu-central-1, eu-west-1/2, sa-east-1, us-east-1/2, us-west-2. GCP: us-central1, us-east1/4, northamerica-northeast1, asia-northeast3, europe-west1/4. Azure: centralus, eastus2, westeurope.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Branch region is chosen at creation and cannot be changed in place. New-region migration requires another branch and data transfer; organization administrators can restrict branch creation to the database's region.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Postgres backups and WAL are held in the same provider/region as the cluster; selected cross-region replicas copy the data elsewhere. DPA permits international processing where PlanetScale/subprocessors operate.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Postgres data/schema can be moved with pg_dump/pg_restore or pgcopydb; moving regions requires a new branch and new connection details. Vitess CLI provides dump/restore tooling, subject to its compatibility limits.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: On termination, access ends and PlanetScale has no general obligation to retain content. DPA: on customer request after termination, return/delete customer data within 30 days and backup copies within 90 days, subject to legal retention.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Controller privacy/account data has purpose/legal retention rules rather than one universal number of days; rights requests are described in the privacy policy.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Postgres production/development backups run every 12 hours, retained 2 days by default. PITR spans oldest retained backup to five minutes before now. Custom/protected backups and longer retention can increase backup/WAL charges.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Postgres restore creates an independent charged branch in the source region. The guide says extensions must be reinstalled. User-defined roles restore ownership, but passwords reset; source credentials do not work on the restored branch.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Vitess includes automated 12-hour backups; custom scheduled backup storage is $0.023/GB-month. Manual/emergency backups can cost extra; emergency backups copy directly from a running shard server and do not support PITR or external keyspaces.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Vitess default backup retained days and the ordinary non-emergency PITR window were not established in the inspected Vitess backup/plan/limit pages.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Neki requires 12-hour backups retained 2 days, covering every managed shard; overall success requires all shards. PITR restores another billed branch through five minutes before now; a changed shard set can leave a recovery gap until another successful all-shard backup.

facts.label: file recovery and protection
facts.value: Object version history, bucket locks and file undelete are not this product's backup interface.

facts.label: identity and old names
facts.value: PlanetScale, Inc.; current database products are PlanetScale Postgres, Vitess/MySQL and Neki. The former Scaler Pro plan is now named Base.

facts.label: hosting and license

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: The hosted Product is licensed for access under commercial terms, for the customer's internal business purposes; resale and source extraction are restricted. It is not an open-source distribution of the full PlanetScale platform.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
