cells.regions: Oregon, Ohio, Virginia, Frankfurt, Singapore

sql.math: $6 for compute, plus 5 GB × $0.30 for storage. The 5 GB allocation assumes the full database fits. The Hobby plan's 5 GB of bandwidth covers outbound data (egress).
$6 for compute while online, plus 5 GB × $0.30 for kept storage. The bill left over for a suspended database is unknown.

files.math: Render Postgres is a database, not file storage.

jobs.math: Postgres does not run worker jobs. Render's worker and cron services are separate.

apps.news: News check 2026-11-09: no sale, shutdown, rebrand, or incident found for Render Postgres.

facts.label: free offer type
facts.value: Free Postgres is a time-limited 30-day database instance, not lasting free production storage. Free Hobby workspace is a separate ongoing $0 workspace offer; upgrading the workspace alone does not remove Free compute limits.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: Free per database: 0.1 CPU, 256 MB RAM, 1 GB fixed storage and 100 simultaneous connections. One active Free Postgres per workspace. No native backups, managed PgBouncer, or production use; restart/maintenance can occur at any time.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: Hobby workspace: one seat, up to 25 services, 5 GB outbound bandwidth/month, 500 standard pipeline minutes/month, 7-day logs and two environments/project. These shared workspace quotas are not all exclusive database allowances.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: At day 30, Free Postgres becomes inaccessible until upgraded to paid compute. There is a further 14-day upgrade grace period; after that Render deletes the database and its data. Email warnings precede expiry/deletion.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: A separate inactivity-based deletion timer for an ordinary paid Postgres database was not found.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: Least paid compute: 0.1c-256mb (legacy Basic-256mb), $6/month for 0.1 CPU/256 MB and 100 connections; database storage $0.30/GB-month additional. Hobby workspace adds $0/month. A 1 GB allocation gives a $6.30 normal full-month baseline before tax/overages.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: Pro workspace $25/month, Scale $499/month, Enterprise custom, plus compute and storage. Unlimited team seats begin on Pro. Pro/Scale subscription waived only for a month with no services, live or suspended, and no activity.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: Terms bill monthly in arrears, generally at calendar-month start, with exceptions for prepayment/removing payment methods/termination. Taxes apply; cancellation is not refundable. Public product rates use '$'; an explicit general billing-currency declaration was not found beyond the $1 USD card check.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Provisioned per-instance compute, prorated to the second; storage allocation is billed separately at $0.30/GB-month. Example compute: 0.5c-1g $19/month; 1c-2g $40; 1c-4g $55; 2c-4g $75; 2c-8g $100. No read/write-operation tariff is listed in this price model.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Read replicas and HA standby use the primary's same compute plan/storage and are billed accordingly. PITR restores/test clones create additional database instances; preview copies also bill separately. Backup-window entitlement varies by workspace.

facts.label: idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: A running paid database is billed for its provisioned instance even with zero queries. No documented automatic Postgres idle-sleep/scale-to-zero rule was found; the 15-minute idle spin-down rule applies to Free web services.

facts.label: idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Manual Postgres suspension is exposed in the CLI, and maintenance docs describe suspension/resumption. Exact residual Postgres compute/storage charges and any maximum suspension-retention window were not established.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: Workspace public outbound allowance: Hobby 5 GB/month, Pro 25 GB/month, Scale 1 TB/month; excess $0.15/GB. Query responses from Postgres to destinations outside Render count. Unused allowance does not roll over.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: Inbound data and same-region private Render-service traffic are unbilled. Service-initiated same-region S3/GCS traffic is exempt. Other-region Render services cannot use the same private network; private-link external traffic is $0.03/GB, with separate plan/link requirements.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: Paid bandwidth overage is billed; with no payment method, exceeding included bandwidth spins services down until next month. Storage autoscaling permanently grows allocated capacity 50%, rounded to the next 5 GB, at 90% full; space cannot be reduced later.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: Database over capacity becomes unhealthy and is suspended; resume then add storage promptly. Build Pipeline has a separate monthly spend limit that stops new pipeline tasks, not running database compute or bandwidth charges.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: A workspace-wide hard dollar cap covering paid Postgres compute, storage, replicas and bandwidth, with an exact cutoff policy, was not found.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Create storage at 1 GB or any multiple of 5 GB; grow to a larger multiple of 5 GB, up to 16 TB self-service. No shrink; wait 6 hours between increases. Autoscaling at 90% grows capacity by 50%, rounded up to 5 GB. Legacy instance storage is fixed until migrated to a flexible plan.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Current connection guide and pricing: under 8 GB RAM 100 direct connections; 8–under 16 GB 200; 16–under 32 GB 400; at least 32 GB 500. Legacy table: at most 6 GB RAM 97; between 6 and 10 GB 197; at least 10 GB 397.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Compute Plans conflicts for some intermediate sizes: its grouping puts 2c-4g under Max 200 connections and 4c-32g under Max 400. Pricing and Create & Connect instead imply 100 and 500 respectively.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Integrated PgBouncer: transaction mode, maximum 30,000 client connections; database pool size max_connections minus 10; 10 connections reserved for direct/internal operations. Idle client timeout 86,400 seconds, connection retry 2 seconds. Pool port 6432.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: A Render-specific maximum row/record size, SQL payload ceiling or universal statement timeout was not established.

facts.label: storage prices
facts.value: Not applicable to Postgres as database-independent file/object storage. Database allocation pricing is C13; separate Render app disks have their own meter.

facts.label: file request and retrieval prices
facts.value: Not applicable to a Postgres file upload/read/retrieval operation tariff.

facts.label: minimum storage and early deletion
facts.value: Not applicable to object-class minimum retention or early-delete charges. Database allocation and no-shrink rules are recorded under D03.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: pgvector is a supported extension. Upstream HNSW limits: vector 2,000 dimensions, halfvec 4,000, bit 64,000, sparsevec 1,000 nonzero elements. The vector column type itself allows up to 16,000 dimensions.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: Render's extension page does not pin a pgvector release or publish a separate vector-record/index/namespace quota. Exact installed extension version and version-specific feature availability remain unresolved.

facts.label: embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: No included database embedding/reranking model allowance or token-based generation rate found. App-generated embeddings and external model/worker costs are separate from storing/querying vectors.

facts.label: run limits and pricing
facts.value: Not applicable to app job invocation/runtime CPU pricing in the Postgres subscription.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Public account and database creation. Paid service use requires a current valid payment method; major credit/debit cards accepted. An explicit no-card guarantee for creating this Free Postgres database was not established.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Users must be at least 16, able to form a binding contract, and not previously removed. Terms restrict sanctioned parties/regions, listing Crimea, Donetsk, Luhansk, Cuba, Iran, North Korea and Syria, plus other embargoed regions and export-law restrictions.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Free-instance docs say not to use Free for production. Paid resources can be used with a Hobby workspace; Pro is positioned for production teams. Standard public terms prohibit listed Sensitive Data, including health, payment/account, government-ID and GLBA data.

facts.label: primary type and other roles
facts.value: Researcher classification: managed hosted SQL database, with optional vector/geospatial extensions, replicas, high availability and logical replication.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: Database subscription supplies PostgreSQL compute/storage, connection endpoints, metrics, paid PITR/logical exports, optional integrated PgBouncer, and eligible paid replicas/HA. It does not bundle Render web/worker/cron/Workflow compute or S3-style file storage.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Native PostgreSQL clients connect on port 5432 using URL or host/port/user/password/dbname. Internal URL requires the same account and region; external URL supports other hosts. Pooled URLs use port 6432.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: External connections require TLS, minimum TLS 1.2 client support; sslmode=disable is rejected. Internal TLS is optional with self-signed certificates: require works, verify-ca/verify-full do not.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: External access is enabled for all IPs by default (0.0.0.0/0) when valid credentials are supplied. Restrict CIDR blocks or disable external access entirely; same-account/same-region services can still use the internal URL.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Database, replica and backup data are encrypted at rest with AES-256. Public connections use Render-managed TLS certificates. SQL users can be managed through dashboard/API or created directly; only Render-managed credentials appear in dashboard/API.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Credential rotation: create new user, update/redeploy clients, confirm old connections drained, then delete old user. Blueprint references update on next Blueprint sync. Original DB user is deactivated rather than fully dropped to preserve owned objects.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: PostgreSQL row security must be enabled/configured by the app. Table owners normally bypass policies; superusers and BYPASSRLS roles always bypass them. Pro+ offers network-isolated environments; higher workspace roles restrict credential visibility.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: Native PostgreSQL SQL engine. New instances support majors 13–18; CLI default is 18. Majors 11/12 are legacy options only for workspaces with an existing database on the corresponding major; 19 is not yet supported by Render.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: Render applies periodic minor security updates, with advance notification for downtime and maintenance-window controls on paid services. In-place major upgrades target the latest supported major (18), require downtime and may take up to an hour; a new-instance migration can target other supported majors.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: PostgreSQL 18 baseline: native multi-statement transactions; default Read Committed uses a committed snapshot per statement. Repeatable Read and Serializable can be selected; Read Uncommitted behaves as Read Committed. Serializable failures require application retries.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Read replicas and HA standby replicate asynchronously. Replicas can lag; automatic HA failover can lose recent writes, usually no more than a few seconds according to Render. Manual failover can also lose the last few seconds in rare cases.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Full-stack preview environments require Pro+; they create fresh services/datastores/configuration but do not copy database or disk contents. Seed sample data yourself. Resources are billed normally, prorated by the second; close/merge PR deletes the environment.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Preview inactivity expiry is optional and defaults to none. Upgrade testing can clone paid data via PITR from ten minutes earlier, producing a separate temporary database; it does not keep receiving source writes.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: HA requires PostgreSQL 13+ and at least 1 CPU (legacy Pro or higher). Standby has same compute/storage, in the same region but a separate zone. Primary unavailable for 30 seconds triggers automatic failover; endpoint remains the same, connections drop and clients must reconnect.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Up to five read replicas per eligible database; at least 0.5 CPU and 10 GB storage (legacy Standard or higher). Each matches primary compute/storage and is separately billed; connects through its own internal/external URL. Replication lag varies with source load.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Native LISTEN/NOTIFY requires direct connection, not Render's transaction pool. Logical replication is opt-in, Pro+ workspace and at least 10 GB storage, enabled through support; publishers can feed non-Render subscribers.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: An included browser realtime API, durable offline client reads/writes and automatic conflict resolution were not found.

facts.label: extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Extension list includes pgvector, PostGIS, pg_trgm, pg_stat_statements, TimescaleDB, pg_duckdb and others. On PG13+ enable supported extensions with CREATE EXTENSION; plpgsql is on by default. Versions 11/12 use a fixed enabled set.

facts.label: extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Restrictions: pg_duckdb and pg_repack need PG16+; pg_partman needs PG14+, database created after February 5, 2026, and no background worker. TimescaleDB requires creation after January 12, 2023; community features unavailable. pg_similarity unavailable on PG16+.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: Not applicable to native multipart/resumable app-file uploads.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Not applicable to a customer-facing Postgres S3 API.

facts.label: delivery and private files
facts.value: Not applicable to native public/private bucket delivery, signed object URLs, object CDN or file domains.

facts.label: filters and mixed search
facts.value: Upstream pgvector supports exact nearest-neighbor search, HNSW and IVFFlat approximate indexes, SQL filtering, and mixed search with PostgreSQL full-text search. Approximate filters apply after the index scan; tune scans/indexes if too few matches remain.

facts.label: execution model and languages
facts.value: Not applicable to Render Postgres as an arbitrary application worker runtime. Render Workflows, background workers and cron are separate services.

facts.label: delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Not applicable to a native Postgres job-delivery/retry/deduplication contract.

facts.label: schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Not applicable to a bundled durable task queue's schedule, message retention or payload contract.

facts.label: logs and run history
facts.value: Not applicable to a native app-job history/replay feature. Postgres diagnostics and platform logs describe database/platform activity.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Not applicable: Render Postgres is a vendor-managed hosted service, with no reviewed self-hosted Render Postgres edition. Render handles engine infrastructure, minor updates and paid backups; user owns schema, access policy, client reconnection, capacity selection and major-upgrade testing.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Selectable service/database regions: Oregon, Ohio, Virginia (USA), Frankfurt (Germany) and Singapore. Choose during creation; changing an existing database's region requires a new database and data migration. Private networks are separate per region.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: HA standby is in the same region but a separate geographic zone. Physical PITR/logical-export storage locations and a backup-specific residency guarantee were not found. DPA says primary processing operations are in the United States and permits protected transfers.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Paid logical exports download as .dir.tar.gz and can restore through pg_restore to Render or another PostgreSQL host. Free users can run their own pg_dump; plaintext SQL and directory exports are documented. Repeat per database or use pg_dumpall.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Deleting a Postgres instance does not retain its backups or snapshots. Download needed exports first. Terms let users cancel their account and require them to export content before termination; DPA provides return/deletion of personal data with legal/practical exceptions.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Exact account-closure workflow and universal physical purge deadline for database data, backups and legally retained account records were not established.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: All current paid databases have continuous PITR: Hobby workspace past 3 days; Pro/Scale/Enterprise past 7 days. Upgrading workspace extends future history rather than backfilling older data. Free has no provider recovery/backups.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: PITR cannot target the most recent 10 minutes. It creates a new instance, copies the source IP allowlist, and leaves the original available for validation/cutover. User updates connection strings and deletes/suspends the old database.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Paid on-demand logical exports retained 7 days regardless of workspace plan; one export at a time per instance. Download .dir.tar.gz for longer retention and restore with matching PostgreSQL client tools. Free can use client-run pg_dump.

facts.label: file recovery and protection
facts.value: Not applicable to file versioning/locks/object undelete. Database backups and restoration are D05.

facts.label: identity and old names
facts.value: Render Postgres, provided by Render Services, Inc. Official database page: https://render.com/docs/postgresql-creating-connecting . Older material calls it Render PostgreSQL.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: Vendor-operated managed database service subject to Render's service terms. No self-hosted Render Postgres platform edition is offered in the reviewed product docs; upstream PostgreSQL software is a separate product.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Operating with public self-service creation and current paid/free plans. No shutdown, sunset or parent-company acquisition notice found in the official product, pricing, terms, changelog and targeted lifecycle search.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Free database lifetime changed from 90 to 30 days for new databases on May 20, 2024. Compute plans were renamed in August 2026 to spec-based IDs; legacy names remain accepted and corresponding specs/prices are unchanged. These notices do not retire Render Postgres.

facts.label: vendor home and main markets
facts.value: Render Services, Inc.; headquartered in San Francisco, California, USA, with remote team members globally. No complete served-country list established.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: Hobby pricing advertises chat support; support@render.com and the community are public help paths. Platform support is available through the dashboard; docs exclude debugging/tuning an app's own code. Enterprise offers contractual uptime/response commitments; premium support options are separate.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: Public status page: https://status.render.com/ . It reported All Systems Operational at check time.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: A public numeric Hobby/Pro Postgres uptime SLA with service-credit terms was not found.

free.text: Dev cap 20GB/GiB unclear; account may end after 1y idle; prod sleeps at 5m

sql.math: 10 active hours, 1 GiB of storage and 0.1 GiB of assumed PITR (point-in-time recovery) use come to $1.97. The $20 Core credit covers it. Direct database transfer is not priced.
After 5 idle minutes, live-data storage is $0.35. History and backup costs remain. The Core plan's $20 subscription still applies.

files.math: Replit App Storage is separate. This product is a SQL database.

jobs.math: Replit Database does not host job workers

apps.news: News check 2026-11-09: no sale, shutdown, rebrand, or incident found for Replit Database.

facts.label: free offer type
facts.value: Ongoing free development database storage is included with every app. Starter also has monthly cloud credits for production database/storage/publishing and one free published link that expires after 30 days; it can be republished. These are different offers.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: Development storage unit conflict: SQL Database says 20 GB per app, or 50 GB Pro/Enterprise; Usage-based Billing says 20 GiB and 50 GiB. It is a hard cap with no development-storage overages.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: Production storage cap: 1 GiB on Starter, 100 GiB per database on paid plans. Each database has a documented 33 MB base storage footprint even when empty. Development is not billed as production usage.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: Starter's exact monthly cloud-credit amount, database compute-hour allowance, peak connection/CPU/RAM allowance and stable free production total were not found.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: Production compute suspends after 5 idle minutes and wakes on another query; data storage keeps billing. Neon may archive production databases after 24 hours without access; scheduled backups are skipped while archived, resuming at the next daily schedule after a connection wakes it.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: Free account inactive after one year without login can be terminated and its apps/data deleted. Paid subscription accounts are excluded from termination due to account inactivity. Starter's published link separately expires after 30 days.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: Core: $20/month, with $20 monthly credit shown on Pricing; Core docs say monthly credits apply to Agent, publishing, network transfer and database storage. Annual display: $18/month billed annually (our arithmetic: $216/year). No standalone paid SQL-only subscription found.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: Pro starts at $100/month; Pricing displays $90/month billed annually (our arithmetic: $1,080/year), $100 credit tier and higher tiers. Enterprise custom. Pro has up to 15 builders without separate per-user fees, Core up to five collaborators.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: Taxes depend on location. Standard terms allow refund of the latest subscription charge within 30 days, excluding usage billing; Enterprise Agreement says paid amounts non-refundable. Contract applicability matters. An explicit general ISO currency declaration was not found; rates retain '$'.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Post-August 1, 2026 production database rates: $0.16 per compute hour, unchanged; database storage $0.35/GiB-month, down from $1.50. Active time includes requests and the next 5 minutes. Monthly storage uses the maximum account-wide storage during the month.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Additional storage categories: PITR history $0.20/GiB-month; scheduled backup storage $0.09/GiB-month. Longer retention and changed data increase stored history; a new database has base engine storage even when empty.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Pro credit-rollover wording conflicts: Pro docs say unused credits roll for two months; the plan announcement says one month; Publishing Pricing says unused credits do not roll. Purchased credit packs expire after six months, do not auto-renew, and auto-reload is optional.

facts.label: idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Production is serverless: after five minutes idle compute billing pauses until another query. Stored data/history/backups remain separate charges. Monitoring query statistics reset when database suspends/restarts.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: Published-app egress: ingress free; Core includes 100 GiB outgoing transfer, then post-August rate $0.05/GiB. Allowance applies to Static/Autoscale/Reserved VM/Scheduled publishing. Pro allowance is referred to current plan pricing, not enumerated in the checked billing page.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: Database-only external-client response traffic, cross-geography database movement and backup export transfer allowances/rates were not explicitly established.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: Usage limits cap spending beyond monthly credits; usage services block at the limit until raised or the next cycle. A service-shutdown limit suspends services. Limits apply after purchased credit packs; docs suggest $0.01 if usage should stop just beyond purchased credits.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: Exact cap enforcement delay, continued retained-storage billing during a service block, and exhaustive per-meter exclusions were not specified.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Production storage: 100 GiB/database on paid plans, 1 GiB Starter; development hard-cap entitlement is 20 GB/GiB or 50 GB/GiB per app depending on plan, with the documented unit conflict in C10. Storage includes engine/data/history, not just application row payload.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Exact direct/pooled maximum simultaneous connections, CPU/RAM range per database, per-record/statement size, request-rate limits and timeout ceilings were not published in the inspected pages.

facts.label: storage prices
facts.value: Not applicable to database-independent file storage in this SQL record. App Storage is a separate GCS-backed product with separate usage billing.

facts.label: file request and retrieval prices
facts.value: Not applicable to an included SQL-database file upload/read/retrieval operation meter.

facts.label: minimum storage and early deletion
facts.value: Not applicable to object-class minimum retention/early-deletion charges. Production SQL storage high-water billing and backup retention are recorded in C13/D05.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: Vector dimension, record/index/namespace limits are not established because Replit's enabled vector extension/index offering was not found.

facts.label: embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: No included database embedding-generation/reranking allowance, model list or token/request tariff was found. Core's Replit AI Integrations is a separate paid-credit feature.

facts.label: run limits and pricing
facts.value: Not applicable to database-bundled job invocations, execution durations or worker CPU/RAM fees.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Starter is publicly offered at no cost. Paid Core setup asks for payment details. Exact card requirement for activating Starter production database credits was not stated in the reviewed pages.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Minimum age 13; under 18 needs parent/guardian permission. Export/sanctions restrictions apply. Terms prohibit abuse, crypto mining, automated/multiple account evasion and other listed misuse.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Core is positioned for personal/simple builds; Pro for commercial/professional builds. Terms say Pro/Enterprise use the Commercial Agreement, whose link currently redirects to a page titled Enterprise Agreement. Exact Pro contract applicability and a blanket Core commercial-production permission remain unresolved.

facts.label: primary type and other roles
facts.value: Researcher classification: hosted managed PostgreSQL integrated into Replit apps, with isolated development and production environments. Replit Auth/Clerk, App Storage and app deployments are companion platform services.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: Native database features: PostgreSQL, SQL/data editor, production monitoring, separate dev/prod, Agent checkpoint rollback, production PITR/scheduled backups and publish-time schema migration review.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: Companions: Users & Auth offers Replit Auth or Clerk; new Starter/Core/Pro auth defaults to Clerk, Enterprise to Replit Auth. App Storage is a separately metered GCS-backed object service. Published compute has separate deployment meters.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Current Helium development DATABASE_URL is app-scoped and cannot connect from another app or external database viewer. Production connects from PostgreSQL-compatible clients using the production connection string. Development and production each have their own DATABASE_URL value.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Production defaults to direct connections; client frameworks manage their own pools. For Neon production URLs, a pooled endpoint is selected by adding -pooler to the host. Legacy individual PGHOST/PGUSER/PGPASSWORD/PGDATABASE/PGPORT are removed on migration to Helium.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Helium development is private/app-scoped, including against external viewers and other owned apps. Production credentials are bearer secrets and externally usable; keep them server-side. Current Helium does not use SSL locally; production Neon connections use SSL.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Agent reads production through a read-only replica and cannot modify it; owners/editors can manually enable production editing. Publish still applies approved schema migrations to live data. Production credential regeneration invalidates existing URLs immediately and can briefly interrupt a supported deployment.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: PostgreSQL roles/row policies are application configuration. Publishing can migrate RLS policies but not grants, functions or triggers, and does not currently create/change/remove roles. PostgreSQL owners/BYPASSRLS roles can bypass row rules.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: Native PostgreSQL. Infrastructure-upgrade docs identify Helium development as PostgreSQL 16, the same version described for the legacy Neon database. Production docs describe Neon connections; actual account engine/patch versions were not inspected.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: Publishing uses drizzle-kit for supported schema migration. Functions, procedures, triggers, domains and grants do not migrate automatically; role support is limited and Publish does not create/change/remove roles. Manual SQL objects may work in development but be missing in production.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: PostgreSQL 16 baseline has native multi-statement transactions. Default Read Committed reads a committed snapshot per statement; Repeatable Read/Serializable are available; Read Uncommitted acts as Read Committed. Serializable failures need application retry.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Agent's read-only production replica may lag very recent changes. No published Replit-specific synchronous-replication guarantee or zero-loss failover bound was found.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Development and production are separate. Remixing a current Helium app creates a new development database with copied data, unlike the retired shared Neon setup. Publishing applies schema changes through explicit review/validation and approval, not every unsupported SQL object.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Publish validates schema migration on a temporary production copy; optional preview deployment uses that migrated copy and expires after 2 hours. Docs say Databricks Lakebase databases skip validation and require manual SQL review. Preview does not change production data.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: An Agent-facing read replica is documented for production and may lag. The billing page markets fully managed high availability. Configurable app-facing replica counts, region options, independent replica prices, standby topology and automatic failover policy were not found.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: A native client realtime-subscription/offline-sync service, durable offline writes and conflict-resolution behavior were not found for Replit Database.

facts.label: extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: No Replit-specific extension/version catalogue, pgvector/PostGIS availability guarantee or supported specialized-index matrix was found.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: Not applicable to native app-file multipart/resumable uploads in the SQL offer.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Not applicable to an S3-compatible database file endpoint. Native PostgreSQL client access is C08; the separate App Storage product uses GCS/client libraries.

facts.label: delivery and private files
facts.value: Not applicable to SQL-native public/private bucket delivery, signed file links or object CDN configuration.

facts.label: filters and mixed search
facts.value: A supported Replit-specific dense/sparse/hybrid search and filtering contract was not found.

facts.label: execution model and languages
facts.value: Not applicable to Replit Database as an arbitrary-code job runtime. Scheduled/Autoscale/Reserved VM deployments are separate runtime products.

facts.label: delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Not applicable to a native SQL-subscription task delivery/retry/ordering/deduplication service contract.

facts.label: schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Not applicable to an included application queue schedule/message-retention/payload contract. Scheduled daily SQL backups are a data-protection schedule, not an app task queue.

facts.label: logs and run history
facts.value: Not applicable to app-job run history/replay in the SQL product. Production query monitoring is a current snapshot/aggregate statistics and resets on restart/suspend.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Not applicable to a self-hosted Replit Database edition. Replit/underlying provider operate the database; user owns app schema, approved migrations, access policy, budget/retention settings and export of needed data.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Project publishing geographies: North America, Europe (EU), Asia, South America and Australia. Core/Pro/Enterprise can choose; Free defaults to North America. Selection is permanent after publish. Workspace development geography can differ.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Docs say published compute/database/Object Storage are colocated by chosen project geography, but pre-created storage may differ. Exact database region IDs, replica/backup placement and an all-copy residency guarantee were not found; Privacy says services are primarily US-hosted, with other jurisdictions possible.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Data studio exports data to a file; official migration guide uses pg_dump custom archives and pg_restore for SQL export/import. Production supports external native SQL clients; Helium export operations must run from the app environment.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Removing production DB disables access, starts a seven-day soft-delete period, and permits Support recovery within those seven days; then permanently deleted. Pro docs/announcement separately say deleted databases can be recovered up to 28 days, conflicting with that unqualified removal rule.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Account deletion is requested through Settings/account billing on web or mobile; deletion docs say all account content is removed and cannot be recovered. Enterprise agreement allows content migration/request for 30 days after termination; DPA allows personal-data return/deletion requests up to 90 days, with legal retention exceptions.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: An exact universal account/database/backup physical purge deadline and a full downloadable backup-export specification for every recovery type were not found.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Development rollback is on by default: Agent checkpoints up to 7 days restore code, development DB and Agent memory together. It never restores production. No separate charge for development checkpoint rollback.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Production PITR defaults to 7 days and supports second-level timestamps. Every plan can choose 6 h, 12 h, 1/2/5/7 days or Disabled; Pro/Teams/Enterprise can choose 28 days. Downgrading to Core reduces longer retention to 7 days.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: PITR replaces live data in place; app connections reconnect with possible brief interruption. After restoring, you can go earlier but not forward. Code restore and production data restore are separate operations.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Opt-in scheduled backups on Core/Pro/Teams/Enterprise take daily full snapshots while DB is active. Core retention 7 days; Pro/Teams/Enterprise 7/14/28. Schedule near browser midnight uses saved UTC offset, so DST can shift timing. Archives after 24 h inactivity skip daily backups.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Database storage $0.35/GiB-month; PITR history $0.20; scheduled snapshots $0.09. PITR price follows changes/window; scheduled backup storage grows with copies retained. Scheduled restore switches to backup data; recovering pre-restore current data requires Support.

facts.label: file recovery and protection
facts.value: Not applicable to app-file versions/locks/object undelete. SQL backup/restore does not protect separate App Storage objects.

facts.label: identity and old names
facts.value: Replit Database, the built-in managed SQL/PostgreSQL product from Replit, Inc. Official URL: https://replit.com/products/database .

facts.label: identity and old names
facts.value: Historical Repl.it Database was introduced as a key-value store in 2020 with Python/Node/Go and HTTP clients. Current SQL database credentials and quotas must not be assigned to that older key-value API.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: Vendor-hosted service. Current development runs on Replit Helium; production guides describe Neon-backed databases. Replit retains platform rights; no self-hosted Replit Database software edition or license is established.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Current SQL offer is operating with public creation/publishing docs. Legacy shared Neon development databases were scheduled to shut down June 8, 2026; current development/production docs say they were shut down on that date.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Teams plan was sunset into Pro starting March 3, 2026; Core became $20/month. Replit announced acquiring Atta on September 25, 2026. No current SQL-product shutdown or acquisition of Replit itself was found in the bounded official search.

facts.value: The current pricing table lists storage and egress charges but does not state a separate ingress rate or explicit no-ingress-fee rule.

facts.label: Inter-tier or cross-region transfer
facts.value: A separate price for moving data between Standard and Advanced placements or between metadata regions is not stated in current pricing and region docs.

facts.label: Paid project limits
facts.value: The documented Pro Account limits are 3 projects, 100 buckets per project, 25 TB storage per project, 100 TB egress per project, and 100,000,000 segments.

facts.label: API and write rate limits
facts.value: The documented Pro limit is 100 metadata requests per second and one write per second to the same object name.

facts.label: Limit increases and charges
facts.value: Users can request higher storage, egress, project, bucket, and API-rate limits. Incremental storage and egress are billed at the normal usage rates; the docs warn that a higher segment limit may incur a segment fee.

facts.label: Spend caps and budget alerts
facts.value: The pricing and billing pages show estimated charges and account balance, but no hard spend cap or automatic budget-alert threshold is documented in the pages checked.

facts.label: Standard storage price
facts.value: Standard storage: $7 USD/TB-month; globally distributed storage placement.

facts.label: Advanced storage price
facts.value: Advanced storage: $10 USD/TB-month; regionally placed, with the current product page naming U.S. SOC 2 Type 2 data centers.

facts.label: Storage class model
facts.value: Current Standard and Advanced plans are placement/compliance tiers, not hot, cool, or archive classes. The former Active Archive tier was mapped to Standard in the July 2026 transition.

facts.label: Billing units and tax
facts.value: Storage is measured hourly, totaled by tier, rounded to whole GB, and billed in decimal GB-months. Display currency is USD; U.S. sales tax may apply where Storj has business nexus.

facts.label: Request charges
facts.value: Storj says its current plans have no API request fees.

facts.label: Operation pricing schedule
facts.value: No separate per-operation schedule for PUT, GET, LIST, multipart parts, or deletes is published for current Standard and Advanced tiers.

facts.label: Segment-fee exception
facts.value: Current pricing says segment fees are removed for new tiers, while the limit-increase guide says a higher segment limit may incur fees for segments above the default.

facts.label: Minimum billable object size
facts.value: Objects below 50 KB are billed as 50 KB under current Standard and Advanced pricing.

facts.label: Minimum storage duration
facts.value: Current July 2026 pricing docs and customer FAQ say objects deleted before 30 days are billed for the remainder of the 30-day period at the tier's storage rate. Object Mount users are exempt.

facts.label: Minimum account charge
facts.value: Active Standard or Advanced storage accounts have a $5 monthly invoice floor. It is not a storage credit and does not buy extra capacity.

facts.label: Account and trial access
facts.value: A Storj account is required for account services. The Object Storage trial is listed as 30 days, works with S3-compatible apps, and does not require a credit card.

facts.label: Minimum user age
facts.value: Terms of Use require users to be at least 18 years old.

facts.label: Sanctions and country eligibility
facts.value: Terms prohibit use in U.S.-embargoed jurisdictions and use that violates applicable export controls or sanctions. A complete country-by-country signup availability list was not found.

facts.label: Commercial-use terms
facts.value: The service terms describe customer applications built using the Storage Services and do not state that Object Storage is limited to personal or non-commercial use. The free-trial page does not separately define production-use eligibility.

facts.label: Primary type
facts.value: Hosted distributed cloud object storage, with bucket and object access through S3-compatible APIs.

facts.label: Other roles and scope
facts.value: The service can hold app uploads, archives, media, and backups. This record covers Object Storage, not the separate Object Mount desktop product or Storj Cloud Compute.

facts.label: Included storage service
facts.value: Core service is storing, listing, retrieving, and deleting objects in buckets through the hosted Storj network and S3-compatible gateway.

facts.label: Other backend features
facts.value: The Object Storage pages and developer docs do not list a managed relational database, user identity service for app end users, serverless functions, or job runner as included features.

facts.label: Object Mount inclusion
facts.value: Every Storj Object Storage account includes two Object Mount licenses at no extra charge. Object Mount is a separate filesystem access product; its extra storage or paid licenses are not counted as Object Storage plan quotas here.

facts.label: Main data API
facts.value: The hosted gateway exposes a RESTful API compatible with the basic S3 object-access model; users provide an endpoint, access key, and secret key to S3 clients.

facts.label: Storj client options
facts.value: Official docs describe the Uplink CLI, libuplink client library, hosted Gateway-MT, and self-hosted Gateway-ST.

facts.label: SDK and language connection
facts.value: The S3 interface can be used with S3-compatible SDKs; official examples include Python with boto3 and an AWS-compatible endpoint configuration.

facts.label: Other integrations
facts.value: Storj publishes connection guides for backup, file-management, content-delivery, and cloud-ops tools, including Rclone, Restic, Duplicati, and FileZilla.

facts.label: Browser and web access
facts.value: S3 presigned URLs can allow unauthenticated uploads or downloads. Storj Linksharing can create browser links, including links with a configurable end date and static-site hosting.

facts.label: Default object privacy
facts.value: Storj says objects and paths are private and encrypted by default. Presigned links can grant unauthenticated access to a selected object.

facts.label: Access grants and S3 credentials
facts.value: An Access Grant carries a satellite address, restricted API key, and path-based encryption key. Storj can create S3 credentials from a grant.

facts.label: Permission scope
facts.value: Grants can restrict read, write, list, and delete permissions, selected buckets or paths, and an expiration.

facts.label: Encryption boundary
facts.value: Storj states stored customer material is encrypted and node operators cannot read its contents. With its hosted Gateway-MT, encryption is performed server-side by Storj's gateway; Uplink and self-hosted Gateway-ST manage encryption keys client-side.

facts.label: Passphrase custody
facts.value: Storj's access-grant documentation says encryption passphrases are not stored by Storj. Losing the passphrase can make existing data unrecoverable, even if an access grant remains.

facts.label: Object Lock permissions
facts.value: S3 credentials can be scoped for Object Lock actions. Storj warns that default owners have governance-bypass permissions and says it does not currently support role-based access controls for default restrictions.

facts.label: Private network access
facts.value: The product, access, and S3-gateway docs checked do not specify a private endpoint, VPC peering, or IP allowlist feature for Object Storage.

facts.label: Object size
facts.value: Storj's S3 compatibility limits table lists no maximum object size or maximum PUT-operation size.

facts.label: Multipart and resumable upload
facts.value: Multipart uploads can be split into parallel parts, paused, resumed, or retried part-by-part. The S3 compatibility table lists up to 10,000 parts, each at least 5 MiB except the final part, which can be 0 B.

facts.label: Bucket and listing limits
facts.value: The Pro limit is 100 buckets per project. S3 listings return up to 1,000 objects per request; bucket names are 3 to 63 characters.

facts.label: Copy size and metadata
facts.value: CopyObject is limited to approximately 671 GB. The compatibility table lists a maximum encrypted object-key length of 1,280 characters and 2 KiB of metadata.

facts.label: S3-compatible API coverage
facts.value: Storj supports basic S3 bucket and object calls, including create/delete bucket, put/get/head/delete object, multipart upload, tags, versioning, and object lock.

facts.label: Unsupported S3 operations
facts.value: The matrix lists bucket CORS, lifecycle rules, ACLs, public-access-block, bucket policies, replication, website hosting, analytics, inventory, restore, and Select as unsupported or unavailable.

facts.label: Partial compatibility caveats
facts.value: GetObject does not support partNumber; list calls have partial compatibility and encrypted-key ordering caveats; listing multipart uploads has prefix and marker limitations.

facts.label: Private objects and temporary links
facts.value: Objects are private by default. S3 presigned URLs can grant temporary unauthenticated GET or PUT access to a specific object.

facts.label: Linksharing and static sites
facts.value: Storj Linksharing supports configurable or perpetual share links; the docs also describe hosting a static site through Linksharing.

facts.label: Secure custom domains
facts.value: The documented Pro account limits include secure HTTPS custom domains for Linksharing. The free-trial pricing page does not state that custom domains are included in the trial.

facts.label: Built-in CDN
facts.value: The product pages describe distributed storage as useful for CDN-origin workloads, but the Object Storage pricing and docs do not list a bundled CDN service or its delivery pricing.

facts.label: Standard data placement
facts.value: Standard is globally distributed across many storage locations; it is priced at the global Standard rate. The page does not promise a single country for each stored object's pieces.

facts.label: Advanced data placement
facts.value: Advanced is regionally placed in U.S. SOC 2 Type 2 compliant data centers at the current published $10/TB-month storage rate.

facts.label: Tier choice by project
facts.value: New projects use either Standard global placement or Advanced regional placement; the current FAQ says a new project cannot mix those placements. Existing mixed projects remain supported and bill per bucket.

facts.label: Metadata regions
facts.value: Storj documents US1, EU1, and AP1 as metadata-region satellites. Object data is stored across globally distributed nodes, so choosing a metadata region does not by itself mean all object pieces stay in that region.

facts.label: Other regional residency options
facts.value: Current pricing identifies global Standard and U.S. Advanced. The older preferred-region guide describes requesting EU, US, or AP placement through support, but the current plan pages do not confirm those as available Advanced data-residency choices.

facts.label: Export and migration
facts.value: Objects can be copied or retrieved through S3-compatible clients, Uplink CLI, and documented third-party tools such as Rclone and Restic.

facts.label: Account closure steps
facts.value: Storj's closure guide says to delete all objects and buckets, remove Access Grants, delete projects, then delete the account. The terms also require removing stored materials before customer termination.

facts.label: Data removal timing
facts.value: A fixed time for physical removal of every object piece or backup copy after bucket/account deletion was not found in the closure guide, terms, or privacy policy checked.

facts.label: Customer backup responsibility
facts.value: The terms say Stored Materials may not be available or retrievable at any time and require customers to keep backup copies.

facts.label: Object versioning and recovery
facts.value: S3-compatible versioning preserves earlier object versions and delete markers so users can retrieve or restore a prior version. Each stored version adds to metered storage.

facts.label: Object Lock and legal hold
facts.value: Storj documents governance mode, compliance mode, and legal hold. Governance bypass permissions are available by default to account owners unless credentials are restricted.

facts.label: Distributed redundancy
facts.value: Storj describes a network design using encryption, segmentation, erasure coding, geographically distributed nodes, and repair when redundancy falls. All current tiers are designed for 99.999999999% durability.

facts.label: Durability and retrieval caveat
facts.value: The service terms disclaim guaranteed on-demand availability or retrieval and require customers to maintain backups. Storage availability is separately covered by the contractual SLA.

facts.label: Separate backup schedule
facts.value: The checked Object Storage price and product docs do not publish a customer-configurable backup schedule or point-in-time restore for buckets.

facts.label: Identity
facts.value: Storj Object Storage, offered by Storj. Official home: https://www.storj.io/.

facts.label: Product terminology
facts.value: Current product pages say “Object Storage”; the developer docs also use “Storj DCS” and “distributed cloud storage.”

facts.label: Hosting model
facts.value: Hosted storage service. Storj operates the account, metadata, gateway, billing, and network services; customer data is placed on third-party storage nodes in Storj's network.

facts.label: Self-hosting boundary
facts.value: Storj documents a self-hosted S3 Gateway-ST, but it connects to the Storj network. The hosted Object Storage network itself is not offered as a self-hosted edition in the product pages checked.

facts.label: Product license
facts.value: Not applicable as a software license: Object Storage is a hosted service governed by Storj's service terms. Gateway and client software are connection tools, not an alternate license for this hosted service.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Current pricing lists a 30-day Object Storage trial and Standard and Advanced paid plans. The official status page showed all listed systems operational on the checked date.

facts.label: Acquisition
facts.value: Inveniam announced an acquisition agreement in October 2025. Storj's July 2026 restructuring announcement later refers to Inveniam “since acquiring Storj,” confirming completion by that update.

facts.label: Financial restructuring and continuity
facts.value: Storj Labs, Inc. filed Chapter 11 on July 26, 2026. Storj said the filing was intended to resolve legacy liabilities while it continued normal operations; its FAQ says it is not shutting down.

facts.label: Shutdown or sunset notices
facts.value: No shutdown or sunset announcement was found in the official blog, current news-and-events page, or the July restructuring posts checked.

facts.label: Current status snapshot
facts.value: All systems shown on the public status page, including AP1, EU1, US1, gateways, APIs, billing, and web console, were marked operational; no incident was listed for November 6, 2026.

facts.label: Vendor location
facts.value: Storj's service terms give a legal-notice address in Atlanta, Georgia, United States. The pages checked do not establish that address as the company's headquarters or state its primary customer market.

facts.label: Support paths
facts.value: Storj lists support through its customer portal, email, and community forum.

facts.label: Support-plan inclusion
facts.value: The terms tie support to the Support Period stated in an order or customer agreement; the public pricing page does not say which support response tier is included with a standard trial or plan.

facts.label: Contractual availability
facts.value: Terms state 99.95% availability for Storage Services and 99.9% for Edge Services, excluding scheduled maintenance and listed causes. Storage credits are 5% when below 99.95% but above 99.0%, and 10% below 99.0%, subject to claim rules.

facts.label: Public status page
facts.value: Storj has a public status dashboard for its metadata regions, API, billing, web console, linksharing, and gateway services. It showed all systems operational on the checked date.
