status.text: India access block 2026-02-24 to 2026-03-03 over one misused project

facts.label: Free offer type
facts.value: Hosted Free is a recurring allowance, not time-limited credit; two active free projects. Supabase source can also be self-hosted without a software subscription.

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: Hosted Free, per project: 500MB database allowance; shared CPU and about 500MB RAM. Two active free projects counted across organizations where the user is Owner/Admin; paused projects excluded.

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: Hosted Free, organization usage: 50,000 MAU and 50,000 third-party MAU, 1GB files, 5GB uncached egress plus separate 5GB cached egress, 500,000 function invocations, 2M realtime messages and 200 realtime peak connections.

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: Hosted Free: unlimited dashboard team members; 100 deployed Edge Functions/project; 50MB maximum file; basic CDN; one-day API/database logs, one-hour Auth audit logs; no managed automatic backup/PITR.

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: Hosted Free upcoming logs allowance: 1GB ingest and 100GB query scanning. Logs billing/enforcement is in a soft-launch grace period.

facts.label: Inactivity, pause and deletion
facts.value: Hosted Free: low database activity over seven days may cause pause; warning and confirmation emails; resume on platform within one year after pausing.

facts.label: Inactivity, pause and deletion
facts.value: Hosted paid projects cannot be paused and do not auto-pause for inactivity; to pause, transfer to a Free organization first, subject to Free eligibility/limits.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: Hosted Pro: USD $25/organization/month, charged upfront, plus compute and overages; $10 monthly primary-compute credit can cover one Micro project.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: Hosted Team: from USD $599/organization/month, plus compute/overages; same $10 organization primary-compute credit.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: Self-host: no mandatory Supabase cloud subscription for running open components. Hardware, storage, network, monitoring and provider accounts separate.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Hosted compute billed in full hours even for part-hour segments; Micro $0.01344/hour (about $10/month), Small $0.0206/hour (about $15/month). Primary compute credit $10/month resets; no accumulation.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Hosted primary gp3 disk: 8GB included/project, extra provisioned disk $0.000171/GB-hour ($0.125/GB-month). io2 disk $0.000267/GB-hour ($0.195/GB-month), billed from first provisioned byte.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Hosted Pro/Team Auth: 100,000 MAU included, then $0.00325/MAU. Third-party MAU has separate 100,000 allowance; SAML SSO 50 included, then $0.015/MAU.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Hosted Pro/Team realtime: 5M messages included, then $2.50 per whole 1M overage block; 500 included peak connections, then $10 per whole 1,000 block.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Hosted add-ons: custom domain $10/domain/project/month; IPv4 separately priced; PITR separately priced; logs drains from $60/drain/project/month plus events and egress.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Self-host: no Supabase per-MAU/invocation/GB cloud meter; chosen infrastructure and external services determine charges.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Hosted IPv4 add-on: $0.0055/hour/address, billed in whole hours; roughly $4/month/address. Not covered by Spend Cap.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Hosted provisioned gp3 above included performance: $0.024 per additional IOPS/month and $0.095 per additional MB/s/month; base 3,000 IOPS and 125MB/s included.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Hosted database compute does not automatically scale to zero: provisioned paid instance charged regardless of usage. Paused Free projects do not accrue compute, but paid projects cannot pause in place.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Self-host: process/container stop and wake are operator-controlled; persistent disk/backups and server allocation may keep billing.

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: Hosted Free: separate 5GB uncached and 5GB cached egress allowances. Pro/Team: separate 250GB each; overage $0.09/GB uncached, $0.03/GB cached.

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: Self-host network/remote-bucket/cross-region prices depend on operator/provider. No cloud egress allowance or rate inherited.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: Hosted direct-billed Pro Spend Cap on by default; Free not charged for overage. Cap only applies to covered usage, not a configurable universal dollar budget.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: Spend Cap excludes compute, branch/replica compute, custom domains, extra disk IOPS/throughput, IPv4, log drains, phone MFA and PITR.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: Exceeding quota can trigger notification/grace, then organization-wide restrictions: pause/read-only/blocked launches or HTTP 402. Grace does not automatically renew after dropping under quota.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Hosted Free: 500MB database quota is distinct from fixed 2GB physical disk. Disk at 95% triggers best-effort read-only mode; full disk can shut down Postgres until upgrade/restart.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Pricing/billing label database allowance per project; database-size guide describes organization-summed, average-daily fair-use evaluation. Effective threshold across two free projects not fully reconciled.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Hosted Free Nano and paid Micro: 60 direct database / 200 pooler client connections. Micro 1GB RAM; Small 90/400 and 2GB RAM.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Hosted gp3 provisioned disk up to 64TB; io2 up to 60TB, subject to compute/disk performance constraints. Micro's recommended DB size is 10GB, not a hard storage entitlement.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: General database-size guide says Pro/Team maximum 60TB; advanced compute/pricing tables distinguish gp3 up to 64TB and io2 up to 60TB.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Data API select returns at most 1,000 rows by default; configurable API setting, with range pagination available.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: No Supabase-wide numeric SQL row/document byte maximum established in the inspected capacity, connection, API and terms/policy pages.

facts.label: Storage prices
facts.value: Hosted Free: 1GB file storage included; no paid overage option on Free. Storage table expresses the allowance as 744 GB-hours.

facts.label: Storage prices
facts.value: Hosted Pro and Team: 100GB files included per organization; published quota 74,400 GB-hours; excess $0.00002919/GB-hour ($0.0213/GB-month).

facts.label: Storage prices
facts.value: Hosted Enterprise file-storage allowance and overage price custom.

facts.label: Storage prices
facts.value: General billing overview lists $0.021/GB overage; dedicated Storage pricing, storage-size usage guide and pricing page list $0.0213/GB-month.

facts.label: Storage prices
facts.value: Self-host file storage: local filesystem by default, or an S3-compatible backend; infrastructure/provider storage costs apply.

facts.label: File request and retrieval prices
facts.value: Separate standard upload/GET/list/delete request charges and archive-retrieval rates were not found in the inspected hosted price schedules.

facts.label: File request and retrieval prices
facts.value: Hosted Pro/Team image transformations: 100 distinct origin images included per cycle, then $5 per whole 1,000 excess origin images, rounded up.

facts.label: Minimum storage and early deletion
facts.value: No explicit minimum billed object size, minimum retention duration or early-deletion charge schedule found for ordinary hosted file buckets.

facts.label: Vector/index limits
facts.value: Postgres pgvector HNSW: vector up to 2,000 dimensions, halfvec up to 4,000 and bit up to 64,000 in documented versions. The 1,536-float32 scenario fits vector dimension support.

facts.label: Vector/index limits
facts.value: Hosted Vector Buckets: Public Alpha on Pro and above, temporarily free alpha usage subject to fair use; normal egress charges still apply. Available in us-east-1, us-east-2, us-west-2, eu-central-1 and ap-southeast-2.

facts.label: Vector/index limits
facts.value: Vector Buckets alpha defaults: 10 buckets/project, 10 indexes/bucket, maximum 4,096 float32 dimensions. Hosted backend Amazon S3 Vectors; local development backend pgvector.

facts.label: Vector/index limits
facts.value: Vector Bucket insert/update maximum differs: limits table says 1,000 vectors/request; introduction/storing guide examples say 500/request.

facts.label: Vector/index limits
facts.value: Vector Bucket total record limit and exact metadata bytes/keys limits not found in the inspected Supabase pages.

facts.label: Embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: Official Edge Function example runs built-in gte-small embeddings with 384 dimensions through Supabase.ai.Session; function execution/invocation limits still apply.

facts.label: Embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: Automatic embeddings recipe uses external OpenAI API plus pgmq, Cron and Edge Functions; external model account, tokens and charges separate from database storage/search.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Hosted all plans: maximum memory 256MB; maximum CPU time 2 seconds/request excluding asynchronous I/O; request idle timeout 150 seconds.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Hosted Free: worker wall lifetime up to 150 seconds; 100 deployed functions/project.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Hosted Pro: worker wall lifetime up to 400 seconds; 1,000 deployed functions/project.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Hosted Team: worker wall lifetime up to 400 seconds; 2,000 deployed functions/project.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Hosted Enterprise: worker wall lifetime up to 400 seconds; unlimited deployed function count.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Hosted Free includes 500,000 invocations/month; Pro/Team 2M, then $2 per whole 1M excess invocations, rounded up. Any response status counts; OPTIONS requests excluded.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Self-host Edge Functions default overall container memory budget 2GiB; default per-worker 256MiB is configurable. Operator infrastructure bill replaces cloud invocation pricing.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Hosted self-service Free access and paid upgrades advertised; invoices USD; normal paid payment route credit card, with larger upfront-payment alternatives by support.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Full country eligibility and an explicit universal no-card condition for Free were not established in the inspected official sources.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Cloud terms require lawful use, ability to enter the agreement and export-control compliance; protected health information requires a BAA, payment-cardholder data requires prior written approval. Privacy says service not intended for under-13s.

facts.label: Primary type and other roles
facts.value: Backend platform (our classification): PostgreSQL, Auth, file storage, realtime, REST/GraphQL, Edge Functions, pgvector, Cron and Queues.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Hosted native Postgres, email/password/passwordless/social/mobile Auth, RLS, object storage/CDN, realtime, Deno functions, Cron and pgmq queues. Additional email/SMS/model providers may be required.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Self-host single project includes core APIs/Auth/Postgres/Storage/Realtime/functions; lacks managed branching, advanced metrics, managed backups/PITR, analytics/vector buckets, ETL and Management API.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Hosted Postgres direct connection, shared Supavisor session/transaction pooler and paid dedicated PgBouncer pooler; REST/GraphQL and client libraries.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Client library entry points: JavaScript, Flutter/Dart, Python, C#, Swift and Kotlin. Current changelog also marks .NET officially supported and Go public alpha.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Database grants plus Postgres row-level security (RLS) restrict access. Enable RLS on exposed schemas; dashboard-created tables and SQL-created tables can differ in defaults.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Publishable keys for shipped clients; secret keys only on trusted backend, bypass RLS. Legacy anon/service_role key deprecation announced for end of 2026; adding new keys does not revoke old ones.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Hosted database network allowlists cover direct Postgres/pooler only, not HTTPS Auth/Storage/PostgREST APIs; credentials still required. Team adds project-scoped/read-only platform roles and dashboard SSO.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Self-host: configure keys/secrets, firewall, HTTPS reverse proxy and Studio basic-auth password; operator hardens all services. Do not use sample default credentials.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: Hosted standard mode is a full PostgreSQL database per project: native SQL/relational tables, JSON/JSONB, functions and extensions; REST via PostgREST, GraphQL interface and native Postgres clients.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: OrioleDB Public Beta remains Postgres with alternative storage engine; same SQL, Auth/RLS and client libraries, but separate extension/index/recovery limitations.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: Self-host uses Supabase Postgres image with extension/services stack under operator upgrade control. Cloud OrioleDB option not in the full self-hosted stack.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: Native SQL transactions available; PostgREST runs a request inside a database transaction. Separate supabase-js queries are not automatically one transaction; multi-statement atomic work uses an RPC database function.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: Read replicas use asynchronous replication and can lag behind primary; immediate read-after-write should not be assumed when routed to a replica.

facts.label: Test environments and branches
facts.value: Hosted paid branches are isolated Supabase environments, normally data-less: schema built from migrations, deployed functions/settings copied, Auth secrets replaced with placeholders. Preview branches deleted when PR closes/merges; persistent branches remain.

facts.label: Test environments and branches
facts.value: Hosted branch compute starts $0.01344/hour on Micro; disk, storage and egress extra at normal meters. No primary-compute credits and no Spend Cap coverage for branch compute.

facts.label: Test environments and branches
facts.value: Self-host: no managed branching. CLI local stack supports development/testing; separate Docker deployments can be operated for staging/production at own cost.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Hosted read replicas are read-only cross-region databases with dedicated endpoints and API geo-routing; Auth, Storage and Realtime still use primary paths.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Replica same compute shape as primary; extra disk 1.25× primary disk, billed from first byte; extra IOPS/throughput/IPv4 may apply. No primary-compute credit or Spend Cap protection.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Automatic multi-node consensus/failover appears in selected paid Multigres Private Alpha only; no PITR/Realtime/cross-region replica support there. Self-host HA operator-managed.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Native realtime WebSocket Broadcast, Presence and Postgres Changes. Free 200 concurrent connections/100 messages per second; capped Pro 500/500; uncapped Pro/Team default 10,000/2,500.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Broadcast replay only for private channels and database-published broadcasts, maximum 25 messages per request. Daily partitions retain at least 72h and at most four days; general realtime delivery not guaranteed.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Native complete offline read/write synchronization and conflict resolution not established in the searched core realtime/SDK/terms/policy pages.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Broadcast replay page states a 25-message maximum, while its Python example requests 100 messages.

facts.label: Extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Postgres extension framework, pgvector HNSW/IVFFlat, ordinary SQL indexes and full-text search available; supported versions depend on project upgrade. Self-host may build/configure its own extensions.

facts.label: Upload and file limits
facts.value: Hosted Free global maximum file size 50MB; configurable bucket limits and allowed MIME types can be lower.

facts.label: Upload and file limits
facts.value: Hosted Pro/Team maximum configurable file size up to 500GB; global and bucket-specific limits remain enforced.

facts.label: Upload and file limits
facts.value: Standard multipart/form-data uploads support up to 5GB, recommended only for files no larger than 6MB; resumable TUS recommended above 6MB. S3 single/multipart uploads support up to 500GB on paid plans.

facts.label: Upload and file limits
facts.value: Self-host upload/storage limits are deployment settings, constrained by local disk, proxy and external bucket; cloud plan file caps are not a self-host entitlement.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Hosted Storage exposes native REST/client APIs, TUS resumable uploads and a partially compatible S3 API.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: S3 matrix lacks bucket versioning, lifecycle configuration, Object Lock create option and S3 encryption/CORS configuration endpoints.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Self-host S3 protocol endpoint and optional S3 storage backend are independent settings; endpoint can serve objects stored on the local filesystem.

facts.label: Delivery and private files
facts.value: Private buckets are the default: downloads need JWT/RLS authorization or a time-limited signed URL. Public bucket downloads bypass read checks; writes, listing, moving and copying retain access checks.

facts.label: Delivery and private files
facts.value: Hosted Free basic CDN; Pro/Team Smart CDN included. Smart CDN update/delete invalidation can take up to 60 seconds, while browser caches can persist separately.

facts.label: Delivery and private files
facts.value: Smart CDN signed URLs have separate cache entries per token; a cached signed URL can remain usable after its token expires until its cache entry expires.

facts.label: Delivery and private files
facts.value: Hosted custom project domains are a paid add-on, $10/domain/project/month; normal project URLs and CDN delivery remain available without it. Self-host domains/TLS/CDN operator-managed.

facts.label: Filters and mixed search
facts.value: Postgres hybrid search combines full-text tsvector/tsquery with pgvector and reciprocal rank fusion in a SQL function; ordinary SQL predicates and RLS can enforce tenant filters.

facts.label: Filters and mixed search
facts.value: Vector Buckets support dense similarity search with metadata filters, hosted topK up to 10,000, pages at most 100 results using nextToken; local topK at most 100 without query pagination.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: Hosted Edge Functions run server-side TypeScript/JavaScript on a Deno-based runtime, with supported npm/WASM modules and geographically routed HTTP execution.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: Cron executes SQL/database functions or invokes HTTP endpoints; Queues persist JSONB messages in Postgres for a consumer to process. Queue storage alone is not managed arbitrary worker compute.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: Self-host includes an Edge Runtime service and deployable function source; operator supplies containers, resources, deployment and restart policy.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Logged pgmq queues persist messages; read makes a message invisible for a configurable number of seconds, then visible again unless deleted/archived.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: pgmq pop deletes on read and can produce at-most-once processing after a worker failure; unlogged queues explicitly trade durability for write throughput.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Background waitUntil work shares worker wall/CPU limits; it does not itself create durable retry/replay semantics.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: No universal built-in retry count/backoff, automatic dead-letter policy, end-to-end deduplication window or complete processing-order guarantee found for the combined queue/function workflow.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Cron schedules from every second to annually; official guidance recommends no more than eight concurrent jobs and jobs no longer than ten minutes.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: pgmq send/send_batch support integer-second delay, default zero. Messages remain until explicitly deleted/archived; archives support long-term retention/replay and consume database space.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: No dedicated maximum queue-payload bytes, maximum delay or fixed hosted queue retention TTL found in inspected Supabase queue pages.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Hosted Free API/database logs retained one day; Auth audit logs one hour.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Hosted Pro API/database logs retained seven days; Auth audit logs seven days.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Hosted Team API/database and Auth audit logs retained 28 days.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Hosted Enterprise API/database logs retained 90 days on public comparison; Auth audit feature included but a numeric Enterprise Auth retention not stated there.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Announced logs pricing: Free 1GB ingest, Pro/Team 20GB organization allowance then $0.50/GB; query scanning not separately billed, starting allowance 100× ingest allowance.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Cron stores run status in cron.job_run_details; queue archive stores messages for inspection/replay. Self-host default stack does not enable vendor log analytics; optional logging services operator-managed.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Fixed default Cron run-history purge age or a universal self-host log retention period not found in the inspected pages.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Production Docker prerequisites: minimum 4GB RAM, two CPU cores and 40GB SSD; recommended 8GB+ RAM, four+ cores and 80GB+ SSD; Docker/Compose, configured keys and external HTTPS access.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Operator owns OS/container upgrades, secrets, networking/TLS, SMTP, monitoring, database/object backups, recovery and availability. Current default API gateway Envoy; optional log analytics adds services/resources.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Self-host Studio manages one project; no hosted branching, managed backups/PITR, advanced platform metrics, analytics/vector buckets, ETL or Management API.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Hosted primary region selectable at creation: us-west-1, us-west-2, us-east-1, us-east-2, ca-central-1, eu-west-1, eu-west-2, eu-west-3, eu-central-1, eu-central-2, eu-north-1, ap-south-1, ap-southeast-1, ap-northeast-1, ap-northeast-2, ap-southeast-2, sa-east-1.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Hosted database/Auth/Storage objects/backups in selected region; account/control data, support access, usage information and logs can be processed elsewhere.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Hosted Edge Functions default to region closest to caller; region can be forced by x-region/client option. Explicit region selection disables automatic failover routing to other regions.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Self-host: choose server, database, file/S3 and backup locations yourself; no hosted AWS region restriction is imposed by deployment guide.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Hosted portable SQL schema/data/roles exports through CLI/pg_dump; migrations/restore guides available. Storage binaries and Edge Function source/config must be exported separately.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Hosted project deletion is irreversible: database/Auth, Storage, functions/config and backups removed from recoverable project access; export first. Billing stops for project, prior usage stays counted.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: DPA provides a request/download opportunity within 30 days of agreement expiry, followed by deletion of covered copies; Privacy allows purpose/legal retention of account information.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Self-host: own database dumps, local/S3 files, function code, configuration and encryption secrets remain under operator control; deletion/backup purge timing operator-defined.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Hosted Free: no managed daily backups or PITR; official recommendation is regular CLI export and off-site copies.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Hosted Pro: daily database backups retained seven days.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Hosted Team: daily database backups retained 14 days.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Hosted Enterprise: daily database backups retained up to 30 days.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Hosted standard Postgres paid PITR requires at least Small compute. Retention 7/14/28 days costs $0.137/$0.274/$0.55 per hour (about $100/$200/$400 monthly).

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Database backups exclude Storage file binaries. Newer projects use physical backups, not directly downloadable; CLI/pg_dump produces portable logical exports.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Self-host backups/PITR/restore are operator-run; update.sh backs up configuration, not Postgres or Storage data.

facts.label: File recovery and protection
facts.value: Deleting Storage objects is permanent and not recoverable through the Storage API; S3 object versioning and Object Lock are not supplied by its compatibility matrix.

facts.label: File recovery and protection
facts.value: Hosted database daily backups/PITR cover storage metadata, not file binaries; restore cannot recover deleted file contents.

facts.label: File recovery and protection
facts.value: Self-host file recovery depends on operator snapshots/backups or the chosen external bucket’s protection settings. Supabase update.sh does not back up file contents.

facts.label: Identity and old names
facts.value: Supabase, at supabase.com; hosted backend platform and separately deployable open source components.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Hosted Free/Pro/Team/Enterprise governed by service terms; underlying open source software does not license the hosted management service.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Self-hosted Docker deployment supported. Main Supabase repository, Storage and Realtime licenses: Apache-2.0; Auth and Edge Runtime: MIT.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Hosted platform active; public pricing and continuously updated docs/changelog. Feature maturity differs by component.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: OrioleDB option: Public Beta from 2026-10-01, including paid plans at standard Postgres pricing; not recommended for production, no SLA. New beta projects use OrioleDB beta18/Postgres 17.11.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Multigres multi-AZ high availability: Private Alpha for selected paid organizations; not a general production entitlement or uptime-SLA feature.

facts.label: Vendor home and main markets
facts.value: Default cloud contracting entity Supabase Pte. Ltd., Singapore; AWS Marketplace purchases default to Supabase, Inc., Delaware, US, unless an Order says otherwise.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Hosted Free: community technical support; billing/account support available to all via official channels.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Hosted Pro: email/ticket technical support, no promised initial response SLA or uptime SLA.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Hosted Team: priority support with initial response targets: urgent 24h 24/7; high/normal one business day; low two business days. No standard Team uptime SLA.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Hosted Enterprise: 99.9% monthly uptime commitment for covered GA services, subject to product scope, dependencies and exclusions. Credits require a claim within 30 days after affected month.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Self-host community support, no managed uptime/backup/support SLA inherited. Hosted public status at status.supabase.com.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Supabase hosted access in India was restricted on 2026-02-24 under a MeitY Section 69A blocking order tied to third-party misuse of one hosted project. Supabase says it disabled that project, the order was rescinded, and access was restored on 2026-03-03; it reported no systemic service vulnerability. The official status incident URL could not be fetched in this check; the company blog gives the dates and explanation.

apps.name: SurrealDB
apps.line: Multi-model database with auth, file buckets, functions, and vector indexes.

free.text: Earth Free: 3M units, 10GB, 100h/mo; pauses at quota until next month

cells.regions: AWS and Azure regions; region locked at creation
cells.selfhost: Yes, BSL 1.1; service-hosting rights are restricted

sql.math: $98.55 for compute + $0.36 for egress. Disk, backup and tax costs are still unknown.
A manual pause keeps the data and stops instance usage charges, but the database address (endpoint) is unavailable.

files.math: File buckets are included, but their storage price is unclear. Earth Pro's $33.75 applies only if its database usage charge applies.

jobs.math: Jobs use database capacity. No separate worker price exists, and whether five jobs running at once fit, and the total, are unknown.

facts.label: free offer type
facts.value: Self-hosted: no hosted allowance or time-limited trial is needed for permitted core use; you supply infrastructure. Earth Free and Cloud Free are distinct recurring hosted free offers.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: Earth Free: 3M request units/month, 10 GB storage and 100 active hours/month shared by the organisation; up to 100 instances, 100 connected clients per instance and 100 cells per instance.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: Cloud Free single node: 0.25 vCPU, 1 GB fixed storage, $0. Pricing lists 1 GB RAM; scaling docs list 512 MB RAM.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: Cloud Free automatically pauses after seven days without use. Manual pause retains data/configuration; resume keeps the endpoint. Deleting an instance is irreversible.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: Earth Free pauses the organisation's Earth instances when the shared allowance is spent, keeps data, and resumes eligibility at the next month's allowance. A Pro upgrade avoids that quota stop.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: A fixed retention deadline or automatic deletion interval for long-paused hosted instances was not found.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: Cloud smallest listed paid node: Burstable Small, 0.5 vCPU/1 GB RAM, $0.021/node-hour ($15.33 at 730 hours), intended for development/testing; minimum provisioned storage is 4 GB.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: Cloud production-labelled General Purpose Medium: 1 vCPU/4 GB RAM, $0.135/node-hour ($98.55 at 730 hours), with 16 GB starting provisioned storage. Scale begins at three nodes, $0.192/node-hour each.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: Earth Pro: $15/organisation/month launch price, including 10M request units, 25 GB storage and 1,000 active hours/month. Self-hosted Enterprise has contact-sales pricing.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: Prices retain the published $ symbol; explicit ISO currency code was not established. Website prices exclude VAT/sales tax.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Cloud paid compute bills per running node-hour. Monthly comparisons assume 730 hours; multiple instances/nodes add usage. Billing aggregates organisation compute, storage and network monthly in arrears.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Cloud storage: up to 1 GB free; single-node over 1 GB to 512 GB $0.239/GB; cluster 128 GB–30 TB per node $0.20/GB; cluster backup storage $0.20/GB. These table entries omit a time denominator.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Earth Pro overage: $0.65 per million request units, $0.25/GB-month storage, $0.05/active hour beyond included amounts. Storage is monthly average instance data.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Earth: keyed read costs one unit per started 16 KiB, writes three units per started 4 KiB per record/index entry/edge; deletes count as writes. Non-writing requests have a one-unit minimum; HTTP adds two units/request.

facts.label: idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Cloud Start/Scale do not automatically scale compute to zero; manual pause stops compute and usage billing while retaining data/configuration, until explicitly resumed.

facts.label: idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Earth scales to zero after idle activity, wakes on the next request and may have a slower first request. Active time adds awake time across every cell, including a short period after the last request; no exact idle delay is stated.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: Cloud: first 1 GB internet egress free, then $0.09/GB; cluster cross-AZ inter-node ingress $0.01/GB and egress $0.01/GB. The published table does not give different region-specific rates.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: Earth: network egress is not billed on either Free or Pro. Self-hosted transfer charges are set by your infrastructure/object-storage providers.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: Earth Free hard-pauses at shared allowance instead of billing overage. Pro continues billing beyond allowance and has no spend-limit setting or billing alerts yet; fewer cells limit peak active-hour use but do not cap the whole bill.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: Cloud Free refuses writes above 1 GB while existing data stays readable. Paid provisioned disks also stop writes at capacity; resizing adds capacity and cost.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: A guaranteed Cloud organisation dollar cap covering compute, transfer and backups was not found.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Cloud Start: Free disk 1 GB; paid starting disk is 4 GB per GB RAM and maximum 8 GB per GB RAM. Small starts 4/max 8 GB; General Purpose Medium starts 16/max 32 GB; largest listed Start reaches 512 GB.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Cloud Scale: at least three nodes; Studio currently deploys up to five. Pricing advertises cluster storage 128 GB–30 TB per node. More nodes change capacity and cost; they are not independent free replicas.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Earth Pro cell ceiling conflicts: pricing says up to 1,000 per instance, docs say up to 100 in Studio with larger counts on request. Free is 100; connected-client caps are 100 Free/10,000 Pro per instance.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Default request limits: HTTP /sql 1 MiB, /rpc 4 MiB, import 4 GiB/request; WebSocket RPC message ceiling 128 MiB. Self-hosted overrides exist; Cloud runs documented defaults.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: A universal Cloud Start/Scale connection cap and maximum stored record size were not found; no single engine-wide number is substituted for endpoint limits.

facts.label: storage prices
facts.value: Self-hosted file buckets can use memory, allowlisted local folders, global backing storage, S3/S3-compatible storage, Google Cloud Storage or Azure Blob. Infrastructure/object-provider storage fees are additional and unpriced here.

facts.label: storage prices
facts.value: Pricing marks object file storage included on Earth/Cloud, but no separate hosted file-byte rate or explicit statement that binary bucket objects use the database storage allowance was found.

facts.label: file request and retrieval prices
facts.value: Hosted per-file upload/read/list/retrieval and image-processing tariffs were not found. Earth publishes query request units, but the mapping for bucket HTTP operations is not specified in the searched pages.

facts.label: minimum storage and early deletion
facts.value: No hosted bucket minimum object size, retained-day minimum or early-deletion tariff was found; no zero-price conclusion follows.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: Vector dimensions are declared per index; HNSW defaults to F32 and supports configurable numeric types. Its graph needs RAM beyond the process-wide 256 MiB default vector cache. DiskANN F32/F16/I8/U8 is disk-backed; 4.0 I8/U8 dimensions are capped at 33,025.

facts.label: embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: Core vector storage/search does not itself create text embeddings. The official hybrid tutorial requires real embeddings generated with a chosen model; optional learned reranking is another model step, with no included model/token allowance established for the database plans.

facts.label: run limits and pricing
facts.value: Async background processing defaults to a five-second polling interval, configurable self-hosted. MAXDEPTH ranges 0–16, default 3. Execution consumes database capacity; no separate per-job price or 0.5 vCPU/0.5 GB worker SKU is published here.

facts.label: run limits and pricing
facts.value: A plan-specific async execution timeout, concurrency ceiling and Earth request-unit/active-time treatment of retries or waiting were not found.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Self-hosted core permits commercial production under its BSL additional use grant. A Database Service letting third parties create/manage/control schemas or tables requires separate permission or a commercial license; employee/contractor internal use is treated differently.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Hosted Free is presented as no-card access; another node-based instance prompts billing information. Cloud Free resources are described as for development and evaluation.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Earth is marketed with production-use guidance, but its docs say beta and MSA §2.4 permits Beta Services only for internal evaluation, with no warranty, support or performance guarantee.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Vendor FAQ restricts Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria and Russian-controlled Crimea, LNR and DNR; it also describes restrictions on the Russian government/entities established in Russia and possible broader geoblocking.

facts.label: primary type and other roles
facts.value: Researcher classification: multi-model database with document, graph, relational-style queries, vectors, authentication, files and reactive database logic.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: Core includes database queries/transactions, custom signup/signin and JWT access, record permissions, live queries, file buckets, custom functions and synchronous/asynchronous events.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: Earth lacks change feeds, JavaScript scripting functions, Surrealism extensions, outbound HTTP access and DiskANN indexes; HNSW, SurrealQL transactions and live queries are supported.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: HTTP API, WebSocket RPC, CLI and official SDKs. Authentication guide links Rust, JavaScript, Python, Go, Java, Kotlin, .NET, PHP, Swift and Mojo; SDK/server compatibility must be checked per language.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: SurrealDB 4 adds PostgreSQL/MySQL wire-protocol support for a defined SQL subset; it is not full PostgreSQL/MySQL engine compatibility. Earth documents TLS TCP access using database-level users.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Managed GraphQL availability disagrees: pricing says included, while the current Cloud FAQ says GraphQL is not yet enabled on managed instances.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: System users have root/namespace/database roles; record users obey table/field permissions. JWT, custom signin/signup and revocable bearer access are native. Root credentials bypass record permissions and must stay out of app clients.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Cloud public endpoint is default. PrivateLink is an Enterprise feature with manual onboarding, currently AWS Oregon only; public/private/dual modes are documented. Outbound HTTP destinations are a separate deny-by-default capability.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Earth address allow/deny policy applies to HTTP/WebSocket; it does not yet apply to PostgreSQL/MySQL connections. Earth cannot enable outbound HTTP capability.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: SurrealDB 4 uses SurrealQL for document/record data, graph relations, schemafull or schemaless tables, vectors and geospatial values. Its SQL wire compatibility does not turn it into PostgreSQL or MySQL.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: ACID transactions: each statement is normally atomic; BEGIN/COMMIT groups statements and errors roll back the group. Default snapshot isolation gives a stable view; competing writes to the same key conflict at commit and require retry.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: FOR UPDATE adds named read records to conflict checks. Serializable isolation is documented for SurrealMX/SurrealDS, not a blanket guarantee for every engine. In 4.0 standalone conflicting statements can auto-retry up to ten attempts, subject to documented exclusions.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Local embedded/single-node databases and separate hosted instances support development; logical export/import can seed a test copy. Cloud/Earth branching and forking are marked coming soon.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Cloud Start has one node and no internal failover; Scale uses three or more nodes across availability zones. Commits wait for sequencer and acker disks; a single-node failure is survivable, simultaneous loss of both write holders pauses writes.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Self-hosted clustered SurrealDS is Enterprise; Community's ordinary on-disk deployment is a single SurrealKV process. Earth cells can be replaced while reading shared durable storage.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: LIVE SELECT pushes changes over a connection; Community receives changes from its subscription's node, while distributed live queries require Enterprise. Disconnect ends subscriptions; JavaScript .live() recreates them on reconnect, unlike manually queried LIVE SELECT.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Full offline-write synchronization and conflict resolution between embedded copies and hosted instances were not established.

facts.label: extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Native unique/full-text BM25, vector HNSW/DiskANN and 4.0 spatial indexes; spatial indexes need the 4.0 datastore format. Earth currently supports HNSW but excludes DiskANN and Surrealism extensions.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: 4.0 HTTP file upload default maximum 5 GiB, configurable self-hosted. Presigned uploads use one PUT; multipart/resumable upload is not supported. Content type and maximum size can be constrained in the signed upload.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Buckets can use S3-compatible backends, but SurrealDB's bucket HTTP route does not accept Amazon S3 client requests. It exposes its own HTTP/SurrealQL file methods instead.

facts.label: delivery and private files
facts.value: Bucket permissions default FULL; configure record-user file rules explicitly. With guests enabled, FULL also permits unauthenticated HTTP reads/writes. Presigned GET/PUT links require a server signing secret and continue until expiry or bucket/server-wide revocation.

facts.label: delivery and private files
facts.value: Signed-link maximum lifetime defaults to one hour, configurable up to seven days self-hosted. Exact hosted signing setup, file-specific custom-domain/CDN availability and delivery billing beyond general egress were not established.

facts.label: filters and mixed search
facts.value: Vector similarity can use filters/record permissions, BM25 keyword search and search::rrf rank fusion. Graph relationships and spatial conditions can constrain retrieval in the same engine.

facts.label: execution model and languages
facts.value: Native events run SurrealQL in the database. Synchronous events share the triggering transaction; ASYNC queues work in that transaction and executes later in a new transaction. Self-hosted/Cloud scripting can use JavaScript where enabled; Earth disables JavaScript and outbound HTTP.

facts.label: delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Async delivery is at least once; order is generally creation order but batches can run in parallel. RETRY controls failure reattempts; from 3.3.1 write-conflict retries do not count against it. External HTTP side effects are not undone with the failed database transaction.

facts.label: delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: A documented retry backoff schedule, default retry count, deduplication window, dead-letter queue and manual failed-event replay procedure were not found.

facts.label: schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Current reactive-pattern documentation says there is no built-in scheduler or automatic record TTL; use an external scheduler such as cron for fixed-time cleanup.

facts.label: schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Fixed queued-event retention/expiry and delayed-job limits were not found.

facts.label: logs and run history
facts.value: Cloud Studio/CLI expose instance metrics and lifecycle/activity logs. This is not a documented per-job history/replay console.

facts.label: logs and run history
facts.value: Exact Cloud log-retention days, per-event run-history retention and payload retention were not found.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Self-hosted: install the executable or Docker image, retain a SurrealKV directory/volume, configure credentials/TLS/capabilities, supervise the process, patch releases and operate backups/monitoring. Embedded Rust/browser options have platform-specific storage support.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Enterprise self-hosted adds SurrealDS multi-node storage, distributed live queries and enterprise controls, requiring an issued commercial key and a separate license for each cluster. Managed Cloud handles infrastructure; Community operators do that work themselves.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Node-based Cloud offers AWS Northern Virginia, Oregon, Ireland and Mumbai; Azure Germany, US East 2 (Virginia) and Brazil. Provider/region fixed at creation; Studio's actual selector is authoritative for an organisation.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Earth compute uses Cloudflare locations, but each instance's data lives in one object-storage location. Residency options Worldwide/EU/US and preferred locations are configurable at creation; residency cannot later change.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Export/import uses portable SurrealQL .surql files, one database at a time; use for cross-region/provider moves and local development. Import commits statements individually, so a partial failure leaves preceding statements committed.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Deleting a Cloud instance destroys its contents and cannot be undone; export or restore to a new instance first. Current FAQ says organisation deletion is not available and directs users to delete instances to stop charges.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: DPA promises deletion of remaining Customer Personal Data within 30 calendar days after agreement termination/expiry unless law requires or permits retention. Privacy Notice retains account/usage data as necessary; this is not an exact purge clock for each instance/object.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Cloud Start/Scale automated daily snapshots, on-demand snapshots and tiered daily/weekly/monthly retention. Scale can change backup frequency. Restore creates a separately provisioned instance in the same region, with at least the source disk size and a compatible version.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Exact retained days/weeks/months by Cloud plan, Earth backup retention/restore procedure, point-in-time restore window and file-object coverage were not established.

facts.label: backups and restore

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior

facts.value: Developer support costs 10% of Cloud usage spend, with a $0 plan minimum. Business costs the greater of $500/month or 10% of usage spend.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Business, Enterprise, and Mission Critical include their stated monthly Actions and Active/Retained Storage allocations before excess usage is billed.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: A Temporal Credit is worth $1 USD. Commitments are purchased in credits, applied to Actions, Storage, and Cloud plan charges; the minimum purchase is the first year of the commitment.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: On Pay-As-You-Go, invoices are monthly for calendar-month consumption; billing cycles normally begin on the first day UTC, with the first month's minimum plan charge prorated by signup date.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: The pricing documentation says the pricing page has a calculator. The current text view shows no monthly/annual switch, but does not expose the calculator's controls, so whether it uses sliders is unclear. Rates in this file come from the published tables, not the calculator.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Provisioned Capacity may add billed Actions: each extra TRU after the first has a minimum of 360,000 Actions per calendar hour. A shortfall is recorded if actual Actions are below this hourly allocation.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Fairness, when enabled, adds 0.1 Action per Action in the Namespace per hour. This is an additional meter, even when Workflow or Activity calls do not supply a fairness key.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: A Workflow History export accrues one Action for each Workflow exported. Export storage and provider charges at the customer's object store are separate.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Workflow starts count when accepted through a client, Continue-As-New, or Child Workflow start. Failed starts and de-duplicated starts using the same Workflow ID do not count; starting a child can generate two Actions for the durable intent and start attempt.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Activity starts and retries count separately. A recorded Activity Heartbeat counts only when it reaches the service; grouped Local Activities in a Workflow Task count as one Action, while the Workflow Task Heartbeat adds an Action.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Each explicit or SDK-created implicit Timer counts when started. Each Signal counts; Signal-With-Start counts one total Action whether or not it starts a new Workflow.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Each Query received by a Worker counts, except the built-in __temporal_workflow_metadata query. Successful and rejected Updates count; an Update-With-Start adds its Update Action to a start Action when it starts a Workflow, while duplicate Update IDs are excluded.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: SCIM is a $500 USD/month add-on on Developer and Business plans and included in Enterprise and Mission Critical. SAML is included on all four plans.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Same-region, multi-region, and multi-cloud High Availability replication approximately doubles the replicated Namespace's Actions and Storage consumption; use a 2x multiplier when estimating.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Each Schedule execution accrues three Actions: two for starting the scheduled Workflow through the Schedule and one for starting that Workflow.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Scheduling or canceling a Nexus Operation counts one Action on the caller Namespace. Workflows, Activities, Signals, and other Temporal primitives inside the handler are billed normally to the handler Namespace; retrying the Nexus operation itself does not add another Action.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Workflow replay on the Worker does not count as a billable Action because replay reconstructs state locally from Event History and does not issue new server operations.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Failed Workflow starts are not charged; de-duplicated starts using the same Workflow ID are not charged as a new start. A duplicate Update with the same Update ID is also excluded.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Action metrics and Event History estimates can differ from final metering by up to 5%; use the Usage Dashboard or Billing API for exact metered usage.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Standard Temporal Cloud does not bill customer Worker compute as part of Actions/Storage rates; customers run Workers on their own compute.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Serverless Worker hosting options are a separate feature path and have been in preview/pre-release stages; their underlying cloud-provider compute charge is separate from core Cloud Actions and Storage rates.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: The core Temporal Cloud plan has no customer-controlled Worker instance that can be configured to sleep or scale to zero. This field is not applicable to the orchestration service itself.

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: A separate Cloud network egress, inter-region replication, or data-transfer price was not found in the pricing docs, product pricing page, Terms, or export docs. This does not prove transfer is free.

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: Self-hosted network charges depend on the operator's hosting provider and network topology; Temporal does not publish a universal self-hosted egress rate.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: Cloud usage over plan allocations is metered and billed; marginal Action prices fall by tier to $25/M through 200M, with sales pricing above 200M. Storage overages use separate Active and Retained rates.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: Temporal documents throttling when a Namespace exceeds Actions/requests/operations per-second limits. Low-priority requests are throttled first; clients may receive ResourceExhausted and retry.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: Account Owners and Finance Admins can view invoices and detailed billing data in the Cloud Billing and Usage pages.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: An account-wide hard spend cap that automatically stops usage is not described in the pricing page, Billing docs, or Usage docs checked.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: A pricing-page question asks about alerts near usage limits, but the accessible page and Billing docs do not specify a budget-alert threshold or guarantee that an alert stops charges.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Temporal Cloud Actions, not Worker CPU seconds, are the primary usage meter. Action categories include Workflow, Activity, Timer, Signal, Query, Update, Schedule, Nexus, Export, Fairness, and Capacity.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Activity starts and retries can each count as Actions. Activity heartbeats count only if they reach the service; SDKs throttle heartbeats by default. Workflow replay does not create a billable Action.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Standard Action rate starts at $50/M with volume rates down to $25/M for the listed tiers; Business+ plans include monthly allocations and charge excess usage by tier.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Cloud single-payload limit is 2 MB; an Event History transaction is limited to 4 MB and a gRPC message to 4 MB. These are separate limits, and the Cloud size limits are not customer-configurable.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: A Workflow Execution's Event History is limited to 50 MB or 51,200 Events, with warnings at 10 MB or 10,240 Events. Temporal recommends keeping large file or model data outside Event History.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Within one Workflow Execution, up to 2,000 incomplete Activities, Signals, Child Workflows, or external cancellation requests are allowed; Temporal recommends 500 or fewer concurrent pending operations for performance.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Cloud Namespace throughput is limited by Actions per second, Requests per second, and Operations per second. On-Demand capacity adjusts with recent use; provisioned capacity is configured in TRUs and has minimum Action accounting.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Standard Worker compute, memory, CPU, and execution duration are not included in Temporal Cloud's core Action and storage price. Any such cost depends on the Worker host or separately selected serverless Worker integration.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Temporal Cloud supports direct self-signup and signup through AWS Marketplace or Google Cloud Marketplace. No account was created.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Temporal advertises $150 in Cloud credits for 90 days. The page frames this as introductory credits, not a continuing monthly free quota.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Whether a credit card is required for current direct signup is not answered in the accessible public pricing text. No form was submitted.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Cloud Terms limit the hosted service to the customer's internal business purposes and require use under the Acceptable Use Policy. Evaluation access is governed by its applicable order and can be ended by Temporal.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: The checked Terms, pricing page, and AUP do not give a complete country eligibility list for self-signup. The Terms do identify embargoed locations and restricted access.

facts.label: Primary type and other roles
facts.value: Primary type: durable workflow and job orchestration. It persists workflow progress and dispatches work to Workers; this record treats it as a backend/workflow service.

facts.label: Primary type and other roles
facts.value: It also provides schedules, timers, task queues, Signals, Queries, Updates, and workflow event-history visibility. It is not a general database or file store.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Temporal Cloud includes Workflow orchestration, Workflow History and visibility, Worker management, API keys, service accounts, SAML, and encryption; the pricing page says features are not locked behind support-plan upgrades.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Workflow features include retries, timeouts, Activities, durable timers, schedules, Signals, Queries, Updates, child Workflows, and event history.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Temporal Cloud can export closed Workflow histories to customer-controlled object storage on AWS S3, Google Cloud Storage, or Azure Blob Storage. The customer pays the destination provider separately.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: The product uses Temporal's gRPC service API; clients and Workers connect to a Temporal Service namespace.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Official SDK quickstarts are available for Go, Java, .NET, PHP, Python, Ruby, Rust, and TypeScript.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: The Worker is customer application code that polls a Task Queue and runs registered Workflow and Activity functions; Workers can be hosted in a customer's chosen cloud or data center.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Temporal Cloud supports API-key or mTLS namespace authentication. Temporal recommends API keys as the simpler option for most teams.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Cloud account access includes roles and service accounts; SAML is listed in plans, while SCIM is an add-on on Developer/Business and included in Enterprise/Mission Critical.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Temporal Cloud documents encryption in transit and at rest, and supports customer Data Converters for payload encryption. Temporal says it cannot read payloads encrypted by a customer-held converter key.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Cloud Terms place responsibility for selecting the processing region and meeting data localization requirements on the customer.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Self-hosted operators control network exposure, credentials, TLS, server authorization and their persistence database. Temporal warns against exposing the service host to the public Internet.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Temporal's security page links to Trust Center certifications and the Cloud Security Whitepaper; compliance claims are not treated as a guarantee of a customer's compliance.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: Temporal Cloud runs the orchestration service. A Worker polls its Task Queue and executes the customer's registered Workflow and Activity code.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: Workflows are written as code and must make replay-safe, deterministic decisions; non-deterministic external calls belong in Activities.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: Cloud Workers can run in the customer's cloud environment or data center. Temporal Cloud is available in listed AWS/GCP regions; limited managed Worker integrations are separately announced as preview features.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: Official SDK languages: Go, Java, .NET, PHP, Python, Ruby, Rust, and TypeScript. The server is a separate project from these SDKs.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: Temporal Server does not run arbitrary application code for a normal Activity. Activity code runs in the Worker process, so the Worker host and its libraries/runtime are managed separately.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Temporal records Workflow progress in Event History and replays Workflow code to restore state after a Worker restart or failure.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Activities can be retried under a retry policy; because an Activity may run again after failure, Temporal recommends idempotent Activity behavior to avoid duplicate side effects.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Workflow code must be deterministic during replay. Time, timers, and randomness should use replay-safe SDK facilities; external network, database, and file calls belong in Activities.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Signals and Updates allow clients to pass messages or requests to running Workflows; Queries read Workflow state.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Temporal Timers persist a wake-up time; the Worker does not need to stay running for the timer's wait period. The pricing page describes timers that can sleep for months.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Cloud closed Workflow History retention is configured per Namespace, charged as Retained Storage, and has a maximum of 90 days in the Cloud service.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: A Schedule starts Workflows at selected times. Each Schedule execution accrues three Actions under the current Actions definition.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Maximum individual payload is 2 MB in Cloud; full gRPC messages can hit a separate 4 MB limit. Keep large blobs in object storage and pass references through Workflows.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Self-hosted deployments can configure archival to supported stores including S3-compatible storage, Google Cloud Storage, local files, or a custom provider; the operator handles that storage and its costs.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Cloud Event History remains queryable according to Namespace retention; closed histories are Retained Storage and can be exported to external storage.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Cloud History Export runs hourly, is delivered at least once, and can take up to 24 hours for a closed Workflow to appear in the destination.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Usage dashboards and billing data show account and Namespace usage; Action metric estimates may differ from metered totals. Use the Billing API or Usage Dashboard for billing totals.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Temporal Cloud billing and Terms pages were checked for a separate fixed log-retention period. They describe Workflow History retention and customer-data deletion, but do not publish a separate general Cloud log-retention duration.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: A sustained self-hosted deployment needs a Temporal Service, a persistence database, and secured network access; deployment topology depends on workload and the operator's platform.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: The official Docker Compose example requires Docker, Docker Compose, Git and a running Docker daemon; its sample includes PostgreSQL and Elasticsearch and exposes the gRPC frontend on port 7233.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Supported persistence choices include Cassandra, PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQLite; SQLite is for development/testing, not production. Temporal v1.20+ supports advanced Visibility on SQL stores; older versions require Elasticsearch for advanced Visibility.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: The tested database versions listed by Temporal include Cassandra 3.11, 4.0, and 5.0.4+; PostgreSQL 13.18–16.6 test versions; and MySQL 5.7/8.0, specifically 8.0.19+. Check release notes for the server version in use.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: No universal CPU/RAM minimum is published for production self-hosting; Temporal says the right deployment depends on the use case and target environment.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: The operator manages upgrades, database schema updates, backups, TLS/network security, availability, scaling, and monitoring. The container image requires schema updates through matching admin tools.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Self-hosted feature rollout and Cloud parity vary by feature. Use the official release-stage page and changelog; the changelog labels features as preview, pre-release, or GA.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Self-host operators can use community docs and project channels, but the Cloud support plans and Cloud SLA do not cover a separately operated server.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Temporal Cloud namespaces are hosted in AWS or Google Cloud regions; Temporal announced Azure Cloud in invite-only pre-release in June 2026, so this is not treated as a generally selectable region set.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: The official region page lists 14 AWS regions across Asia Pacific, Canada, Europe, South America, and the United States, and 6 GCP regions. Region availability and replication pairs differ.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: On November 7, 2026, new GCP namespaces were temporarily restricted in Iowa (us-central1), Northern Virginia (us-east4), and Frankfurt (europe-west3); approved account exceptions can be requested. Existing namespaces continue to operate.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: In self-hosting, the operator chooses the infrastructure region and data location. Temporal does not place the self-hosted database in a vendor region.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Cloud customers can export closed Workflow Event Histories to S3, GCS, or Azure Blob in protobuf format; exports run hourly and may take up to 24 hours to appear.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Self-signup Cloud account owners can request account deletion in the Billing page. Billing stops immediately and full deletion is scheduled within 72 hours; account data and Active Storage are permanently deleted, while Retained Storage follows its configured retention period.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Terms say Customer Data is retained up to 30 days after an order ends. The self-signup deletion instructions instead say Retained Storage is deleted according to its configured Namespace retention period, which can be up to 90 days. The different triggers may explain the difference, but the public pages do not reconcile the timelines.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Self-hosted server data is in the operator's persistence database or configured archival store; backup, export, and deletion timing depend on operator settings.

facts.label: Identity and old names
facts.value: Product: Temporal, durable execution platform. Vendor: Temporal Technologies Inc. Canonical product URL is https://temporal.io/.

facts.label: Identity and old names
facts.value: No former product name or rebrand notice was listed on the checked product home, changelog, or server repository.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Self-hosted Temporal Server is available under the MIT License. This applies to the server repository, not to Temporal Cloud.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Temporal Cloud is vendor-hosted software under Temporal's service terms; the service is not offered under the server's MIT license.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Temporal Cloud's persistence layer is separate from the database choices for self-hosting. Temporal says Cloud uses a custom persistence layer.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Temporal Cloud is active. The current changelog lists new Cloud features through October 2026, including a public preview for serverless Workers on Google Cloud Run.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: The server repository is active; its latest release listed on the official releases page is v1.32.2, dated November 2, 2026.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: No Temporal shutdown or Temporal license-change notice was found in the official blog, changelog, or server repository checked. The current repository license remains MIT.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: The blog says the Oso security team joined Temporal on October 6, 2026 to accelerate authorization work. It says the news did not change current product availability; it does not call this an acquisition of Oso as a company.

facts.label: Vendor home and main markets
facts.value: Temporal Technologies Inc. is the Cloud contracting entity. Terms use Washington State law and the Privacy Policy lists a Bellevue, Washington mailing address. This does not establish every market served.

facts.label: Vendor home and main markets
facts.value: The checked legal and product pages do not state an exhaustive country list of markets served.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Developer plan includes support access and basic platform guidance; it has no base plan minimum but support costs 10% of Cloud usage.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Business advertises a two-hour P0 response SLA during business hours and advanced technical support; plan minimum is greater of $500/month or 10% of usage.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Enterprise offers P0 response under 30 minutes, 24/7 and private Slack. Mission Critical offers under 15 minutes, 24/7, a dedicated platform architect, and private Slack; prices are annual and custom.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: The current SLA (version date September 15, 2026) sets 99.9% for a standard single-region Namespace and 99.99% for same-region replication, multi-region, or multi-cloud Namespace deployments.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: The official status page reports live region and global-service incidents. Self-hosted users have documentation and public community support; no Temporal-operated uptime promise applies to their deployment.

facts.label: free offer type

facts.label: free offer type
facts.value: The quota is automatically granted when a new user activates COS; the docs do not describe it as a non-production-only offer.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: Free allowance: 50 GB of STANDARD storage, valid for 180 days from COS activation.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: The free package applies to public-cloud regions, not finance-cloud regions. Public regions listed include mainland cities, Hong Kong, Singapore, Seoul, Bangkok, Jakarta, Tokyo, Riyadh, Silicon Valley, Virginia, Frankfurt, and São Paulo.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: The free package offsets only STANDARD storage. It does not offset MAZ storage, other storage classes, requests, retrieval, traffic, or management features.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: The package applies before purchased packs and pay-as-you-go charges; usage above its eligible allowance falls through to paid billing.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: No free numeric quota for object requests, retrieval, public egress, CDN origin-pull, cross-region replication, or management operations was listed in the free-tier page.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: No inactivity-based pause, sleep, expiry, or deletion interval was stated in the COS product, pricing, free-tier, and general FAQ pages checked.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: If an account goes overdue, COS may suspend service after 24 hours; the published FAQ says data is retained for 15 days before destruction if the balance is not restored.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: Resource-pack expiry alone does not delete stored data; charges move to pay-as-you-go if usage continues.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: COS activation is free, and the billing guide describes pay-as-you-go as the default billing mode; prepaid resource packs are optional.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: A minimum paid order, minimum account spend, or fixed monthly service charge for international COS was not published in the pricing center pages or billing overview checked.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: COS billable groups are storage usage, read/write and monitoring requests, data retrieval, network traffic, and management features.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Pay-as-you-go storage charges use average storage usage multiplied by storage time and the class/region price. COS storage and traffic units use 1,024 GB per TB.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Read/write request charges count user and feature-generated backend requests, including failed requests; the stated billing unit is 10,000 requests, with actual counts used below that amount.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Usage-based retrieval charges can apply when reading STANDARD_IA/MAZ_STANDARD_IA data or restoring archive-class objects.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: COS storage, request, and retrieval fees are generally settled daily, with prior-day charges billed the following day.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Optional prepaid packs cover eligible STANDARD/IA storage, request, public downstream, or global-acceleration usage; unsupported items continue pay-as-you-go.

facts.label: idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Not applicable: COS is object storage and has no customer-managed compute instance to idle or scale to zero.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: Public-network downstream traffic from COS to a client is billable; direct object URLs and static website endpoints count as public downstream traffic.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: Public-network upload traffic into COS is free of COS traffic charges; write requests and storage usage can still be charged.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: Tencent Cloud products in the same region use COS private-network transfer by default; private upstream and downstream traffic have no COS traffic fee.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: Same-region replication has no replication traffic fee; cross-region replication is billed using the source bucket region’s traffic rate.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: When COS is a CDN/EdgeOne origin, COS bills origin-pull traffic and requests; CDN/EdgeOne bills delivery traffic separately.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: Global acceleration uses separate upstream and downstream traffic meters and has separate eligible resource packs.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: The current international USD rates for public egress, CDN origin-pull, cross-region replication, and global acceleration were not recoverable from the official live pricing page.

facts.label: overages and bill controls

facts.label: overages and bill controls
