facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: A hard COS spending cap that automatically stops all billable use was not found in the pricing, billing, or terms pages checked.

facts.label: overages and bill controls

facts.label: primary type and other roles
facts.value: Researcher classification: versioned document/knowledge-graph database, with schema-checked JSON/JSON-LD data, RDF storage, graph querying and Git-style data history. Search is an additional version-dependent role.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: Included engine capabilities: document/graph database, schema validation, WOQL, generated GraphQL/HTTP API, version history and access-control users/roles/capabilities. These database users are not a separate managed consumer-login product.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: Operator-installed plugins add database lifecycle hooks and custom behavior; Prolog or native Rust/C/Go components run in the server. RC 12.1 adds versioned hybrid search and GraphQL SSE subscriptions.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: HTTP REST Documents API, GraphQL and JSON WOQL over HTTP; CLI and official JavaScript/TypeScript/Python clients. Rust and Elixir clients are explicitly community contributions.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: JS client supports browser and Node.js. Self-hosted Basic Auth/JWT and Cloud API tokens are documented; Cloud git-for-data API works like the self-hosted API.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Capability-based access links users, roles and organisation/database scopes; organisation grants are inherited, database grants add rather than reduce permissions. Admin is broad; consumer is read-only for instance/schema data.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Production guide says authentication is always required, with Basic Auth and optional JWT/OIDC key validation; JWT is off by default. Use strong admin credentials and a TLS reverse proxy; default local bindings are intended for local access.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Older self-hosting text says TERMINUSDB_AUTOLOGIN=true skips local authentication; current production guide says no flag disables authentication. The precise local bypass behavior is not resolved by the docs alone.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: The SaaS terms' linked Data Processing Agreement could not be read: original PDF returns 404; same-path Gettier copy and /dpa also return 404.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: TerminusDB stores typed graph documents over RDF triples and immutable delta layers. Native query interfaces are WOQL (Datalog), GraphQL and REST documents; it is not a PostgreSQL, MongoDB or SPARQL wire-protocol service.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Each write is an atomic, schema-validated commit. Readers see immutable snapshots; optimistic write concurrency restarts conflicting transactions. Rebase can replay transactions in a different order, so read-condition behavior needs attention.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Self-hosted maximum conflicting-transaction retries defaults to 3, configurable through TERMINUSDB_SERVER_MAX_TRANSACTION_RETRIES.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Native isolated branches share history until they diverge; every write commits, and structural diff, merge/conflict detection, reset and time-travel queries are supported. A branch is addressed in the database API path.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Public managed branch-count/lifetime limits and additional-branch fees were not found.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Git-for-data can replicate/synchronize database content between instances. Community production examples use a single server; Enterprise README mentions clustering, but a current automatic failover topology, read-replica contract and replica costs were not established.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: 12.1 RC GraphQL subscriptions stream added/updated/deleted document events over SSE, with optional NDJSON, through long-lived authenticated HTTP connections. This must not be presented as a stable 12.0.9 feature.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Local/remote clone and push/pull/rebase support disconnected data workflows. Automatic client-side offline conflict resolution, durable subscription replay and resume retention were not found.

facts.label: extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Triple storage is automatically indexed; 12.1 RC adds VectorLink 2.0 semantic, full-text and fused hybrid retrieval, either embedded or remote. Legacy VectorLink instructions describe an OpenAI-key-based integration.

facts.label: filters and mixed search
facts.value: 12.1 RC supports vector, full-text and hybrid search with reciprocal-rank fusion. API filters doc_type and doc_id combine with AND across sets and OR within each set; results deduplicate chunks to documents.

facts.label: filters and mixed search
facts.value: Search is commit-aware and can serve the nearest indexed ancestor while indexing catches up; TerminusDB-Data-Version reports the served commit. No indexed ancestor means 404.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: Not applicable as app-file upload limits: the API stores graph documents; its record/traversal limits are recorded under D03. Backup bundle transfer is an administrative restore path.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Not applicable: the public product API is HTTP documents/WOQL/GraphQL, not an S3 object-store service. External object stores are mentioned only as destinations for copied backups.

facts.label: delivery and private files
facts.value: Not applicable: native file buckets, signed download links and a file CDN were not identified as an app-storage module. Protect database APIs with the C18 access controls instead.

facts.label: execution model and languages
facts.value: Not a hosted job/queue product. Operators can write Prolog or native shared-object plugins that react to database lifecycle hooks; this runs inside the operated database process.

facts.label: delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Queue delivery, message deduplication, dead-letter handling and job retry guarantees are outside the scoped product. Transaction-conflict retries are covered under D02.

facts.label: schedules and queue retention
facts.value: A durable delayed-job/cron queue with retention and payload quotas is outside this database record. Backup cron examples run in operator-managed external scheduling.

facts.label: logs and run history
facts.value: No general per-job history/replay product is established. Server logs are operator-managed; production docs support JSON log shipping, while Enterprise adds Prometheus metrics.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Operate persistent local storage, process/container restarts, TLS reverse proxy, strong credentials, health checks, backups and upgrades. Linux/macOS x86_64/arm64 are documented; Windows uses WSL2/Docker. No universal minimum production CPU/RAM budget is stated.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Enterprise adds HTTP binary backup, multi-format RDF/JSON-LD exchange, high-resolution history and Prometheus observability. RC 12.1 vector deployment also needs search-store persistence plus an embedding runtime/provider.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Self-hosted data and backups live where the operator deploys them. Managed early access offers Azure/AWS/Google Cloud in a preferred region; no public selectable region-ID matrix or backup-location guarantee was found.

facts.label: leaving and deleting

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: HTTP document export and Enterprise bundle/unbundle API offer migration paths; Enterprise binary bundle includes schema, instance data and commit history.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Community CLI bundles capture all branches, commits and database data in a portable file; restore to an instance of the same version. Full-instance backup is a stopped storage-volume archive.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Enterprise HTTP bundle/unbundle captures schema, instance documents, layer data and full history. Target database must exist; unbundle replaces its contents. Off-site object-storage copies are explicitly suggested.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Managed automatic backup cadence, retained days, billable size and exact-point recovery window were not found; Enterprise capability advertising does not specify a Cloud plan's recovery service.

facts.label: file recovery and protection
facts.value: Not applicable for file versioning/locks/undelete. Database commits and backup protection are recorded under D04/D05, which do not establish recovery of external application files.

apps.name: TiDB Cloud
apps.line: Managed distributed SQL with optional vector search and a self-hosted Community edition.

free.text: MySQL: 5 instances get 5GiB row + 5GiB column, 50M RUs/mo; no idle rule

cells.regions: AWS, Google Cloud and Azure; availability varies by plan

sql.math: 1 GB fits the row allowance, but 100,000 reads and 20,000 writes do not show the total RUs (request units).
Kept storage can fit the free allowance. Background RUs (request units) are unknown, so the idle total is incomplete.

files.math: $101.50–129 at published rates, minus the shared $5 allowance. The storage tier and metadata are unknown.

jobs.math: TiDB has no matching app-worker product for the 10,000-job workload.

facts.label: free offer type
facts.value: Self-hosted Community: free software license without hosting credits or a hosted quota. Hosted MySQL Starter: recurring monthly free allowance, not a time-limited trial. PostgreSQL Starter: free only during the public preview, with billing disabled.

facts.label: free offer type
facts.value: Cloud proof-of-concept credits are a separate offer: CSA defines a PoC period ending after 14 days or credit exhaustion, whichever comes first. This does not limit the recurring Starter free allowance.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: MySQL Starter: first 5 eligible instances per organization each get 5 GiB row storage, 5 GiB columnar storage and 50 million RUs/month. Allowances apply separately per instance; the headline 25/25 GiB and 250M RU cannot all be spent on one instance.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: PostgreSQL Starter preview: first 10 eligible instances per organization each get 50 GiB row storage and 500 million RUs/month. Paid organizations have a default aggregate limit of 100 Starter instances across both protocols, including MySQL branches.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: Filesystem preview: USD 5 monthly free allowance per organization, shared across filesystems, regions and billed meters. Without a card: one filesystem per region and 2,000-file limit; storage/file-size units conflict, recorded in F04.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: Self-hosted Community: hosted inactivity, account expiry and provider pause rules do not apply; the operator controls uptime and deletion.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: Current MySQL Starter free-project idle-expiry or automatic data-deletion interval was not found. Its 340-second idle network connection timeout is a connection rule, not project deletion. Filesystem FAQ says post-preview retention/deletion policy is not finalized.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: Dedicated: for organizations created after 2024-11-12, pause is capped at 7 days and automatically resumes, with a reminder 24 hours before. Older organizations can retain longer-pause behavior until migrated. Paused compute stops billing; node/backup storage continues.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: Self-hosted Community: no hosted subscription minimum; infrastructure, operations and any purchased support remain external costs.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: MySQL Starter: pay for actual usage above eligibility/allowance, without a fixed monthly subscription shown. The minimum configurable positive spend limit is USD 0.01; it is a spending ceiling, not a monthly plan price. PostgreSQL preview has no paid tariff enabled.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: Essential preview: 2,000 RCU minimum; AWS Oregon Zonal USD 0.20/RCU-month gives USD 400/month minimum compute, plus other meters. Limited-mode minimum is max(2,000, 10% of configured maximum), subject to the legacy-instance transition.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: Premium preview: pricing headline starts at USD 1,800/month compute. Limited mode bills max(5,000 RCUs, 25% of maximum); Oregon USD 0.36/RCU-month. Elastic mode bills its configured Baseline RCU; other meters are extra.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: Dedicated: advertised cluster from USD 1,376/month using an AWS 4-vCPU-per-node configuration; not a universal all-in total. BYOC: quoted PingCAP service fee plus infrastructure and mandatory Enterprise-or-higher support.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: MySQL Starter AWS Oregon/us-west-2: USD 0.10/million RUs, USD 0.20/GiB-month row storage, USD 0.05/GiB-month columnar storage. AWS Singapore, Tokyo and Frankfurt: USD 0.12, 0.24 and 0.06 respectively in those same units.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Starter RU is a sum of resource usage: 2 read batches, 8 storage reads or 64 KiB read payload each represent 1 RU; 2 write batches, 2 storage writes or 2 KiB write payload each represent 1 RU; SQL CPU 3 ms/RU. Components are added, not alternate query prices.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Essential/Premium AWS Oregon: row USD 0.20/GiB-month, columnar USD 0.05/GiB-month; automatic/manual backup storage USD 0.02829/GB-month; changefeed capacity USD 0.1307/CCU-hour. Premium PITR preview package price requires Sales.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Dedicated AWS Oregon: TiDB or TiKV 4 vCPU/16 GiB node USD 0.4416/hour each; optional TiFlash 8 vCPU/64 GiB USD 1.3708/hour. Compute billed by the minute. TiKV Standard storage displayed USD 0.000197 per size-unit-hour; Basic USD 0.000109 plus USD 0.001026/hour IOPS/throughput fee for 4-vCPU nodes.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Lake preview, separate analytics service: Personal X-Small warehouse USD 1.60/hour, Business USD 2.40/hour; storage USD 23/TB-month; API requests USD 1/10,000 Personal or USD 2/10,000 Business. Data Integration is a separate continuous service, from USD 0.20/hour Personal 4X-Small.

facts.label: idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Starter: request-driven compute can scale to zero; retained storage and background activities can still incur charges. Essential and Premium retain minimum billable provisioned capacity, even idle. Dedicated has explicit pause; BYOC infrastructure/support remain customer costs.

facts.label: idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Lake warehouse: auto-suspend defaults to 5 minutes of inactivity; running Data Integration and storage are billed separately. Filesystem persistent storage has storage/operation/transfer meters, without an application-worker idle charge.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: MySQL Starter public endpoint: 1 KiB outbound data = 1 RU; private endpoint: 4 KiB = 1 RU, at the region's RU rate. Transfer consumes the free RU allowance or paid spend limit along with query resources.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: Essential and Premium AWS Oregon: public egress USD 0.10/GB, private USD 0.02/GB; ingress free. Essential separate egress billing rolls out to instances created on/after 2026-09-01 and removes network egress from RCU charging for those instances.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: Dedicated: cloud-provider transfer and load-balancer charges are passed through at published AWS/Google Cloud/Azure rates without additional PingCAP fees. Applies to app reads, same-region/cross-region traffic, backup/recovery, migration and changefeeds; no single universal egress price.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: Starter: instance monthly spend limit is enforced; reaching allowance/cap denies new connections and throttles existing ones. Raising the cap or the next UTC monthly reset restores quota. A card/positive cap enables paid usage.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: Essential/Premium: Limited mode caps capacity and can throttle requests; this is not a cap on storage, backup, transfer or total USD. Elastic mode has no configured maximum; alerts do not set a hard bill cap. Filesystem pricing explicitly says financial spending limits are not supported.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Self-hosted stable limits: one row defaults to 6 MiB, configurable to 120 MiB; 1,017 columns default, configurable to 4,096; 64 indexes default, configurable to 512; index key length 3,072 bytes; up to 16 columns per index.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: MySQL Starter: 400 concurrent connections when free, 5,000 with positive spending limit; free query memory 256 MiB; transactions limited to 30 minutes. Public AWS endpoint idle TCP timeout is 340 seconds; long-lived connections can be terminated after 30 minutes.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: PG Starter preview has its own storage/RU quotas, but a protocol-specific concurrent connection/query memory limit was not located. The 400/5,000 limits above come from MySQL Starter documentation.

facts.label: storage prices
facts.value: Filesystem preview, AWS Oregon: database storage for small files/metadata USD 0.30/GB-month; object storage for large files USD 0.025/GB-month. Monthly USD 5 organization allowance is shared across operations, storage and egress; storage prorated hourly.

facts.label: storage prices
facts.value: Filesystem automatic placement uses database versus object storage according to file size, but the size threshold and complete billed metadata/index overhead were not found in pricing, Filesystem intro/FAQ or limits docs.

facts.label: file request and retrieval prices
facts.value: Filesystem all listed regions: reads USD 0.04/1,000 operations; writes USD 0.50/1,000. List/stat count as reads. AWS Oregon internet egress USD 0.09/GB; requests are metered separately from stored bytes.

facts.label: minimum storage and early deletion
facts.value: Filesystem minimum billed object size, minimum retained days and early-deletion penalties were not specified in the pricing page, limits, FAQ or Cloud CSA inspected.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: TiDB self-hosted v8.4+ (v8.5+ recommended) and MySQL Cloud Starter offer preview vector search: up to 16,383 float32 dimensions, no NaN/Infinity; vectors cannot be primary/unique/partition keys. ANN uses HNSW on TiFlash with cosine or L2 distance and fixed VECTOR(n).

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: PG Starter preview advertises pgvector-compatible search; the MySQL VECTOR(16383) limit is not proven to apply to its PG types. Filesystem custom embedding provider must return exactly 1,024 dimensions.

facts.label: embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: SQL Auto Embedding: only AWS MySQL Starter. Hosted Titan Text Embedding V2 is free, supports 1,024 default / 512 / 256 dimensions, max 8,192 input tokens or 50,000 characters. BYOK embedding providers bill through the customer's provider account; TiDB does not charge model usage for BYOK.

facts.label: embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: Numeric recurring free model-usage/rate limits were not located in Auto Embedding Overview, Titan model page, Starter pricing, CSA AI terms or privacy notice; overview says usage caps may apply. External reranking/embedding costs are not assumed zero.

facts.label: embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: Filesystem optional media extraction/custom embeddings send file/text content to the chosen provider. API keys are stored encrypted; enabling/replacing a provider sends a validation request that the provider may charge for. Custom embeddings require 1,024 dimensions; database_auto configurations cannot be replaced.

facts.label: run limits and pricing
facts.value: The fixed 0.5-vCPU/0.5-GB application-job scenario has no matching TiDB SQL/Filesystem worker SKU.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Hosted Starter: public self-service, no card to begin within the free quota; a card is needed to enable paid MySQL usage. BYOC onboarding requires contacting Sales. MySQL Starter is described as production-ready; PostgreSQL preview is for evaluation, with advice to wait for GA for production.

facts.value: Cloud CSA excludes service provision in mainland PRC (excluding Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan from that exclusion). Restrictions include building competitive services, unauthorized benchmarking disclosure and certain service-bureau/warehouse offerings; normal app use is subject to the full agreement.

facts.label: primary type and other roles
facts.value: Researcher classification: SQL database, with transactional and analytical processing; hosted managed databases, optional search/vector features, and separate Filesystem and Lake services.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: Self-hosted: distributed SQL, TiKV row storage, optional TiFlash columnar analytics, backups and change-data capture tools. Applications supply their own end-user login, application code and file service.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: Cloud SQL plans provide managed databases and plan-dependent backup, scaling, connectivity and changefeeds. Filesystem and Lake are separate offers. The plan catalog does not establish an included end-user-auth or general application-functions bundle.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Self-hosted and MySQL-compatible Cloud: MySQL wire protocol, SQL and MySQL ecosystem clients/drivers; incompatibilities remain. PostgreSQL Starter preview: PostgreSQL-compatible clients and drivers through a public endpoint, psql/COPY imports; private endpoints currently unsupported.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Self-hosted: SQL users, roles and GRANT/REVOKE permissions; operator configures credentials and deployment/network security. Column-level privileges require TiDB v8.5.6 or later and must not be assumed on every Cloud kernel.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: MySQL Starter/Essential: encrypted cloud-provider storage, TLS connection guide, public/private endpoint options; no VPC peering and no CMEK in the limitations page. Optional second encryption layer for paid Starter and Essential costs extra. PG Starter currently has public endpoints only.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Dedicated: newly created clusters have public endpoints disabled by default as of 2026-10-20; enabling public access also requires an IP access list. Existing clusters retain their settings. Premium CMEK/VPC-peering entries are private-preview features in the feature table.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: Self-hosted TiDB: distributed SQL with stateless TiDB SQL nodes, TiKV row storage, PD coordination and optional TiFlash columnar storage. MySQL 5.7/8.0 protocol/common SQL compatibility; not stock MySQL. Stored procedures/functions, triggers, events, XA, GIS and MySQL replication protocol are unsupported.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: Cloud engines differ: Starter uses a customized classic-based TiDB X kernel (default v8.5.3); newer Essential and Premium use TiDB-X-CLOUD.202603.1; Dedicated default v8.5.8. PostgreSQL Starter preview offers PostgreSQL wire compatibility and selected extensions, not all PostgreSQL behavior.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Self-hosted/MySQL TiDB: ACID distributed transactions with snapshot isolation, exposed as REPEATABLE-READ compatibility; not serializable, and write skew is possible. Default pessimistic transactions since v3.0.8; READ-COMMITTED is supported with pessimistic transactions, while optimistic transactions remain snapshot-isolated.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: The PG Starter preview FAQ does not specify exact transaction-isolation equivalence or all extension semantics; MySQL TiDB snapshot-isolation rules were not assumed to describe its PostgreSQL compatibility layer.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Self-hosted: deploy separate test clusters or restore/export copies yourself. Hosted Starter MySQL branching is public preview and copy-on-write; child/parent changes do not synchronize. Default 5 branches per organization; same-region only, parent no larger than 100 GiB; larger branch counts require an Instance Capacity Plan.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Cloud feature table marks Data Branch available for Essential, while the detailed branching guide documents Starter quotas only. Essential-specific branch count, size and billing scope were not established from the checked pages.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Self-hosted: TiKV uses Raft with replicated storage and majority commitment; production topology separates failure domains. An optional TiFlash columnar replica serves analytical/search workloads and consumes its own resources.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Cloud availability differs by plan. Essential Regional HA launched in AWS Tokyo on 2026-10-27 with more regions rolling out; Premium is regional-only. Older feature table still marks Essential Cross-AZ failover unavailable. New Essential regional rates apply immediately to instances created on/after Oct 26; earlier instances switch in Jan 2027.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Self-hosted TiCDC replicates database changes to downstream systems. Hosted changefeeds: Premium/BYOC/Dedicated supported, Essential private preview in feature table, Starter not available. This is backend change-data replication, not an offline mobile-client synchronization contract.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Managed client-side offline writes, conflict resolution and reconnect catch-up guarantees were not found in the database overview, Cloud Features, Starter FAQ or CSA.

facts.label: extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: MySQL full-text indexes: Cloud Starter only in selected AWS regions (Oregon, N. Virginia, Tokyo, Frankfurt, Singapore). Self-hosted and Dedicated can parse FULLTEXT syntax but cannot use those indexes. PG Starter preview separately advertises full-text and selected PostgreSQL extensions.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: Filesystem no-card limits conflict in units: pricing says 2 GB per filesystem and 500 MB per file; limits docs say 2 GiB and 500 MiB. Both state 2,000 files and one filesystem per region. Adding a card removes these no-card limits, with configurable resource limits still possible.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Filesystem interfaces: CLI, Drive9 SDKs (TypeScript, Go, Python, Rust, Kotlin, Swift), filesystem mounts via FUSE on Linux/macOS and WebDAV on macOS. Windows supports CLI file operations, not mounts; layers/checkpoints require FUSE.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: An S3-compatible bucket API/operation matrix, multipart/resumable upload limits and a general paid-plan maximum file size were not located in Filesystem intro, regions/limits, FAQ, pricing or Cloud CSA.

facts.label: delivery and private files
facts.value: Filesystem private access: Cloud API credentials for administration; owner token for broad filesystem access; scoped tokens constrain path and read/list/search/write/delete operations. Revoking an owner token does not revoke already-issued scoped tokens; revoke them separately.

facts.label: delivery and private files
facts.value: Bundled CDN, custom public delivery domain and temporary signed public-download URL support were not established from Filesystem authorization, intro, FAQ, pricing or CSA.

facts.label: filters and mixed search
facts.value: MySQL vector SQL can combine relational filtering and semantic distance. Filtering before ANN can require a full exact scan rather than the vector index; ANN in a subquery followed by filtering can return fewer than K results. Hybrid search combines full-text and vectors where the full-text feature is available.

facts.label: execution model and languages
facts.value: Not applicable to this database/Filesystem comparison: these offers do not quote a general application-job execution plan with managed worker languages.

facts.label: delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Application-job retries, duplicate suppression, ordering and dead-letter replay are outside the SQL/Filesystem product scope researched.

facts.label: schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Application-queue schedules, payload limits and queued-message retention are outside this product scope.

facts.label: logs and run history
facts.value: Application-job run-history retention/replay is outside this product scope.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Self-hosted production components: TiDB, PD and TiKV; TiFlash optional for columnar/ANN workloads. TiUP deployment on supported Linux/CPU combinations, or an operator-managed Kubernetes deployment; user handles infrastructure, upgrades, networks/TLS, credentials, monitoring and backup/recovery.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Published production table recommends TiDB 16 cores/48 GB RAM, at least 2 instances; PD 8 cores/16 GB, at least 3; TiKV 16 cores/64 GB, at least 3, with SSDs. Optional TiFlash: 48 cores/128 GB, at least 2. These are production guidance, not a minimum laptop/dev footprint or a hosting quote.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Hosted region selection depends on plan: Starter/Essential price tables include AWS Oregon us-west-2, N. Virginia us-east-1, Singapore ap-southeast-1, Tokyo ap-northeast-1 and Frankfurt eu-central-1. Premium lists AWS Oregon, Singapore, Tokyo and Sydney ap-southeast-2. Dedicated advertises AWS, Google Cloud and Azure.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: PostgreSQL Starter preview: AWS us-east-1 only. BYOC data plane runs in the customer's AWS account/VPC while PingCAP manages the control plane. Self-hosted: operator chooses infrastructure and backup location.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Filesystem selectable locations: AWS us-east-1, us-west-2, ap-southeast-1; Alibaba ap-southeast-1; Google gcp-us-east1; Azure azure-centralus. SQL database/backup location must be assessed separately.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Self-hosted: BR/snapshot and log recovery, Dumpling logical exports and TiCDC replication are available tools; operator controls deletion and external backups. Hosted Starter/Essential export guide supports SQL, CSV and Parquet exports.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Hosted instance deletion: Starter cannot be restored after deletion; Essential/Dedicated backups can remain in Recycle Bin and continue billing until removed. The latest automatic backup can remain without automatic expiry; manual backups remain until deleted.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: CSA termination: customer can email deal-management@pingcap.com or delete all clusters. §5.5 allows requested data retrieval within 60 days after termination; deletion may follow, not a guaranteed exact erasure deadline. PoC expiry has a separate requested backup retrieval window of 7 days.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Exact time to purge every hosted replica, log and backup after ordinary cluster/account deletion was not found; Filesystem post-preview retention/deletion policy is explicitly not finalized.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Self-hosted: operator runs and stores BR physical snapshots/log backups for point-in-time recovery or Dumpling logical exports. Restore compatibility and backup protection remain operator duties; vector data needs BR v8.4+ and cannot restore into earlier TiDB.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: MySQL Starter free: automatic daily backup, fixed randomly selected time, 1-day retention. Starter with positive spending limit: daily, configurable 1–30 days, default 14 days; no manual backups or PITR. PG preview uses the configurable paid-Starter backup settings even though its preview is free.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Essential automatic backups: daily, configurable 1–30-day retention, default 14; PITR listed supported. Manual backup conflict: October 13 release supports it on CLOUD.202603.x+ and retains it until explicitly deleted, while the backup guide/feature table still say unsupported.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Premium/BYOC: Standard backup bundle includes 7-day PITR, hourly snapshots for 7 days and daily snapshots for 33 days. Custom retention supports PITR and daily snapshots for 3–33 days; manual backups also available. Backup storage is billable; Premium PITR package pricing is quoted during preview.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Dedicated: automatic daily backups by default, configurable weekly scheduling; default 7-day retention. Manual backups retained until deleted/account closure. PITR supported for v6.4+; some bulk import paths require a new snapshot because logs do not cover the imported data. Physical backup export requires Support.

facts.label: file recovery and protection
facts.value: Filesystem committed remote data survives client/sandbox replacement; buffered local writes can be lost if the client stops abruptly, so drain/unmount first. Layers/checkpoints provide overlays/fork/commit/rollback; checkpoints are not independent complete snapshots or backup/authorization boundaries.

facts.label: file recovery and protection
facts.value: Complete accidental-delete recovery retention, independent version-history window and post-preview workspace deletion policy were not established. FAQ explicitly says post-preview retention/deletion policy is not finalized; preview has no SLA.

facts.label: identity and old names
facts.value: TiDB is PingCAP's distributed SQL database; TiDB Cloud is the hosted product family. Cloud Serverless was renamed Starter on 2025-08-12.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: Self-hosted Community: TiDB source is Apache License 2.0; run on your own infrastructure. TiKV and PD companion repositories also publish Apache 2.0 licenses.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: Hosted: Starter, Essential, Premium and Dedicated run under the TiDB Cloud Services Agreement. BYOC is managed deployment into the customer's AWS account, with PingCAP's control plane; it is separate from self-hosted Community.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: No overall closure or acquisition notice found in the official product, release and support-policy pages checked. Starter MySQL is offered publicly; Essential, Premium, BYOC, Lake and Filesystem are marked public preview. PostgreSQL-compatible Starter is a public preview launched 2026-10-15, not recommended for production.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: 2026-10-20: Chat2Query and the Chat2Query API retired from Starter SQL Editor and Data Service; other SQL Editor and Data Service features remain. 2026-10-27: Essential Regional HA preview launched in AWS Tokyo.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Self-hosted v8.5 Community: maintenance ends 2027-12-19, extended-support EOL 2028-12-19. v8.5 Enterprise: maintenance ends 2029-12-19, EOL 2030-12-19. Both released 2024-12-19.

facts.label: vendor home and main markets
facts.value: Cloud contracting entities: PingCAP (US), Inc. for the Americas; PingCAP Kabushiki-Kaisha for Japan; PingCAP Pte. Ltd. elsewhere. Privacy notice gives PingCAP (US), Inc. a Sunnyvale, California, USA address.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: Cloud Basic support is free: billing/account tickets for all users, technical help via Slack/Discord, docs and TiDB.AI. Guaranteed technical ticket response requires paid Developer/Enterprise/Premium support. S1 initial response: Developer 4 business hours, Enterprise 1 hour, Premium 30 minutes.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: Published SLA: MySQL Starter 99.9%; Essential Zonal 99.9%, Regional 99.99%; Premium 99.99%; Dedicated multi-node 99.99%, single-node credit schedule uses 99.9%. PG Starter and Filesystem previews explicitly offer no SLA.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: Paid support subscription prices were not listed in the inspected public support detail/pricing pages. BYOC requires Enterprise or higher.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: Official Cloud public status page is https://status.tidbcloud.com/, with product and cloud-region components and incident history.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: PingCAP disclosed unauthorized access to internal systems from 2026-09-09 through 2026-10-07. The attacker copied customer-related records, including TiDB Cloud account/query-history information and business/billing data; encrypted API-key values were among exported records. PingCAP reports no evidence that customer database contents were accessed or that the reviewed production systems were used, and customer-specific impact review was continuing. It advised customers to rotate management keys and secrets shared with support.

facts.label: Data access controls

facts.label: Transactions and consistency

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior

cells.regions: 6 listed regions

USD 5.99 subscription + USD 0 storage + USD 0 query usage. The Free plan is USD 0, but it is archived after 10 days.

facts.label: free offer type
facts.value: Hosted Free: ongoing monthly usage allowance, with no fixed trial expiry stated; separate paid plans above it. Free databases can archive after inactivity. Local MIT engines are free software, not free hosted capacity.

facts.label: free limits
facts.value: Hosted Free per plan/organization: 100 databases, 5 GB stored data, 500 million rows read/month, 10 million rows written/month and 3 GB monthly sync transfer; 1-day PITR, Community support. Overages are unavailable on Free; upgrade when any quota is exhausted.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: Free databases archive after 10 days of inactivity. Restore access with turso group unarchive; this is a group-level operation. The guide does not say the database has been permanently deleted at that point.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: A maximum archived-data retention/deletion deadline and an automatic wake-on-first-query promise were not located in the unarchive, billing, recovery, Terms or privacy pages checked.

facts.label: inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: Self-hosted/embedded: provider free-account archiving rules do not apply; the operator/application controls the database file and process lifetime.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: Hosted monthly subscriptions: Developer USD 5.99/month; Scaler USD 29/month; Pro USD 499/month. Enterprise is custom-priced, not USD 0. Developer is the smallest published ongoing paid plan; no mandatory extra seat fee is shown.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: Annual-billing display: Developer USD 4.99/month equivalent, Scaler USD 24.92/month equivalent, Pro USD 416.58/month equivalent. These are annual-billing equivalents, not monthly-cancelable prices. Exact annual invoice totals were not established from the rounded display.

facts.label: least paid commitment
facts.value: Self-hosted engines: no Cloud subscription minimum. Terms say taxes are the customer's responsibility, paid subscriptions renew, and paid current-term fees generally are not refundable/prorated on cancellation.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Developer: includes 9 GB storage, 2.5 billion monthly row reads, 25 million row writes and 10 GB sync. Enabled overages: USD 0.75/GB storage, USD 1/billion row reads, USD 1/million row writes and USD 0.35/GB sync.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Scaler: includes 24 GB storage, 100 billion reads/month, 100 million writes/month and 24 GB sync/month. Enabled overages: USD 0.50/GB storage, USD 0.80/billion reads, USD 0.80/million writes, USD 0.25/GB sync.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Pro: includes 50 GB storage, 250 billion reads/month, 250 million writes/month and 100 GB sync/month. Enabled overages: USD 0.45/GB storage, USD 0.75/billion reads, USD 0.75/million writes, USD 0.15/GB sync. Enterprise shows those included quantities but custom pricing.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Billable reads are rows touched/scanned, including joins, aggregates and update scans, not just returned rows or HTTP calls. Writes include affected indexes; aborted inserts/updates can count. Studio queries also consume quota. Storage includes tables and indexes, measured in database pages.

facts.label: billing meters
facts.value: Exact storage-usage sampling/pro-rating, top-up block sizes/minimum overage invoices and whether published GB means decimal GB or binary GiB were not established from pricing, Usage & Billing or Terms.

facts.label: idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Hosted usage model has no separate vCPU-hour charge on these plans; pricing says idle databases consume storage only. Paid subscription and any excess retained-storage fees remain even with zero queries. No 730-hour compute allocation is required for this tariff.

facts.label: idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Exact cache/compute eviction timer and wake latency are not published in the current pricing, billing, Cloud overview or inactivity command pages checked. Free's 10-day archiving is a separate explicit lifecycle rule.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: Embedded Syncs are measured as pages transferred between Cloud and a local embedded database in either direction. Free includes 3 GB/month; Developer 10 GB then USD 0.35/GB; Scaler 24 GB then USD 0.25/GB; Pro 100 GB then USD 0.15/GB.

facts.label: data transfer costs
facts.value: A separate ordinary remote-query internet egress, cross-region transfer or bulk-export rate/explicit unlimited-free exemption was not located in pricing/FAQ, billing, private-endpoint, export or Terms pages. Whether newer logical Turso Sync uses precisely the legacy page-sync billing rule is not fully specified.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: Free or paid with Overages disabled: exceeding any one of storage/read/write/sync quotas blocks database access, even if other quotas remain. Paid with Overages enabled: usage continues and extra consumed metrics are charged. Previously accrued overages are payable when overages are disabled.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: Pricing FAQ offers “Vegas Blackout”: once per month before invoice close, pick one day whose reads/writes/storage/sync usage charges are removed. Usage counters remain, and Overages must still be enabled to run beyond quota. This is bill relief, not guaranteed automatic spend prevention.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Cloud plan storage and database counts are in C10/C13; an optional per-database size_limit and read/write blocks can be configured, with delete protection. Newer SQL-over-HTTP drivers do not need persistent connections.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: A universal hosted maximum database size, maximum row/BLOB size, concurrent connection/query cap, query-memory ceiling or request-rate ceiling was not located in Cloud Limitations, configuration, SDK transaction docs, pricing or Terms.

facts.label: storage prices
facts.value: Core Turso Cloud is database storage, not a separate hot/archive object-store tariff. AgentFS can put files/state in a SQLite database and sync it; Cloud rows/storage/sync quotas then matter, but local files have no Turso subscription by themselves.

facts.label: file request and retrieval prices
facts.value: No independent per-upload/download/list/retrieval/image-transform rate for AgentFS was found. Cloud use is governed by database usage; file API calls were not mapped to a fixed number of billable row scans/writes or sync bytes in the inspected docs.

facts.label: minimum storage and early deletion
facts.value: Object-store class minimum retention, per-object billing floors and early-deletion tariffs are not applicable to this embedded filesystem/database offer. Cloud subscription and retained database storage remain billable under the SQL plan.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: Both engines document vector dimensions up to 65,536. New Turso engine guide supports dense float32/64, sparse, quantized and binary BLOB vectors, but currently describes similarity search as a linear scan; its README puts vector indexing on the roadmap.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: libSQL has native vector BLOBs and DiskANN approximate indexes, queried explicitly by vector_top_k. Float32 payload storage is 4×dimensions bytes. Index needs ROWID or one-column primary key; composite-PK WITHOUT ROWID is unsupported. Index copies/graph neighbors consume extra storage.

facts.label: embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: Vector docs show inserting embeddings generated by external tools/providers; no bundled embedding-generation/reranker service with included tokens or fixed model rate was established in the vector docs, pricing or Terms.

facts.label: run limits and pricing
facts.value: No matching Turso-hosted 0.5-vCPU/0.5-GB app-job SKU for the approved job workload.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Hosted Free is public self-service with no credit card required. Quickstart supports account signup through the CLI/browser. Terms exclude children under 16 and require legal capacity or guardian agreement; use must obey applicable law/export controls.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Commercial-use scope needs clarification: the March 2024 Terms limit use to internal-business/personal/non-commercial purposes and exclude third-party-benefit use, while current product/pricing pages promote customer-facing production apps and tenants. A country-by-country eligibility list was not located.

facts.label: primary type and other roles
facts.value: Researcher classification: SQL database and managed database service, with embedded/local-first use, vector search, sync and optional AgentFS filesystem/state tooling.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: Cloud includes SQL databases, native vector functions, database tokens, branching, usage analytics, backup/recovery and sync options. Clerk/Auth0 integration can issue database JWTs; it is not an included end-user identity/email/SMS service. No general hosted function/queue worker plan is listed.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: AgentFS adds file operations, key-value state and auditability in a portable SQLite-backed file, with copy-on-write isolation and optional Cloud sync. Agent programs run on infrastructure supplied by the user.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Remote database access: SQL over HTTP with bearer credentials. New Turso remote drivers use fetch without native libraries; libSQL clients are separate. Core official SDK matrix covers TypeScript, Python, Go and Rust; package choice depends on local, synced or remote mode.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: For libSQL, TypeScript ORM support includes Drizzle/Prisma. New remote Turso driver ORM support is not yet listed; local Turso Drizzle support is beta. Embedded/sync packages need appropriate local filesystem/native runtime support; fetch-only remote access suits serverless/edge runtimes.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Cloud database authorization uses JWTs scoped to group/database, read-only or table/action permissions and expiration. Grants are additive, not deny rules; system metadata reads remain allowed. data_add also permits INSERT OR REPLACE, so insert permission alone can replace rows.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: External JWKS providers: Clerk/Auth0 are the documented beta-supported OIDC providers. Without a specifically scoped JWT template, generated tokens can reach all databases/groups. This is an external-auth integration; keep broad platform credentials out of client apps.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Paid Developer and above list IP/AWS VPC allow lists. Empty rules permit any network source, but database credentials are still required; setting both lists requires both IP and VPC rules to match. Pro/Enterprise add BYOK encryption; encryption-at-rest at volume level is documented for all Cloud databases.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: libSQL is a SQLite fork with SQLite file-format/API compatibility; Turso Database is a Rust rewrite with SQLite-oriented SQL/file compatibility. Current Turso COMPAT matrix still has gaps: WITH RECURSIVE missing, several window functions/frame specifications missing, and WITHOUT ROWID experimental/insert-only.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: Hosted Turso limits PRAGMAs: user_version/application_id are read-only; busy_timeout and journal_mode cannot be controlled by clients. Self-hosted Turso README also labels its PostgreSQL dialect/wire frontend experimental; this is not a promised hosted PostgreSQL plan.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Turso engine supports atomic explicit transactions and autocommit; default local WAL mode has a single writer. MVCC with BEGIN CONCURRENT provides snapshot isolation and concurrent nonconflicting writes; write/write conflicts require rollback/retry. One top-level transaction per connection, with savepoints for partial rollback.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: libSQL SDK batch statements run atomically: success commits all, failure rolls back all. Interactive write transactions lock writing until commit/rollback and have a 5-second timeout; replica writes forward to the primary. Read-only transactions can run on replicas.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Cloud branching creates a separate database from a current or point-in-time source; schema/data merging is manual. Branches count toward database quota and storage quota; pricing states no separate branching feature charge. Local Turso/libSQL development also available.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: AWS Cloud uses diskless compute with WAL backed by S3 Express One Zone and database files by S3; commit acknowledgement waits for that storage. Current new-user geographical edge replicas are deprecated; local Embedded Replicas/Turso Sync remain distinct options.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: An exact failover recovery-time/recovery-point target or currently orderable new-user multi-region HA tariff was not located in durability, Cloud overview, deprecated Data Edge, pricing or Terms.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Turso Sync: local reads/writes, explicit push/pull; last push wins for conflicting remote changes. Pull atomically rolls back to synced state, applies remote changes, then replays unpushed local operations. Partial sync lazily fetches missing pages, so uncached data still needs network access.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: libSQL Embedded Replicas: local reads; default writes and read/write transactions go to Cloud primary; optional offline:true permits local writing. Read-your-writes is default for the initiating replica; other replicas see changes after sync/periodic sync. It uses page replication and can amplify transfer.

facts.label: extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: libSQL Cloud preloads JSON, FTS5, R*Tree and SQLean crypto/fuzzy/math/stats/text/UUID 0.24.1. Optional Regexp and sqlite-vec 0.1.3 are described for legacy Fly Pro/Enterprise. New Turso engine has experimental Tantivy-based FTS, not SQLite FTS3/4/5 or arbitrary SQLite shared-library extensions.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: AgentFS TypeScript API supports binary Buffer/string writes, reads, directories and stat sizes. A vendor maximum file size, multipart/resumable-upload limit or hosted-file type restriction was not located in the AgentFS introduction, SDK, sync, Cloud limits or Terms.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: AgentFS supplies CLI/SDK filesystem operations and a user-run NFSv3 server. The NFS example defaults to loopback; remote exposure needs user-managed network protection. No hosted S3-compatible API/operation matrix was located.

facts.label: delivery and private files
facts.value: No managed public/private bucket controls, temporary signed file-download URL service, custom delivery domain or bundled CDN was established from AgentFS/Cloud API, pricing, Terms or privacy docs. Database JWT scopes and NFS firewall rules are different access mechanisms.

facts.label: filters and mixed search
facts.value: Relational WHERE filters can combine with exact vector scans. libSQL DiskANN supports partial indexes and vector_top_k joined to base rows with post-filtering; the example's WHERE can reduce the final matches. libSQL FTS5 and Turso's own FTS are engine-specific keyword options.

facts.label: execution model and languages
facts.value: Not applicable: Turso SQL/AgentFS supplies database/filesystem state, not a general managed app-worker language/runtime plan.

facts.label: delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Application-job retries, ordering, duplicate suppression and dead-letter replay are outside this database/filesystem offer.

facts.label: schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Managed app-queue schedules, payloads and retention are outside this offer.

facts.label: logs and run history
facts.value: Application-job execution logs/history/replay are outside this offer.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Embedded Turso runs in the app process with a persistent local file and compatible SDK/runtime. The shell starts in transient memory until a file is opened. Local libSQL dev server loses changes on stop unless --db-file is used; libSQL Docker requires a persistent /var/lib/sqld volume.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Self-hosted libSQL offers primary/replica Docker deployments; local Turso sync server implements the sync protocol for development without Cloud. Cloud proprietary orchestration, managed PITR, dashboard/organization features and SLA are not reproduced by merely running that server.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Cloud groups have a selected primary region; closest region is chosen unless --location overrides it. More than one group requires Scaler, Pro or Enterprise. Location API docs list example AWS Tokyo, Mumbai, Ireland, Virginia, Ohio and Oregon codes; private-endpoint guide supports those six regional setups.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Existing legacy Fly regional replicas and new-user AWS deployments have different availability. BYOC is Enterprise on current pricing; durability guide says Pro/Enterprise can use their own S3 buckets but still describes customer-account compute as future work. Exact current full-compute BYOC scope requires clarification.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Exports: turso db export writes a SQLite snapshot file, which may omit latest changes until SDK sync catches up. Local-development guide also documents .dump to SQL then importing with SQLite. Encrypted export requires the proper key.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Cloud account cancellation is requested through support/contact or account settings under Terms; subscriptions generally run to the paid term end without refund. Account termination may destroy content. Privacy retention can continue for legal/billing/dispute/backup purposes.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Paid deleted databases/groups can be recovered for five days, with admin/owner permission, restore enabled and regional support. Free deletions are not guaranteed recoverable by upgrading later. Disable-restore blocks restoration but does not remove deleted listings immediately; delete protection can prevent deletion.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: An exact deadline to purge every hosted copy, log and backup after account/database closure was not located.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Cloud backups occur automatically at COMMIT. PITR windows: Free 24 hours, Developer 10 days, Scaler 30 days, Pro 90 days; Enterprise pricing lists 90 days. Restore creates a new database/connection string and needs a new database token or group token.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Paid deleted-database recovery is a separate five-day feature with no additional recovery fee, subject to regional support. Self-hosted/embedded files have no vendor-operated PITR window; the operator must retain/export/restore copies and account for WAL/sync state.

facts.label: file recovery and protection
facts.value: AgentFS copy-on-write isolation, portable single-file state and audit records help inspect agent changes; optional Cloud sync can store remote state. Sync is not independent historical backup: deletion recovery/PITR follows the containing database's plan if supported.

facts.label: file recovery and protection
facts.value: A separate AgentFS accidental-file-delete recovery/version-retention window and file-lock/WORM guarantee were not located in AgentFS intro, TypeScript SDK, sync, PITR/recovery, Terms or privacy pages.

facts.label: identity and old names
facts.value: Turso is the product/project name. Turso Cloud hosts libSQL (a SQLite fork) and the newer Turso Database engine (a Rust rewrite). The rewrite was formerly called Limbo; its rename was announced 2025-01-21.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: Self-hosted/embedded: Turso Database is MIT licensed; libSQL is also MIT licensed under its own repository LICENSE.md. Local use does not require a Cloud account or subscription.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: Hosted Cloud runs under Turso's Terms of Use. The 2025-01-21 roadmap notice explicitly says the newer multitenant Cloud server is proprietary; this did not relicense the open-source libSQL server. Self-hosting libSQL is not hosting the identical Cloud platform.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: AgentFS companion CLI/SDK: project README states MIT license; it runs on user-supplied infrastructure and optionally syncs to Cloud.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: 2026-10-02 acquisition announcement: Turso is joining Supabase. The notice says existing databases, APIs and workflows continue and the engine remains open source/actively developed. The acquisition notice, current docs/changelog and status page were rechecked on 2026-11-09; no product shutdown notice was found.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Cloud libSQL remains production-ready; the newer Turso engine on Cloud is explicitly early preview. AgentFS is beta. Self-hosted engine is described as in production, but quickstart still warns that several experimental flags are not for critical data.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: 2025-01-21: geographical edge replicas, Multi-DB Schemas and hosted ATTACH were withdrawn for new users, with existing paid use retained. 2026-05-03: paid active-database limits removed; current paid plans include unlimited databases and active databases.

facts.label: vendor home and main markets
facts.value: US contact address: 2093 Philadelphia Pike, #6336, Claymont, Delaware 19703. March 2024 Terms name CHISELSTRIKE INC.; current pricing-page organization metadata says Turso, Inc. No updated public contract identity reconciles those names after the acquisition.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: Free/Developer/Scaler: Community support. Pro: priority email and Slack; Enterprise: 24×7 priority email and Slack. Current pricing FAQ directs account/billing tickets through dashboard Support; info@turso.tech is general inquiries only. Public status: https://status.turso.tech/.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: No numeric contracted uptime SLA/service-credit schedule was located in current pricing, Cloud docs, Terms or durability page. Durability page advertises 99.999999999% data durability for users registering/upgrading after 2025-03-17, not query-service availability.

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: Cloud Free includes 720 node-hours per account lifetime.

facts.value: At USD $500 of spend in a billing cycle, Typesense may invoice the account early; this does not cap further use or charges.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: The exact behavior when a Free allowance is consumed without a payment method, and whether a usage alert can stop all billable meters, was not published in the Free, billing, or termination pages checked.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits

facts.label: Vector/index limits

facts.label: Primary type and other roles
facts.value: Primary: typo-tolerant full-text search engine and search database. Secondary: vector/semantic and hybrid search, filtering, faceting, and geosearch.

facts.label: Primary type and other roles
facts.value: Typesense is designed as a secondary search index, not a replacement for the application's primary source-of-truth database; it does not crawl the web for customer data.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Server provides collections/documents, indexing, text and vector search, filtering, faceting, and REST APIs.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Cloud provides managed cluster provisioning, monitoring, and operations; optional features include high availability, backups, capacity auto-upgrade, and support plans.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Neither edition is presented as end-user authentication, general object/file storage, a user-code function platform, or a durable job queue. Cloud's team access controls manage the Typesense account and clusters.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Typesense uses a RESTful HTTP API with JSON; the default server API port is 8108.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Official API clients include JavaScript/TypeScript, PHP, Python, and Ruby. Official and community client support varies by language.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Search-only scoped API keys can be used from a browser; admin/bootstrap keys must remain server-side. Keys can be restricted by collection, action, filter, and selected fields.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Cloud cluster clients use the Typesense API; separate Cloud Management APIs support cluster and account operations and require corresponding API capabilities.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Docker, package installs, and platform binaries are documented for self-hosting; the install guide covers Linux and macOS architectures.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Server API keys can be restricted to collections and actions; scoped search keys can include filters and field restrictions.

facts.label: Data access controls

facts.label: Data access controls

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Self-hosted network exposure, TLS termination, firewalling, key rotation, and access policy remain operator responsibilities; Typesense recommends securing the server/API key.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: Typesense is a document-oriented search database: records are JSON documents grouped into collections with defined fields; it is not a relational SQL database.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: Querying uses Typesense's search, filter, sort, facet, and vector APIs over HTTP/JSON; SQL compatibility is not documented.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: The official use-case guide advises keeping an application's primary/source-of-truth database elsewhere and synchronizing searchable records into Typesense.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: No multi-document transaction API or transactional isolation guarantee was found in the document, collection, syncing, or API pages checked.

facts.label: Test environments and branches
facts.value: Cloud supports cloning a cluster into a new cluster, including a selected region/configuration; the new cluster is separately billed. This is a copy workflow, not copy-on-write branching.

facts.label: Test environments and branches
facts.value: No native copy-on-write collection or database branching feature was found in the collection, Cloud, clone, or snapshot docs checked.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Self-hosted high availability uses Raft-based replication; the HA guide describes writes being routed through a leader and replicas maintaining copies.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Cloud HA clusters use 3–7 nodes with replicated datasets; a 3-node cluster tolerates one node failure, while 5 and 7 nodes tolerate two and three respectively.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Cloud HA can be enabled but the help page says it cannot later be disabled; additional HA nodes increase throughput, not per-cluster data capacity.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Typesense accepts record inserts, updates, deletes, and searches through its API, but an application-client offline read/write store or conflict-resolution sync mechanism was not found in the client and syncing guides checked.

facts.label: Extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Typesense supports full-text search, filters, facets, sorting, geo fields, and dense vector search, with hybrid keyword/vector querying and rank fusion.

facts.label: Extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Typesense collections support field schemas and document indexing; it is not an SQL database with third-party SQL extensions.

facts.label: Upload and file limits
facts.value: Not applicable: Typesense ingests search documents and vectors, not end-user files into a hosted file bucket.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Not applicable: Typesense does not provide an S3-compatible application object-storage API.

facts.value: Typesense supports hybrid keyword and dense vector search, filtering, faceting, and ranking controls; vectors can be supplied by the app or generated with a supported embedding model.

facts.label: Filters and mixed search
facts.value: Search-only API keys can embed filters and collection/action restrictions for multi-tenant access, but application authorization still has to issue the right scoped key.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: Not applicable: Typesense is a database/search service and does not host arbitrary customer worker or function code.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Not applicable: Typesense does not offer a user task scheduler or durable application queue.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Not applicable: Typesense does not offer user-job execution history. Cloud operational logs are for the database service, not a workflow runner.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: The system guide recommends at least 2 vCPU and roughly 2–3× RAM versus indexed data on disk; vector indexes need about 7 bytes per dimension per record, and built-in embedding models can add 2–6 GB RAM.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Server persists data locally and rebuilds indexes after restart; self-host operators must manage storage, backups, updates, TLS/network security, monitoring, and availability.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps

facts.label: embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: No included embedding-generation/reranking token allowance or per-model tariff was established from managed-Postgres product, extension list, pricing, BYOC or Terms. Ubicloud AI inference is a separate service; database hosting does not establish that its model usage is bundled.
