facts.value: No separate per-invocation/vCPU-second pg_cron tariff is listed; allocated database capacity is billed. Managed max concurrent SQL jobs, job-specific memory/time cap and a standalone 0.5-vCPU/0.5-GB worker shape were not established in configuration/pricing, pg_cron docs or Terms.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Managed service: public signup; active valid card required before creating resources. Card verification may preauthorize up to USD 5, cancelled after verification; bank release can take up to two weeks. Terms require age 18 or otherwise sufficient lawful consent/capacity.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Terms allow customer-facing products/end users subject to customer responsibilities. They require a DPA for customer personal-data processing and separate written agreement for HIPAA PHI/GDPR special-category data. Published restrictions include sanctions/prohibited parties and export-control compliance.

facts.label: primary type and other roles
facts.value: Researcher classification: managed SQL database, with optional HA standbys, read replicas, PITR and PostgreSQL extensions. Separate Ubicloud products include VMs, Kubernetes, AI inference and GitHub Actions runners.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: Included database operations: backups/PITR, health monitoring, configurable HA, read replicas, PgBouncer, metrics/log export, upgrades and maintenance windows. PostgreSQL SQL/users/extensions are provided; general app auth, file delivery and worker hosting are not established as an included Postgres bundle.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Standard PostgreSQL connections: postgres:// URL, psql/libpq and JDBC formats, plus environment/YAML connection representations. Superuser connection is provided; create narrower app users yourself. Bundled PgBouncer is selectable for pooling; public/private DNS are available.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: TLS minimum is 1.3 by default. New instances use a public-CA certificate chain; older self-signed-CA instances require the downloadable CA bundle for verification. Prefer documented verify-full connection settings.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Database data access: superuser is supplied, enabling creation of least-privilege SQL roles. PostgreSQL row security supports row policies, but superusers and BYPASSRLS roles bypass it; table owners ordinarily bypass unless FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY applies.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Public internet reachability is the documented default; restrict client CIDRs using firewall rules or connect private subnets/use private DNS. API also has restrict_by_default to require allow rules. Project management access uses Ubicloud ABAC and is separate from database SQL roles.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: Database boot/data disks encrypted at rest by default using separate per-VM data/key-encryption keys; client/control-plane/server traffic and backups are encrypted in transit, and backups at rest with separate keys and per-database bucket isolation.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: Native PostgreSQL with standard SQL/wire protocol; provisioning API lists major versions 16, 17 and 18. Bundled PgBouncer handles connection pooling. Major upgrades go to the next version and may require app compatibility testing.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Standard PostgreSQL transactions/MVCC: upstream default READ COMMITTED gives a new committed-data snapshot per statement. REPEATABLE READ and SERIALIZABLE are supported; serialization conflicts can require whole-transaction retry. Async standby availability does not imply committed primary writes survive every primary failure.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Backup/Restore Fork creates a new instance at a selected restore time. Major Upgrade provides Create a test fork for staging. No copy-on-write merge workflow, free branch quota or automatic fork expiry was located in these guides; new allocated resources follow instance billing.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: No standby: primary only, automatically monitored/healed but recovery may need operator work. One standby: same size as primary, asynchronous by default, optional synchronous. Two standbys: same size each, synchronous by default with acknowledgement from at least one, optional asynchronous.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Read replicas follow native PostgreSQL replication, isolate read/reporting workloads and can be promoted. HA adds one/two standbys with console pricing; a complete public replica/standby tariff and cross-region placement/replication promise was not located.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Native replication slots are advertised on the AWS page, and pglogical/pglogical_origin are supported extensions. A bundled app-client realtime subscription/offline-write sync/conflict-resolution contract was not located in the database product, Connection, replica/extension docs or Terms.

facts.label: extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Current supported extension list includes PostGIS 3.6.2, pg_trgm 1.6, pglogical 2.4.6, pg_cron 1.6, vector 0.8.2, VectorChord vchord 1.1.1 and vchord_bm25 0.3.0, among others. PostgreSQL superuser access permits extension setup within the supported installation.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: App-file single/multipart/resumable upload limits are outside this offer.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: No app-facing S3 bucket API is established as part of the subscription.

facts.label: delivery and private files
facts.value: Public/private object delivery, signed app-file links, custom file domains and CDN are outside this subscription.

facts.label: filters and mixed search
facts.value: pgvector supports exact scan or HNSW/IVFFlat approximate search with SQL filters. Approximate filtering occurs after index candidates and can return fewer results; iterative scans/settings, partial indexes and partitioning can help. VectorChord/BM25 extensions are separately listed, not one identical index implementation.

facts.label: execution model and languages
facts.value: pg_cron 1.6 is supported for scheduled SQL commands inside PostgreSQL. Jobs use the database's processes/resources; this is not a general hosted container/function worker runtime. Separate Ubicloud VMs, Kubernetes and GitHub runners are outside this Postgres record.

facts.label: delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Upstream pg_cron can run distinct jobs in parallel but only one instance of the same job at a time; an overlapping next run waits for the preceding run to finish. This is schedule serialization, not a documented app-message exactly-once/retry/dead-letter contract.

facts.label: schedules and queue retention
facts.value: pg_cron supports five-field cron schedules and 1–59-second intervals; cron.timezone is configurable, upstream default GMT. No managed app-queue payload-byte/retention or delayed-message contract is established by that SQL scheduler.

facts.label: logs and run history
facts.value: pg_cron exposes cron.job_run_details; upstream records are not cleaned automatically, users can delete their own history and can disable logging. Actual Ubicloud pg_cron cleanup/retention defaults were not located in extension/config/Terms docs. Separate PostgreSQL/PgBouncer console logs retain up to 7 days, with max 24-hour query span.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Self-hosting Ubicloud means running its Ruby-based control plane and backing PostgreSQL, then leasing/preparing bare-metal data-plane servers. Published demo uses Docker Compose and Hetzner cloudify tooling; README specifies Ubuntu 24.04 for that setup. Operator supplies networking/IPs, durable disks, security, upgrades, backup storage and recovery.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Managed HA/PITR capabilities are present in open platform code/docs, but deployment/configuration and operational support are the self-host operator's work. The quickstart's control-plane containers are a demo, not a published cheap production hardware minimum or full availability guarantee.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Metal locations: eu-central-h1 = Hetzner Falkenstein, Germany; eu-north-h1 = Hetzner Helsinki, Finland; us-east-a2 = Leaseweb Manassas, Virginia, US. AWS region/account selection is separate; exact GCP preview regions were not established.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Backup docs say EU-instance backups stay in the EU and US-instance backups in the US. However Terms §4.8 allow transfers to other regions/jurisdictions at Ubicloud's discretion unless agreed otherwise in writing. Region selection alone is not an unconditional residency promise.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Exit/export: native PostgreSQL pg_dump supplies logical SQL/custom/directory/tar archives; backup downloads expose WAL-G physical base/WAL files using temporary read-only bucket credentials. Downloads default on AWS, require support enablement on metal, unavailable on GCP or read replicas; use primary and Postgres:view permission.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Delete through Settings; backups retained 7 days after database deletion and support can restore the deleted database. Terms allow immediate account termination/data destruction and generally non-refundable fees, so service-level recovery is not an account-termination preservation guarantee.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Exact purge deadline for every database copy, backup, log and account record was not found in backup/deletion docs, Terms or Privacy Notice. Privacy Notice covers account data, with purpose/legal retention; it does not itself set database-content erasure timing.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: All advertised metal plans include daily full backups and 7-day PITR. WAL files archived every 60 seconds or 16 MB of WAL, whichever comes first. Restore selects a target minute and creates a new instance. Longer retention requires support.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Backup files use an internal blob service with per-database bucket credentials; docs describe erasure coding across four servers, tolerating two unavailable servers. EU instances back up in EU, US in US. Seven-day backup retention continues after deletion, with support-led restore.

facts.label: file recovery and protection
facts.value: Object-file versioning/WORM/deleted-upload recovery is outside the Postgres offer.

facts.label: identity and old names
facts.value: Ubicloud Postgres / Ubicloud Managed PostgreSQL, operated by Ubicloud. It is a managed PostgreSQL service within the broader Ubicloud cloud platform; no former product name was established.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: Hosted service on Ubicloud metal/AWS; Google Cloud is labelled preview on the Postgres product page. AWS BYOC is privately supported for select customers, with Ubicloud managing resources in the customer's AWS account.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: Self-managed Ubicloud platform source is GNU AGPL version 3. PostgreSQL itself has the separate PostgreSQL License. Ubicloud Overview explicitly supports managing the Postgres service yourself; the repository contains platform/control-plane software.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Operating: metal and AWS are offered; Google Cloud is preview with engineer-led onboarding. No overall shutdown, sunset or acquisition notice found in official product, current docs and provider announcements checked.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: April 27, 2026 price-change notice: new deployments changed May 1 and existing deployments June 1; metal regions affected, AWS unchanged. That notice lists lower example prices than current pricing/product pages, so its historical amounts are not used as today's quotes.

facts.label: vendor home and main markets
facts.value: Ubicloud B.V., Netherlands, contracts with EEA residents; Ubicloud Inc., United States, contracts elsewhere. Payments go to Ubicloud Inc. Privacy notice gives Amstelveen and San Francisco contact addresses.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: Support: community forum for all; managed-service customers also get account-specific email support at support@ubicloud.com. Guaranteed response times/enterprise terms require contacting support. Public component/incident status is https://status.ubicloud.com/.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: AWS Postgres marketing advertises 99.99% uptime SLA with HA and 24/7 database-engineer support. A public service-credit schedule, qualifying tier/standby conditions, claim procedure or numeric small-plan response-time contract was not located in support, HA/pricing or Terms.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Ubicloud Postgres news check 2026-11-09: no sale, shutdown, rebrand, or customer-data incident found. Checked the official company blog, PostgreSQL product/docs and status page, plus a quick web search. The status page showed PostgreSQL operational; it listed a same-day partial outage for separate Actions/Webhooks services, with mitigation reported.

facts.label: Trial usage caps

facts.label: Free file-type eligibility
facts.value: The April 2026 release notes say Free-plan restrictions on non-image uploads were removed; the upload guide still says only images are available on Free and asks for a card to upload other file types.

facts.label: Other plan limits
facts.value: File type filtering and a project-specific maximum file size are configurable. The maximum-size setting in documentation supports values up to 5 TB.

facts.label: Inactivity rules
facts.value: No inactivity-based pause, sleep, or automatic expiration of a Free account was stated in pricing, billing, storage docs, or terms checked.

facts.label: Temporary upload expiry
facts.value: An upload explicitly marked unstored is removed after 24 hours; new accounts using the default auto setting normally follow the project auto-store setting, which is on by default.

facts.label: Stored file retention
facts.value: A file marked stored remains until explicitly deleted, subject to account/service termination rules.

facts.label: Free price
facts.value: Free: $0 per month, USD, for ongoing use within its limits.

facts.label: Pro yearly price
facts.value: Pro yearly billing displays $66 per month equivalent, USD, with the page advertising 16% savings; the subscription fee is paid upfront for the annual period.

facts.label: Pro monthly price
facts.value: Pro monthly billing: $79 per month, USD.

facts.label: Business yearly price
facts.value: Business yearly billing displays $166 per month equivalent, USD, with the page advertising 16% savings; charged upfront for the annual period.

facts.label: Business monthly price
facts.value: Business monthly billing: $199 per month, USD.

facts.label: Enterprise price
facts.value: Enterprise plan price and minimum commitment are custom; contact sales for a quote.

facts.label: Currency and taxes
facts.value: Terms say all fees are payable in USD and listed service fees exclude applicable taxes, which the customer pays.

facts.label: Renewal and payment
facts.value: Paid subscriptions renew for their chosen monthly or annual period unless cancelled through the customer portal before the period ends; paid fees are non-refundable under the terms.

facts.label: What counts as operations
facts.value: Operations are consumed by Upload API/REST API requests, outgoing webhooks, uploads, image transformations, video processing, document conversion, and other file-management actions.

facts.label: Upload operation formula
facts.value: A successful upload uses API request(s), plus one upload-volume operation per 100 MB rounded up and one virus-scan operation per 100 MB rounded up. The guide examples show one API request for 20 MB and two for a 250 MB multipart upload.

facts.label: Image transformation operations
facts.value: A unique uncached image URL costs one operation regardless of the number of standard actions in its transformation chain; cached requests cost zero operations.

facts.label: Extra image operations
facts.value: AVIF compression, animated image optimization, and face-detection transformations use 2 operations per request; background removal uses 750 operations.

facts.label: Video operation meter
facts.value: Video processing costs 100 operations per minute in the general file-management table; adaptive streaming is separately calculated per emitted rendition, with resolution and codec multipliers and source duration rounded up to 10-second chunks.

facts.label: File-analysis and conversion operations
facts.value: Auto-tagging and unsafe-content detection each use 5 operations per image; document conversion uses 100 operations per 50 MB.

facts.label: Operation rounding and overage rates
facts.value: Account operation totals round up to the nearest 1,000. Pro overage is $1.60 per additional 1,000 operations; Business is $0.80 per additional 1,000; Enterprise custom rates start as low as $0.10 per 1,000.

facts.label: Traffic usage meter
facts.value: Traffic counts bytes delivered from Uploadcare CDN to end users and bytes transferred between the CDN and Uploadcare servers.

facts.label: Storage usage meter
facts.value: Stored usage is the total original file size in the account, measured on average across the billing period; cached image transformations do not count as stored files.

facts.label: Usage fee billing time
facts.value: Subscription charges are paid in advance; overage usage fees are charged at the end of each month in which the plan allowance was exceeded.

facts.label: Upload and API request rate prices
facts.value: The public price table meters operations, traffic, and storage; it does not publish a separate price for each request endpoint.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Not applicable: Uploadcare is a managed file upload, storage, processing, and delivery service, not user-controlled compute that can be paused or scaled to zero.

facts.label: Traffic directions
facts.value: Uploadcare traffic includes CDN-to-user delivery and data transfers between the CDN and Uploadcare servers.

facts.label: Included transfer and overage
facts.value: Free includes 5 GB/month; Pro 25 GB/month then $0.35 USD/GB; Business 125 GB/month then $0.25 USD/GB; Enterprise custom, as low as $0.04 USD/GB.

facts.label: Upload ingress
facts.value: The docs do not list a separate user-to-Upload-API ingress rate. They define traffic as CDN-to-user delivery and transfers between Uploadcare CDN and its servers; upload requests and file size still count as operations.

facts.label: Customer-owned storage transfer
facts.value: Enterprise can upload directly to its own AWS S3 bucket; AWS storage, requests, and networking charges for that bucket are separate from Uploadcare's published managed-service rates.

facts.label: Paid-plan overages
facts.value: Pricing says paid plan limits are soft; usage above included operations, traffic, and storage is billed automatically at published overage rates.

facts.label: Free-plan over-limit action
facts.value: Pricing FAQ says exceeding Free limits temporarily suspends service until the next month; terms say certain Free subscribers may be offered an option to unblock by paying overages.

facts.label: Spend caps and budget controls
facts.value: No customer-set dollar spending cap or guaranteed hard cutoff was identified in the pricing, billing, or terms pages checked.

facts.label: Usage reporting
facts.value: Dashboard analytics report operations, uploads, storage, traffic, API requests, CDN traffic, and API error breakdowns.

facts.label: Free storage allowance
facts.value: Free includes 1 GB stored-file capacity at $0 per month.

facts.label: Pro managed storage
facts.value: Pro includes 10 GB; extra storage is $0.35 per GB of average storage per billing month, USD.

facts.label: Business managed storage
facts.value: Business includes 50 GB; extra storage is $0.25 per GB of average storage per billing month, USD.

facts.label: Enterprise managed storage
facts.value: Enterprise storage allowance and final price are custom; price page lists storage as low as $0.03 per GB, USD, per billing period.

facts.label: Storage classes and replicas
facts.value: Uploadcare lists one managed storage meter, not hot/archive tiers or a public replica surcharge.

facts.label: Upload request operation cost
facts.value: A successful 20 MB upload uses 3 operations in the billing example; a 250 MB upload uses 8, due to requests, 100 MB rounding, and virus scanning.

facts.label: Image request operation cost
facts.value: An uncached unique transformed image URL costs 1 operation; cached delivery costs 0 operations.

facts.label: Image enhancement operation cost
facts.value: Advanced processing has extra operation counts: AVIF, animated-image optimization, and face-detection use 2 per request; background removal uses 750.

facts.label: Video operation cost
facts.value: Video processing is listed at 100 operations per minute; adaptive streaming uses per-rendition resolution/codec multipliers and rounds source duration up to 10 seconds.

facts.label: Document and file analysis operation cost
facts.value: Document conversion uses 100 operations per 50 MB; auto-tagging and unsafe-content detection use 5 operations per image each.

facts.label: Billable operation rounding
facts.value: Total operations are rounded up to the nearest 1,000; paid plans charge overage per additional 1,000 operations.

facts.label: Minimum storage and duration
facts.value: No minimum object size, minimum billed capacity, or early-deletion period was stated in Uploadcare's pricing or storage docs.

facts.label: Temporary versus stored files
facts.value: Files set not to store are removed after 24 hours; stored files remain until explicitly deleted.

facts.label: Billing after deletion
facts.value: Deleting near the end of a billing period does not erase the storage already counted; storage is based on the average amount held during the billing period.

facts.label: Self-service access
facts.value: The pricing page offers a Free plan and self-service paid plans; no account was created and no signup form was submitted.

facts.label: Free-plan use restriction
facts.value: Free is labelled “Personal use only”; the Pro plan is positioned for production apps and websites.

facts.label: Free-plan trial status
facts.value: The Free plan is ongoing, not just the 14-day Pro trial. Uploadcare's FAQ says the Free plan is free forever, subject to plan changes for future customers.

facts.label: Payment card for Free
facts.value: Whether a card is required depends on file type and the current signup path: the upload guide says non-image uploads require a card for KYC, while the April 2026 release notes say Free-plan non-image upload restrictions were removed.

facts.label: Country restrictions
facts.value: The terms prohibit use by people or entities restricted by applicable U.S. export-control and sanctions rules; no general country-by-country eligibility page was found.

facts.label: Using the service with an app
facts.value: The service license permits integrating Uploadcare with proprietary applications and making the service available to the app's customers in conjunction with those applications. It bars unsupported use on behalf of third parties and resale/sublicensing of the service.

facts.label: Primary type
facts.value: Hosted file and media infrastructure for uploading, storing, processing, optimizing, and delivering files through a CDN.

facts.label: Other roles
facts.value: Includes user file intake, image transformations, video processing and adaptive streaming, document conversion, malware screening, file management APIs, and delivery.

facts.label: Product boundary
facts.value: The standard product is file infrastructure, not a general-purpose database, authentication provider, or app compute host.

facts.label: Upload and storage
facts.value: Uploadcare provides a hosted Upload API, file uploader, project-based file storage, and CDN-ready file URLs.

facts.label: File management
facts.value: REST API supports listing, searching, reading metadata, storing, copying, tagging, and deleting files; webhooks report file events.

facts.label: Media processing
facts.value: Includes image URL transformations and optimization, asynchronous video processing/streaming, and document conversion.

facts.label: Delivery and integrations
facts.value: Files are delivered through Uploadcare's global CDN. Enterprise plan material lists connecting AWS S3 storage; this can be a separate storage destination.

facts.label: APIs and protocols
facts.value: Uploadcare documents its own HTTPS Upload API, REST API, and URL-based delivery/transformation API.

facts.label: Official backend and mobile libraries
facts.value: Official integrations include JavaScript, PHP, Python, Ruby/Rails, Java, Go, Rust, Swift, and Kotlin.

facts.label: Front-end and upload integrations
facts.value: Official uploader integrations include JavaScript, React, Angular, Vue, Svelte, Next.js, iOS, and Android. The uploader supports browser and mobile file selection and multipart uploads.

facts.label: Default file visibility
facts.value: Newly uploaded files are available on Uploadcare's CDN by default. URLs use a project subdomain and a UUID; an unguessable URL is not access control.

facts.label: Signed delivery
facts.value: Signed URLs are available on all plans, including Free. A backend signs a time-limited token; the CDN rejects missing, expired, or mismatched tokens.

facts.label: Public-domain bypass
facts.value: To fully close unsigned access, disable the public subdomain and, for older projects, disable the legacy ucarecdn.com domain.

facts.label: Signed upload control
facts.value: Signed uploads are off until enabled. A server-issued short-lived credential can restrict upload endpoints and operation counts.

facts.label: Project keys and access
facts.value: Public API keys identify a project; secret keys authorize file-management REST calls and signed uploads. Project collaborators can access project files, settings, and secret keys.

facts.label: Additional file controls
facts.value: Project settings support MIME-type filtering, maximum file size, malware rules, EXIF removal, signed uploads, signed URLs, and search-indexing controls. Search indexing is disabled by default.

facts.label: Plan file-size maximums
facts.value: Free 500 MB/file; Pro 1 GB/file; Business 10 GB/file; Enterprise up to 5 TB/file.

facts.label: Multipart and large uploads
facts.value: Multipart uploading supports large files up to 5 TB; files larger than 100 MiB should use multipart rather than the direct upload endpoint.

facts.label: Resumable and parallel upload
facts.value: Mobile SDKs support pausing and continuing multipart uploads; uploader settings control chunk size and concurrent file uploads.

facts.label: File types and sources
facts.value: Uploadcare accepts images, video, audio, documents, archives, and other files; sources include local files, cameras, URLs, and listed cloud services.

facts.label: File validation
facts.value: Project settings can restrict file size and MIME types; the service determines MIME type from file contents, not only the extension/header.

facts.label: Upload authentication
facts.value: Direct uploads can use the project public key; enabling Signed Uploads requires a valid short-lived server-issued token/signature.

facts.label: API compatibility
facts.value: Uploadcare documents its own Upload API, REST API, and URL API; no S3-compatible Uploadcare API endpoint or S3 operation parity table was listed in those docs.

facts.label: Own-S3 integration
facts.value: Enterprise can upload directly to its AWS S3 bucket and process/deliver files with documented limits; adaptive bitrate streaming is unavailable in this mode.

facts.label: Import and export tools
facts.value: The CLI/API can download files, upload files, and manage them in batches; this is a migration path rather than S3 protocol compatibility.

facts.label: CDN and public delivery
facts.value: Every uploaded file is made available through a global CDN using a project subdomain; custom CDN CNAMEs are supported according to plan.

facts.label: Private files
facts.value: Signed delivery requires a valid time-limited backend-generated token; it is available on Free and paid plans.

facts.label: CDN hostname charges
facts.value: Custom CDN/Proxy CNAME is listed as $25 USD per month on Pro, one included on Business, and custom on Enterprise.

facts.label: Egress and delivery cost
facts.value: CDN delivery uses the combined traffic meter; there is no separate public CDN-request fee in the pricing table.

facts.label: CDN caching
facts.value: Uploaded files are cached for up to one year by default; deleting a file invalidates its CDN versions, usually near-instantly.

facts.label: Default indexing privacy
facts.value: CDN responses tell search engines not to index project files by default; this behavior can be changed in project settings.

facts.label: Service and CDN geography
facts.value: Uploadcare advertises a geographically distributed global CDN; no selectable CDN region or app-side CDN region pinning was described.

facts.label: Managed storage location
facts.value: The current subprocessor list identifies AWS as the cloud-service provider for data in Uploadcare storage and lists the United States, but it does not state a specific AWS region or customer-selected managed-storage region.

facts.label: Customer S3 region
facts.value: In Enterprise's own-S3 mode, the customer selects/configures the AWS bucket, so its AWS region is customer controlled; adaptive bitrate streaming is not supported for files uploaded directly to that bucket.

facts.label: File export
facts.value: Files can be listed/read through REST API and downloaded with the Uploadcare CLI; CLI docs show mirroring all stored files with pagination and parallel downloads.

facts.label: Customer-managed backup
facts.value: Uploadcare can copy stored files to a connected AWS S3 bucket; the storage guide says one bucket can be connected per project.

facts.label: File deletion
facts.value: A file can be deleted through Dashboard or API; batch file storage/deletion APIs handle up to 100 files per request. CDN cached versions are invalidated, normally near-instantly.

facts.label: Project deletion
facts.value: The CLI warns that deleting a project is permanent and removes all files and settings associated with it.

facts.label: Account termination and access
facts.value: On termination, the current terms say the right to use Uploadcare ends immediately and the customer loses access to account data.

facts.label: Data removal timing
facts.value: Privacy policy says account data may be retained for varying periods after closure, never longer than 12 months; exact file-content deletion timing is not specified there.

facts.label: Migration path
facts.value: Uploadcare's CLI/API can list and download files; its Enterprise pricing offer advertises free migration. I found no fixed public migration price or one-click archive export limit.

facts.label: File versioning
facts.value: Uploaded files are immutable; a new local copy can create a new file version. No automatic user-configurable version-history retention period was published.

facts.label: Backup destination
facts.value: Stored files can be copied to a connected AWS S3 bucket; only one S3 bucket can be connected to a project.

facts.label: Backup schedule
facts.value: The storage page says backups occur “on a timely basis,” but does not publish a fixed schedule or point-in-time recovery guarantee.

facts.label: S3 connected-bucket deletion
facts.value: In connected-S3 mode, files marked removed are permanently deleted from the customer's S3 bucket 90 days later; unstored uploads are marked removed after one day.

facts.label: Recovery responsibility
facts.value: Uploadcare's public docs describe file deletion and S3 copying, but no built-in restore-from-backup workflow or immutable backup lock was found.

facts.label: Identity and old names
facts.value: Uploadcare is a hosted file infrastructure service from Uploadcare Inc. Official homepage: https://uploadcare.com/.

facts.label: Former product names
facts.value: No former product name was identified in the official homepage, company blog, current documentation, or acquisition announcement checked.

facts.label: Hosting model
facts.value: Uploadcare operates the hosted service. Official SDKs and CLI are client tools; the checked docs do not offer a self-hosted Uploadcare server edition.

facts.label: Software license
facts.value: A self-hosted server license is not applicable to the hosted Uploadcare service. The terms grant a time-bounded right to use the hosted service, not a license to run its platform software.

facts.label: Lifecycle
facts.value: Uploadcare has current public plans, product documentation, API guides, and release notes.

facts.label: Service status
facts.value: Upload API, REST API, CDN, processing, document processing, video processing, dashboard, and website were marked operational on the status page.

facts.label: Company ownership
facts.value: Uploadcare announced that it joined Tiugo Technologies in January 2024; Tiugo's official announcement calls this an acquisition. Uploadcare is listed among Tiugo's portfolio brands.

facts.label: Shutdown and sunset search
facts.value: No shutdown or sunset notice was found in the Uploadcare blog, release notes, product/pricing pages, status page, or Tiugo's acquisition news checked.

facts.label: Recent activity
facts.value: Uploadcare release notes list changes through 2026-10-20; the blog index lists posts through 2026-10-07.

facts.label: Vendor location
facts.value: Uploadcare Inc. identifies itself as a U.S. company. Its current terms give a Boston, Massachusetts contact address; the privacy policy identifies U.S. registration.

facts.label: Markets
facts.value: Uploadcare markets its developer file service to customers worldwide. U.S. trade and sanctions restrictions apply under the terms.

facts.label: Support by plan
facts.value: Pricing lists community support for Free, email support for Pro, priority email support for Business, and enterprise support with optional private Slack and dedicated customer success.

facts.label: Public status page
facts.value: Uploadcare maintains a public component status page.

facts.label: Availability SLA
facts.value: The formal SLA lists monthly uptime of at least 99.9% for Upload API and REST API and 99.99% for CDN; the pricing FAQ says paid plans include a 99.9% SLA.

facts.label: SLA remedy
facts.value: SLA credits are applied to future payments, require a claim within the stated window, and are not issued if the credit is $1 or less.

facts.label: Support response time
facts.value: No guaranteed response-time target by plan was found in the pricing page, docs, SLA, or terms checked.

facts.value: Financial overages, vendor budget alerts and a hosted account spend cap are not applicable. Native maxmemory/eviction controls constrain server memory behavior, not the hosting invoice.

facts.label: overages and bill controls
facts.value: For self-hosted 64-bit builds, maxmemory defaults to no configured limit. The default policy is noeviction; write commands needing more memory can return errors, while configured eviction policies can delete keys.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: The 9.1.3 example config documents maxclients 10000, constrained by OS file descriptors/resources. Standalone logical databases default to 16; these numbers are configurable, not free-plan quotas.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: The configurable protocol limit for a bulk-string element normally defaults to 512 mb. Overall stored data is limited by configured memory and real host resources, with data-structure/index overhead.

facts.label: capacity and connection limits
facts.value: The live Valkey JSON guide describes a configurable document-size limit (default 0, no module-imposed size limit). Its default nesting-depth limit is 128, also documented in the 1.0.3 README.

facts.label: storage prices
facts.value: Independent file/object storage classes and bucket GB-month rates do not describe upstream Valkey.

facts.label: file request and retrieval prices
facts.value: Object upload/list/retrieval and image-transformation request tariffs are outside this self-hosted command server.

facts.label: minimum storage and early deletion
facts.value: Object minimum billed capacity, archive retention and early-deletion penalties are outside this software offer.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: Stable Search 1.2.1 supports FLAT exact vector indexing and HNSW approximate indexing, with FLOAT32 fields and L2, IP or COSINE distance.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: Live docs list FLOAT16/BFLOAT16 but tie them to module 1.3.0; FT.CREATE history marks those additions 1.3.0-RC1. They are not recorded as supported by stable 1.2.1.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: Stable HNSW defaults documented in FT.CREATE: M 16 (maximum 512), EF_CONSTRUCTION 200 (maximum 4096), EF_RUNTIME 10 (maximum 4096). Increasing them changes memory/build/query tradeoffs.

facts.label: vector/index limits
facts.value: Search exposes configurable maximum vector dimensions, vector attributes and index count, but their numeric defaults/maxima were not established from the inspected published configuration table.

facts.label: embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: A bundled embedding-generation or reranking service, model catalog and inference allowance were not found in the stable module's server/query interface.

facts.label: run limits and pricing
facts.value: Upstream per-job invocation/CPU-second, waiting-time, retry and concurrency billing is not applicable. Worker CPU/RAM/timeouts depend on the external worker host, while the broker uses the operator's Valkey resources.

facts.label: run limits and pricing
facts.value: Lua scripts execute atomically and block other server activity while running. The example 9.1.3 configuration's default busy-reply threshold is 5000 ms; it is not a promise that an executing script is automatically killed at five seconds.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Public source/releases and installation instructions are available without a Valkey cloud signup or card. The server is downloaded and operated by the user; no software-use account or timed activation requirement is stated in BSD-3-Clause.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: A hosted service signup-country list, free-tier card condition, paid-seat minimum and trial activation process are outside this upstream self-hosted product.

facts.label: signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Valkey and its logo are LF Projects trademarks. BSD software permission does not provide unrestricted rights to imply project endorsement or brand an unrelated service as official.

facts.label: primary type and other roles
facts.value: Primary type: self-hosted key-value database/cache. Other documented roles include structured data, message coordination, and optional JSON/vector/text search modules. These are our directory labels.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: Core includes Redis-style data structures/commands, Streams, Pub/Sub, persistence, replication, scripting in Lua-enabled builds, and extensibility through modules. JSON and Search require their respective loaded modules.

facts.label: included backend services
facts.value: End-user signup/login, file buckets, general application-worker hosting, managed backups and a hosted control plane are not supplied by the documented upstream server installation.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Native clients communicate using the binary-safe RESP protocol over TCP; Unix sockets are also documented. RESP2 and RESP3 modes and cluster redirection support are available in valkey-cli.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: Valkey GLIDE has a shared Rust core with Python, Java, Node.js, Go, C#, PHP and Ruby interfaces. The client directory also lists project-maintained valkey-py/iovalkey/valkey-java and separately identifies community clients.

facts.label: app connection options
facts.value: The migration guide targets Redis OSS 7.2 and earlier compatibility. Redis CE 7.4+ data files are not compatible with Valkey under that guide; later Redis commands/modules should not be assumed interchangeable.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: The security model requires trusted clients/networks and recommends an application layer between browsers and Valkey. Restrict access with firewall/binding, configure credentials and avoid exposing administrative commands.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: ACLs support named users with command/key/channel restrictions. Valkey 9.1 adds per-database ACL permissions; new connections can otherwise use the configured default user without an explicit password.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: The shipped 9.1.3 configuration binds loopback and enables protected mode. Starting without that file uses built-in defaults; general security/install prose describes all-interface binding with protected-mode restrictions.

facts.label: data access controls
facts.value: TLS is optional and must be built/configured with certificates; plaintext TCP can be disabled using port 0. TLS can protect client, replication and cluster links, with separate settings for those routes.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: Core is an in-memory data-structure server, with optional disk persistence and commands for strings, hashes, lists, sets, sorted sets and more. It is not an SQL engine.

facts.label: engine and query model
facts.value: Release APIs use major.minor.patch versioning. Patch releases are backward-compatible fixes; major releases may change behavior. Upgrade replicas before primaries and review engine/module release notes.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: MULTI/EXEC executes queued commands sequentially without other clients interleaving; WATCH supplies optimistic conditional execution. Errors during EXEC do not roll back other successful commands.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Replication is asynchronous by default. WAIT/WAITAOF can request acknowledgments but do not establish a strongly consistent replicated system; acknowledged writes can still be lost during failover.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Cluster shards keys across slots; related multi-key operations generally need one slot, with hash tags used to colocate keys. The cluster specification documents asynchronous replication and write-loss windows.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Search module indexes are maintained separately at each node; replicas inherit replication lag, and index-definition convergence across shards is eventually consistent. Initial backfill can leave queries seeing only the portion indexed so far.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Developers can run isolated instances on separate ports/hosts or restore an RDB into another instance. The administration guide describes running a second instance during migration/upgrades.

facts.label: test environments and branches
facts.value: Native copy-on-write development branches, managed preview lifetimes and branch quotas were not found in the inspected core deployment/backup materials.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Replication copies a primary to one or more replicas; replicas can serve reads subject to lag. Initial synchronization and catch-up require replication bandwidth and backlog resources.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Sentinel provides monitoring, service discovery and automatic primary promotion for non-clustered Valkey. Its guide calls for at least three Sentinel instances in independent failure domains for a robust deployment.

facts.label: replicas and failover
facts.value: Valkey Cluster provides partitioning and failover with operator-managed nodes. Native multi-region Active-Active and stronger durability discussed in the October 2026 roadmap remain development work.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Pub/Sub pushes live messages with at-most-once delivery; disconnected subscribers miss messages. Streams retain entries for consumer-group processing and recovery when configured durably.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Client-side caching tracks keys and sends invalidations. The documentation requires flushing local cached values when the invalidation connection is lost to avoid stale reads.

facts.label: live updates and offline sync
facts.value: An integrated local-first browser/mobile database, offline write queue and automatic client conflict-resolution SDK were not found in the inspected project docs.

facts.label: extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Valkey JSON is separately loaded and documented for core 8.0+. Its JSONPath operations manipulate nested documents; latest stable module metadata identifies 1.0.3, released 2026-08-31.

facts.label: extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Valkey Bloom is a separate first-party module for core 8.0+. Its membership checks can have false positives; it is not an exact uniqueness constraint or proof of absence from the real dataset.

facts.label: extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Stable Search 1.2.1 supplies vector, text, numeric and tag indexing, plus FT.SEARCH/FT.AGGREGATE, on HASH or JSON data. It requires core 9.0.1+ and is loaded separately.

facts.label: upload and file limits
facts.value: Multipart/resumable app-file uploads are outside the native server interface; binary strings remain subject to D03 protocol/memory limits.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: The native endpoint is RESP, not a documented S3 object-storage API. An operator's separate backup bucket does not change that interface.

facts.label: delivery and private files
facts.value: Public/private buckets, signed download URLs, custom-domain file delivery and an included CDN are outside upstream Valkey.

facts.label: filters and mixed search
facts.value: Stable Search combines full-text, tag, numeric-range and vector similarity clauses, including boolean filters and aggregations. Per-prefix indexing can narrow which HASH/JSON keys enter an index.

facts.label: filters and mixed search
facts.value: Search can fan queries across a cluster and merge results. Its docs describe explicit options for partial or inconsistent results; applications must inspect query options and target-version behavior rather than assume every distributed query is a complete snapshot.

facts.label: execution model and languages
facts.value: Streams coordinate consumer applications running outside Valkey. Server-side Lua scripting executes data-local logic when the build includes Lua; 9.1 can be built without that engine.

facts.label: delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: XREADGROUP deliveries remain pending until acknowledged with XACK; XAUTOCLAIM can transfer idle pending entries for recovery. Recovered work can repeat application side effects, so consumers need safe duplicate handling.

facts.label: delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: XACK removes a group's pending reference, rather than generally deleting the retained stream entry. Pub/Sub separately offers at-most-once broadcast and has no equivalent durable pending-entry recovery.

facts.label: schedules and queue retention
facts.value: XTRIM supports length-based MAXLEN or ID-based MINID trimming, exact or approximate. Queue retention is configured by the application and constrained by persistence, eviction and host memory.

facts.label: schedules and queue retention
facts.value: A built-in managed cron/delay scheduler, timezone contract and one fixed universal message-payload limit were not established in the inspected queue documentation.

facts.label: logs and run history
facts.value: COMMANDLOG can retain slow, large-request and large-reply command entries by configurable thresholds/counts; SLOWLOG likewise has a count-based maximum. Native diagnostics are not per-job application execution logs.

facts.label: logs and run history
facts.value: An included worker run-history dashboard, failed-job replay retention in days and upstream log-storage tariff are not applicable to this self-hosted broker.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Core 9.1.3 can be compiled on Linux, macOS and BSD platforms; Linux receives the main production/stress-testing focus. Windows is not officially supported; WSL is documented for development.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Operators must provision RAM with data/index/allocator overhead, durable disks, backups, upgrades, network controls and monitoring. Write-heavy RDB saves/AOF rewrites can use up to twice normal memory according to the administration guide.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: A universal production-safe CPU/RAM/disk minimum or cheapest monthly hosting cost for the directory's workloads was not established.

facts.label: operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Optional modules add build/version/port requirements. Search supports standalone and cluster operation and uses an extra intra-cluster RPC port; JSON/Bloom must also be installed and loaded where their commands/data are needed.

facts.label: regions and data location
facts.value: Database, replicas and off-box backups run where the operator deploys them. There is no upstream selectable-region catalogue or data-residency service commitment.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: RDB snapshots and AOF files provide data portability; valkey-cli --rdb can copy a remote RDB snapshot to a local file. Compatible engine/module versions are required to reload the data.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: FLUSHALL deletes keys from all logical databases; asynchronous mode only targets keys present when invoked. It does not document erasure of independent RDB/AOF archives, replicas or external logs.

facts.label: leaving and deleting
facts.value: Upstream account closure, a vendor-held customer-dataset purge deadline and a managed export fee are not applicable. LF Projects' website privacy policy concerns site/community information, not the user's self-hosted dataset.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: RDB snapshots capture the dataset at configured intervals or through SAVE/BGSAVE. AOF records writes with configurable fsync behavior; both can be used together, and restart recovery favors AOF when both are enabled.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: The shipped 9.1.3 config has appendonly no; appendfsync everysec matters only when AOF is enabled. Operators must deliberately configure persistence and a durable data directory.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: Off-box backup copying, retention, storage encryption/access and restore testing are operator work. RDB files can be copied for backup; replicas alone do not preserve historical states after accidental deletions.

facts.label: backups and restore
facts.value: An upstream managed backup-retention allowance, included backup-storage price or arbitrary-timestamp recovery service is not applicable.

facts.label: file recovery and protection
facts.value: Object versions, bucket locks and file undelete are outside this database scope. RDB/AOF backups are documented separately under D05.

facts.label: identity and old names
facts.value: Valkey is the Linux Foundation-hosted continuation forked from Redis OSS 7.2.4. Its official project and downloads are at valkey.io; it is distinct from Redis Cloud and later Redis editions.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: Valkey core 9.1.3 is BSD-3-Clause. Its COPYING file retains the Valkey-contributor and inherited Redis copyright notices under that license.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: BSD-3-Clause permits source/binary use and redistribution, with or without modification, subject to notice, disclaimer and non-endorsement conditions. Commercial deployment is not limited to a trial or a non-production edition.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: Valkey Search 1.2.1 and Valkey Bloom 1.0.1 are separate first-party modules, each BSD-3-Clause.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: Project technical direction is governed by a Technical Steering Committee (TSC). No more than one third of its members may represent the same organization or affiliates.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: The TSC seeks consensus. Major governance changes require a two-thirds vote of the entire TSC; technical major decisions follow the documented majority process, with a narrowly defined two-member approval path when no member objects.

facts.label: hosting and license
facts.value: Valkey JSON 1.0.3 is also BSD-3-Clause under its own release-pinned LICENSE file.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Latest designated mainline stable release: Valkey 9.1.3, released 2026-10-26. GitHub's latest endpoint marks it non-prerelease and the release urges prompt application of security fixes.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Valkey 9.2.0-rc1 was released 2026-09-16. The 9.2 page explicitly says no stable release exists yet and release candidates are unsupported for production.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Core maintenance lasts three years from a minor release; the selected final minor of each major receives five-year security support. Version 9.1 maintenance/security ends 2029-05-19/2031-05-19; 8.1 ends 2028-03-31/2030-03-31; 7.2 ends 2027-04-16/2029-04-16.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: No project shutdown, database sunset or acquisition notice was found in the inspected Valkey blog and Linux Foundation press searches. Valkey was publicly launched under the Foundation on 2024-03-28.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: The 2026-10-14 Planet Valkey announcement retires the old Planet for the Valkey Community aggregator in favor of planet.valkey.io. It does not retire the Valkey server.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: The 2026-10-29 roadmap describes stronger durability, Cluster V2, data tiering and Active-Active replication as work in development.

facts.label: lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Latest designated stable Valkey Search is 1.2.1 (2026-07-07), requiring core 9.0.1+. Live command docs also contain 1.3.0-RC1 changes; those are kept separate from stable 1.2.1.

facts.label: vendor home and main markets
facts.value: Valkey is a community project hosted by the Linux Foundation, with LF Projects, LLC holding project trademarks. LF Projects identifies itself as a Delaware series limited liability company in the US; this is not a database hosting region.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: Community support uses the Valkey project channels and public issue/discussion workflow. Security issues are reported privately to the project security address rather than as public GitHub issues.

facts.label: support and service promises
facts.value: An upstream paid-hosting uptime SLA, outage credit and managed-service status promise are not applicable. BSD software is supplied as is; separate providers may offer their own contracts.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: PostgreSQL supports SQL transactions and isolation levels; upstream PostgreSQL 16 defaults to Read Committed, where each statement sees a new committed-data snapshot.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: MySQL InnoDB supports the four SQL isolation levels; the upstream MySQL 8.4 manual states Repeatable Read as its default.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Valkey MULTI/EXEC executes queued commands together without interleaving; WATCH supplies optimistic checks. It does not offer SQL-style rollback after a command error.

facts.label: transactions and consistency
facts.value: Kafka ordering and replication operate per partition. Producer transactions and consumer isolation can coordinate Kafka records and offsets; they do not automatically make external database/email side effects exactly once.

facts.value: pgvector 0.7.4 supports distance search with SQL WHERE filters and can be combined with PostgreSQL full-text search. Its approximate indexes apply filtering after scanning, which can return fewer matches.

facts.value: Kafka delivery depends on producer acknowledgements/retries, consumer offset commits and processing. facts.label: Free limits

facts.label: Free limits

facts.label: Free limits

facts.label: Free limits

facts.label: Free limits

facts.label: Free limits

facts.label: Free limits

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: Premium Dedicated Cloud has no object-count ceiling, up to 1,000 collections, and 45-day backup retention.

facts.label: Free limits

facts.label: Free limits

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: Current pricing matrix names paid plans Flex and Premium (Shared or Dedicated); the separate Support Plans page still describes a Plus plan.

facts.label: Free limits

facts.label: Inactivity, pause, and deletion
facts.value: Paid Cloud clusters continue to incur charges while active; billing stops only after all active clusters are deleted. No paid-cluster idle suspension or idle data-retention rule was found in the billing and terms pages checked.

facts.value: Flex is the lowest paid Cloud database tier, with a published minimum of $45 per month and monthly pay-as-you-go terms.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: Premium is quote-based in the plan matrix; the pricing FAQ gives a starting minimum from $400 per month. The page does not split that floor into separate Shared and Dedicated quotes.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Cloud database charges use vector dimensions, persistent storage, and backups. The published dimension formula is number of objects × vector dimensionality × replication factor.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Flex vector dimension rate starts at $0.00465 per 1 million dimensions; the exact rate varies by index type, compression, cloud provider, and region.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Premium Shared vector dimension rate starts at $0.003875 per 1 million dimensions; the exact rate varies by index type, compression, provider, and region.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Premium Dedicated vector dimension rate starts at $0.002718 per 1 million dimensions; the exact rate varies by index type, compression, provider, and region.

facts.label: Billing meters
