facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Backup storage starts at $0.03036 per GiB for Flex, $0.021 per GiB for Premium Shared, and $0.014 per GiB for Premium Dedicated; volume, retention, cloud provider, and region affect the bill.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Data transfer is currently listed as free for a limited promotional period on paid Cloud plans. Weaviate may introduce a charge later with advance notice; the promotion's end date is not stated.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: The minimum monthly amount covers the baseline cluster cost plus vector dimensions and storage; backup storage is charged on top.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Weaviate Embeddings rates are $0.025 per 1 million tokens for Snowflake Arctic Embed M v1.5, $0.040 per 1 million for v2.0, and $0.065 per 1 million for ModernVBERT ColModernVBERT.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Query Agent offers a $30 per organization monthly plan including 4,000 requests; additional requests are usage-based with no public overage rate shown.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Cloud billing is calculated for active clusters and invoiced monthly; customers who subscribe through AWS or GCP marketplaces are billed through that marketplace.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Free Cloud suspends after seven idle days and is not billed; its data is preserved during the suspension period but deleted after 30 total inactive days.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Flex has a $45 monthly minimum while an active cluster exists; no paid scale-to-zero or idle-compute billing pause is described in current pricing or billing docs.

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: Current Cloud pricing says data transfer has no additional cost during a limited promotional period on paid plans; its end date and later rate are not published.

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: Self-hosted transfer costs are paid to the operator's infrastructure provider; Weaviate's self-hosted docs do not set an egress rate.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: Cloud usage is metered by dimensions, storage, and backup volume; the free-tier limits and paid “unlimited objects” wording do not publish a bill cap or automatic stop rule.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: The Cloud Console has a Running Costs module for current estimates, but the pages checked do not document a user-configurable hard spend cap or its exclusions.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Cloud Free publishes 100,000 objects, 1 GB memory, 10 GB disk, one collection, and up to three tenants; paid Cloud object count is listed as unlimited and is resource-metered.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: The Cloud default query limit is 10 results; the documented default maximum query result count is 100,000. These are query defaults, not monthly request quotas.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: The current docs do not state a universal maximum vector dimensionality, database object size, or concurrent connection count. Self-hosted capacity depends on resources and configured indexes.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Server-side batch import is available from v1.36 and dynamically adjusts batch size/concurrency using server feedback; request-size failures can occur when a client sends one oversized batch, so the docs recommend streaming ingestion.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Active multi-tenant shard counts depend on operating-system file limits and node sizing; the docs describe a 50,000-or-more active shards per node design scale, not a universal hosted account cap.

facts.label: Storage prices
facts.value: Not applicable: Weaviate stores database objects and indexes, not general customer files in hot/archive object-storage classes.

facts.label: File request and retrieval prices
facts.value: Not applicable: Weaviate does not price customer file uploads, listings, retrieval, or image-processing requests as a file-storage service.

facts.label: Minimum storage and early deletion
facts.value: Not applicable: Weaviate does not sell customer file classes with minimum file size or early deletion rules.

facts.label: Vector/index limits
facts.value: Weaviate stores single or named dense vectors and supports multi-vector representations on applicable indexes. The docs checked publish no universal maximum vector dimension.

facts.label: Vector/index limits
facts.value: Cloud Free is limited to 100,000 objects, one collection, and three tenants; paid plans list unlimited objects and up to 1,000 collections, subject to billed resources.

facts.label: Vector/index limits
facts.value: HNSW memory use grows with vector count and dimensionality; Resource Planning gives float32 size as dimensions × 4 bytes and recommends budgeting index overhead and connections.

facts.label: Vector/index limits
facts.value: The default vector cache limit is 1 trillion objects per collection; this configurable cache setting is not a published account-wide record ceiling.

facts.label: Embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: Self-hosted Weaviate can accept supplied vectors or use configured provider modules; model-provider API usage and credentials are separate from the BSD database license.

facts.label: Embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: Weaviate Cloud Embeddings hosts listed models and bills by token; the current listed rates are $0.025, $0.040, and $0.065 per million tokens by model.

facts.label: Embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: Cloud Query Agent is usage-based after plan allowances; its additional-request rate is not published on the current pricing page. Reranker model charges depend on the external or configured provider.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Not applicable: Weaviate does not offer customer jobs with execution seconds, worker CPU/RAM, or retries as a job product.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Weaviate Cloud Free is self-service, always free, and requires no credit card. Paid Shared Cloud requires billing details.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Cloud Free is described for learning, hobby projects, and small workloads. The pages checked do not expressly say that commercial use is prohibited; the self-hosted BSD Community Edition expressly permits commercial production use.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: The self-serve terms select Weaviate LLC for U.S. registration and Weaviate B.V. for non-U.S. registration or other stated mechanisms. The terms and pages checked do not publish a general country eligibility list.

facts.label: Primary type and other roles
facts.value: Primary: vector database for AI applications. Secondary: full-text search, semantic search, hybrid search, metadata filtering, and multi-tenant data storage.

facts.label: Primary type and other roles
facts.value: Weaviate describes itself as an application-search database generally used as a secondary search index, with more critical transactional data kept in another system.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Core database functions include collections, object and vector storage, vector/keyword/hybrid search, filters, APIs, and optional multi-tenancy.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Weaviate Cloud adds managed cluster creation and updates, console tools, Weaviate Embeddings, Query Agent, and guided data import.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Weaviate does not provide a general application user-authentication product, file/object bucket, app function runtime, or customer job scheduler in the database offer pages checked.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Query Agent is a Cloud query assistant, not a general-purpose background worker or arbitrary customer-code execution service.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: The database provides REST and gRPC APIs. Self-hosted default ports are 8080 for REST and 50051 for gRPC; Cloud uses TLS endpoints and gRPC over port 443.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Official database clients are available for Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, Go, Java, and C#. The TypeScript web client also supports browser and edge runtimes through gRPC-Web.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: GraphQL remains in older clients and self-hosted deployments during its deprecation window, but is disabled on new Cloud clusters and is scheduled to be turned off in Cloud on May 1, 2027.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: The Search REST API is currently marked preview; official client libraries use gRPC for search operations.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Cloud clusters use API-key authentication and enable RBAC on new clusters; users can create role-scoped keys.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Self-hosted Weaviate supports API-key and OIDC authentication and fine-grained RBAC; anonymous access is enabled by default in the basic Docker example and is strongly discouraged for production.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Weaviate Cloud configures TLS for managed database connections.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Premium Dedicated lists AWS PrivateLink and customer-key encrypted volumes; these are not listed for Free, Flex, or Premium Shared.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: The pricing matrix lists HIPAA compliance for Premium Dedicated; the FAQ and product copy scope HIPAA availability to Enterprise Cloud on AWS.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Weaviate Cloud always enables its MCP server, with write tools enabled by default; the user can switch on MCP Read-Only after cluster creation.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: The self-serve agreement says Weaviate owns service/system data while customers own Customer Data.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: Weaviate is an object/document database with collections, typed properties, references, vector embeddings, inverted indexes, and vector indexes; it is not SQL-compatible.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: Query methods include vector similarity, BM25 keyword, hybrid, filters, aggregation, and retrieval; REST and gRPC are current interfaces, while GraphQL is deprecated on a published retirement schedule.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: Replicated collections expose configurable read/write consistency levels; replication may be asynchronous, so replicas can converge eventually rather than immediately.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: The database docs checked do not publish a multi-object ACID transaction contract or relational isolation levels. Treat object/batch operations as database APIs, not as a transaction guarantee for money or inventory records.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: Consistency level affects replicated object reads/writes; it does not turn a group of unrelated object mutations into an ACID transaction.

facts.label: Test environments and branches
facts.value: No copy-on-write database branching feature was found. Cloud allows separate clusters, subject to one Free cluster per user and a default six Shared Cloud clusters per organization.

facts.label: Test environments and branches
facts.value: Self-hosted test environments can be separate deployments or collections, but the documentation does not describe database branches with shared copy-on-write storage.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Self-hosted Weaviate can configure shard replication and consistency levels across nodes; the operator provisions nodes, zones, storage, and recovery capacity.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Every current paid Cloud plan includes HA/replication; Free has no HA/replication.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Cloud's plan availability targets are 99.5% Flex, 99.9% Premium Shared, and 99.95% Premium Dedicated per quarter, subject to SLA exclusions.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Weaviate supports object writes and database replication, but the docs checked do not describe a client subscription/changefeed API or automatic offline reads/writes and conflict resolution.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Weaviate's Kafka connector can stream inserts and deletes from Kafka into Weaviate, but it is not a client-side offline sync protocol.

facts.label: Extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Vector index options include HNSW, Flat, Dynamic, and HFresh; HFresh is disk based, while HNSW provides in-memory approximate nearest-neighbor search.

facts.label: Extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Built-in inverted indexes support BM25 keyword search and property filters; vector search can be combined with keyword search using hybrid search.

facts.label: Extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Model integrations and modules can connect vectorizers, generative models, and rerankers; Cloud services and self-hosted modules have different availability and external provider costs.

facts.label: Upload and file limits
facts.value: Not applicable: Weaviate ingests database objects and vectors, not user files into a file bucket; its CSV/PDF import feature parses data into database records.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Not applicable: Weaviate does not expose an S3-compatible user-file storage API. S3 support in its deployment docs is for backups and exports.

facts.label: Delivery and private files
facts.value: Not applicable: Weaviate does not provide customer file buckets, signed file URLs, file CDN delivery, or custom file domains.

facts.label: Filters and mixed search
facts.value: Weaviate supports dense vector similarity search, BM25F keyword search, and hybrid search that fuses keyword and vector results.

facts.label: Filters and mixed search
facts.value: Queries support structured property filters; the current default HNSW filter strategy is ACORN, with PathSeer and sweeping alternatives available in documented versions.

facts.label: Filters and mixed search
facts.value: Multi-tenancy stores tenants on separate shards and keeps tenant data isolated; queries to a multi-tenant collection must name the tenant.

facts.label: Filters and mixed search
facts.value: Cloud Free uses HFresh cost-optimized settings; paid Cloud plans offer flexible index types and compression.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: Not applicable: Weaviate is a database and does not host arbitrary customer worker/function code.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Not applicable: Weaviate does not offer an application queue or scheduled job delivery system.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Not applicable: Weaviate does not provide customer task schedules or a durable job queue.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Not applicable: Weaviate does not provide job execution logs or run history for customer worker code.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Community Edition can be run using Docker or Kubernetes/Helm. Kubernetes docs require Kubernetes 1.23 or newer, Helm 3+, and persistent volumes.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: No universal hardware minimum is specified; HNSW memory depends on vector bytes, connections, garbage collection, and query/import workload. Disk-based HFresh can reduce memory pressure.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: The self-host operator must provision durable storage and network exposure, configure authentication and TLS, schedule off-host backups, monitor capacity, and manage version upgrades.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Cloud Embeddings, Query Agent, console imports, managed upgrades, and Cloud plan support are managed-service features; they are not all bundled with self-hosted CE. Self-hosted EE adds separately licensed enterprise features.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Free Cloud runs on AWS. The current pricing matrix lists limited availability in two regions and lets the user select a region during cluster setup.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Flex and Premium Shared support AWS or GCP in a limited set of seven regions; Premium Dedicated lists AWS, GCP, and Azure across about 40 regions.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Exact region identifiers for each current plan are not listed in the public pricing matrix. The CLI region page and plan matrix do not provide one consistent complete list.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: A customer selects the cloud provider and region for a Cloud cluster; the DPA says Weaviate will not change the customer-selected provider or region without written consent.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Cloud plan backup retention is described as same-region storage: seven days Flex, 30 days Premium Shared, and 45 days Premium Dedicated.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: The DPA describes a separate immutable personal-data backup retention period of up to 90 days, with residual cloud-provider copies potentially remaining inaccessible for up to 90 days after closure.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Self-hosted collection export is a preview feature that exports object properties and vectors to Apache Parquet with Zstandard compression; external backends include S3, GCS, and Azure Storage.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: The collection export feature is not available in Weaviate Cloud. Cloud data can be read through the database APIs, but the documented Parquet export workflow is self-hosted only.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Cloud stop-billing workflow is to delete every active cluster; billing continues through cluster deletion and a final usage invoice is issued.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: The DPA says personal data is deleted from production without undue delay after a customer deletion request. On termination, Weaviate must delete or return personal data within 30 days; inaccessible residual infrastructure copies and immutable backups can remain up to 90 days.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: The agreement says the customer owns Customer Data, but the self-serve terms do not define a database export format or an exact deletion time for all non-personal Customer Data.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Self-hosted backup can cover an entire instance or selected collections, and supports S3, GCS, Azure Storage, or a local filesystem. Multi-node production backups require external storage.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Backups can be incremental; tenant data is included within its collection, but there is no tenant-level restore. Offloaded/frozen tenant data is skipped because it is not on local disk.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Cloud plan restore-point retention is seven days Flex, 30 days Premium Shared, and 45 days Premium Dedicated. Daily backups are listed for these paid plans.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: The public pricing matrix marks Free plan backup retention as unavailable, while Cloud default-settings says each Cloud instance is automatically backed up daily. The user-facing Free restore/retention behavior is not resolved by these pages.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Weaviate Cloud backup storage is separately metered by stored backup volume and retention; restore testing or external snapshots should be budgeted separately from the database floor.

facts.label: File recovery and protection
facts.value: Not applicable to customer files: database backups and exports protect database content; Weaviate has no customer-file versioning, object-lock, or file-recovery product.

facts.label: Identity and old names
facts.value: Weaviate is a vector database and managed cloud service. The official product home is https://weaviate.io/.

facts.label: Identity and old names
facts.value: Weaviate's company was called SeMI Technologies before it adopted the Weaviate company name in January 2023. This is a company name history, not a separate database product name.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Self-hosted Community Edition runs without a license key. Code outside the repository's wl/ directory is under BSD-3-Clause and may be used commercially and in production at no software license charge.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Self-hosted Enterprise Edition adds code in wl/ under the Weaviate License. It requires a commercial agreement and valid license key; a 30-day trial key is available by request.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Weaviate Cloud is a managed service using the Weaviate open-source project, with managed operations and additional services. Cloud customers do not need a self-hosted license key.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Cloud-specific additions include hosted Embeddings, Query Agent, data import, and managed cluster operations; these services are not a license grant to run Enterprise Edition features yourself.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Weaviate Database and Weaviate Cloud are operating and available. The official release page marks v1.40.4 as the latest stable release and shows November 5 as its release date.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: GraphQL is deprecated as of October 26, 2026. New Weaviate Cloud clusters have GraphQL disabled; Cloud disables it on existing clusters by May 1, 2027. Self-hosted keeps it until at least May 1, 2027, after which a minor release disables it by default before a later removal.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Engram, a separate managed memory service from Weaviate, no longer accepts new projects; existing projects are scheduled to stop working after December 31, 2026.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Transformation Agent, a separate product, is marked sunset and points users to Query Agent and Engram.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: The official EOL policy describes support windows for software versions; it does not announce end of life for the current product.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: No acquisition or shutdown announcement for Weaviate Database or Weaviate Cloud was found in the official blog/archive, company pages, release notes, or EOL policy checked.

facts.label: Vendor home and main markets
facts.value: The privacy policy identifies Weaviate B.V. as a private limited company established in Amsterdam, the Netherlands. U.S. self-serve accounts may contract with Weaviate LLC instead.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Free Cloud support is community-only in the Support Plans page; Free is best-effort with no uptime commitment under the SLA.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Flex includes email support during business hours, public status-page monitoring, and a 99.5% availability target per quarter; its severity-one response target is one business day.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Premium Shared lists 99.9% quarterly availability and a four-hour severity-one response in the current pricing matrix.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Premium Dedicated lists 99.95% quarterly availability and a one-hour severity-one response; phone, Slack, and technical account team options are listed for Premium.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: SLA service credits require a claim within 30 days of the availability failure; the Free service is excluded from SLA credits.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Self-hosted Community Edition users are directed to GitHub issues and the community forum. Enterprise Edition support requests go through the support portal; paid self-host support packages are available by arrangement.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: A current public status-page URL was not found in the pricing, support, Cloud status, or terms pages checked; Flex support mentions status-page monitoring without linking a public page.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: Cloud Team annual pricing is $120 USD/year per builder and $60 USD/year per non-builder; the page shows no annual discount for these seat rates.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: Cloud Enterprise starts at $840 USD/month or $8,400 USD/year in the pricing calculator; the minimum configuration includes its core package, one builder seat, and two standard worker compute units.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: Self-host Enterprise starts at $120 USD/month or $1,200 USD/year in the calculator: one builder seat plus two standard workers (2 CUs). Hardware and database charges are extra.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: Self-host Pro is a distinct lower-size Enterprise tier, available only to individuals, businesses under 10 employees and $250,000 revenue, or seed-stage startups. It is not the general Enterprise offer.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: Prices are shown in USD and exclude applicable taxes; the Terms place applicable sales, VAT, GST, and similar taxes on the customer.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Cloud Free is limited by executions; Cloud Team is billed by seats and execution usage; Cloud Enterprise is billed by active seats and provisioned worker compute units.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Cloud Team builders cost $10/month ($120/year) and half-seat operators/external JWT users cost $5/month ($60/year); one seat includes 10,000 executions per month.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Team extra executions are billed at month-end, but the public pricing page and Terms do not state the per-execution overage price or its rounding unit.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Cloud Enterprise Cloud's calculator prices a 2 GB standard worker at $100/month (1 CU) and a native worker with 8 subworkers at $100/month (1 CU).

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Cloud Enterprise Cloud charges a $600/month core package in addition to seats and worker CUs; the annual calculator shows $6,000/year for this package.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Cloud Enterprise seats cost $40/month per builder and $20/month per non-builder; annual values shown are $400/year and $200/year.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Self-host Enterprise prices a builder at $20/month ($200/year), a non-builder at $10/month ($100/year), and each 2 GB worker CU at $50/month ($500/year).

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: One CU equals 2 worker-GB-month. A 1 GB worker is 0.5 CU; a 2 GB worker is 1 CU; a native worker is 1 CU for eight native subworkers.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: On Cloud, CU count scales linearly with worker memory. On self-hosted subscriptions, any worker above 2 GB is capped at 2 CUs; total CUs round up to a whole number.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Enterprise Cloud and self-host subscriptions count active users in the last 30 days: a builder is 1 seat; two non-builders or external JWT users total 1 seat.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Enterprise Cloud guest users are free up to 100 distinct guest emails per trailing 30 days; each four beyond that count as one seat. Cloud Free and Team do not include guest apps.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Worker billing is based on provisioned memory rather than job memory actually used. With Enterprise autoscaling, worker uptime is counted by the minute; only production CUs count, while seat counts remain across instances.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Cloud Free and Team price executions and seats; the public plan comparison does not expose a separate customer-configured CU worker pool for these shared plans.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Cloud Enterprise usage is based on provisioned worker CUs, not script memory or job count. The public pricing/docs do not establish that idle Enterprise Cloud worker capacity scales to zero automatically.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Self-hosted Windmill has no Windmill Cloud compute charge; the operator's servers and database can continue to incur the hosting provider's idle costs.

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: No general Cloud egress or transfer rate was found in the pricing page, Cloud Terms, or Cloud DPAs checked. This is not evidence that all transfer is free.

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: Self-hosted transfer charges are set by the operator's infrastructure and network providers, not by Windmill.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: Cloud Team charges for added seats and execution overage; Terms allow $50 USD incremental debits as unbilled charges accumulate, then charge any remainder at month-end. That billing cadence is not a spend cap.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: The Cloud Free page states the 1,000 execution monthly allowance but the checked pricing, docs, and Terms do not say whether exceeding it hard-stops, queues, or bills automatically.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: For Enterprise subscriptions, usage above the subscribed seat or CU limit triggers notice and a 35-day window to correct, change plan, or reduce usage before the license key stops renewing.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: A self-service account-wide dollar spend cap or automatic Cloud shutdown at a customer-set budget was not documented in the pricing, Terms, or billing pages checked.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Cloud Free includes 1,000 execution units per month; Team includes 10,000 per seat per month; Enterprise Cloud lists unlimited executions and meters provisioned worker CUs.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: One execution is one job lasting less than one second; each additional second of computation adds another execution unit.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: A flow's execution usage is based on its job/step compute; time spent asleep or in state transitions is not counted as compute execution time.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Cloud Enterprise Cloud's 2 GB worker costs $100/month per CU; self-host Enterprise's 2 GB worker costs $50/month per CU. These are separate deployment modes.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Each worker runs one job at a time. Windmill estimates up to about 26 million jobs/month per worker only for jobs lasting 100 ms; actual throughput depends on workload and duration.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Job timeout is configurable at instance and step/script level. The instance setting accepts seconds/days/hours, while a step timeout cannot exceed the instance timeout.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: A single maximum job timeout value common to all Cloud plans was not published in the instance-settings, jobs, flow-timeout, pricing, or Cloud Terms pages checked.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Cloud Free signup is self-serve through Google, GitHub, GitLab, or Microsoft sign-in. The pricing page says no credit card is required for Free. No account was created.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Cloud Team is upgraded at workspace level from the app; a valid payment method is required for purchases under the Terms.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Cloud Enterprise is not direct self-serve in the public guide: customers contact Windmill and receive a dedicated Cloud instance.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Self-hosted Community Edition can be downloaded and run without a Windmill account or license key. Self-hosted Enterprise needs a purchased or trial license key.

facts.label: Primary type and other roles
facts.value: Primary type: job and workflow runner. Secondary roles: developer platform, internal-app builder, API/script host, and data-pipeline runner. This is an editorial classification based on the product's own feature descriptions.

facts.label: Primary type and other roles
facts.value: Windmill is not presented as a general-purpose hosted database or object store. It uses PostgreSQL for its own state and can connect to external databases and storage.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Windmill includes scripts, workflows/flows, schedules, webhooks, HTTP routes, APIs, resources, variables, and job execution.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: It includes visual workflow construction and code-first workflow-as-code, with retries, parallel steps, approvals, and sleeps.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Windmill can build full-code React or Svelte apps whose backends are Windmill scripts and flows; public and authenticated app modes are documented.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: The platform also supports data pipelines and first-class dbt projects, but customer warehouses and object storage remain separate services.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Scripts can use TypeScript (Bun or Deno), Python, Go, Bash, PowerShell, Nu, SQL for PostgreSQL/MySQL/MS SQL/BigQuery/Snowflake, REST/GraphQL, or Docker.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Official developer interfaces include a REST API, Python and TypeScript clients, and the wmill CLI; scripts and workflows can also call external APIs.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Windmill workers connect to PostgreSQL and run customer code; self-hosted instances can connect to managed PostgreSQL and customer-controlled object storage.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Windmill supports workspace and instance roles, groups, identity-provider sign-in, OAuth, and public, guest, or member-only apps; some SSO/SCIM and role features vary by plan.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Enterprise Cloud's DPA says workspace secrets use per-workspace AES-256 keys; its data-location clause lets the customer choose US or EU for its dedicated instance.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Windmill states that Cloud Team uses service providers to host the service and that data may be transferred outside a user's jurisdiction; the Privacy Policy does not promise local residency for that plan.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Community Edition is not covered by Windmill's Trust Center SOC 2 Type II coverage; Windmill says Enterprise Edition is covered.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Self-hosting requires the operator to secure exposed endpoints, configure authentication and TLS, restrict network access, and secure PostgreSQL credentials and backups.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: Windmill dispatches scripts and flow steps to worker processes; PostgreSQL holds the job queue and application state. On Cloud, Windmill runs the platform; with self-hosting, the operator runs the server, workers, and database.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: Jobs can be initiated by HTTP endpoints/webhooks, schedules, email, database events, WebSockets, or tier-specific message/event triggers.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: Windmill supports code in 20+ languages/runtimes, with SQL, REST/GraphQL, and Docker options in addition to general-purpose languages.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: Jobs execute on Windmill workers, not on a third-party queue alone; standard self-hosted deployments need separate server and worker containers plus PostgreSQL.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Flow steps and workflow-as-code tasks can retry after errors with configurable attempts and fixed or exponential delay.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Each retry is a separate job, so it consumes another Cloud execution unit when it runs; sleep/retry waiting itself uses no worker compute.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Flows can use error handlers and continue-on-error behavior; the default is to stop the flow and propagate a step error.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: The checked job, flow retry, and schedule docs do not promise exactly-once delivery or general duplicate suppression.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Scripts and flows support cron schedules and one-off delayed runs. A schedule keeps only one future occurrence queued; if runs fall behind, missed occurrences may be skipped.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Flows can sleep for seconds, hours, days, months, or years; the worker is released during the sleep and the sleep is passive.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: The sleep(seconds) workflow-as-code API has a minimum of 1 second.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Cloud request size has an instance setting, but the docs only call it a maximum size in MB and do not publish a default or common maximum value.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Cloud Community and Team retain job run details for 60 days; Cloud Enterprise and self-host Enterprise list unlimited retention; self-host Community defaults to a maximum of 30 days.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Cloud Team audit logs are retained for 7 days; Cloud Enterprise's plan table says unlimited, while the audit guide describes 60 days in-product and storage up to a year, extendable by request.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Community Edition stores up to 5,000 log characters per job in PostgreSQL; Enterprise can stream larger logs to configured instance object storage.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Windmill can retry failed jobs and resume queued jobs; the checked docs do not describe a general replay/export archive for all historical run details.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Minimum single-machine self-host setup: 2 CPU cores, 4 GB RAM, and 20 GB disk; this is for getting started, not a production capacity guarantee.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Windmill requires PostgreSQL 14 or newer; PostgreSQL holds all Windmill state, including the job queue. External managed PostgreSQL can be used.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: A basic installation needs a server container, worker container, and PostgreSQL. LSP, multiplayer editing, and a reverse proxy are optional components; Multiplayer is Cloud and Enterprise Self-host only.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Docker Compose fits small deployments; Windmill recommends its Helm chart/Kubernetes for larger or production setups. Its rule of thumb is one worker per vCPU and 1–2 GB of RAM per worker.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: The operator controls upgrades: Windmill does not auto-update; pulling new images and restarting containers applies database migrations at startup. The operator must handle database backups and recovery.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Community Edition lacks Enterprise SAML/SCIM, audit-log export/extended retention, dedicated worker controls, Git sync for more than two users, and priority support; exact feature gaps vary by self-host or Cloud plan.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Windmill Cloud Community and Team are hosted in the United States. The public guide does not identify the exact underlying region for those shared plans.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Dedicated Enterprise Cloud can be deployed in the United States (us-east) or European Union (eu-central), as recorded in the customer's order. Windmill says EU processing is available at no extra charge and won't move the instance without prior written agreement.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Self-hosted users choose the region and infrastructure provider; Windmill does not host their Community or Enterprise instance.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: The UI can export a workspace ZIP containing scripts, flows, apps, resources, and variables; secrets are included as encrypted values.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: The CLI can sync scripts, flows, apps, resources, and variables to local files. Secrets, triggers, and schedules are skipped by default unless explicitly included; an export needs those flags and settings when required.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Windmill says Cloud customer data can be migrated into another Windmill system, including a self-hosted OSS instance. Cloud Team DPA says customer data is deleted when the contract ends; it does not state a fixed deletion delay.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Cloud Team backups are daily and retained for seven days, with point-in-time recovery available within that backup window.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Cloud Enterprise DPA says Windmill will delete Customer Data and remaining copies within 30 days after termination or written request, subject to legal/claims exceptions; it also allows a customer to request a database snapshot.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Self-hosted Windmill stores all product state in PostgreSQL; the operator must back up and delete that database and any configured object-storage files.

facts.label: Identity and old names
facts.value: Product: Windmill, a code-first developer platform. Vendor: Windmill Labs, Inc. Canonical product URL: https://www.windmill.dev/.

facts.label: Identity and old names
facts.value: No former product name or rebrand is stated on the checked home, brand/about, changelog, or repository pages.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Windmill Cloud is a vendor-hosted service under Windmill's Terms of Service; the service is not licensed under the self-hosted repository's AGPL license.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: The compilable Community Edition core without the Enterprise feature flag is AGPLv3. The repository also licenses the Python, Deno, Go, and PowerShell clients and OpenAPI specifications under Apache 2.0.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Windmill's downloadable Community Edition image/binaries contain both AGPL/Apache sources and some proprietary code. Windmill grants free use and as-is redistribution of CE, but bars selling, reselling, modifying, wrapping, or offering it as a managed service without permission.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Self-hosted Enterprise Edition is a paid, proprietary subscription license. The self-host license allows internal use under seat and compute capacity purchased; it prohibits reselling or offering the software as a service.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Windmill is operating and actively maintained. The official GitHub Releases page listed v1.858.0, released November 3, 2026, as the latest tagged release checked.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: The changelog contains 2026 product releases, including October's v1.843.0 and September's v1.812.0 entries; the repository has later November releases.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: No acquisition, Windmill shutdown, or repo-license replacement notice was found in the official blog through its November 4, 2026 entry, changelog, release page, or repository license.

facts.label: Vendor home and main markets
facts.value: Windmill says it is based between San Francisco and Paris. Its Cloud Team service is hosted in the United States; dedicated Cloud Enterprise can be placed in the US or EU. These are product locations, not a full market list.

facts.label: Vendor home and main markets
facts.value: An exhaustive list of countries where Windmill accepts Cloud customers was not published on the product home, pricing, Terms, or Privacy Policy pages checked.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Cloud Free and self-host Community list community support on Discord; the status page is at https://status.windmill.dev/.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Cloud Team receives priority Discord support; the support guide describes Team response goals of up to 48 hours.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Enterprise Cloud and self-host Enterprise list 24/7 priority support, 3-hour response for P0 issues, engineer assistance, and a dedicated Slack or Discord channel.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: The official status page redirected to its UptimeRobot host but returned “There was an error while fetching the data”; the current incident/component status could not be checked.

apps.name: Xano
apps.line: Backend platform with PostgreSQL, APIs, authentication, files and background tasks.

free.text: 1GB DB, 100K records; no scheduled tasks; term unclear; no idle rule found

cells.metered: $99/mo Essential: 3 WS, 5 seats; $249/mo Pro: 5 WS, 10 seats
cells.regions: US Free; 15 listed paid countries

sql.math: The Essential plan costs $99. 1 GB of data fits within 10 GB of SSD, and 10 peak connections fit the 45-connection pool. Performance, how output is counted and index overhead are not yet confirmed.
The Essential plan stays at $99 a month when idle. Pause, add-ons and outside services are not included.

files.math: The Essential plan at $99 a month includes exactly 100 GB of files, with no room to grow, and 250 GB of file bandwidth. 100 GB of output fits if it is counted there. Each upload must fit within 128 MB.

jobs.math: The Essential plan supports tasks with no fee per run. Whether 0.5 vCPU and 0.5 GB fits is unknown. Schedules shorter than a minute need the Pro plan at $249 a month.

facts.label: Free offer type
facts.value: Free is a $0 development/testing offer with no numeric trial duration on pricing; Terms refer to suspension at the “end of the free plan” without defining when that is. Lasting duration unresolved.

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: Free: 1 workspace, 1 team member, 100,000 records, 1GB database SSD, 1GB watermarked images, 1GB file bandwidth, 64MB upload limit, 10 API requests per 20 seconds.

facts.label: Free limits
facts.value: Free: unlimited REST endpoint definitions and Lambda functions within rate/resources; no background tasks, private storage, automatic backups, direct DB access, paid branching or extra data sources. Separate MAU/function-invocation quota not listed.

facts.label: Inactivity, pause and deletion
facts.value: No numeric inactivity sleep/expiry/deletion interval or resume window found for idle Free environments.

facts.label: Inactivity, pause and deletion
facts.value: On failed paid renewal, Terms remove access after the first failed attempt; collection attempts continue for seven days, then instance termination causes loss of data and live endpoints if unpaid.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: Essential monthly: USD $99/month for the instance bundle, including 3 workspaces and 5 team seats.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: Essential annual: USD $85/month equivalent, billed annually. Annual arithmetic is $85 × 12 = $1,020 (our calculation).

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: Pro monthly: USD $249/month for 5 workspaces and 10 seats.

facts.label: Least paid commitment
facts.value: Pro annual: USD $224/month equivalent, billed annually. Annual arithmetic is $224 × 12 = $2,688 (our calculation).

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Hosted billing is a fixed subscription plus selected add-ons; Billing says no overage/usage charges beyond the subscription. Changes restart the subscription period with credit for unused time.

facts.label: Billing meters
facts.value: Current pricing advertises CPU/Autoscale boost $180/month (Pro), increased storage $5–$10/month for additional 5–10GB, and enhanced security $500/month.

facts.label: Idle compute and scale to zero
facts.value: Subscription cannot be paused; zero traffic does not remove the recurring plan fee. Autoscale boost handles load and does not publish an idle zero-dollar plan.

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: Free: 1GB file bandwidth allowance.

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: Essential and Pro: 250GB file bandwidth allowance each; Custom configurable.

facts.label: Data transfer costs
facts.value: Rates/actions beyond file bandwidth and treatment of API response output, cross-region moves and full data export remain unpublished in inspected sources.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: Free API excess requests are rejected with ERROR_CODE_TOO_MANY_REQUESTS; wait up to 20 seconds or upgrade. Paid plans have no platform-enforced API rate limit.

facts.label: Overages and bill controls
facts.value: Exact cutoff/grace/resume behavior for exceeding database/media capacity or bandwidth, and a monetary cap covering external services, were not established.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Essential: 10GB database SSD; unlimited record count within storage/compute limits; 3 workspaces and 5 seats share the instance bundle.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Pro: 25GB database SSD; unlimited record count within storage/compute limits; 5 workspaces, 10 seats and managed load balancer. Custom capacity negotiated.

facts.label: Capacity and connection limits
facts.value: Numerical simultaneous DB connections, pool size, maximum query/record bytes and paid per-instance execution concurrency were not found.

facts.label: Storage prices
facts.value: Free: 1GB images only, watermarked; no general attachment/private-storage entitlement.

facts.label: Storage prices
facts.value: Essential: 100GB image/file storage included in the subscription.

facts.label: Storage prices
facts.value: Pro: 250GB image/file storage included; Custom lists unlimited file storage subject to its agreed infrastructure.

facts.label: File request and retrieval prices
facts.value: No separate per-file upload/list/read/retrieval/image-processing fee published; Billing describes fixed plan/add-on charges. External S3/cloud calls can create separate provider bills.

facts.label: Minimum storage and early deletion
facts.value: Object minimum billed size, hot/archive class minimum days and early-deletion billing were not found for native files.

facts.label: Vector/index limits
facts.value: Native vector field holds a fixed-length numeric array per field; vector indexes and similarity metrics are documented.

facts.label: Vector/index limits
facts.value: Published maximum indexed dimensions, vector/index/namespace counts and vector metadata ceiling were not established.

facts.label: Embedding and reranking extras
facts.value: Embedding generation in the tutorial calls an external model API. Agents accept provider API keys; limited free Gemini development test credits do not reset. No included production embedding/reranking token allowance established.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Essential allows 10 background-task definitions; Pro unlimited definitions plus sub-minute schedules. Free has no scheduled background tasks, though it has Lambda functions. No per-invocation/GB-second tariff.

facts.label: Run limits and pricing
facts.value: Lambdas have configured timeouts, but numerical self-serve per-run duration/RAM/vCPU/concurrency limits were not established. BYOC Task Resources are shared by all tasks, not per-job machines.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Public self-service registration offered; Terms require age 18+ and lawful use. Regulated health data requires the designated plan/add-on and an effective written health-data agreement before processing.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Whether a payment card is required to open Free was not established in inspected public pages.

facts.label: Signup and use restrictions
facts.value: Free is marketed for development/testing; Essential is the production entry point. A blanket commercial-production permission or prohibition for Free was not clearly established.

facts.label: Primary type and other roles
facts.value: Backend platform (our classification): managed PostgreSQL, API/business-logic builder, authentication, files, realtime, jobs and AI/MCP tooling.

facts.label: Included backend services
facts.value: Native database, API builder/function stacks, user authentication, file storage, Lambdas and realtime. Background tasks start on Essential; private files and Redis caching start on Pro.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Standard REST/HTTP and autogenerated Swagger/OpenAPI; official @xano/js-sdk for JavaScript/TypeScript in browser/Node.js. Native WebSocket interface for Realtime V2.

facts.label: App connection options
facts.value: Direct PostgreSQL connector included on Essential/Pro, with full-access or read-only credentials and IP allowlist. Connection covers the whole instance, not one workspace.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Require authentication per API; new endpoints default to auth off. Filter/authorize records using $auth.id; a valid token alone does not enforce record ownership. Native auth uses JWE tokens.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Account authenticator 2FA is available. Pro adds builder role/permissions management; Custom adds enterprise SSO/security controls. Direct DB credentials support IP allowlisting, regeneration and read-only access.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: DPA with SCCs is available on paid plans by request, excluding Free. Privacy Notice distinguishes Xano’s controller role for its website from processor role for customer applications.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: Managed PostgreSQL with relational tables, typed fields, SQL, JSON/objects/lists, geography and vectors. New workspaces default to standard SQL columns since release 1.68 (2025-05-27); older tables may use JSONB layouts.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: Database Transaction groups database operations so the group can roll back on database errors. Only database operations count toward rollback; other function errors may not cause a database rollback.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: Formal isolation level, cross-database transaction scope and replica-read consistency guarantees were not established.

facts.label: Test environments and branches
facts.value: Essential/Pro include logic branching/merging and three data sources; Free has neither. Branches copy business logic, not databases. Data sources hold separate records with the same schema; paid CLI sandbox has separate database isolation.

facts.label: Test environments and branches
facts.value: Data Sources guide says as many sources as desired; current pricing caps Essential and Pro at three.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Pro includes a managed backend load balancer. Custom offers horizontal database scaling and Highly Available multi-zone deployment with automatic failover/recovery on zone outage.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Realtime V2 provides WebSocket channels and function-stack message handlers; channels choose at_most_once or at_least_once delivery and optional per-recipient tracking. Conversation transcript has configurable count and TTL.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Native offline database reads/writes, conflict resolution and a complete reconnect/replay protocol window were not established.

facts.label: Extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Indexes include primary, GIN, standard, unique, hash, spatial, fuzzy-search and vector. Vector metrics listed: L2, L1, inner product and cosine distance.

facts.label: Upload and file limits
facts.value: Free maximum file upload: 64MB; storage limited to watermarked images.

facts.label: Upload and file limits
facts.value: Essential maximum file upload: 128MB.

facts.label: Upload and file limits
facts.value: Pro maximum file upload: 2GB; Custom maximum configurable.

facts.label: Upload and file limits
facts.value: Native multipart/resumable upload contract, part counts, content-type enforcement and maximum signed-link TTL were not established.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Xano offers external AWS S3 functions for listing, signed URLs, upload, delete, reading and metadata; upload has Object Lock parameters. Also lists Azure Blob and Google Cloud Storage integrations.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: A native S3 wire-compatible endpoint/operation matrix for Xano-hosted files was not found.

facts.label: Delivery and private files
facts.value: Public file URLs are static and remain accessible without authentication/other permission checks to anyone holding the URL. Essential has no native private-file entitlement.

facts.label: Delivery and private files
facts.value: Pro/Custom private file fields expose no ordinary public URL; function stack generates time-limited signed URL with TTL in seconds. A field is public or private, not mixed. Paid plans support custom instance domains.

facts.label: Filters and mixed search
facts.value: Vector-distance sorting can be combined with application query filters; separate fuzzy/full-text search supports language, weighted fields and ranking. Packaged sparse+dense fusion/BM25 contract not established.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: Xano runs function stacks/XanoScript, JavaScript/TypeScript Lambdas in Deno, scheduled background tasks and async custom functions on its managed instance. Custom/BYOC can also run Docker sidecars.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Async functions run without blocking the caller and return an execution ID; Async Function Await retrieves outputs. Try/Catch/Finally provides application-controlled error handling.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior

apps.line: Hosted vector database for similarity, filtered and hybrid search.

free.text: 5 GB storage; 2.5M vCUs/mo; 7 consecutive idle days to suspend; resumable

sql.math: Free is $0 only if 2.5M vCUs (compute units) and 5 GB storage fit. The paid minimum for reads is 100,000 × 6 minimum vCUs × $4 per million = $2.40. Writes, storage, index overhead and transfer leave the total unknown.
Free is $0 if the data plus indexes fit within 5 GB. 0.7168 GB is raw data before index overhead. After 7 inactive days it suspends, and it can be resumed.

files.math: Managed Volumes are for imports and migrations, not general app file storage.

jobs.math: Zilliz Cloud does not provide a customer job or workflow runner.

facts.value: Full-text and model-based search functions can call integrated model providers; Zilliz also documents hosted models as a separate private-preview feature in its January 2026 release notes.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: API keys and cluster username/password credentials protect serving-cluster connections. On-Demand project endpoints require an API key.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Zilliz Cloud supports organization/project/data-plane roles; September 2026 docs added separate organization and project roles and custom project roles.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Organization account registration supports MFA options; Enterprise and above can enforce organization MFA. If SSO is enabled, the identity provider controls MFA.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Enterprise SSO and audit logs are plan features. Current pricing also lists granular RBAC and audit logs for Enterprise.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Cluster IP allowlists accept up to 100 IP addresses/CIDR entries per project’s clusters. With an empty list, connections are allowed from any IP; adding entries restricts cluster access.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Console IP allowlists support up to 100 IPs/CIDR entries and require Enterprise or higher. This restricts console access, not cluster data-plane access.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Up to 10 private endpoints are allowed per project. Enterprise pricing lists private endpoints and VPC peering; private-endpoint API traffic does not incur Zilliz data transfer charges.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Data is encrypted in transit with TLS 1.2 or later and at rest with AES-256. The standard security page says mutual TLS is not available.

facts.label: Data access controls
facts.value: Business Critical adds customer-managed encryption keys and full-path in-transit encryption; current pricing labels this plan HIPAA-eligible. A badge is not treated as a legal compliance determination.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: Zilliz Cloud is a managed vector database service powered by the Milvus core; app access uses Milvus-compatible APIs/SDKs. This identifies the hosted engine only and does not restate the separate Milvus project’s license or release facts.

facts.label: Engine and query model
facts.value: The service supports vector and scalar data fields, vector indexes, filtering, and similarity search. The current limits page lists AUTOINDEX for vector fields and L2, inner product, or cosine metrics.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: Documented read consistency choices are Strong, Bounded Staleness, Eventually, and Session; Bounded Staleness is the default.

facts.label: Transactions and consistency
facts.value: I did not find a published multi-operation ACID transaction guarantee in the Cloud consistency, collection, and API docs checked.

facts.label: Test environments and branches
facts.value: Separate projects can be used for development and production; the public limits page allows up to 100 projects per user in one organization. I found no copy-on-write database branching feature.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Replicas require at least eight CUs, are capped at 100 per cluster, and total Query CU × replica count may not exceed 204,800. Some older compatible clusters need at least 12 CUs.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Enterprise supports multiple availability zones and advertises 99.95% uptime; Business Critical reaches 99.99% when multi-replica is enabled. Standard has no published SLA in the current comparison.

facts.label: Replicas and failover
facts.value: Business Critical includes global clusters, multi-region replication, automated failover, and point-in-time recovery; these are not standard Free/Serverless features.

facts.label: Live updates and offline sync
facts.value: Offline client sync and conflict-resolution behavior are not applicable to this hosted vector-search service; the reviewed product docs describe server-side database operations and search APIs.

facts.label: Extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Cloud vector fields support AUTOINDEX with L2, inner product, or cosine metrics; scalar fields list TRIE or STL_SORT indexes as applicable.

facts.label: Extensions and specialized indexes
facts.value: Built-in BM25 full-text, hybrid search and keyword matching are documented. Zilliz states its BM25 function runs inside the database engine without external model inference.

facts.label: Upload and file limits
facts.value: Managed Volume pay-as-you-go accepts up to 100 GB and unlimited file count per upload. The docs do not state a separate maximum size for an individual file.

facts.label: Upload and file limits
facts.value: Free trial volume is limited to 5 GB total and up to 1 GB/1,000 files per upload. It expires and is deleted after 30 days.

facts.label: S3 and other API compatibility
facts.value: Managed Volume is not documented as an S3-compatible application file service. The docs expose Zilliz SDK management and note upload is not exposed through the current v2 volume REST API.

facts.label: Delivery and private files
facts.value: Managed Volumes are described as staging files for import and migration, not as public/private end-user delivery, signed URLs, custom domains, or CDN storage. These delivery features are not applicable to the documented volume use.

facts.label: Filters and mixed search
facts.value: Cloud supports dense and sparse vector search, scalar filtering, hybrid search across vector fields, and built-in full-text/BM25 search.

facts.label: Filters and mixed search
facts.value: Hybrid search combines multiple vector result sets and supports reranking; one AnnSearchRequest can contain only one query datum.

facts.label: Filters and mixed search
facts.value: External collections support read-only search/query against supported external data, but do not support insert, upsert, delete, import, flush, compact, backup, restore, or migration.

facts.label: Execution model and languages
facts.value: Not applicable: Zilliz Cloud sells a hosted database/search service; On-Demand compute runs search and index tasks, not arbitrary customer code.

facts.label: Delivery and failure behavior
facts.value: Not applicable: On-Demand is a search/index compute mode, not a message queue or job delivery product.

facts.label: Schedules and queue retention
facts.value: Not applicable: there is no customer job queue or scheduled-job retention service in the hosted database offer checked.

facts.label: Logs and run history
facts.value: Not applicable as job-run history. Database Job Center tracks import, backup, and index operations; this is not a general code-run history service.

facts.label: Operating requirements and feature gaps
facts.value: Not applicable: Zilliz Cloud has no self-hosted software edition. BYOC remains Zilliz-managed software in the customer cloud account, with separate cloud ownership.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Managed SaaS supports AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure. Project region is chosen at setup and cannot later be changed; create a project in another region to move the deployment.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Always-on Free and Serverless managed regions listed are AWS eu-central-1 and Google Cloud us-west1. The current matrix lists no Azure Free/Serverless region.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Managed Dedicated regions listed are AWS us-west-2, us-east-1, us-east-2, ca-central-1, eu-central-1, eu-west-1, eu-west-2, ap-northeast-1, ap-southeast-1, ap-northeast-2, ap-southeast-2; Google Cloud us-west1, us-east4, us-central1, europe-west3, europe-west4, asia-southeast1, asia-northeast1; Azure East US, East US 2, Central US, Germany West Central, North Europe, Central India, and Japan East.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Managed On-Demand regions in the current matrix are AWS us-west-2, us-east-1, us-east-2, ca-central-1, eu-central-1, eu-west-1, eu-west-2, ap-northeast-1, ap-southeast-1, ap-northeast-2, ap-southeast-2; Azure East US, East US 2, Central US, Germany West Central, North Europe, and Central India. No GCP On-Demand region is listed.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: AWS ap-east-1, AWS ap-southeast-7, and Google Cloud europe-west9 are BYOC-only in the October 29 launch notes. The 28-region marketing total includes BYOC-only locations.

facts.label: Regions and data location
facts.value: Backups are stored in the source cluster’s region by default. Cross-region backup is Business Critical SaaS only, supports AWS and GCP, and is unavailable on Azure; destination must use the same cloud provider.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Cloud offers in-console and API migration; current external migration guides list Pinecone, Qdrant, Elasticsearch, PostgreSQL, Tencent Cloud VectorDB, and OpenSearch.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Data import supports JSON, Parquet, and NumPy from object storage; console upload supports local JSON or Parquet up to 1 GB. Free object-storage imports are limited to 1 GB per request/file and 1,000 files.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Paid Serverless/Dedicated object-storage imports can total up to 1 TB per request, with files up to 10 GB and up to 1,000 files. Free imports remain smaller.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Dedicated clusters support manual backups and scheduled automatic backups. Automatic backup default retention is 7 days and can be set up to 30 days; manual backups remain until deleted.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Backups exclude collection TTL settings, the default db_admin password, and dynamic/scheduled scaling settings. Restores must use the original region and same CU type; cluster and selected-collection restores are supported.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Manual backup export to object storage is Private Preview for Dedicated clusters in Enterprise projects and requires support enablement. It is not a general public export path.

facts.label: Leaving and deleting
facts.value: Closing an account requires removing its clusters or organization first in the documented cases. After account closure, the account cannot log in; all account data is cleaned after 30 days.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Manual and automatic cluster backups are available only for Dedicated clusters; automatic backup is disabled by default and applies to the whole cluster.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Automatic backups default to seven days’ retention and can be set from one to 30 days. Manual backups are retained until the user deletes them.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Backups cost extra by stored backup size and region; current AWS us-east-1 example uses $0.025/GB/month, billed daily with one-day minimum.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Restore is limited to the same region as the source backup and the same CU type. Backups omit TTL settings, db_admin password, and dynamic/scheduled scaling settings.

facts.label: Backups and restore
facts.value: Cross-region backup is an optional Business Critical SaaS feature, limited to AWS and GCP; storage and inter-region transfer both cost extra.

facts.label: File recovery and protection
facts.value: Files/folders deleted from a Managed Volume cannot be recovered. A frozen organization deletes managed-volume files; the docs do not advertise object versioning or undelete.

facts.label: Identity and old names
facts.value: Zilliz Cloud is the vendor’s managed vector database service. The official product URL is https://zilliz.com/.

facts.label: Identity and old names
facts.value: The company is broadening its product framing to “Vector Lakebase”; the current pricing and docs still call the hosted service Zilliz Cloud. I found no separate former product name for Zilliz Cloud.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Zilliz Cloud is a hosted SaaS. Zilliz manages its serving infrastructure on AWS, Google Cloud, or Azure where each plan and region is available.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: BYOC is a Zilliz-managed deployment in the customer’s cloud account and VPC/VNet. The customer owns the cloud account and infrastructure; BYOC is not a self-hosted software license.

facts.label: Hosting and license
facts.value: Zilliz Cloud has no separate self-hosted edition or self-host software license. The open-source Milvus project is a separate directory entry and is outside this file’s scope.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Zilliz Cloud is operating and available. The company’s newest visible product changelog entry is dated October 29, 2026 and includes new product features.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: Vector Lakebase was announced as a public preview in September 2026 as an expansion of Zilliz Cloud. Zilliz’s May 2026 explanation says the direction does not abandon vector databases.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: On-demand compute and search are also marked Public Preview in the official docs; this is a preview feature within Zilliz Cloud, not a shutdown of the hosted service.

facts.label: Lifecycle and access stage
facts.value: No shutdown, sunset, or acquisition notice for Zilliz Cloud was found in the official blog, newsroom, changelog, product home, or pricing pages checked.

facts.label: Vendor home and main markets
facts.value: Zilliz’s privacy policy names Zilliz Inc. as the company responsible for its products and services. The page does not state the company’s country of incorporation.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Free and Standard pricing cards list community support. Enterprise includes Enterprise support; Business Critical includes priority support.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Current pricing lists Enterprise and Business Critical on-call availability 24/7/365; emergency response is 30 minutes on-call, urgent one hour, high priority four hours, and normal one business day.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: Enterprise plan advertises 99.95% uptime SLA. Business Critical advertises 99.99% when multi-replica is enabled. Standard pricing does not publish an uptime SLA.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: The official status page shows components for AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, control plane, API, authentication, and billing. At the checked page view, all systems were operational and the visible incident list had no reports for November 1–3, 2026.

facts.label: Support and service promises
facts.value: General support contact path is the Zilliz Cloud support portal; a separate public response-time promise for the Free or Standard community channel was not listed.
